The connection was completed but a disconnect occurred while trying to perform protocol-specific initialization, usually due to use of different network protocols by opposite sides of the connection. This usually is caused by incorrect Oracle Net administrative setup for database links or external procedure calls. The most frequent specific causes are: -- The connection uses a connect string which refers to a Heterogeneous Services agent instead of an Oracle server. -- The connection uses a connect string which includes an (HS=) specification. -- Hitting Ctrl+C before connection initialization is complete. -- Using DRCP on Windows with SQLNET.AUTHENTICATION_SERVICES set to NTS. -- Connection timeout due to SQLNET.INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT parameter when all shared servers are busy in shared server configuration. -- The character set of the database is not recognized by the client process, which may be caused by an incorrect or unnecessary setting of the ORA_NLS10 client environment variable or by a new or user-defined character set installed in the Oracle server and used for the database.
action: Check Oracle Net administration in the following ways: -- When using TNSNAMES.ORA or an Oracle Names server, make sure that the client connection to the Oracle server uses the correct service name or SID. -- Check LISTENER.ORA on the connection end point's host machine to assure that this service name or SID refers to the correct server. -- Confirm in TNSNAMES.ORA or the equivalent service definition that the connect string does not contain (HS=). -- Set SQLNET.AUTHENTICATION_SERVICES to NONE when using DRCP on Windows. -- Verify the NLS configuration of the Oracle client process. Ensure that the database character set is supported by the Oracle client software. If necessary, upgrade the Oracle client software or install the missing user-defined character set.

description: pass-through SQL: cursor not found
cause: A value passed to a pass-through SQL function or procedure call as the cursor did not identify a currently open cursor.
action: Use a cursor number returned by the pass-through SQL OPEN_CURSOR call.

description: pass-through SQL: SQL parse error
cause: A non-Oracle system rejected text supplied as a pass-through SQL statement.
action: Ensure that the SQL supplied to the pass-through SQL PARSE call is valid for the non-Oracle system.

description: pass-through SQL: call flow error
cause: A pass-through SQL function was called in an invalid order.
action: Correct the program flow by changing the order of API calls to match the flow described in the manual.

description: pass-through SQL: invalid bind-variable position
cause: A pass-through SQL function referring to the position of a bind variable in the currently parsed SQL statement supplied an invalid bind-variable position. Valid values are 1 through N, where N is the number of bind-variable place-holders in the SQL text.
action: Verify that the bind-variable position parameter is in the correct range to represent a place-holder in the SQL text. Confirm that the SQL text uses the correct syntax for a bind-variable place holder, as required by the non-Oracle system.

description: pass-through SQL: out of cursors
cause: The pool of available cursors had been exhausted.
action: Close existing open cursors by using the pass-through SQL CLOSE_CURSOR function.

description: pass-through SQL: required parameter missing or NULL
cause: An attempt was made to pass a NULL value to a non-NULL parameter.
action: Use a non-NULL value for the parameter.

description: authorization insufficient to access table
cause: A query attempted to access a table in the non-Oracle system that is either privileged or has privileged columns.
action: Contact the DBA for the non-Oracle system. The DBA can grant permission to access the privileged table or columns.

description: unknown %s for database link to non-Oracle system
cause: When attempting to connect to a non-Oracle system through a Heterogeneous Services database link, the agent supporting this non-Oracle system failed to return FDS_CLASS_NAME and/or FDS_INST_NAME. ORACLE requires these names to configure the heterogeneous database link.
action: Contact the DBA to check setup of the connection and the Heterogeneous Services agent.

description: HS_FDS_CONNECT_STRING undefined for non-Oracle system
cause: A database link to a non-Oracle system had no HS_FDS_CONNECT_STRING initialization parameter in the ORACLE server's data dictionary for Heterogeneous Services. Without this parameter, the connection could not be completed.
action: Contact your DBA to verify correct setup of an HS_FDS_CONNECT_STRING entry in the ORACLE Heterogeneous Services data dictionary.

description: FDS_CLASS_NAME is %s, FDS_INST_NAME is %s
cause: An associated error was reported in another message, and this message supplies supplementary information to assist diagnosis of that error. FDS_CLASS_NAME and FDS_INST_NAME are used to access information in tables and views of the ORACLE data dictionary that direct operation of Heterogeneous Services on a database link to a non-Oracle data store.
action: Use the FDS_CLASS_NAME and FDS_INST_NAME values to check ORACLE data dictionary contents when necessary to diagnose the cause of the associated error.

description: error in configuration of agent process
cause: An ORACLE server invoked a function not supported by the connected agent (Heterogeneous Services or external procedures). The most probable cause is incorrect Net8 setup, resulting in use of the wrong agent executable.
action: Check Net8 administration in the following ways: -- When using TNSNAMES.ORA or an Oracle Names server, make sure that the connection from the ORACLE server uses the correct SID. -- Check LISTENER.ORA on the agent's host machine to assure that this SID refers to the correct agent executable in its (PROGRAM=...) clause.

description: unable to set date format on non-Oracle system
cause: Initialization of a Heterogeneous Services connection to set the date format to be used on the connected non-Oracle system.
action: If the Oracle data dictionary supplies a value for the HS_NLS_DATE_FORMAT parameter, confirm that this value is formatted correctly by the rules of the non-Oracle system. Also check for additional information in log and trace files generated by the Heterogeneous Services agent.

description: Heterogeneous Services data truncation error
cause: A select operation was attempted with an insufficient data buffer to satisfy the request.
action: Contact your DBA to verify whether your gateway initialization parameter HS_KEEP_REMOTE_COLUMN_SIZE is set appropriately based on your requirement. If it is, make sure the sizes of bind parameters are sufficient. If the problem persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: unable to open RPC connection to external procedure agent
cause: Initialization of a network connection to the Extproc agent did not succeed. This problem could be caused by network problems, incorrect listener configuration, or incorrect transfer code.
action: Check listener configuration in LISTENER.ORA and TNSNAMES.ORA, or check Oracle Names Server.

description: lost RPC connection to external procedure agent
cause: A fatal error occurred in either an RPC network connection, the extproc agent, or the invoked 3GL after communication had been established successfully.
action: First check the 3GL code you are invoking; the most likely cause of this error is abnormal termination of the invoked "C" routine. If this is not the case, check for network problems. Correct the problem if you find it. If all components appear to be normal but the problem persists, the problem could be an internal logic error in the RPC transfer code. Contact your customer support representative.

description: argument %s of external procedure %s has unsupported datatype %s
cause: While transferring external procedure arguments to the agent, an unsupported datatype was detected.
action: Check your documentation for the supported datatypes of external procedure arguments.

description: A protocol error occurred during a callback from an external procedure.
cause: An internal protocol error occurred while trying to process a callback to the Oracle server from an external procedure or function.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: network error during callback from external procedure agent
cause: An internal network error occurred while trying to execute a callback to the Oracle server from the user's 3GL routine.
action: Contact Oracle customer support.

description: recursive external procedures are not supported
cause: A callback from within a user's 3GL routine resulted in the invocation of another external procedure.
action: Make sure that the SQL code executed in a callback does not directly call another external procedure, or indirectly results in another external procedure, such as triggers calling external procedures, PL/SQL procedures calling external procedures, etc.

description: protocol error while executing recursive external procedure
cause: An internal protocol error occurred while trying to execute an external procedure resulting from a callback in another external procedure.
action: Contact Oracle customer support.

description: a direct connection to this agent is not allowed
cause: A user or a tool tried to establish a direct connection to either an external procedure agent or a Heterogeneous Services agent, for example: "SVRMGR> CONNECT SCOTT/TIGER@NETWORK_ALIAS". This type of connection is not allowed.
action: When executing the CONNECT statement, make sure your database link or network alias is not pointing to a Heterogeneous Option agent or an external procedure agent.

description: remote references are not permitted during agent callbacks
cause: A Heterogeous Services agent issued a callback to the Oracle server which attemted to to access a remote system. This is not supported.
action: Make sure that SQL code issued by Heterogeneous Services agents does not reference a database link.

description: heterogeneous apply internal error
cause: The apply slave process encountered an error while trying to apply changes through a gateway to a non-Oracle system.
action: Make sure that the apply database link is correctly configured and that the gateway listener and the non-Oracle system are correctly set up and are up and running. If everything is configured correctly and the problem still occurs, contact Oracle customer support. errors 28590 - 28599 are reserved for the HS agent control utility

description: agent control utility: illegal or badly formed command
cause: The user has issued an unrecognized or syntactically incorrect command.
action: Refer to documentation and correct the syntax of the command.

description: agent control utility: unable to access parameter file
cause: The agent control utility was unable to access its parameter file. This could be because it could not find its admin directory or because permissions on directory were not correctly set.
action: The agent control utility puts its parameter file in either the directory pointed to by the environment variable AGTCTL_ADMIN or in the directory pointed to by the environment variable TNS_ADMIN. Make sure that at least one of these environment variables is set and that it points to a directory that the agent has access to.

description: agent control utility: agent SID not set
cause: The agent needs to know the value of the AGENT_SID parameter before it can process any commands. If it does not have a value for AGENT_SID then all commands will fail.
action: Issue the command SET AGENT_SID <value> and then retry the command that failed.

description: agent control utility: command terminated with error
cause: An error occurred during the processing of the command. There could be several causes. A SET or an UNSET command could have been issued after the agent was started. This is illegal. The user may have attempted to start two agents with the same SID value or the user could have attempted to shutdown an agent that is no longer running.
action: If the user wishes to issue a SET or an UNSET command, he should make sure the agent is shutdown first by issuing the SHUTDOWN command.

description: agent control utility: invalid parameter name
cause: The user tried to set or unset an invalid agent parameter.
action: Refer to documentation and correct the parameter name.

description: Extproc agent: Invalid DLL Path
cause: The path of DLL supplied for the extproc execution was invalid.
action: Ensure that the DLL path is set properly using the EXTPROC_DLLS environment variable.

description: Extproc agent : invalid or disabled credential %s
cause: The credential of the PL/SQL library supplied for extproc processing was invalid or disabled.
action: Ensure that the credential of the PL/SQL library is both valid and enabled.
params: 1) credential_name: The name of the credential.

description: invalid [no]MINIMIZE option
cause: user didn't type this alter table <table_name> MINIMIZE RECORDS_PER_BLOCK or alter table <table_name> NOMINIMIZE RECORDS_PER_BLOCK
action: reenter correct sql command

description: statement not permitted on tables containing bitmap indexes
cause: table has bitmap indexes and user is minimizing or nominimizing records_per_block
action: drop all bitmap indexes before changing records_per_block

description: statement not permitted on empty tables
cause: table is empty and statement does not work on empty tables
action: try statement after loading your data

description: table too fragmented to build bitmap index (%s,%s,%s)
cause: The table has one or more blocks that exceed the maximum number of rows expected when creating a bitmap index. This is probably due to deleted rows. The values in the message are: (data block address, slot number found, maximum slot allowed)
action: Defragment the table or block(s). Use the values in the message to determine the FIRST block affected. (There may be others).

description: bitmap indexes cannot be reversed
cause: user tried to create reverse bitmap index
action: don't do this; it is not supported

description: block too fragmented to build bitmap index (%s,%s)
cause: The block(s) exceed the maximum number of rows expected when creating a bitmap index. This is probably due to maximum slot allowed set too low. The values in the message are: (slot number found, maximum slot allowed)
action: alter system flush shared_pool; update tab$ set spare1 = 8192 where obj# = (select obj# from obj$ where NAME=<table_name> AND owner# = <table_owner>; commit;

description: bitmap index is corrupted - see trace file for diagnostics
cause: Validate Index detected bitmap corruption in its argument index
action: Drop this bitmap index and create a new one.

description: automatic CDR delta resolution cannot be enabled on non-numeric column "%s"
cause: Automatic conflict detection and resolution delta resolution cannot be configured on non-numeric columns.
action: None.

description: Temporary LCR is incorrectly formed
cause: Temporary logical change record used for LOB assembly is invalid.
action: None.

description: Copy from source to target LOB buffer failed
cause: LOB construction copy failed.
action: None.

description: This is an attempt to drop the ACDR resolution columns directly.
cause: An attempt is being made to directly drop the Automatic Conflict Detection and Resolution (ACDR) timestamp using the ALTER TABLE statement.
action: Drop the ACDR resolution columns by using the appropriate procedures in DBMS_GOLDENGATE_ADM.

description: Failed to free Apply subheap.
cause: An attempt failed to free an apply subheap.
action: None.

description: Primary index on an IOT cannot be rebuilt
cause: An attempt is made to issue alter index rebuild on IOT-TOP
action: Use Alter table MOVE to reorganize the table(IOT)

description: Primary index on IOTs can not be marked unusable
cause: An attempt is made to mark IOT-TOP unusable thru ALTER INDEX
action: Remove the option UNUSABLE

description: overflow segment attributes cannot be specified
cause: During ALTER MOVE ONLINE of a index-organized table, the user attempted to enter one or more of the following options: OVERFLOW, PCTTHRESHOLD,INCLUDING.
action: Remove the illegal option(s).

description: tables must both be index-organized
cause: Attempt to exchange a non IOT table/partition with a partition/table respectively
action: Ensure that non-partitioned and partitioned tables are both index-organized.

description: table and partition not overflow compatible
cause: If one of the tables (partitioned/non-partitioned) has overflow data segment and the other one doesn't.
action: Ensure that non-partitioned and partitioned tables both have overflow data segment or neither one does.

description: Alter table add overflow syntax error
cause: Syntax error
action: Check the syntax.

description: incomplete attribute specification
cause: The attribute specification is not done for all partitions"
action: Specify the storage attributes either for ALL partitions or NONE NLS_DO_NOT_TRANSLATE [28657,28657]

description: Allow IOT w/o overflow though overflow is required
cause: N/A
action: THIS IS NOT A USER ERROR NUMBER/MESSAGE. THIS DOES NOT NEED TO BE TRANSLATED OR DOCUMENTED. IT IS USED ONLY BY IMPORT CODE.

description: This operation is supported only for Index-Organized tables
cause: Attempt to perform some IOT specific operation on a non-IOT
action: don't do this. This is not supported

description: COMPRESS must be specified at object level first
cause: Attempt to specify COMPRESS at partition level without first specifying at the table level
action: Specify COMPRESS at table level. Use ALTER TABLE xxx MODIFY DEFAULT ATTRIBUTES COMPRESS ...

description: Partitioned Index-Organized table may not be MOVEd as a whole
cause: Attempt to MOVE partitioned IOT as a whole
action: don't do this. This is not supported

description: Object already has COMPRESS clause specified
cause: Attempt to specify compress for iot/index which already has a compression clause.
action: This is a 'create time only' attribute

description: IOT index and overflow segments must share the same LOGGING attribute
cause: Attempt to specify LOGGING for one segment and NOLOGGING for the other segment.
action: don't do that

description: Logging/Nologging attribute can not be specified in the statement ALTER TABLE ADD OVERFLOW
cause: Attempt to specify LOGGING for a Alter Table Add Overflow.
action: don't do that

description: a partitioned table may not be coalesced as a whole
cause: User attempted to coalesce a partitioned IOT using ALTER TABLE COALESCE statement, which is illegal
action: Coalesce the table a partition at a time (using ALTER TABLE MODIFY PARTITION COALESCE)

description: table and partition must have same compression attribute
cause: User attempted to EXCHANGE a compression enabled partition with a compression disabled table or vice versa OR the # of columns compressed is different for table and partition
action: Make sure the compression attributes match If they don't, fix it using ALTER TABLE MOVE [PARTITION] COMPRESS

description: option not allowed for an index on UROWID column(s)
cause: User attempted to build a REVERSE or COMPRESSED or GLOBAL partitioned index on UROWID column(s)
action: Build the index without these options

description: USING INDEX option not allowed for the primary key of an IOT
cause: User attempted to define storage attributes for the primary key index of an Index-Organized table with USING INDEX clause. All the storage attribute defined for the (IOT)table applies to the primary key index and a separate USING INDEX clause is not required.
action: Remove the USING INDEX clause and specify all attributes directly for the table

description: cannot reference mapping table of an index-organized table
cause: An attempt to directly access the mapping table of an index-organized table
action: Issue the statement against the parent index-organized table containing the specified mapping table.

description: bitmap index can not be created on an IOT with no mapping table
cause: User attempted to create a bitmap index on an index-organized table without a mapping table.
action: Enable bitmap indexes on the Index-organized table by creating a mapping table using 'ALTER TABLE .. MOVE MAPPING TABLE'.

description: mapping table cannot be dropped due to an existing bitmap index
cause: User attempted to drop the mapping table with NOMAPPING option when the IOT has one or more bitmap indexed.
action: Drop the bitmap index(es) before dropping the mapping table.

description: UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES may not be used on a partitioned index as a whole
cause: User attempted to UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES on a partitioned index using ALTER INDEX UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES statement, which is illegal.
action: Issue a partition level operation with ALTER INDEX .. PARTITION .. UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES

description: UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES may not be used on a global index
cause: User attempted to UPDATE BLOCK REFERENCES on a global partitioned or non-partitioned index. This feature is not supported for non-partitioned or global partitioned index on a partitioned IOT and a global partitioned index on a non-partitioned IOT.
action: Use online index [partition] rebuild to fix the block references

description: Merge operation not allowed on an index-organized table
cause: User attempted merge operation on an index-organized table. Merge is not supported on a IOT .
action: Use updates and inserts on index-organized table .

description: cannot reference transient index-organized table
cause: An attempt was made to directly access a transient table created created on behalf of a index-organized table partition maintenance operation.
action: Issue the statement against the associated permanent index-organized table.

description: Only roles can be granted to or revoked from program units.
cause: An attempt was made to grant or revoke object privileges or system privileges to program units.
action: Grant the privileges to a role first, and then grant the role to the program units. Also, do not attempt to revoke privileges from a program unit.

description: Keyword PROCEDURE, FUNCTION, or PACKAGE is either missing or not correct.
cause: The keyword PROCEDURE, FUNCTION, or PACKAGE was either missing before the program unit, or it was not consistent with the type of the program unit.
action: Include the correct keyword PROCEDURE, FUNCTION or PACKAGE right before each program unit according to its type.

description: Program unit %s is not owned by the grantor.
cause: An attempt was made to attach roles to or detach roles from one or more program units by someone other than the owner or SYS. Only a program unit owner or SYS can attach roles to or detach roles from a program unit.
action: Specify only the program units owned by the grantor in the command.

description: Only regular database roles can be attached to or detached from program units.
cause: An attempt was made to attach non-supported types of roles to or detach them from program units. Application roles, secure application roles, external roles, global roles, and light-weight roles cannot be attached to or detached from program units.
action: Remove any application role, secure application role, external role, global role, and light-weight role from the command.

description: Role %s is not directly granted to the owner of the program units.
cause: An attempt was made to attach roles that were not directly granted to the owner of the program units. The roles must be granted to the owner directly in order to attach them to the owner's program units.
action: Grant the role to the owner of the program unit first.

description: The grantor does not have privileges to grant the role %s to the program units.
cause: Privileges to grant a role to a program unit were insufficient. The grantor must have the GRANT ANY ROLE privilege or the ADMIN option or the DELEGATE option for the role to do the operation.
action: Obtain the required privilege and retry.

description: duplicate program unit %s found in grantee list
cause: A duplicate program unit was found in the GRANTEE clause.
action: Specify each program unit in the grantee list only once.

description: Reserved word ALL was used with roles in the REVOKE command to detach roles from program units.
cause: An attempt was made to use reserved word ALL jointly with roles in a REVOKE command to detach roles from program units.
action: Do not specify roles in the privilege clause except for the reserved word ALL.

description: More than %s roles were attached to the program unit.
cause: Too many roles were attached to the program unit.
action: Detach some roles from the program unit and retry the operation.

description: Role with DELEGATE option can only be granted to user.
cause: One of the grantees was not a user when trying to grant a role with the DELEGATE option.
action: Verify that each grantee is a user and try the operation again.

description: OCI_BATCH_ERRORS or OCI_RETURN_ROW_COUNT_ARRAY mode can only be specified for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE statement.
cause: OCI_BATCH_ERRORS or OCI_RETURN_ROW_COUNT_ARRAY mode was specified in a statement which is not INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE.
action: Specify OCI_BATCH_ERRORS or OCI_RETURN_ROW_COUNT_ARRAY only for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE statements.

description: OCI_STMT_SCROLLABLE_READONLY can only be specified for SELECT statements.
cause: OCI_STMT_SCROLLABLE_READONLY mode was specified for a non-SELECT statement.
action: Specify OCI_SCROLLABLE_READONLY only for SELECT statements.

description: Invalid buffer or buffer size for OCIServerRelease2()
cause: A zero length or null buffer was specified for the OCIServerRelease2().
action: Specify a valid buffer and length.

description: invalid argument %s
cause: Passed an invalid argument to an Oracle Call Interface (OCI) application programming interface (API).
action: Check the validity of parameters passed to the API. If the error persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: invalid file handle
cause: The file parameter handle was not valid.
action: Ensure that the correct parameter handle is provided.

description: Invalid service context parameter supplied.
cause: The service context parameter was not valid.
action: Ensure that a proper service context is provided and retry.

description: OCI encountered OraCoroutine Error(%d) from (%s)
cause: OCI encountered an internal error
action: Contact Oracle Support Services

description: Connection initialization failed, probable invalid configuration for CMAN in Traffic Director mode
cause: A failure occurred during initialization of connection to connect to Connection Manager (CMAN) in Traffic director mode. The most frequent specific causes are: -- Invalid configuration specified in Connection Manager (CMAN) in Traffic Director mode. -- The database instance/service was down -- Instance does not not currently know of requested service
action: Check CMAN in Traffic Director mode administration in the following ways: -- Correct the configuration of CMAN in Traffice Director mode before starting it. -- Check and correct the wallet credentials and proxy authorization. -- Ensure that the specified service is valid and reconnect. -- Check with CMAN in Traffic Director mode administrator to get more information from traces and sqlnet.log.

description: set current schema operation failed because the given schema name is either invalid or does not exist
cause: An attempt was made to set the schema to a non-existent value.
action: Specify an existing schema name or ask the database administrator to create a new schema.

description: trace event set or reset operation failed
cause: An attempt was made to set or reset a trace event dynamically.
action: Use the correct event number and trace level.

description: A view protected by a data redaction policy cannot be dropped in a different edition.
cause: An attempt is being made to drop a view protected by a data redaction policy in an edition that is different from the one in which it was created.
action: Drop the view in the edition in which it was created.

description: A view protected by a data redaction policy cannot be editioned.
cause: A data redaction policy protects the view that you are attempting to replace with an editioned view. Data redaction does not have support for editioned views.
action: To replace this view with an editioned view, first drop the data redaction policy of the view.

description: internal error code, arguments: [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s]
cause: This is the generic internal error number for program exceptions. This indicated that a process encountered an exceptional condition.
action: Report as a bug - the first argument is the internal error number.

description: thread terminated by fatal error
cause: The thread was in an unrecoverable state.
action: Examine the thread trace file for more information.

description: out of process memory
cause: Operating system memory was exhausted or a per-process limit on private memory usage was reached. The database has an internal limit of 32 GB per Oracle process.
action: Check the use of memory by other Oracle instances and other applications. Exceeding 32 GB in a single process may indicate a memory leak. Consider reducing the size of shared memory to allow more room for private memory.

description: out of shared memory in %s
cause: More shared memory was needed than was available.
action: If using one of the initialization parameters SGA_TARGET, MEMORY_SIZE, or MEMORY_TARGET, increase the value of that parameter. If it is not feasible to increase the parameter, then reduce the value of DB_CACHE_SIZE (if set). If you are not using SGA_TARGET, MEMORY_SIZE, or MEMORY_TARGET, increase the size of the pool that is out of memory. For example, increase SHARED_POOL_SIZE for the shared pool or INMEMORY_SIZE for an IMC heap.

description: illegal argument for function
cause: An illegal argument was passed to dbgc_alloc.
action: Report as a bug.

description: user requested cancel of current operation
cause: NA
action: NA

description: name is already used by an existing product type
cause: An attempt was made to define a product type with the same name as an already defined product type.
action: Use the already existing product type with the specified name, or use a different name for the product type.

description: id is already used by an existing product type
cause: An attempt was made to define a product type with the same id as an already defined product type.
action: Choose a different name for the product type.

description: error encountered when attempting to open a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to open a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check that the specified directory name, file name, and open options are valid.

description: error encountered when attempting to read a file [%s] [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to read a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the specified arguments to the read interface.

description: encountered the end-of-file when reading the file
cause: The ADR file interface encountered the end-of-file when reading the file.
action: Handle the end of file condition.

description: error encountered when attempting to write a file [%s] [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to write a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the specified arguments to the write interface.

description: read mismatch on blocks requested and returned, [%s], [%s]
cause: There was a mismatch between the number of blocks requested for reading and the number of blocks actually returned.
action: Check the file to make sure there are no partial blocks.

description: write mismatch on blocks requested and returned, [%s], [%s]
cause: There was a mismatch between the number of blocks requested for writing and the number of blocks actually written.
action: Check that there is enough space left on the device to write the requested number of blocks.

description: error initializing the ADR %s object
cause: There was an error encountered during the initialization of one of the ADR file objects.
action: Check the validity of the specified directory name and file name.

description: invalid Bfile input, [%s]
cause: An invalid Bfile was passed into the routine to convert the bfile into a file handle.
action: Verify the contents of the specified Bfile.

description: invalid value given for the diagnostic_dest init.ora parameter
cause: The value given for the diagnostic_dest directory is not a valid directory. Either the directory does not exist or the process does not have read/write privileges on the directory.
action: Use a value for diagnostic_dest that is a valid directory with the proper read and write privileges.

description: invalid lock mode for file descriptor, [%s]
cause: The lock mode associated with the file descriptor was invalid in the context of the routine.
action: Verify that a file is not trying to obtain multiple locks and that the file is holding a lock when attempting to release the lock.

description: error encountered while attempting to get a file lock [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered while trying to get a file lock.
action: Check the state of the file and operating system.

description: error encountered while attempting to release a file lock [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered while trying to release a file lock.
action: Check the state of the file and operating system.

description: invalid flags for open file, %s
cause: Invalid flags were passed in to the open file routine.
action: Check to see if the flags are a valid combination.

description: unable to write to stream file because of out of space condition
cause: The system is unable to write the requested number of bytes to a stream file. This is due to an out of space condition. The additional information shows how many bytes were not written.
action: Check that there is enough space left on the device to write the requested number of bytes.

description: error encountered when attempting to close a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to close a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the validity of the file descriptor.

description: error encountered while seeking a file position
cause: There was an error encountered while seeking a position in a file.
action: Check that the requested file position falls within the file boundaries.

description: error encountered when attempting to create a directory [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to create a directory.
action: Check the directory name.

description: error encountered when attempting to remove a directory [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to remove a directory.
action: Check the directory name.

description: error encountered with list directory [%s]
cause: There was an error with listing the elements of a directory.
action: Check the state of the operating system.

description: error encountered when attempting to remove a file [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to remove a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory name and file name.

description: error encountered when attempting to retrieve the file size [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to retrieve the file size with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory name and file name.

description: error with opening the ADR stream file [%s] [%s]
cause: An error was encountered when attempting to open an ADR stream file.
action: Check the rest of the error stack for details of the actual error that was encountered.

description: error with opening the ADR block file [%s] [%s]
cause: An error was encountered when attempting to open an ADR block file.
action: Check the rest of the error stack for details of the actual error that was encountered.

description: error encountered when attempting to flush a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to flush a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the state of the file.

description: device full encountered during write to a file
cause: The device full error was encountered during the write to a file.
action: Check the amount of free space on the device.

description: illegal identifier length, argn:%s, len:%s, lim:%s
cause: An input identifier was passed in that has a length that is greater than the max length.
action: Make sure the input identifier has a length that is less than the max length.

description: attempting to create a file that already exists
cause: The client attempted to create a file that already exists.
action: Either remove the file or check if it is okay if the file already exists.

description: attempting to open a file that does not exist
cause: An attempt was made to open a file that does not exist.
action: Either create the file or check why the file does not exist.

description: opening of a symbolic link is disallowed
cause: An error was encountered when attempting to open a file that is a symbolic link. Users are not allowed to open symbolic links.
action: Check the specified file name.

description: invalid input for the full path specification
cause: Input was incorrectly specified for the full path specification, or the default extension may have been incorrectly specified. Or an empty string was passed in for the full path.
action: Check that the full path string is non-NULL. If you want to specify a relative path from ADR Home for the full path specification, then use '<ADR_HOME>' instead of the actual path to ADR Home. For ADR Base, use '<ADR_BASE>'.

description: invalid lock parameters for get file lock [%s]
cause: Invalid lock parameters passed in for the get file lock routine. The user must pass in file as the lock type. Or, there is a lock mode mismatch. Exclusive locks are not allowed in read-only mode, and shared locks are not allowed in write-only mode.
action: Check that correct lock type is specified and that the correct lock mode is requested for the file given its open flags.

description: error encountered when attempting to tell the file position
cause: An error was encountered when attempting to tell the file position using the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory and file name of the file along with the open state.

description: requested file lock is busy, [%s] [%s]
cause: The requested file lock is busy because another process is holding the file lock.
action: Try to get the file lock again at a later time.

description: file descriptor has already been opened [%s] [%s]
cause: The specified file descriptor has already been opened.
action: Do not open a file that has previously been opened, or check your code to make sure you are cleaning up a file descriptor that is being reused correctly.

description: invalid file descriptor state for operation, %s, %s, %s
cause: The state of the file descriptor was invalid for the requested operation. An example is that a file was opened for read, but a write operation to the file was requested.
action: Check the state of the file descriptor and make sure it matches the operation.

description: uninitialized file descriptor
cause: The specified file descriptor is uninitialized.
action: Make sure the file descriptor is initialized before passing it into the routine.

description: directory already exists [%s]
cause: Operation failed because the specified directory already exists.
action: Remove the directory or ignore this error.

description: uninitialized file handle
cause: The specified file handle is uninitialized.
action: Make sure the file handle is initialized before passing it into the routine.

description: invalid directory name input for client address
cause: An invalid directory name was specified as part of the address path specification.
action: Check that the directory name is non-NULL and that the directory name length does not exceed the maximum length.

description: invalid input to ADR initialization routine
cause: There was an invalid input to the ADR initialization routine.
action: Check the length of the ADR base, product ID, and instance ID input arguments.

description: the specified ADR Base directory does not exist [%s]
cause: The specified ADR Base Directory does not exist.
action: Check that the specified ADR Base Directory is a valid path name and that the directory exists.

description: error creating directory during ADR initialization [%s]
cause: Error encountered when creating a directory during the initialization of the ADR subsystem.
action: Check the input arguments to the ADR initialization routine and the state of the operating system.

description: invalid permissions input for change permissions
cause: Invalid permissions passed into change permissions routine.
action: Check the value of the permissions input.

description: error changing permissions for a file
cause: Error encountered while changing the permissions for a file
action: Check the specified directory and file and the state of the operating system.

description: error encountered while performing standard file I/O
cause: Error encountered while performing standard file I/O
action: Check the validity of standard in, out, and error.

description: invalid seek location, [%s], [%s]
cause: Invalid seek location specified for routine.
action: Check the validity of specified seek location.

description: missing read, write, or exec permission on directory during ADR initialization [%s] [%s]
cause: Error encountered when checking if the process has read, write, and exec privileges on directories needed by the ADR subsystem. This error occurs during the initialization of the ADR subsystem.
action: Check the input arguments to the ADR initialization routine and the state of the operating system. Ensure that the user has the proper permissions on the ADR directories.

description: invalid home location specification for ADR, [%s], [%s], [%s]
cause: Invalid read or write home location specification for ADR.
action: An invalid home was specified for the ADR Read or Write Home location.

description: error encountered when attempting to move a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to move a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory name and file name.

description: error encountered when attempting to copy a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to copy a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory name and file name.

description: error encountered with set current working directory
cause: There was an error with setting the current working directory.
action: Check the path used, or the state of the operating system.

description: error getting operating system time for a file
cause: Error encountered while getting the operating system time for a file.
action: Check the specified directory and file and the state of the operating system.

description: lock table is full
cause: Lock table is full - too many locks granted
action: Try again later

description: error encountered when getting ADR base directory default
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to get the ADR base directory default value.
action: Check your environment to see if the $ORACLE_BASE and $ORACLE_HOME environment variables are set.

description: reached end of file for alert log
cause: The end of file was reached for reading the Alert Log. There are no more messages to read in the Alert Log.
action: Do not read from the Alert Log

description: error encountered when read alert log [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to read a message from the Alert Log.
action: Check the error message and the contents of the alert message.

description: Alert log purge has occurred - retry operation
cause: The purge of the alert log has occurred.
action: Retry the operation.

description: null input to ADR initialization
cause: There was an null input to the ADR initialization routine.
action: Check the ADR base, product ID, and instance ID input arguments.

description: invalid input for ADR base directory
cause: An invalid input was passed in for the ADR base directory name. The ADR base directory name is either NULL or too long of a string.
action: Check the ADR base directory input argument.

description: invalid input for ADR product type
cause: An invalid input was passed in for the ADR product type. The ADR product type is out of bounds.
action: Check the ADR product type input argument.

description: invalid input for ADR product id
cause: An invalid input was passed in for the ADR product id. The ADR product id is either NULL or too long of a string.
action: Check the ADR product id input argument.

description: invalid input for ADR instance id

description: invalid value %s (length = %s) for parameter _MAX_INCIDENT_FILE_SIZE
cause: The string supplied for the parameter _MAX_INCIDENT_FILE_SIZE was not an integer, an integer followed by 'K', 'M' or 'G', nor the special value UNLIMITED.
action: Provide a proper value for this parameter.

description: The maximum metadata version that can be processed is [%s]
cause: The metadata file version being read is greater than the maximum version that can be processed by the parser.
action: Upgrade the client to a later release.

description: The trace record level [%s] exceeded the max level that can be parsed [%s]
cause: The trace file contained higher level records than could be processed in linear time by parser.
action: Report to Oracle.

description: A vertex variable has the same name as an edge variable.
cause: A vertex variable was specified with the same name as an edge variable.
action: Use a different name for the vertex and edge variables.

description: A singleton variable has the same name as a group variable.
cause: A singleton variable was specified with the same name as a group variable.
action: Use a different name for the singleton and group variables.

description: Group variables contained in different quantified path patterns have the same name.
cause: Two group variables contained in different quantified path patterns had the same name.
action: Use a different name for group variables in different quantified path patterns.

description: Using a question mark in path pattern is not supported.
cause: A question mark was specified in the path pattern expression in the MATCH clause of a GRAPH_TABLE operator.
action: Modify the path pattern specification and retry the operation.

description: Two consecutive vertex patterns are specified in the path pattern.
cause: Two consecutive vertex patterns were specified in the path pattern expression in the MATCH clause of a GRAPH_TABLE operator.
action: Modify the path pattern specification and retry the operation.

description: Group function is not allowed inside a quantified path pattern.
cause: One of the group functions, such as AVG, COUNT, MAX, MIN, or SUM, was used in an element patten WHERE clause or a parenthesized path pattern WHERE clause inside a quantified path pattern.
action: Specify the group function outside of the quantified path pattern.

description: A group function inside GRAPH_TABLE() must have a group reference.
cause: A group function inside GRAPH_TABLE() has no group reference.
action: Modify the group function specification and retry the operation.

description: A group function inside GRAPH_TABLE() must reference the same group variable.
cause: A group function inside GRAPH_TABLE() references multiple group variables.
action: Modify the group function specification and retry the operation.

description: Invalid property reference "%s" because the label expression for variable "%s" is not satisfied.
cause: A property of an element variable is being referenced while the label expression associated with the variable is not satisfied.
action: Modify the label expression so that it can be satisfied.
params: 1) property_name: The name of the referenced property. 2) variable_name: The name of the element variable of the property reference.

description: Empty COLUMNS clause because %s.* expands to zero properties
cause: variable.* does not have any properties and there is no other expressions in the columns clause.
action: Make sure that variable has at least one property.

description: invalid vertex reference in an IS [NOT] SOURCE OF or IS [NOT] DESTINATION OF predicate
cause: The first argument of a SOURCE or DESTINATION predicate is not a valid vertex.
action: Use a valid vertex as the first argument of a SOURCE or DESTINATION predicate.

description: invalid edge reference in an IS [NOT] SOURCE OF or IS [NOT] DESTINATION OF predicate
cause: The second argument of a SOURCE or DESTINATION predicate is not a valid edge.
action: Use a valid edge as the second argument of a SOURCE or DESTINATION predicate.

description: data mining function is not allowed inside GRAPH_TABLE()
cause: A data mining function is used inside the GRAPH_TABLE().
action: Do not use data mining function inside the GRAPH_TABLE().

description: Variable in ONE ROW PER %s not unique: %s
cause: The variable for ONE ROW PER VERTEX or STEP is already declared.
action: Use a new variable name for iterator variables.
params: 1) rows_per_option: The rows per option (VERTEX or STEP). 2) variable_name: The duplicate variable.

description: ONE ROW PER %s is only supported for variable length path patterns.
cause: ONE ROW PER VERTEX or STEP is being used without a variable length path pattern.
action: Do not use ONE ROW PER STEP or add variable length path pattern.
params: 1) rows_per_option: The rows per option (VERTEX or STEP).

description: Property "%s" in JSON dot-notation access does not have one of the expected data types JSON, VARCHAR2, CLOB, BLOB.
cause: Property has a data type that is not compatible with any of the expected input data types for JSON dot-notation access.
action: Modify the JSON dot-notation access.
params: 1) property_name: The name of the referenced property.

description: BINDING_COUNT() is not allowed outside of GRAPH_TABLE().
cause: A function allowed only within the GRAPH_TABLE() is used outside of the GRAPH_TABLE().
action: Rewrite the SQL statement.

description: Invalid argument specified in BINDING_COUNT operator
cause: An invalid argument is specified in a BINDING_COUNT operator.
action: Use the group variable name as an argument to the BINDING_COUNT operator.

description: Query containing %s but user is missing READ or SELECT privilege on the underlying database tables of the specified property graph.
cause: An attempt is being made to run a query containing VERTEX_ID or EDGE_ID operators but the user does not have READ or SELECT privilege on the underlying tables of the specified property graph.
action: Grant READ or SELECT on the underlying database tables of the property graph specified in GRAPH_TABLE.

description: Missing MATCH, VERTEX or STEP keyword
cause: ONE ROW PER is being used without MATCH, VERTEX or STEP.
action: Add MATCH, VERTEX or STEP.

description: Invalid reference of iterator variable %s in the WHERE clause of a GRAPH_TABLE operator
cause: An iterator variable is referenced in the WHERE clause inside GRAPH_TABLE.
action: Move the filter outside of GRAPH_TABLE or remove the reference to the iterator variable.
params: 1) iterator_variable: The name of the referenced iterator variable.

description: The PL/SQL variable %s is referenced inside a GRAPH_TABLE operator.
cause: The use of PL/SQL variables is not supported in a GRAPH_TABLE operator.
action: Remove the PL/SQL variable.
params: 1) plsql_variable: The name of the referenced PL/SQL variable.

description: Invalid vertex or edge reference in PROPERTY_EXISTS function.
cause: The first argument of a PROPERTY_EXISTS reference is not a valid vertex or edge.
action: Use a valid vertex or edge reference for the first argument of the PROPERTY_EXISTS reference.

description: ONE ROW PER %s without IN clause but with multiple path patterns requires all path patterns to be named.
cause: ONE ROW PER VERTEX or STEP without the IN clause is being used for a query with one or more unnamed path patterns.
action: Either remove ONE ROW PER VERTEX or STEP or add an IN clause or add a name to every path pattern.
params: 1) rows_per_option: The rows per option (VERTEX or STEP).

description: Invalid property reference in PROPERTY_EXISTS function.
cause: The second argument of a PROPERTY_EXISTS reference is not a valid property name.
action: Use a valid property reference for the second argument of the PROPERTY_EXISTS reference.

description: ELEMENT_NUMBER can only be used for iterator variables.
cause: ELEMENT_NUMBER is being used for a non-iterator variable.
action: Remove the ELEMENT_NUMBER call or change the parameter to be an iterator variable.

description: ELEMENT_NUMBER can only be used in combination with ONE ROW PER VERTEX or STEP.
cause: ELEMENT_NUMBER is being used in combination with ONE ROW PER MATCH.
action: Remove the ELEMENT_NUMBER call or use ONE ROW PER VERTEX or STEP.

description: MATCHNUM can only be used in the COLUMNS clause inside a GRAPH_TABLE.
cause: MATCHNUM is being used outside of the COLUMNS clause of a GRAPH_TABLE.
action: Remove the MATCHNUM reference.

description: Property graph %s has errors.
cause: The specified property graph has a reference to a non-existent vertex or edge table.
action: Check the property graph definition and create referenced objects as necessary.

description: %s is not allowed inside an aggregation.
cause: MATCHNUM or ELEMENT_NUMBER is being used inside an aggregation.
action: Remove the MATCHNUM or ELEMENT_NUMBER call from the aggregation.
params: 1) function_name: The name of the function (MATCHNUM or ELEMENT_NUMBER).

description: Invalid vertex or edge reference in IS [NOT] LABELED predicate.
cause: The first argument of a IS [NOT] LABELED predicate is not a valid vertex or edge.
action: Use a valid vertex or edge reference for the first argument of the IS [NOT] LABELED predicate.

description: Invalid label reference in IS [NOT] LABELED predicate.
cause: The second argument of a IS [NOT] LABELED predicate is not a valid label.
action: Use a label reference for the second argument of the IS [NOT] LABELED predicate.

description: Path variable not unique: %s
cause: The path variable is already declared.
action: Use a new variable name for path variable.

description: Path variable %s is never declared.
cause: The variable in the IN clause is either never declared or not a path variable.
action: Reference only path variables in the IN clause.
params: 1) variable_name: The variable name not referencing a path variable.

description: PATH_NAME can only be used in the COLUMNS clause inside a GRAPH_TABLE.
cause: PATH_NAME is being used outside of the COLUMNS clause of a GRAPH_TABLE.
action: Remove the PATH_NAME reference.

description: PATH_NAME can only be used in combination with ONE ROW PER VERTEX or STEP.
cause: PATH_NAME is being used without ONE ROW PER VERTEX or STEP.
action: Either add ONE ROW PER VERTEX or STEP or remove the PATH_NAME reference.

description: Label expression "%s" can never be satisfied for element variable "%s".
cause: The label exists in the property graph, but the specified variable can never match the specified label.
action: Change the label parameter or remove the IS LABELED predicate reference.
params: 1) label: The label that the variable parameter can satisfy. 2) variable: The vertex or edge.

description: Property "%s" is never defined when evaluating the label expression for element variable "%s".
cause: The property exists in the property graph, but the specified variable can never have the specified property.
action: Change the property parameter or remove the PROPERTY_EXISTS predicate reference.
params: 1) variable: The vertex or edge. 2) property: The property that the variable parameter can have.

description: The number of path patterns in the MATCH clause exceeds the maximum number of path patterns: %s.
cause: The MATCH clause contains too many path patterns.
action: Reduce the number of path patterns.
params: 1) max_number: The maximum number of path patterns

description: Invalid syntax for VECTOR type specification
cause: The VECTOR column type specification is incorrect.
action: Ensure that the correct syntax is used VECTOR(<vector_dimension_count>, <vector_dimension_format>). The vector dimension count can either be flexible (*) or an integer between 1 and 65535. The vector dimension format can either be flexible (*) or one of INT8, FLOAT32, or FLOAT64.

description: Invalid VECTOR type specification. Invalid dimension format (%s).

action: Ensure that the dimension format is either flexible (*) or one of INT8, FLOAT32, or FLOAT64.
params: 1) dimension_format: The dimension format parsed from the user query.

description: Vector dimension count must match the dimension count specified in the column definition (expected %s dimensions, specified %s dimensions).
cause: The dimension count of the vector does not match the dimension count specified in the column definition.
action: Ensure that the vector has the same dimension count as specified in the column definition.
params: 1) dimension_count_1: The dimension count specified in the column definition. 2) dimension_count_2: The dimension count parsed from the user query.

description: Invalid syntax for VECTOR value. Must be a string of the form DENSE vector: '[<number> , <number> ..., <number>]' SPARSE vector: '[<total dimension count (optional)>, [<sparse index array>], [<sparse dimension value array>]]'.
cause: The text string for the vector does not match the required vector value syntax.
action: Ensure that the vector is in the correct string format. A valid vector in the string format must be enclosed in square brackets and the dimension values must be numerical and separated by commas. Spaces are optional.

description: Invalid syntax for VECTOR value. The specified dimension value at position %s could not be converted to a number.
cause: The vector has a dimension value that cannot be converted to a number.
action: Ensure that the dimension value is in a valid numerical format.
params: 1) error_position: The position of the error.

description: Vector dimension value at position %s is outside the range allowed by the dimension format %s.
cause: The vector has one or more dimension values outside the precision range allowed by the dimension format.
action: Ensure that all dimension values are within the allowed precision range.
params: 1) error_position: The position of the error. 2) dimension_format: The dimension format of the specified vector.

description: Vector Norm or Vector Distance value is outside the allowed precision range of DOUBLE data type.
cause: Vector Norm or Vector Distance output is outside the allowed precision range of DOUBLE data type.
action: Ensure that the Vector Norm or Vector Distance output falls within the allowed precision range of IEEE DOUBLE data type.

description: %s requires all vectors to have the same dimension count. Encountered %s.
cause: The specified operation does not allow vectors with different dimension counts.
action: Ensure that all the vectors in the operation have the same dimension counts.
params: 1) operation_name: The name of the operation that is encountering an error. 2) dimension_counts: Dimension count tuple that was encountered.

description: Invalid data type %s used for FROM_VECTOR() or VECTOR_SERIALIZE() function in RETURNING clause. Must be VARCHAR, VARCHAR2, or CLOB.
cause: The data type used for FROM_VECTOR() or VECTOR_SERIALIZE() function in the RETURNING clause is invalid.
action: Ensure that the correct data type is used in the RETURNING clause for FROM_VECTOR() or VECTOR_SERIALIZE() function. The correct syntax is FROM_VECTOR | VECTOR_SERIALIZE(<vector> RETURNING <VARCHAR | VARCHAR2 | CLOB>).
params: 1) data_type: The data type specified by the user.

description: Insufficient buffer size for VECTOR to CHAR or VARCHAR conversion.
cause: The VECTOR column cannot be converted to the specified CHAR or VARCHAR format due to insufficient buffer size.
action: Ensure that the specified CHAR or VARCHAR buffer size is sufficient for storing the converted VECTOR column value. Use LENGTH(FROM_VECTOR(<vector>)) to determine the appropriate buffer size.

description: Vector dimension count exceeds the maximum supported value of 65535.
cause: VECTOR columns do not support dimension counts greater than 65535.
action: Ensure that the dimension count is less than the maximum supported value of 65535.

description: The vector SQL function %s requires all input vectors to have the same dimension format : encountered dimension formats (%s, %s).
cause: The specified vector SQL function does not allow vector operands with different dimension formats.
action: Ensure that all the input vector operands for the specified vector SQL function have the same dimension formats.
params: 1) function: vector SQL function that was invoked 2) format1: dimension format of the first input vector operand 3) format2: dimension format of the second input vector operand

description: Vector of BINARY format should have a dimension count that is a multiple of 8.
cause: VECTOR columns of BINARY format should have dimension count that is a multiple of 8.
action: Ensure that the dimension count is a multiple of 8.

description: Vector of BINARY format cannot have any operation performed with vector of any other type.
cause: VECTOR columns of BINARY format cannot have operations performed with vector of any other type.
action: Ensure that the vector operations happen between vectors of BINARY format.

description: INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH HNSW vector index snapshot is too old.
cause: An attempt is being made to query on the old snapshot of an INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH Hierarchical Navigable Small World Graphs Index (HNSW) vector index while a new snapshot is just built and becomes available.
action: Retry operation.

description: Vector format %s is invalid and not supported. Valid formats are (%s - %s).
cause: The specified vector format is invalid.
action: Ensure that a valid vector format is used. Refer to oci.h for valid vector formats.
params: 1) vector_format: The format of the vector operand. 2) first_vector_format: The first supported format value of the vector operand. 3) last_vector_format: The last supported format value of the vector operand.

description: INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH HNSW vector index snapshot is not present.
cause: An attempt is being made to query on an INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH Hierarchical Navigable Small World Graphs Index (HNSW) vector index for which no snapshot is available.
action: Check if vector index is still available.

description: Vector rendering format %s is invalid. Valid formats are SPARSE or DENSE.
cause: The specified vector rendering format is invalid.
action: Ensure that a valid vector rendering format (SPARSE or DENSE) is used.

description: Sparse vector input is missing dimension count.
cause: The sparse vector input with flex dimension count is missing dimension count.
action: Ensure that the sparse vector input has the dimension count as the first element in the input array (ie) [<dimension count>, [pos array], [val array]].

description: Dimension count in vector input doesn't match with specified vector dimension count.
cause: The dimension count in vector input doesn't match with specified vector dimension count.
action: Ensure that the sparse vector input has the same dimension count as the specified vector dimension count.

description: Number of index array values in sparse vector doesn't match with number of data array values.
cause: The number of index array values doesn't match with number of data array values.
action: Ensure that the sparse vector input has the same dimension count in both index array and data array.

description: The index values in sparse vector are not in strictly ascending order.
cause: The index values in sparse vector are not in strictly ascending order.
action: Ensure that the index values in sparse vector are in strictly ascending order.

description: Sparse vectors are not supported for BINARY element format.
cause: Sparse vectors are not supported for BINARY element format.
action: Ensure that the sparse vectors are created with other element formats, or make use of BINARY element format with dense vectors.

description: The input text for sparse vector is invalid.
cause: The input text for sparse vector is not valid.
action: Ensure that the input text for sparse vector follows [<optional dimension count>, [<dimension index array>], [<dimension value array>]].

description: The index array in sparse vector input text is missing opening bracket.
cause: The index array in sparse vector input text is missing opening bracket.
action: Ensure that the input text for sparse vector follows [<optional dimension count>, [<dimension index array>], [<dimension value array>]].

description: The index array in sparse vector is missing value from dimension index %s.
cause: The index array in the sparse vector input is incomplete.
action: Ensure that the input text for sparse vector follows [<optional dimension count>, [<dimension index array>], [<dimension value array>]].

description: The sparse dimension index value at %s is not a number or infinity.
cause: The sparse dimension index value is not a number or infinity.
action: Ensure that the sparse dimension index value are valid numbers.

description: The sparse dimension index value at %s is outside the allowed precision.
cause: The sparse dimension index value is outside the allowed precision.
action: Ensure that the sparse dimension index value are within the allowed range.

description: The value array in sparse vector input text is missing opening bracket.
cause: The value array in sparse vector input text is missing opening bracket.
action: Ensure that the input text for sparse vector follows [<optional dimension count>, [<dimension index array>], [<dimension value array>]].

description: The value array in sparse vector is missing value from dimension index %s.
cause: The value array in the sparse vector input is incomplete.
action: Ensure that the input text for sparse vector follows [<optional dimension count>, [<dimension index array>], [<dimension value array>]].

description: The sparse dimension value at %s is not a number or infinity.
cause: The sparse dimension index value is not a number or infinity.
action: Ensure that the sparse dimension index value are valid numbers.

description: The sparse dimension value at %s is outside the allowed precision.
cause: The sparse dimension value is outside the allowed precision.
action: Ensure that the sparse dimension value are within the allowed range.

description: Textual input conversion between sparse and dense vector is not supported.
cause: Textual input conversion between sparse and dense vector is not supported.
action: Ensure that the text input matches with SPARSE or DENSE format.

description: Distance computation between sparse and dense vector is not supported.
cause: Distance computation between sparse and dense vector is not supported.
action: Ensure that both the vectors are either sparse or dense. Note that conversion between sparse and dense vector is supported.

description: Dimension count in vector input is invalid.
cause: The provided value for dimension count in vector input is invalid.
action: Ensure that the provided value for dimension count in vector input is valid.

description: The sparse dimension index value at %s is greater than total dimension count.
cause: The sparse dimension index value is greater than total dimension count.
action: Ensure that the sparse dimension index value is equal to or less than total dimension count.

description: VECTOR_DISTANCE() with Jaccard metric or JACCARD_DISTANCE() requires BINARY format input vectors: encountered dimension formats (%s, %s)
cause: Inputs with dimension formats other than BINARY are given in VECTOR_DISTANCE() with Jaccard metric or JACCARD_DISTANCE().
action: Ensure that all of the input vector operands for VECTOR_DISTANCE() with Jaccard metric or JACCARD_DISTANCE() are of BINARY formats.
params: 1) format1: dimension format of the first input vector operand 2) format2: dimension format of the second input vector operand

description: Input vectors with BINARY format are not allowed in vector arithmetic operations.
cause: Inputs with BINARY dimension format are given in vector arithmetic operation.
action: Ensure that all of the input vector operands for the vector arithmetic operation have a dimension format other than BINARY.

description: Vector index cannot be created on top of SPARSE vector columns.
cause: The vector index cannot be created on top of SPARSE vector columns.
action: Ensure that the vector index is created only on top of DENSE vector columns.

description: Jaccardian distance is not supported for sparse vectors.
cause: Jaccardian distance is computed for sparse vectors.
action: Ensure that all of the input vector operands for Jaccardian distance computation do not have sparse format.

description: The specified sparse vector is invalid.
cause: The specified sparse vector is not valid.
action: Ensure that the specified sparse vector follows [<optional dimension count>, [<dimension index array>], [<dimension value array>]].

description: An internal error occurred during rescoring for this query.
cause: The quantized HNSW index ran into an error while running rescoring for the results.
action: Retry the top-K search query.

description: Default value specification not supported for VECTOR column.
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: VECTOR columns not allowed in function-based index expression.
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: VECTOR columns not allowed in constraints.
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: A VECTOR column cannot serve as a partitioning column.
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: Temporary tables cannot contain VECTOR columns.
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: Index-organized tables cannot contain VECTOR columns.
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: Triggers cannot contain VECTOR columns.
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: Type VECTOR is not supported for this function or operator.
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: Unsupported VECTOR column modification.
cause: The VECTOR column is being modified to something other than VECTOR(*,*)
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: Unsupported VECTOR column addition.
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: JSON to VECTOR conversion failed. JSON must be an array of numerical values to be converted to VECTOR.
cause: JSON is not an array of numerical values to be converted to VECTOR.
action: Ensure that the input is a JSON array of numerical values.

description: VECTOR library processing error in '%s'
cause: This is an interal VECTOR library processing error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: invalid VECTOR descriptor detected
cause: An invalid VECTOR descriptor is detected.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: prefetch buffer or its length in VECTOR descriptor is null
cause: An invalid VECTOR descriptor is detected.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: invalid LOB locator encountered or VECTOR data is null
cause: OCIVectorToArray or OCIVectorToText returned this error as a result of invalid LOB locator or VECTOR data is NULL.
action: To resolve the issue, perform any one of the following: - Associate an indicator variable with all define variables to record the presence of the NULL value. This technique permits your program to take a specific action if a NULL value is returned. - Use the NVL function to convert the retrieved NULL to another value, such as zero or blank. This is the simplest solution. - Revise the query to eliminate inclusion of columns that / might contain a NULL value.

description: Lvector buffer too small. Use a buffer of at least %s bytes.
cause: Buffer is too small for the lvector data.
action: Increase the size of the buffer to the specified value.
params: 1) buffer_size: The minimum size of the buffer to be used.

description: Dimension count of the constructed vector(%s) does not match the dimension count argument (%s) of the constructor.
cause: The constructed vector has a dimension count that does not match the dimension count argument of the constructor.
action: Remove the dimension count argument of the constructor or ensure that the vector string generates a vector of the desired dimension count.

description: %s is not supported for vectors with different element formats (%s, %s).
cause: The specified VECTOR PL/SQL function does not allow vector operands with different element formats.
action: Ensure that the vector operands have the same element formats.

description: Vector datatype is not supported with %s
cause: This functionality is not yet supported for VECTOR type.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for additional details.

description: Vector of BINARY format cannot be used for index creation.
cause: Vector of BINARY format is not supported for index creation.
action: Ensure that you use vector of different format for index creation.

description: Analyze index is not supported for vector index.
cause: This functionality is not supported for vector index.
action: Use DBMS_STATS.GATHER_INDEX_STATS to gather stats for vector index.

description: Error converting BLOB to VECTOR
cause: BLOB bytes are invalid VECTOR bytes.
action: Ensure that the BLOB bytes are valid VECTOR bytes or contact Oracle Support.

description: %s is not supported for vectors with different storage formats (%s, %s).
cause: The specified VECTOR PL/SQL function does not allow vector operands with different storage formats.
action: Ensure that the vector operands have the same element formats.

description: ALTER VECTOR INDEX REBUILD ONLINE %s.%s failed as the column %s has 0 vectors.
cause: There are 0 non-null vectors in the table when rebuilding VECTOR INDEX.
action: Add rows with non-null vectors to table before executing ALTER INDEX REBUILD DDL.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) column_name: column name

description: XA or database link transaction on IVF vector index concurrently being rebuild is not currently allowed.
cause: XA or database link transaction on IVF index is not allowed while it is concurrently being rebuild.
action: Wait for IVF vector index rebuild to complete before performing XA or database link transaction.

description: DML on %s.%s with INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH local vector index %s.%s is not currently allowed.
cause: DML is not currently allowed on tables with INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH local vector index.
action: Drop the INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH local vector index before performing DML on the table.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the table. 2) table_name: The table name. 3) owner_name: The owner of the index. 4) index_name: The index name.

description: ALTER VECTOR INDEX %s.%s REBUILD is not supported or disabled for given vector index configuration and/or parameter combination.
cause: Alter index rebuild is not supported or disabled for given index and index parameter combination.
action: Drop the NEIGHBOR PARTITION index and create the vector index again with the desired configuration.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: ALTER VECTOR INDEX %s.%s REBUILD SUBPARTITION ONLINE is not allowed.
cause: Alter index rebuild subpartition is failing because it is not currently supported.
action: Drop the NEIGHBOR PARTITION index and create the vector index again.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: Operation on the partition object of the table %s.%s is not allowed as the table has one or more vector indexes.
cause: Operation on the partition object is failing as it has one or more vector indexes.
action: Drop the vector index and perform the operation on the partitioned object.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the table. 2) table_name: The table name.

description: ALTER VECTOR INDEX %s.%s REBUILD failed for partition %s.
cause: An attempt to rebuild a local NEIGHBOR PARTITION vector index is failing due to an underlying error.
action: Review other error messages and the attention log for further information.
params: 1) owner_name: index owner name 2) index_name: index name 3) partition_name: partition name of the index

description: Vector index maintenance failed because %s format is not supported with %s distance metric of the index.
cause: Insert or update into vector index is failing because the vector format is not supported for index's distance metric.
action: Insert or update vector with a different format supported for index's distance metric.
params: 1) vector_data_type: The vector's data format. 2) distance_metric: The index's distance metric.

description: Cannot create a vector index on non-vector columns
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index on an unsupported data type. Vector indexes can be created only on a vector data type column.
action: Do not create a vector index on an unsupported data type.

description: Cannot create a vector index on more than one column
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index on more than one column.
action: Create the vector index only on a single vector data type column.

description: Cannot create a vector index on a vector column with different dimensions
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index on a vector column whose dimension values are not all the same.
action: Create the vector index on a vector column having same dimension values.

description: Cannot drop auxiliary tables for vector indexes
cause: An attempt is being made to drop auxiliary tables for vector indexes.
action: Do not drop auxiliary tables for vector indexes.

description: Failed to drop auxiliary tables for the vector index
cause: Failed to drop an auxiliary table for the vector index.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Failed to truncate auxiliary tables for the vector index
cause: Failed to truncate an auxiliary table for the vector index.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Failed to create auxiliary tables for the vector index
cause: Failed to create an auxiliary table for the vector index.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Clustering failed for the neighbor partitions vector index.
