cause: Building or removing a clustering model during the neighbor partitions vector index creation is failing.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Centroid assignment failed for the neighbor partitions vector index.
cause: Assigning a centroid ID to base table rows during the neighbor partitions vector index creation is failing.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Creating vector index %s.%s is failing because %s distance is attempted on %s format.
cause: Creating a vector index is failing since vector indexes that use HAMMING or JACCARD distance can only be created on vectors with INT8 or BINARY format.
action: Use a distance metric other than HAMMING or JACCARD distance, or ensure all vectors are of INT8 or BINARY format.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) col_type: The column type.

description: Creating vector index %s.%s is failing because %s distance is used with vectors that have BINARY format.
cause: Creating a vector index is failing since vector indexes that have BINARY format can only use HAMMING or JACCARD distance.
action: Use HAMMING or JACCARD distance as distance metric for BINARY format.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) col_type: The column type.

description: DBMS_VECTOR not supported for local HNSW checkpoints.
cause: Local HNSW index does not support DBMS_VECTOR for checkpoints related operations.
action: Call DBMS_VECTOR checkpoint related operations only on global HNSW index.

description: Syntax error in CREATE VECTOR INDEX. Specified quantization rescore factor without specifying the QUANTIZATION clause.
cause: The CREATE VECTOR INDEX statement specified quantization rescore factor in the PARAMETERS clause without specifying the QUANTIZATION clause.
action: Specify "QUANTIZATION [SCALAR] COMPRESSION [2/4/8]" to create a quantized index, or remove the quantization field from PARAMETERS.

description: Syntax error in CREATE VECTOR INDEX. Syntax for QUANTIZATION RESCORE FACTOR is missing or incorrect.
cause: The CREATE VECTOR INDEX statement for a quantized index should correctly specify quantization rescore factor in the PARAMETERS clause.
action: Specify QUANTIZATION RESCORE FACTOR in the PARAMETERS clause.

description: Missing ORGANIZATION clause when creating a vector index
cause: ORGANIZATION clause is missing for creating a vector index.
action: Add ORGANIZATION clause to the vector index creation syntax.

description: Invalid value specified for the vector index parameter %s
cause: An attempt is being made to specify an invalid value for one vector index parameter.
action: Use the valid value that is within the range as specified in the documentation.
params: 1) field_name: The name of the field specified in the vector index clause.

description: Parameter %s not supported for the given vector index type
cause: An invalid or unsupported parameter is used to create a specific type of vector indexes.
action: Use valid and supported parameters for each type of vector indexes.
params: 1) field_name: The name of the field specified in the vector index clause.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. Invalid value %s specified for the parameter "TYPE" for vector index with ORGANIZATION %s.
cause: The value specified for the parameter \"TYPE\" is not compatible with the specified vector index ORGANIZATION.
action: Refer to the documentation for CREATE VECTOR INDEX for the supported values of the PARAMETER \"TYPE\" for the specified vector index ORGANIZATION.
params: 1) index_name: The index name. 2) type_name: The index type name. 3) organization_name: The index organization name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. The parameter %s is specified more than once.
cause: The same parameter is specified more than once in the parameter list.
action: Ensure that each parameter is specified only once in the parameter list.
params: 1) index_name: The index name. 2) field_name: The name of the field specified in the VECTOR INDEX clause.

description: Vector indexes cannot be created on %s.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index on unsupported tables.
action: Do not create a vector index on unsupported tables.
params: 1) table_type: The type of the base table.

description: Cannot create a function-based vector index
cause: An attempt is being made to create a function-based vector index.
action: Do not create a function-based vector index.

description: Failed to create a INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH HNSW vector index
cause: An attempt is being made to create a INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH Hierarchical Navigable Small World Graphs Index (HNSW) vector index but failed with an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Failed to drop a INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH HNSW vector index
cause: An attempt is being made to drop a INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH Hierarchical Navigable Small World Graphs Index (HNSW) vector index but failed with an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Cannot create quantized vector index for vector column with format %s.
cause: Vector index creation is not supported for a vector column with data format other than FLOAT32 and FLOAT64.
action: Remove the QUANTIZATION keyword to create an unquantized vector index.

description: Generic vector index failure
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index but failed due to an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Too many rows in base table to create INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH HNSW index
cause: The base table is too large to create an INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH Hierarchical Navigable Small World Graphs Index (HNSW) vector index.
action: Use a table that has less than 4,294,967,296 rows.

description: Cannot alter an existing vector index
cause: This ALTER VECTOR INDEX operation is not allowed. The ALTER operations allowed today are to change the index to Unusable, Invisible, or Visible. ALTER VECTOR INDEX also allows REBUILD ONLINE for IVF INDEX with no covering columns.
action: Instead of trying to ALTER the vector index, DROP the index and CREATE it again with the desired index properties.

description: Invalid degree of parallelism for vector index creation
cause: The specified degree of parallelism for the DDL exceeds system limits.
action: Specify a lower degree of parallelism for the DDL.

description: Data Manipulation Language (DML) on tables with in-memory neighbor graph vector index is not supported.
cause: An attempt is being made to run Data Manipulation Language (DML) on tables that have Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds (HNSW) vector index.
action: Drop the Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds (HNSW) vector indexes before performing Data Manipulation Language (DML) operations on the table.

description: In-memory neighbor graph vector indexes are not supported in an Oracle RAC environment.
cause: An attempt is being made to create an unsupported vector index in an Oracle RAC environment.
action: Create the in-memory neighbor graph vector index in a non-RAC environment.

description: Syntax error in CREATE VECTOR INDEX. Missing SCALAR for quantized index.
cause: The CREATE VECTOR INDEX statement for a quantized index is missing the SCALAR keyword.
action: Specify the SCALAR keyword after QUANTIZATION.

description: Syntax error in CREATE VECTOR INDEX. Syntax for ALGORITHM is incorrect.
cause: The CREATE VECTOR INDEX statement for a quantized index should correctly specify quantization ALGORITHM in the PARAMETERS clause.
action: Specify correct ALGORITHM in the PARAMETERS clause.

description: Mismatched dimension count in the maintainence of a vector index (input %s, required %s)
cause: An attempt to insert or update a row with a vector value whose dimension count doesn't match the requirement of a vector index on this column.
action: Retry the Data Manipulation Language (DML) operation with a vector value of the required dimension count.
params: 1) input_dimension: The dimension value provided in the DML. 2) expected_dimension: The dimension value expected in the DML that matches with the vector index dimension value.

description: Local vector indexes are not supported for partitioned tables.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a local vector index on partitioned tables.
action: Create a global vector index instead.

description: Cannot create a vector index on a vector column with different storage types.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index on a vector column whose storage type values are not all the same.
action: Create the vector index on a vector column having same storage types.

description: Mismatched dimension storage type in the maintainence of a vector index (input %s, required %s).
cause: An attempt is being made to insert or update a vector index column with a value of a different storage type than the required one.
action: Change the storage type of new vector value used in the insert or update operations.

description: Cannot create quantized vector index for a vector column with format %s.
cause: Vector index creation is not supported for a vector column with data format other than FLOAT32 and FLOAT64.
action: Remove the QUANTIZATION keyword to create an unquantized vector index.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. Invalid value %s for PARAMETER %s.
cause: An attempt is being made to specify an invalid value for one vector index PARAMETER.
action: Use the valid value that is within the range as specified in the documentation.
params: 1) index_name: The index name. 2) given_val: The value specified in the VECTOR INDEX PARAMETERS clause. 3) field_name: The field name specified in the VECTOR INDEX PARAMETERS clause.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX failed. Invalid syntax in PARAMETERS.
cause: There is an extra comma found in vector index PARAMETERS list.
action: Remove the extra comma from the vector index PARAMETERS list.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s ONLINE is not supported for %s.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index online using an unsupported feature or option.
action: Remove the unsupported feature or option.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) feature_name: The name of the feature.

description: Element is not a number or is out of range for vector dimension.
cause: An array has an element that cannot be stored as a dimension of a vector.
action: Ensure that elements do not contain 'Nan', 'Inf', or '-Inf' values, and that all elements can be represented in the vector element type.

description: Error processing vector type for JSON
cause: This is an internal vector type error for JSON.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed. Local vector indexes on sparse vector columns are not currently allowed.
cause: Local vector indexes on sparse vector columns are not currently allowed
action: Ensure that the indexed vector column does not have sparse format.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: XA or database link transaction on INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index is not currently allowed.
cause: XA or database link transaction is not currently allowed on tables with INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index.
action: Drop the INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index before performing DML on the table.

description: Insert or Update into vector index %s.%s is failing because %s distance is used with vectors that have BINARY format.
cause: Insert or Update into vector index is failing since vector indexes that have BINARY format can only use HAMMING or JACCARD distance.
action: Use HAMMING or JACCARD distance as distance metric for BINARY format.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) col_type: The column type.

description: Scan of vector index %s.%s is failing due to an internal table failure.
cause: An internal maintenance is encountered while an attempt is being made to scan a Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) vector index internal table. This is a transient internal operation.
action: Retry the operation.

description: ALTER TABLE %s.%s MOVE is not allowed as the table has one or more vector indexes.
cause: Vector Index maps rowid of base table for fast lookup. If rows of the base table move, it causes incorrect results when the execution plan uses a vector index.
action: This is currently not supported.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the table. 2) table_name: The name of the table.

description: Scan of a vector index is failing due to the missing internal table %s.%s.
cause: An attempt is being made to scan a vector index whose internal auxiliary table is not found.
action: Check if the vector index is still available and retry the operation.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the missing internal auxiliary table. 2) table_name: The name of the missing internal auxiliary table.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s of ORGANIZATION INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH failed. Local HNSW indexes not currently allowed with Oracle RAC.
cause: Local HNSW vector indexes are not currently allowed with Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC).
action: Create a Local NEIGHBOR PARTITIONS vector index instead.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: The Oracle Database Vector Memory size cannot be increased.
cause: Oracle Database Vector Memory cannot be enabled because an invalid value is specified for the initial Database Vector Memory size.
action: Specify a non-zero Oracle Database Vector Memory size in the initialization VECTOR_MEMORY_SIZE initialization parameter.

description: The Oracle Database Vector Memory size must be increased by a minimum of %s MB.
cause: Oracle Database Vector Memory size does not increase by the minimum required value.
action: Specify an Oracle Database Vector Memory size that increases by the minimum required value.

description: A reduction in the Oracle Database Vector Memory size cannot be completed.
cause: The parameter is set to disable any reduction of the Oracle Database Vector Memory size.
action: Enable Oracle Database Vector Memory shrink.

description: The Oracle Database Vector Memory size must be at least the initial value %s MB.
cause: An attempt is made to reduce the Oracle Database Vector Memory size is less than the initialized size.
action: Specify the Oracle Database Vector Memory size to at least the initialized value.

description: The Oracle Database Vector Memory size must be less than %s MB.
cause: The Oracle Database Vector Memory size is larger than 70% of the system global area (SGA) target.
action: Specify an Oracle Database Vector Memory size of no more than 70% of the total capacity, or increase the SGA target.

description: The Oracle Database Vector Memory size cannot be increased more than %s MB for PDB ID %s.
cause: The The Oracle Database Vector Memory size for the pluggable database (PDB) exceeds the total Database Vector Memory size for the container.
action: Specify an Oracle Database Vector Memory size no larger than the container Database Vector Memory size.

description: The Oracle Database Vector Memory size cannot be increased more than %s MB for PDB ID %s.
cause: The Oracle Database Vector Memory size of the pluggable database (PDB) exceeds the PDB system global area (SGA) target size.
action: Specify an Oracle Database Vector Memory size no larger than the PDB SGA target, or increase the PDB SGA target size.

description: An Oracle Database Vector Memory resize is already in progress
cause: Changing the Oracle Database Vector Memory size cannot be performed until the current resize completes.
action: Recheck the Oracle Database Vector Memory size and retry, if required.

description: The Oracle Database Vector Memory resize cannot be completed.
cause: Changing the Oracle Database Vector Memory size cannot be performed due to insufficient space for the resize.
action: Recheck the Oracle Database Vector Memory size and retry if required.

description: The Oracle Database Vector Memory size cannot currently be shrunk below value %s MB.
cause: The attempt to reduce the Oracle Database Vector Memory size cannot be completed because the space to be freed is still in use.
action: Set the Oracle Database Vector Memory size to at least the specified value or try the shrink again later.

description: The Oracle Database Vector Memory resize operation is too large and the change in size must be less than %s MB.
cause: The attempt to reduce the Oracle Database Vector Memory size cannot be performed because it is too large for a single request.
action: Set the Oracle Database Vector Memory size to the desired value in smaller increments given by the maximum of the specified value.

description: The vector memory area is out of space.
cause: The vector memory area does not have any free space.
action: Add free space either by removing vector memory objects, or by increasing the size of the vector memory area.

description: The vector memory area is out of space for the current container.
cause: There is no free space in the vector memory area for the current container.
action: Remove vector memory objects in the current container to make space or increase the maximum size limit by changing the VECTOR_MEMORY_SIZE initialization parameter.

description: Vector index cannot be created in non-automatic segment space management tablespace (tablespace number = %s).
cause: The attempt to create a vector index cannot be performed because SecureFiles LOBs (Large Objects) cannot be used in non-automatic segment space management tablespace.
action: Change the tablespace and retry.

description: Invalid or unsupported metric specified for VECTOR_DISTANCE
cause: The provided metric is invalid or not supported for the VECTOR_DISTANCE operator.
action: Specify a valid metric for the VECTOR_DISTANCE operator. Valid metrics are COSINE, DOT, EUCLIDEAN, EUCLIDEAN_SQUARED, HAMMING, and MANHATTAN.

description: Cannot modify internal table %s.%s of a vector index.
cause: An attempt is being made to modify (for example, alter table, rename, create index on) an existing vector index auxiliary table.
action: Do not modify the existing vector index internal table directly. Drop the existing vector index and then create the index again.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) table_name: The table name.

description: TopK RowIDs HNSW memory allocation is failing.
cause: The specified K value is too high in the FETCH APPROX FIRST K ROWS ONLY clause of the vector search query resulting in a memory allocation issue.
action: Specify reasonable K values in the FETCH APPROX FIRST K ROWS ONLY clause of the vector search query.

description: The specified vector arithmetic function signature does not support parallel execution.
cause: The attempt to create a vector index with the specified vector arithmetic function failed because the function doesn't support parallel execution.
action: Ensure that either the degree of parallelism is set to 1, or that the vector arithmetic function is created using the PARALLEL_ENABLE clause.

description: Custom vector arithmetic functions are not supported for this vector index type.
cause: An attempt is being made to use a vector arithmetic function on an unsupported vector index type.
action: Use a built-in vector distance function, or switch to a HNSW vector index.

description: Custom vector arithmetic functions used in vector indexes can't be defined in packages.
cause: An attempt was made to use a vector arithmetic package function on an unsupported vector index type.
action: Define a standalone vector arithmetic function which isn't in a package.

description: Vector distance CUSTOM is undefined outside of vector indexes.
cause: Can only use vector distance CUSTOM for expressions which use a vector index with user-provided vector arithmetic function defined.
action: Define a vector index with a user-provided, custom vector arithmetic function.

description: Vector index %s.%s is disabled due to modification of the custom vector arithmetic function.
cause: The vector arithmetic function used to created this vector index has been changed.
action: Ensure that the vector arithmetic function is valid and rebuild the index.

description: Custom vector arithmetic functions used in vector indexes must use definer's rights.
cause: An attempt was made to use a invoker's rights vector arithmetic function.
action: Define a vector arithmetic function which uses AUTHID DEFINER.

description: The specified vector arithmetic function is invalid.
cause: The attempt to create a vector index with the specified vector arithmetic function failed because the function is invalid or doesn't exist in the current schema.
action: Verify that the vector arithmetic function exists and is executable in the current schema.

description: The specified vector arithmetic function signature is invalid.
cause: The attempt to create a vector index with the specified vector arithmetic function failed because the function signature is invalid.
action: Verify that a valid function signature is used. A valid function signature takes two vector arguments, returns BINARY_DOUBLE and is deterministic, therefore is created using the DETERMINISTIC clause.

description: RowIDs buffer memory allocation is failing during HNSW scan.
cause: RowIDs buffer allocation is failing during Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds (HNSW) index scan due to an internal memory issue.
action: Retry operation.

description: Maximum number of vector index covering columns is 31.
cause: While creating a vector index with covering column, more than 31 columns are being specified.
action: Remove some covering columns from the vector index definition. If all the covering columns indexed are required, split them into two indexes.

description: Creating a vector index with covering columns is supported only on IVF indexes.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with covering columns with an index type other than Inverted File Flat (IVF).
action: Create the vector index with covering columns on an IVF index.

description: Cannot create vector index with covering columns on type [%s]
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with covering column on a column whose underlying data type is not on the allowed list.
action: Create the vector index with covering columns, whose underlying data types are on the allowed list.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX failed. Covering columns are not allowed on expressions or functions.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with covering columns, which are based on an expression or a function.
action: Create the vector index with the covering columns on columns without expressions or functions.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX [%s].[%s] failed. Covering columns are not supported on virtual columns.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with covering columns on virtual columns.
action: Create the vector index with the covering columns on non-virtual columns.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX [%s].[%s] failed. Covering columns on a partitioned table are not currently allowed.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with covering columns on a partitioned table.
action: Create the vector index with the covering columns on an unpartitioned table.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: Cannot drop column [%s] on table [%s].[%s]. Dropping a column that is covered by a vector index is unsupported.
cause: An attempt is being made to drop a column that is covered by a vector index.
action: Drop the index and drop the column in the base table again.
params: 1) column_name: The column name. 2) owner_name: The owner of the index. 3) table_name: The index name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX [%s].[%s] failed. Covering columns cannot be named '[%s]'.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with covering columns on a column with reserved name.
action: Use a different name for the column to be covered.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) column_name: The column name.

description: Data Manipulation Languages (DMLs) on a table with an included column HNSW index is disallowed
cause: An attempt is being made to update a HNSW vector index with a included column.
action: Drop the index and create the index again.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX [%s].[%s] failed. Each included JSON column in HNSW index must be less than 1 MB
cause: An attempt is being made to create a HNSW vector index with a included column of JSON type larger than 1 MB.
action: Use a smaller JSON size for the column to be included.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX [%s].[%s] is failing. Cannot create vector indexes with covering columns on a column that has a Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with covering columns on a column that has a VPD policy.
action: Drop the VPD policy and try again.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: Cannot add a Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy to column [%s] on table [%s].[%s], since there exists a vector index with covering columns on it.
cause: An attempt is being made to add a VPD policy to a column that is covered by a vector index.
action: Drop the index and try again.
params: 1) column_name: The column name. 2) owner_name: The owner of the index. 3) table_name: The table name.

description: Cannot modify column [%s] on table [%s].[%s]. Modifying a column that is covered by a vector index is unsupported.
cause: An attempt is being made to modify a column that is covered by a vector index.
action: Drop the index and modify column in the base table again.
params: 1) column_name: The column name. 2) owner_name: The owner of the index. 3) table_name: The index name.

description: Cannot rename column [%s] on table [%s].[%s]. Renaming a column that is covered by a vector index is unsupported.
cause: An attempt is being made to rename a column that is covered by a vector index.
action: Drop the index and rename the column in the base table again.
params: 1) column_name: The column name. 2) owner_name: The owner of the index. 3) table_name: The index name.

description: Cannot add a Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy on table [%s].[%s], since there exists a vector index with covering columns on it.
cause: An attempt is being made to add a VPD policy to a table that has a covering column index.
action: Drop the index and try again.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) table_name: The table name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX [%s].[%s] failed. Cannot create covering column index without patch 37306139 during RAC Two-Stage Rolling Update.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with a covering column without patch 37306139 during RAC Two-Stage Rolling Update.
action: Install the patch on this node and create the index again.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: Cannot grow vector memory size. Vector memory autogrow disabled.
cause: An attempt is being made to grow vector memory size with vector memory autogrow disabled.
action: Enable vector memory autogrow.

description: Cannot autogrow vector memory size inside root container
cause: An attempt is being made to autogrow vector memory size inside a root container.
action: Switch to a pluggable database.

description: Cannot autogrow vector memory size to %s. Size exceeds %s% SGA target size.
cause: An attempt is being made to autogrow vector memory size to a size that exceeds the allowed percentage of system global area (SGA).
action: Increase the allowed SGA target percentage for vector memory.
params: 1) memory_size: The new vector memory size for the pluggable database. 2) target_percentage: The allowed percentage of SGA target.

description: Cannot autogrow vector memory size to %s. Total data memory size exceeds 70% SGA target size.
cause: An attempt is being made to autogrow vector memory size to a size that would cause the total data memory size to exceed 70% of system global area (SGA) target.
action: Increase the pluggable database SGA target.
params: 1) memory_size: The new vector memory size for the pluggable database.

description: Cannot autogrow vector memory size to %s. Vector memory resize already in progress.
cause: An attempt is being made to autogrow vector memory size while a vector memory resize operation is in progress.
action: Retry the operation
params: 1) memory_size: The new vector memory size for the pluggable database.

description: Cannot autogrow root container vector memory size to %s. Size exceeds 70% SGA target size.
cause: An attempt is being made to autogrow root container vector memory size to a size that exceeds 70% of system global area (SGA) target.
action: Increase the root container SGA target.
params: 1) memory_size: The new vector memory size for the root container.

description: Vector memory size cannot be changed when vector memory autogrow is enabled.
cause: An attempt is being made to change vector memory size while vector memory autogrow is enabled.
action: Disable vector memory autogrow.

description: PromQL syntax error: found "%s" at column "%s"
cause: The specified Prometheus Query Language (PromQL) query has invalid syntax.
action: Specify valid syntax for the PromQL query.

description: PromQL internal error. Error code ("%s").
cause: The tokenizer cannot parse the Prometheus Query Language (PromQL) correctly.
action: Contact Oracle Support with the error code.

description: PromQL error: %s
cause: The user has passed invalid input.
action: Specify valid input for the PromQL query to get the result JSON.

description: Error in executing PromQL Query. Error codes ("%s"-"%s").
cause: Execution of the Prometheus Query Language (PromQL) query is not successful.
action: Contact Oracle Support with the error code.

description: Cannot change container in a RESET_STATE %s session.
cause: An invalid attempt is being made to change the container or the service while RESET_STATE is enabled at LOGIN or higher.
action: To alter the container, connect to a service in which RESET_STATE is set to NONE or LEVEL1.

description: RESET_STATE capability event for forcing fake client capability to RESET_STATE LOGIN.
cause: This event is internal and for testing purposes only. It expects the version number to be used as follows: event 52101 no defined ==> Use current driver capability event="52101 trace name context forever, level 0" ==> current version event="52101 trace name context forever, level 2" ==> force driver capability as LOGIN
action: Internal use only.

description: RESET_STATE event for forcing fake conditions.
cause: This event is internal and for testing purposes only. It expects the version number to be used as follows: event 52102 no defined ==> No fake conditions to be used event="52102 trace name context forever, level N" ==> Where N is a Bit mask with the combination of fake conditions. Bit Mask Values: 0x01 - fake login template creation failure condition 0x02 - fake login template read failure condition 0x04 - fake clearing failure condition 0x08 - fake state context init failure condition 0x10 - fake getting the version state failure condition 0x20 - fake templates can be created failure condition 0x40 - fake reset level changed at failover failure condition 0x80 - fake invalid reset level sent by the client driver failure condition
action: Internal use only.

description: Cannot restore RESET_STATE = %s, RESET_STATE = %s was used during failover.
cause: At failover, the requested RESET_STATE level sent by the client driver is not supported by the client driver itself.
action: Resubmit the work needed. Consider deferring using a different value for the RESET_STATE service attribute.

description: Cannot restore RESET_STATE = NONE during failover.
cause: RESET_STATE level in failover differs from RESET_STATE = NONE which was used in the original session. The actions performed by reset state cannot be reverted.
action: Resubmit the work needed. Consider deferring using a different value for the RESET_STATE service attribute.

description: RESET_STATE options for ORDS
cause: This event is internal and expects the level to be used as follows: event 52105 no defined ==> Use current RESET_STATE value event="52105 trace name context forever, level 0" ==> No operation event="52105 trace name context forever, level 1" ==> Disable forcing the max reset state value when ORDS is detected.
action: Internal use only.

description: Invalid path expressions in multivalue index (MVI) creation
cause: Invalid path expressions are encountered in multivalue index (MVI) creation, such as non-wildcard array step and predicates.
action: Ensure that valid path expressions are specified.

description: Nested JSON array is encountered for path evaluation.
cause: Input JSON data has a nested JSON array.
action: Ensure that there is no nested JSON array input for the path evaluation.

description: Data type %s of input %s to multi-value index is incompatible with the expected data type JSON.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a multi-value index on an input that is not a JSON data type.
action: Ensure that the input document is of JSON data type.
params: 1) data_type: The data type of the input. 2) column_name: The column name of the input.

description: Duplicate path expressions in multi-value index creation
cause: Duplicate path expressions are encountered in a multi-value index creation.
action: Ensure that there is no duplicate path expression.

description: Multi-value index cannot have parallel arrays.
cause: Parallel arrays are encountered for a multi-value index.
action: Ensure that there is only one array for a multi-value index.

description: Syntax error in CREATE VECTOR INDEX. Syntax for QUANTIZATION RESCORE FACTOR is missing or incorrect.
cause: The CREATE VECTOR INDEX statement for a quantized index should correctly specify quantization rescore factor in the PARAMETERS clause.
action: Specify QUANTIZATION RESCORE FACTOR in the PARAMETERS clause.

description: Syntax error in CREATE VECTOR INDEX. Missing COMPRESSION RATIO clause for quantized index.
cause: The CREATE VECTOR INDEX statement for a quantized index is missing the COMPRESSION RATIO clause.
action: Specify COMPRESSION RATIO [2/4/8] as required.

description: Cannot create quantized vector index for vector column with format %s.
cause: Vector index creation is not supported for a vector column with data format other than FLOAT32 and FLOAT64.
action: Remove the QUANTIZATION keyword to create an unquantized vector index.

description: Syntax error in CREATE VECTOR INDEX. Syntax for ALGORITHM is incorrect.
cause: The CREATE VECTOR INDEX statement for a quantized index should correctly specify quantization ALGORITHM in the PARAMETERS clause.
action: Specify correct ALGORITHM in the PARAMETERS clause.

description: LOCAL is not supported for DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index %s.%s.
cause: Incompatible feature specified for DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index.
action: Remove the unsupported option and retry the operation.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. Cannot specify DISTRIBUTE and DUPLICATE clauses together.
cause: Both DISTRIBUTE and DUPLICATE clauses are being specified.
action: Use either the DISTRIBUTE clause or the DUPLICATE clause, but not both.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. DISTRIBUTE clause requires a RAC-enabled environment.
cause: A distributed index is being requested in a non-RAC environment.
action: Use a RAC-enabled environment to create a distributed vector index.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed on node %s due to insufficient Vector Pool memory.
cause: Not enough vector memory on one or more nodes to complete index creation.
action: Ensure sufficient memory is available on all participating nodes, or add more nodes.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed on node %s due to an internal error.
cause: Unspecified internal error.
action: Check traces on the node where the error occurred for further diagnostic information.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed. Node %s was restarted during index creation.
cause: A participating node restarted while the index is being being built.
action: Retry the operation after ensuring cluster stability.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX failed. The sum of lengths of all included columns in HNSW index must be less than 1 MB.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a HNSW vector index with a total included column footprint larger than 1 MB.
action: Use lesser number of included columns or smaller sized included columns.

description: Failed to perform memory allocation during hnsw_scan_perform_scan.
cause: Insufficient memory available in PGA for the requested operation.
action: Reduce the value of efsearch or adjust other parameters to lower memory requirements.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX [%s].[%s] failed. Cannot create covering column hnsw index without patch 37911705 & 38547870 during RAC Two-Stage Rolling Update.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with a covering column without patch 37911705 & 38547870 during RAC Two-Stage Rolling Update.
action: Install the patch on this node and create the index again.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed. No response received from node %s.
cause: Node did not respond, possibly due to instance failure or closed PDB.
action: Check node status and ensure all PDBs are open.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed. Operation timed out on node %s.
cause: Primary instance waited too long for a node to complete its portion of index creation.
action: Check node status and retry.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed. Unable to read table data on node %s.
cause: Table scan failed on the specified node.
action: Check table accessibility and node status.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed while checkpointing the graph on node %s.
cause: Error occurred while checkpointing the index on a node.
action: Check traces for failure details.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: DBMS CREATE CHECKPOINT ON VECTOR INDEX %s.%s of ORGANIZATION INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH DISTRIBUTE failed.
cause: At least one participating node failed to create a graph checkpoint.
action: Check traces for failure details.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: DBMS CREATE CHECKPOINT ON VECTOR INDEX %s.%s of ORGANIZATION INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH DISTRIBUTE was skipped: another session is already checkpointing.
cause: Another session is currently performing a checkpoint on the same index.
action: Wait for the ongoing operation to complete and retry.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index is not available on node %s.
cause: Vector index graph is missing from node memory.
action: Ensure the index is fully loaded and available across all participating nodes.
params: 1) inst_id: Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed on node %s. DISTRIBUTE BY PARTITION specified for a subpartitioned table.
cause: DISTRIBUTE BY PARTITION is being specified for a subpartitioned table.
action: Use DISTRIBUTE BY SUBPARTITION or AUTO instead.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: ONLINE is not supported for DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index %s.
cause: Incompatible ONLINE clause is being specified for DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index.
action: Remove the ONLINE clause and retry the operation.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed on node %s. DISTRIBUTE BY SUBPARTITION requires a subpartitioned table.
cause: Distribution by subpartition is being specified for a table that is not subpartitioned.
action: Use DISTRIBUTE BY PARTITION OR AUTO instead.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: Repopulation is not supported for DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index %s.%s.
cause: Distributed vector index repopulation triggered by the user.
action: Ensure that index repopulation is disabled for a DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: FOR SERVICE is not supported for INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index %s.
cause: Incompatible FOR SERVICE clause is being specified for INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index.
action: Remove the FOR SERVICE and retry the operation.

description: QUANTIZATION is not supported for DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index %s.%s.
cause: Incompatible QUANTIZATION clause is being specified for DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index.
action: Remove the QUANTIZATION clause and retry the operation..
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: INCLUDED COLUMNS is not supported for DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index %s.%s.
cause: Incompatible included columns clause is being specified for DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index.
action: Remove the included columns clause and retry the operation.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: DISTRIBUTE is not supported for IVF vector index.
cause: The DISTRIBUTE clause is being specified for an IVF vector index, but IVF indexes do not support distribution.
action: Remove the DISTRIBUTE clause or use a different index type that supports distribution, such as INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed. Could not enable index on node %s.
cause: Index creation succeeded but enabling the index failed on one or more nodes.
action: Check traces for further diagnostic information and retry the operation.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) inst_id : Instance ID on which the failure was observed.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. Cannot specify more than one DUPLICATE clause.
cause: More than one DUPLICATE clause is being specified in the create index DDL.
action: Specify only one DUPLICATE clause.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. All keyword missing while specifying DUPLICATE clause.
cause: All keyword missing while specifying DUPLICATE clause.
action: Add ALL to the DUPLICATE clause.

description: DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index cannot be used inside an open transaction.
cause: DISTRIBUTED INMEMORY NEIGHBOR GRAPH vector index is used inside an open transaction.
action: Commit or rollback the open transaction.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. Cannot specify more than one DISTRIBUTE clause.
cause: More than one DISTRIBUTE clause is being specified in the create index DDL.
action: Specify only one DISTRIBUTE clause.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. Missing or unsupported DISTRIBUTE option.
cause: The DISTRIBUTE clause is either missing or contains an unsupported value.
action: Use one of the supported options: BY ROWID RANGES, BY PARTITION, BY SUBPARTITION, or AUTO.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s.%s failed. DISTRIBUTION BY PARTITION requires a partitioned table.
cause: DISTRIBUTE BY PARTITION is being specified on an unpartitioned table.
action: Use a partitioned table or choose a different distribution option.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s with DISTRIBUTE or DUPLICATE ALL clause failed. Feature is not enabled.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with DISTRIBUTE or DUPLICATE ALL clause without enabling the feature.
action: Enable the feature and retry creating vector index.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX WITH INCLUDED COLUMNS failed. HNSW index with Included Columns does not support index creation on sparse vector column.
cause: An attempt to create an HNSW index with included columns is being made with sparse vector index column.
action: HNSW index with Included Columns is not supported on Sparse Vector Columns.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX [%s].[%s] ONLINE failed. Cannot create vector index in an online manner without enabling Two-Stage patch 37782449.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index in an online manner without enabling Two-Stage patch 37782449.
action: Install and enable the patch on this node and create the index again.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: ALTER INDEX [%s].[%s] REBUILD ONLINE failed. Cannot rebuild vector index in an online manner without enabling Two-Stage patch 37956740.
cause: An attempt is being made to rebuild a vector index in an online manner without enabling Two-Stage patch 37956740.
action: Install and enable the patch on this node and rebuild the index again.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX with HNSW SCALAR QUANTIZATION failed. Cannot create vector index without enabling the required Two-Stage patch.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index for HNSW SCALAR QUANTIZATION without enabling Two-Stage patch 37956731 and 38586272.
action: Install and enable the patch on this node and create the index again.

description: ALTER INDEX [%s].[%s] REBUILD ONLINE failed. Invalid value %s specified for the %s PARAMETER field. Valid values are between 1 and 10000000.
cause: The value specified for the PARAMETER field in the ALTER INDEX REBUILD ONLINE DDL is invalid.
action: Ensure that the value specified for the PARAMETER clause in the ALTER INDEX REBUILD ONLINE VECTOR INDEX DDL is between 1 and 10000000.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner name. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) given_value: The value of the field specified in the PARAMETER clause. 4) field_name: The name of the field specified in the PARAMETER clause.

description: ALTER INDEX [%s].[%s] REBUILD ONLINE failed. Invalid value %s specified for the %s PARAMETER field. Valid values are between 0 and 4294967295.
cause: The value specified for the PARAMETER field in the ALTER INDEX REBUILD ONLINE DDL is invalid.
action: Ensure that the value specified for the PARAMETER clause in the ALTER INDEX REBUILD ONLINE VECTOR INDEX DDL is between 0 and 4294967295.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner name. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) given_value: The value of the field specified in the PARAMETER clause. 4) field_name: The name of the field specified in the PARAMETER clause.

description: ALTER INDEX [%s].[%s] REBUILD ONLINE failed. Invalid value %s specified for the %s PARAMETER field. Valid values are between 1 and 4294967295.
cause: The value specified for the PARAMETER field in the ALTER INDEX REBUILD ONLINE DDL is invalid.
action: Ensure that the value specified for the PARAMETER clause in the ALTER INDEX REBUILD ONLINE VECTOR INDEX DDL is between 1 and 4294967295.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner name. 2) index_name: The index name. 3) given_value: The value of the field specified in the PARAMETER clause. 4) field_name: The name of the field specified in the PARAMETER clause.

description: ALTER INDEX [%s].[%s] REBUILD ONLINE failed. The parameter %s is specified more than once.
cause: The same parameter is specified more than once in the parameter list.
action: Ensure that each parameter is specified only once in the parameter list.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner name. 2) index_name: The index name. 2) field_name: The name of the field specified in the VECTOR INDEX clause.

description: ALTER INDEX [%s].[%s] REBUILD ONLINE failed. Invalid syntax in PARAMETERS.
cause: There is an extra comma found in vector index PARAMETERS list.
action: Remove the extra comma from the vector index PARAMETERS list.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner name. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: ALTER INDEX [%s].[%s] REBUILD [SUB]PARTITION ONLINE failed. WITH TARGET ACCURACY not supported.
cause: WITH TARGET ACCURACY not supported for partition index.
action: Remove the WITH TARGET ACCURACY clause when rebuilding [SUB]PARTITION
params: 1) owner_name: The owner name. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: ALTER INDEX [%s].[%s] REBUILD ONLINE failed. Invalid value %s for TARGET ACCURACY value. Valid values are between 1 and 100.
cause: An attempt is being made to specify an invalid value for the TARGET ACCURACY vector index parameter.
action: Use the valid value that is within the range as specified in the documentation.
params: 1) index_name: The index name. 2) given_val: The value specified for TARGET ACCURACY in the VECTOR INDEX clause.

description: ALTER INDEX [%s].[%s] REBUILD PARTITION ONLINE failed. Cannot rebuild partition local vector index in an online manner without enabling Two-Stage patch 37874653.
cause: An attempt is being made to rebuild a partition local vector index in an online manner without enabling Two-Stage patch 37874653.
action: Install and enable the patch on this node and rebuild the index again.
params: 1) owner_name: The owner of the index. 2) index_name: The index name.

description: CREATE VECTOR INDEX %s failed. Cannot create vector index with DISTRIBUTE or DUPLICATE ALL without enabling Two-Stage patches 38320710 and 38542926.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a vector index with DISTRIBUTE or DUPLICATE ALL clause without enabling Two-Stage patches 38320710 and 38542926.
action: Install and enable the patches on this node and create the index again.

description: One or more vector indexes exist that cannot be downgraded.
cause: The database contains vector indexes that are unsupported in Oracle releases or versions pre-23.10.
action: Drop the unsupported vector indexes before downgrading the database to the selected release.

description: Export terminated unsuccessfully
cause: Export encountered an Oracle error.
action: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual, and take appropriate action.

description: data field truncation - column length=%lu, buffer size=%lu actual size=%lu
cause: Export could not fit a column in the data buffer.
action: Record the given size parameters and the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support. (Part of the table has been exported. Export will continue with the next table.)

description: error in writing to export file
cause: Export could not write to the export file, probably because of a device error. This message is usually followed by a device message from the operating system.
action: Take appropriate action to restore the device.

description: no storage definition found for segment(%lu, %lu)
cause: Export could not find the storage definitions for a cluster, index, or table.
action: Record the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

description: invalid username or password
cause: An invalid username or password was specified.
action: Retry with a valid username and password.

description: all allowable logon attempts failed
cause: Attempts were repeatedly made to log on with an invalid username or password.
action: Shut down the utility, then restart and retry with a valid username and password.

description: internal inconsistency error
cause: Export's data structure was corrupted.
action: Record the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

description: dictionary shows no columns for %s.%s
cause: Export failed to gather column information from the data dictionary. The table may have been dropped.
action: Retry the export and, if this error recurs, report it as an Export internal error to customer support.

description: ORACLE error %lu encountered
cause: Export encountered the referenced Oracle error.
action: Look up the Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

description: no privilege to export %s's table %s
cause: An attempt was made to export another user's table. Only a database administrator can export another user's tables.
action: Ask your database administrator to do the export.

description: %s is not a valid username
cause: An invalid username was specified.
action: Shut down the utility, then restart and retry with a valid username.

description: %s.%s does not exist
cause: Export could not find the specified table.
action: Retry with the correct table name.

description: %s is not a valid export mode
cause: An invalid export mode was specified.
action: Retry with a valid export mode.

description: respond with either 'Y', 'N', RETURN or '.' to quit
cause: An invalid response was entered.
action: Enter any of the responses shown in the message.

description: error on row %lu of table %s
cause: Export encountered an Oracle error while fetching rows.
action: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

description: error on row %lu of table %s, column %s, datatype %lu
cause: Export encountered an error while fetching or writing the column. An accompanying message gives more information.
action: Correct the error and try again.

description: ORACLE error encountered while reading default auditing options
cause: Export encountered an Oracle error while reading the default auditing options (those for updates, deletes, and so on).
action: Look up the accompanying Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

description: feature "%s" is needed, but not present in database
cause: The command entered requires the specified feature. Either that feature is not installed, or the row describing the feature is missing from table V$OPTION
action: Reinstall Oracle with the feature specified in the message.

description: datatype (%lu) for column %s, table %s.%s is not supported
cause: Export does not support the referenced datatype.
action: Retry with an acceptable datatype (CHAR, NUMBER, DATE, LONG, or RAW).

description: failed to process parameters, type 'EXP HELP=Y' for help
cause: Invalid command-line parameters were specified.
action: Check the online help screen for the set of valid parameters, then retry.

description: failed to allocate memory of size %lu
cause: Export failed to allocate the necessary memory.
action: Decrease the export buffer size so that less memory is required, or increase the runtime memory size for Export.

description: can only perform incremental export in Full Database mode
cause: USER or TABLE mode was specified when doing an incremental export.
action: Specify FULL database mode (FULL=Y) and retry.

description: must be SYS or SYSTEM to do incremental export
cause: The privileges needed to do an incremental export do not exist. Only a data base administrator can do incremental exports.
action: Ask the database administrator to do the incremental export.

description: must be a DBA to do Full Database or Tablespace export
cause: The privileges needed to do a FULL database export do not exist. Only a database administrator can do a FULL database export.
action: Ask the database administrator to do the FULL database export.

description: Export views not installed, please notify your DBA
cause: The necessary Export views were not installed.
action: Ask the database administrator to install the required Export views.

description: dictionary shows no column for constraint %s.%lu
cause: Export failed to gather column information about the referenced constraint from the data dictionary. The constraint may have been altered.
action: Retry the export and, if this error recurs, report it as an Export internal error to customer support.

description: conflicting modes specified
cause: Conflicting export modes were specified.
action: Specify only one parameter and retry.

description: failed to calculate ORACLE block size
cause: Export failed to calculate the Oracle block size.
action: Report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

description: failed to open %s for write
cause: Export failed to open the export file for writing. This message is usually followed by device messages from the operating system.
action: Take appropriate action to restore the device.

description: Incremental export mode and consistent mode are not compatible
cause: Both consistent and incremental exports were specified.
action: None. Consistent mode is turned off.

description: Unexpected End-Of-File encountered while reading input
cause: Encountered an End-Of-File while reading the user input.
action: If input to export is being redirected, check the file for errors.

description: Arraysize not in valid range. Using arraysize=%u
cause: The arraysize value specified is not in the valid range.
action: None

description: Non-DBAs may not export other users
cause: Only database administrators can export to other users. A non- database administrator attempted to specify owner=user where exporter is not the user.
action: Request that this operation be performed by the database administrator.

description: Could not find environment character set
cause: The environment character set is missing or incorrectly specified.
action: Ensure that the environment character set is correctly specified and is present.

description: error on rowid: file# %lu block# %lu slot# %lu
cause: Identifies the rowid on which an error occurred.
action: This is an information message. No action is required.

description: QUERY parameter valid only for table mode exports
cause: You specified the QUERY parameter in an export command, but you are not performing a table mode export. The QUERY parameter cannot be used for a user mode export, a full export, nor a point in time recovery export.
action: If you want to select a subset of rows for a table, you must export the table independently with a table mode export. Issue a table mode export command that specifies the table name and the query you want to execute during export.

description: Object %lu non-existent in dictionary
cause: The specified object could not be found in the dictionary. The object might have been dropped during the export
action: The object no longer exists; no action is needed.

description: Export views not compatible with database version
cause: The Export utility is at a higher version than the database version and is thereby incompatible.
action: Use the same version of Export utility as the database.

description: Bad Hash cluster id in clu$
cause: The function id in clu$ is not a legal number. Clu$ has become corrupted.
action: Contact Worldwide Support

description: export file %s must be on a disk
cause: On some platforms, export can read files from tape. This message is displayed if the first file in an export file set was on disk and you specified a tape device for a second or subsequent file.
action: Verify that you have specified the correct file name for the export file. Remember that all export files can be either on disk or all files can be on tape, but not mixed both tape and disk.

description: Dump file and log file must be different
cause: The dump file and log file cannot be the same file.
action: Specify different file names for the dump file and the log file, then retry the operation.

description: INCTYPE parameter is obsolete
cause: Export encountered the INCTYPE parameter when parsing Export options. Incremental Exports are no longer supported.
action: Consult the Oracle Backup and Recovery guide. Export will attempt to continue.

description: Missing NLS_CHARACTERSET/NLS_NCHAR_CHARACTERSET in props$
cause: A value for NLS_CHARACTERSET/NLS_NCHAR_CHARACTERSET was not entered in the props$ table"
action: internal error.

description: Invalid data dictionary information in the row where column "%s" is "%s" in table %s
cause: The export utility retrieved invalid data from the data dictionary.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Suport.

description: must be connected 'AS SYSDBA' to do Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace import
cause: The user must log in 'as SYSDBA' to perform transportable tablespace imports or Point-In-Time Recovery imports.
action: Ask your database adminstrator to perform the Transportable Tablespace import or the Tablespace Point-in-time Recovery import.

description: Cannot export SYSTEM Tablespace for Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace
cause: SYSTEM tablespace cannot be part of recovery set or transportable tablespace set.
action: Contact Oracle Wordwide Support.

description: Tablespace named %s does not exist
cause: The specified tablespace does not exist in dictionary.
action: Contact Oracle Wordwide Support.

description: Missing tablespace name(s)
cause: Tablespace name(s) were not supplied
action: Provide tablespace name(s)

description: Cannot export SYSAUX Tablespace for Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace
cause: SYSAUX tablespace cannot be part of recovery set or transportable tablespace set.
action: Contact Oracle Wordwide Support.

description: %s option is not compatible with Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace Export
cause: An option was specified incompatible with Point-in-time Recovery or Transportable Tablespace Export.
action: Retry the Export without the displayed option.

description: Cannot perform Partition Export "%s" on non-partitioned table "%s"
cause: The table specified in this Partition Export is not a partitioned table.
action: Use Table mode, or specify a non-partitioned table.

description: "%s" - given partition or subpartition name is not part of "%s" table
cause: The specified partition or subpartition name is not in the specified table.
action: Check if the correct table, partition or subpartition name was specified.

description: error on row %lu of partition %s
cause: Export encountered the referenced Oracle error while fetching rows.
action: Look up the Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

description: unable to execute QUERY on table %s because the table has inner nested tables
cause: You specified the QUERY parameter on a table that has one or more inner nested tables. The QUERY parameter cannot be specified on tables that have inner nested tables.
action: Export the entire table by omitting the QUERY parameter.

description: error on row %lu of subpartition %s
cause: Export encountered the referenced Oracle error while fetching rows.
action: Look up the Oracle message in the ORA message chapters of this manual and take appropriate action.

description: %s.%s is marked not exportable
cause: An object was marked as non-exportable in the NOEXP$ table.
action: Consult your database administrator.

description: placeholder for OCI error
cause: filler
action: filler

description: Failure to initialize parameter manager
cause: The parameter manager failed in intialization.
action: Record the messages that follow and report this to Oracle Wordwide Support as an Export internal bug.

description: Password Verify Function for %s profile does not exist
cause: Cannot find the function for the profile.
action: Check if the profile was created properly.

description: error converting an object type's identifier to characters
cause: An invalid length of an object type identifier prevented its conversion.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support

description: an object type had multiple TYPE BODYs
cause: More than one TYPE BODY was found for an object type.
action: Try dropping the TYPE BODY, if that is not successful, contact Oracle Worldwide Support

description: unable to find the outer table name of a nested table
cause: While exporting a bitmap index or posttable action on an inner nested table, the name of the outer table could not be located, using the NTAB$ table.
action: Verify the table is properly defined.

description: invalid source statements for an object type
cause: TYPE was not found in the statements in SOURCE$ for an Object Type
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

description: error in changing language handle
cause: Unable to change language handle.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

description: %s is an inner nested table and cannot be exported.
cause: An attempt was made to export an inner nested table without its parent table.
action: Export the parent of the inner nested table.

description: Error writing lob to the dump file.
cause: The current LOB could not be written to the dump file.
action: Identify the cause of the write failure and fix it.

description: Object table %s is missing its object identifier index
cause: All object tables must have an object identifier index, but the specified table was missing an index on its object identifier column.
action: Recreate the type table and retry the operation.

description: tablespace %s is offline
cause: Export failed to export tablespace (tablespace being offline).
action: Make tablespace online and re export.

description: placeholder for column level ORA error
cause: filler
action: filler

description: attempt to free unallocated memory
cause: An attempt was made to free memory that was not allocated.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support

description: QUERY parameter not compatible with Direct Path export
cause: You specified a value for the QUERY parameter for a direct path export. The QUERY parameter cannot be used with a direct path export.
action: Re-issue the export command with DIRECT=N or omit the DIRECT parameter from the command line.

description: error closing export file %s
cause: An error occurred while trying to close the export file.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

description: dump file size too small
cause: You specified either the FILESIZE parameter or the VOLSIZE parameter (if your platform supports it), and the value of the parameter is too small to hold the header information for the export file, plus any data.
action: Increase the value of the FILESIZE or VOLSIZE parameter.

description: rounding VOLSIZE down, new value is %s
cause: The VOLSIZE parameter must be a multiple of the RECORDLENGTH, but the value you specified for VOLSIZE does not meet this requirement. The value of VOLSIZE has been rounded down to be a multiple of the RECORDLENGTH used for the dump file.
action: No action is required. You can adjust the VOLSIZE or RECORDLENGTH parameter to avoid this message. When importing this file, you must specify the VOLSIZE value reported by this message.

description: rounding FILESIZE down, new value is %s
cause: The FILESIZE parameter must be a multiple of the RECORDLENGTH, but the value you specified for FILESIZE does not meet this requirement. The value of FILESIZE has been rounded down to be a multiple of the RECORDLENGTH used for the dump file.
action: No action is required. You can adjust the FILESIZE or RECORDLENGTH parameter to avoid this message. When importing this file, you must specify the FILESIZE value reported by this message.

description: multiple devices specified for tape output
cause: You specified multiple file names when doing an export to a tape device. EXPORT uses the same device for writing all files, of the number of tape volumes required. For this reason, export will accept only one value for the FILE parameter when writing to tape.
action: Reenter the EXPORT command, but specify only one tape device in the FILE parameter.

description: multiple output files specified for unbounded export file
cause: You specified multiple file names when doing an export and you also specified a value of 0 for the FILESIZE parameter. Note that 0 is the value used if FILESIZE is not specified on the command line. Since a value of 0 for FILESIZE means that only one file will be written and there is no size limit for that file, the other files you specified in the FILE parameter can never be used.
action: If you intended to write multiple files, respecify the command but use the FILESIZE to specify the maximum number of bytes that EXPORT should write to each file. If you intended to write only one file with no limits on it's size, reissue the EXPORT command but specify only one file name for the FILE parameter.

description: Error exporting metadata for index %s. Index creation will be skipped
cause: Domain indexes export private metadata via anonymous PL/SQL blocks prior to the CREATE INDEX statement. Export does this by calling the ODCIIndexGetMetadata method on the implementation type associated with the index. A problem occurred inside this routine. Because the metadata is considered an integral part of the index, the CREATE INDEX statement was not written to the dump file.
action: Contact the developer of the index's implementation type. If this is an Oracle-supplied index (perhaps via a data cartridge), contact Oracle Worldwide Support.

description: Data in table "%s" is protected. Conventional path may only be exporting partial table.
cause: User without the execute privilege on DBMS_RLS, the access control package, tries to export a table that has access control. Since table owner is also subjected to access control, the owner may not be able to export all rows in the table, but only the ones he can see. Also, to preserve integrity of the table, user exporting the table should have enough privilege to recreate the table with the security policies at import time. Therefore, it is strongly recommended the database administrator should be handling exporting of this table. Granting the table owner execute privilege would also satisfy this security check, though it might have other security implications. If the table does not have objects, can use direct mode.
action: Ask the database administrator to export/import this table/view.

description: Data in table "%s" is protected. Using conventional mode.
cause: User without the execute privilege on DBMS_RLS, the access control package, tries to direct export a table that has access control enabled. Using conventional export mode instead. Note that because of access control, only a partial table may be exported.
action: Ask the database administrator to export/import this table/view.

description: Exporting access control for table/view "%s" as non-DBA.
cause: A non-DBA user tries to export table/view and the associated fine grain access control policies. The user may not have enough privilege to recreate the access control policies when importing the table/view. And such an event may cause inconsistency in the security model of the table/view.
action: Ask the database administrator to export/import this table/view.

description: Invalid function name passed to procedural object support: %s
cause: Internal inconsistency error: The listed function is not a method on export's procedural object interface specification.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support

description: The previous problem occurred when calling %s.%s.%s
cause: The listed package provides export/import support for procedural actions. The previously listed error occurred while calling the specified function.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support. Most packages are supplied by Oracle internal cartridge or server development groups. The package name will help Support determine the correct owner of the problem.

description: Unexpected DbmsJava error %d at step %u
cause: The error was returned from a call to a DbmsJava procedure.
action: Record the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

description: The previous problem occurred when calling %s.%s.%s for object %lu
cause: The listed package provides export/import support for procedural objects, i.e, those whose DDL is supplied by stored procedures. The previously listed error occurred while calling the specified function.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support. Most packages are supplied by Oracle internal cartridge or server development groups. The package name will help Support determine the correct owner of the problem.

description: Primary key REFs in table "%s"may not be valid on import
cause: The specified table contains primary key REFs which may not be valid in the import database.
action: Do not use Export/Import to move Primary key REFs between databases having differing character sets.

description: Problem with internal hash table of schema/table names
cause: Most likely a problem with allocating memory for the hash table entries.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support NLS_DO_NOT_TRANSLATE [88,88]

description: null error message, just signal error
cause: filler
action: filler

description: invalid FILE_FORMAT specification
cause: The FILE_FORMAT specification did not contain an instance of "%s". This wildcard string must be present.
action: Correct the error and reenter the EXPORT command.

description: cannot pin type "%s"."%s"
cause: Export was unable to pin the specified type in the object cache. This is typically caused because a type could not be made valid (for example because of authorization violations in accessing subtypes).
action: Fix the problem with the offending type until the type can be successfully compiled.

description: Exporting questionable statistics.
cause: Export was able export statistics, but the statistics may not be usuable. The statistics are questionable because one or more of the following happened during export: a row error occurred, client character set or NCHARSET does not match with the server, a query clause was specified on export, only certain partitions or subpartitions were exported, or a fatal error occurred while processing a table.
action: To export non-questionable statistics, change the client character set or NCHARSET to match the server, export with no query clause, export complete tables. If desired, import parameters can be supplied so that only non-questionable statistics will be imported, and all questionable statistics will be recalculated.

description: Unable to set NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS to required defaults.
cause: Export was unable to set NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS to '.,'
action: Record the accompanying messages and report this as an Export internal error to customer support.

description: Could not convert to server character set's handle
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact Worldwide support.

description: Could not convert to server national character set's handle
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact Worldwide support.

description: Flashback_time and Flashback_scn are not compatible
cause: Both flashback_time and flashback_scn paramerers were specified.
action: Reissue command with only one flashback parameter.

description: The template name specified can not be found.
cause: NA
action: The template name specified does not exist. Verify template name by looking up view %_ias_template.

description: Object type "%s"."%s" is not in a valid state, type will not be exported
cause: The object type's status is invalid which may be caused by a dependant type's modification (or removal) without cascading the change.
action: The type must be recompiled using ALTER TYPE COMPILE.

description: Data in table has not been upgraded, table will not be exported
cause: Export is attempting to process a table containing references to a type which has evolved. In order for Export to process the table successfully, all data within each table must be upgraded to the latest revision of each referenced type.
action: The table must be updated using ALTER TABLE UPGRADE DATA.

description: Table "%s"."%s" is not in a valid state, table will not be exported
cause: A table or one of its dependant types has modified without cascading the change. This left the table in an INVALID state.
action: The table must be updated using ALTER TABLE UPDATE.

description: error converting an object type's hashcode to characters
cause: An invalid length of an object type identifier prevented its conversion.
action: Contact Oracle Worldwide Support

description: Version 1 extensible index "%s"."%s" can not be included in Transportable Tablespace Export
