cause: NA
action: NA

description: file truncated error
cause: A truncated file was used for the load operation.
action: Verify unload operation completed successfully.

description: files not from the same unload operation
cause: Files used for the load operation were not from the same unload operation.
action: Verify the files used are from the same unload operation.

description: unable to read data chunk %s
cause: A read or seek to this data chunk was not possible. This chunk may not have existed.
action: Verify the files used for the load operation are correct.

description: bad data encountered while reading from file %s
cause: There was a datatype conversion error while attempting to convert the data in the data file to match the datatype of a column in the external table. The message that follows this one displays the name of the column and the start of the data for the column that could not be converted. The row containing the bad data is rejected and not included as a row in the external table.
action: If the row containing the bad data should not be filtered out, then modify the definition of the external table so that the datatypes of the columns match the datatypes of the fields in the data file.

description: requested version %s not supported by ORACLE_DATAPUMP
cause: This database version (defaulted to COMPATIBLE if not user-specified) was not supported by ORACLE_DATAPUMP external table access driver. Note: Database versions before 9.2 were not supported.
action: Specify a supported version and rerun the operation.

description: error seeking in file: %s
cause: An attempt to seek to the specified position in file failed.
action: Review the error message. Resolve the problem and retry the the operation. Contact Oracle Support Services if the problem cannot be resolved.

description: file truncated error in %s
cause: A truncated or incomplete file was used for the load operation.
action: Verify unload operation completed successfully.

description: conversion error loading table %*.*s.%*.*s
cause: A row could not be loaded into the table because there was a conversion error for one or more columns in a row.
action: See the message that follows for more information about the row that could not be loaded. To avoid this error, make sure the definition of the table being loaded matches the definition of the table being unloaded.

description: conversion error loading table %*.*s.%*.*s partition %*.*s
cause: A row could not be loaded into the table because there was a conversion error for one or more columns in a row.
action: See the message that follows for more information about the row that could not be loaded. To avoid this error, make sure the definition of the table being loaded matches the definition of the table being unloaded.

description: data for row: %*.*s
cause: A conversion error occurred while loading data into a table. The message shows values for the field in the row that had the conversion error.
action: None. This is only an informational message.

description: unable to open at least one dump file for fetch
cause: None of the files in the LOCATION clause can be opened for a fetch on an external table.
action: A fetch operation on an external table in SQL mode requires that at least one file could be opened. Check that the directory object and file names to the dump files are correct.

description: the following file is not valid for this load operation
cause: This file could not be used for this load operation. See the following message for more information.
action: Verify all the files in the LOCATION clause are from the same unload operation and that the unload was successful.

description: file %s in %s already exists
cause: The specified file could not be used for this unload because that would mean overwriting an existing file.
action: Specify a file that does not currently exist.

description: internal number in header in file %s is not valid
cause: The specified file could not be used for this operation because the internal number in the header was not valid.
action: If the dump files were transferred over, verify the transfer operation was done correctly.

description: internal metadata in file %s is not valid
cause: The specified file could not be used for this operation because the internal metadata stored in this file does not match the metadata stored in the first file piece set.
action: Verify all the files in the LOCATION clause are the correct dump files to use.

description: error in unloading or loading data
cause: An error has occurred in a stream unload or load operation.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: database version in file %s is not valid
cause: The specified file could not be used for this fetch because its database version was not compatible with the database version in the other files in the LOCATION clause.
action: Verify all the files in the LOCATION clause were populated with compatible database versions.

description: file %s not found
cause: The file was not found.
action: Verify the correct file (path and file name) was specified.

description: file %s not a valid dump file
cause: This file did not have the correct file format. It could not be used for an external table fetch operation.
action: Verify this file is from a SQL mode external table populate operation and that the operation was successful.

description: the following file is not valid for this fetch operation
cause: A file could not be used for this fetch. See the following message for more information.
action: Verify all the files in the LOCATION clause are from successful populate operations. If the files were generated from various populate operations, then verify that those were done with common attributes such as with the same tables and compatible database versions.

description: header in file %s may not contain correct information
cause: The header for ORACLE_DATAPUMP file was invalid.
action: Ensure that you have specified the correct file.

description: header in file %s has an incompatible version number
cause: A dump file was specified for a load operation whose version number is incompatible with the dump file version currently produced by the Oracle server on the system. Usually this message indicates that the dump file was produced by a newer version of the Oracle server.
action: Load this dump file using the same version of the Oracle server that created the file.

description: specified path for directory object "%s" is invalid
cause: The default directory or a directory object specified for a dump or log file contained an invalid path name or was null.
action: Specify a valid path name for the directory object.

description: This external table can only be accessed from within a Data Pump job.
cause: An attempt was made to access a temporary external table that was created by Data Pump to be used internally during the execution of an export or import job.
action: None.

description: LOCATION clause is not allowed for ORACLE_HIVE external tables.
cause: The LOCATION clause was specified for an ORACLE_HIVE access driver. The ORACLE_HIVE access driver gets LOCATION information from the metadata in the Hive catalog.
action: Omit the LOCATION clause when creating an external table using the ORACLE_HIVE access driver.

description: bad header format at start of granule [%d] detected
cause: The granule header was read but did not appear to be formatted correctly. The incorrect format could be due to a dump file corruption.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: A stream format internal error was detected unloading data "%s".
cause: An error occurred in a stream unload operation.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Data load operation detected data stream format error %(1)d for granule %(2)d.
cause: The format of the dump file data stream was not correct.
action: The stream format error may have been caused by a corrupted dump file. If possible, re-create the dump file and try again. If the problem persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Data load operation detected data stream format error for granule %d, attempting to continue.
cause: The format of the dump file data stream was not correct.
action: The stream format error may have been caused by a corrupted dump file. If possible, re-create the dump file and try again. If the problem persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: ambiguous filename column "%.*s" found in %s
cause: A filename column was ambiguous when a comparison found multiple matches with column names in the table or location clause.
action: Change the case of the filename column to match the case of its associated table or location column name.

description: duplicate file name column "%.*s" found
cause: A duplicate filename column was found in the filename columns access parameter.
action: Remove the duplicate filename column from the filename columns access parameter.

description: invalid file name columns, %s
cause: The path in the location clause either contained mixed file name column formats ("/key=value/" and "/value/") or there were not enough elements in the path to support the file name columns specified.
action: Use only a single type of file name column format or correct the element mismatch between the file name column definition and the location path name.

description: ORACLE_BIGDATA access driver does not support modifying access parameters
cause: A select of an ORACLE_BIGDATA external table used the EXTERNAL MODIFY clause to specify additional access parameters. An ORACLE_BIGDATA external table does not support modification of access parameters.
action: Remove the EXTERNAL MODIFY clause from the SELECT statement.

description: unexpected error loading Java Virtual Machine
cause: The external procedure agent for the external table access driver was unable to load the Java Virtual Machine.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: cannot access cluster
cause: An attempt was made to access table data in an ORACLE_HIVE or an ORACLE_HDFS external data source.
action: Contact the database administrator about gaining access to ORACLE_HIVE and ORACLE_HDFS external data sources.

description: error from external driver: %s
cause: An error occurred while attempting to access data in an ORACLE_HIVE or an ORACLE_HDFS external data source.
action: Correct the problem as suggested by the error message and retry the operation.

description: invalid value "%(1)s" specified for access parameter "%(2)s"
cause: A NULL or invalid value was supplied for the access parameter.
action: Correct the invalid value and retry the operation.

description: cannot change cluster in the same session
cause: An attempt was made to change the cluster in the same session. The first access to an Oracle BigData external table within a database session establishes the cluster for that session. This is determined by the cluster specified in the table's access parameters or, if no cluster was specified in the table's access parameters, by the default cluster set in the Oracle Big Data configuration file. Accessing an Oracle BigData external table in a different cluster within the same database session is not allowed.
action: Establish a new database session and retry the operation.

description: missing separator at offset %(1)d in line "%(2)s"
cause: Access parameters in an Oracle Big Data external table as well as entries in the Oracle Big Data configuration file were lists of one or more property name or value pairs. In some cases, the property name does not require a value. In other cases where a value must be supplied with the property name, the two must be separated by an equal sign ('=') or a colon (':').
action: Correct the problem as suggested by the error message and retry the operation.

description: invalid character at offset %(1)d in line "%(2)s"
cause: An invalid multibyte UTF character was encountered in the access parameters of an Oracle Big Data external table.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: invalid escape sequence at offset %(1)d in line "%(2)s"
cause: An invalid escape sequence was encountered in the access parameters of an Oracle Big Data external table. This may be caused by \unnnn Unicode code point that does not generate a valid Unicode character.
action: Correct the problem as suggested by the error message and retry the operation.

description: missing value at offset %(1)d in line "%(2)s"
cause: Access parameters in an Oracle Big Data external table as well as entries in the Oracle Big Data configuration file were lists of one or more property name or value pairs. In some cases, the property name does not require a value. In other cases, where a value must be supplied with the property name, the two must be separated by an equal sign ('=') or a colon (':'). In this instance, a property name and a separator were found without a corresponding value.
action: Correct the problem as suggested by the error message and retry the operation. Supply a value if the property name requires one. Otherwise, remove the separator and supply only the property name.

description: failed to initialize logging in external driver
cause: The external driver code could not initialize a context for logging messages. This usually indicates a problem with the value of the Java classpath used by the external driver.
action: Contact your system administrator to examine the contents of both the Oracle Big Data configuration file and the Oracle Big Data log4j configuration file to ensure that the entries in these files contain correct information.

description: memory allocation error while initializing the Java Virtual Machine
cause: An error occurred while trying to allocate memory in order to initialize the Java Virtual Machine in the external driver.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: invalid value when attempting to modify access parameter "%s"
cause: An attempt was made to modify an invalid access parameter.
action: The only valid access parameters which can be modified are: "com.oracle.bigdata.log.qc" "com.oracle.bigdata.log.exec" "com.oracle.bigdata.log.opt" "com.oracle.bigdata.debug" "com.oracle.bigdata.datamode" Correct the invalid access parameter and retry the operation.

description: external driver failed with unexpected error: %s
cause: The ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS external driver encountered an unexpected error condition.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: initialization failure for Java Native Interface (JNI) call
cause: The external driver encountered an unexpected error while trying to initialize its internal context for calling the Java Native Interface (JNI). This may indicate a classpath problem in the Oracle Big Data configuration file or a problem in the Oracle Big Data log4j configuration file.
action: Contact your system administrator to examine the contents of both the Oracle Big Data configuration file and the Oracle Big Data log4j configuration file to ensure that the entries in these files contain correct information.

description: The external driver was unable to attach to the Java Virtual Machine.
cause: The external driver encountered an unexpected error while trying to attach a thread to the Java Virtual Machine.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: memory allocation failure for Java Native Interface (JNI) call
cause: An error occurred while trying to allocate memory in order to make a Java Native Interface (JNI) call in the external driver.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: The external driver was unable to attach to shared memory.
cause: The external driver encountered an unexpected error while trying to attach to a shared memory segment.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: access to cluster "%s" is not properly defined
cause: Access to an ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS external data source was not defined as documented.
action: Contact the database administrator.

description: class "%(1)s" is invalid for %(2)s external tables
cause: An invalid value was specified for the COM.ORACLE.BIGDATA.CLASS access parameter for an ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS external table access driver. The ORACLE_HIVE and ORACLE_HDFS access drivers use a built-in class in order to access their data source.
action: Omit the COM.ORACLE.BIGDATA.CLASS access parameter when creating an external table using the ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS access driver. Alternatively, the builtin class names, COM.ORACLE.BIGDATA.AD.HIVE and COM.ORACLE.BIGDATA.AD.HDFS, may be used when creating an external table using the ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS access driver.

description: value for com.oracle.bigdata.buffersize larger than maximum allowed value %d
cause: The com.oracle.bigdata.buffersize was specified for the external table and the value specified was larger than the maximum allowed value.
action: Change the value specified for com.oracle.bigdata.buffersize to be smaller than the maximum value reported in the message.

description: missing mandatory property "%s" in the Oracle Big Data configuration file
cause: A mandatory property was not found in the Oracle Big Data configuration file.
action: Contact your system administrator to modify the Oracle Big Data configuration file so that it contains all of the required information.

description: duplicate property "%s" in the Oracle Big Data configuration file
cause: A duplicate property was found in the Oracle Big Data configuration file.
action: Contact your system administrator to remove all duplicate properties from the Oracle Big Data configuration file.

description: error collecting JVM information: %s
cause: The ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS external driver encountered an unexpected error while trying to collect information such as memory usage from the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: external driver JNI initialization failure: %s
cause: The ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS external driver encountered an unexpected error while trying to initialize its internal context for calling the Java Native Interface (JNI). This may indicate a classpath problem in the Oracle Big Data configuration file or a problem in the Oracle Big Data log4j configuration file.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: XAD version "%s" incompatible with JXADProvider version "%s"
cause: A version mismatch between the ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS access driver and the external driver Java components has been detected.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: external driver MTA initialization failure: %s
cause: The ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS multithreaded external agent encountered an initialization failure that prevented it from starting.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: %s
cause: NA
action: NA

description: error initializing dynamic-link librarian: %s
cause: An error occurred while trying to initialize the dynamic-link librarian needed to access the Java Virtual Machine library.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: error accessing the Java Virtual Machine library: %s
cause: An error occurred while trying to open the Java Virtual Machine library in the external driver.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: error locating symbol address in the Java Virtual Machine library: %s
cause: An error occurred while trying to locate a symbol address in the Java Virtual Machine library.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: unable to set NLS %s to required value %s
cause: An error occurred while the ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS external agent was trying to set up its NLS environment.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: external driver unable to attach to shared memory: [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s][%s]
cause: The ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS external driver encountered an unexpected error while trying to attach to a shared memory segment.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: external driver unable to detach from shared memory: [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s][%s]
cause: The ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS external driver encountered an unexpected error while trying to detach from a shared memory segment.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: error encountered creating shared memory: [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s][%s]
cause: The ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS access driver encountered an unexpected error while trying to create a shared memory segment.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: error encountered destroying shared memory: [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s][%s]
cause: The ORACLE_HIVE or ORACLE_HDFS access driver encountered an unexpected error while trying to destroy a shared memory segment.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: invalid JNI version "%s" encountered while initializing the Java Virtual Machine
cause: A Java Native Interface (JNI) version error occurred while trying to create and initialize the Java Virtual Machine in the external agent.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: error generating file name for file "%(1)s" in directory "%(2)s": %(3)s
cause: An error occurred while trying to generate a full file name specification.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: error initializing the Java Virtual Machine: %s
cause: An error occurred while trying to create and initialize the Java Virtual Machine in the external agent.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: The Oracle Big Data configuration file "%s" is empty.
cause: There was no content in the Oracle Big Data configuration file.
action: Contact your system administrator to correct the configuration files for the Hadoop cluster.

description: error accessing the Oracle Big Data configuration file "%(1)s": %(2)s
cause: A file I/O error occurred while attempting to access the Oracle Big Data configuration file.
action: Contact your system administrator to correct the configuration files for the Hadoop cluster.

description: error opening the Oracle Big Data configuration file "%(1)s": %(2)s
cause: A file I/O error occurred while trying to open the Oracle Big Data configuration file.
action: Contact your system administrator to correct the configuration files for the Hadoop cluster.

description: error reading the Oracle Big Data configuration file "%(1)s": %(2)s
cause: A file I/O error occurred while trying to read from the Oracle Big Data configuration file.
action: Contact your system administrator to correct the configuration files for the Hadoop cluster.

description: error closing the Oracle Big Data configuration file "%(1)s": %(2)s
cause: A file I/O error occurred while trying to close the Oracle Big Data configuration file.
action: Contact your system administrator to correct the configuration files for the Hadoop cluster.

description: invalid cluster name "%s"
cause: An invalid cluster name was specified for the external table in the com.oracle.bigdata.cluster access parameter. The name must contain only alphanumeric characters or the underscore character. In Oracle Database 12c release 12.1.0.2, the cluster name is limite to 15 bytes. In Oracle Database 12c release 12.2 and higher, the cluster name is limited to 113 bytes.
action: Correct the cluster name for the external table and retry the operation.

description: invalid default cluster name "%s"
cause: An invalid cluster name was specified for the bigdata.cluster.default property in the Oracle Big Data configuration file. The name must contain only alphanumeric characters, the hyphen or underscore character. In Oracle Database 12c release 12.1.0.2, the cluster name is limited to 15 bytes. In Oracle Database 12c release 12.2 and higher, the cluster name is limited to 113 bytes.
action: Contact your system administrator to correct the value of the bigdata.cluster.default property in the Oracle Big Data configuration file and retry the operation.

description: error accessing the Oracle Big Data cluster directory "%(1)s": %(2)s
cause: A file I/O error occurred while attempting to access the Oracle Big Data cluster directory file.
action: Contact your system administrator to correct the configuration files for the Hadoop cluster.

description: error while attempting to allocate Java memory: %s
cause: An error occurred while trying to allocate Java memory to the external driver.
action: Examine the accompanying text in the error message and contact your system administrator.

description: error while attempting to allocate %s bytes of native memory
cause: An error occurred while trying to allocate native memory to the external driver.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: unable to find first record in a split with I/O buffer size of %d kilobytes
cause: The access driver was unable to find the first record in the split for a Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) file.
action: The access driver requires that the size of records in the file are not larger than the size of the I/O buffers. Try increasing the size of the I/O buffers with the access parameter com.oracle.bigdata.fieldmode.buffersize.

description: record exceeded the maximum record size of %d kilobytes
cause: The access driver found a record in a Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) file that is longer than the largest size allowed for this table.
action: The access driver requires that the size of records in the file are not larger than the size of the I/O buffers. Try increasing the size of the I/O buffers with the access parameter com.oracle.bigdata.fieldmode.buffersize.

description: conversion error for column %(1)s in column array row %(2)d
cause: There was a data type conversion error while attempting to convert the data in the data file to match the data type of a column in the external table.
action: Make sure the data is correct. Also, verify that the data types specified for the fields are correct.

description: no directory object specified for bad file
cause: The file name in the BADFILE clause was specified without a directory object and the DEFAULT DIRECTORY clause was not specified for the external table.
action: Either specify a directory object as part of the BADFILE clause or specify the DEFAULT DIRECTORY clause.

description: no directory object specified for log file
cause: A log file for an external table did not have a directory object.
action: Either specify a directory object as part of the log file name in the ACCESS PARAMETERS or query, or specify the DEFAULT DIRECTORY clause in the ACCESS PARAMETERS or query. ORACLE_LOADER and ORACLE_DATAPUMP access drivers will create a log file by default. If you do not want a log file, then use the NOLOG clause in the access parameters.

description: no directory object specified for discard file
cause: The file name in the DISCARDFILE clause was specified without a directory object and the DEFAULT DIRECTORY clause was not specified for the external table.
action: Either specify a directory object as part of the DISCARDFILE clause or specify the DEFAULT DIRECTORY clause.

description: no directory object specified for PREPROCESSOR file
cause: The file name in the PREPROCESSOR clause was specified without a directory object and the DEFAULT DIRECTORY clause was not specified for the external table.
action: Either specify a directory object as part of the PREPROCESSOR clause or specify the DEFAULT DIRECTORY clause.

description: sequential data files were not supported by BIGDATA access driver, %s
cause: The file names in the message was a sequential file. The BIGDATA access driver does not support sequential files.
action: Modify the files listed in the LOCATION clause to omit the sequential file.

description: conversion error for column %s in file %s/%s row %d
cause: There was a data type conversion error while attempting to convert the data in the data file to match the data type of a column in the external table.
action: Ensure that the data is correct. Also, verify that the data types specified for the fields are correct.

description: conversion error for column %s in file %s/%s
cause: There was a data type conversion error while attempting to convert the data in the data file to match the data type of a column in the external table.
action: Ensure that the data is correct. Also, verify that the data types specified for the fields are correct.

description: field setting error for column %(1)s in file %(2)s/%(3)s row %(4)d
cause: There was a field setting error while attempting to parse the data in the data file.
action: Ensure that the data format for the field is correct.

description: field setting error for column %(1)s in file %(2)s/%(3)s
cause: There was a field setting error while attempting to parse the data in the data file.
action: Ensure that the data format for the field is correct.

description: quoting error
cause: The field was not properly quoted.
action: Ensure that the use of quotes for the field is correct.

description: character overflow error
cause: The character field size was exceeded.
action: Reduce the data size or increase the field size. NLS_DO_NOT_TRANSLATE [12000,12999]

description: compression type %s not supported
cause: File compression codec cannot be decompressed by Oracle.
action: Specify a supported compression codec.

description: unable to read %(1)s file %(2)s: %(3)s
cause: Trying to open the big data file failed. The file either was not a big data file or it was corrupted.
action: Ensure that the files named in the location clause are valid big data files.

description: invalid value %s for access parameter %s
cause: The value given to the access parameter was not valid.
action: Try another value.

description: cannot retrieve metadata for column %s
cause: This problem might be caused by corrupted column metadata.
action: None.

description: unsupported column type encountered for column %s
cause: The data type of the indicated column is currently not supported.
action: None.

description: cannot fetch access parameter %s
cause: An unknown error was encountered while trying to fetch the value of the specified parameter.
action: Check the access parameter syntax in the table definition.

description: encountered a file with unspecified URI
cause: A file was defined with an empty URI.
action: Check whether all files in the table definition have URIs.

description: cannot open file %s
cause: This problem might occur for several reasons.
action: Check whether the file exists and look for additional logs and tracing information.

description: cannot set iterator to vector in file %s
cause: This might be an indication of a corrupted big data file.
action: Look for additional logs and tracing information.

description: cannot initialize IO context
cause: This is an internal error. It might occur when there is limited available memory.
action: None.

description: cannot retrieve granule information
cause: This could happen due to an internal error.
action: Look for additional logs and tracing information.

description: encountered a vector in file %s with more than %li rows
cause: A vector exceeded the maximum supported number of rows.
action: Create file with smaller vectors.

description: cannot configure granules, no input files
cause: No bigdata files found.
action: Please verify files in the table definition.

description: %(1)s cannot be a negative value: %(2)d
cause: The simple granule block size and minimum size cannot be negative.
action: Ensure that the sgranblksize and sgranminfsize access parameters have non-negative values.

description: HTTP request for %(1)s failed: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: An HTTP request for a given URL failed.
action: Ensure the URL is correct, that the credential used is valid or required, that the proxy, if necessary, is correctly set, and that proper ACLs are in place to allow access.

description: failed to get an HTTP response for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: An HTTP response for a specified URL could not be retrieved. The server may have disconnected or sent some data that could not be understood.
action: Check the error reason which indicates the operation can be tried again later, or that a configuration issue is apparent. Use the reference code if set for any inquiries.

description: unexpected HTTP response status for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: The HTTP request returned an unexpected response.
action: Ensure that the URL is in compliance if the response status code is in the 300 range. If the response status code is in the 400 range, ensure that the correct credentials are applied and that the object is accessible on the remote server. If the response status code is in the 500 range, ensure that the remote service is available, that the proxy server is working correctly, and that the remote bandwidth quotas are sufficient. Use the reference code if set for any inquiries.

description: invalid URI for service %(1)s: %(2)s is required in %(3)s
cause: The specified universal resource identifier (URI) was incorrectly formulated for the targetted service.
action: Ensure that the URI is formulated correctly.

description: IO read failed for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: Read returned less bytes than expected.
action: Check the (remote) service is up and reachable, and that the requested resource is complete and undamaged.

description: IO read failed for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: An attempt was made to request more data than what was available.
action: Ensure that the object being read is not modified while reading.

description: IO read failed for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: Positioning the file stream to return a location failed.
action: Check the requested resource is complete and undamaged and that positionings are supported by the (remote) service.

description: IO read failed for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: The underlying read function returned an error.
action: Ensure that the network is working properly, and that the requested resource is available.

description: requested object %(1)s not found
cause: The LOCATION clause pointed to a remote object that did not exist.
action: Check whether the object exists in the remote storage or that its name is entered correctly.

description: nothing matched wildcard query %(1)s
cause: The LOCATION clause used a wildcard expression that failed to match any objects on the remote storage.
action: Check whether the expression is correct and that the objects exist on the remote storage.

description: incompatible URIs %(1)s and %(2)s found in LOCATION clause
cause: At least one of the specified universal resource identifiers (URI) was incorrectly formulated. All URIs in the location clause must be the same type.
action: Ensure that the URIs specified are all of the same type.

description: failed to begin HTTP request for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: A configuration problem prevented the request to be made.
action: The given ORA error code describes the problem encountered, refer to the error cause and action.

description: failed to establish connection for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: A configuration problem prevented the request to be made.
action: The given ORA error code describes the problem encountered, refer to the error cause and action.

description: unable to establish connection for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: A problem occurred while attempting to connect.
action: Ensure the URL is correct, that the proxy, if necessary, is correctly set, and that proper ACLs are in place to allow access.

description: cannot write POST data for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: Sending the POST data for the HTTP request failed.
action: Ensure the URL is correct and that the remote system is available and configured to accept POST requests.

description: cannot create request, network library unavailable
cause: The system is improperly configured.
action: Ensure the system is properly installed, all libraries relinked and installation files are undamaged.

description: cannot create request, setting proxy configuration failed
cause: The system is improperly configured.
action: Verify the values for the HTTP_PROXY and NO_PROXY properties are valid.

description: cannot create request, setting wallet configuration failed
cause: The system is improperly configured.
action: Verify the wallet property points to a valid wallet file.

description: IO read failed for %(1)s: %(2)s, reference: %(3)s
cause: The underlying read function returned an error.
action: Ensure that the network is working properly, and that the requested resource is available.

description: timeout waiting for available resources to offload query, reference: %(1)s
cause: The pool of available offload servers is empty.
action: Ensure offload servers are available. Check resource limits and other pending queries offload server usage.

description: remote host appears not to be a supported offload server, reference: %(1)s
cause: The remote contacted host did not identify itself as an offload server, or as a supported offload server.
action: Ensure access to the remote host is permitted and possible by e.g. proxy servers, and that a correct tracker url is setup.

description: problem handling offload server response, reference: %(1)s
cause: The interaction between database and offload server went wrong. The database could not understand or handle the message received.
action: Verify the health of the offload server, use the given reference for further support.

description: offload server failed to execute task, reference %(1)s
cause: The offload server could not complete the request because one of the sub-tasks failed after repeated tries.
action: Retry the query, if the issue persists, use the reference given when asking for support.

description: wildcard listing not supported on non-REST or non-ObjectStorage uri %(1)s
cause: The LOCATION does not point to a REST target, or a REST target that is not of ObjectStorage type.
action: Ensure that the LOCATION is of type REST, and that it is pointing to a supported ObjectStorage endpoint.

description: IO read failed for %(1)s: maximum IO budget exceeded
cause: An attempt to read more data failed because an IO budget was set and the read exceeded the limit.
action: Evaluate the budget and the source files to see if the budget needs increasing.

description: timeout waiting for available resources to execute query on offload server, reference: %(1)s
cause: The pool of available offload servers was empty.
action: Ensure offload servers are available. Check resource limits and other pending queries offload server usage.

description: execution of %(1)s aborted: query timeout exceeded
cause: Executing the query took longer than the set timeout.
action: Evaluate the budget and the source files to see if the budget needs increasing.

description: execution of %(1)s aborted: maximum IO budget exceeded
cause: Executing the query took more bytes than the set IO limit.
action: Evaluate the budget and the source files to see if the budget needs increasing.

description: An error occured during JSON reader initialization: %(1)s
cause: Internal system error.
action: Evaluate the health of the executing node and available memory.

description: JSON reader parsing error: %(1)s
cause: JSON file contains syntax errors.
action: Evaluate the file and correct errors.

description: invalid or unsupported traceflag: %(1)s
cause: A provided traceflag could not be recognized as valid or supported.
action: Check the traceflag or flags for their validity.

description: Out of memory
cause: System run out of memory
action: Evaluate the health of the executing node and available memory.

description: offload server was shut down, reference %(1)s
cause: The offload server could not complete the request because it was explicitly shut down.
action: Retry the query. If the issue persists, contact Oracle Support Services and supply the given reference.

description: failed to start Transport Layer Security (TLS) for HTTP connection: %(1)s
cause: Starting an HTTP connection failed to complete the security handshake.
action: Ensure that the certificates match and can be verified, and that the client supports the necessary ciphers for the connection.

description: tracker URL must be set for offloading via BDCell
cause: The com.oracle.bigdata.tracker.url parameter was empty or unset.
action: Define the parameter for the ORACLE_BIGDATA external table.

description: delta sharing profile invalid: %(1)s
cause: The delta sharing profile retrieved was invalid.
action: Ensure that the profile is a valid JSON document conforming to the profile file format specification of delta sharing.

description: Column %(1)s does not exist in source %(2)s
cause: Requested column that did not exist in the file.
action: Request an existing column.

description: Cannot evaluate condition %(1)s %(2)s %(3)s: %(4)s
cause: Cannot evaluate condition in predicates.
action: Give a valid condition.

description: Attempting to allocate memory beyond configured limit of %(1)lu bytes (%(2)lu bytes in use).
cause: More memory than allowed was requested to be allocated.
action: Review the memory limit, and possibly increase it to allow completion of processing.

description: Internal error: attempting to free a previously freed object.
cause: The program tried to free a previously freed object. This is an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Internal error: attempting to free an invalid or corrupted object.
cause: The program tried to free an invalid or corrupted memory block. This is an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Internal error: attempting to allocate 0 bytes.
cause: The program tried to allocate 0 bytes of memory. This is an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Iceberg listing failed: %(1)s.
cause: There is an error during Iceberg listing.
action: Verify Iceberg configuration.

description: Error while processing at offload server %(1)s.
cause: There was an error raised during processing at the given offload server.
action: Consult the follow-on error messages in the stack for details.

description: Cannot detect file format.
cause: Only Avro, ORC and Parquet file formats are auto detected.
action: Use the com.oracle.bigdata.fileformat access parameter to specify the file format.

description: Implicit partitioning failed: %(1)s.
cause: There is an error during implicit partitioning.
action: Specify a query with a valid location.

description: Implicit partitioning access parameter %(1)s error: %(2)s.
cause: There is an error in the implicit partitioning access parameter.
action: Specify a query with a valid access parameter.

description: Object has changed during execution.
cause: Object has changed during execution.
action: Do not change the object during execution.

description: Access to local file '%(1)s' denied.
cause: Access to local files (on disk) is prohibited.
action: Use files on a remote service like object storage.

description: Duplicate column mapping for %(1)s.
cause: The com.oracle.bigdata.colmap parameter contains multiple mappings for the same table column.
action: Remove the duplicate mapping. Each column can only be mapped once onto a field.

description: Table column %(1)s not found for column mapping.
cause: The com.oracle.bigdata.colmap parameter refers to a table column that is not declared in the column list.
action: Ensure that the correct name was specified in the column transformation. The column mapping for the table name is case sensitive.

description: Colmap entry incorrectly formed, missing %(1)s key.
cause: The com.oracle.bigdata.colmap parameter has incorrectly formed JSON objects.
action: Ensure that the JSON objects contain 'col' and 'field' keys in lowercase.

description: Colmap incorrectly formed, invalid JSON document.
cause: The com.oracle.bigdata.colmap parameter cannot be parsed as a valid JSON document.
action: Ensure that the argument contains a correctly formed JSON array or object.

description: header block format is not supported for object-store URI dump file.
cause: User specified an explicit version for a DBMS_DATAPUMP.OPEN API which is incompatible with an object-store Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) dump file. The explicit version specified produces a dump file containing header blocks. Header block format is incompatible with an object-store Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) dump file.
action: Specify a version or file specification which is compatible.

description: %(1)s not supported without JG granulation.
cause: The functionality is not supported without json granulation.
action: Ensure that json granulation is enabled.

description: Partitions are not supported by ORACLE_BIGDATA DESC reader.
cause: Use of partitions in combination with DESC reader.
action: Drop the partitions in order to use DESC.

description: Too many LOCATIONs in use for ORACLE_BIGDATA DESC reader.
cause: Too many LOCATIONs specified in the table DDL in combination with DESC reader.
action: Use com.oracle.bigdata.desc.action=first parameter or reduce the number of LOCATIONs specified using wildcards.

description: invalid query: %(1)s
cause: The specified query had invalid syntax.
action: Specify valid syntax for the query.

description: invalid or missing token
cause: The specified query has an invalid token.
action: Specify a valid token for the query.

description: token is not supported: %(1)s
cause: The specified token is not supported.
action: Specify only supported tokens for the query.

description: type mismatch in values provided in IN operator, expecting %(1)s and got %(2)s
cause: The specified query had an IN operator with values of different type.
action: Use the same type for all values in the IN operator. NLS_DO_NOT_TRANSLATE [14100,14999]

description: integer conversion error or negative integer [%.*s]
cause: A bad or negative integer was assigned to an integer parameter
action: Self explanatory

description: illegal boolean response [%.*s]
cause: You a value than TRUE or FALSE to a boolean parameter
action: Boolean parameters only take TRUE or FALSE

description: unrecognized keyword [%.*s]
cause: You have misspelled the parameter name
action: Spell the parameter name correctly

description: invalid positional parameter value [%.*s]
cause: An invalid positional parameter value has been entered
action: Remove the invalid positional parameter

description: ORACLE error (possible syntax error) parameter [%.*s]
cause: Possible syntax error. Additional messages follow.
action: Correct the parameter in error.

description: could not open specified filename [%.*s]
cause: The file specified does not exist
action: Create an appropriate parameter file

description: missing keyword [%.*s]
cause: A keyword is expected but none was found
action: Add a keyword followed by an '=' sign and a parameter value

description: left parenth and no parameter specified [%.*s]
cause: A parameter list was started but no parameter was specified
action: Add an appropriate list of values and close the parameter list

description: unbalanced parentheses [%.*s]
cause: Self explanatory
action: Balance the parentheses

description: positional parameter entered after keyword [%.*s]
cause: An '=' sign is missing
action: All keywords must be followed by '=' signs

description: nested parentheses encountered [%.*s]
cause: Only one set of parentheses is permitted
action: Remove the nested parentheses

description: unexpected keyword in value list [%.*s]
cause: A keyword was found instead of a value
action: Insert an appropriate value for the given parameter

description: missing value for keyword at end of string [%.*s]
cause: A keyword is specified with no value
action: Specify a valid value for the keyword

description: illegal assignment operator [%.*s]
cause: You used a sign other than '=' to assign a keyword a value
action: Use only the '=' sign

description: unexpected delimiter [%.*s]
cause: An invalid delimiter was found between values
action: A comma or a space is a valid delimiter

description: runaway quoted string [%.*s]
cause: The parameter value was quoted on the left side but not on the right
action: Quote the parameter value on both sides

description: parameter files nested too deep [%.*s]
cause: Too many levels of indirection of file parameters. Maximum is 3.
action: Reduce the level of indirection to less than 3

description: failure while processing file parameter [%.*s]
cause: An error occurred while processing the specified file parameter
action: Specific details will appear in other messges

description: error in file [%.*s]
cause: An error occurred in the particular file.
action: Refer to the other messages for the specific error.

description: nested include file [%.*s] is too large
cause: There is a limit on the size of a parameter file, and it was exceeded. This limit is now 8192 bytes.
action: Remove characters from the file to make it smaller, or use another level of nesting.

cause: The mandatory parameter TARGET was not specified.

description: Need to specify "LOGFILE=<logfile>" when using APPEND=YES option
cause: The APPEND parameter was specified without a LOGFILE.
action: Specify APPEND=YES only when LOGFILE is also specified.

description: LOGIN to target database failed with Oracle error: %s
cause: An Oracle error was reported while attempting to log in to the target database.
action: Follow the actions for the specified Oracle error.

description: File I/O error on datafile "%s" during %s operation (%d/%s)
cause: An operating system error was reported while performing the specified operation in the specified file.
action: Verify the datafile and check for operating system errors.

description: DBNAME string length %d exceeds maximum length of %d
cause: The specified new database name exceeded the maximum size.
action: Specify a shorter, valid name.

description: Cannot use REVERT and specify a database name at the same time
cause: Conflicting options were specified in the command line.
action: Choose only one of the options.

description: Oracle error reported from target database while executing %s %s
cause: An Oracle error was reported when executing an OCI operation.
action: Follow the actions for the specified Oracle error.

description: unsupported connection mode
cause: A mode different than SYSDBA or SYSBACKUP was specified for the connection to the target.
action: Specify only AS SYSDBA or AS SYSBACKUP.

description: Error reading answer - aborting
cause: Response caused an error.
action: Retry the operation.

description: Must specify new database name when SETNAME is used
cause: SETNAME=YES was specified but no DBNAME was provided.
action: Specify DBNAME or remove the SETNAME=YES option.

description: Database should be mounted
cause: The database was not mounted.
action: Mount the database.

description: The Oracle Pluggable Database option specified is invalid.
cause: The Oracle Pluggable Database option specified was not valid.
action: Remove the Oracle Pluggable Database option, or specify ALL or NONE options.

description: Database should be mounted exclusively
cause: The database was started in parallel mode. To change the DBID, the database must be mounted exclusively.
action: Shut down the database and start it in exclusive mode.

description: Database should not be open
cause: The database was open. To change the DBID, the database must be mounted exclusively.
action: Shutdown the database and mount it in exclusive mode.

description: Database should have no offline immediate datafiles
cause: The database has one or more datafiles that are in OFFLINE IMMEDIATE mode.
action: Drop the datafiles or recover them and bring them online.

description: Magic number for datafile "%s" is incorrect
cause: Block 0 header has an incorrect magic number for the specified datafile.
action: Verify that the datafile is correct and retry the operation.

description: Mismatched dbid for datafile %s, expected %lu, found %lu
cause: The dbid of the datafile does not match the 'old' DBID or the 'new' DBID.
action: Verify that this datafile belongs to the database. You may need to restore a backup of the datafile.

description: Database should have no disabled datafiles
cause: The database has one or more datafiles that are disabled.
action: Drop the datafiles or recover them and bring them online.

description: Database should have no datafiles in unknown state
cause: The database has one or more datafiles that are in an unknown state.
action: Drop the datafiles or recover them and bring them online.

description: All online files in the database must have the same checkpoint SCN
cause: The database has one or more datafiles that have a checkpoint SCN that does not match the database checkpoint SCN.
action: Restart the database and shut it down cleanly, then retry the operation.

description: Cannot revert change of database, change not in progress
cause: The REVERT option was used, but the control file does not show that a change of DBID was in progress.
action: Do not use the REVERT option, or possibly restore the control file that was in place when the utility was started.

description: Invalid DBID for datafile "%s", expecting %lu, found %lu
cause: A datafile header shows a different DBID from the rest of the database files.
action: Ensure that the file belongs to this database.

description: Mismatched CHECKPOINT_CHANGE# in datafile "%s", expecting %s, found %s
cause: The datafile header does not match information in the control file.
action: Revert the change, open the database, and verify that all datafiles are consistent. Then, shut down the database and retry the operation.

description: Control file is not current
cause: A non-current control file is currently mounted.
action: Perform necessary actions to make the control file current and retry.

description: CHECKPOINT_CHANGE# in datafile "%s": %s in the future of controlfile: %s
cause: The checkpoint in the datafile header is ahead of the checkpoint in the control file.
action: Make the database consistent and retry.

description: Database should have only consistent datafiles
cause: The database has one or more datafiles that are marked FUZZY in the control file.
action: Restart the database and shut down consistently, then retry the operation.

description: Datafile "%s" is not consistent
cause: The datafile is marked as fuzzy in its header.
action: Restart the database and shut down cleanly, then retry the operation.

description: There are %d active threads
cause: There are active threads in the database. The most likely cause is that the database crashed the last time it was shut down.
action: Ensure that all threads are closed before retrying the operation. Start and open the database to perform crash recovery, then shut down with the NORMAL or IMMEDIATE options to close it cleanly. Finally, try running the utility again.

description: All datafiles that are not dropped should be readable
cause: The database had one or more files that could not be read.
action: Restore the missing files and retry the operation.

description: Block verification failed for datafile %s (%d)
cause: Block header checksum yields a nonzero value for the specified datafile.
action: Verify that the datafile is correct and retry the operation.

description: Mismatched dbname for datafile %s, expected %s, found %s
cause: The dbname of the datafile does not match the 'old' dbname or the 'new' dbname.
action: Verify that this datafile belongs to the database. You may need to restore a backup of the datafile.

description: Specified database name %s does not match previous name used %s
cause: This is a continuation of a failed attempt. However in the failed attempt, the database name is different than the one used in the last attempt.
action: Retry the command using the original database name.

description: No database name specified, previous attempt used %s
cause: This is a continuation of a failed attempt. However, in the failed attempt, a database name was provided.
action: Retry the command using the original database name.

description: Only changing database name, previous attempt changed dbid to %lu
cause: This is a continuation of a failed attempt. However, in the failed attempt, the database id was also being changed.
action: Retry the command removing SETNAME=YES.

description: Mismatched controlfile %s
cause: A controlfile did not have the correct status.
action: Shutdown the database, remove the mismatched controlfile, mount the database, and retry the operation.

description: New name for database %s is the same as current name %s
cause: The specified name is the same as the current name of the database.
action: Specify a different name or do not use the DBNAME option.

description: nls subsystem initialization failure for product=%s, facility=%s
cause: The NLS product/facility error message file could not be located or properly initialized.
action: Check that the error message directory and file(s) have been properly installed.

description: Execution cannot continue - Program Terminating
cause: This is a generic message that indicates a process failure.
action: Look for other messages in the process report and error log that provide more context for this failure. If you cannot determine and resolve the problem, contact Oracle Support.

description: Missing directory name
cause: The directory name is missing from the DIRECTORY option of the TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY parameter.
action: Specify a directory for temporary storage with the DIRECTORY option, or use the default storage by removing the DIRECTORY option.

description: Missing directory name end quote
cause: A trailing (end) quote is missing from the directory specification in the DIRECTORY option of the TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY parameter.
action: Enclose the directory name within double quotes.

description: Directory too long
cause: The directory name that is specified with the DIRECTORY option of TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY exceeds the length limit that is supported by the operating system.
action: Specify a directory that has a path name that is within the operating system limitations.

description: Invalid number for directory file size
cause: The DIRECTORY option of TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY contains an invalid value for the maximum file size, such as a non-numeric value or an invalid size specifier.
action: Specify a valid value. See the Oracle GoldenGate reference documentation for valid directory size and valid size specifiers (such as GB for gigabytes and MB for megabytes).

description: Directory options must be enclosed in parentheses
cause: The directory specification of the DIRECTORY option of TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY is not enclosed within parentheses.
action: Enclose the entire directory specification in parentheses, as in this example: DIRECTORY (c: estdirtmp, 3000000000, 300000000)

description: Invalid number for directory size
cause: The DIRECTORY option of TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY contains an invalid value for the maximum directory size, such as a non-numeric value or an invalid size specifier.
action: Specify a valid value. See the Oracle GoldenGate reference documentation for valid directory size and valid size specifiers (such as GB for gigabytes and MB for megabytes).

description: Missing directory file size
cause: The file size specification is missing from the DIRECTORY option of TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY.
action: Specify a fully qualified directory name, a maximum directory size, and the maximum size of each file, as in: DIRECTORY (c: estdirtmp, 3000000000, 300000000).

description: Directory parentheses must contain valid options
cause: The DIRECTORY option of TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY contains parentheses but no specification within them.
action: Specify a fully qualified directory name, a maximum directory size, and the maximum size of each file, as in: DIRECTORY (c: estdirtmp, 3000000000, 300000000).

description: Missing directory size and directory file size
cause: The DIRECTORY option of TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY does not contain a specification for the maximum directory and file size.
action: Specify a fully qualified directory name, a maximum directory size, and the maximum size of each file, as in: DIRECTORY (c: estdirtmp, 3000000000, 300000000).

description: Missing directory file size
cause: The DIRECTORY option of TRANSMEMORY or LOBMEMORY does not contain a specification for the maximum file size.
action: Specify a fully qualified directory name, a maximum directory size, and the maximum size of each file, as in: DIRECTORY (c: estdirtmp, 3000000000, 300000000).

description: Command line error:invalid startup syntax: {0}
cause: An unknown parameter is specified for the Extract or Replicat process that is being started from the command line
action: Correct the syntax. The command can only contain PARAMFILE and REPORTFILE parameters, for example: /oggdir/extract paramfile dirprm/ext.prm reportfile /user/reports/ext.rpt.

description: Missing {0} argument at startup.
cause: An argument is missing from the specified parameter.
action: Supply the correct syntax. For help, see the Oracle GoldenGate reference documentation.

description: Unrecognized parameter: {0}. Parameter could be misspelled or unsupported.
cause: The specified parameter is not valid for this version of Oracle GoldenGate.
action: Check the parameter file for the correct syntax, spelling, and any required terminators such as the semi-colon. Also make certain the parameter is supported for this version of Oracle GoldenGate. To do both of those things, check the reference documentation for your version of Oracle GoldenGate.

description: {0} is not supported. Check spelling or see Oracle GoldenGate Reference Guide for supported parameters.
cause: The specified parameter is not valid for this version of Oracle GoldenGate.
action: Check the parameter file for the correct syntax, spelling, and any required terminators such as the semi-colon. Also make certain the parameter is supported for this version of Oracle GoldenGate. To do both of those things, check the reference documentation for your version of Oracle GoldenGate.

description: {0} is not supported. Check spelling or see Oracle GoldenGate Reference Guide for supported parameters.
cause: The specified parameter is not valid for this version of Oracle GoldenGate.
action: Check the parameter file for the correct syntax, spelling, and any required terminators such as the semi-colon. Also make certain the parameter is supported for this version of Oracle GoldenGate. To do both of those things, check the reference documentation for your version of Oracle GoldenGate.

description: Not enough stack space. Specify FUNCTIONSTACKSIZE greater than {0}
cause: The size of the memory stack that is used for processing Oracle GoldenGate column-conversion functions needs to be increased.
action: Add the FUNCTIONSTACKSIZE parameter to the parameter file before the point where parameters that contain conversion functions are listed, and set it to at least the value shown in the error message. The value specifies the number of function arguments to allow in a parameter clause.

description: {0} ignored when running as a RMTTASK.
cause: The specified parameter is not supported for a remote task and is being ignored.
action: Remove the parameter from the parameter file to avoid future messages like this.

description: No GROUP value given for RMTTASK in Extract parameter file. Correct: GROUP group_name.
cause: The RMTTASK parameter is missing the required GROUP clause.
action: Add the GROUP clause so that the syntax is RMTTASK REPLICAT, GROUP group_name, where group_name is the name of the Replicat group on the target.

description: The GROUP value in RMTTASK in the Extract parameter file is too long.
cause: The name of the group in the GROUP clause of RMTTASK is probably too long. An Oracle GoldenGate group name can be up to eight characters long.
action: Reduce the length of the group name.

description: The REPLICAT parameter in RMTTASK in the Extract parameter file is not present.
cause: The RMTTASK parameter requires the REPLICAT keyword.
action: The correct syntax is RMTTASK REPLICAT, GROUP group_name, where group_name is the name of the Replicat group on the target.

description: The GROUP clause in RMTTASK line in the Extract parameter file is not present.
cause: The RMTTASK parameter is missing the required GROUP clause.
action: Add the GROUP clause so that the syntax is RMTTASK REPLICAT, GROUP group_name, where group_name is the name of the Replicat group on the target.

description: TCPBUFSIZE and TCPFLUSHBYTES are not supported in RMTTASK mode
cause: The RMTHOST parameter contains the TCPBUFSIZE or TCPFLUSHBYTES option (or both), which are not supported for a remote task.
action: Remove these options from the parameter file.

description: Cannot specify both FORMATASCII and ENCRYPTTRAIL for '{0}'
cause: ENCRYPTTRAIL and NOENCRYPTTRAIL cannot be used when FORMATASCII is used to write data to a file in ASCII format. The trail or file must be written in the default Oracle GoldenGate canonical format when encryption is used.
action: Remove either FORMATASCII or ENCRYPTTRAIL from the parameter file, depending on the configuration requirement.

description: Bulk load not implemented for this database type.
cause: The BULKLOAD parameter is being used for Replicat against a database that is not an Oracle database.
action: Do not use the BULKLOAD initial load method. See the Oracle GoldenGate administration documentation for other supported load methods.

description: {0} was not specified. Check Oracle GoldenGate documentation for correct usage.
cause: The specified parameter is required but missing from the parameter file.
action: Add the parameter. See the Oracle GoldenGate reference documentation for help with syntax and usage.

description: Failed to retrieve column handle for table {0}, column #{1} while getting table definition.
cause: The process could not retrieve the metadata for the specified table. Most likely, the table does not exist.
action: Exclude the table from the TABLE or MAP statement.

description: Failed to retrieve column list handle for table {0} while getting table definition.
cause: The process could not retrieve the metadata for the specified table. Most likely, the table does not exist.
action: Exclude the table from the TABLE or MAP statement.

description: Could not resolve parameter {0}. Check spelling and usage in parameter file.
cause: Oracle GoldenGate could not resolve the specified parameter. It might be misspelled or used incorrectly.
action: Check the Oracle GoldenGate reference documentation for correct syntax and usage.
