cause: One or more conditions required by Data Guard observer were not met.
action: Confirm that Data Guard technology is used for replication, the database belongs to disaster recovery group with FSFO enabled, and there is an online primary database in that group.

description: data type or length of a partitionset column in a sharded table cannot be changed
cause: An attempt was made to issue an ALTER TABLE statement to modify the data type or length of a column used to super-partition the specified sharded table.
action: Do not modify the data type or length of a sharded table super- partitioning column or columns.

description: unsupported SQL construct: %s
cause: The query had a construct that was not supported for inter shard query.
action: Rewrite the query to avoid using an unsupported construct. Consult Oracle documentation for details.

description: DML are not allowed on more than one shard
cause: The DML was applied to more than one shard.
action: Rewrite the DML to limit operation to a single shard.

description: cannot update sharding key
cause: An attempt was made to update the sharding key value using the UPDATE command.
action: Drop and re-create the sharding key.

description: %s maps to multiple shards
cause: The aggregate, group by, semi-join, or anti-join subquery was mapped to multiple shards.
action: Rewrite the query so that subqueries map to a single shard.

description: illegal join predicate on sharding key
cause: The query had illegal or no join predicate on the sharding key.
action: Rewrite the query to include join on sharding columns.

description: sharded table %s outer joined with replicated table %s
cause: The query had a sharded table outer joined to the replicated table.
action: Rewrite the query to remove the outer join.

description: non-equality join on sharding key
cause: The query had a non-equality join on the sharding key.
action: Rewrite the query to remove the non-equality join.

description: queries not supported on objects with user-specified sharding
cause: The query had an object defined by user-specified sharding.
action: None.

description: cross shard queries not supported on composite sharding
cause: The query had an object defined under composite sharding.
action: None.

description: queries involving private and sharded tables not supported
cause: The query referenced a private and a sharded table.
action: Rewrite the query to refer to either private tables or sharded tables, but not both.

description: unsupported construct referred in the query
cause: The query referenced unsupported constructs which could not be fetched from the shard.
action: Rewrite the query to avoid using unsupported constructs.

description: array DML not supported on a sharded table
cause: The statement attempts an array DML operation on a sharded table.
action: Rewrite the array DML statement as separate DML statements.

description: shard key missing in INSERT statement
cause: The INSERT statement was used to insert a row in the sharded table without inserting a value for the shard column.
action: Insert a value for the shard key column.

description: inconsistent shard schema
cause: The schema definition on the shard and the coordinator did not match.
action: Verify and fix the schema inconsistency between the shard and the coordinator.

description: invalid partition for the chunk %s
cause: A valid partition was not found for the chunk number passed to the shard database.
action: Check the chunks handled by the shard database.

description: cannot rename a duplicated table on a shard database
cause: An attempt was made to rename a duplicated table on a shard database.
action: Rename the duplicated table in the shard catalog database, if required.

description: query returned data from %s percent of total chunks
cause: Some of the chunks were not accessible in the system.
action: Ensure that all shards are online and accessible from the query coordinator.

description: target partition key does not map to any partition
cause: An attempt was made to update or delete a record of a range or list-based sharded table with a partition key that did not belong to any of the partition.
action: Use the correct partition key that belongs to a defined partition.

description: sharded table %s does not exist
cause: An attempt was made to add a partition set to a sharded table that did not exist.
action: Create the sharded table with the partition sets.

description: cannot alter duplicated table until GSM_REQUEST to CREATE DUPLICATED TABLE are completed on all shards
cause: An attempt was made to alter a duplicated table when the GSM_REQUEST to create duplicated table materialized view was pending execution.
action: Ensure that GSM_REQUEST to create the duplicated table materialized view is completed on all shards before altering the duplicated table.

description: cannot add existing value to partition sets
cause: The value added to the list partition set already existed for the table.
action: Add new value to the partition set.

description: duplicate partition set name
cause: The name of a partition set of a sharded table being created was not unique.
action: Rename the partition set to ensure that their names are unique among partitions of the sharded table being created.

description: cannot perform cross-shard operation. Some shards are unavailable.
cause: One or more shards were unavailable during the cross-shard operation.
action: Rerun the command when the shards become available.

description: invalid shard ID
cause: An invalid shard ID was specified in the query.
action: Verify the shard ID and retry the operation.

description: The read write option is not supported for sharded tables.
cause: An invalid option is specified while creating a sharded table.
action: Verify the specified option.

description: A shard key cannot be a user-defined type member.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a sharded table having a shard key based on members of user-defined type, which is not allowed.
action: Do not use user-defined type members for shard key.

description: Invalid attempt to use Sharding Raft replication on non-sharded table %s.%s
cause: Sharding Raft replication can only be used with a sharded table. This error can occur if one or more of the shards in a sharded database contains a local table with the same name as a sharded table in the catalog and other shards.
action: Drop the non-sharded table, use GDSCTL to recover that shard, and rerun the DML that failed to be replicated.
params: 1) schema_name: The schema name of the non-sharded table. 2) table_name: The name of the non-sharded table.

description: Required parameter TopN is not specified in the query.
cause: TopN value is required in performing Hybrid Vector Search.
action: Add TopN to the query.

description: HVI SEARCHPIPELINE function's second argument should be set to TRUE on sharding.
cause: The second argument is needed for Hybrid vector search on sharding.
action: Set HVI SEARCHPIPELINE function's second argument to TRUE.

description: HVI SEARCH function is not supported in sharding. Please use SEARCHPIPELINE function.
cause: Hybrid vector SEARCH function is not supported in sharding.
action: Use SEARCHPIPELINE function instead.

description: osnoraenv: error translating ORACLE_SID
cause: Two-task driver could not find the value of ORACLE_SID in the environment.
action: Make sure that the ORACLE_SID environment variable has been properly set and exported.

description: osnoraenv: error translating oracle image name
cause: ORACLE_HOME environment variable not set.
action: Make sure that the ORACLE_HOME environment variable has been properly set and exported.

description: osnoraenv: error translating orapop image name
cause: ORACLE_HOME environment variable not set.
action: Make sure that the ORACLE_HOME environment variable has been properly set and exported.

description: osnpopipe: pipe creation failed
cause: The pipe driver failed to create pipes for communications with the orapop process.
action: You have probably exceeded the maximum number of open file descriptors per user or the system file table is full. Note the operating system error code and contact your system administrator.

description: osndopop: fork failed
cause: The two-task driver could not fork orapop.
action: Verify that there are enough system resources to support another process. The user or system process limit may have been exceeded, or the amount of free memory or swap space may be temporarily insufficient.

description: osnpol: polling of communication channel failed
cause: The pipe driver failed while polling the communications channel.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnshs: host name too long
cause: The length of your host-string specified by the TWO_TASK environment variable exceeds the ORACLE system-imposed limit.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnacx: cannot allocate context area
cause: The invoked Unix two-task driver could not allocate heap space for the context area.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnrntab: connect to host failed, unknown ORACLE_SID
cause: The invoked Unix two-task driver failed to find an entry in oratab for the sid you supplied.
action: First, check whether you have read access to oratab, and see if the desired sid is there. Add an entry to oratab for the desired sid, if necessary.

description: osnpop: pipe creation failed
cause: The pipe driver failed to create pipes for two-task communications with the oracle shadow process.
action: You have probably exceeded the maximum number of open file descriptors per user or the system file table is full. Note the operating system error code and contact your system administrator.

description: osnpop: fork failed
cause: The pipe driver could not fork the oracle shadow process.
action: Verify that there are enough system resources to support another process. The user or system process limit may have been exceeded, or the amount of free memory or swap space may be temporarily insufficient.

description: osnpvalid: write to validation channel failed
cause: The pipe driver failed to write to the orapop process.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpop: malloc failed
cause: The pipe driver failed to allocate enough heap space for its context area buffers.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnprd: message receive failure
cause: The pipe driver failed to read a message from the communications channel.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpwr: message send failure
cause: The pipe driver failed to write a message to the communications channel.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpgetbrkmsg: message from host had incorrect message type
cause: The pipe driver received a message having an unrecognizable message type.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpgetdatmsg: message from host had incorrect message type
cause: The Pipe driver received a message having an unrecognizable message type.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpfs: incorrect number of bytes written
cause: The Pipe driver sent a message that was apparently successful, but the number of bytes transmitted did not match the number of bytes furnished to the driver.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnprs: reset protocol error
cause: The two-task driver could not reset the connection.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnfop: fork failed
cause: The fast driver could not fork the oracle shadow process.
action: Verify that there are enough system resources to support another process. The user or system process limit may have been exceeded, or the amount of free memory or swap space may be temporarily insufficient.

description: osnfop: shmat failed
cause: When the fast driver was invoked, processes failed to attach to the shared memory buffer. You probably supplied an illegal shared memory attach address, or the system ran out of data space to accomodate the buffer.
action: Try invoking the Fast driver later, or use the default attach address.

description: osnseminit: cannot create semaphore set
cause: The Fast driver failed to get a semaphore set.
action: The system-imposed limit on semaphores or semaphore identifiers may have been exceeded. Read the returned operating system error code and check with your system administrator.

description: osnpui: cannot send break message to orapop
cause: The Pipe driver could not send a break message to orapop.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpui: cannot send break signal
cause: The Pipe driver could not send a break message to the ORACLE shadow process.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpbr: cannot send break message to orapop
cause: The Pipe driver could not send a break message to orapop.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpbr: cannot send break signal
cause: The Pipe driver could not send a break message to the ORACLE shadow process.
action: Kill system call failed. Check errno and contact customer support.

description: osnpop: access error on oracle executable
cause: The Pipe driver could not access the oracle executable.
action: Check the permissions on the ORACLE executable and each component of the ORACLE_HOME/bin path.

description: osnpop: access error on orapop executable
cause: The Pipe driver could not access the orapop executable.
action: Check the permissions on the orapop executable and each component of the ORACLE_HOME/bin path.

description: osnfop: access error on oracle executable
cause: The Fast driver could not access the oracle executable.
action: Check the permissions on the ORACLE executable and each component of the ORACLE_HOME/bin path.

description: osncon: driver not in osntab
cause: The driver you have specified is not supported.
action: Check with your database administrator which drivers are supported.

description: osnrnf: cannot find user logon directory
cause: The driver you have specified could not find your logon directory while searching for your local .sqlnet file.
action: Set and export the HOME environment variable to identify your home directory. Check with your system administrator to make sure that your uid and home directory are correct in the /etc/passwd file.

description: osnrnf: malloc of buffer failed
cause: The specified driver could not find enough heap space to malloc a buffer.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnrnf: cannot find a matching database alias
cause: Database alias specified was not identified in either $HOME/.sqlnet or /etc/sqlnet.
action: Create the alias in a file called .sqlnet in your home directory for personal use or ask your system administrator to create the alias in /etc/sqlnet for system-wide use.

description: osnsnf: database string too long
cause: While converting a database alias to a database ID, the resulting database ID string exceeded the ORACLE system-imposed limit.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnftt: cannot reset shared memory permission
cause: The Fast driver was unable to reset shared memory permissions.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnfpm: cannot create shared memory segment
cause: The Fast driver failed to create a shared memory segment for two-task communication.
action: Check whether the system-imposed limit on shared memory identifiers has already been reached for your system.

description: osnfpm: illegal default shared memory address
cause: The Fast driver failed to establish a default shared memory address.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpcl: cannot tell orapop to exit
cause: The Pipe driver failed to send orapop the command to exit.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnpwrtbrkmsg: incorrect number of bytes written
cause: The pipe driver apparently sent an imcomplete break message.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osncon: host alias is too long
cause: The alias used for a sqlnet host is longer than 161 characters.
action: Use a shorter alias.

description: osnfsmmap: cannot open shared memory file ?/dbs/ftt_<pid>.dbf
cause: The Fast driver failed to create a shared memory file for two-task communication.
action: Check the permissions on the directory ?/dbs

description: osnfsmmap: cannot map shared memory file
cause: The Fast driver failed to map a shared memory file for two-task communication.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnfsmmap: illegal shared memory address
cause: The Fast driver failed to attach shared memory at the expected location.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnfsmmap: cannot close shared memory file
cause: The Fast driver cannot close the shared memory file.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnfsmmap: cannot change shared memory inheritence
cause: The Fast driver could not alter the inheritence attributes of the shared memory.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnfsmcre: cannot create chared memory file ?/dbs/ftt_<pid>.dbf
cause: The Fast driver failed to create a file for shared memory.
action: Check the permissions on the directory ?/dbs

description: osnfsmnam: name translation failure
cause: The Fast driver encountered an error translating the shared memory file name ?/dbs/ftt_<pid>.dbf.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: osnfop: fork_and_bind failed
cause: The Fast driver failed to fork a process onto the desired cluster and node number.
action: Check the desired node number in sercose[0] and cluster ID in sercose[1]. If these seem valid, contact customer support.

description: Allocation of internal array failed
cause: The package was unable to allocate memory for an array because the system ran out of memory.
action: Either reclaim memory by killing other processes or reboot the machine with more memory.

description: Not enough request descriptors available
cause: All of the package's request descriptors are in use performing other requests.
action: Either wait until enough requests are done, or shut the package down and re-initialize it with more request descriptors.

description: Client close of file failed.
cause: The client was unable to close a file after forking the servers.
action: This is a system problem - contact your System Administrator.

description: File number to be canceled is negative.
cause: The file number contained with the sfiov structure is less than zero.
action: This may be a programming error. If it is not, contact ORACLE support.

description: file number to be cancelled is greater than the maximum.
cause: The file number contained with the sfiov structure is greater than the maximum.
action: This may be a programming error. If it is not, contact ORACLE support.

description: Unable to cancel at least one request
cause: No requests were found that could be cancelled.
action: This error can occur if all the requests dealing with that file number have already been filled.

description: Invalid package mode
cause: The mode of the package can only be parallel or duplex.
action: See sfa.h for the correct values.

description: Invalid maximum number of servers
cause: The number of servers given was less than or equal to zero.
action: Use a number greater than zero.

description: Invalid maximum of request descriptors
cause: The number of request descriptors was less than or equal to zero.
action: Use a number greater than zero.

description: Less than one request descriptor was allocated per server
cause: The package requires that the number of request descriptors be greater than or equal to the number of servers used.
action: Use a higher number

description: Maximum number of files is invalid
cause: The maximum number of files to be used by the package was less than or equal to zero.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Setting of handler for SIGTERM failed
cause: The package was unable to set up handling by the server for the termination signal. This is an internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Total number of blocks is invalid
cause: The total number of blocks to be allocated for use by the package was not greater than zero.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Illegal request time out value
cause: The number was not a positive number.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Invalid maximum server idle time
cause: The time given was not a positive number.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Invalid maximum client wait time
cause: The time given was not a positive number.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Invalid request list latch time out value
cause: The time given was not a positive number.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Invalid request done signal
cause: The signal number was not a positive number.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Value for request done signal exceeds maximum
cause: The value sent to the package for use as the "request done" signal exceeds the maximum allowed by the operating system.
action: Contact your system administrator.

description: Stat failed on log directory
cause: The package was unable to get information about the directory in which the log files are to reside.
action: Check the permissions on the directory or use a different directory name.

description: Name given for the log directory is invalid
cause: The name given for the directory in which the logs are to be kept does not correspond to a directory.
action: Use a different name.

description: Stat failed on core dump directory
cause: The package was unable to get information about the directory into which the servers are to dump core in the event of an exception.
action: Check the permissions on the directory or use a different directory name.

description: Name given for the core dump directory is invalid
cause: The name given for the directory in which the server processes are to dump core in the event of an exception does not correspond to a directory.
action: Use a different name.

description: Invalid value given for the timing wanted flag
cause: The value given was not TRUE or FALSE.
action: Specify TRUE or FALSE for the timing wanted flag.

description: Both read and write functions were not specified
cause: To ensure that the functions act symmetrically, pointers to both the read and write functions must be given.
action: Either specify both functions or specify neither. The package will supply its own functions.

description: Both post and wait functions were not specified
cause: To ensure that the functions act symmetrically, pointers to both the posting and waiting functions must be given.
action: Either specify both functions or specify neither. The package will supply its own functions.

description: Invalid shared memory ID specified
cause: The ID of the segment specified for use as the shared buffer region was invalid.
action: Use a different ID, or let the package specify its own.

description: Invalid shared memory buffer size
cause: The size given for the shared memory segment to be used as the shared buffer region was less than or equal to zero.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Size needed for shared region is greater than segment size
cause: The size of the shared segment that was specified for the shared buffer region is less than the number of bytes required. The first field of the "additional information" field is the size needed. The second is the size of the segment.
action: Use a larger size segment or let the package allocate its own.

description: Unable to allocate memory for segment list
cause: The package cannot allocate memory for an internal segment list because the system has run out of memory. The "additional information" field is the amount of memory that the package attempted to allocate.
action: Close some processes or contact your system administrator.

description: Unable to find kernel process pointer in async process array
cause: Internal error - Contact ORACLE support.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Maximum number of files reached
cause: The maximum number of files that can be used for asynchronous I/O has been reached.
action: Shut down the servers and re-initialize the package with a higher number.

description: File name is too long
cause: The length of the name of a file that is being opened for asynchronous I/O is longer than the maximum. The "additional information" field is the maximum length.
action: Use a shorter name.

description: Unable to open file for use with asynchronous I/O
cause: The package could not open file for some reason.
action: Check the file name.

description: Unable to fstat() a file being used for asynchronous I/O.
cause: The fstat(2) call on a file being used for asynchronous I/O failed.
action: Check the file name.

description: Close of asynchronous I/O failed.
cause: The client was unable to close a file being used for asynchronous I/O.
action: Contact ORACLE support - this should not happen.

description: Client unable to get key for shared memory
cause: The client was unable to get a key so that it obtain shared memory for use with shared memory.
action: Contact ORACLE support - this is an internal error.

description: Request list is empty
cause: The client was signalled by a server that it was done with a request but the "done" list was empty.
action: Internal error - contact ORACLE support.

description: Done request is not in correct state
cause: A request is not in the right state.
action: Internal error - contact ORACLE support.

description: No requests available
cause: No free request descriptors are available.
action: Wait until some requests are filled and then retry the request, or shutdown the servers and initialize the package with a higher number of requests.

description: Invalid number of requests
cause: The number of operations sent to either sfard() or sfawrite() is less than zero.
action: This is a user programming error.

description: Unable to arm signal handler
cause: The arming of a signal handler for the "done" signal failed.
action: Internal error - contact ORACLE support.

description: Requests timed out
cause: Some of the requests for asynchronous input or output were not serviced in the required amount of time.
action: If the load on the system is high, it is possible that the timeout limit is too low. Reset it with sfainit(). If the server processes are dying due to unexpected signals, this is an internal error, and ORACLE support should be contacted.

description: Operations timed out
cause: Some asynchronous operations timed out in kernel mode.
action: Internal error - contact ORACLE support.

description: No idle servers available in parallel mode
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Retrieval of current time failed
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Allocation of memory failed for log file name
cause: The client was unable to allocated a buffer for the name of the log file.
action: Contact your System Administrator.

description: Unable to set handler for SIGTPA
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Unable to set handler for SIGALRM
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Allocation of memory for I/O vectors failed.
cause: The client was unable to allocate memory for the array of I/O vectors that the servers are to use.
action: Contact your System Administrator.

description: Allocation of memory of open files array failed.
cause: The client was unable to allocate memory for an array of flags that the servers are to use.
action: Contact your System Administrator.

description: Jump buffer not valid
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Unable to make temporary file name for memory mapped file
cause: This is an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to attach shared memory segment
cause: This is an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Bad attach address
cause: This is an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to make temporary file name in order to get key
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Unable to get shared memory
cause: Shmget(2) failed.
action: Check the UNIX number. If you are unsure about what it means, contact ORACLE customer support.

description: Unable to attach shared memory
cause: Shmat(2) failed.
action: Check the UNIX number. If you are unsure about what it means, contact ORACLE customer support.

description: Unable to kill a process
cause: A server did not die after being sent a kill signal.
action: The process may be a runaway - contact ORACLE customer support.

description: Read failed
cause: A server could not read a requested amount of data.
action: Check the call to sfard(). An incorrect file descriptor may have been sent to sfard(). The number in the "additional information" field is the starting block number of the data segment being read in.

description: Less than the number of blocks requested was read in
cause: A server could not read in the request amount of data. The first number in the "additional information" field is the block number being read in. The second is the actual number of bytes that was read in.
action: This is a programming error.

description: Write failed
cause: A server was unable to perform a write. The number in the "additional information" field is the starting block number of the data segment being written out. The first number in the "additional information" field is the block number being written out. The second is the actual number of bytes that was written out. The disk may have filled up.
action: Check the UNIX error number.

description: Unable to write the requested number of blocks
cause: A server could not write the requested amount of data out to disk. The disk may have run out of space.
action: Check the UNIX error number.

description: could not allocate memory to receive message from LGWR
cause: A redo transport SYNC process could not allocate memory to receive a message from the log writer process (LGWR).
action: No action is required.

description: Invalid block offset
cause: A server was unable to seek to the designated block.
action: Check the UNIX error number.

description: Buffer is not aligned.
cause: The buffer on which an I/O was being done was not on the correct boundary.
action: Check the calling program.

description: Request free list is empty
cause: The list from which the package allocates request descriptors is empty because all of the descriptors is in use.
action: Wait until some become free, or initialize the package with a higher number of request descriptors.

description: Request on free list was not free
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Illegal block size
cause: A negative number was given for the I/O block size to be used by the asynchronous I/O package.
action: This is a programming error - use either a positive number or zero to get the default value.

description: Invalid file number
cause: The file number upon which an operation is to done is either less than zero or greater than the maximum number of files than can be open.
action: This is a programming error. Since the calling program should not touch this number, this is a programming error.

description: Segment free list is empty
cause: No segments are available to allocated.
action: Free some segments or shut down the package and re-initialize it with a higher number of segments.

description: No segment of the proper size is available
cause: No segment of the proper size is ready for use by the caller.
action: Free some segments and try again.

description: Segment could not be split - no free segments available
cause: A segment that is larger than that desired could not be split because no free segment was available.
action: Free some segments and try again.

description: Segment deallocation failed - empty segment list
cause: The caller attempted to deallocate a segment but the "in use" list was empty. This is a programming error.
action: Check the calling program.

description: Segment deallocation failed - segment not on list
cause: The caller attempted to deallocate a segment that was not on the "in use" list. This is a programming error.
action: Check the calling program.

description: Server was unable to close file
cause: A server was unable to close a file being used for asynchronous I/O.
action: See the UNIX error number for more information.

description: Server unable to open file
cause: The server was unable to open a file for use with asynchronous I/O.
action: Check the UNIX error number for more information.

description: Server unable to send signal to client
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Unable to create temporary key file
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Unable to unlink temporary file
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Unable to arm signal handler for the alarm signal
cause: The arming of a signal handler for the alarmsignal failed.
action: Internal error - contact ORACLE support.

description: Sync of blocks to disk failed.
cause: The server was unable to flush its writes out to disk.
action: Check the UNIX error number.

description: Open of log file by client failed
cause: The client process was unable to open its log file.
action: Check the UNIX error number for more information.

description: Server died on start up
cause: A server exited during its initialization process.
action: Check the servers' logs for more information.

description: Client unable to fork a server
cause: The client could not spawn a server. A possible reason is that the operating system has reached its limit on the number of processes that it can spawn.
action: Either reduce the number of servers that are to be used, or reconfigure the operating system so that it can handle more processes.

description: Invalid value for kernel flag
cause: An illegal value was given for the kernel flag in the information structure. Only TRUE and FALSE are permitted.
action: This is a programming error - check the calling routine.

description: Invalid value for the leave open flag
cause: A value was given for the flag that determines whether a file is to be left open after the client checks it to see if the servers can use it. Only TRUE and FALSE are supported.
action: This is a programming error - check the calling routine.

description: Invalid value for the timing wanted flag
cause: A value was given for the flag that indicates that operations are to be timed out. Only TRUE and FALSE are supported.
action: This is a programming error - check the calling routine.

description: Unkillable server
cause: A server would not respond to the termination signal. The first number is the number of the server. The second is its UNIX process number. This is an internal problem.
action: This is an operating system problem.

description: Server did not terminate when posted
cause: A server did not respond to a posted request to shutdown. The first number is the number of the server. The second is its UNIX process number. This is an internal problem.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Asynchronous I/O package is not running
cause: An operation using the asynchronous I/O package was attempted without first initializing the package using sfainit().
action: Call sfainit() before using the package.

description: Read failed because of an error
cause: A server could not read the requested amount of data from disk.
action: Check the UNIX error number.

description: File is closed
cause: A file upon which an asynchronous I/O operation is to be performed has already been closed by the package.
action: This is a programming error.

description: Request list is empty when it should not be
cause: This is an internal problem.
action: Contact ORACLE support.

description: Invalid critical-section time out value
cause: The time given was not a positive number.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Invalid server list latch time out value
cause: The time given was not a positive number.
action: Use a positive number.

description: Invalid number of request buffers
cause: The value given for "db_slave_buffers" in your INIT.ORA file is less than 0.
action: Use a number that is greater than or equal to 0.

description: Number of requests is less than the number of slaves
cause: The value given for 'db_slave_buffers' in the initialization parameter file was less than the number specified for the number of slaves, 'db_slaves.'
action: Specify a number that is greater than that given for 'db_slaves.' Alternatively, specify 0. The kernel will supply the appropriate number.

description: smpini: Unable to get shared memory for PGA
cause: Stated in errno.
action: Resolve the problem.

description: smpini: Unable to attach to shared memory for PGA
cause: Stated in errno.
action: Resolve the problem.

description: smpini: Unable to initialize memory protection
cause: The adspcinit program has not been executed.
action: Execute the adscpinit program as shown in your Installation and Users' Guide. If the problem persists, try rebooting your computer.

description: sou2o: Variable smpdidini overwritten
cause: The variable smpdidini was overwritten, probably by client code.
action: Verify client code, e.g. Pro*C, for illegal memory access. If the problem occurs outside Single Task operation, contact your customer support representative.

description: sou2o: Could not gain access to protected memory
cause: This is an internal error, note error code in errno.
action: Report to your customer support representative. Restarting your application or your computer may cure the problem.

description: smpini: Could not register PGA for protection
cause: This is an internal error, note error code in errno.
action: Report to your customer support representative. Restarting your application or your computer may cure the problem.

description: sou2o: Could not revoke access to protected memory
cause: This is an internal error, note error code in errno.
action: Report to your customer support representative. Restarting your application or your computer may cure the problem.

description: sou2o: Could not register SGA for protection
cause: This is an internal error, note error code in errno.
action: Report to your customer support representative. Restarting your application or your computer may cure the problem.

description: smscre: Cannot create SGA with Extended Shared Memory feature
cause: The environment variable EXTSHM was set before starting oracle.
action: Unset the environment variable EXTSHM and startup oracle.

description: unimplemented feature
cause: This feature was not implemented.
action: None.

description: obsolete feature
cause: User attempted to use a feature which is no longer supported.
action: None.

description: Incompatible OCI function call
cause: An incompatible OCI function call was issued for new functionality.
action: Do not use V7 OCI calls for this functionality.

description: QUALIFY clause and MODEL clause used in the same query block
cause: The QUALIFY clause is not supported with MODEL clause in the same query block.
action: Do one of the folllowing: 1. Remove the QUALIFY clause from the query block. 2. Remove the MODEL clause from the query block.

description: Encountering the QUALIFY clause in the recursive member of the subquery factoring clause
cause: The QUALIFY clause is not supported in the recursive member of the subquery factoring clause of the WITH clause.
action: Remove the QUALIFY clause from the recursive member of the subquery factoring clause.

description: %s option already specified
cause: The option is being specified more than once.
action: Remove the repeated option.
params: 1) repeated_option: The option that was repeated.

description: Invalid value specified for EFSEARCH parameter (%s). Must be a positive integer literal.
cause: The value specified for the EFSEARCH parameter is not a numeric value greater than 0.
action: Modify the EFSEARCH parameter value and retry the operation.
params: 1) param_value: The value specified for EFSEARCH parameter.

description: Invalid value specified for accuracy percentage (%s). Must be an integer literal between 1 and 100.
cause: The value specified for the accuracy percentage is not a numeric value between 1 and 100.
action: Modify the accuracy percentage value and retry the operation.
params: 1) accuracy_value: The value specified for accuracy percentage.

description: Invalid value specified for the number of rows or partitions to fetch (%s). Must be a positive integer literal.
cause: The value specified for the number of rows or partitions to fetch in the ROW LIMITING clause is not a numeric value greater than 0.
action: Modify the value for the number of rows or partitions and retry the operation.
params: 1) number_of_rows_or_partitions: The value specified for the number of rows or partitions.

description: Invalid value specified for NEIGHBOR PARTITION PROBES parameter (%s). Must be a positive integer literal.
cause: The value specified for the NEIGHBOR PARTITION PROBES parameter is not a numeric value greater than 0.
action: Modify the NEIGHBOR PARTITION PROBES parameter value and retry the operation.
params: 1) param_value: The value specified for NEIGHBOR PARTITION PROBES parameter.

description: DISTINCT or UNIQUE keyword in select_list of SELECT statement
cause: The DISTINCT or UNIQUE keyword is encountered in the select_list of a SELECT SQL statement. This is syntactically invalid.
action: The DISTINCT or UNIQUE keyword can be used before the select_list to return only one copy of each set of duplicate rows selected. For example: - SELECT DISTINCT ENAME, JOB, SAL FROM EMP; - SELECT UNIQUE ENAME, JOB, SAL FROM EMP;

description: string '%s' is not syntactically valid following '%s'
cause: An unexpected keyword was encountered in the SQL statement at or near the position printed in the error message. One of the following occurred: 1. You had a typo in your SQL statement. 2. Unsupported syntax was encountered for a clause in the statement. 3. An unsupported clause was encountered in the statement. 4. A string was terminated prematurely leading to the rest of the string to be interpreted as keywords. For example, an apostrophe in the string may be causing it to end prematurely. 5. If keyword_value does not appear in the statement and CURSOR_SHARING is set to FORCE, an unexpected bind variable was encountered in the statement. 6. If keyword_value does not appear in the statement and a function was called in the statement, an unexpected keyword was encountered during function execution. This typically occurs when a function attempts to execute a statement it has constructed.
action: Take the action that corresponds with the Cause: 1. Check that your SQL statement has no typos. 2. Check Oracle Database documentation to find the correct syntax for the clause and update the problematic clause appropriately. 3. Check Oracle Database documentation to find the correct syntax for the statement and remove the unsupported clause. 4. Enter two single quotes instead of one to represent an apostrophe within a string. 5. Set CURSOR_SHARING to EXACT and execute the statement again. This may either resolve the issue or provide additional information regarding the error. 6. Check that the function is not executing a statement that contains any of the issues listed in Causes 1 through 5.
params: 1) keyword_value: Either the keyword causing the error or the keyword near the keyword causing the error. The keyword value may be truncated for readability if it is too long. 2) previous_keyword_values: a sequence of keyword values that immediately precede the keyword_value in the command. The sequence of previous keyword values may be truncated if it is too long.

description: invalid identifier: %s is a reserved word
cause: A reserved word was used when an identifier or column name was expected.
action: Enter a valid identifier or column name. A valid identifier must begin with a letter, be less than or equal to 128 characters, and consist of only alphanumeric characters and the special characters $, _, and #. If it contains other characters, then it must be enclosed in double quotation marks. It must not be a reserved word, unless it is enclosed in double quotation marks.

description: missing required keyword INNER or OUTER in SYS_OP_KEY_VECTOR_USE operator
cause: The keyword INNER or OUTER was not specified for the SYS_OP_KEY_VECTOR_USE operator.
action: Specify the INNER or OUTER keyword for the SYS_OP_KEY_VECTOR_USE operator.

description: invalid argument for STANDARD_HASH function
cause: The second argument provided for STANDARD_HASH was invalid.
action: Provide a valid second argument for the STANDARD_HASH function, to specify the name of the hash algorithm to be used. Valid algorithms are SHA1, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512 and MD5. The second argument can be omitted, in which case SHA1 will be used.

description: unable to parse string '%s' as a date
cause: The given string could not be parsed as a date.
action: Change the string so that it can be parsed as a date.

description: invalid identifier: %s is a number
cause: A number was used when an identifier or column name was expected.
action: Enter a valid identifier or column name. A valid identifier must begin with a letter, be less than or equal to 128 characters, and consist of only alphanumeric characters and the special characters $, _, and #. If it contains other characters, such as numbers, then it must be enclosed in double quotation marks. It must not be a reserved word, unless it is enclosed in double quotation marks.

description: missing keyword: expected TIMESTAMP, SCN, PERIOD FOR, or SNAPSHOT
cause: The AS OF keywords were not followed by one of TIMESTAMP, SCN, PERIOD FOR, or SNAPSHOT.
action: Correct the syntax. After the AS OF keywords, insert TIMESTAMP, SCN, PERIOD FOR, or SNAPSHOT.

description: invalid expression in SELECT INTO clause
cause: An invalid expression was specified in the SELECT INTO clause.
action: Correct the expression in the SELECT INTO clause.

description: invalid expression in RETURNING INTO clause
cause: An invalid expression was specified in the RETURNING INTO clause.
action: Correct the expression in the RETURNING INTO clause.

description: %s: invalid cursor name in WHERE CURRENT OF clause
cause: The cursor name that was provided in the WHERE CURRENT OF clause was invalid.
action: Provide a valid cursor name in the WHERE CURRENT OF clause.

description: The expression %s is invalid.
cause: The specified expression was invalid. Expected column name, dot-notation syntax, or TREAT expression.
action: Enter a valid expression. It must be a column name, an expression using dot-notation syntax, or a TREAT function. Valid column names start with a letter, are 128 characters or less, and use only alphanumeric characters and the special characters $, _, and #. If the expression uses other characters, those characters must be enclosed in double quotation marks. The name cannot be a reserved word, unless it is enclosed in double quotation marks.

description: Data type %s is invalid.
cause: The data type entered in the CREATE or ALTER TABLE statement was not valid.
action: Correct the syntax. This may involve doing one of the following: - Fix the mispelled data type. - If the data type is an ADT, then remove any specified parameters. - If the data type is an Oracle supplied data type, then remove any specified parameters.

description: Precision cannot be specified for data type %s.
cause: The data type entered in the CREATE or ALTER TABLE statement did not support a precision parameter.
action: Remove the precision parameter.

description: missing comma or right parenthesis
cause: One of the following occurred: - There was no comma separating the two column definitions. - A left parenthesis was entered without a closing right parenthesis, or extra information was contained in the parentheses. - A data type was misspelled.
action: Insert a comma between the column definitions.

description: Packing or unpacking data types is not supported.
cause: Packed or unpacked data types were not supported in this statement.
action: Remove the PACKED or UNPACKED keyword.

description: encountered FROM clause but expected optional WHERE, RETURNING or ERROR_LOGGING clauses
cause: FROM clause was encountered after the UPDATE_SET clause in an UPDATE statement. UPDATE statement supports only optional WHERE, RETURNING or ERROR_LOGGING clauses after the UPDATE_SET clause.
action: Remove the FROM clause or replace it with the optional WHERE, RETURNING or ERROR_LOGGING clauses.

description: invalid GV$ query
cause: An error occurred while processing a query involving a GV$ view.
action: Check the GV$ query.

description: invalid PL/SQL expression
cause: The PL/SQL expression that was provided was invalid.
action: Correct the PL/SQL expression.

description: invalid PL/SQL record variable in INSERT or UPDATE
cause: The record variable used in the VALUES clause of a PL/SQL INSERT statement or the SET clause of a PL/SQL UPDATE statement was was invalid.
action: Correct the record variable in the VALUES clause of the PL/SQL INSERT statement or the SET clause of the PL/SQL UPDATE statement.

description: invalid expression in the PARTITION BY clause of a partitioned outer join
cause: The PARTITION BY clause of a partitioned outer join contained an invalid expression.
action: Correct the PARTITON BY clause of the partitioned outer join. There should be no subqueries, and the expressions should only refer to the table reference immediately preceding the PARTITON BY clause. For more information refer to the section on the outer join clause in the SQL Language Reference manual.

description: unsupported use of SYS_OP_LBID operator
cause: The SYS_OP_LBID operator was used when there was no index present.
action: Ensure that there is an index that the SYS_OP_LBID operator can process.

description: GROUP BY position must be the ordinal number of a SELECT list expression
cause: GROUP BY position was not the ordinal number of a SELECT list column.
action: The GROUP BY position must be a number between 1 and the number of columns in the SELECT list. Check the column number and retry the statement.

description: ENABLE DICTIONARY PROTECTION already specified
cause: ENABLE DICTIONARY PROTECTION was already specified.
action: Remove ENABLE DICTIONARY PROTECTION.

description: DISABLE DICTIONARY PROTECTION already specified
cause: DISABLE DICTIONARY PROTECTION was already specified.
action: Remove DISABLE DICTIONARY PROTECTION.

description: IDENTIFIED clause is specified with ENABLE DICTIONARY PROTECTION clause
cause: IDENTIFIED clause not supported when using DICTIONARY PROTECTION clause.
action: Remove the IDENTIFIED clause and retry the operation.

description: Size cannot be specified for data type %s.
cause: The data type entered in the CREATE or ALTER TABLE statement did not support a size parameter.
action: Remove the size parameter.

description: unexpected item %s in an out-of-line constraint
cause: An unexpected item occurred in an out-of-line constraint. Either there was a missing comma or right parenthesis, or there were items out of order or misspelled.
action: Check the item and the list to correct the error.

description: unexpected item %s in a column definition or inline constraint
cause: An unexpected item occurred in a column definition or inline constraint definition. Either there was a missing comma or right parenthesis, or there were items out of order or misspelled.
action: Check the item and the list to correct the error.

description: unexpected left parenthesis after %s
cause: An unexpected left parenthesis occurred after the indicated symbol. Either there was a missing or incorrect item, or there were items out of order or misspelled.
action: Check the item and the list to correct the error.

description: unexpected right parenthesis after %s
cause: An unexpected right parenthesis occurred after the indicated symbol. Either there was a missing or incorrect item, or there were items out of order or misspelled.
action: Check the item and the list to correct the error.

description: missing required column definition list
cause: The statement required a column definition list, but the list was not included.
action: Add a column definition list.

description: '%s': invalid character in '%s'
cause: An invalid character has been encountered in the SQL statement.
action: Remove the invalid character. If it is part of an identifier, enclose the identifier in double quotation marks.
params: 1) character_value: The invalid character causing the error. 2) string_value: The string in which the invalid character causing the error occurs.

description: invalid character encountered during direct path conversion
cause: TODO
action: TODO

description: VALIDATE keyword not allowed in view constraints
cause: The view constraint definition included the VALIDATE keyword, which was not allowed. Only NOVALIDATE can be used.
action: Modify the view constraint definition to either remove VALIDATE or replace it with NOVALIDATE.

description: Missing column or expression in the SET clause of an UPDATE statement
cause: Another column or expression was expected after the comma or left parenthesis in the SET clause of an UPDATE statement but was not found.
action: One of the following: - Remove the dangling comma if the intention was to end the SET clause. - Double quote the keyword after the comma if it is a reserved word and the intention was to add another column or expression.

description: invalid character set ID (CSID) %s
cause: The specified character set ID (CSID) was invalid.
action: Specify a valid character set ID (CSID).

description: invalid timeout value
cause: The timeout value was not a valid number.
action: Specify a valid number as the timeout value.

description: invalid depth %s in the hierarchy cube SQL function
cause: The depth for the hierarchy cube SQL function HIER_DESCENDANTS, HIER_LEVEL_MEMBERS or HIER_COLUMN was invalid.
action: Specify a valid number as the depth for the hierarchy cube SQL function HIER_DESCENDANTS, HIER_LEVEL_MEMBERS or HIER_COLUMN.

description: unable to convert BINARY_FLOAT or BINARY_DOUBLE NaN (Not a Number) value to NUMBER
cause: The conversion from BINARY_FLOAT or BINARY_DOUBLE NaN (Not a Number) value to NUMBER failed.
action: Check BINARY_FLOAT and BINARY_DOUBLE, and make sure they are valid.

description: invalid policy ID in the HAVING clause for the SYS_CTX_MKIVIDX function
cause: The policy ID in the HAVING clause for the SYS_CTX_MKIVIDX function was not a number.
action: Specify a valid number as the policy ID in the HAVING clause for the SYS_CTX_MKIVIDX function.

description: invalid number containing %s
cause: The number containing specified character or string was invalid. Only numeric fields are allowed.
action: Check the number in the function or expression. Ensure that they contain only numbers, a sign, a decimal point, and the character "E" or "e", and retry the operation.

description: invalid number containing %s for '%s'
cause: The number containing specified character or string for column or expression was invalid. Only numeric fields are allowed.
action: Check the number in the column or expression. Ensure that they contain only numbers, a sign, a decimal point, and the character "E" or "e", and retry the operation.

description: character limit must be greater than zero
cause: The specified character limit was invalid.
action: Specify a valid character limit that is greater than zero.

description: Too many columns or values for %s, maximum %s
cause: The INSERT or UPDATE statement has too many columns or values.
action: Modify the SQL statement by limiting the number of columns and values to 1000 or 4000 depending on the database version.
params: 1) dml_type: The type of SQL statement: INSERT or UPDATE. 2) max_cols: The maximum number of columns or values allowed.

description: expression level is too deep, maximum %s
cause: The SQL statement has an expression that is too complicated to parse.
action: Modify the SQL statement by simplifying complicated expressions or removing excessive parentheses.
params: 1) max_depth: The maximum depth of expressions allowed.

description: invalid argument [%s] passed to function SYS_OP_COUNTCHG
cause: The specified argument to SYS_OP_COUNTCHG is invalid. The first argument should be a column or a function. The second argument should be a constant literal integer greater than 0 and less than 256.
action: Ensure that the arguments passed to SYS_OP_COUNTCHG are valid.
params: 1) argument_position: The position of the invalid argument.

description: windowing clause not allowed for function %s
cause: Windowing clause was not allowed for the given function.
action: Use the function without specifying windowing clause.

description: unexpected item %s in an expression
cause: An unexpected item occurred in an expression. Either there was a missing operator or extra operator, or there were items out of order or misspelled, or the types of the operands were not compatible with the operator.
action: Check the item and the expression to correct the error.

description: unexpected item %s in a column definition
cause: An unexpected item occurred in a column definition. Either there was a missing comma or right parenthesis, or there were items out of order or misspelled, or an inline constraint was misspelled.
action: Check the item and the list to correct the error.

description: communication area cannot be allocated; insufficient memory
cause: An attempt to allocate stack space for communication purposes failed. This is an internal error message not usually issued.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: invalid input data for %s
cause: Invalid input data was detected for the specified data type.
action: Pass a valid value for the specified data type.

description: invalid character set detected during data conversion either to or from the client
cause: Either a malformed network packet describing the character set was received or the client character set was invalid. Hence, the character set was not recognized.
action: If the error persists, verify network stability. Contact Oracle Support Services, if necessary.

description: malformed network packet from client rejected for network RPC (%s) with reason %d
cause: An invalid input was detected for the specified Remote Procedural Call (RPC).
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: internal protocol error
cause: NA
action: NA

description: fatal two-task communication protocol error
cause: The communication path between Oracle and the user task has stopped. This is an internal error message not usually issued.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: oranet buffer underflow
cause: This is an internal error message not usually issued.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: this version of the Oracle Client libraries is not supported by the database version
cause: A connection attempt was made from an application using a version of the Oracle Client libraries that is not supported by the database version.
action: Upgrade to the latest version of the Oracle Client libraries and try again.

description: oranet buffer overflow
cause: Data being transferred between the user program and Oracle overflowed the buffer space available. This is an internal error message not usually issued.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: oranet: ORACLE does not support this SQL version
cause: The version of Oracle connected to via Net8 does not support the version of the Net8 protocol.
action: Upgrade the older version of Oracle and try again.

description: break received on communication channel
cause: A break was processed on the communications channel, but was not properly handled by Net8 software. This is an internal error message not usually issued.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: a server linked as single-task cannot use SQL*Net
cause: A statement containing a SQL*Net connect string was issued to the single-task server. For example, a database link was used in a SQL statement.
action: Do not use SQL*Net connect strings in a single-task environment.

description: end-of-file on communication channel
cause: The connection between the Client and Server process was broken. The cause may be that the database instance experienced a maintenance or unplanned outage, or that the Server process had a fatal error, or that the network connection was interrupted.
action: Check the alert log of the database instance to see if a planned or unplanned outage occurred. Check the alert log to see if a process termination (ORA-07445, kill, or ORA-00600) occurred. Check for network problems and review the SQL*Net setup. After the problem is identified and resolved, retry the operation.
remediation: 1) This is a symptom: the server process went away. It is never the root cause, so do not tune the network until the alert log is ruled out. `SELECT value FROM v$diag_info WHERE name IN ('Diag Trace','Diag Alert');` 2) Look in the alert log at the exact timestamp for ORA-00600, ORA-07445, a process termination, or an instance crash. 3) Check the OS for the process being killed externally -- the Linux OOM killer in `dmesg` or /var/log/messages is a common cause under memory pressure. 4) If it happens only on idle connections after a fixed interval, it is a firewall or load-balancer idle timeout. Set `SQLNET.EXPIRE_TIME = 10` in the server sqlnet.ora and enable TCP keepalive. 5) If it reproduces with one specific statement, it is a server-side crash on that plan -- capture the incident (`adrci> show incident`) and open an SR. 6) Check for a killed session: `SELECT sid, serial#, status FROM v$session WHERE status = 'KILLED';` and review whether a resource manager plan or a DBA script is terminating sessions.

description: not connected to ORACLE
cause: The connection between the Client and Server process did not exist. This is likely the result of an earlier ORA-03113 error. The cause may be that the database instance experienced a maintenance or unplanned outage, or that the Server process had a fatal error, or that the network connection was interrupted.
action: Check the alert log of the database instance to see if a planned or unplanned outage occurred. Check the alert log to see if a process termination (ORA-07445, kill, or ORA-00600) occurred. Check for network problems and review the SQL*Net setup. After the problem is identified and resolved, retry the operation.

description: unsupported data type or representation was received from remote connection
cause: An unsupported data type was provided for this bind or define operation.
action: Upgrade to the latest client and server versions.

description: invalid buffer length passed to a conversion routine
cause: This is an internal error message not usually issued.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: memory to save variables in two-task buffer has overflowed
cause: This is an internal error message that is not usually issued.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: two-task coroutine has invalid state
cause: This is an internal error message that is not usually issued.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: two-task detected inconsistent data type specification
cause: There was both a data type, and an anonymous data type declaration found.
action: Correct the specification.

description: two-task conversion routine: integer overflow
cause: An integer value in an internal Oracle structure overflowed when being sent or received over a heterogeneous connection. This can happen when an invalid buffer length or too great a row count is specified. It usually indicates a bug in the user application.
action: Check parameters to Oracle calls. If the problem recurs, reduce all integer parameters, column values not included, to less than 32767.

description: no interface driver connected - function not performed
cause: This message occurred usually because the Net8 driver was not loaded into memory or there was a mismatch of the version of the driver. A user program linked with an obsolete library may also cause this message. Only programs provided by Oracle Corporation should use this interface.
action: If the message occurred during use of a program provided by Oracle Corporation, contact Oracle Support Services. If a user program caused the message, relink the program with current versions of the Oracle libraries.

description: attempt to close ORACLE-side window on user side
cause: This is an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: current operation is still executing in non-blocking mode
cause: This is a status code that indicates that the operation cannot complete now.
action: This is not an error. The operation should be retried again for completion.

description: two-task internal error
cause: Internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: client-server protocol violation
cause: The application received a bad escape sequence from the server and may indicate a problem with the client application user code.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: network driver does not support non-blocking operations
cause: A non-blocking operation was attempted and the network driver does not support non-blocking operations.
action: Use default blocking operations or use a driver supporting non-blocking operations.

description: no new operations allowed until the active operation ends
cause: An attempt was made to execute a new operation before the active non-blocking operation completed or a new operation was attempted before all the pieces of a column were inserted or fetched.
action: Execute the new operation after the non-blocking operation completes. If piecewise binds/defines were done, execute the new operation after all the pieces have been inserted or fetched.

description: connection is in blocking mode
cause: The OCI test for non-blocking mode on a connection indicates that the connection is in blocking mode.
action: If non-blocking mode is required use appropriate OCI calls to change the mode.

description: the next piece to be inserted is required
cause: The application performed a piecewise bind on a column.
action: Provide the next piece of this bind variable.

description: the buffer for the next piece to be fetched is required
cause: The application performed a piecewise define on the column.
action: Provide the next buffer for the next piece to be retrieved.

description: an invalid buffer was provided for the next piece
cause: The application either provided the length of the buffer for the next piece to be zero or provided a null pointer.
action: Verify if the buffer pointer for the next piece is null or if the length is zero.

description: two-task default value overflow
cause: The default value specified for a record field was too large.
action: Change the default value to fit the field size.

description: Piggyback function casued error.
cause: Piggyback function has returned an error.
action: Check, edit, and retry the piggyback function.

description: Connections to this server version are no longer supported.
cause: An unsupported connection attempt was made to an Oracle server of an older version.
action: See Oracle Database documentation for additional information.

description: connection lost contact
cause: 1) Server unexpectedly terminated or was forced to terminate. 2) Server timed out the connection.
action: 1) Check if the server session was terminated. 2) Check if the timeout parameters are set properly in sqlnet.ora.

description: inbound connection timed out
cause: The inbound connection was timed out by the server because user authentication did not complete within the time specified by SQLNET.INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT or its default value.
action: 1) Check the SQL*NET and RDBMS logs for traces of suspicious connections. 2) Configure SQL*NET with a larger value for the SQLNET.INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT parameter, if necessary.
remediation: 1) Authentication did not complete inside the timeout. Check both settings: SQLNET.INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT in the server sqlnet.ora (default 60s) and INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_<listener> in listener.ora. 2) Check the listener log for the source host -- repeated entries from one address are often a port scanner or a health check that opens a socket and never authenticates. 3) If authentication is genuinely slow (LDAP, Kerberos, a loaded host), raise both values rather than disabling them; setting either to 0 removes protection against connection-exhaustion attacks. 4) Check host load and whether the listener is starved: a CPU-saturated host produces this under load. 5) Correlate with ORA-00020 -- an instance at its process limit makes authentication hang long enough to hit the timeout.

description: malformed TTC packet from client rejected: [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s] [%s]
cause: A malformed TTC (Two-Task Common) packet was received from the client.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: connection terminated due to security policy violation
cause: The connection was terminated due to a security policy violation.
action: Contact the database administrator.

description: This OCI call has been disabled by the DBA
cause: The SEC_DISABLE_OLDER_ORACLE_RPCS initialization parameter was enabled.
action: Contact the Database Administrator

description: I/O operation in progress
cause: The current I/O operation was not complete. The error is typically returned from vectored and/or asynchronous I/O calls.
action: Perform the necessary operation to complete or abort the current I/O.

description: I/O request queue full
cause: The I/O request queue was full and no more requests could be queued.
action: Perform the proper operations to complete part or all of the current in-progress I/O requests.

description: Session ID: %ld Serial number: %ld
cause: Connection was lost for the specified session and serial number. This is either due to session being killed or network problems.
action: Reconnect and if error persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Process ID: %s Thread ID: %s
cause: Connection was lost for the specified process ID and thread ID. This is either due to session being killed or network problems.
action: Reconnect and if error persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Process ID: %s
cause: Connection was lost for the specified process ID. This is either due to session being killed or network problems.
action: Reconnect and if error persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: I/O streaming direction error
cause: Attempted to PUT data when GET streaming was in progress or attempted to GET data when PUT streaming was in progress.
action: Complete current stream read or write I/O before attempting I/O in reverse direction.

description: invalid buffer length for TTC field
cause: A malformed TTC (Two-Task Common) packet was received.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: missing mandatory TTC field
cause: A malformed TTC (Two-Task Common) packet was received.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: OCI_ATTR_ROW_COUNT cannot return a row count exceeding UB4MAXVAL. The actual row count is [%s]
cause: The row count was larger than UB4MAXVAL. OCI clients using OCI_ATTR_ROW_COUNT cannot see row counts larger than UB4MAXVAL.
action: Upgrade Oracle client to version 12 client libraries or higher and use OCI_ATTR_UB8_ROW_COUNT instead.

description: invalid Oracle error code
cause: An invalid Oracle error code was received by the server.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: end-of-file on communication channel for database link
cause: The connection between the client and the remote server process was broken.
action: Look in the alert.log file of the remote server for any errors. Also, check to see whether the remote server process is dead and whether a trace file was generated at failure time.

description: schema name length exceeding UB1MAXVAL
cause: The schema name length was larger than UB1MAXVAL, and clients older than Release 12.2 were unable to process longer names.
action: Upgrade the client to Release 12.2 or higher.

description: object name length exceeding UB1MAXVAL
cause: The object name length was larger than UB1MAXVAL, and clients older than Release 12.2 wree unable to process longer names.
action: Upgrade the client to Release 12.2 or higher.

description: column name length exceeding UB1MAXVAL
cause: The column name length was larger than UB1MAXVAL, and clients older than Release 12.2 were unable to process longer names.
action: Upgrade the client to Release 12.2 or higher.

description: Deprecated TTC operation is disallowed.
cause: A Deprecated Two-Task Common (TTC) remote procedural call (RPC) was invoked.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services for further assistance.

description: SQL statement not supported for remote execution
cause: Statement execution could not proceed because the rewritten statement that was issued to the remote had a different ordering (or number) of bind variables as compared to the original statement issued locally.
action: Rewrite the statement issued locally to more closely match the rewritten statement issued to the remote (especially in terms of order and number of bind variables). Contact Oracle Support Services for further assistance.

description: OCI call timed out
cause: The OCI call was timed out because it was not completed within the timeout specified by OCI_ATTR_CALL_TIMEOUT.
action: Check the current value of OCI_ATTR_CALL_TIMEOUT and increase it to an appropriate value.

description: An invalid client operation was requested by the server
cause: You are using an Oracle client application linked with libraries with lower version than the current server version.
action: Upgrade client libraries to be same as or higher than the server version.

description: illegal target ID (%s) in multi-target database link name (%s)
cause: The target ID in the multi-target database link name was either non-numeric or its value was greater than UB4MAXVAL.
action: Fix the target ID in the multi-target database link name to be numeric and at most UB4MAXVAL.

description: %s: must appear in the GROUP BY clause or be used in an aggregate function as 'group_by_position_enabled' is FALSE
cause: The specified expression is not part of either the GROUP BY clause, an aggregate function, or a constant but appears in a part of the query that is processed after the GROUP BY clause, such as the SELECT clause, the ORDER BY clause, or the HAVING clause. Because group by position is disabled by default, the integer number in the GROUP BY clause is not treated as the position of an expression in the SELECT list.
action: Either add the expression to the GROUP BY clause or enable group by position and add the position of the expression in the GROUP BY clause. Ensure that any columns in the SELECT list that are not part of an aggregate function are present in the GROUP BY clause. Ensure parameter 'group_by_position_enabled' is set to TRUE if the integer number in the GROUP BY clause is intended as the position of an expression in the SELECT list.
params: 1) expression: The expression that is missing from the GROUP BY clause.

description: data mining analytic function is not allowed inside SQL MODEL clause
cause: A data mining analytic function is used inside SQL MODEL clause.
action: Do not use data mining function inside SQL MODEL clause.

description: deadlocked on readable physical standby (undo segment %s)
cause: A new undo segment was added. A query can occasionally deadlock when issued around the time an undo segment is added and used immediately on the primary.
action: Retry the query. Avoid creating new undo segments when using standby as a regular part of operation.

description: Recovery was terminated during query execution
cause: Recovery was terminated. A query can occasionally deadlock when recovery is terminated because it needs a block with changes that are made after the point at which recovery was terminated.
action: Retry the query. Avoid cancelling recovery on standby.

description: STANDBY_MAX_DATA_DELAY of %s seconds exceeded
cause: Standby recovery fell behind the STANDBY_MAX_DATA_DELAY requirement.
action: Tune recovery and retry the query later, or switch to another standby database within the data delay requirement.

description: Standby may not be synced with primary
cause: ALTER SESSION SYNC WITH PRIMARY did not work because either the standby was not synchronous or in a data-loss mode with regard to the primary, or the standby recovery was terminated.
action: Make the standby synchronous and no-data-loss with regard to the primary. Make the standby recovery active.

description: STANDBY_MAX_DATA_DELAY does not apply to SYS users
cause: ALTER SESSION SET STANDBY_MAX_DATA_DELAY did not work for SYS users.
action: Issue ALTER SESSION SET STANDBY_MAX_DATA_DELAY for non-SYS users.

description: parameter %s mismatch
cause: The value of the %s parameter was not the same in all instances.
action: Check %s in all instances.

description: %s only works on an open physical or logical standby database
cause: The database was not an open physical or logical standby database.
action: Issue the command on an open physical or logical standby database.

description: enable read-only violation logging
cause: NA
action: NA

description: duplicate SESSION or GLOBAL specifications
cause: Duplicate SESSION or GLOBAL specifications were specified.
action: Remove the duplicate specification.

description: NOCACHE or ORDER sequences cannot be accessed from Active Data Guard standby
cause: NOCACHE or ORDER sequences were not supported for Active Data Guard standby.
action: Alter the sequence properties.

description: Sequence values cannot be allocated for Oracle Active Data Guard standby or at True Cache.
cause: Connection to the primary database failed. The primary database might be down.
action: Verify that the primary database is up and retry.

description: The sequence %s.%s on the Oracle Active Data Guard primary database is no longer accessible.
cause: The Oracle Active Data Guard standby database tried to access the referenced sequence on the primary database and found it was no longer accessible. This can happen when the sequence on the primary database is dropped, or its access permissions have changed.
action: Check the sequence and its status on the primary database. Ensure that it exists and is accessible.
params: 1) schema_name: The schema in which the sequence resides. 2) sequence_name: The sequence name.

description: The sequence object is no longer a global sequence for the Oracle Active Data Guard standby database.
cause: The sequence object might have been altered by the primary database.
action: Check the sequence status on the primary database.
