action: Verify the specified option.

description: cannot use tablespace %s for partition %s
cause: At attempt was made to specify a tablespace that was used for a different chunk or partition in the tables already created.
action: Verify the specified option.

description: cannot purge an individual chunk tablespace
cause: An attempt was made to purge an individual chunk tablespace which is a part of a tablespace set.
action: Verify the specified option.

description: The creation of Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) policy is not supported for duplicated tables.
cause: An invalid option was specified while creating duplicated tables.
action: Verify the specified option.

description: invalid partition set value
cause: The attempt to update or insert into a partition set column failed.
action: Ensure that inserted partition set values are within the shard partition set values.

description: invalid number of partitions specified for the child table
cause: An attempt was made to create a child table with a number of partitions not equal to the number of partitions in the parent table.
action: Create the child table with a number of partitions that equal the number of partitions in the parent table.

description: invalid list value or values specified for the partition %s
cause: The list values specified for a partition of the table could not exactly be matched with the list values of the corresponding partition of the parent table.
action: Create the child table with the list values of a partition that matches the list values of the corresponding partition in the parent table.

description: invalid range value specified for the partition %s
cause: The range value specified for a partition of the table could not be matched with the range value of the corresponding partition of the parent table.
action: Create the child table with the range values of a partition that match the range values of the corresponding partition in the parent table.

description: invalid number of list values specified for the partition %s
cause: The number of list values specified for a partition of the table was not equal to the number of list values specified for the corresponding partition of the parent table.
action: Create the child table with partitions that have the same number of list values as the corresponding partition in the parent table.

description: invalid range or list value specified for the partitionset %s
cause: The value specified for the range or list of the partitionset did not exactly match the value specified for the partitionset in the parent table.
action: Create the child table with partitionsets whose values for range or list exactly matches the values specified for the partitionset in the parent table.

description: cannot drop a tablespace set used for a composite sharded table
cause: The tablespace was used for a composite sharded table and cannot be dropped unless the contents are dropped manually.
action: Drop the contents of the tablespace set first and then drop the tablespace set.

description: cannot alter a user-defined sharded table directly in the shard database
cause: An attempt was made to alter a user-defined sharded table directly on the shard database.
action: All alter operations on a user-defined sharded table must be executed on the catalog database to maintain consistency in the shards.

description: duplicate partitionset name
cause: Name of a partitionset of a table being created is not unique.
action: rename partitionset(s) to ensure that their names are unique among partitionsets of the table being created.

description: DEFAULT tablespace is not supported for sharded tables or indexes.
cause: An attempt was made to use DEFAULT tablespaces for sharded tables or indexes.
action: Use valid tablespace or tablespace set names for sharded tables and indexes on sharded tables.

description: invalid use of STORE IN clause for a sharded table or index
cause: The STORE IN (tablespace list) clause was used to specify tablespaces for partitions of a sharded table or for partitions of an index where the sharded table did not have subpartitions or the subpartition method was not hash.
action: Use the TABLESPACE SET clause or SUBPARTITION TEMPLATE clause to specify tablespaces for table and index partitions or table subpartitions, respectively.

description: Invalid attempt to add a Sharding Raft replication unit to an active transaction (dml_statement = %s, ru_id = %s, allocated_ru = %s)
cause: Sharding Raft replication determines the number of replication units allocated for your transaction when the transaction begins. Adding a new replication unit to the Oracle instance while your transaction is active may exceed the number already allocated.
action: Add the replication unit to your Oracle instance before you begin your transaction, or commit the current transaction and begin a new one for the added replication unit.
params: 1) dml_statement: The type of DML statement being executed. 2) ru_id: The ID of the replication unit being added to the transaction. 3) allocated_ru: The number of replication units already allocated.

description: CREATE TABLE...AS SELECT statement is not supported for sharded tables.
cause: An attempt was made to create a sharded table AS SELECT from another table, which is not supported.
action: Do not create any sharded table AS SELECT from other tables.

description: Editions are not supported for sharded tables.
cause: An attempt was made to create a sharded table using editions, which is not supported.
action: Do not create any sharded table using editions.

description: maximum number of sharding columns for consistent hash is 15.
cause: The number of columns in a sharding key column list exceeded the legal limit of 15.
action: Modify the sharding key column list so that it consists of at most 15 columns.

description: cannot create the default shard tablespace on the catalog when shard DDL is enabled
cause: An attempt was made to create a tablespace in the catalog which is created on the shards by default in user-defined sharding.
action: Disable shard DDL on the catalog if the tablespace has to be created on the catalog.

description: An all-shard object cannot depend on any local objects.
cause: An attempt was made to create or alter an all-shard object to depend on a local user object, which is not allowed.
action: Do not create or alter an all-shard object to depend on any local user objects.

description: An all-shard index cannot be created on local tables.
cause: An attempt was made to create an all-shard index on a local user table, which is not allowed.
action: Do not create such indices.

description: A sharded table cannot have columns that depend on local objects.
cause: An attempt was made to create or alter a sharded table to contain columns that depend on local objects, which is not allowed.
action: Do not create or alter sharded tables to have such columns.

description: cannot use a sharded tablespace for non-sharding purposes
cause: An attempt was made to use a sharded tablespace for non-sharding purposes.
action: Use a normal tablespace instead of a sharded tablespace.

description: The creation of Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) policy is not supported for duplicated tables.
cause: An invalid option was specified while altering duplicated tables.
action: Verify the specified option.

description: cannot create duplicated tables on a shard database
cause: An attempt was made to create a duplicated table on a shard database, which is not supported.
action: Connect to each shard and create the table locally.

description: cannot specify a data file name for a tablespace in a sharding setup
cause: The data file name was specified during creation of the tablespace. Only Oracle Managed Files are supported by a tablespace used in a sharding setup.
action: Remove the file name from the data file definition.

description: A trigger cannot be created on any sharded table.
cause: An attempt was made to create a trigger on a sharded table, which is not allowed.
action: Do not create such triggers.

description: A shard key or partition set key column cannot be a sequence.
cause: An attempt was made to create a sharded table having a shard key or a partition set key column based on a sequence, which is not allowed.
action: Do not use sequences for shard key or partition set key columns.

description: cannot create temporary tablespace sets
cause: An attempt was made to create a temporary tablespace set, which is not allowed.
action: Do not create temporary tablespace sets.

description: zone maps are not supported on sharded tables
cause: An attempt was made to create a materialized zone map on a sharded table, which is not supported.
action: Do not create materialized zone maps on sharded tables.

description: cannot specify PARENT clause for duplicated tables
cause: An invalid option was specified while creating duplicated tables.
action: Verify the specified option.

description: Cannot perform the operation on the child table before performing the same operation on the root table
cause: An attempt was made to alter the child table to add or drop or split a partition whose root partition has not been added or dropped or split yet.
action: Alter the root table to add or drop or split the partition before trying to add or drop or split the partition in the child table.

description: Operation is not supported on a user-defined sharded table
cause: An attempt was made to perform an unsupported partition operation on a user-defined sharded table.
action: Do not perform the operation.

description: cannot create an autolist or interval partitioned sharded table
cause: An attempt was made to create an autolist or interval partitioned sharded table.
action: Create a sharded table that is not an autolist or interval partitioned.

description: A DEFAULT partition or partition set cannot be specified for a sharded table.
cause: An attempt was made to create a partition or partition set with a DEFAULT high value on a sharded table.
action: Do not create a partition or partition set with a DEFAULT high value.

description: password is required for encrypted columns in a sharded table
cause: An attempt was made to create a sharded table containing an encrypted column without specifying a password.
action: Provide a password for the encrypted column(s) in the CREATE

description: GoldenGate error: %s
cause: An operation failed when performed using Oracle GoldenGate.
action: Correct the error specified in Oracle GoldenGate output.

description: Invalid OGG service descriptor - OGG message: %s
cause: One or more components of the Oracle GoldenGate (OGG) service descriptor could not be verified.
action: Refer to the Oracle GoldenGate message for the required action.

description: OGG %s URI: %s is not reachable - HTTP message: %s
cause: Oracle GoldenGate (OGG) AdminService or DistributionService could not be reached.
action: Refer to the HTTP message for the required action.

description: OGG %s URI: %s failed to %s %s: %s - OGG message: %s
cause: Oracle GoldenGate (OGG) AdminService or DistributionService operation failed.
action: Refer to the Oracle GoldenGate message for the required action.

description: OGG sharding function called in an invalid context: %s function called in %s
cause: Internal error. An Oracle GoldenGate (OGG) sharding functionality was called in an invalid context, for example, catalog function in shard or vice versa.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Invalid combination of OGG deployment parameters specified for shardgroup: %s (S=%s, C=%s, R=%s)
cause: The values specified for Oracle GoldenGate (OGG) deployment parameters (number of shards - S, number of chunks - C and replication factor - R) for the shardgroup were not compatible with each other.
action: Ensure that the following invariants hold for the shardgroup: number of chunks >= number of shards number of shards >= replication factor

description: Invalid entry in the OGG command payload: %s
cause: Internal error. The payload for Oracle GoldenGate (OGG) command sent from the sharding catalog to the shard database contained an invalid entry.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Sharding configuration parameter '%s' is not set in the shard database.
cause: Internal error. A database initialization parameter required by the shard database was not set during deployment.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Failure to remove shard: %s - %s
cause: A request to remove a shard database failed.
action: Check the shard error message for details.

description: chunk allocation error in shardgroup: %s - %s
cause: Internal error. Chunk allocation algorithm for Oracle GoldenGate (OGG) detected inconsistencies in the sharding configuration.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Chunk number '%s' already exists on the target shard.
cause: An invalid chunk number or target shard name was provided.
action: Check the chunk number, shard name and try again.

description: A move chunk request already exists for chunk number '%s' from the source shard.
cause: An invalid chunk number or source shard name was provided.
action: Check the chunk number, shard name and try again.

description: invalid SPLIT PARTITION command for a user-defined sharded object
cause: Tablespaces for resulting partitions in a SPLIT PARTITION command were either unspecified or in use.
action: An unused tablespace should be provided for each resulting partition of the SPLIT PARTITION command.

description: Sharding Raft replication does not support XA transactions (statement = %s, XA ID = %s, branch = %s).
cause: Sharding Raft replication only supports Oracle-managed local or Oracle-managed distributed transactions. Using an XA transaction is not supported.
action: Replace the use of the XA transaction management with the default Oracle transaction management.
params: 1) statement: The type of DML statement being executed. 2) XA transaction ID: The global XA transaction ID. 3) XA branch: The type of XA transaction branch (local or remote).

description: updated or deleted row of duplicated table is not synchronized with catalog
cause: An attempt was made to update or delete the row of a duplicated table that was recently inserted on this shard database. This table did not have primary key; therefore, any modifications of the inserted row cannot be performed until after the next duplicated table refresh (the default timeout is 1 minute).
action: Wait until the duplicated table is refreshed and repeat the operation.

description: updated or deleted row of duplicated table is not found on catalog
cause: An attempt was made to update or delete the row of a materialized view on a shard database but the materialized view was not synchronized with the catalog and the affected rows were already deleted from the catalog by another shard database.
action: Wait until the duplicated table is refreshed and repeat the operation.

description: cannot alter duplicated table materialized views on shards
cause: An attempt was made to manually alter materialized views of a duplicated table on shard databases.
action: Alter the duplicated table on the catalog database, if required.

description: failed to rename the materialized view log when renaming duplicated table
cause: An attempt was made to rename the duplicated table, and the internal statement to rename the materialized view log failed.
action: Drop the duplicated table, and re-create it.

description: Invisible column is not supported for duplicated tables.
cause: An invalid option was specified while creating duplicated tables.
action: Verify the specified option.

description: failed to rename the index on materialized view when renaming duplicated table
cause: An attempt was made to rename the duplicated table, and the internal statement to rename the index on materialized view failed.
action: Drop the duplicated table, and re-create it.

description: Cannot continue transaction (statement %s) on leader shard after replication unit %s term changed from term %s to term %s
cause: A replication unit RAFT term was changed since the transaction started. This can happen if the replication unit leader on the current shard was re-elected sometime during the current transaction.
action: Retry the full transaction in the leader shard for this replication unit.

description: Latch-free queue reached it's peak size
cause: The size of LFQ buffer needed by foreground process reached maximum.
action: Increase LFQ buffer size setting.

description: The passed DDL with ID %s is invalid.
cause: The passed DDL was not valid.
action: Validate the DDL against the catalog database.

description: Sync point for Barrier DDL with ID %s on %s.%s timed out after waiting %s seconds for the replication units %s
cause: The sync point for DDL statement failed or timed out on a replication unit follower shard that was waiting for a leader shard to send a DDL completion message.
action: Ensure that all database shards for a given replication unit are running with minimal disruptions when executing DDL.

description: cannot perform DML operations during switchover to shard %s for replication unit %s
cause: This shard received a switchover request.
action: Retry the user DML operations in the leader shard for this replication unit after switchover.

description: invalid replication unit specified: %s
cause: The specified replication unit did not exist, no shards containing the replication unit were available, the database specified did not contain the replication unit, or the replication unit specified conflicted with the value of another parameter.
action: Retry the command with a valid replication unit specified.

description: 'move chunk' and 'alter move' commands not supported with Raft replication
cause: A 'move chunk' or 'alter move' command was issued against a sharding catalog that was configured for Raft replication.
action: Use 'relocate chunk' instead of 'move chunk' and use 'alter task' instead of 'alter move' for configurations using Raft replication.

description: the number of shards in a shardgroup must not be less than its replication factor
cause: A deployment was attempted where the number of shards in a shardgroup was less than the replication factor for that shardgroup.
action: Add more shards to the shardgroup or decrease the configured replication factor and retry the deployment.

description: command not supported with the current replication configuration
cause: A command was issued that was incompatible with the current replication configuration in use for the sharded database.
action: Only run compatible commands applicable to the current replication configuration (DataGuard, Raft replication, GoldenGate).

description: shard name parameter values must be unique
cause: A command was issued that specified the same shard name for multiple parameters.
action: Validate parameter values and retry command.

description: shard %s is the leader for replication unit %s
cause: The specified shard was the leader for the given replication unit.
action: Validate parameter values and retry command.

description: shard %s is not a follower for replication unit %s
cause: The specified shard was not a follower for the given replication unit.
action: Validate parameter values and retry command.

description: invalid number of replicas
cause: The specified command created more replicas than were allowed by the current replication factor setting.
action: Remove an existing replica and retry the command.

description: shard %s already contains replication unit %s
cause: The specified shard already contained the given replication unit.
action: Validate parameter values and retry command.

description: shard %s does not contain replication unit %s
cause: The specified shard does not contain the specified replication unit.
action: Validate that the replication unit exists in this shard and retry the command.

description: replication units %s and %s are not collocated
cause: The specified replication units were not located on the same set of shards or did not have the same leader.
action: Validate parameter values and replication topology then retry command.

description: Switchover process has been started
cause: Replication unit switchover information message.
action: NA

description: Switchover process completed
cause: Replication unit switchover information message.
action: NA

description: Shutdown of apply process group
cause: Replication unit copy and move information message.
action: NA

description: no available source replica found in replication unit %s
cause: A source replica was not specified in the copy command and a valid replica could not be found to act as the source replica.
action: Specify a valid follower replica using the -source parameter.

description: Target shard does not recognize caller %s as a peer for replication unit %s.
cause: Replication unit inter-communication was attempted between non-peer shards.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Sharding capture does not support "%s"."%s" because of the following reason: %s
cause: Sharding capture encountered a table with an unsupported property. The most common reason is an unsupported column data type.
action: Do not include this table in a sharding Raft replication configuration. Alternatively, remove the unsupported property.

description: background tasks are pending
cause: Background tasks were pending when the command was issued.
action: Monitor the completion of the background tasks using the GDSCTL 'config task' command. After all tasks are completed or after cancelling the tasks with the GDSCTL 'alter task' command, retry the original command.

description: opaque column type not supported
cause: A column with opaque column type, such as XMLType or AnyData, exists for the given table.
action: Remove the relevant column and retry the operation.

description: failed to block DML on %s.%s for Barrier DDL with ID %s (root cause error = %s)
cause: Long running DML transactions blocked the DDL execution on shard.
action: Retry the DDL or recover shard when DML transaction load is less.

description: shard %s is not available
cause: The specified shard was not available because it was shut down or was unreachable from the catalog database.
action: Validate the state of the shard and retry the command. Alternately, if attempting an incremental deployment, use the '-no_rebalance' option on the GDSCTL 'deploy' command to allow deployment while shards are not available.

description: cannot perform %s operations during recovery of the leader for replication unit %s
cause: Recovery of the replication log was in progress for this shard.
action: Retry the user DML operations after the recovery completes.

description: DML statement failed because a column or table is currently being used in a Barrier DDL statement with ID %s.
cause: Cannot perform DML on the column or table currently being used by Barrier DDL. In sharding replication setup, DMLs affecting the columns involved in a Barrier DDL statement are restricted until the DDL has completed.
action: Retry the DML operations after the barrier DDL statement completes.

description: SNR peer closure error
cause: Internal.
action: Internal.

description: bad digest when calling an internal procedure
cause: An internal procedure was passed a bad digest.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: the sum of PCTUSED and PCTFREE cannot exceed 100
cause: the sum of PCTUSED and PCTFREE for a cluster or table exceeds 100
action: create the table/cluster specifying values whose sum is <= 100

description: SEQUENCE parameter %s must be an integer.
cause: The specified SEQUENCE parameter was not an integer.
action: Create the SEQUENCE specifying an integer value for the parameter.

description: INCREMENT is not a positive integer.
cause: The specified increment sequence integer value was zero.
action: Specify a positive integer value for INCREMENT.

description: sequence parameter %s exceeds maximum size allowed (%s digits)
cause: %s (a sequencer parameter) had too many digits
action: specify the parameter with the allowed number of digits

description: The MINVALUE integer value is not less than the MAXVALUE integer value.
cause: The specified minimum value was greater than or equal to the specified maximum value.
action: Specify an integer for the MINVALUE that is less than the integer for the MAXVALUE.

description: The INCREMENT must be less than the MAXVALUE minus MINVALUE.
cause: The specified INCREMENT integer value was either greater than or equal to the difference between the MAXVALUE integer value and the MINVALUE integer value.
action: Specify an INCREMENT integer value that is less than the difference between the MAXVALUE integer value and the MINVALUE integer value.

description: START WITH cannot be less than MINVALUE
cause: the given starting value is less than MINVALUE
action: make sure that the starting value is >= MINVALUE

description: MINVALUE cannot exceed the current value
cause: The given MINVALUE was greater than the current value.
action: Ensure that the MINVALUE is less than or equal to the current value.

description: START WITH cannot be greater than MAXVALUE
cause: The starting value was greater than the MAXVALUE.
action: Ensure that the starting value is less than the MAXVALUE.

description: MAXVALUE cannot be made to be less than the current value
cause: the current value exceeds the given MAXVALUE
action: make sure that the new MAXVALUE is larger than the current value

description: the number of values to CACHE must be greater than 1
cause: The value in the CACHE clause was one.
action: Either specify NOCACHE, or provide a value greater than one.

description: Sequence %s must be in the range of %s and %s.
cause: The value specified for one of the sequence parameters exceeded the limits.
action: Specify parameters within the indicated range and retry the operation.

description: object is not a sequence
cause: the object specified cannot have sequence ddl's performed on it
action: re-enter the statement being careful with the spelling of the name

description: The CACHE value may not exceed the CYCLE value.
cause: Specified CACHE value exceeded the CYCLE value.
action: Reduce the CACHE value, increase the CYCLE value, or do both.

description: MINVALUE must be specified for cycling descending sequences
cause: The wrap value was not specified for the sequences that cycle.
action: Re-create the sequence, specifying a MINVALUE.

description: MAXVALUE must be specified for ascending sequences that cycle.
cause: The MAXVALUE was not specified for this ascending SEQUENCE that was created with the CYCLE option.
action: Re-create the SEQUENCE and specify a MAXVALUE for sequences that use the CYCLE option.

description: Sequence %s no longer exists.
cause: The sequence was dropped while processing its next value.
action: Re-create the sequence.

description: invalid value %s (length = %s) for parameter MAX_DUMP_FILE_SIZE
cause: The string supplied for the parameter MAX_DUMP_FILE_SIZE was not an integer, an integer followed by 'K', 'M', or 'G', nor the special value UNLIMITED.
action: Provide a proper value for this parameter.

description: The '%s' parameter cannot be altered in Oracle Database Standard Edition or Oracle Database Free version.
cause: An attempt was made to alter the specified parameter in the Standard Edition or Free version.
action: Do not attempt to alter the parameter in the Standard Edition or Free version.

description: deadlock detected while trying to lock object %s%s%s%s%s
cause: While trying to lock a library object, a deadlock is detected.
action: Retry the operation later.
remediation: 1) This is a library cache (DDL) deadlock, not a row-level one. Find what holds the object: `SELECT s.sid, s.serial#, s.username, s.program, d.name, d.type, d.mode_held, d.mode_requested FROM dba_ddl_locks d JOIN v$session s ON s.sid = d.session_id WHERE d.name = UPPER('<object>');` 2) The usual trigger is a package being recompiled while sessions are executing it, or two sessions compiling interdependent objects at once. 3) Terminate the holder if the compile must proceed: `ALTER SYSTEM KILL SESSION '<sid>,<serial#>' IMMEDIATE;` 4) Serialize deployments: recompile in a maintenance window, or use `utlrp.sql` when the application is quiesced. 5) Edition-Based Redefinition avoids this class of error entirely for online code changes.

description: timeout occurred while waiting to lock object %s%s%s%s%s
cause: While waiting to lock a library object, a timeout occurred.
action: Retry the operation later.
remediation: 1) Same cause as ORA-04020 but surfaced as a timeout. Identify the holder with dba_ddl_locks as above. 2) `SELECT sid, event, seconds_in_wait, p1, p2 FROM v$session WHERE event LIKE 'library cache%';` 3) Kill the blocking session or retry once it finishes. 4) If a long-running job holds the object for hours, the fix is scheduling, not a longer timeout.

description: nowait requested, but had to wait to lock dictionary object
cause: Had to wait to lock a library object during a nowait request.
action: Retry the operation later.

description: Object %s%s%s%s%s could not be validated or authorized
cause: A number of attempts were made to validate or authorize an object but failed.
action: Please report this error to Oracle Support Services.

description: self-deadlock detected while trying to mutex pin cursor %s
cause: While trying to mutex pin a cursor, a self-deadlock is detected.
action: Retry the operation later.

description: maximum allowed library object lock allocated for %s%s%s%s%s
cause: Too many active locks for the object has been allocated. This error can be a result of too many cursors kept open per session.
action: Close cursors, reduce session_cached_cursors value.

description: %d is an invalid library cache namespace
cause: Passed in namespace value is invalid and violates protocol.
action: Pass correct namespace value.

description: self-deadlock during automatic validation for object %s.%s
cause: An attempt was made to validate an invalidated object but it failed because of a self-deadlock.
action: Identify the root cause of the self-deadlock and take corrective action, e.g. compile the invalidated object separately.

description: cannot generate diana for object %s%s%s%s%s
cause: Cannot generate diana for an object because of lock conflict.
action: Please report this error to your support representative.

description: error ORA-%s occurred when querying %s%s%s
cause: The table or view being queried might be missing. The error number indicates the error.
action: Fix the error.

description: out of process memory
cause: Operating system memory was exhausted or a per-process limit on private memory usage was reached. The database has an internal limit of 32 GB per Oracle process.
action: Check the use of memory by other Oracle instances and other applications. Exceeding 32 GB in a single process may indicate a memory leak. Consider reducing the size of shared memory to allow more room for private memory.
remediation: 1) This is process-private memory (PGA), not the SGA. Check the instance total: `SELECT name, value/1024/1024 mb FROM v$pgastat WHERE name IN ('total PGA allocated','total PGA inuse','aggregate PGA target parameter','over allocation count');` 2) Find the consuming process: `SELECT s.sid, s.username, s.program, p.pga_used_mem/1024/1024 used_mb, p.pga_max_mem/1024/1024 max_mb FROM v$process p JOIN v$session s ON s.paddr = p.addr ORDER BY p.pga_max_mem DESC FETCH FIRST 20 ROWS ONLY;` 3) Check the OS before the database: free RAM, swap, and the per-process address-space limit (`ulimit -v`, `ulimit -s`) for the oracle user. On Linux also check vm.max_map_count and any cgroup memory limit. 4) The usual application cause is an unbounded BULK COLLECT or a PL/SQL collection built in memory -- add a `LIMIT` clause and process in batches. 5) Raise pga_aggregate_target only if the host genuinely has the memory: `ALTER SYSTEM SET pga_aggregate_target = <n>G SCOPE=BOTH;` 6) Note that pga_aggregate_target is a target, not a cap -- PGA can exceed it, which is why the host runs out before the parameter does.

description: out of shared memory in %s
cause: More shared memory was needed than was available.
action: If using one of the initialization parameters SGA_TARGET, MEMORY_SIZE, or MEMORY_TARGET, increase the value of that parameter. If it is not feasible to increase the parameter, then reduce the value of DB_CACHE_SIZE (if set). If you are not using SGA_TARGET, MEMORY_SIZE, or MEMORY_TARGET, increase the size of the pool that is out of memory. For example, increase SHARED_POOL_SIZE for the shared pool or INMEMORY_SIZE for an IMC heap.
remediation: 1) This is shared memory (SGA). See where it went: `SELECT pool, name, bytes/1024/1024 mb FROM v$sgastat WHERE pool = 'shared pool' ORDER BY bytes DESC FETCH FIRST 20 ROWS ONLY;` 2) The dominant cause is literal SQL flooding the library cache. Confirm it: `SELECT force_matching_signature, COUNT(*) versions, MIN(sql_text) sample FROM v$sql WHERE force_matching_signature <> 0 GROUP BY force_matching_signature HAVING COUNT(*) > 50 ORDER BY versions DESC;` Hundreds of near-identical statements means the application is not using bind variables. 3) The correct fix is bind variables in the application. `ALTER SYSTEM SET cursor_sharing = FORCE;` is a stopgap that has its own plan-stability costs. 4) Also check for high version counts on a single statement: `SELECT sql_id, version_count FROM v$sqlarea WHERE version_count > 50 ORDER BY version_count DESC;` then `SELECT * FROM v$sql_shared_cursor WHERE sql_id = '<id>';` to see why cursors are not being shared. 5) Size the pool: `SELECT shared_pool_size_for_estimate mb, estd_lc_time_saved FROM v$shared_pool_advice;` then raise sga_target or shared_pool_size if the advisory shows benefit. 6) `ALTER SYSTEM FLUSH SHARED_POOL;` is emergency relief only -- expect a hard-parse storm immediately after, and it does nothing about the cause.

description: PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET must be non-zero when WORKAREA_SIZE_POLICY in auto mode.
cause: An attempt was made to set WORKAREA_SIZE_POLICY to AUTO while PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET was not specified or attempt was made to set PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET to zero while WORKAREA_SIZE_POLICY was AUTO.
action: Before setting WORKAREA_SIZE_POLICY, set PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET to a value representing the total private memory available to the instance. This total is generally the total physical memory available in the system minus what is needed for the system global area (SGA) minus what is needed for the operating system (for example, 500MB).

description: Insufficient memory to grow pool
cause: The system had insufficient memory to grow the pool to the specified size.
action: Specify a smaller value to grow the pool.

description: unable to shrink pool to specified size
cause: The pool could not shrink to the specified size as it could not free memory.
action: Specify a larger value to which to shrink the pool to.

description: unable to allocate %s bytes of shared memory in shared object cache "%s" of size "%s"
cause: More shared memory is needed than was allocated in the shared object cache.
action: NA

description: PGA memory used by the instance or PDB exceeds PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT.
cause: Private memory across the instance or pluggable database (PDB) exceeded the limit specified in the PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT parameter. If the limit was reached when allocating from private memory used by more than one Oracle process (MGA or DGA), that process was interrupted. Otherwise, the largest sessions using Program Global Area (PGA) memory were interrupted to get under the limit.
action: Increase the PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT initialization parameter or reduce memory usage.
remediation: 1) The instance or PDB crossed pga_aggregate_limit and Oracle is terminating the largest PGA consumers to enforce it. `SHOW PARAMETER pga_aggregate` 2) Identify the consumers before raising anything: `SELECT s.sid, s.username, s.program, p.pga_used_mem/1024/1024 used_mb FROM v$process p JOIN v$session s ON s.paddr = p.addr ORDER BY p.pga_used_mem DESC FETCH FIRST 20 ROWS ONLY;` 3) `SELECT name, value/1024/1024 mb FROM v$pgastat WHERE name LIKE '%PGA%';` 4) Raise the limit only with RAM to back it: `ALTER SYSTEM SET pga_aggregate_limit = <n>G SCOPE=BOTH;` Setting it to 0 disables the protection and lets the host run out of memory instead -- do not. 5) In a CDB, the limit can be set per PDB; check whether one PDB is starving the rest. 6) Treat the underlying runaway SQL or PL/SQL as for ORA-04030.

description: unable to allocate memory on another instance in the cluster
cause: The instance ran out of memory as its allocated memory was less than the required memory.
action: Refer to the alert log for the instance which ran out of memory.

description: insufficient HugePages to grow System Global Area (SGA)
cause: The number of system configured HugePages was insufficient to grow the database System Global Area (SGA) to the specified size.
action: Specify a smaller value of System Global Area (SGA) target or increase the size of the HugePages.

description: package specification must be created first before creating package body
cause: Attempt to create a package body before creating its package specification.
action: Create the package specification first before creating the package body.

description: procedure, function, package, or package body does not exist
cause: An attempt was made to access a procedure, function, package, or package body that did not exist.
action: Ensure that the name is correct.

description: Object %s does not exist.
cause: An object name was specified that was not recognized by the system. There are several possible causes: - An invalid name for a table, view, sequence, procedure, function, package, or package body was entered. Since the system could not recognize the invalid name, it responded with the message that the named object did not exist. - An attempt was made to rename an index, cluster, or some other object that cannot be renamed.
action: Check the spelling of the named object and rerun the code. Valid names of tables, views, functions and other database objects can be listed by querying the data dictionary.

description: procedure, function, package, or type is not allowed here
cause: A procedure, function, or package was specified in an inappropriate place in a statement.
action: Make sure the name is correct or remove it.

description: errors during recompilation or revalidation of %s.%s
cause: The errors occurred during implicit recompilation or revalidation of the object. This message indicates the object to which the following errors apply.
action: Check the following errors for more information and make the necessary corrections to the object.

description: results of compilation are too large to support
cause: Attempt to compile and store a large stored procedure that results in compilation data that is too large for the system to support or store.
action: Reduce the size of the store procedure by splitting it into smaller stored procedures.

description: object specified is incompatible with the flag specified
cause: The object type implied by the flag did not match the type of object specified.
action: Specify the correct object, or use the appropriate flag.

description: invalid or missing procedure, function, or package name
cause: The required procedure, function, or package name is invalid or missing.
action: Specify a valid name.

description: user %s cannot use database link %s.%s
cause: During forwarding of a remote object access, an attempt was made to use a non-existent database link or one owned by a user other than the logon user or PUBLIC.
action: Change your database link structure so that all indirect remote accesses are done from the same userid that originates the request.

description: error occurred when looking up remote object %s%s%s%s%s
cause: An error occurred when trying to look up a remote object.
action: Fix the error. Make sure the remote database system has run CATRPC.SQL to create necessary views used for querying or looking up objects stored in the database.

description: error occurred when validating remote object %s%s%s%s%s
cause: An error occurred when trying to validate a remote object.
action: Fix the error. Make sure the remote database system has run CATRPC.SQL to create necessary views used for querying or looking up objects stored in the database.

description: database link %s does not exist
cause: During compilation of a PL/SQL block, an attempt was made to use a non-existent database link.
action: Either use a different database link or create the database link.

description: Aborted: "%s" formed a non-REF mutually-dependent cycle with "%s".
cause: This compilation was aborted because the library unit that was compiled would have formed a non-REF mutually-dependent cycle with some other library units. This happens when an attempt is made to compile types that have attributes of other types that may participate in a cycle with this type. For example: create type t1; create type t2 (a t1); create type t1 (a t2);
action: Break the cycle (possibly by adding a REF or by using another type).

description: insufficient privileges to execute %s
cause: Attempt to execute a stored procedure without sufficient privileges.
action: Get necessary privileges.

description: existing state of %s has been invalidated
cause: Attempt to resume the execution of a stored procedure using the existing state which has become invalid or inconsistent with the stored procedure because the procedure has been altered or dropped.
action: Try again; this error should have caused the existing state of all packages to be re-initialized.
remediation: 1) A dependency changed and this object's compiled state is stale. Usually the next call succeeds after automatic recompilation -- the application should retry once. 2) If it does not recover, the object has real errors: `SELECT line, text FROM dba_errors WHERE owner = UPPER('<o>') AND name = UPPER('<n>') ORDER BY sequence;` -- then treat as ORA-04063. 3) Find the trigger for the invalidation: `SELECT object_name, object_type, last_ddl_time FROM dba_objects WHERE last_ddl_time > SYSDATE - 1 ORDER BY last_ddl_time DESC;` 4) Recompile the dependency tree: `EXEC UTL_RECOMP.RECOMP_PARALLEL(4);` 5) Repeated occurrences in business hours mean DDL is being applied live -- move schema changes to a window, or adopt Edition-Based Redefinition.

description: %s of %s has been changed
cause: Attempt to execute a stored procedure to serve an RPC stub which specifies a timestamp or signature that is different from the current timestamp/signature of the procedure.
action: Recompile the caller in order to pick up the new timestamp.

description: %s has errors
cause: Attempt to execute a stored procedure or use a view that has errors. For stored procedures, the problem could be syntax errors or references to other, non-existent procedures. For views, the problem could be a reference in the view's defining query to a non-existent table. Can also be a table which has references to non-existent or inaccessible types.
action: Fix the errors and/or create referenced objects as necessary.
remediation:
1) The object compiled with errors. Read them: `SELECT line, position, text FROM dba_errors WHERE owner = UPPER('') AND name = UPPER('') ORDER BY sequence;` 2) List everything invalid: `SELECT owner, object_name, object_type FROM dba_objects WHERE status = 'INVALID' ORDER BY owner, object_name;` 3) Recompiling will not fix a genuine error, but it will clear objects invalidated only by a dependency change: `ALTER PACKAGE .

COMPILE; ALTER PACKAGE .

COMPILE BODY;` or in bulk `@?/rdbms/admin/utlrp.sql` / `EXEC UTL_RECOMP.RECOMP_PARALLEL(4);` 4) If the errors are 'table or view does not exist' style, the owner is missing a grant -- see ORA-00942, and grant directly rather than through a role. 5) Find what invalidated it: `SELECT owner, name, type, referenced_owner, referenced_name FROM dba_dependencies WHERE referenced_name = UPPER('');`

description: not executed, invalidated %s
cause: Attempt to execute a stored procedure that has been invalidated.
action: Recompile it.

description: not executed, altered or dropped %s
cause: Attempt to execute a stored procedure that has been altered or dropped thus making it not callable from the calling procedure.
action: Recompile its dependents.

description: non-executable object, %s
cause: Attempt to execute a non-procedure.
action: Make sure that a correct name is given.

description: not executed, %s does not exist
cause: Attempt to execute a non-existent stored procedure.
action: Make sure that a correct name is given.

description: existing state of packages%s%s%s has been discarded
cause: One of errors 4060 - 4067 when attempt to execute a stored procedure.
action: Try again after proper re-initialization of any application's state.
remediation: 1) Harmless in isolation: a package with global state was recompiled while this session held instantiated state, so the state was discarded. The session's next call succeeds -- the application should catch and retry once. 2) Find what was recompiled: `SELECT owner, object_name, object_type, last_ddl_time FROM dba_objects WHERE object_type LIKE 'PACKAGE%' AND last_ddl_time > SYSDATE - 1 ORDER BY last_ddl_time DESC;` 3) If it happens constantly, something is invalidating packages continuously -- look for a job recompiling objects or DDL on a dependency: `SELECT * FROM dba_dependencies WHERE referenced_name = UPPER('<obj>');` 4) Stop recompiling packages with package-level variables during business hours. 5) `PRAGMA SERIALLY_REUSABLE` or Edition-Based Redefinition removes the exposure for code that must change online.

description: cannot drop or replace a library with table dependents
cause: An attempt was made to drop or replace a library that has dependents. There could be a table which depends on type which depends on the library being dropped.
action: Drop all table(s) depending on the type, then retry.

description: invalid trigger name
cause: An invalid trigger name was specified.
action: Verify that trigger name is not a reserved keyword.

description: missing BEFORE, AFTER or INSTEAD OF keyword
cause: The trigger statement is missing the BEFORE/AFTER/INSTEAD OF clause.
action: Specify either BEFORE, AFTER or INSTEAD OF.

description: invalid trigger type
cause: An invalid trigger type was given.
action: Specify either INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE.

description: column list not valid for this trigger type
cause: A column list was specified for a non-update trigger type.
action: Remove the column list.

description: invalid REFERENCING name
cause: An invalid name was given in the referencing clause.
action: Verify the referencing name is not a reserved word.

description: invalid trigger action
cause: An statement was given for the trigger action.
action: Re-specify the trigger action.

description: invalid NEW or OLD specification
cause: An invalid NEW or OLD specification was given for a column.
action: Re-specify the column using the correct NEW or OLD specification.

description: WHEN clause cannot be used with table level triggers
cause: The when clause can only be specified for row level triggers.
action: Remove the when clause or specify for each row.

description: OLD and NEW values cannot be identical
cause: The referencing clause specifies identical values for NEW and OLD.
action: Re-specify either the OLD or NEW referencing value.

description: invalid trigger specification
cause: The create TRIGGER statement is invalid.
action: Check the statement for correct syntax.

description: trigger '%s' does not exist
cause: The TRIGGER name is invalid.
action: Check the trigger name.

description: trigger '%s' already exists
cause: The TRIGGER name or type already exists.
action: Use a different trigger name or drop the trigger which is of the same name.

description: NEW or OLD references not allowed in table level triggers
cause: The trigger is accessing "new" or "old" values in a table trigger.
action: Remove any new or old references.

description: invalid trigger variable '%*.s'
cause: The variable referenced in the trigger body is invalid.
action: See the manual for valid trigger variable types.

description: cannot change NEW values for this trigger type
cause: New trigger variables can only be changed in before row insert or update triggers.
action: Change the trigger type or remove the variable reference.

description: cannot change the value of an OLD reference variable
cause: Old values can only be read and not changed.
action: Do not attempt to change an old variable.

description: trigger description too long, move comments into triggering code
cause: The trigger description is limited to 2000 characters (for dictionary storage reasons). The description does not include the text of the "when" clause or the text of the pl/sql code executed for the trigger.
action: If the trigger description contains a large comment, move that comment into the pl/sql code for the trigger.

description: cannot change the value of ROWID reference variable
cause: Rowid's can only be read and not changed.
action: Do not attempt to change an rowid value.

description: error during execution of trigger '%s.%s'
cause: A runtime error occurred during execution of a trigger.
action: Check the triggers which were involved in the operation.

description: cannot create triggers on objects owned by SYS
cause: An attempt was made to create a trigger on an object owned by SYS.
action: Do not create triggers on objects owned by SYS.

description: '%s' specifies same table, event and trigger time as '%s'
cause: Trigger is of duplicate event and trigger time.
action: Combine the triggering information into one trigger which is fired at the given time.

description: table %s.%s is mutating, trigger/function may not see it
cause: A trigger (or a user defined PL/SQL function that is referenced in this statement) attempted to look at (or modify) a table that was in the middle of being modified by the statement which fired it.
action: Rewrite the trigger (or function) so it does not read that table.

description: cannot %s in a trigger
cause: A trigger attempted to commit or rollback.
action: Rewrite the trigger so it does not commit or rollback.

description: references to columns of type LONG are not allowed in triggers
cause: A trigger attempted to reference a long column in the triggering table.
action: Do not reference the long column.

description: table %s.%s is constraining, trigger may not modify it
cause: A trigger attempted to modify a table that was constraining for some referential constraint of a parent SQL statement.
action: NA

description: trigger '%s' already exists on another table, cannot replace it
cause: Cannot replace a trigger which already exists on a different table than the one being replaced.
action: Drop the trigger with the same name and re-create it.

description: trigger '%s' has a WHEN clause which is too large, limit 2K
cause: A trigger's 'when' clause is limited to 2K for dictionary storage reasons. The trigger being created exceeded that size.
action: Use a smaller 'when' clause. Note, the trigger body could be used to perform the same limiting action as the 'when' clause.

description: DDL conflict while trying to drop or alter a trigger
cause: An attempt was made to concurrently perform two DDL operations on a trigger or trigger table.
action: Investigate the new state of the trigger and retry the DDL operation, if still appropriate.

description: trigger '%s.%s' is invalid and failed re-validation
cause: A trigger was attempted to be retrieved for execution and was found to be invalid. This also means that compilation/authorization failed for the trigger.
action: Options are to resolve the compilation/authorization errors, disable the trigger, or drop the trigger.

description: trigger '%s' is valid but not stored in compiled form
cause: A trigger was attempted to be retrieved for execution and was found to be valid, but not stored. This may mean the an upgrade was done improperly from a non-stored trigger release.
action: Alter compile the trigger to create the trigger in stored form. Also, you may want to review that a proper upgrade was done.

description: cannot create triggers owned by PUBLIC
cause: An attempt was made to create a trigger owned by PUBLIC.
action: Do not create triggers owned by PUBLIC.

description: Multilingual Engine does not support the language %s.
cause: An attempt was made to use an unsupported language in Multilingual Engine (MLE).
action: Use a supported language when creating an MLE module or calling DBMS_MLE.eval(). A list of supported languages can be obtained by calling DBMS_MLE.get_available_languages().
info: The list of languages supported in Multilingual Engine (MLE) can be obtained by using the following PL/SQL query: ``` DECLARE l_languages dbms_mle.languages_t; BEGIN l_languages := dbms_mle.get_available_languages; FOR in IN 1..l_languages.count LOOP dbms_output.put_line(l_languages(i)); END LOOP; END; / ```

description: An MLE module named %s already exists.
cause: An attempt was made to create a Multilingual Engine (MLE) module with the same name as one that already exists. MLE module names must be unique.
action: Choose a different name for the MLE module. Alternatively, drop the existing MLE module before deploying the new one or replace the existing MLE module using CREATE OR REPLACE MLE MODULE.

description: MLE module %s does not exist.
cause: An attempt was made to use, modify, or drop a nonexistent Multilingual Engine (MLE) module.
action: Create the named MLE module or use an existing MLE module.

description: An environment named %s already exists.
cause: An attempt was made to create an environment whose name conflicted with an existing environment.
action: Choose a different name for your environment. Alternatively, remove the existing environment before deploying the new one or replace the existing environment using CREATE OR REPLACE MLE ENV.

description: MLE environment %s does not exist.
cause: An attempt was made to use, modify, or drop a nonexistent Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment.
action: Create the named MLE environment or use an existing MLE environment.

description: Module %s referred to by %s has been modified since the execution context was created.
cause: An attempt was made to use a function of a module that has been modified since the execution context was created.
action: Rerun the function. Rerunning the function after encountering this error implicitly creates and uses a new execution context. Alternatively call DBMS_SESSION.reset_package() to reset the session.

description: Environment %s or one of the modules imported by it has been modified since it has been loaded.
cause: The Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment or one of the modules that it imports has changed since the execution context was created.
action: Create a new dynamic context, or rerun the function. Rerunning the function creates and uses a new execution context. Alternatively call DBMS_SESSION.reset_package() to reset the session.

description: Effective userid, roles, or container changed since context creation.
cause: An attempt was made to access an execution context with a different userid or roles or from a different container compared to when it was created.
action: Use the same userid, roles, and container that you used when creating the execution context when accessing it.

description: An import named %s already exists in the MLE environment.
cause: An attempt was made to add an import whose name conflicted with an existing import in the Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment.
action: Use a different import name, alter the existing import using ALTER IMPORTS, or drop the existing import before adding the new one. The data dictionary view ALL_MLE_ENV_IMPORTS lists the imports for all MLE environments accessible to the current user.

description: import %s does not exist in the MLE environment.
cause: An attempt was made to ALTER or DROP a nonexistent import in a Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment.
action: Use an existing import name. The data dictionary view ALL_MLE_ENV_IMPORTS lists the imports for all MLE environments accessible to the current user.

description: duplicate import name %s
cause: An import name was used more than once for this environment.
action: Do not use the same import name multiple times for one environment.

description: invalid or missing version string provided to Multilingual Engine (MLE) module %s
cause: The value for the VERSION clause of the CREATE MLE MODULE DDL was either missing, too long, or not a valid string.
action: Provide a valid string as part of the VERSION clause or remove the VERSION clause. VERSION strings must have 256 or fewer characters.

description: invalid or missing language option string provided to Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment %s
cause: The value for the LANGUAGE OPTIONS clause of the CREATE or alter MLE ENV statement was either missing, too long, or not a valid string.
action: Provide a valid string as part of the LANGUAGE OPTIONS clause or remove the LANGUAGE OPTIONS clause. LANGUAGE OPTIONS strings must have 4000 or fewer characters.

description: invalid or missing import name specified in MLE environment %s
cause: The import name was either missing, too long, or not a valid string.
action: Provide a valid import name. Import names must have 2048 or fewer characters.

description: invalid or missing MLE module name
cause: The Multilingual Engine (MLE) module name was either missing or not a valid identifier.
action: Provide a valid MLE module name. MLE module names must be valid database object names.

description: invalid or missing MLE environment name
cause: The Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment name was either missing or not a valid identifier.
action: Provide a valid MLE environment name. MLE environment names must be valid database object names.

description: MLE environment %s has errors
cause: The Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment had errors.
action: Ensure that for each MLE module referenced by the MLE environment the following conditions are met: - The module exists. - The owner of the environment must either own the mapped module or must be granted the EXECUTE privilege on it. For each mapping not satisfying these conditions, perform whichever of the following actions is appropriate: - Create the missing MLE module. - Grant the EXECUTE privilege on the module. - Drop the mapping from the environment.
params: 1) environment_name: The name of the MLE environment with errors.

description: Module import %s is a synonym for a remote object.
cause: An attempt was made to specify a synonym for a remote object as an import in a Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment. Synonyms referring to remote objects are not allowed in an MLE environment's import clause. In this context a remote object is any object accessed using a database link.
action: Replace the synonym of a remote object with a local MLE module.

description: MLE module %s has errors
cause: The Multilingual Engine (MLE) module had errors.
action: Resolve any compilation errors on the MLE module.

description: insufficient privileges to use MLE module %s
cause: An attempt was made to import a Multilingual Engine (MLE) module in an MLE environment, or use the module in an MLE call specification, without sufficient privileges on the module.
action: Obtain the EXECUTE privilege on MLE modules that you do not own before importing them in MLE environments or using them in call specifications.

description: invalid privilege used for an MLE module
cause: An attempt was made to GRANT or REVOKE a privilege other than EXECUTE or COLLECT DEBUG INFO on a Multilingual Engine (MLE) module.
action: GRANT or REVOKE only the EXECUTE and COLLECT DEBUG INFO privilege on MLE modules.

description: invalid privilege used for an MLE environment
cause: An attempt was made to GRANT or REVOKE a privilege other than EXECUTE on a Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment.
action: GRANT or REVOKE only the EXECUTE privilege on MLE environments.

description: insufficient privileges to use MLE environment %s
cause: An attempt was made to use a Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment without sufficient privileges on the environment itself or on MLE modules that are imported by the environment.
action: Get the necessary privileges on the MLE environment and all MLE modules that it imports.

description: authorization error for MLE module referenced in MLE environment
cause: The Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment was not authorized to include the MLE module as an import definition.
action: For each MLE module included as an import in the MLE environment, ensure that the environment owner either owns the module or has the EXECUTE privilege on it.

description: Empty MLE modules are not supported.
cause: An attempt was made to create an empty Multilingual Engine (MLE) module.
action: Create only non-empty MLE modules.

description: invalid or missing MLE language identifier
cause: The provided Multilingual Engine (MLE) language identifier used to create an MLE schema object was either invalid or missing.
action: Ensure that a supported language identifier is provided. The list of supported language identifiers can be obtained using DBMS_MLE.get_available_languages. Verify that the language identifier does not contain typos or extraneous characters, such as single quotes.

description: duplicate import name %s in drop list
cause: The specified import list in the DROP IMPORTS statement contained duplicate entries.
action: Ensure that there are no duplicate entries in the drop list.

description: empty import name for MLE module %s
cause: The provided import name for the Multilingual Engine (MLE) module was empty.
action: Provide a non-empty import name.

description: insufficient privileges to use MLE language %s
cause: An attempt is being made to use the language in a Multilingual Engine (MLE) call specification, without sufficient privileges on the language.
action: Obtain the EXECUTE privilege on MLE languages before using them in call specifications.

description: authorization error for MLE language used in MLE module
cause: The owner of the Multilingual Engine (MLE) module is not authorized to use the MLE language.
action: For each MLE language used in the MLE environment, ensure that the module owner has the EXECUTE privilege on it.

description: malformed SIGNATURE clause %s in PL/SQL call specification %s: %s
cause: Invoking Multilingual Engine (MLE) modules requires the definition of call specifications, including a reference to an MLE module, an optional environment, and a signature. The signature clause in the call specification was malformed. The error was triggered by one of the following situations: - The number of parameters in the PL/SQL program unit did not match that of the JavaScript function referenced. - The PL/SQL program unit used OUT or IN OUT parameters not matching those of the JavaScript function referenced. - The signature syntax is invalid. It should be the function name, optionally followed by a comma-separated sequence of types surrounded by parentheses.
action: Review the error message and determine the exact cause of the error from the list above. Then provide a valid signature clause to the PL/SQL program unit.

description: Environment %s specifies an unrecognized language option %s
cause: An attempt was made to use a Multilingual Engine (MLE) environment specifying a language option that was not recognized by MLE.
action: Update the environment to specify only valid language options.

description: An invalid context handle was provided.
cause: A valid context handle needs to be passed to DBMS_MLE subprograms that perform actions on execution contexts. An invalid context handle was passed to such a subprogram.
action: Use a valid context handle.

description: cannot create a context handle on behalf of user ID %s because it is invalid
cause: The user_id passed to DBMS_SYS_MLE.create_context_as_user() is either NULL or invalid because it does not map to an existing user.
action: Provide a valid user id. Compare the user ID passed in the code snippet with those found in the data dictionary. Pluggable databases store information about local users and their corresponding numeric user IDs in DBA_USERS.

description: Unable to convert database %s value to MLE %s value. Reason: %s
cause: A type conversion from a database value (SQL or PL/SQL) to a Multilingual Engine (MLE) value failed. This can occur if the input database value does not fit the supported range of values for the MLE target type.
action: Ensure that the database input value fits the supported range of values for the MLE target type.

description: Unable to convert MLE value to database %s value. Reason: %s.
cause: The given input Multilingual Engine (MLE) value cannot be converted to the specified database (SQL or PL/SQL) target type. This can occur for the following reasons: - the type of the input value is not supported for conversion to the target type - the type of the input value can be converted to the target type, but the input value is not in the supported range for the target type.
action: Ensure that the input MLE value is of a type that can be converted to the target database type, and that it fits into the supported value range.

description: An attempt was made to exchange an invalid property between Multilingual Engine (MLE) and PL/SQL.
cause: An attempt was made to use an empty string or a NULL value as property_name when importing or exporting values in DBMS_MLE.
action: Pass a valid property_name that is neither an empty string nor a NULL value. Review the code for occurrences of - DBMS_MLE.export_to_mle() - DBMS_MLE.import_from_mle() For each of these, ensure the property_name meets the requirements mentioned above.

description: Property %s does not exist in dynamic MLE execution context.
cause: An attempt was made to import a property from a Multilingual Engine (MLE) execution context into PL/SQL using the DBMS_MLE package. The property name that was specified does not exist in the execution context.
action: Specify the name of a property that has been exported by code in the execution context, or export the property from MLE language code in the execution context before importing into PL/SQL.
params: 1) property name: The name of the property that was attempted to import.

description: Access to DBMS_MLE functionality is denied
cause: Executing code dynamically in Multilingual Engine (MLE) requires the use of execution contexts. An execution context is passed to MLE when evaluating a code snippet. The context handle referring to such an execution context provided previously was invalid. Access to dynamic MLE code execution has been disabled for this session.
action: Start a new session to use DBMS_MLE functionality again.

description: %s
cause: A syntax error was encountered while parsing a Multilingual Engine (MLE) code snippet or module.
action: Fix the syntax error in the MLE code snippet or module.

description: %s
cause: A runtime error occurred while evaluating a Multilingual Engine (MLE) code snippet or call specification.
action: Fix the MLE language code that causes the runtime error. Use the source location reported in the error message to identify the code that needs to be fixed. Use the DBMS_MLE.get_error_stack or DBMS_MLE.get_ctx_error_stack functions to retrieve the MLE language stack trace for the error.

description: Unsupported type %s in signature clause of MLE call specification
cause: A procedure or function was created with a Multilingual Engine (MLE) call specification. The signature clause of the call specification contains a type name that is not supported for the MLE language.
action: Change the signature clause of the call specification so that it only contains types supported by the corresponding MLE language.
params: 1) type name: The name of the unsupported type.

description: MLE call specification specifies invalid mapping from database type %s to MLE language type %s
cause: The signature clause in a Multilingual Engine (MLE) call specification maps the database type of a procedure argument to an MLE language type that is not supported for the given database type.
action: Change the signature clause of the MLE call specification to use an MLE language type that is valid for the given type of the procedure argument.
params: 1) source type: The database type of the procedure argument. 2) target type: The MLE language type specified in the signature clause.

description: Missing COLLECT DEBUG INFO privilege on MLE module %s.
cause: The user who enabled debugging was missing the COLLECT DEBUG INFO privilege on the specified Multilingual Engine (MLE) module.
action: Grant the COLLECT DEBUG INFO privilege on the MLE module to the debugging user or disable debugpoints for the MLE module before executing code from the MLE module.

description: invalid debug specification - %s
cause: The provided debug specification was not valid.
action: Fix the debug specification error identified in the error message.

description: Cannot process the debug output provided.
cause: The Multilingual Engine (MLE) post-execution debug output provided for processing was not well formed. The debugging information passed to post-processing tools such as DBMS_MLE.parse_debug_output requires the input to be in a specific format.
action: Ensure that the debug output provided contains MLE post-execution debugging output.

description: environments contain a conflicting import name: %s
cause: The Multilingual Engine (MLE) environments that were used to configure the context import a module under the same import name.
action: Alter one of the environments to not use the conflicting import name.

description: environments contain a conflicting language option: %s
cause: The Multilingual Engine (MLE) environments that were used to configure the context specify different values for a language option.
action: Alter one of the environments to remove the conflicting language option.

description: SIGNATURE clause of call specification %s specifies a function name %s that is not exported by module %s.
cause: An attempt was made to call a Multilingual Engine (MLE) call specification whose SIGNATURE clause specifies a function name that does not correspond to any exported function of the call specification's MLE module.
action: Modify the SIGNATURE clause of the call specification or the corresponding function in the MLE module so that the SIGNATURE clause refers to a function that is exported in the MLE module.

description: No MLE context found for the specified pair [module = %s, environment = %s] for the current user.
cause: The specified module or environment names did not correspond to a valid MLE context for the current user. Either the specified module or environment do not exist, or no MLE context has been created for them yet.
action: Specify a valid module or environment name, or make sure that an MLE context has been created for them. MLE module contexts are created lazily upon first calling an MLE module function or procedure.

description: at %s
cause: Location context for an unhandled error raised during execution of programs by the Multilingual Engine (MLE). The location information points to the code location at which the error occurred.
action: Fix the problem causing the error, or catch and handle the error.

description: error in database callout from MLE at %s
cause: An error occurred during execution of a database callout (for example, a SQL statement executed from a JavaScript program) in a program run by the Multilingual Engine (MLE). The location information points to the code location in the program at which the SQL statement was executed.
action: Inspect the location information to determine the location of the error, and review additional error messages that indicate the nature of the callout error. Fix the problem causing the error, or catch and handle the error in the program.
params: 1) code_location: The code location in the program at which the database callout was performed.

description: %s
cause: Error message for an unhandled error that occurred in a database callout from a program executed by the Multilingual Engine (MLE).
action: Fix the problem causing the error, or catch and handle the error.
params: 1) error_message: A string representation of the error that occurred during the database callout.

description: MLE Resource Limit: %s
cause: A resource limit is reached while evaluating a Multilingual Engine (MLE) code snippet or call specification.
action: Fix the MLE language code that is causing the resource exhaustion. Use the source location reported in the error message to identify the code that needs to be fixed. Use the DBMS_MLE.get_error_stack or DBMS_MLE.get_ctx_error_stack functions to retrieve the MLE language stack trace for the error.
params: 1) resource_limit: Resource limit for the resource that is exhausted.

description: internal error %s
cause: An internal error occurred while evaluating a code snippet or a function.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: system error %s
cause: A system error occurred while evaluating a function or a code snippet.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: Multilingual Engine (MLE) does not support Multi Process Multi Threads (MPMT).
cause: An attempt was made to use the Multilingual Engine (MLE) with Multi Process Multi Threads (MPMT) enabled.
action: Disable the Multi Process Multi Threads (MPMT) before using the Multilingual Engine (MLE). Retry after MPMT is disabled.

description: Multilingual Engine (MLE) does not support shared servers.
cause: An attempt was made to use the Multilingual Engine (MLE) with a shared server.
action: Use a dedicated server to use the Multilingual Engine (MLE).

description: cannot start the Multilingual Engine (MLE), instance PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT too low
cause: The instance PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT prevented from starting the Multilingual Engine (MLE).
action: Increase the instance PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT.

description: Cannot start MLE because the amount of available PGA memory in the PDB is insufficient.
cause: The amount of memory allocated to the Program Global Area (PGA) using PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT is too low in this Pluggable Database (PDB), preventing Multilingual Engine (MLE) from starting.
action: Increase the amount of PGA memory available to the PDB either by raising the PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT parameter or by reducing the PGA memory consumption of other workloads in the PDB.

description: Cannot start the Multilingual Engine (MLE) because the per-session Program Global Area (PGA) limit is too low.
cause: Database Resource Manager enforced a limit for this session's use of private memory, referred to as the session's Program Global Area. The Resource Manager limit, session_pga_limit, is too low for MLE to start.
action: Identify the session's resource consumer group and use it to identify the session_pga_limit. Increase the consumer group's session_pga_limit using Database Resource Manager API, then retry the operation.
info: To identify the session experiencing the `ORA-04258` error, the resource consumer group, and the currently active Oracle Database Resource Manager (Resource Manager) plan, connect as an administrative user to `CDB$ROOT` and run the following query: ``` SELECT s.sid, s.serial#, s.inst_id, s.resource_consumer_group, ( SELECT name FROM gv$rsrc_plan p WHERE s.con_id = p.con_id AND s.inst_id = p.inst_id ) dbrm_plan FROM GV$SESSION s WHERE s.username = '&username'; ``` Once the resource consumer group and Resource Manager plan are identified, look up the value of `SESSION_PGA_LIMIT`. For example: ``` SELECT PLAN, GROUP_OR_SUBPLAN, SESSION_PGA_LIMIT FROM cdb_rsrc_plan_directives WHERE PLAN = '&PDB_RESOURCE_MANAGER_PLAN' AND GROUP_OR_SUBPLAN = '&RESOURCE_CONSUMER_GROUP'; ``` A call to the `DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER.UPDATE_PLAN_DIRECTIVE()` PL/SQL package can be used to increase the limit.

description: Multilingual Engine (MLE) failed to load
cause: A severe error prevented Multilingual Engine (MLE) from loading and initializing. This might have been caused by a corrupted software installation.
action: Please contact Oracle Support for further assistance.

description: Multilingual Engine (MLE) is not available on this platform
cause: An attempt was made to use the Multilingual Engine (MLE) on a platform where MLE was not available.
action: Use the Multilingual Engine (MLE) on a platform where MLE is available.

description: Multilingual Engine (MLE) cannot be enabled if disabled at instance or PDB level.
cause: An attempt was made to enable MLE while it was disabled at instance or PDB level. MLE may only be enabled at instance level, at PDB level if enabled at instance level, and at session level if enabled at PDB level.
action: Enable MLE at instance or PDB level first.

description: Memory Protection Keys (MPK) for Multilingual Engine (MLE) are not supported on this machine.
cause: An attempt was made to enable Memory Protection Keys (MPK) for the Multilingual Engine (MLE) on a machine that does not support MPK.
action: Disable Memory Protection Keys (MPK) for the Multilingual Engine (MLE) using the initialization parameter or use a machine with MPK support.

description: Session time zone region %s is not available in Multilingual Engine (MLE)
cause: The time zone region currently configured in the session is not available in MLE.
action: Choose another session time zone.
params: 1) time zone: The name of the unsupported time zone region.

description: A Vector arithmetic function used in a vector index must be a valid Multilingual Engine (MLE) inline call specification.
cause: An attempt was made to create a vector index using a vector arithmetic function which isn't an inline call specification.
action: Use an MLE inline call specification.

description: The specified Multilingual Engine (MLE) procedure or function must be pure in this context.
cause: An attempt is being made to use an MLE procedure or function which has not been declared as pure.
action: Use the PURE keyword when declaring the MLE procedure or function.

cause: An internal error is occurring.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support.

description: Invalid textual JSON
cause: Buffered textual JSON is not valid and cannot be converted to another representation.
action: Use valid textual JSON.

description: Invalid OSON
cause: Buffered Oracle Binary JSON (OSON) is not valid and cannot be converted to another representation.

description: cannot create foreign key constraints on columns referencing a sharded table
cause: An attempt was made to create a foreign key constraint in a duplicate table on a column referencing a sharded table.
action: Remove the foreign key constraint referencing a column in the sharded table.

description: source and target shardspaces have different number of chunks
cause: ALTER TABLE SPLIT PARTITIONSET operation did not have an equal number of chunks in source and target shardspaces.
action: Make number of chunks equal on the source and target shardspaces by using the SPLIT CHUNK command and then retry.

description: names assigned to resulting partitionsets must be distinct
