cause: An error was returned from SYS$SETIMR while trying to queue a process spin-watch timer.
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sspsck: $QIO failure at AST level
cause: An error was returned from SYS$QIO while trying to read the process dump mailbox.
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sspscm: SYS$GETDVIW failure
cause: An error was returned from SYS$GETDVIW while trying to get information about the process dump mailbox.
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfop: LIB$GET_VM failure
cause: An error was returned from LIB$GET_VM while attempting to allocate memory for an i/o vector.
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfop: SYS$OPEN failure
cause: An error was returned from SYS$OPEN while attempting to open the data file for reading
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfcl: SYS$CLOSE failure
cause: An error was returned from SYS$CLOSE while attempting to close the input data file
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfcl: LIB$FREE_VM failure
cause: An error was returned from LIB$FREE_VM while attempting to free the memory for the i/o vector
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfop: LIB$GET_VM failure
cause: An error was returned from LIB$GET_VM while attempting to allocate memory for data and index buffers
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfcl: LIB$FREE_VM failue
cause: An error was returned from LIB$FREE_VM while attempting to free memory used by data and index buffers
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfop: %s byte record too big for %s byte user buffer
cause: The longest record in the file will not fit into the largest data buffer that can be allocated
action: Modify the RMS file to have smaller records

description: sllfop: $CONNECT failure
cause: An error was returned by SYS$CONNECT while attempting to open the data file
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfrb: $GET failure
cause: An error was returned by SYS$GET while attempting to read the data file
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfsk: $GET failure
cause: An error was returned by SYS$GET while attempting to skip records in the input file
action: Check system error and refer to VMS documentation

description: sllfop: bad option
cause: You are using a bad option to loader Fixed= is one legal option. Check documentation for others.
action: Check documentation

description: osnsoi: error setting up interrupt handler
cause: An error occurred while setting up the control interrupt handler
action: This is an internal error. Contact your Oracle representative.

description: sdopnf: internal error
cause: A list of all files open by this process could not be obtained.
action: This is an internal error. Contact your customer support representative.

description: Maximum number of session sequence lists exceeded.
cause: The sequence parent state objects for this session are all used.
action: Quit this session and begin a new session.

description: Deprecated
cause: This bug has been deprecated. Do not use it.
action: N/A

description: Sequence %s.CURRVAL is not yet defined in this session.
cause: Sequence CURRVAL was selected before sequence NEXTVAL.
action: Select NEXTVAL from the sequence before selecting CURRVAL.

description: Sequence %s.NEXTVAL exceeds internal limits.
cause: The sequence was created with invalid values for some of the parameters. The calculation of NEXTVAL cannot be made because it exceeds the maximum allowed size.
action: Alter or re-create the sequence number within the allowed limits.

description: Sequence %s.NEXTVAL %s %sVALUE and cannot be instantiated.
cause: Instantiating NEXTVAL violates either the MINVALUE or the MAXVALUE.
action: Alter the sequence so that a new value can be requested.

description: specified row does not exist
cause: A row with the given rowid does not exist in any of the tables given
action: check the query for misspellings of table names and the rowid

description: specified row no longer exists
cause: the row has been deleted by another user since the operation began
action: re-try the operation

description: Further changes to this block by this transaction not allowed
cause: Max locks have been reached for this transaction in this block
action: Commit changes

description: another instance is mounted with USE_ROW_ENQUEUES = %s
cause: the shared instance being started does not have the same value for use_row_enqueues as already running instances
action: ensure that all instances' INIT.ORA files specify the same value for the parameter 'use_row_enqueues'

description: index is not valid - see trace file for diagnostics
cause: Validate Index detected an inconsistency in its argument index
action: Send trace file to your customer support representative

description: index key does not exist file %s: (root %s, node %s) blocks (%s)
cause: Internal error: possible inconsistency in index
action: Send trace file to your customer support representative, along with information on reproducing the error

description: Key not found in index %s obj# %s, file %s, block %s (%s)
cause: This is an internal error. There is a possible inconsistency between the table and index.
action: The general method to repair such inconsistency is to rebuild the index. Send the trace files and the alert.log file to Oracle Support along with information about reproducing the error.

description: object no longer exists
cause: The object has been deleted by another user since the operation began, or a prior incomplete recovery restored the database to a point in time during the deletion of the object.
action: Delete the object if this is the result of an incomplete recovery.
remediation: 1) Either a concurrent DDL removed the segment under an open cursor, or the segment header is inconsistent. Establish which. 2) Check for recent DDL on the object: `SELECT owner, object_name, object_type, last_ddl_time FROM dba_objects WHERE object_name = UPPER('<obj>');` A TRUNCATE or MOVE concurrent with a long query produces this legitimately -- serialize them. 3) If no DDL is involved, test the structure: `ANALYZE TABLE <o>.<t> VALIDATE STRUCTURE CASCADE;` 4) `RMAN> VALIDATE DATAFILE <f>;` for the segment's files, then `SELECT * FROM v$database_block_corruption;` 5) For a partitioned table, check whether a partition was dropped or exchanged during the query. 6) If structural damage is confirmed, treat it as ORA-01578 and recover from backup.

description: this index object %s is being online built or rebuilt
cause: the index is being created or rebuild or waited for recovering from the online (re)build
action: wait the online index build or recovery to complete

description: Oracle event to turn off smon cleanup for online index build
cause: set this event only under the supervision of Oracle development
action: debugging only

description: cannot create journal table %s.%s
cause: The online index builder could not create its journal table
action: Rename the conflicting table or rerun the SQL statement. There may be a concurrent online index rebuild on the same object.

description: cannot perform DDL on an internal journal table %s.%s
cause: DDL is not allowed on an internal journal table created for online index build.
action: Wait for SMON to drop the internal journal table that is not being used, or try the function ONLINE_INDEX_CLEAN in PL/SQL package DBMS_REPAIR to clean it on demand.

description: may not build or rebuild this type of index online
cause: only support normal index or IOT top-level index
action: change your index type

description: nosort is not a supported option for online index build
cause: may not specify nosort for online index build
action: get rid of nosort in the index creation command

description: Oracle event to test SMON cleanup for online index build
cause: Oracle Kernel test only
action: Donot set this event(for test only)

description: a partitioned index may not be coalesced as a whole
cause: User attempted to coalesce a partitioned index using ALTER INDEX COALESCE statement, which is illegal
action: Coalesce the index a (sub)partition at a time (using ALTER INDEX MODIFY (sub)PARTITION COALESCE)

description: a composite partition may not be coalesced as a whole
cause: User attempted to coalesce a composite partition
action: Coalesce the index a subpartition at a time (using ALTER INDEX MODIFY SUBPARTITION COALESCE)

description: composite partition index may not be compressed
cause: User attempted to compress a composite partition index
action: create uncompressed composite partition index

description: can not alter a fake index
cause: User attempted to alter a fake index
action: drop fake index

description: can not online create/rebuild this index type
cause: User attempted to create index type that online doesnot support
action: use offline index create/rebuild command

description: can not acquire dml enough lock(S mode) for online index build
cause: User attempted to create index online without allowing DML Share lock
action: allow DML share lock on the base table

description: Index Organized Table operation released its block pin
cause: Block maintenance forced the release of a block pin
action: Contact your customer support representative

description: Deferred FK constraints cannot be enforced, index too big (%s)
cause: Deferred Foreign Key constraints cannot be enforced due to the index key being too big and built on a non-default DB_BLOCK_SIZE.
action: First try to drop the Foreign Key and then the primary key.

description: The new initrans will make the index too big
cause: Specifying the initrans need additional space to hold the index key which might make the index too big
action: Try giving a smaller initrans value

description: Need to create SYS.IND_ONLINE$ table in order to (re)build index
cause: Alter index Build/Rebuild online require existing of SYS.IND_ONLINE$ table.
action: User/DBA needs to create sys.ind_online$ before alter the index /rdbms/admin/catcio.sql contains script to create ind_online$.

description: Too many offline indexes need to be maintained.
cause: The limit is 65,536 offline indexes for each statement.
action: Change the index maintenance to online. If indexes need to be maintained offline, drop some indexes.

description: Online (re)build of index rolled back due to DML conflict
cause: The online (re)build journal is inconsistent with ongoing DML and cannot be used successfully to complete the online index (re)build.
action: Reissue the online (re)build operation, after performing any cleanup, if needed.

description: discrete transaction restriction violated (%s)
cause: An attempt was made to perform an action that is not currently supported in a discrete transaction.
action: Rollback the transaction, and retry it as a normal transaction.

description: consistent read failure; rollback data not available
cause: Encountered data changed by an operation that did not generate rollback data: create index, direct load or discrete transaction.
action: In read/write transactions, retry the intended operation. Restart the read-only transactions.

description: can't serialize access for this transaction
cause: Encountered data changed by an operation that occurred after the start of this serializable transaction.
action: In read/write transactions, retry the intended operation or transaction.

description: illegal SERIALIZABLE clause specified for user INTERNAL
cause: Serializable mode is not supported for user INTERNAL.
action: Reconnect as another user and retry the SET TRANSACTION command.

description: concurrency check failed
cause: Encountered data changed by an operation that occurred after a specific snapshot. This is usually used to indicate that a particular cached copy of a datablock is stale. This is used for internal use for now.
action: refresh the cached copy of the datablock and retry operation.

description: no snapshot found based on specified time
cause: Could not match the time to an SCN from the mapping table.
action: try using a larger time.

description: specified number is not a valid system change number
cause: supplied scn was beyond the bounds of a valid scn.
action: use a valid scn.

description: operation not supported while in Flashback mode
cause: user tried to do dml or ddl while in Flashback mode
action: disable Flashback and re-attempt the operation

description: Flashback cannot be enabled in the middle of a transaction
cause: user tried to do Flashback in the middle of a transaction
action: do a commit

description: attempting to re-enable Flashback while in Flashback mode
cause: as stated above
action: disable first before re-enabling

description: flashback not supported for user SYS
cause: The user was logged in as SYS.
action: Log on as a different (non-SYS) user.

description: invalid timestamp specified
cause: as stated above
action: enter a valid timestamp

description: snapshot expression not allowed here
cause: A snapshot expression using AS OF was specified when not allowed.
action: Do not use the AS OF clause

description: cannot flashback the table because row movement is not enabled
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on a table for which row movement has not been enabled. Because the Flashback Table does not preserve the rowids, it is necessary that row movement be enabled on the table.
action: Enable row movement on the table

description: restore point %s is from a different incarnation of the database
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation using a restore point from a different incarnation of the database
action: Provide a restore point from the current database incarnation

description: Flashback Table operation is not supported on remote tables.
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on a remote table. This was not supported.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on remote tables.

description: Flashback Table operation is not allowed on fixed tables, external tables, and hybrid partitioned tables.
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on a fixed table, external table, or a hybrid partitioned table. This was not supported.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on fixed tables, external tables, or hybrid partitioned tables.

description: Flashback Table operation is not allowed on temporary tables.
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on a temporary table. This was not supported.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on temporary tables.

description: Flashback Table operation is not allowed on materialized views.
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on a materialized view. This was not supported.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on materialized views or snapshot logs.

description: Flashback Table operation is not supported on partitions.
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on a partition. This was not supported.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on partitions.

description: Flashback Table operation is not allowed on Advanced Queue tables.
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on Advanced Queue tables. This was not supported.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on Advanced Queue tables.

description: Flashback Table operation is not supported on clustered tables.
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on a clustered table. This was not supported.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on clustered tables.

description: Flashback Table is not supported on object tables, nested tables.
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on a object table or a nested table or a table with nested table column. This was not supported.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on such tables.

description: Flashback Table operation is not supported on this object.
cause: An attempt was made to perform Flashback Table operation on an object on which the operation was not supported.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on such objects.

description: ora_addr: $ORACLE_SID not set in environment
cause: The environment variable ORACLE_SID is not set.
action: Set the ORACLE_SID environment variable.

description: ora_addr: cannot translate address file name
cause: Cannot translate $ORACLE_HOME/dbs/sgadef$ORACLE_SID.dbf.
action: Ensure that ORACLE_HOME and ORACLE_SID are properly set.

description: ora_addr: cannot open address file
cause: The address file could not be opened.
action: Check that ORACLE is up. Check that the file $(ORACLE_HOME)/dbs/sgadef$(ORACLE_SID).dbf exists and has correct permissions.

description: ora_addr: cannot read from address file
cause: The address file could not be read.
action: Check that the file $(ORACLE_HOME)/dbs/sgadef$(ORACLE_SID).dbf exists and contains a single line of text.

description: scngrs: SCN not yet initialized
cause: The System Commit Number has not yet been initialized.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: Requested I/O error
cause: Oracle requested that an I/O error be returned for this operation.
action: This should not occur in normal Oracle operation. Contact support.

description: smscre: failed to allocate SGA
cause: The n_core system call failed, maybe due to insufficient memory.
action: Specify a smaller number of buffers. Check INIT.ORA parameters.

description: smscre: unable to attach to SGA
cause: The process cannot attach to the SGA. This can happen if either the listener can't attach, or the process cannot communicate with the listener.
action: Verify that the instance is up and running. Contact your customer support representative.

description: smsdes: cannot detach from SGA
cause: Probably, the listener process has died.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: smsdes: cannot unmap SGA
cause: The n_core system call failed while detaching from the SGA.
action: Note nCX error returned; contact your customer support representative.

description: smsget: cannot get instance listener address
cause: The instance listener address cannot be read from the sgadef file.
action: Verify $(ORACLE_HOME) and $(ORACLE_SID) are set correctly. Additional information gives error return from ora_addr.

description: smsget: listener not on this node
cause: A process wishing to attach to the SGA is on a different node from its instance's listener.
action: Verify $(ORACLE_HOME) and $(ORACLE_SID) are set correctly. Contact your customer support representative.

description: smsget: cannot share subcube with listener
cause: The n_share call failed, probably because the listener has died.
action: Check if the listener is running, and contact your customer support representative.

description: smsget: SGA region not yet created
cause: Attempting to attach to an SGA which has not yet been created.
action: Verify that the instance is running. Contact your customer support representative.

description: smsfre: cannot detach from SGA
cause: The n_core system call failed while detaching from the SGA.
action: Check nCX error, and contact your customer support representative.

description: recursive audit operation attempted
cause: A recursive operation subject to an enabled audit policy was attempted during an auditing operation or an audit table movement operation. The most likely reasons are: (1) Space management operations were running to free up space in the audit tablespace. (2) A SQL operation was being performed on dictionary tables (either directly or using database triggers) that produced more audit records.
action: Check the space in the tablespace for SYS.AUD$ or SYS.FGA_LOG$ and extend the tablespace, if necessary. Or, if the problem was caused by recursively auditing SQL operations, change or remove the audit policy on such objects or statements.

description: ora_addr: cannot open nameserver
cause: A process could not connect to the nameserver.
action: Make sure the nameserver is up and running. Additional information gives nameserver's returned status.

description: ora_addr: cannot find name in nameserver
cause: The listener nameserver entry for an instance could not be found.
action: Make sure the nameserver is up and running. Additional information gives nameserver's returned status.

description: ora_addr: cannot free listener address
cause: The listener nameserver entry could not be freed
action: Additional information gives nameserver's returned status. Contact your customer support representative.

description: ora_addr: cannot close nameserver
cause: The connection to the nameserver could not be closed.
action: Additional information gives nameserver's returned status. Contact your customer support representative.

description: create_ora_addr: cannot open nameserver
cause: A process could not connect to the nameserver.
action: Make sure the nameserver is up and running. Additional information gives nameserver's returned status.

description: create_ora_addr: cannot register name in nameserver
cause: The listener's addressing information could not be registered.
action: Make sure the nameserver is up and running. Additional information gives nameserver's returned status.

description: destroy_ora_addr: cannot close nameserver
cause: The connection to the nameserver could not be closed.
action: Additional information gives nameserver's returned status. Contact your customer support representative.

description: create_ora_addr: cannot close nameserver
cause: The connection to the nameserver could not be closed.
action: Additional information gives nameserver's returned status. Contact your customer support representative.

description: destroy_ora_addr: cannot destroy name
cause: The listener's addressing information could not be removed.
action: Additional information gives nameserver's returned status. Contact your customer support representative.

description: sksachk: Illegal archival control string
cause: Archive files cannot be created with the given archival control string.
action: Check that the volume exists

description: sksabln: Buffer size not large enough for archive control string
cause: The given archival control string expands into too many characters.
action: Reduce archive control string length.

description: Out of memory for environment variable
cause: There is insufficient memory to return the requested value
action: Reduce memory usage and retry.

description: Environment variable unset
cause: The requested environment variable is not set
action: Ensure that the variable name requested is correct.

description: No room in nameserver for pid
cause: There is no room to record the pid for a background process
action: Shutdown abort and restart the database.

description: Cannot set environment variable
cause: There is insufficient memory to expand the environment.
action: Reduce memory usage and retry.

description: Cannot get CPU statistics
cause: Could not retrieve CPU times because n_stat failed.
action: Contact customer support.

description: sllfop: Cannot open file
cause: Oracle could not open a file.
action: Check the Unix errno returned as additional information.

description: sllfop: Cannot fstat file
cause: Oracle could not obtain information about an open file.
action: Check the Unix errno returned as additional information.

description: sllfop: Bad value for recsize
cause: An illegal value for the record size was specified.
action: Specify a value for the recsize option that is greater than 0.

description: sllfop: bad value for maxrecsize
cause: An illegal value for the maximum record size was specified.
action: Specify a value for the maxrecsize option that is greater than 0.

description: sllfop: unrecognized processing option
cause: An unrecognized processing option was specified.
action: Check the Oracle for nCUBE 2 User's Guide for valid options.

description: sllfop: could not allocate buffers
cause: Memory for the load buffers could not be allocated.
action: Reduce the maximum record size. Eliminate any unnecessary processes on your current node before running SQL*Loader again.

description: sllfcf: Error closing file
cause: An error occurred trying to close a file.
action: Check the Unix errno returned as additional information.

description: sllfrb: Error reading file
cause: An error occurred trying to read from a file.
action: Check the Unix errno returned as additional information.

description: sllfsk: Error seeking in file.
cause: The lseek system call returned an error.
action: Check the Unix errno returned as additional information.

description: sllfsk: Error seeking in file.
cause: The lseek system call returned an error.
action: Check the Unix errno returned as additional information.

description: sllfsk: Error reading file
cause: An error occurred trying to read from a file.
action: Check the Unix errno returned as additional information.

description: sllfsk: Error reading file
cause: An error occurred trying to read from a file.
action: Check the Unix errno returned as additional information.

description: scnget: Call to scnget before scnset or scnfnd.
cause: An internal error
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: scnmin: NOT IMPLEMENTED YET
cause: An internal error
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: scnmin: open/convert of bias lock failed
cause: A call to the lkmgr failed to open and convert the bias lock
action: Check to make sure the lkmgr is up.

description: scnmin: close of bias lock failed
cause: A call to the lkmgr failed to close the bias lock
action: Check to make sure the lkmgr is up.

description: Printing not supported
cause: An attempt was made to automatically spool a file to the printer
action: none

description: Wait operation timed out
cause: Oracle timed out waiting for an event
action: Contact your Oracle support representative

description: rollback segment #%s specified not available
cause: (same as 1545)
action: (same as 1545). Also, make sure you have created enough rollback segments for the number of instances you are trying to start.

description: This command not allowed on nCUBE, only one thread is ever used.
cause: An illegal command was executed for the nCUBE platform.
action: There is no need to issue this command.

description: On nCUBE, this command can only be executed from instance 1.
cause: A command that can only be issued on instance 1 was issued elsewhere.
action: Log on to instance 1 and repeat the command.

description: sropen: failed to open a redo server connection
cause: An error occurred trying to connect to the redo server.
action: The OS specific error message should tell you what to do.

description: srclose: failed to close a redo server connection
cause: An error occurred trying to close the redo server connection.
action: The OS specific error message should tell you what to do.

description: srapp: failed to send redo data to the redo server
cause: An error occurred trying to send redo to the redo server.
action: The OS specific error message should tell you what to do.

description: invalid compiler name: %s
cause: An invalid compiler name <compname> was passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine.
action: Correct the compiler name parameter in the PL/SQL code that called the conversion routine.

description: error executing PL/SQL code coverage
cause: An error occurred during execution of a PL/SQL code coverage procedure.
action: Check the error stack for more details.

description: error encountered in WMSGBSIZ, size for WMSGBLK is not big enough for warning message
cause: The WMSGBSIZ is the maximun size for warning message block, it is recommanded to be 1024 bytes to 8 kbytes.
action: Defined WMSGBLK of size between 1k to 8k bytes and update the WMSGBSIZ to the sizeof(WMSGBLK).

description: invalid compiler type in FORMAT parameter at %s
cause: An invalid compiler type is defined in format control block. The format control block is invalid.
action: Check to be sure that the format parameter was built by MAKE_RAW_TO_NUMBER_FORMAT or MAKE_NUMBER_TO_RAW_FORMAT, and that it was not accidentally overwritten or modified by the PL/SQL procedure.

description: error encountered in %s
cause: The function <routine> returned an error. Where <routine> may be: RAW_TO_NUMER NUMBER_TO_RAW RAW_TO_NUMBER_FORMAT NUMBER_TO_RAW_FORMAT MAKE_NUMBER_TO_RAW_FORMAT MAKE_RAW_TO_NUMBER_FORMAT
action: This message will be preceded by messages providing details about the error. Check those messages to determine what action to take.

description: raw data has invalid digit in display type data
cause: The input raw buffer passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine contained invalid data. The picture mask parameter specified a digit, but the corresponding input from the raw data did not contain a valid digit.
action: Either the input data is incorrect, or the picture mask is incorrect. Correct the appropriate item.

description: raw data missing leading sign
cause: The input raw buffer passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine had no leading sign, but the mask options parameter specified a leading sign.
action: Correct the input raw data or the mask options so that they match.

description: raw data missing zero as defined in picture
cause: The picture mask parameter passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine contained a zero, but the corresponding input from the raw data was not a zero.
action: Either the input data is incorrect, or the picture mask is incorrect. Correct the appropriate item.

description: raw data has invalid floating point data
cause: The input raw data passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine contained invalid floating point data.
action: Correct the input raw data.

description: invalid picture type in convert raw to number
cause: The picture mask parameter passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine contained non-numeric characters, but the conversion was to a numeric data type.
action: Correct the picture mask parameter.

description: raw data has invalid trailing sign
cause: The input raw buffer passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine had no trailing sign, but the mask options parameter specified a trailing sign.
action: Correct the input raw data or the mask options so that they match.

description: PICTURE MASK missing the leading sign when SIGN IS LEADING specified
cause: The input MASK passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine had no leading sign, but the mask options parameter specified a leading sign.
action: Correct the input raw data or the mask options so that they match.

description: raw data has invalid sign digit
cause: The input raw buffer passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine had an invalid sign digit in the position where the picture mask specified a sign.
action: Correct the input raw data or the picture mask so that they match.

description: invalid picture type in picture mask
cause: The picture mask parameter passed to a UTL_PG NUMBER_TO_RAW conversion routine contained non-numeric characters, but the conversion was to a numeric data type.
action: Correct the picture mask parameter.

description: raw buffer is too short to hold converted data
cause: The output raw buffer passed to a UTL_PG NUMBER_TO_RAW conversion routine was not large enough to contain the results of the conversion based on the picture mask.
action: Increase the raw buffer size to the size necessary to hold the entire result of the conversion.

description: closed parenthesis missing in picture mask
cause: A closed parenthesis was missing from the picture mask passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine.
action: Correct the picture mask.

description: syntax error in BLANK WHEN ZERO clause in mask options
cause: A syntax error was found in the BLANK WHEN ZERO clause in the mask options parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. Valid specifications are: BLANK ZERO BLANK ZEROS BLANK ZEROES BLANK WHEN ZERO BLANK WHEN ZEROS BLANK WHEN ZEROES
action: Correct the mask options parameter.

description: syntax error in JUSTIFIED clause in mask options
cause: A syntax error was found in the JUSTIFIED clause in the mask options parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. Valid specifications are: JUST JUST RIGHT JUSTIFIED JUSTIFIED RIGHT
action: Correct the mask options parameter.

description: syntax error in SIGN clause in mask options
cause: A syntax error was found in the SIGN clause in the mask options parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. Valid specifications are: SIGN LEADING SIGN LEADING SEPARATE SIGN LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER SIGN TRAILING SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE CHARACTER SIGN IS LEADING SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER SIGN IS TRAILING SIGN IS TRAILING SEPARATE SIGN IS TRAILING SEPARATE CHARACTER
action: Correct the mask options parameter.

description: syntax error in SYNCHRONIZED clause in mask options
cause: A syntax error was found in the SYNCHRONIZED clause in the mask options parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. Valid specifications are: SYNC SYNC LEFT SYNC RIGHT SYNCHRONIZED SYNCHRONIZED LEFT SYNCHRONIZED RIGHT
action: Correct the mask options parameter.

description: syntax error in USAGE clause in mask options
cause: A syntax error was found in the USAGE clause in the mask options parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. Valid specifications are: USAGE DISPLAY USAGE COMP USAGE COMP-3 USAGE COMP-4 USAGE COMPUTATIONAL USAGE COMPUTATIONAL-3 USAGE COMPUTATIONAL-4 USAGE IS DISPLAY USAGE IS COMP USAGE IS COMP-3 USAGE IS COMP-4 USAGE IS COMPUTATIONAL USAGE IS COMPUTATIONAL-3 USAGE IS COMPUTATIONAL-4
action: Correct the mask options parameter.

description: syntax error in DECIMAL-POINT environment clause
cause: A syntax error was found in the DECIMAL-POINT environment clause parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. Valid specifications are: DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA
action: Correct the environment clause parameter.

description: invalid numeric symbol found in picture mask
cause: An invalid numeric symbol was found in the picture mask parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine.
action: Correct the picture mask parameter.

description: invalid specification of CR in picture mask
cause: The CR suffix was incorrectly specified in the picture mask parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. The CR suffix can only appear at the end of a picture mask.
action: Correct the picture mask parameter.

description: invalid specification of DB in picture mask
cause: The DB suffix was incorrectly specified in the picture mask parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. The DB suffix can only appear at the end of a picture mask.
action: Correct the picture mask parameter.

description: specification of E in picture mask is unsupported
cause: The floating point exponent symbol 'E' was specified in the picture mask parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. The floating point data type is currently not supported by the UTL_PG conversion routines.
action: Correct the picture mask parameter, and the data, if necessary.

description: more than one V symbol specified in picture mask
cause: The picture mask passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine contained more than one decimal point indicator ('V'). Only one decimal point indicator is allowed in the picture mask.
action: Correct the picture mask parameter.

description: more than one S symbol specified in picture mask
cause: The picture mask passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine contained more than one operational sign indicator ('S'). Only one operational sign indicator is allowed in the picture mask.
action: Correct the picture mask parameter.

description: syntax error in CURRENCY SIGN environment clause
cause: A syntax error was found in the CURRENCY SIGN environment clause parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. Valid specifications are: CURRENCY SIGN IS x where x is a valid currency sign
action: Correct the environment clause parameter.

description: no sign in picture mask but SIGN clause in mask options
cause: The picture mask parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine contained no sign symbol ('S', '+', or '-'), but the mask options parameter contained a SIGN clause. A sign symbol is required in the picture mask parameter when the mask options parameter contains a SIGN clause.
action: Correct the picture mask parameter or the mask options parameter.

description: syntax error in SEPARATE CHARACTER option of SIGN clause
cause: A syntax error was found in the SEPARATE CHARACTER option of the SIGN clause in the mask options parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine. Valid specifications are: SEPARATE SEPARATE CHARACTER
action: Correct the mask options parameter.

description: invalid format parameter
cause: The format parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine was invalid. The format parameter should have been built by a prior call to either MAKE_RAW_TO_NUMBER_FORMAT or MAKE_NUMBER_TO_RAW_FORMAT.
action: Check to be sure that the format parameter was built by MAKE_RAW_TO_NUMBER_FORMAT or MAKE_NUMBER_TO_RAW_FORMAT, and that it was not accidentally overwritten or modified by the PL/SQL procedure.

description: invalid format parameter length
cause: The format parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine was not the correct length. Format parameters must be 2048 bytes in length.
action: Check to be sure that the format parameter was built by MAKE_RAW_TO_NUMBER_FORMAT or MAKE_NUMBER_TO_RAW_FORMAT, and that it was not accidentally overwritten or modified by the PL/SQL procedure.

description: invalid environment clause in environment parameter
cause: The environment parameter passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine contained an unsupported or invalid environment clause. Only the CURRENCY SIGN and the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA environment clauses are supported.
action: Correct the environment parameter.

description: raw buffer contains invalid decimal data
cause: The input raw buffer passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine contains invalid decimal data.
action: Correct the input data.

description: overflow converting decimal number to Oracle number
cause: The output variable passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER was not large enough to hold the Oracle number resulting from the input decimal number.
action: Be sure that the input decimal number is valid, and besure that the output variable is large enough to hold the Oracle number value.

description: input raw decimal data contains more than 42 digits
cause: The input raw buffer passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine contained more than 42 digits. This exceeds the maximum size of an Oracle number.
action: Correct the raw input buffer.

description: input mask contains more than 32 characters
cause: The input mask passed to UTL_PG numeric conversion routine contained more the 32 characters.
action: Correct the mask input buffer.

description: raw buffer length %s is too short for %s
cause: The input raw buffer passed to a UTL_PG RAW_TO_NUMBER conversion routine was less than %s bytes long, but the picture mask parameter specified that %s bytes of input data were to be converted.
action: Either the input data is incorrect, or the picture mask is incorrect. Correct the appropriate item.

description: error converting Oracle number to %s
cause: An error occurred when converting an Oracle number to a COBOL <type> of: DISPLAY COMP-3 or character variable. The Oracle number was not in the correct format.
action: Correct the call to the conversion routine. The input must be a valid Oracle number variable.

description: mask option %s is not supported
cause: The mask option <clause> was passed to a UTL_PG conversion routine, but is not supported by UTL_PG. The <clause> can be: USAGE IS POINTER USAGE IS INDEX USAGE IS COMP-1 USAGE IS COMP-2 POINTER
action: Remove the <clause> from the mask options parameter in the PL/SQL call to UTL_PG.

description: must use the SIGN IS SEPARATE clause in mask options
cause: A signed numeric entry with DISPLAY usage was converted using a non-defaulted character set and its PICTURE character-string contains an S. In these circumstances, a SIGN IS SEPARATE clause must be specified in the mask options.
action: Either specify a valid SIGN IS SEPARATE clause in the mask options, use the defaulted character set, or don't specify an S in the PICTURE character-string.

description: Warning: picture mask '%s' overrides picture mask option 'USAGE IS %s' to 'USAGE IS DISPLAY'
cause: Picture mask USAGE option was overridden by the picture mask.
action: This is an informational message only. The message may be eliminated by changing the USAGE option to match the picture mask.

description: Warning: picture mask options '%s' ignored by UTL_PG
cause: Picture mask options such as OCCUR, SYNC and others are not processed by the UTL_PG numeric conversion routines.
action: This is an informational message only. The message may be eliminated by removing the unnecessary picture mask options from the parameter list passed to the UTL_PG routine.

description: session tag does not exist
cause: There was no tagged session with the specified session tag.
action: Check the specified session tag and resubmit the BEIRUT action.

description: session tag is already used
cause: The session tag was already used by another tagged session.
action: Use another session tag.

description: current session is already tagged
cause: The current session was already tagged. A session could only be tagged once.
action: To change a session tag, untag the session, then tag it again with the new tag.

description: current session is not tagged
cause: The current session was not tagged before the BEIRUT action.
action: Tag the current session using the BEIRUT_TAG action before executing your action.

description: session tag string is too long: greater than %s character(s)
cause: The specified session tag was too long.
action: Use a shorter session tag string.

description: session tag string is too short: less than %s character(s)
cause: The specified session tag was too short.
action: Use a longer session tag string.

description: invalid BEIRUT action.
cause: The specified action to the BEIRUT event was invalid
action: Ensure that the specified BEIRUT action is valid.

description: A session cannot terminate itself.
cause: Tried to make a tagged session kill itself.
action: Try to terminate the tagged session using another session.

description: An attempt to terminate a critical background process %s failed.
cause: Tried to terminate a critical background process.
action: Try to terminate the critical background process using the operating system KILL command.

description: background process name does not exist
cause: An attempt to tag a named background process failed because there was no background process name matching the specified tag.
action: Check the background process name and resubmit the tag action.

description: process does not have a session state object
cause: An attempt to tag a process failed because the process did not have a session state object.
action: Ensure that the process has a session state object and resubmit the tag action.

description: session tag is reserved for background process name.
cause: An attempt was made to tag a database session with a reserved background process name.
action: Use another session tag that differs from the reserved names of background processes.

description: breakpoint is not enabled
cause: An attempt was made to process a BEIRUT action assuming a breakpoint is enabled but it is not.
action: Enable the breakpoint before processing the BEIRUT action.

description: breakpoint is explicitly disabled
cause: An attempted was made to process a BEIRUT action assuming a breakpoint was enabled but it was explicity disabled.
action: Enable the breakpoint again before processing the BEIRUT action.

description: breakpoint name is too long: greater than %s character(s)
cause: The specified breakpoint name was too long.
action: Check the breakpoint length upper limit in the error message and update the breakpoint name accordingly.

description: breakpoint list length is too long: greater than %s character(s)
cause: The specified breakpoint list was too long.
action: Check the the breakpoint list length upper limit in the error message and update the breakpoint list accordingly.

description: deadlock detected: current session waits on breakpoint %s while test session waits on breakpoint %s.
cause: Faulty test scenarios led to a deadlock. The current session waited on a breakpoint while test session waited for current session on another breakpoint.
action: Check your test script to ensure that the test session WAIT_FOR is on the same breakpoint that the current session hits first.

description: current session waiting on breakpoint %s timed out after waiting for %s seconds
cause: The current session waited on a breakpoint until timeout.
action: Fix the test script to post the database session out of its waiting using the BEIRUT_CONTINUE action.

description: test session timed out waiting for database session %s on breakpoint %s after %s seconds
cause: The database session did not hit the breakpoint that the test session is waiting on.
action: Fix the code to hit the specified breakpoint or the test script to wait on the correct breakpoint name.

description: Oracle event to test fix for bug-33741649
cause: Oracle Kernel test only.
action: Do not set this event in production (for test only).

description: SQL assertion (%s.%s) violated.
cause: The DML being executed does not satisfy the SQL assertion definition.
action: Avoid running DML statements that violate the SQL assertion definition.

description: SQL assertion violated.
cause: The DML being executed does not satisfy the SQL assertion definition.
action: Avoid running DML statements that violate the SQL assertion definition.

description: Named or inline view%s is not supported.
cause: The named or inline view is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the named or inline view from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Collection iterator%s is not supported.
cause: Collection iterator is not allowed in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the collection iterator from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Remote table%s is not supported.
cause: Remote table is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the remote table from the SQL assertion definition.

description: PL/SQL function is not supported.
cause: PL/SQL function is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the PL/SQL function from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Outer join or semijoin is not supported.
cause: Outer join or semijoin is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the outer join or semijoin from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Bind variable is not supported.
cause: Bind variables are not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the bind variable from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Pivot or unpivot is not supported.
cause: Pivot or unpivot is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the pivot or unpivot from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Subquery in the SELECT list not supported.
cause: Subuqery in the SELECT list is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the subquery from the SELECT of the SQL assertion definition.

description: Subquery is not supported.
cause: Subquery is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the subquery from the SQL assertion definition.

description: WITH clause is not supported.
cause: WITH clause is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the WITH clause from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Aggregates are not supported.
cause: Aggregates are not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the aggregates from the SQL assertion definition.

description: ORDER BY clause is not supported.
cause: ORDER BY clause is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the ORDER BY clause from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Set operators are not supported.
cause: Set operators (for example, UNION, UNION ALL or MINUS) are not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the set operator from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Window function is not allowed.
cause: Window function is not allowed in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the window function from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Spread sheet is not supported.
cause: Spread sheet is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the spread sheet from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Temporary table%s is not supported.
cause: Temporary table is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the temporary table from the SQL assertion definition.

description: MATCH_RECOGNIZE sheet is not supported.
cause: MATCH_RECOGNIZE is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the MATCH_RECOGNIZE from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Row limit clause is not supported.
cause: Row limit clause is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the row limit clause from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Analytic view is not supported.
cause: Analytic view is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the analytic view from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Graph function is not supported.
cause: Graph function is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the graph function from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Filter predicate %s found will not participate in the incremental validation.
cause: The filter predicate is found in a query block where the table is not defined.
action: This is an informational message. Consider moving the predicate to a query block where the table is defined.

description: Filter predicate %s found will participate in incremental validation.
cause: The filter predicate found will participate in the incremental validation of the SQL assertion.
action: This is an informational message only.

description: Equijoin %s found does not meet the criteria to do a FAST validation.
cause: One of the columns in the equijoin either lacks a NOT NULL property or the data types do not match.
action: Consider adding a NOT NULL constraint to the column or including the predicate, <col> IS NOT NULL in the assertion definition within the query block where the table is referenced. For example: CREATE ASSERTION AS1 CHECK ( NOT EXISTS(select 1 from t1 where t1.c1 is NOT NULL and NOT EXISTS(select 1 from t2 where t1.c1 = t2.c2 and t2.c2 is NOT NULL)) Also, ensure that the column data types are identical. For example, ensure that the data type of columns t1.c1 and t2.c2 are the same.

description: Filter predicate %s found will participate in incremental validation.
cause: The filter predicate found will participate in the incremental validation of the SQL assertion.
action: This is an informational message.

description: Equijoin %s found will not participate in the incremental validation.
cause: The equijoin is found in a query block where the table is not defined.
action: This is an informational message. Consider moving the join to a query block where the table is defined.

description: Virtual columns%s are not supported.
cause: Virtual columns are not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the virtual columns from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Certain SQL functions are not supported.
cause: Non-determinstic functions like SYSDATE are not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the objectionable functions from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Synonym%s is not supported.
cause: Synonym is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the synonym from the SQL assertion definition.

description: External table%s is not supported.
cause: External table is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the external table from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Consider splitting the SQL assertion definition.
cause: The SQL assertion definition is not supported in its current form but can be split into multiple assertions that can be supported.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for more information about the various techniques to split the SQL assertion definition.

description: Unsupported SQL assertion definition.
cause: The SQL assertion definition in its current form is not supported.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for information about the supported forms.

description: Unsupported SQL assertion definition.
cause: The SQL assertion definition in its current form is not supported.
action: Refer to Oracle documentation for information about the supported forms.

description: Abstract data type attributes not supported.
cause: Abstract data type attributes are not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the abstract data type attributes from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Abstract Data Type (ADT) table%s not supported.
cause: ADT table is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the ADT table from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Columns of certain data types are not supported.
cause: Data types like LOB, BFILE, LONG, JSON, and ADT are not supported.
action: Remove the violating columns from the assertion definition.

description: Assertion%s does not exist.
cause: The specified SQL assertion does not exist.
action: Ensure that the name and the required privileges are valid.

description: Cannot defer an assertion that is not deferrable.
cause: An attempt is being made to defer a nondeferrable SQL assertion.
action: Alter the assertion definition to make it deferrable.

description: Name is already used by an existing constraint.
cause: An attempt is being made to create an assertion with a name that is already used in a constraint.
action: Enter a unique name for the assertion or retry the operation after dropping the existing constraint.

description: CREATE ASSERTION failed
cause: An error occurred during create assertion.
action: See accompanying errors.

description: Validation of SQL assertion%s is not supported in ISOLATION_LEVEL=SERIALIZABLE.
cause: SQL assertion is not supported in ISOLATION_LEVEL=SERIALIZABLE.
action: Use READ COMMITTED instead.

description: Creation of SQL assertion is not supported in ISOLATION_LEVEL=SERIALIZABLE.
cause: SQL assertion is not supported in ISOLATION_LEVEL=SERIALIZABLE.
action: Use READ COMMITTED instead.

description: Too many table references (maximum allowed = %s).
cause: SQL assertions are not supported when there are more than the maximum allowed table references.
action: Use fewer than the maximum allowed tables.

description: Cannot rename a SQL assertion.
cause: Renaming a SQL assertion is not supported.
action: Do not rename a SQL assertion.

description: Cannot rename a table referenced in SQL assertion.
cause: Renaming a table referenced in a SQL assertion is not supported.
action: Drop the SQL assertions in which the table is referenced and then try renaming the table.

description: A subquery within an OR condition is not supported.
cause: The SQL assertion definition does not support a subquery within an OR condition.
action: Avoid using a subquery within an OR condition.

description: Partition extension clause%s is not supported.
cause: Partition extension clause is not supported.
action: Try using the corresponding predicates instead.

description: SYS owned tables are not supported.
cause: SYS owned tables are not supported.
action: Do not use SYS owned tables.

description: Sharded table%s is not supported.
cause: Sharded table is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the sharded table from the SQL assertion definition.

description: SQL ASSERTION event
cause: An event to control SQL assertion behavior.
action: None

description: Attempting to set SQL assertion to DISABLE VALIDATE.
cause: SQL assertion does not support DISABLE and VALIDATE options together.
action: Use DISABLE NOVALIDATE, ENABLE VALIDATE or ENABLE NOVALIDATE options.

description: Columns are referenced by SQL assertion %s.%s.
cause: An attempt is being made to drop or alter columns of a table referenced by SQL assertion.
action: Before performing the above operations to the table, drop the SQL assertion and try again.

description: SQL assertion property is changed during DDL.
cause: Another session has modified SQL assertion property during DDL.
action: Run the same DDL again if SQL assertion properties still need to be changed.

description: SQL assertion is enabled but failed to validate existing data.
cause: An assertion violation occurred when SQL assertion validated existing data, the assertion state is set to ENABLE NOVALIDATE instead of ENABLE VALIDATE.
action: Execute the ALTER ASSERTION VALIDATE DDL command for full validation. If the validation succeeds, the SQL assertion will transition to the ENABLE VALIDATE state. If it fails, the SQL assertion will remain in the ENABLE NOVALIDATE state.

description: CASCADE CONSTRAINTS must be specified to perform REVOKE ASSERTION REFERENCES.
cause: During this REVOKE, some SQL assertions that reference this table cannot be dropped. To perform this automatically, CASCADE CONSTRAINTS must be specified.
action: Drop SQL assertions that reference this table or specify CASCADE CONSTRAINTS.

description: Test error %s.
cause: Test error messsage.
action: This is an internal error. Report to Oracle Support.

description: General event for SQL assertion.
cause: N/A
action: This internal event is used to enable various actions associated with SQL assertion.

description: SQL assertion semantic error: %s.
cause: SQL assertion has a semantic error.
action: Correct the error indicated in this message.

description: Reads from SQL assertion auxiliary tables are restricted.
cause: An attempt is being made to query a system-created table to support SQL assertion. Names are prefixed with "ORA$SA$".
action: Do not directly query such tables.

description: SQL assertion not supported in SYS schema.
cause: An attempt is being made to create assertion in SYS schema.
action: Do not create SQL assertions in SYS schema.

description: Filtered PMOP is unsupported on tables referenced in SQL assertion.
cause: A filtered partition-maintenance Operation (PMOP) is being attempted on a table that is referenced in SQL assertion.
action: Disable SQL assertion before attempting PMOP.

description: Query block nesting limit exceeded (maximum allowed level of nesting = %s).
cause: SQL assertions are not supported when there are more than the maximum allowed level of nesting of query blocks. Following is an example of two-level nesting assertion: CREATE ASSERTION ASRT_LEVEL_2 CHECK (NOT EXISTS(SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM t2 WHERE t1.c1=t2.c2)
action: Use fewer levels of nesting.

description: Number of query blocks limit exceeded (maximum allowed = %s).
cause: SQL assertions are not supported when there are more than the maximum allowed number of query blocks.
action: Use fewer number of query blocks.

description: Must use DROP ASSERTION to drop the assertion that uses "%s"."%s".
cause: An attempt is being made to drop the internal table of the SQL assertion using a command other than DROP ASSERTION.
action: Use DROP ASSERTION to drop the SQL assertions that uses this table.

description: Diagnostic event for SQL assertion.
cause: N/A
action: This internal event is used to enable diagnostics associated with SQL assertion.

description: Subpartition-maintenance operation is unsupported on tables referenced in SQL assertion.
cause: A subpartition-maintenance operation is being attempted on a table that is referenced in SQL assertion.
action: Disable SQL assertion before attempting a subpartition-maintenance operation.

description: EXCHANGE PMOP is unsupported on tables referenced in SQL assertion.
cause: An EXCHANGE partition-maintenance Operation(PMOP) is being attempted on a table that is referenced in SQL assertion.
action: Disable the SQL assertion before attempting such PMOP.

description: DDL on SQL assertion auxiliary tables are not allowed.
cause: The table on which this DDL is executed is a system-created table to support SQL assertion. Names are prefixed with "ORA$SA$".
action: Do not execute DDLs on such tables.

description: Conversion to a partitioned table using a filtered clause is not supported for tables referenced in the SQL assertion.
cause: An attempt is being made to convert a table referenced by a SQL assertion into a partitioned table using a filtered clause, which is currently unsupported.
action: Disable the SQL assertion before converting.

description: A subquery with ALL or ANY operator is not supported.
cause: The following cases are not supported: - col1 op ANY (subquery) Where "op" is any supported operator except '=' or '!=' - col1 op ALL (subquery) Where "op" is any supported operator except '!=' - col1+5 != ALL (subquery) Expressions "col1+5" are not supported
action: Rewrite the SQL assertion definition without the ANY or ALL operator.

description: Name already used by an existing SQL assertion.
cause: The specified constraint name has to be unique across constraints and assertions.
action: Specify a unique constraint name for the constraint.

description: DROP or TRUNCATE of subpartition is unsupported on tables referenced in a SQL assertion.
cause: A DROP or TRUNCATE of subpartition is being attempted on a table that is referenced in a SQL assertion.
action: Disable the SQL assertion before attempting such PMOP.

description: IOT table%s is not supported.
cause: Index-organized table (IOT) is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the IOT from the SQL assertion definition.

description: Attempting to set SQL assertion to INITIALLY DEFERRED NOT DEFERRABLE.
cause: INITIALLY DEFERRED conflicts with NOT DEFERRABLE.
action: Use INITIALLY DEFERRED DEFERRABLE or INITIALLY IMMEDIATE NOT DEFERRABLE.

description: Attempting to modify deferrability of SQL assertion.
cause: The [NOT] DEFERRABLE option cannot be changed in SQL assertion .
action: SQL assertion must be dropped and created with new deferrability.

description: Number of columns per table limit exceeded (maximum allowed = %s).
cause: SQL assertions are not supported when a table has more than the maximum allowed number of columns.
action: Use fewer number of columns.

description: SQL Assertion definition is too large(maximum allowed = %s bytes).
cause: SQL assertions are not supported when the definition text exceeds the the maximum allowed size.
action: Use a smaller definition.

description: Materialized view%s is not supported.
cause: Materialized view is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the materialized view from the SQL assertion definition.

description: SQL assertion auxiliary table "%s"."%s" is in use.
cause: An attempt is being made to alter a SQL assertion auxiliary table that is used by other concurrent transaction.
action: Do not attempt to run this DDL until the concurrent transaction is complete.

description: User table "%s"."%s" conflicts with a SQL assertion auxiliary table.
cause: The user table has the same name as a SQL assertion auxiliary table.
action: The user table must be dropped or renamed in order to create SQL assertion.

description: Date, timestamp or system variable wrongly specified.
cause: An attempt is being made to use a date constant, timestamp constant or system variable that is not completely specified. For example, a date is being specified without the century, or a timestamp specified without a time zone.
action: Completely specify the date constant, timestamp constant or system variable.

description: The Direct Path Load method for loading data into a table referenced in SQL assertion is not allowed.
cause: An attempt is being made to load data into a table referenced in SQL assertion using direct path method, which is not supported.
action: Use the conventional path method to load the data instead.

description: Blockchain or immutable table%s is not supported.
cause: Blockchain or immutable table is not supported in the SQL assertion definition.
action: Remove the blockchain or immutable table from the SQL assertion definition.

cause: One Oracle process died while still holding a lamport latch.

cause: The internal limit on the number of user interrupt handlers has been exceeded.
action: Reduce the number of simulataneous logons or reduce the number of user interrupt handlers.

description: osnsui: cannot set up user interrupt handler.
cause: Malloc() failed to allocate space to hold user interrupt handler.
action: Possible memory resource shortage.

description: osncui: invalid handle.

action: Use a valid handle.

description: slsget: cannot get virtual memory region statistics.

action: Check return code in sercerrno. Possible operating system failure.

description: spwat: error waiting for a post.

action: Check return code in sercerrno. Port name is returned in sercose[0].

description: sppst: error during a post.
cause: Msg_send system call returned an error. Internal error.
action: Check return code in sercerrno. Port name is returned in sercose[0].

description: smscre: could not attach shared memory.

action: Contact Oracle support.

description: smsget: mmap returned an error.
cause: The mmap system call returned an error. Internal error.
action: Contact Oracle support.

description: smscre: vm_allocate error, unable to create shared memory.
cause: Error in system call vm_allocate. Failed to create SGA as a single shared memory segment.
action: Check result code returned in sercerrno. Verify that the SGA attach address is valid.

description: smscre: shared memory attach address incorrect.
cause: The vm_allocate system call attached the SGA at an incorrect location.
action: Verify that the SGA attach address is valid.

description: pw_detachPorts: server call pws_detach failed.
cause: The call pws_detach to (Oracle helper) failed.
action: Make sure the server is still active. Check the error code returned in sercerrno, and look for error messages in the server log file.

description: pws_look_up: fork failed
cause: The pws_look_up call could not fork the (Oracle helper) process.
action: Verify that there are enough system resources to support another process. The user or system process limit may have been exceeded, or the amount of free memory or swap space may be temporarily insufficient.

description: pws_look_up: port lookup failure
cause: The pws_look_up could not find a port to (Oracle helper).
action: Make sure the (Oracle helper) server has been started correctly by pws_look_up, and that the network name server is still running.

description: pw_attachPorts: port_rename failed.
cause: The port_rename system call failed; possible internal error.
action: Check return code in sercerrno, report to Oracle customer support.

description: pw_attachPorts: server call pws_attach failed.
cause: The call pws_attach to (Oracle helper) failed.
action: Make sure the server is still active. Check the error code returned in sercerrno, and look for error messages in the server log file.

description: pw_attachPorts: port_allocate failed.
cause: The port_allocate system call failed; possible resource exhaustion.
action: Check return code in sercerrno, report to Oracle customer support.

description: spwat: invalid process number.

description: sppst: invalid process number passed to sppst.
cause: Function was passed an invalid oracle process id.
action: Internal error. Contact Oracle support.

description: osngpn: port allocation failure.

action: Possible system resource shortage; check the error code in sercerrno.

description: osnpns: no port in the name server.

action: Check the error code in sercerrno. Make sure the shadow process and network name server are still running.

description: osnipn: port allocation failure.

action: Possible system resource shortage; check the error code in sercerrno.

description: osnipn: could not check port in name server.

action: Check the error code in sercerrno. Make sure the network name server is running.

description: osnsbt: bad message received.

action: Internal error. Report the error code returned in sercerrno.

description: osnpui: cannot send break message
cause: The Pipe driver could not send a break message to the ORACLE shadow process break thread.
action: Contact your customer support representative.

description: pw_destroyPorts: server call pws_stop_instance failed.
cause: The call pws_stop_instance to (Oracle helper) failed.
action: Make sure the server is still active. Check the error code returned in sercerrno, and look for error messages in the server log file.

description: sNeXT_instanceName: translation error.
cause: A failure was detected while translating the value of ORACLE_SID.
action: Make sure ORACLE_SID is defined, and that it is of legal length.

description: osnmpx: send/receive error exchanging Mach ports.
cause: The Mach driver failed to exchange port information with the other side of the connection. Either msg_send (sercose[0] == 1) or msg_receive (sercose[0] == 2) failed.
action: Check return code in sercerrno. Make sure both sides of the connection are still running.

description: osnmop: access error on oracle executable

action: Check the permissions on the ORACLE executable and each component of the ORACLE_HOME/bin path.

description: osnmop: fork failed

action: Verify that there are enough system resources to support another process. The user or system process limit may have been exceeded, or the amount of free memory or swap space may be temporarily insufficient.

description: osnmop: buffer allocation failure.

description: osnmfs: bad return code from msg_send.

description: osnmgetmsg: could not read a message

action: Internal error. Contact your customer support representative.

description: pws_look_up: access error on (Oracle helper) executable

action: Check the permissions on the (Oracle helper) executable and each component of the ORACLE_HOME/bin path.

description: osnpbr: cannot send break message
cause: The pipe driver could not send a break message to the ORACLE shadow process break thread.
action: Internal error. Contact your customer support representative.

description: Memory allocation of role name object failed.

action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system failure.

description: Failed to get O/S MAC privileges.
cause: The operating system would not allow the retrieval of this process' privileges.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system failure. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Label comparison failed.

action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system failure. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: File label retrieval failed.

action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system error. Also check the "additional information" field for the SQL*Net error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Conversion of binary label to string failed.
cause: ORACLE was unable to convert a binary label to a string.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system failure. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Allocation of string buffer failed.
cause: a buffer used to hold the name of the file for which a label was to be obtained could not be allocated.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system failure. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services. The number of bytes that ORACLE attempted to allocate is in the "Additional Information" field.

description: Class conversion from binary to ORACLE failed.
cause: ORACLE was unable to convert a class component from binary format to ORACLE format.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system failure. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: conversion of category number to string failed.
cause: ORACLE was unable to translate a category number to its corresponding string representation failed.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system failure. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services. The category number is contained in the "Additional information" field.

description: Allocation of label string buffer failed.
cause: a temporary buffer used to hold a label could not be allocated.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system failure. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services. The number of bytes that ORACLE attempted to allocate is in the "Additional Information" field.

description: Conversion of label from string to binary failed.
cause: ORACLE was unable to convert the string representation of a label to binary format.
action: Re-enter a valid label.

description: Could not obtain user clearance.
cause: ORACLE was unable to get a user's clearance level.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system failure. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to get user's group ID from connection
cause: ORACLE was unable to retrieve the user's group ID number from the SQL*Net connection.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system error. Also check the "additional information" field for the SQL*Net error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to get process ID from connection
cause: ORACLE was unable to retrieve the user's process ID number from the SQL*Net connection.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system error. Also check the "additional information" field for the SQL*Net error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to initialize package.
cause: ORACLE was unable to initialize the library used to obtain security information.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to get user clearance from connection
cause: ORACLE was unable to retrieve the user's operating system session clearance from the SQL*Net connection.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system error. Also check the "additional information" field for the SQL*Net error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to get directory status
cause: ORACLE was unable to determine if a directory is multilevel.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to expand file name
cause: ORACLE was unable to expand the name of a file that resides in multilevel directory.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Audit file path name exceeds the maximum limit of 512 bytes.
cause: The buffer that was passed to hold the full path name of the audit file was too small. The maximum limit for the Linux platform is 512 bytes.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support.

description: Unable to set effective privileges
cause: This is an internal error.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Write to audit file failed.
cause: A failure occurred while writing an entry to the file used as the audit trail.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Number is too large
cause: ORACLE was unable to convert a component string to a number because the number is larger than the largest possible value for an integer. The additional information field specifies the maximum.
action: Correct the string and repeat the conversion.

description: Number exceeds maximum legal value
cause: the number specified for a component was greater than the maximum value allowed for that component.
action: Change the component to a value less than the maximum and repeat the conversion. The maximum component number is contained in the "Additional information" field.

description: Conversion of class string to numeric representation failed.
cause: ORACLE was unable to convert a class string to a number because all of the characters in the string were not numeric.
action: Change the string to be either all numbers or all non-numeric characters and repeat the conversion.

description: Numeric label is not valid
cause: A label specified in ORACLE numeric format was found not to be valid.
action: Re-enter a valid label. Consult your system's encodings for valid numeric component values.

description: Translation of audit file name failed.
cause: Oracle was unable to translate the value of the AUDIT_FILE_DEST initialization parameter.
action: Check the UNIX error number for a possible operating system error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: device name is too long
cause: The name of a device was too long to fit into an internal buffer. The additional information field contains the length of the device name.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to enable allowmacaccess privilege.
cause: ORACLE was not able to turn on allowmacaccess privilege so that it could do a label comparison.
action: Check the UNIX error number. If it indicates that ORACLE does not have the allowmacaccess privilege, add the allowmacaccess privilege to the potential privilege set of $ORACLE_HOME/bin/oracle using chpriv (1M). If the executable already has the allowmacaccess privilege, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Unable to disable allowmacaccess privilege.
cause: ORACLE was not able to turn off the allowmacaccess privilege after doing a label comparison.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: SCLIN: cannot initialize atomic latch.
cause: System call atomic_op() return error.
action: Check additional information in the trace file.

description: SCLGT: atomic latch return unknown error.

action: Check additional information in the trace file.

description: SCLFR: atomic latch return error.
cause: System call atomic_op() return unexpected error.
action: Check additional information in the trace file.
