cause: An attempt to generate a workload capture subset failed. Possible reasons are included in the error message.
action: Correct the issue and try again.

description: Failed to create subpath %s under path %s.
cause: Either the path does not exist, is inaccessible, or the subpath specification is invalid.
action: Verify that the path exists and is accessible, the subpath specification is valid, and retry the command.

description: force an idle session to flush in-memory captured data upon finish_capture()
cause: Idle sessions might lose in-memory workload capture data when the capture is about to finish.
action: No external action; used internally.

description: a user call cannot be replayed because not enough information was captured; extra details: %s
cause: An attempt to replay a user call failed because the workload was captured with an old version of Oracle. The information needed for replay was not recorded.
action: Capture the workload using a newer version of Oracle or use the replay filters to skip the user call.

description: failed to validate user password for capture
cause: One of the following occurred: 1- The password was not specified for the encrypted capture. 2- The password did not match the one used for the encrypted capture. 3- The specified password was for an unencrypted capture.
action: For scenario 1 or 2 stated in the Cause, provide the correct password for the encrypted capture. For scenario 3, do not specify the client single sign-on (SSO) wallet path.

description: failed to retrieve password for Database Replay from Oracle Wallet
cause: Either the Database Replay identifier was not found in the Oracle Wallet or the password was not set.
action: Set the password for the Database Replay identifier in the Oracle Wallet.

description: failed to encrypt a workload capture: "%s"
cause: An attempt to encrypt a workload capture failed. Possible reasons are included in the error message.
action: Fix the issue and retry.

description: failed to decrypt a workload capture: "%s"
cause: An attempt to decrypt a workload capture failed. Possible reasons are included in the error message.
action: Fix the issue and retry.

description: Directory contains a capture recorded with a newer Oracle release.
cause: The capture was recorded with a newer Oracle release.
action: Retry with a newer release of Oracle.

description: workload capture encountered unexpected error: %s
cause: Workload capture encountered an unexpected error.
action: Check the server trace files to address the reported error.

description: workload replay encountered unexpected error: %s
cause: Workload replay encountered an unexpected error.
action: Check the server trace files to address the reported error.

description: workload replay client cannot connect to database server
cause: The server connection identifier was invalid.
action: Restart the client with correct server connection identifier.

description: workload replay client cannot login to database server
cause: 1) the replay client used an invalid username or password; 2) the replay user does not have the privilege to switch user; 3) the recorded username does not exist in the replay database.
action: 1) restart replay client with correct username and password 2) grant user switching prvilege to the replay user 3) verify whether the replay database was restored properly

description: workload replay client cannot execute the DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPLAY package
cause: Workload Replay Client's replay user did not have EXECUTE permission on the DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPLAY package.
action: Grant execute permission on the DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPLAY package to replay user and restart the Workload Replay Client.

description: cannot start workload replay client because the database server is not in PREPARE mode
cause: The Workload Replay Client could not connect to the database server because the database server was not in the PREPARE mode.
action: Put the database in PREPARE mode by using DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPLAY.PREPARE_REPLAY, and restart the Workload Replay Client.

description: workload replay client encountered unexpected error: "%s"
cause: Workload Replay Client encountered an unexpected error.
action: Check the Workload Replay Client's log files and the database server alert log to diagnose the problem.

description: invalid input specified to the workload replay client; type 'wrc HELP=Y' for help
cause: Invalid input was specified.
action: Use the Workload Replay Client's HELP=Y option to know more about valid input options.

description: workload replay client cannot access the replay directory or the database version do not match the preprocessing one
cause: The Workload Replay Client could not access the directory that contained the workload to be replayed, or the workload was preprocessed by a different version of the database.
action: Restart the workload replay after specifying the correct replay directory, or preprocess it with the correct database.

description: replay thread encountered unexpected error
cause: A single replay thread got disconnected from the server due to an unexpected error.
action: Check the Workload Replay Client's log files and the database server alert log to diagnose the problem.

description: workload replay client cannot open workload capture file
cause: The Workload Replay Client could not access one or more workload capture files from the replay directory.
action: Restart the workload replay after copying all the workload capture files to the replay directory.

description: Workload replay client cannot access the work directory.
cause: The workload replay client could not access the work directory to write log files for debug information.
action: Restart the workload replay client after specifying an existing work directory, or ensure that the user has access privileges.

description: workload replay client cannot connect to the remapped connection with conn_id : %s
cause: The specified connection is invalid or the specified host is inaccessible.
action: Test the specified connection using other methods and redefine the connection remapping, if necessary. Consult the view DBA_WORKLOAD_CONNECTION_MAP to inspect connection remappings.

description: workload replay client cannot read the DBA_WORKLOAD_CONNECTION_MAP view
cause: The DBA_WORKLOAD_CONNECTION_MAP view did not exist or was not accessible.
action: Re-create the workload capture and replay views. For additional information, see the documentation.

description: workload replay client cannot spawn new threads
cause: The Workload Replay Client does not have enough resource (CPU or memory) to spawn new threads.
action: Restart the workload replay after allocating more resource (CPU and memory) to the Workload Replay Client or use more hosts as replay clients to drive the workload.

description: contents of the replay directory provided to the workload replay client do not match with the replay directory provided to the database server
cause: The processed workload capture files given to the workload replay client directory did not match the contents of the replay directory given as input to DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPLAY.INITIALIZE_REPLAY.
action: Provide the same processed workload capture files to both the database server and all the workload replay clients and restart the replay. If the same workload capture files were processed more than once, provide a copy of the latest processed workload capture files to all the workload replay clients and the database server.

description: workload replay client cannot replay user call in the current version
cause: The workload replay client encountered a user call in the captured workload that was not supported for replay in the current version.
action: Look in the DBA_WORKLOAD_REPLAY_DIVERGENCE view for details about the call that encountered this error. Refer to the documentation for more details on the types of workload that are not supported in the current version.

description: replay user %s encountered an error during a sanity check
cause: The replay user encountered an error when accessing internal objects for Database Replay or switching user.
action: Set up the replay user appropriately at the replay database. Ensure that the replay user can access SYS-owned objects and has been granted the BECOME USER privilege.

description: login of user %s during workload replay failed with ORA-%s
cause: The recorded user did not exist in the replay database or encountered other problems during log in.
action: Check the returned error number and set up the recorded user appropriately at the replay database.

description: timeout encountered during the replay of a recorded user call
cause: The replay of a recorded user call was terminated since it was significantly slower than the workload capture.
action: Find the root cause for the performance issue. Or, use DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPLAY API to disable the timeout check if the replay is expected to be slower.

description: Directory object "%s" does not exist.
cause: The directory object did not exist.
action: Ensure that the specified directory object exists.

description: encountered incomplete workload capture files
cause: The captured workload contained one or more incomplete recording files. This can happen when the original workload capture's FINISH_CAPTURE command timed out while waiting for all the active sessions to close their workload capture files.
action: Incomplete capture files will not interfere with the processing and replaying of the captured workload. This is simply a warning message to point out that some database calls might not have been recorded due to FINISH_CAPTURE command timing out.

description: corrupt workload capture files
cause: The captured workload contained one or more corrupt recording files.
action: Check the alert log for lines containing DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPLAY.PROCESS_CAPTURE after capture processing. The files will be replayed up to the point of the corruption. You could also remove the corrupt files and run DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPLAY.PROCESS_CAPTURE again. In this case, no workload from the corrupt files is replayed.

description: Last message reserved for WCR (KEC)
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Reserved for Automated Maintenance Tasks
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Invalid value specified for parameter "%s"
cause: An invalid value was specified for the given parameter.
action: Correct the value being specified for the parameter.

description: Parameter "%s" cannot be NULL.
cause: An attempt was made to call a procedure without a required parameter.
action: Specify a valid value for this parameter.

description: Action cannot be performed when database is in read-only mode.
cause: A procedure in DBMS_AUTO_TASK_ADMIN package was invoked when database was open in read-only mode.
action: Retry when database is open in read/write mode.

description: Initialization parameters prevent client from being enabled.
cause: An attempt was made to enable a client that was disabled for automatic execution by an initialization parameter.
action: Check the related client parameters and try again.

description: "%s" is not a Maintenance Window
cause: Window name passed to DBMS_AUTO_TASK_ADMIN.ENABLE procedure must be a member of the MAINTENANCE_WINDOW_GROUP.
action: Make the window a member of the MAINTENANCE_WINDOW_GROUP and retry the call.

description: Reserved autotask operations only allowed in root.
cause: An attempt was made to issue a reserved autotask operation in a pluggable database.
action: Switch to CDB$ROOT and issue the operation.

description: Autonomous task could not be scheduled. Reason: "%s".
cause: An attempt was made to schedule a manual Autonomous task but the operation failed. The possible causes were: - The task was disabled. - The task was currently running in another process. - The number of concurrently running autonomous tasks exceeded max limit.
action: Check the task status in adb_task views. Ensure that: - The task is enabled. - The task is not currently running in another process. - The number of concurrently running autonomous tasks is within max limit. Then, retry the operation.

description: Fail to read the Autonomous Task metadata from the persistent storage
cause: An attempt is being made to read Autonomous Task metadata from the persistent storage but the operation failed. The possible causes are: - Cannot get the enqueue within the specified time limit. - Other underlying errors were hit during the read operation.
action: Identify which enqueue cannot be grab by looking into the trace. Analyze the error stack to see if the failure is the consequence of other errors.

description: Last message reserved for Automated Maintenance Tasks (KET).
cause: NA
action: NA

description: invalid DIRECT_ACCESS command
cause: NA
action: NA

description: invalid option "%s" for "%s" in DIRECT_ACCESS command
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Fixed table "%s" does not exist.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Fixed table "%s" is not supported by DIRECT_ACCESS.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: No more than %s columns can be specified in a DIRECT_ACCESS SELECT query.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Fixed table "%s" cannot be accessed safely in prelim connection.
cause: NA
action: Run ORADEBUG DIRECT_ACCESS SET MODE=UNSAFE and query again.

description: DIRECT_ACCESS statement is too long.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Column "%s" does not have a fixed index defined.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Type is not supported type for DIRECT_ACCESS filters.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Multi-column indexes not supported for DIRECT_ACCESS filters.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: last message reserved for DIRECT_ACCESS
cause: NA
action: NA

description: SQL limit already reached by prior task execution
cause: An attempt was made to resume the execution of a task when the prior execution already reached the SQL limit.
action: Task execution is complete. Examine the report to review Advisor's recommendations.

description: All "SQL Tuning Set(s)" with name like "%s" and owner like "%s" are empty
cause: An attempt was made to pack one or more SQL Tuning Sets, none * of which contained any statements.
action: Check the input and try again.

description: duplicate values for plan line ID in input collection
cause: An invalid input was provided containing duplicate values for plan line IDs causing the load of the statement to fail.
action: Check the input and try again.

description: invalid version number "%d" for SQL tuning set staging table
cause: An invalid version number was provided for a staging table used to pack a SQL tuning set.
action: Check the input and try again.

description: This operation is not supported for Oracle RAS users.
cause: An attempt was made to execute an unsupported operation. This operation is not supported for Oracle Real Application Security (Oracle RAS) users.
action: Retry the operation as a non-Oracle RAS user.

description: staging table does not exist
cause: An attempt was made to use a staging table that did not exist.
action: Verify the name of the staging table and retry the operation.

description: concurrent execution of the task terminated unexpectedly
cause: Parallel slaves have died unexpectedly.
action: Check your system for anomalies and resume the executing task.

description: Default parameters for SPA Quick Check are not set.
cause: The required default parameters for SQL Performance Analyzer Quick Check (SPA Quick Check) were not set.
action: Set default values for all of the required SPA Quick Check parameters and try again.

description: invalid name "%s" for SQL Performance Analyzer task
cause: An invalid SQL Performance Analyzer task name was used.
action: Check the name of the SQL Performance Analyzer task to ensure that it is correct.

description: parameter "%s" not set for SQL Performance Analyzer task "%s"
cause: Could not find the specified parameter name for the SQL Performance Analyzer task.
action: Check that the specified parameter exists for the SQL Performance Analyzer task so that the parameter is set.

description: no COMPARE_PERFORMANCE execution exists for SQL Performance Analyzer task "%s"
cause: Could not find an execution of type COMPARE_PERFORMANCE for specified SQL Performance Analyzer task.
action: Ensure that the given SQL Performance Analyzer task has at least one execution of type COMPARE_PERFORMANCE.

description: specified execution name "%s" is not a valid COMPARE_PERFORMANCE execution for SQL Performance Analyzer task "%s".
cause: The specified execution name was not a valid execution of type COMPARE_PERFORMANCE for the SQL Performance Analyzer task.
action: Ensure that a valid COMPARE_PERFORMANCE execution name is used for the SQL Performance Analyzer task.

description: need to specify the object ID if the tuning task is on a SQL set.
cause: There could be multiple objects in the SQL tuning task. Specify which one.
action: Add object ID to the interface.

description: The directory name is null.
cause: The directory name for finding the SQL traces was null.
action: Create the directory.

description: The plan type is not valid.
cause: The specified plan type was not valid
action: Check the existing plan types and specify the right one.

description: Missing EXECUTE privilege on DBMS_AUTO_SQLTUNE.
cause: The current user was missing the necessary privileges to execute the API.
action: Grant the privilege and try again.

description: The previous Oracle Data Masking job is unfinished. "%s" table is not empty.
cause: The previously executed Oracle Data masking job was not successfully completed.
action: Execute Oracle Data masking cleanup.

description: invalid container name specified
cause: The container name specified for this API was invalid. When this API is run at the multitenant container database (CDB) root, the acceptable container names are any valid containers in that CDB. When it is run in a pluggable database, the only acceptable container name is its own name.
action: Specify a valid container name.

description: last message reserved for SQL tuning
cause: NA
action: NA

description: The current node is not configured for remote operations.
cause: An attempt to perform a Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation failed because the node attempting to perform the operation was not configured for remote operations.
action: Configure the node and retry the operation.

description: The Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation failed.
cause: An attempt to perform a Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation failed due to an unexpected error condition.
action: Retry the operation. Contact Oracle Support Services, if the operation continues to fail.

description: Current node is already configured for remote operations.
cause: An attempt to configure a node failed because the node was already configured for Remote Management Framework (RMF) operations.
action: Remove the node from the configuration and retry.

description: The node is not registered in an Remote Management Framework (RMF) topology.
cause: Attempt to perform a Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation failed because the node attempting to perform the operation was not registered in a topology.
action: Register the node in a topology, or create a new topology and retry.

description: A concurrent Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation is in progress.
cause: An attempt to perform a Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation failed because a concurrent RMF operation was already running.
action: Retry after the other operation has finished.

description: already registered in an RMF topology
cause: An attempt to register the specified node failed because the node was already registered in a Remote Management Framework (RMF) topology.
action: Ensure that the specified node name matches the node to be registered and that the database link connects to the intended node. Unregister the specified node before registering it into another topology.

description: RMF topology [%s] does not exist.
cause: A topology with the specified topology name was not created in the Remote Management Framework (RMF).
action: Verify that the topology name is valid and retry the operation.

description: RMF topology [%s] already exists.
cause: A topology with the specified topology name was already created in the Remote Management Framework (RMF).
action: Verify that the topology name is valid and retry the operation. Specify a different topology name that has not been used yet.

description: Node [%s] is not registered in Remote Management Framework (RMF) topology [%s].
cause: A node with the specified node name was not registered in the specified Remote Management Framework (RMF) topology.
action: Ensure that the specified node name and topology name is correct, and that the specified node is currently registered in the specified topology.

description: Node [%s] is already registered in Remote Management Framework (RMF) topology [%s].
cause: A node with the specified node name was already registered in the specified Remote Management Framework (RMF) topology.
action: Ensure that the specified node is not currently registered in the specified topology, and ensure that the node to be registered in the specified topology is configured with a unique name.

description: parameter [%s] is invalid: %s
cause: The value for the specified parameter was invalid.
action: Provide a value that fulfills the requirements specified in the error message.

description: parameter [%s] exceeds %s characters
cause: The value for the specified string parameter was too long.
action: Provide a value for the specified parameter that has a length below the character limit specified in the error message.

description: parameter [%s] does not allow NULL values
cause: A NULL value was provided for the specified parameter but the parameter only allows non-NULL values.
action: Provide a non-NULL value for the specified parameter.

description: parameter [%s] conflicts with the value in the remote node [%s]
cause: An attempt to perform a Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation failed because the specified parameter was different from the actual value stored in the node performing the operation.
action: Ensure that the database link connects to the intended node and that the specified parameter matches the value configured in the node that will perform the operation.

description: database not open in read/write mode
cause: An attempt to perform a Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation failed because the node was not open in read/write mode.
action: Ensure that the node performing the operation is open in the correct mode and retry the operation.

description: candidate target missing links to source nodes
cause: An attempt to perform a Remote Management Framework (RMF) destination switch failed because the candidate target could not find a link to one or more nodes in the topology.
action: Ensure the candidate target has an RMF link to every node participating in the topology and retry the operation. If the current RMF destination node is no longer available or the missing links cannot be created at this moment, retry the operation with FORCE_SWITCH to bypass this check.

description: remote node registration could not be completed
cause: An attempt to register a node in a Remote Management Framework (RMF) topology failed because the remote node could not obtain the registration information from the RMF destination node.
action: Ensure that the provided database links are valid and correspond to the intended nodes. Check for additional error messages, if any, to determine the exact cause of the problem and correct the error. Unregister the node from the topology and retry the operation.

description: link from %s to %s does not exist in topology %s
cause: An attempt to perform a Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation failed because a link between the specified nodes could not be found in the topology.
action: Verify the topology and nodes are correct. Create a link between the nodes in the specified direction using DBMS_UMF.CREATE_LINK and retry the operation.

description: RMF operation failed: %s
cause: An attempt to perform a Remote Management Framework (RMF) operation failed because an unexpected condition was encountered.
action: Check the exact error message and accompanying error messages, if any, for more information. If the situation described can be corrected, take appropriate action and retry the operation. Otherwise, contact Oracle Support Services for assistance.

description: Number of enabled APPMAP has reached the maximum limit of [%s].
cause: The APPMAP cannot be enabled because the maximum number of enabled APPMAP allowed in Automatic Workload Repository (AWR) has been reached.
action: Consider disabling an existing APPMAP before enabling additional ones. Retry the operation after disabling one or more existing APPMAP.

description: An APPMAP with name %s already exists.
cause: The APPMAP cannot be created because an APPMAP with the same name already exists.
action: Check the existing APPMAP list and consider whether a new APPMAP still needs to be created or if the existing one should be replaced. If the new one is needed, specify a name that does not conflict with existing APPMAP. Otherwise, if the existing APPMAP needs to be replaced, drop it and retry the operation.

description: AWR Analytics operation failed: %s
cause: An attempt to perform an Automated Workload Repository (AWR) Analytics Framework operation failed because an unexpected error condition happened.
action: Correct the indicated problem and retry the operation. Contact Oracle Support Services if the condition persists.

description: error encountered during SQL execution
cause: An error occurred when performing an Automated Workload Repository (AWR) Application Framework operation due to an underlying SQL execution error.
action: Retry the operation and contact Oracle Support Services if the condition persists.

description: parameter [%s] is invalid: %s
cause: The value for the specified parameter was invalid.
action: Provide a value that fulfills the requirements specified in the error message.

description: AWR Application Report is disabled
cause: The operation failed because the Automatic Workload Repository (AWR) Application Report feature was disabled..
action: Enable AWR Application Report and retry the operation.

description: Attempting to modify database or pluggable database that is open for read-only access.
cause: This database or pluggable database was open for read-only access. Attempts to modify the database using DML or DDL statements generated this error.
action: In order to modify the database or pluggable database, it must first be shut down and reopened with read/write access.

description: database already open for read-only access by another instance
cause: The database has been opened for read-only access by another instance, and cannot be opened for read/write access by this instance.
action: This instance must be opened for read/write access, or all other instances must first be shut down and reopened for read-only access.

description: database or pluggable database already open for read/write access by another instance
cause: The database or pluggable database has been opened for read/write access by another instance, and cannot be opened for read-only access by this instance.
action: This instance must be opened for read-only access, or all other instances must first be shut down and reopened for read/write access.

description: standby database is restricted to read-only access
cause: An attempt was made to open a physical standby database in read/write mode.
action: Reissue the ALTER DATABASE OPEN specifying READ ONLY.

description: backup database required recovery
cause: The database could not be opened for read-only access by this instance because it requires recovery.
action: Perform the necessary recovery and reopen for read-only access.

description: database requires recovery
cause: The database required recovery, and therefore could not be opened for read-only access by this instance.
action: If the database was terminated abnormally (possibly using a shutdown abort), the database first needs to be opened in read/write mode. Otherwise, perform the necessary recovery and reopen for read-only access.

description: The remote archival request was canceled due to a database shutdown operation.
cause: When opening or closing a database instance, the database may wait for pending remote archival requests to complete before proceeding with the operation. This error was reported because a shutdown was detected.
action: This is an informational message so no action is required.

description: invalid backup control file checkpoint
cause: The database could not be opened for read-only access because its control file did not contain a valid control file checkpoint.
action: Open the database for read/write access to create a valid control file checkpoint. The database can then be opened for read-only access.

description: indeterminate control file checkpoint
cause: The control file for the database being opened for read-only access was created using the CREATE CONTROLFILE statement. Therefore, a control file checkpoint could not be calculated and the database could not be opened for read-only access.
action: First, open the database for read/write access. This creates a valid control file checkpoint. Then, reopen the database for read-only access.

description: invalid redo transport destination
cause: Either the redo transport destination could not accept redo data because it was not a valid redo transport destination type, or the connection was SYNC for Zero Data Loss Recovery Appliance (ZDLRA) destination.
action: Verify that all redo transport destinations are either standby databases or downstream capture databases, or change the ZDLRA destination to not use SYNC.

description: disable stale RFS process extermination
cause: Disables the termination of RFS processes waiting for tcp_keepalive_interval to expire.
action: No action is required.

description: Remote File Server (RFS) process is in an error state.
cause: The Remote File Server (RFS) process at the specified redo transport destination experienced an unrecoverable error and was unable to receive further redo data. There may be additional information in the alert log and trace file.
action: Correct the problem at the redo transport destination.

description: database identifier mismatch
cause: The database identifier of a target physical standby, snapshot standby, or far sync did not match that of the primary database. See the alert log file for additional information.
action: Ensure that the database identifier of each physical standby, snapshot standby, and far sync matches that of the primary database.

description: log %s sequence# %s does not need archiving
cause: An attempt was made to archive the named file manually, but the file did not require archiving. The file had previously been successfully archived.
action: No action is required.

description: Log %s sequence# %s could not be archived successfully, there are no destinations available.
cause: You tried to archive the named log file, but the operation was unsuccessful. The archival of the log file failed because of one of the following reasons: - No archive log destinations were specified in the initialization file. - All destinations were found to be in an error state.
action: Verify that the archive log destinations are specified correctly. Review additional error messages provided in addition to this one to learn more about the cause. Common issues include running out of space on the file system/Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) disk group, or misspelled paths. In Oracle Data Guard environments, consider file name conversion parameters, database roles, and the database unique name.

description: log %s sequence# %s was not archived since destination is in no ARCHIVELOG mode
cause: An attempt was made to archive the named log to a destination, but the operation failed because the destination was not in ARCHIVELOG mode.
action: Enable ARCHIVELOG mode for all destinations and retry the operation.

description: archived log for thread %s sequence# %s unavailable
cause: Redo apply timed out waiting for the requested archived log file.
action: Verify that the primary database is still archiving redo data to the standby database and reissue the RECOVER STANDBY DATABASE command.

description: cannot use LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST without a primary archive destination
cause: The parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST was set to a non-NULL value when LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST was set to NULL explicitly.
action: Set LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST to a valid non-NULL value.

description: Cannot use %s with LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n or DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST.
cause: One of the following events caused an incompatibility: LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST or LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST parameter was in use when a LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) parameter was encountered while fetching initialization parameters. An ALTER SYSTEM ARCHIVE LOG START TO command was in effect when a LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter was encountered while fetching initialization parameters. A LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter was in use when an ALTER SYSTEM command was used to define a value for either the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST or LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST parameter. DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST parameter was in use when an attempt was made to use an ALTER SYSTEM or ALTER SESSION command to define a value for LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST or LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST.
action: Identify and remove any incompatible parameter definitions.

description: Cannot use %s with LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST or LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST.
cause: One of the following events caused an incompatibility: The LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST or LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST parameter was in use when the specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) or DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST parameter was encountered while fetching initialization parameters. The LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST or LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST parameter was in use when an attempt was made to use an ALTER SYSTEM or ALTER SESSION command to define a value for the specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n or DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST parameter. An ALTER SYSTEM ARCHIVE LOG START TO command was in effect when the specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter was encountered while fetching initialization parameters. An ALTER SYSTEM ARCHIVE LOG START TO command was in effect when an attempt was made to use an ALTER SYSTEM or ALTER SESSION command to define a value for the specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter.
action: Identify and remove any incompatible parameter definition.

description: fewer destinations available than specified by LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST
cause: The number of archive log destinations that could be used was less than the LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST parameter value.
action: Either adjust the log archive destination parameters, or lower the value of LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST.

description: session %s destination cannot be the same as session %s destination
cause: An attempt was made to change the first specified log archive destination parameter using ALTER SESSION to have a value that duplicates the session-level value of the second specified log archive destination parameter.
action: Specify a different session value for one of the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameters.

description: LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST cannot be NULL because LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST is non-NULL
cause: An attempt was made to change parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST to NULL when parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST was non-NULL.
action: Either set parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST to a non-NULL value, or set parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST to a NULL value.

description: system %s destination cannot be the same as session %s destination
cause: An attempt to change the first specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) parameter produced a destination that duplicated the session destination value of the second specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter. This error occurred when setting a non-NULL value with the ALTER SYSTEM command. Or, this error can occur when setting a NULL value with ALTER SESSION command, because then the associated system destination value may appear as a duplicate.
action: Specify a different destination value for the first specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter.

description: parameter %s cannot be parsed
cause: The value for the indicated LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) parameter could not be parsed. Common causes for this error are a misplaced equal sign, an unrecognized attribute, or an attribute that is missing a required value.
action: Correct the value for the indicated LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter.

description: parameter %s contains repeated or conflicting attributes
cause: The value for the specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) parameter contained either repeated attributes or attributes that conflicted with each other. If LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n role attribute is TRUE_CACHE, the database unique name cannot be in DG_CONFIG.
action: Correct the value for the indicated LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter.

description: parameter %s contains an invalid attribute value
cause: The value for the specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) parameter contained an attribute with an invalid value.
action: Correct the value for the indicated LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter.

description: parameter %s is missing a destination option
cause: The value of the specified parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) did not include a destination option. A destination option can be specified using either the LOCATION or SERVICE attribute.
action: Correct the value of the specified parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n to include either the LOCATION or SERVICE attribute.

description: new %s causes fewer destinations to be selected than LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST requires
cause: An attempt was made to change the indicated LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n or LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_STATE_n parameters (n = 1...31) to a value that reduces the number of archive log destinations to less than the value specified in the LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST parameter.
action: Either select different options for the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n or LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_STATE_n parameters, or reduce the value for the LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST parameter.

description: cannot change LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST, no archive log destinations defined
cause: An attempt was made to change the LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST parameter when there were no archive log destinations.
action: Define one or more archive log destinations using parameters LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST, LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST, or LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31). Then, change the value of parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST.

description: session specific change to the LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST parameter requires a LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n destination
cause: The following event caused an incompatibility: The parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST or LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST was in use when an attempt was made to change the LOG_ARCHIVE_MIN_SUCCEED_DEST parameter with an ALTER SESSION command.
action: Replace any LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST and LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST parameters with LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) parameters.

description: parameter %s destination string exceeds %s character limit
cause: The value for the specified parameter contained a destination string that exceeded the character limit.
action: Replace the destination value for the specified parameter with a character string that has a length less than or equal to the limit specified in the error message.

description: parameter %s destination string cannot be translated
cause: The value for the specified parameter contained a destination string that could not be translated.
action: Use a valid destination string in the specified parameter.

description: parameter %s destination cannot be the same as parameter %s destination
cause: An attempt was made to change the first specified archive log parameter to have a destination value that duplicates the system-level destination value of the second specified archive log parameter.
action: Specify a different value for one of the archive log parameters.

description: Recovery could not be started.
cause: Database recovery could not be started because the FROM and MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE clauses were both specified when attempting to start recovery.
action: Retry the command with either the FROM or MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE clause, but not both.

description: missing required keyword %s
cause: The indicated keyword is required but was not specified.
action: Correct the syntax and retry the command.

description: invalid CANCEL option
cause: A mode other than IMMEDIATE followed the CANCEL keyword in RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE statement.
action: Specify either nothing or IMMEDIATE following CANCEL.

description: user requested cancel of managed recovery operation
cause: The managed standby database recovery operation has been canceled per user request.
action: No action is required.

description: log %s sequence# %s cannot be archived
cause: An attempt was made to archive the named file, but the file could not be archived.
action: Check the secondary error messages in the trace file to determine the cause of the error.
remediation: 1) The log cannot be archived, so redo will stall once it wraps. Check the destinations: `SELECT dest_id, status, error, destination FROM v$archive_dest WHERE status = 'ERROR';` 2) Most often the FRA is full -- follow ORA-00257. 3) Check the log group's state: `SELECT group#, sequence#, archived, status FROM v$log;` and `SELECT * FROM v$archive_dest_status WHERE status <> 'VALID';` 4) After clearing the underlying problem: `ALTER SYSTEM ARCHIVE LOG ALL;` 5) If a member is corrupt and the log is already archived elsewhere, `ALTER DATABASE CLEAR LOGFILE GROUP <n>;` -- use `CLEAR UNARCHIVED LOGFILE` only as a last resort, as it breaks recoverability and requires a fresh backup.

description: RFS request version mismatch
cause: A request to archive a redo log to a redo transport destination failed because of an Oracle software version mismatch at the destination.
action: Verify that a compatible version of Oracle software is running at the redo transport destination.

description: The destination archive log file is locked.
cause: The target archive log file was locked. This indicates that the file is being archived to another Remote File Server (RFS) process.
action: Ensure that each remote redo transport destination uses a unique network service name.

description: remote file server (RFS) unrecoverable error
cause: The Remote File Server (RFS) process at a redo transport destination encountered an error and was no longer available. Further redo transmission to this destination may not be possible.
action: Refer to the appropriate RFS trace file located at the redo transport destination for details regarding the error encountered and take corrective action.

description: user requested cancel immediate of redo apply
cause: Redo apply was canceled immediately per user request. Processing of the current archive log file has been interrupted and, therefore, the database is in an inconsistent state.
action: No action is required.

description: Redo apply has been canceled.
cause: Redo apply was canceled per user request or operation timeout.
action: More specific messages will accompany this message.

description: Destination %s attribute cannot be specified at session level.
cause: An attempt was made to modify a redo transport destination attribute using the ALTER SESSION command instead of the ALTER SYSTEM command.
action: Use the ALTER SYSTEM command to modify the destination attribute.

description: circular redo transport destination dependency chain
cause: An attempt was made to make a redo transport destination dependent on a redo transport destination that was already dependent on it.
action: Ensure that no redo transport destination is dependent on any destination that is already dependent on it.

description: The redo transport destination failed due to failed dependent destination.
cause: The redo transport destination was dependent on another destination, which failed. Therefore, this destination failed.
action: No action required.

description: DGID mismatch between destination setting and target database
cause: The DB_UNIQUE_NAME specified for the destination does not match the DB_UNIQUE_NAME in the target database.
action: Ensure that the DB_UNIQUE_NAME specified in the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter matches with the DB_UNIQUE_NAME parameter defined at the destination.

description: enable simulated error on archive log write
cause: Caused an I/O error to be signaled during the writing of an archival operation.
action: No action is required.

description: simulated error on archive log write
cause: An I/O error was returned for a simulated archival failure during an archival operation.
action: No action is required.

description: Destination exceeded quota size.
cause: Attempted to create an archive log in a destination with a maximum quota size and whose quota would be exceeded by this creation. The destination has been set as inaccessible for future archival operations.
action: Increase the quota size, if appropriate. Remove unneeded archive logs.

description: parameter %s contains an invalid delay time
cause: The value for the specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) parameter contained a DELAY attribute with an invalid numeric value. The valid range is 0-5760 (in minutes).
action: Correct the value for the specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter.

description: DB_UNIQUE_NAME attribute is required
cause: The DB_UNIQUE_NAME attribute was not specified. The value of the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter for each remote redo transport destination must contain the DB_UNIQUE_NAME attribute if the LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG parameter value contains the DG_CONFIG attribute.
action: Use the DB_UNIQUE_NAME attribute to specify the DB_UNIQUE_NAME for the destination.

description: DB_UNIQUE_NAME %s is not in the Data Guard Configuration
cause: The specified DB_UNIQUE_NAME was not in the Data Guard Configuration. Also, this problem could occur if a non-standby destination was specified with a DB_UNIQUE_NAME attribute that did not match the DB_UNIQUE_NAME initialization parameter for the current instance.
action: Specify a valid DB_UNIQUE_NAME if the DG_CONFIG attribute of the LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG parameter is enabled. The list of valid DB_UNIQUE_NAMEs can be seen with the V$DATAGUARD_CONFIG view.

description: test gap detection
cause: This is an Oracle internal event code to test the gap detection code.
action: N/A, this is an Oracle internal event code.

description: fetch archive log FAL request rejected
cause: Fetch archive log (FAL) server rejected a redo gap fetch request from the client. This may have various causes.
action: Check the alert log on the primary or cascading database. Take the appropriate action to solve the problem. Note that a snapshot standby database is not allowed to cascade redo, even through the FAL server.

description: Backup control file archival requires proper syntax.
cause: Attempted to perform an online log file archival using a backup control file. The USING BACKUP CONTROLFILE syntax was not specified.
action: Use the USING BACKUP CONTROLFILE clause to perform an online log file archival using a backup control file.

description: server not in Data Guard configuration
cause: The primary database or fetch archive log (FAL) server was not found in the Data Guard configuration of the standby database.
action: Add the database unique name of the primary database or FAL server to the DG_CONFIG attribute of the LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG database initialization parameter.

description: standby database instance not ready to receive redo log
cause: The Remote File Server (RFS) process on the standby database was not ready to receive the redo log. To receive the redo log, the physical standby, snapshot standby, and far sync databases must be mounted to receive the redo log. There could also be a role change or some other activity on the target database that requested for non-receipt of the redo log during that operation.
action: Check the standby alert log and RFS trace files for more information. Ensure that the database is mounted.

description: Cannot archive an empty or invalid log file.
cause: Attempted to archive an empty or invalid log file. See trace file or alert log file for additional information.
action: No action needed.

description: Log file is current.
cause: Attempted to archive current log file.
action: No action is required.

description: log file status has changed
cause: The online log file was reclaimed as a new log file either before the archival operation started or during this operation.
action: None.

description: standby database not in Data Guard configuration
cause: The standby database was not found in the Data Guard configuration of the server.
action: Add the database unique name of the standby database to the DG_CONFIG attribute of the LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG database initialization parameter.

description: A destination is being evicted from multi-destination ASYNC process.
cause: The LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter is unsuitable for the multi-destination ASYNC process. The network connecting to a destination might be significantly slower than the others.
action: No action is required. The destination can be managed by a single-destination ASYNC process.

description: redo decompression failed
cause: The incoming network buffer containing compressed redo could not be decompressed. See the alert log for additional information.
action: As a workaround, disable compression on the database that is sending this redo.

description: remote archival disabled at standby destination
cause: The receipt of remote archived redo log files was disabled at the associated standby destination host database.
action: Perform one of the following actions to resolve this issue: - Change the associated archive log parameter to specify a local destination with the LOCATION keyword, if appropriate. - Defer the associated archive log destination, if appropriate. - Set the standby REMOTE_ARCHIVE_ENABLE parameter to TRUE, if possible. - Enable the RECEIVE attribute of the LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG parameter. After performing one of these actions, restart the standby database instance before further attempts are made to archive redo log files.

description: remote archival disabled
cause: The remote archival of redo log files was disabled for this database. The associated archive log destination had been disabled. An archive log destination parameter had specified a remote destination with the SERVICE keyword.
action: Perform one of the following actions to correct the issue: - Change the archive log parameter to specify a local destination with the LOCATION keyword, if appropriate - Set the REMOTE_ARCHIVE_ENABLE parameter to TRUE, if appropriate - Enable the SEND attribute of the LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG parameter After performing one of these actions, restart the database instance before further attempts are made to archive redo log files.

description: activation identifier mismatch in archive log %s
cause: The activation identifier in the archive log file header did not match with the activation identifier of the database that was being recovered. The indicated archive log cannot be applied to the database.
action: Locate the appropriate archive log for the database.

description: redo log file activation identifier mismatch
cause: The activation identifier of the indicated redo log file does not match the activation identifier of the database.
action: NA

description: activation identifier mismatch
cause: Redo transport failed because the activation identifier of the primary and physical standby databases did not match. This could happen if the physical standby database was not created from a backup of the primary database.
action: Create a valid configuration and re-try the failed operation.

description: Parameter %s contains an invalid REGISTER attribute value.
cause: The specified LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n (n = 1...31) parameter value contained a REGISTER attribute that specified an invalid file name template string. If specified, the REGISTER file name template must indicate an operating system-specific file path name including thread and log sequence number substitution directives (%t, %T, %s, %S).
action: Correct the value for the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter.

description: archive log file %s was not found at dependency destination
cause: The specified archive log file was not found at a redo transport destination that was dependent on another destination.
action: Verify that all redo transport destinations that are dependent upon another destination or upon which other destinations are dependent are configured correctly.

description: A minimum of one SYNC standby database destination is required.
cause: No SYNC standby database archive log destinations were specified, and the protection mode requires at least one.
action: Specify a SYNC standby archive log destination in the initialization parameter file or change the protection mode to not require a SYNC standby archive log destination.

description: archiving must be enabled
cause: Online log file archiving is disabled.
action: Enable log file archiving.

description: No ARCH processes are active.
cause: All ARCH processes have stopped.
action: Restart the instance.

description: standby database destination mismatch
cause: Another instance had access to a standby database destination that this instance did not. If the initialization parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG does not define a DG_CONFIG, then this may be due to a standby database becoming unavailable recently.
action: Ensure that at each instance the set of standby databases referred to by LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter is the same and defines a DG_CONFIG at each instance to identify those databases explicitly. See the alert log file for more information.

description: unknown standby database destination
cause: A standby database destination was specified that was not accessed by another instance. If the initialization parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG does not define a DG_CONFIG, then this mismatch may be due to a standby database having been restarted recently.
action: Ensure that at each instance the set of standby databases referred to by LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter is the same and defines a DG_CONFIG at each instance to identify those databases explicitly. See the alert log file for more information.

description: simulate network transmission error
cause: Used for internal testing - DO NOT USE.
action: If set, value will be returned as error.

description: media recovery disabled
cause: The database was not in ARCHIVELOG mode, but ARCHIVELOG mode was required for the media recovery.
action: Place the database in ARCHIVELOG mode and retry the operation.

description: standby archival not enabled
cause: The standby database did not have archival enabled.
action: In order to allow the standby database to access the standby log files, the standby database must be in ARCHIVELOG mode.

description: invalid LogMiner session %s for APPLY
cause: Logical standby apply engine was started with an invalid LogMiner session identifier.
action: Fix the problem with the LogMiner session or create a new session.

description: insufficient number of processes for APPLY
cause: Logical standby apply engine was started with fewer processes available than needed.
action: Increase the values of the initialization parameters PROCESSES and or the MAX_SERVERS parameter seen in the DBA_LOGSTDBY_PARAMETERS view.

description: logical standby is not initialized correctly
cause: Logical standby apply engine was started but it found inconsistencies in its metadata.
action: Look in the trace file for more information.

description: LogMiner session has not been created
cause: Logical standby apply engine was started without creating a LogMiner session.
action: Create a LogMiner session and restart the apply engine.

description: an apply engine is already running
cause: A logical standby apply engine was running when another was created.
action: Shut down the previous apply engine before starting a new one.

description: apply engine related event
cause: NA
action: NA

description: redo cannot be written to the standby redo log
cause: The primary database was in MAXIMUM PROTECTION or MAXIMUM AVAILABILITY mode, but redo could not be written to the standby redo log at the standby database or databases.
action: Check the Remote File Server (RFS) trace file for specific errors and reconfigure the standby redo log as appropriate.

description: Switchover requires standby or current control file.
cause: An attempt was made to perform a switchover operation using a backup or clone control file.
action: Convert the backup control file into a current control file prior to attempting a switchover operation. A clone control file cannot be used for a switchover operation.

description: archive log has not been completely archived
cause: An attempt was made to register an archive log that has not been completely archived. The specified archive log may be a current log file.
action: Specify a completed archive log.

description: Archive log was already registered.
cause: Attempted to register an archive log that matched a branch, thread, and sequence entry in the control file.
action: Use V$ARCHIVED_LOG fixed view to verify the archive log information.

description: archive log to be replaced not created by managed standby process
cause: An attempt was made to replace an archive log entry that was not originally created by the managed standby process.
action: No user action required.

description: dependent archive log destination already archived
cause: An archive log destination contains a dependency to another archive log destination that has previously been archived.
action: The parent archive log destination cannot be dependent on another archive log destination. Use the ALTER SYSTEM command to remove one of the dependency attributes.

description: dependent archive log destination is not active
cause: An archive log destination contained a dependency with another archive log destination that was not active. The child archive log destination cannot be dependent on another inactive archive log destination.
action: Use the ALTER SYSTEM command to remove one of the dependent attributes.

description: dependent archive log destination is not LGWR-enabled
cause: An archive log destination contained a dependency with another archive log destination that was not enabled for the Log Writer (LGWR) process. The child archive log destination cannot be dependent on another archive log destination that is not archived by the LGWR process.
action: Use the ALTER SYSTEM command to change the parent archive log to specify the LGWR process.

description: Database shut down during archival operation.
cause: The database was shut down while an online log file archival was active.
action: None required.

description: dependent destination removal for inactivation
cause: A dependent archive log destination was inactive because the parent archive log destination became ineligible for archival. This may be because the parent destination was manually deferred by an application user.
action: None.

description: ALTER DATABASE COMMIT TO SWITCHOVER TO PHYSICAL STANDBY
cause: None
action: Specify this command to switch the primary database to the physical standby role.

description: ALTER DATABASE COMMIT TO SWITCHOVER TO PRIMARY
cause: None
action: Specify this command to switch the physical standby database to the primary role.

description: The primary database has been shut down to prevent data loss.
cause: The primary database was shut down because it was operating in maximum protection mode and no suitable standby databases were available to protect the primary database from data loss.
action: Diagnose and correct any errors that exist in the configuration or configure the primary database for maximum availability or maximum performance mode.

description: an internal error occurred at standby database
cause: The Remote File Server (RFS) process on the standby database received // an internal error.
action: Check the standby alert log and RFS trace files for more information.

description: not a valid Logical Standby database
cause: This database has not been completely configured as a Logical Standby database.
action: Verify that the database is the intended Logical Standby database. Ensure that you already started logical standby apply with the ALTER DATABASE START LOGICAL APPLY INITIAL statement. See the Oracle8i SQL Reference manual for the statement syntax.

description: a valid start SCN could not be found
cause: An SCN from which to start could not be found.
action: Register the first log file following the backup from which this database was generated. Using the ALTER DATABASE REGISTER LOGILE statement to register the database is recommended. Alternatively, you can provide a starting SCN value with this startement.

description: remote information is not available on the specified primary
cause: The new primary has not completed generating the necessary information for the standby to begin consuming its log stream.
action: Verify that the database link provided references a system that is about to become a new primary. Wait a short time before retrying the command to allow the primary some time to generate the necessary information.

description: Logical Standby apply must be stopped to allow this operation
cause: Logical Standby is currently applying changes. The apply must complete or be stopped to allow the requested operation.
action: Execute the ALTER DATABASE STOP LOGICAL STANDBY APPLY statement, then re-enter or respecify the operation.

description: Invalid Logical Standby parameter
cause: The specified parameter is not valid.
action: Check spelling or refer to the DBMS_LOGSTDBY PL/SQL package documentation for the correct statement syntax.

description: Logical Standby is already running in background
cause: A Logical Standby apply operation is already running.
action: none

description: loading previously applied transaction information
cause: Logical Standby coordinator was performing a scan to identify previously applied transactions.
action: No action necessary. This informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: all log data from primary has been processed
cause: On the primary system, the log stream has been ended by the ALTER DATABASE COMMIT TO SWITCHOVER TO LOGICAL STANDBY command.
action: Issue one of the following commands to make this standby a primary or resume applying changes from a new primary. ALTER DATABASE COMMIT TO SWITCHOVER TO LOGICAL PRIMARY; ALTER DATABASE START LOGICAL STANDBY APPLY NEW PRIMARY dblink;

description: database is no longer a standby database
cause: The current database has already been made a primary database.
action: Issue the following commands to make this primary a standby. ALTER DATABASE COMMIT TO SWITCHOVER TO LOGICAL STANDBY; ALTER DATABASE START LOGICAL STANDBY APPLY NEW PRIMARY dblink;

description: failed to apply log data from previous primary
cause: Log data from previous primary could not be completely applied.
action: Check DBA_LOGSTDBY_EVENTS for failures and take corrective action. Then, reissue command.

description: user procedure processing of logical standby apply DDL
cause: A user provided stored procedure has been called to inspect a DDL statement prior to it being processed.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record user involvement in the processing of a statement. Additional information can be found in the DBA_LOGSTDBY_EVENTS and the DBA_LOGSTDBY_SKIP views.

description: log mining and apply setting up
cause: This logical standby process is setting up to begin processing changes.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: Log mining and apply is stopping.
cause: The logical standby process is cleaning up and stopping logical standby apply.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: applying change to table or sequence %s
cause: The process is applying changes to a specific schema object.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: applying DDL transaction with commit SCN %s
cause: The process is applying a DDL change that's committed at the given SCN.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: %s% of LogMiner dictionary loading is done
cause: The process is loading dictionary information from the redo stream. This activity may take a few minutes.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: no work available
cause: The process is idle waiting for additional changes to be made available.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: processing
cause: The process is performing its primary function and is not waiting on any significant event.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: building transaction at SCN %s
cause: The transaction being committed at the given SCN is being prepared for apply.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: dependencies being computed for transaction at SCN %s
cause: The transaction committed at the given SCN is being analyzed for dependencies.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: applying transaction with commit SCN %s
cause: The transaction committed at the given SCN is being applied.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: applying large dml transaction at SCN %s
cause: A large transaction is being applied before the commit has been seen. The current redo being applied ends as the given SCN.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: transaction %s %s %s is waiting for commit approval
cause: The apply process is waiting for approval to commit a transaction. This transaction may depend on another or other synchronization activity may delay the committing of a transaction.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: transaction %s %s %s is waiting on another transaction
cause: The apply process is waiting to apply additional changes. This transaction likely depends on another.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: large transaction %s %s %s is waiting for more data
cause: The apply process is waiting until additional changes for a large transaction are retrieved from the log stream.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: loading table or sequence %s
cause: Information on the given table or sequence is being loaded into an in memory cache for future use.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: stalled waiting for additional transactions to be applied
cause: This process is waiting for additional memory before continuing. Additional log information cannot be read into memory until more transactions have been applied to the database, thus freeing up additional memory.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes. If this message occurs often and changes are not being applied quickly, increase available SGA or the number of apply processes.

description: User initiated stop apply successfully completed
cause: Logical standby was shutdown in an orderly fashion.
action: No action necessary, this informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes.

description: unsupported DML encountered
cause: One or more DMLs to an unsupported table were encountered and skipped.
action: No action necessary. This informational statement is provided to record the event for diagnostic purposes. Optionally, check the DBA_LOGSTDBY_EVENTS view for more information including the impacted table owner and name.

description: supplemental log information is missing from log stream
cause: Supplemental logging is not enabled at the primary database.
action: Issue the following command to enable supplemental logging. ALTER DATABASE ADD SUPPLEMENTAL LOG DATA (PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE INDEX) COLUMNS;

description: An error occurred during a terminal recovery of the standby database.
cause: An error occurred during a terminal recovery operation of the standby database.
action: Check the standby alert log for additional information.

description: An error occurred during activation of the standby.
cause: An error occurred during activation of the standby database following a Terminal Recovery.
action: Check the standby alert log additional information.

description: Datafile %s has incorrect terminal recovery stamp.
cause: After activation of a standby database following a terminal recovery (recovery of standby using current logs), recovery of a datafile from before the activation must have completed the same terminal recovery to avoid corruption.
action: A backup of the datafile taken after the terminal recovery and before activating the standby must be used for recovery.

description: invalid MANAGED recovery FINISH option
cause: A mode other than NOWAIT follows the FINISH keyword in RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE statement.
action: Specify either nothing or NOWAIT following FINISH.

description: invalid LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG modification while in protected mode
cause: The LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG parameter could not be modified if any of the Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) instances were opened in either the maximum protection or maximum availability mode. Also, this parameter could not be modified because it caused all destinations to fail while in maximum protection mode.
action: Modify the LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG parameter before opening the database in any instance.

description: Managed recovery is not active.
cause: There was an attempt to cancel a managed recovery session; but no managed recovery session was active.
action: No action needed.

description: invalid state change to a managed alternate destination
cause: An attempt was made to explicitly change the state of a destination participating in an internally managed set of alternate destinations. For example, a destination in the ALTERNATE state was explicitly changed to the ENABLED state. This change prevents the internal mechanisms from managing these cooperating destinations.
action: Reset the destination before changing the state of the destination.

description: end of log stream not received from primary
cause: The standby system has not received notification that the primary system log stream has been terminated. A graceful switchover is not possible.
action: Verify that the primary log stream has been terminated. Ensure that the standby has applied all necessary redo from the primary system and, if appropriate, reissue the graceful switchover command.

description: media recovery required
cause: An error has occurred while performing a switchover.
action: If you were switching a primary database to the standby role, the conversion was successful, but one or more errors occurred after the conversion completed. See the alert log for more information. You can proceed with switching the target standby database to the primary role, but you must address the errors reported at the old primary database before it can protect the new primary database. If you encountered this error while switching a physical standby database to the primary role, the switchover did not succeed because additional redo must be applied. Verify that redo apply is active and wait until the SWITCHOVER_STATUS column of the V$DATABASE dynamic performance view reports TO_PRIMARY or SESSIONS_ACTIVE before retrying the switchover.

description: standby online logs have not been recovered
cause: The standby database has online logs containing redo that has not been recovered. Activating the standby would lose redo contained in the online logs.
action: To recover the standby online logs issue the following command: ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE FINISH. Then reissue the ALTER DATABASE ACTIVATE STANDBY DATABASE command. To activate the standby without recovering the online logs, issue the following command: ALTER DATABASE ACTIVATE STANDBY DATABASE SKIP STANDBY LOGFILE.

description: enable simulated archive log error
cause: This is an internal event used to signal an error during an archival operation.
action: No action is required.

description: simulated archive log error
cause: Error returned for a simulated archival failure during an archival operation.
action: No action is required.

description: Connections to the remote file server (RFS) are not allowed during or after terminal recovery.
cause: An attempt was made, by a source database, to access a physical standby database during or after terminal recovery.
action: The primary database must not attempt to archive to a physical standby database during or after terminal recovery.

description: simulate RFS error while terminal recovery in progress
cause: Used for internal testing - DO NOT USE.
action: If set, value will be returned as error.

description: archival for thread# %s sequence# %s in progress
cause: The indicated archived log file is not available for recovery due to the fact that it is still being archived.
action: Verify that archival of the indicated log file has completed and reissue the RECOVER STANDBY DATABASE command.

description: %s control file enqueue unavailable
cause: The control file enqueue was currently unavailable.
action: No Action is required. The operation will be attempted at a later time.

description: standby database referenced by multiple archive log destinations
cause: Multiple archive log destinations referenced the same standby database using different service names. This is not allowed.
action: Remove one of the duplicate archive log destinations. See the alert log file for more information.

description: user requested expiration of managed recovery operation
cause: The managed standby database recovery operation has been canceled per user specified EXPIRE option of the RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE statement.
action: No action is required.

description: enable simulated ARCH RAC archival testing
cause: This is an internal test event to allow ARCH archival even when Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) is not enabled.
action: None.

description: FINISH recovery was performed on another, older standby database.
cause: An archive log containing a FINISH recovery indicator was received by a standby database that received archive logs in the future of the received archive log. Because of the possibility that these future archive logs have been applied to this standby database, the received archive log must be rejected. See the remote file server (RFS) trace file for additional information.
action: No action required, but you may want to check the remote file server (RFS) trace file.

description: managed standby recovery not available
cause: The attempted operation failed because of a pending CANCEL of the managed standby recovery operation.
action: Wait for the managed standby recovery session to end. Then retry the operation.

description: standby database is in 'no-data-loss' protected mode
cause: The attempted database operation is not allowed while the standby database is in 'no-data-loss' protected mode.
action: Verify that the attempted database operation is warranted, ALTER DATABASE SET STANDBY DATABASE UNPROTECTED and reissue the statement.

description: reserved for redo transport
cause: This event is reserved for redo transport.
action: This event is reserved for redo transport.

description: suspect attribute: %s
cause: Use of the specified attribute was invalid in the given context.
action: Make the appropriate changes and run the statement again.

description: enable arch procs to not exceed log_archive_max_processes
cause: disallow arch processes to exceed log_archive_max_processes in releases prior to 9i. Note that in 9i and subsequent releases this event is not required. We reserve this event for 9i and subsequent releases to allow us to backport the new log_arch_max_processes behavior for earlier releases.
action: No action is required.

description: LGWR archive log dependency not allowed if database is standby protected
cause: The use of a log writer (LGWR) archive log dependency was not allowed when the primary was protected by a standby database because this required the use of the standby redo log files.
action: Remove the LGWR archive log dependency and use non-dependent LGWR archival.

description: media recovery not allowed following successful FINISH recovery
cause: A RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE FINISH command has previously completed successfully. Another media recovery is not allowed.
action: Issue one of these operations following a FINISH recocvery: ALTER DATABASE OPEN READ ONLY or ALTER DATABASE COMMIT TO SWITCHOVER TO PRIMARY.

description: simulated failure during terminal recovery
cause: Causes an error to be signalled during terminal recovery.
action: No action is required.

description: cannot change protected standby destination attributes
cause: An attempt was made to change the Log Writer (LGWR) or synchronous (SYNC)/asynchronous (ASYNC) attributes for a destination that was participating in the standby protection mode of the database.
action: None.

description: cannot change protected standby database configuration
cause: An attempt was made to change the standby database configuration when the primary database is in standby protected mode.
action: Add the standby database to the configuration before opening the primary database.

description: Cannot mix standby and online redo log file members for group %s
cause: An attempt was made to add a log file member that did not match the other member types. This problem typically occurs when adding a standby log file member to an online redo log file group, or adding an online redo log file member to a standby redo log file group.
action: Verify the log file group type using the TYPE column of the V$LOG fixed view.

description: cannot add new standby databases to protected configuration
cause: An attempt was made to enable a new standby database destination when the primary database was in standby protected mode.
action: Add the standby database to the configuration before opening the primary database.

description: LGWR network server host attach error
cause: The Log Writer (LGWR) network server could not attach to remote host.
