action: Select and remove an existing member from the broker configuration, then reissue the command to add another member to the configuration. The maximum number of members permitted in a broker configuration is 253.

description: The Oracle Data Guard broker configuration already exists.
cause: A request to create or import an Oracle Data Guard broker configuration is being made while connected to a database that is part of an existing configuration; or to add a second Oracle Data Guard broker configuration with the same configuration name or DRC_UNIQUE_ID as the local configuration.
action: To create or import a new configuration, the existing configuration must be deleted. To add a second configuration, remove one of the configurations and re-create it, optionally with a different configuration name if it is the same as the first configuration. If the configurations have the same DRC_UNIQUE_IDs, the act of re-creating results in a different DRC_UNIQUE_ID. Once both configurations have different names and DRC_UNIQUE_IDs, reissue the ADD CONFIGURATION command.

description: site identifier is invalid
cause: The request contained an invalid site identifier. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: out of memory
cause: Process exceeded private or shared memory limits.
action: Check for memory leaks, increase system parameters, and restart.

description: unrecognized request identifier
cause: The specified request identifier was not recognized by the Oracle Data Guard broker. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: channel handle not initialized
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: request timed out
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker timed out the request.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for more information. Ensure that the network connections between the databases are functioning properly and retry the request.

description: messaging error using ksrwait
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: messaging error using ksrget
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: parameter exceeded maximum size limit
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: maximum requests exceeded
cause: The maximum number of requests that the broker can service on the database instance was exceeded.
action: Wait for the broker to complete processing the requests before issuing more requests.

description: request was not found
cause: An attempt was made to read a response but a matching request was not found. This is an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: no receive channel
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: current state is invalid for the attempted operation
cause: The broker may have returned this error for either switchover operations or for database state change operations. If this error was returned for a switchover operation, the broker determined that either: - The databases changing roles were shut down. - The primary database was not shipping redo data. - The standby database that will become the primary database was not applying redo data. If this error was returned for database state change operations, the database state specified was invalid.
action: If this error is returned when attempting a switchover operation, ensure that: - The databases changing roles are started. - The primary database is shipping redo data. - The standby database is applying redo data. If this error is returned when attempting a database state change operation, ensure that a valid database state is specified.

description: Data Guard broker simulated error.
cause: This was a simulated error returned for testing purposes.
action: None.

description: unable to allocate virtual instance ID
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Resource handle is invalid.
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: unable to allocate resource ID
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Service name specified in connect identifier connects to a PDB.
cause: The connect identifier that was specified resulted in a connection to a pluggable database (PDB) and not to the multitenant container database root.
action: Check the connect identifier and confirm that it specifies a service name that results in a connection to the multitenant container database root.

description: The configuration is part of the Global Data Services pool.
cause: The attempted command was not allowed because the configuration was part of a Global Data Services pool.
action: Remove the configuration from the Global Data Services pool using GDSCTL. Then, retry the broker command. If the command was attempting to repair a database, then disable or remove the individual database from the configuration and fix the issue. After the problem is resolved, re-enable the database, or add the database back to the configuration if it had been removed.

description: Switchover or failover operation requires client connection to instance "%s".
cause: The switchover or failover operation required the client to connect to the apply instance of the specified database.
action: Connect to the specified instance and retry the command.

description: unsupported command, option, or argument
cause: A command, option, or fast-start failover condition argument was specified that is not supported in this release.
action: If trying to enable or disable a fast-start failover condition, try a different Oracle error number. Otherwise, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: The Oracle Data Guard broker is not yet available.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker process was either not yet started, was initializing, or failed to start.
action: If the broker has not been started, set the DG_BROKER_START initialization parameter to true and allow the broker to finish initializing before making the request. If the broker failed to start, check the Oracle Data Guard log for possible errors. Otherwise, retry the operation.

description: Unable to allocate memory to process request.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker was unable to allocate memory for a request.
action: Increase the size of the System Global Area (SGA).

description: Unable to create output file for broker configuration metadata.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker was unable to create the output file to capture the contents of the broker configuration metadata.
action: Verify space, permissions, and the file name specified to ensure that the file can be created.

description: Unrecognized role change event for reinstatement.
cause: The Data Guard broker did not recognize the role change event that required a database to be reinstated. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Switchover and failover operations are restricted to databases specified in the PrimaryDatabaseCandidates configuration property.
cause: An attempt is being made to switchover or failover to a database that is not specified in the PrimaryDatabaseCandidates configuration property.
action: Check the value of the PrimaryDatabaseCandidates configuration property and specify a database for switchover or failover that is listed. Alternatively, add the database that was specified in the switchover or failover command to the PrimaryDatabaseCandidates configuration property or reset the property value.

description: invalid buffer or length
cause: A NULL buffer or a length of zero was specified.
action: Correct the command parameters and retry the command.

description: Process %(1)s failed to publish a command message to process %(2)s.
cause: The sending process failed to publish a message to the receiving or destination process. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker configuration does not exist.
cause: The broker operation could not be performed because the broker configuration did not exist.
action: Create a Data Guard broker configuration prior to attempting the operation. If only one instance of an Oracle Real Application Cluster (RAC) database reports this error, verify that the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters are set to shared file locations accessible to all RAC instances.

description: error for Oracle Data Guard broker system state dump
cause: This was an Oracle internal error message used when the Oracle Data Guard broker component signaled a system state dump. DO NOT USE.
action: No action is necessary. This is an Oracle internal error message code.

description: Switchover, failover or convert operation is in progress.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker returned this status because a switchover, failover or convert operation was in progress. The broker could not accept new commands until the operation finished.
action: Wait until the operation is complete and retry.

description: Oracle Restart or Oracle Clusterware prevented completion of broker operation.
cause: The broker could not complete the operation because Oracle Restart (for single instance databases) or Oracle Clusterware (for Oracle RAC databases) could not stop services or instances on this database.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for more information and stop the appropriate services or instances using SRVCTL. Then retry the broker operation.

description: unrecognized member type specified in request
cause: The member type specified in the request was not recognized by Oracle Data Guard broker. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: The property PrimaryDatabaseCandidates does not contain current primary database.
cause: A switchover or failover operation was performed using SQL*Plus, or a failover was performed to a database that is not specified in the PrimaryDatabaseCandidates configuration property.
action: When Data Guard broker is used to manage a Data Guard configuration, use DGMGRL or Oracle Enterprise Manager to perform switchover and failover operations. If this error was returned after doing a failover operation, a failover was attempted to a standby database that had not been specified in the PrimaryDatabaseCandidates configuration property.

description: Unrecognized property or state name.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker did not recognize the specified property or state name.
action: Check that the name of the property or state exists and then retry the command with a valid property or state name.

description: task element not found
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: invalid argument
cause: One of the arguments for the specified command was invalid.
action: Verify the arguments and then reissue the command.

description: member is not enabled
cause: An attempt was made to modify or query a disabled member. This error is also returned when an attempt is made to enable, modify, or query a member that the broker has disabled because of a switchover or failover operation. The broker disables its management of a member when it detects that the database needs to be re-created because of a failover or switchover operation.
action: If broker management of the member is disabled, re-create it if necessary, enable it and reissue the command.

description: unrecognized operation
cause: This was an internal error caused by an unrecognized XML document.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: An invalid request was made to the Oracle Data Guard broker.
cause: The input XML document sent to the Oracle Data Guard broker was either NULL or contained invalid arguments. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: modifying DG_BROKER_START requires SID='*' qualifier
cause: The setting for the DG_BROKER_START parameter must be exactly the same on all RAC database instances. The SID='*' qualifier was required in the command.
action: Reenter the command using the SID='*' qualifier.

description: Client did not receive a response to a prior request from the Data Guard broker.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker was unable to return the result of a previous request to the client. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: missing or invalid value
cause: The value of the request to return was not specified or was invalid. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Cannot disable or remove the primary database.
cause: An attempt was made to disable broker management of the primary database or remove the primary database from the broker configuration while the configuration was enabled.
action: To disable the primary database, disable the configuration. To remove the primary database, remove the configuration.

description: SQL Apply encountered one or more corrupt log files.
cause: SQL Apply encountered a corruption while reading redo records from one or more foreign archived logs and re-fetching a new copy of the archived log did not resolve the problem.
action: Query the APPLIED column of the DBA_LOGSTDBY_LOG view to determine which logs are corrupt (the column value will contain "CORRUPT"). Manually copy and register a new copy of the foreign archived log so that SQL Apply can continue.

description: invalid string
cause: An invalid or NULL string value was specified.
action: Correct the command parameters and retry.

description: truncated result
cause: A string property value was truncated due to insufficient buffer size.
action: Specify a larger receive buffer.

description: short string copied - information only - no action required
cause: A string property value that did not fill the receive buffer was placed in the receive buffer.
action: No action needed; this situation did not cause the software to stop. This is an informational message only.

description: error occurred while generating directives for client
cause: The client could not provide the required assistance to the broker because of the accompanying error.
action: See the accompanying error message for more information and follow the directions provided in the Action of that message. Then, retry the operation.

description: the specified database is in PrimaryDatabaseCandidates
cause: An attempt is being made to disable or remove a database in PrimaryDatabaseCandidates.
action: Remove the specified database from PrimaryDatabaseCandidates. Then retry the command.

description: Member is not active.
cause: Attempted an operation on an inactive member.
action: Verify that the member is active and retry.

description: Observer version incompatible with Oracle database server version.
cause: Observer version was incompatible with the Oracle database version to which the observer attempted to connect.
action: Use an observer version compatible with the Oracle database server being observed.

description: Member already exists in the configuration.
cause: Attempted to create a duplicate member in the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration, or to add a duplicate instance (SID) for an existing member in the configuration.
action: Check the configuration to avoid duplicate members.

description: database specified for switchover is not a standby database
cause: An attempt was made to switchover to a database that was not a standby database.
action: Locate an enabled standby database and select that database as the target of the switchover.

description: out of memory at %s
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: unable to convert document, syntax error at "%s"
cause: There was an error in the specified string.
action: Correct the errors and submit the request again.

description: cannot remove an active instance
cause: The instance to be removed was running.
action: Shut down the instance and reissue the REMOVE command.

description: INTENDED_STATE not specified, syntax error at "%s".
cause: The XML document did not specify an INTENDED_STATE value. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: unable to add value, syntax error at "%s"
cause: There was an error in the specified string.
action: Correct the errors and submit the request again.

description: lookup failed, syntax error at %s
cause: There was an error in the specified string.
action: Correct the errors and submit the request again.

description: duplicate property, syntax error at "%s"
cause: A property with the same name was specified twice during an add operation. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: unsupported document type
cause: The XML document type was not supported.
action: Correct the errors and submit the request again.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker internal parser error at "%s"
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: cannot set property %s
cause: The specified property could not be modified because it was either a monitorable property or a property that did not exist.
action: Retry the command with a valid configurable property.

description: Oracle Data Guard configuration is not enabled.
cause: The command could not be completed because broker management of the Oracle Data Guard configuration was not enabled.
action: Enable the Oracle Data Guard configuration and reissue the command.

description: Database needs to be restarted.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker operation required this database instance to be shut down and restarted.
action: If DGMGRL or Oracle Enterprise Manager has not already done so, restart the database instance.

description: Oracle Data Guard configuration file creation failure.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker was unable to create the configuration file on permanent storage.
action: Verify space, permissions and file name as indicated by the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters and retry the operation.

description: Oracle Data Guard configuration file not found.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker configuration file was either unavailable or did not exist.
action: Verify that the configuration file was successfully created. If the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters were changed, then check that the file name on disk and the parameter value match, that there is space on the device, and that the proper permissions are granted. For an Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) database, check that the initialization parameters are set to file locations that are accessible and shared by all instances of the Oracle RAC database.

description: attempt to change or access configuration file for an enabled broker configuration
cause: The operation was rejected because the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration file was in use. The attempted operation was unsafe while broker management of the configuration was enabled. For example: - An attempt was made to alter the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters while the broker was running. - Non-broker access (such as DBMS_FILE_TRANSFER) to the configuration files was attempted. See the alert log for additional information.
action: Disable the broker configuration and shut down the Oracle Data Guard broker, then retry the operation. If the operation includes altering the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters, be sure that the new parameter values correctly specify the files at their expected location before reenabling broker management of the configuration.

description: Switchover is disallowed when required databases are shut down.
cause: Switchover failed because either the primary database or the designated standby database was shut down.
action: Ensure that the primary and standby databases are running and that primary database is shipping redo data to the designated standby database. Also ensure that the designated standby database is applying the redo data received from the primary database.

description: LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter conflicts with the new member to be added
cause: One or more LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameters on existing members were already set for the new member to be added when attempting to add a standby database, far sync instance, Recovery Appliance, or external destination to the configuration.
action: Clear the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter that specifies the standby database, far sync instance, Recovery Appliance, or external destination to be added.

description: Failed to update Data Guard broker configuration file.
cause: The broker failed updating the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration file on permanent storage.
action: Verify that sufficient space exists on the device containing the the configuration files and the files specified by the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters permit read and write access.

description: Corruption detected in Data Guard configuration file.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected errors while loading the configuration file.
action: Verify space, permissions and file name as indicated by the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters. Contact Oracle Support.

description: failed to read Oracle Data Guard configuration file
cause: A failure was encountered while the broker was reading the configuration file on permanent storage.
action: Verify that sufficient space exists on the device containing the the configuration files and the files specified by the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters permit read and write access.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker network process failed.
cause: This was an internal error caused by the unexpected termination of the Oracle Data Guard broker network process.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: bad network link
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker could not reach remote member.
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Cannot change an instance-specific property.
cause: An attempt was made to change an instance-specific property for a member that had more than one instance.
action: Retry the command and identify a specific instance whose property value is to be changed.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker has a bad connection process state.
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: operation cannot be performed on a standby database
cause: The database specified for the operation was a standby database, or the operation was attempted on a standby database.
action: Check the database type and retry the operation. If the command must be executed on a primary database, connect to the primary database and retry the operation.

description: This operation cannot be performed on a primary database.
cause: The database specified for the operation was a primary database, or the operation was attempted on a primary database.
action: Check the database type and retry the operation. If the command must be executed on a standby database, then connect to a standby database and retry the operation.

description: Cannot change member property with EDIT INSTANCE command.
cause: Attempted to change a member level property using an EDIT INSTANCE command instead of an EDIT DATABASE, EDIT FAR_SYNC, or EDIT RECOVERY_APPLIANCE command.
action: Use the EDIT DATABASE, EDIT FAR_SYNC, or EDIT RECOVERY_APPLIANCE command to change member level properties.

description: Ambiguous member specified to Oracle Data Guard broker.
cause: A member was specified that the broker could not uniquely distinguish from other members in the configuration.
action: Try to further distinguish the member specified for the operation and retry the command.

description: The primary database was added to property PrimaryDatabaseCandidates
cause: Data Guard broker added the primary's DB_UNIQUE_NAME to property PrimaryDatabaseCandidates since the specified property value does not contain current primary.
action: NO

description: Oracle Data Guard broker detected a network transfer error.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected an error while transferring data from one member to another. This may happen when either the Oracle Data Guard broker: - Detected an inconsistency in the block count of the configuration file when the file is transmitted between members - Encountered an error when writing the configuration file. - A member received an incorrect message from another member.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Oracle Data Guard configuration does not contain a primary database.
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: There is an unknown field "%s" in the XML document.
cause: The XML document contained an unrecognized field. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: There is a missing field "%s" in the document.
cause: The XML document was missing a required field. This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: XML conversion failed
cause: There was an error in the XML document.
action: Correct the errors and submit the request again.

description: DMON background process is not running
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker background process, DMON, was not running.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and DMON process trace file to determine why the DMON process is not running.

description: process %s failed to terminate
cause: The specified process did not terminate at the request of the Data Guard broker.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Member is not part of the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration.
cause: The member was not in the Data Guard broker configuration.
action: Retry the command using a member in the Data Guard broker configuration.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker detects two or more primary databases.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected two or more primary databases in the broker configuration and could not continue.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker detected a mismatch in configuration.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected a significant mismatch while performing configuration membership validation between two or more members in the broker configuration. This can occur when the primary database has stale broker configuration files.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker detected a stale configuration
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected a stale configuration during initialization for this member.
action: The broker will automatically resolve this situation once the primary database completes its initialization.

description: Client is not connected to target standby database.
cause: The SWITCHOVER or FAILOVER command failed because the client was not connected to the target standby database.
action: Explicitly connect to the standby database that is to become the the new primary and retry.

description: site contains required resources that are disabled
cause: Resources required to complete this command were disabled.
action: Enable all required resources and reissue the command.

description: The member must be disabled to perform this operation.
cause: An attempt was made to edit a member property while the member was enabled.
action: Disable the member and retry the command.

description: The member is part of another Oracle Data Guard broker configuration.
cause: The member was part of another Oracle Data Guard broker configuration. This could occur if the original configuration was re-created while this member was disconnected from the network or the same member was added to two different Oracle Data Guard broker configurations.
action: Ensure that the member belongs to only one broker configuration. Shut down the broker by setting the DG_BROKER_START initialization parameter to 'false'. Then, remove the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration files. Finally, restart the broker by setting the DG_BROKER_START initialization parameter to 'true'.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker configuration file '%s' is inaccessible.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker was unable to access the configuration file specified by the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters.
action: Verify space, permissions and file name as indicated by the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters.

description: unable to find property "%s"
cause: The specified property did not exist.
action: Specify a valid property name and reissue the command.

description: One or more members have failed.
cause: A failure was detected for one or more members in the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration.
action: Locate the member or members with a failure status and correct it.

description: one or more members have warnings
cause: A warning was detected for one or more members of the Data Guard broker configuration.
action: Locate the member or members with warning status, and correct it.

description: Database is being disabled.
cause: Attempted a command on a database that was being disabled. For example, attempted to reinstate the old primary database, the database that was the primary database prior to the most recent failover, before it was ready to be reinstated.
action: Wait for Oracle Data Guard broker to disable the database then retry the command.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker command "%s" in progress.
cause: Specified Data Guard broker command was already running and could not be completed.
action: Wait for the specified command to finish and then retry.

description: command aborted at user request
cause: The command was aborted at the user's request.
action: No action required.

description: string value too long for attribute "%s"
cause: The string value for the named attribute was too long.
action: Specify a shorter string value.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker initialization in progress for member.
cause: A request was made that required access to the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration before it had completed initialization.
action: Wait until the Oracle Data Guard broker has completed initialization, then reissue the command.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker configuration is disabled.
cause: An attempt to enable a member failed because the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration was disabled.
action: Enable the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration and issue the DGMGRL CLI SHOW CONFIGURATION command to see if there are any members that are still disabled. If the member you tried to enable is still disabled, then issue the DGMGRL CLI SHOW command to check the status of the member. If the member is a database whose status indicates that the database must be reinstated, then issue the DGMGRL CLI REINSTATE DATABASE command to reinstate and enable the database. If the member does not require reinstatement, then issue the DGMGRL CLI ENABLE command to enable the member.

description: testing event for Oracle Data Guard broker network process
cause: This is an Oracle internal event code.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: event for Data Guard monitor testing
cause: This is an Oracle internal event code. This event is used for verifying Monitor functionality in Data Guard. DO NOT USE.
action: N/A, this is an Oracle internal event code.

description: unrecognized member specified in request
cause: The member specified in the request was not part of the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration.
action: Check the member name specified in the request. Confirm that the member specified appears in the output of the DGMGRL SHOW CONFIGURATION command. Retry the request using one of the the member names shown in the SHOW CONFIGURATION command output.

description: response document of size "%s" bytes is too large
cause: The document response could not be returned because the size of the document was too large.
action: View the broker log file for the given member directly.

description: condition for fast-start failover is already enabled
cause: The condition specified for fast-start failover was already enabled.
action: No action is required. Use the DGMGRL CLI SHOW FAST_START FAILOVER command to view the conditions that are enabled.

description: one or more members could not be reached for a remove operation
cause: One or more members could not be reached for either a DGMGRL CLI REMOVE DATABASE, REMOVE FAR_SYNC or a REMOVE CONFIGURATION command.
action: This typically indicates a network problem where the member is unable to respond to the primary database. If this is the case, examine the primary database Oracle Data Guard broker log file to determine which members cannot be reached. For each member not reached, connect to that member and shut down the broker by setting the DG_BROKER_START initialization parameter to 'false'. After the broker has been shut down for the member, locate the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration files from the member's DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameter values and delete them. Then, restart the broker by setting DG_BROKER_START to 'true'.

description: A member with that name already exists in the configuration.
cause: An attempt was made to add a member to the broker configuration that already included a member with the specified name. The member names must be unique.
action: Verify that a unique name is specified for the new member to be added. Also, the member name must match the DB_UNIQUE_NAME initialization parameter of the member.

description: two or more broker member objects resolve to the same member
cause: Multiple member objects referred to the same member.
action: Examine the details of all members in the broker configuration and verify that two or more members are not referring to the same member. If two or more members in the broker configuration have the same value for the DGConnectIdentifier configurable property, either: - Remove and re-add the incorrectly defined member or members to resolve the ambiguity. - Ensure that the DGConnectIdentifier configurable property for each member allows the broker to properly connect to that member.

description: member detected role change
cause: A successful switchover or failover operation had been completed and was detected during member startup or broker health check. If this member was a database that was unavailable during a switchover or failover operation, it may not be a viable standby database for the new primary database and was disabled by the Oracle Data Guard broker.
action: Connect to the new primary database and examine the broker configuration for databases that were disabled and that may require reinstatement or re-creation.

description: broker protocol version mismatch detected
cause: A network protocol version number mismatch was detected. This could happen if the members in the broker configuration were not running the same version of Oracle. The broker would disable members that were not running the same version of Oracle as the primary database if this situation was detected.
action: Examine the version of Oracle installed on all members in the broker configuration to ensure they are identical. Once all of the members in the broker configuration are running the same version of Oracle, reenable the members that were disabled.

description: cannot reach member "%s"
cause: The command could not be executed because the member noted in the error text was not reachable.
action: See accompanying messages for more information. Check the network connections to the specified member. After ensuring connectivity, retry the command.

description: failed to enable specified member
cause: This status was returned when attempting to enable a member that: - Could not locate itself in the broker configuration file. - Failed to distinguish itself from two or more members in the configuration file. - Determined it missed a role change within the configuration.
action: To correct the problem, try one of these actions: - Confirm that the host and SID names for the member exactly match the values in the HOST_NAME and INSTANCE_NAME columns of the V$INSTANCE view. - Confirm that two or more members do not have the same connect identifier. That is, multiple members in the broker configuration should not reach the same member. - If a failover has been performed and the old primary database has been re-created (or a standby database has been re-created), then ensure that the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration files have been removed for that database. Do not remove the configuration files that are in use by the new primary database.

description: No member available to support the protection mode.
cause: Either there are no standby databases in the configuration whose redo transport mode supports maximum protection mode, or an operation is being attempted that would result in no standby database remaining to support maximum protection mode. This prevents the current operation from completing successfully.
action: Ensure that at least one standby database has its redo transport mode set to SYNC mode before attempting the operation again. Alternatively, consider lowering the protection mode to maximum availability or maximum performance.

description: broker protection mode inconsistent with the database setting
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker protection mode saved in the broker configuration file was inconsistent with the actual database setting.
action: Reset the protection mode through the Oracle Data Guard broker.

description: Database reports a different protection level from the protection mode.
cause: The current database protection level was different from the configured protection mode. This was typically caused if there were redo transport problems or if the primary database was not open.
action: Check: - The database alert log files and Oracle Data Guard broker log files for more details. - The redo transport status. - That one standby database supports the configured protection mode. - That the network to that standby database is working properly. - That the primary database is open.

description: configurable property has been deprecated
cause: The property that was specified in the command was deprecated.
action: Check the broker documentation to identify a replacement property.

description: operation requires shutdown of database or instance "%s"
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker operation required a shutdown of the database or instance.
action: If the database or instance has not been shutdown by the DGMGRL CLI or Oracle Enterprise Manager, then shut down the database or instance manually.

description: instance being added to member profile
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker determined that an instance successfully found its member profile within the broker configuration file, but lacked an instance-specific profile. The broker automatically created an instance-specific profile and associated the instance with its database profile.
action: No user action is required. The broker will automatically associate the instance with its member profile and incorporate the instance into broker activity.

description: The only instance of a member cannot be removed.
cause: The instance to be removed was the only instance of the corresponding member that was known to the broker.
action: Remove the corresponding member from the broker configuration instead of the individual instance of the member.

description: event for Data Guard broker network process tracing
cause: This is an Oracle internal event code. This event is used to control trace output of the Oracle Data Guard broker network process. DO NOT USE.
action: N/A, this is an Oracle internal event code.

description: Network connection failed during transmission.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected a connection failure to a member in the broker configuration. This failure happened in the middle of a transmission session.
action: In most cases, no action is required. The Oracle Data Guard broker tries to resend the data. The error indicates a problem in the network communication between broker managed members. If this persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Fast-start failover target standby in error state. Cannot stop observer.
cause: A STOP OBSERVER operation could not be completed when fast-start failover was enabled because the target standby database could not participate in the STOP OBSERVER operation.
action: Additional information about this failure is recorded in the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for the primary database. This information helps to identify the reason why the target standby database was unable to participate in the STOP OBSERVER operation. If the problem can be corrected by the information in the broker log file, retry the operation. Alternatively, fast-start failover may be forcibly disabled by connecting to the primary database and issuing the DISABLE FAST_START FAILOVER FORCE command from the DGMGRL CLI. Once fast-start failover has been forcibly disabled, the observer can be stopped regardless of the current state of the target standby database.

description: maximum number of Oracle error numbers for fast-start failover already reached
cause: The broker could not enable any more Oracle error numbers for initiating a fast-start failover.
action: Use the DGMGRL CLI SHOW FAST_START FAILOVER command to help identify an Oracle error number that can be disabled before attempting to enable an additional error number for initiating a fast-start failover.

description: Could not obtain instance status.
cause: The broker could not determine whether the specified instance was running.
action: See the next error message in the error stack for more detailed information. If the situation described in the next error in the stack can be corrected, do so. Otherwise, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: specified instance inactive or currently unavailable
cause: An attempt was made to perform an operation on an instance that was not running or was unavailable.
action: Ensure that the instance specified in the operation is running and then retry the operation.

description: Oracle Clusterware was unable to shutdown database instances.
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: failed to acquire broker configuration metadata lock.
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: DB_UNIQUE_NAME mismatch.
cause: The DB_UNIQUE_NAME value did not match the actual DB_UNIQUE_NAME value for the member that the broker contacted using the connect identifier associated with that member.
action: Verify that the connect identifier correctly connects to the intended member. Verify that the name of the member the broker expects to find by that connect identifier matches the actual DB_UNIQUE_NAME for that member.

description: Unable to determine location of broker configuration files.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker was unable to determine the location of its configuration files from the DG_BROKER_CONFIG_FILE[1|2] initialization parameters.
action: Retry the operation. If the error persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Standby database does not have an apply instance available.
cause: The broker operation could not finish, because it required a running apply instance for the standby database. There was no such instance designated for the standby database, or the designated apply instance was not currently available.
action: Use the DGMGRL CLI SHOW DATABASE command to see if the standby database has a designated apply instance. If an apply instance is designated in the output, restart that instance. If the output does not show an instance designated to run apply, then wait until the broker specifies an instance to be the apply instance and retry the command.

description: startup of an instance not part of the broker configuration interrupted current operation
cause: The startup of an instance, that was not part of the broker configuration prevented the operation from completing.
action: Restart the operation after the new instance has joined the Data Guard configuration.

description: Fast-start failover is disabled.
cause: This operation was not allowed because fast-start failover was disabled.
action: Enable fast-start failover and retry the command.

description: maximum number of observers has already been started
cause: The attempt to start an observer failed because the maximum number of observers was already running. For Oracle Database releases earlier than 12.2, only a single observer can be started. For Oracle Database releases 12.2 through 19c, a maximum of three observers can be started. For Oracle Database release 21c and later, a maximum of 4 observers can be started.
action: Stop one of the existing observers and retry the command.

description: A new observer registered with identifier %s.
cause: An observer was registered with the Oracle Data Guard broker and will begin observing the Oracle Data Guard configuration for conditions that warrant doing a fast-start failover.
action: No actions needed.

description: Data Guard prevented this database from opening.
cause: The primary database could not be opened because one of the following reasons. A fast-start failover has occurred, and there was another primary. Data Guard had detected a possible fast-start failover but could not contact the observer or target standby to verify. The database was configured for maximum protection and no standby database was available to support the protection mode.
action: Check if a failover did occur. If it did, reinstate the database. If the failover did not occur and fast-start failover is enabled, ensure that connectivity exists between the primary database and either the observer or the target standby database, then retry opening the database.

description: unrecognized member specified in a RedoRoutes rule
cause: One of the members specified in a RedoRoutes configurable property rule was not part of the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration.
action: Check the member names in the value specified for the RedoRoutes configurable property. Confirm that the names appear in the output of the DGMGRL SHOW CONFIGURATION command. Retry changing the RedoRoutes configurable property using the member names shown in the SHOW CONFIGURATION command output.

description: upgrade to maximum protection mode not possible
cause: An upgrade to maximum protection mode was attempted when the current protection mode was maximum performance mode.
action: To upgrade the protection mode to maximum protection mode, first upgrade the protection mode to maximum availability mode, then upgrade the protection mode to maximum protection mode.

description: fast-start failover target standby database is disabled
cause: The command to enable or disable fast-start failover could not be run because the Data Guard broker management of the fast-start failover target standby database was disabled.
action: Enable broker management of the target standby database and rerun the command. If an attempt was made to disable fast-start failover when this error was reported, then disable fast-start failover forcibly using the DGMGRL DISABLE FAST_START FAILOVER FORCE command. Refer to the documentation for more information.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker failed to reinstate database.
cause: The Data Guard broker failed to reinstate the database because the reinstatement could not be completed or the database was already reinstated.
action: Additional information about the failure is recorded in the primary database or the specified database Data Guard broker log files. This information helps determine how to proceed.

description: fast-start failover is enabled
cause: The attempted command was not allowed while fast-start failover was enabled. This occurred because: - The FastStartFailoverTarget property may not be modified. - The LogXptMode property for either the primary database or the fast-start failover target standby database may not be modified. - The protection mode of the configuration may not be modified. - Neither the broker configuration nor the fast-start failover target standby database was disabled using the DGMGRL CLI DISABLE command. - Neither the broker configuration nor the fast-start failover target standby database was removed using the DGMGRL CLI REMOVE command. - The FAILOVER IMMEDIATE command was not allowed. - The DG_BROKER_START initialization parameter may not be set to FALSE.
action: Disable fast-start failover, using the FORCE option if required. Then retry the attempted command.

description: The specified standby database is not the current fast-start failover target standby database.
cause: The attempted command was not allowed because fast-start failover was enabled for this Data Guard broker configuration and the standby database specified in the command was not the current fast-start failover target standby database associated with the current primary database.
action: Retry the attempted command by specifying the current fast-start failover target standby database. Alternatively, disable fast-start failover and retry the command using the originally specified target standby database.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker detected role change.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected a role change during database startup or health check.
action: Additional information about this failure is recorded in the Oracle Data Guard broker log files, one for the primary database and one for each standby database in the Oracle Data Guard configuration. This information is helpful in determining how best to resolve this failure.

description: Reinstatement of database in progress.
cause: Reinstatement of this database was in progress.
action: None

description: unobserved fast-start failover configuration
cause: The fast-start failover configuration was currently unobserved and so failover was not possible.
action: Ensure that the observer is running and has connectivity to both the primary and the target standby databases. If the primary is not available and failover must be performed, then disable fast-start failover to perform a failover in the absence of the observer process. If both primary and standby databases are available, and only one observer is registered, restart that observer. If it cannot be restarted, then use the DGMGRL CLI STOP OBSERVER command to deregister that observer and then start a new observer using the DGMGRL START OBSERVER command. If multiple observers are registered, this error will be temporary since the broker will select a new observer to be the primary observer from the set of observers that have been registered.

description: Failover operation is in progress.
cause: A primary database that restarted contacted a standby database while the failover is active to that standby database.
action: Shut down the primary database and wait for failover to complete on the standby database. Once failover is complete, restart the old primary database.

description: Fast-start failover operation attempted in absence of a broker configuration.
cause: Attempted to enable or disable fast-start failover when connected to a standby database for which broker configuration details are currently unavailable. For instance, the standby database may currently require re-creation (or flashback reinstantiation) before it may respond to broker client commands.
action: 1) Attempts to enable or disable (non-FORCE) fast-start failover at this standby database will be rejected until the broker configuration details are available to the standby database from the primary database. This typically occurs when the standby database is successfully recreated or flashed back, and then re-enabled on the primary database. 2) Use the FORCE option to override fast-start failover enabled on the standby database even when the broker configuration details are currently unavailable to the standby database. In this case, the status message is only a warning. Note that fast-start failover is not formally disabled in the broker configuration. The effect of this command issued under these circumstances may or may not be permanent, depending upon when the primary and standby databases regain full communication between each other and if the state of fast-start failover has been altered at the primary database in the meantime.

description: The standby database must be reinstated.
cause: A role change operation caused this database or pluggable database to require reinstatement.
action: Use Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL REINSTATE DATABASE or REINSTATE PLUGGABLE DATABASE command to reinstate the database or pluggable database.

description: Network timeout when contacting a member.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker attempted to contact a member and failed because there was no response from the member within timeout specifiedby the CommunicationTimeout configuration property.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for the details of the failure. Fix the problem and retry.

description: event to control broker actions in the development environment
cause: This is an Oracle internal event code. This event is used to control the broker actions in the development environment. DO NOT USE.
action: None. This is an Oracle internal event code.

description: unable to receive the result from a member
cause: During execution of a command, a member in the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration failed to return a result.
action: Check Oracle Data Guard broker log files for the details of the failure. Ensure network communications are working properly amongst the members of the configuration. Use the DGMGRL CLI VALIDATE NETWORK command to identify any communication issues in the configuration. Fix any identified network problems and retry the command.

description: Timed out waiting for a result from a member.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker was forced to time out a network connection to a remote member because: - The network call to the remote member did not complete in a timely manner - The remote member was unable to process the command due to an instance failure
action: Check Data Guard broker log files for the details of the failure. If the network call did not complete in a timely manner, increase the CommunicationTimeout configuration property value and reissue the command.

description: Unable to initiate fast-start failover on a bystander standby database.
cause: The request to initiate a fast-start failover using DBMS_DG.INITIATE_FS_FAILOVER was made on a bystander standby database.
action: Call DBMS_DG.INITIATE_FS_FAILOVER on either the primary or fast-start failover target standby database.

description: request Oracle Data Guard broker client to reissue command
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker operation required that the same command be issued again from the client.
action: If DGMGRL or Enterprise Manager has not already done so, reissue the same command to the Oracle Data Guard broker manually.

description: operation cannot be performed on the fast-start failover target standby database
cause: The database specified for the operation was the fast-start failover target standby database.
action: Retry the operation on a different database. Alternatively, disable fast-start failover, and retry the operation.

description: instance cannot be opened because the Oracle Active Data Guard option is disabled
cause: The attempt to open the instance failed because the Oracle Active Data Guard option was not enabled, and Redo Apply was either running or was about to be started by the Oracle Data Guard broker.
action: Stop Redo Apply or set the database state to APPLY-OFF, and then open the database.

description: instance-specific property must be set uniquely for instances of an Oracle RAC database
cause: An attempt was made to set an instance-specific property to the same value for all instances of an Oracle RAC database for a property whose value must be unique for each instance.
action: Use the EDIT INSTANCE command and specify the SID of each instance whose instance-specific property value is to be changed.

description: switchover not permitted to standby database with non-zero DelayMins property value
cause: Switchover was attempted to a standby database that had a non-zero value for its DelayMins configurable property.
action: For switchover to a standby database, set the DelayMins configurable property to zero for the standby database, wait for its apply lag to become zero seconds, and then retry the switchover command.

description: A member is running a different Oracle version from that of the primary database version.
cause: The standby member was running a different version of Oracle than the primary database.
action: Ensure that all members of the configuration are running the same versions of Oracle.

description: standby database type has changed
cause: An attempt to enable a database whose standby type changed from physical or snapshot to logical (or vice versa) was disallowed.
action: If the intention is to retain the database conversion to the new type, the database must be removed and added back into the configuration in order to obtain the correct values for database properties specific to the new standby type.

description: Database instance restart required for the property value modification to take effect.
cause: One or more properties that correspond to static initialization parameters were modified, but the database instances were not restarted. Or, a static initialization parameter that corresponds to a broker property was modified using an ALTER SYSTEM SQL*Plus statement.
action: Restart the database instances for the modified property values to take effect. If the error persists after having restarted the instance, use the DGMGRL CLI or Enterprise Manager to modify the property to which the static initialization parameter corresponds.

description: RedoRoutes property for two or more members contains a circular route
cause: The value of a RedoRoutes property for two or more members was set such that a member that sent redo also received redo data data in the same route. For example, A sends to B, B sends to C, and C sends to A.
action: Correct the setting of the RedoRoutes propety on one or more members to eliminate the circular route.

description: Modification to RedoRoutes property may prevent one or more members from receiving redo data.
cause: The change to the RedoRoutes property for the specified member may result in some members not receiving redo data. This may happen if another member has a LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter set to the same or higher value for the PRIORITY attribute.
action: Use the DGMGRL SHOW CONFIGURATION WHEN PRIMARY IS command for each database that may become a primary database to ensure that all members continue to receive redo data after any role change.

description: unrecognized or duplicate attribute specified
cause: The specified value contained an unrecognized or duplicated attribute.
action: Ensure the property string does not contain any undefined or duplicate attributes. See the Oracle Data Guard broker documentation for supported attributes.

description: one or more disallowed keywords found
cause: The specified value contained one or more disallowed keywords.
action: See the Oracle Data Guard broker documentation for the supported keywords.

description: value contains unbalanced set of parentheses
cause: The specified value contained an unbalanced set of parentheses or a missing set of parentheses.
action: Ensure the parentheses are correctly matched and specify parentheses when required. See the Oracle Data Guard broker documentation for more information.

description: Value does not contain a colon.
cause: The specified value did not contain a colon (:).
action: Include the colon (:) in the value.

description: value contains duplicate databases or far sync instances
cause: The specified value contained the same database or far sync instance multiple times.
action: Ensure that a database or far sync instance is specified only once.

description: disallowed, empty substring specified in property value
cause: The value specified contained a disallowed, empty string or substring, e.g. "()".
action: Remove the disallowed empty strings and retry the command.

description: maximum number of destinations exceeded
cause: The value specified for the RedoRoutes property contained more than the maximum of 30 destinations.
action: Ensure that no more than 30 destinations are specified.

description: database does not receive redo data
cause: The RedoRoutes property for all members of the configuration were set such that this database did not receive redo data. Or, the transport state of the database that sends redo data to this database was not valid.
action: Check the setting of the RedoRoutes property for all members of the configuration. Ensure that at least one member's RedoRoutes property value is set to ship redo data to this database. Also check the transport state of the database that sends redo data to this database.

description: member may not receive redo data if redo source is an alternate destination
cause: This member may not receive redo data if the redo source is an alternate destination that does not ship redo to this database.
action: Ensure that any alternates for the redo source for this member includes this member in its redo destination list.

description: member has multiple redo sources
cause: Two or more members had their RedoRoutes property set to ship redo data to the same member.
action: Examine the RedoRoutes property values for all members to see which members are shipping redo data to the same member. Change the value of the RedoRoutes property for those members so that only one of them sends redo to the member that had multiple redo sources.

description: command cannot be issued on a disabled member
cause: The command was issued on a member that was disabled.
action: Connect to an enabled member of the configuration and retry the command.

description: invalid sender specified for RedoRoutes property
cause: A far sync instance or a recovery appliance was specified as the redo source in a RedoRoutes property rule.
action: Check the setting of the RedoRoutes property and confirm that a far sync instance or a recovery appliance is not specified as the redo source in the RedoRoutes property rule.

description: invalid destination specified for RedoRoutes
cause: A destination specified in a RedoRoutes rule either appeared in the primary setting of the same rule or was the same member whose RedoRoutes property was being changed.
action: Ensure that any destination specified in a RedoRoutes rule does not appear in the primary setting of the same rule and is not the member whose RedoRoutes property is being changed.

description: cannot remove a configuration member that is specified in a RedoRoutes property
cause: An attempt was made to remove a database or far sync instance that was specified in another configuration member's RedoRoutes property.
action: First remove the database or far sync instance from all other member's RedoRoutes property values. Then retry the remove command.

description: operation disallowed for a member that is currently shipping redo to another member
cause: An attempt was made to remove, disable, or convert (physical standby database) a member that currently shipped redo data to another member.
action: Modify the value of the RedoRoutes property for the member to be removed, disabled, or converted (physical standby database) to not ship redo data for the current primary database and then retry the operation.

description: requirements not met for enabling fast-start failover
cause: The attempt to enable fast-start failover could not be completed because one or more requirements were not met: - The effective redo transport mode for both the primary database and the fast-start failover target standby database must be set to either SYNC or FASTSYNC if the configuration protection mode was set to MaxAvailability mode. - The effective redo transport mode for both the primary database and the fast-start failover target standby database must be set to either SYNC if the configuration protection mode was set to MaxProtection mode. - The effective redo transport mode for both the primary database and the fast-start failover target standby database must be set to ASYNC if the configuration protection mode was set to MaxPerformance mode. - No valid target standby database was specified in the primary database FastStartFailoverTarget property prior to the attempt to enable fast-start failover, and more than one standby database existed in the Oracle Data Guard configuration. - fast-start failover target standby database did not receive redo data directly from the primary database when the protection mode was set to MaxPerformance. - The primary database has multiple routes to the fast-start failover target standby database. - Logical standby databases could not be the fast-start failover targets because the configuration protection mode was set to MaxProtection.
action: Retry the command after correcting the issue: - Ensure that the effective redo transport mode for both the primary database and the fast-start failover target standby database are either SYNC or FASTSYNC if the configuration protection mode is set to MaxProtection or MaxAvailability. - Ensure that the LogXptMode property for both the primary database and the fast-start failover target standby database are set to ASYNC if the configuration protection mode is set to MaxPerformance. - Ensure the RedoRoutes property of the primary includes the name of the fast-start failover target standby database when the protection mode is set to MaxPerformance. - Ensure the RedoRoutes property of the primary database has only one route to the fast-start failover target standby database.

description: one or more databases involved in switchover need to be restarted
cause: An error occurred during the restart of either the old or new primary databases or both in a switchover operation.
action: Manually restart both the old and new primary databases, including all their Oracle RAC instances if it is an Oracle RAC database.

description: a RedoRoutes rule requires asynchronous redo transport mode
cause: The member could not receive redo data from its source because the source was either a standby database or far sync instance, but the redo transport was not set to asynchronous mode. Standby databases and far sync instances cannot send redo data in synchronous mode. The asynchronous transport mode must be set in either the RedoRoutes parameter of the source member or in the LogXptMode configurable property of the receiving member.
action: Set the LogXptMode configurable property for the receiving member to ASYNC before changing the RedoRoutes configurable property of the standby database or far sync instance that is to send redo data. Or, specify ASYNC in the RedoRoutes configurable property of either the sending standby database or far sync instance to override the value specified in the LogXptMode configurable property of the receiving member.

description: cannot enable the member because its redo source is disabled
cause: An attempt was made to enable a member, but its redo source was disabled.
action: Check that the redo source configured for this member (primary, database, physical standby database, or far sync instance) is enabled. If the redo source is disabled, enable it first and then retry the command.

description: current role of the member only allows a LOCAL rule in RedoRoutes property
cause: A logical or snapshot standby database was specified as a redo data source in a RedoRoutes configurable property rule.
action: Logical and snapshot standbys cannot be configured as a redo source. The only valid rules a logical or snapshot standby database can contain are those that specify LOCAL or its database unique name value in the redo source field of a redo routing rule. Check that the member for which you are setting the RedoRoutes configurable property is a primary database, physical standby database, or a far sync instance. Note that a Oracle Zero Data Loss Recovery Appliance cannot be a redo source.

description: member has a LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter with SERVICE attribute set
cause: One or more LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameters that contain a SERVICE attribute for another member in the configuration were set on the new member when attempting to add a standby database or far sync instance to the configuration.
action: Clear all LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameters that contain a SERVICE attribute for another member in the configuration on the new member to be added.

description: Connect identifier was not specified.
cause: The connect identifier was not specified for the member being added to the configuration.
action: Retry the ADD command with a connect identifier for the member to be added.

description: The standby database has diverged from the primary database.
cause: The primary database may have been flashed back or restored from a backup set and then reopened with the RESETLOGS option. Or, a role change to a logical standby database was performed.
action: Re-create the standby database from the primary database or flashback the standby database to the same point the primary database had been flashed back to. If the roles are switched back to the original primary database, then no action is necessary.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker command failed.
cause: The command to modify or query the member failed.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for the reason for the failure and reissue the command.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker command warning
cause: The command to modify or query the member resulted in a warning.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for the warning and, if necessary, reissue the command.

description: cannot set property while the member is enabled
cause: An attempt was made to change a member property while the member was enabled.
action: Disable the member first, update the property, and then reenable the member.

description: standby database not valid for primary database
cause: The standby database was not added to the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration because it was not a valid standby database for the primary database.
action: Add a database to the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration that is a valid standby database to the primary database.

description: internal error in Data guard broker
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker worker process not available.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker worker process was not available to process the request.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: The value of property %s is invalid. Valid values are %s.
cause: An invalid property value was specified while broker management of the member was disabled.
action: Reset the property to a valid value.

description: The state name supplied to the Oracle Data Guard broker worker process is invalid.
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Standby archived log location settings conflict with database recovery area.
cause: The StandbyArchiveLocation or AlternateLocation property was set to USE_DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST, but the initialization parameter DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST did not specify a valid destination.
action: Use a value other than USE_DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST for StandbyArchiveLocation or AlternateLocation, or set up a valid database recovery area by setting DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST to a valid destination.

description: Snapshot standby database should be converted back to a physical standby database as soon as possible.
cause: A failover operation caused the snapshot standby database to enter a state that would require it to be re-created if another failover operation occurs before it is converted back to a physical standby database.
action: Re-enable the snapshot standby database if it is disabled and convert it back to a physical standby database as soon as possible, because the snapshot standby database will have to be re-created if another failover occurs while it is a snapshot standby database.

description: resource manager service function not defined
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: The resource handle is invalid.
cause: This is an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: The Oracle Data Guard broker command timed out.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker timed out a health check, get property, or set property command because it took longer than the number of seconds specified by the OperationTimeout configuration property to complete.
action: Enable support level tracing (the TraceLevel configuration property should be set to SUPPORT) and then examine the Data Guard broker log files for warnings or errors to see what may be causing the operation to be timed out.

description: The value of property %s is inconsistent with the member setting.
cause: The value of the specified configuration property was inconsistent with the in-memory settings or the server parameter file settings for the member. This may be caused by changing an initialization parameter that corresponds to a configuration property.
action: Query the InconsistentProperties property on the member to determine which properties are set inconsistently and set the properties to make them consistent.

description: redo transport-related property %s of member "%s" is inconsistent
cause: The value of the specified redo transport-related configuration property of the given member was inconsistent with the primary database redo transport service setting. This may be caused by a change in an initialization parameter that corresponds to a configuration property.
action: Query the InconsistentLogXptProps property on the primary database to determine which redo transport properties are set inconsistently. Reset the properties on the member to make them consistent with the primary database redo transport settings.

description: Unable to clear the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter.
cause: An attempt to clear the LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter failed.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log files and the Oracle Database alert log for more information. Resolve any errors and retry the operation. If the problem persists, contact Oracle Support.

description: clearing parameter LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST failed
cause: An attempt to clear the LOG_ARCHIVE_DUPLEX_DEST parameter failed.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Failed to locate member.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker was unable to locate the member in the broker configuration.
action: Add the member to the broker configuration and retry the command.

description: Unable to query V$ARCHIVE_DEST fixed view.
cause: The broker failed to query the V$ARCHIVE_DEST fixed view.
action: Retry the query. If this persists, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: No LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameters are available.
cause: All LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameters were in use, or all initialization parameters from LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_1 through LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_10 that can support SYNC were in use.
action: Clear one or more LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameters so that Oracle Data Guard broker can use them to set up the primary database redo transport.

description: unable to set LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameters
cause: The broker was unable to set one or more LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameters.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: unable to set LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_STATE_n initialization parameters
cause: The broker was unable to set one or more LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_STATE_n initialization parameters.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log files for more details.

description: Modification to RedoRoutes property may result in a terminal member having a higher priority than the cascading member.
cause: The change to the RedoRoutes property for the specified member resulted in a terminal member having a higher priority setting than the cascading member.
action: Use the DGMGRL CLI SHOW ALL MEMBERS RedoRoutes command to check the value of the RedoRoutes property for all members. Use the DGMGRL SHOW CONFIGURATION WHEN PRIMARY IS command for each database that may become a primary database to ensure that all members continue to receive redo data after any role change.

description: Cannot resolve gap for one or more members.
cause: Primary database could not resolve a gap request from one or more members.
action: To identify the member with the unresolvable gap, check the status of the primary database using either Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL CLI SHOW DATABASE command. Copy the missing archived log files from backups or from another member in the configuration that has the files for the member with missing files.

description: The phase supplied to the Oracle Data Guard broker worker process is invalid.
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: the external condition supplied to Data Guard broker worker process is invalid
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Cannot close database.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker could not close the database.
action: Terminate all active sessions connected to the database and retry.

description: Consistency check for property %s found %s error.
cause: Consistency check for specified property caused the specified error.
action: Check the error message, clear the error, and retry.

description: Found error %s when validating value for property %s.
cause: An error was encountered while validating the specified value for the configurable property.
action: Check the error message, clear the error, and retry.

description: SQL Apply was not started.
cause: SQL Apply was not started because there were no pluggable databases opened in read/write mode.
action: Open at least one pluggable database in read/write mode. Oracle Data Guard will automatically start SQL Apply.

description: No pluggable databases are opened in read/write mode.
cause: Operation failed because there were no pluggable databases opened in read/write mode.
action: Open at least one pluggable database in read/write mode and retry.

description: Oracle Clusterware is restarting the database instance.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker operation required this database instance to be shut down and restarted.
action: If Oracle Clusterware has not already done so, shut down the Oracle instance and then restart it. No action is required if this error was returned from DBMS_DG.SWITCHOVER and Oracle Clusterware has restarted the database. If this error was returned by DBMS_DG.CONVERT_TO_PHYSICAL or DBMS_DG.REINSTATE, wait for the database to start, and wait for the broker to complete initialization using DBMS_DG.WAIT(WAIT_BOOT, <wait time in seconds>). Then, for reinstate and convert operations, retry the operation.

description: Member previously posted a phase done message for the task.
cause: A phase done message was already posted for this task.
