action: No action necessary.

description: An archive location property is empty while its alternate location property has a non-empty value.
cause: The ArchiveLocation property value was empty while the AlternateLocation property had a non-empty value. Or, the the StandbyArchiveLocation property value was empty while the StandbyAlternateLocation had a non-empty value.
action: Ensure that the member's ArchiveLocation property is set to a valid directory location that is different than the value specified for the AlternateLocation property. Or, ensure that the StandbyArchiveLocation property is set to a valid directory location that is different that the value specified for the the StandbyAlternateLocation property.

description: primary redo generation suspended
cause: Redo generation on the primary database was suspended because either the fast-start failover target was unavailable or the network connection between both databases was disrupted.
action: Ensure that the fast-start failover target standby database is running and the network connection between both databases is restored.

description: unable to find the destination entry of member "%s" in V$ARCHIVE_DEST
cause: Either the destination was manually changed or the member was removed from the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration, or there was no available LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter that could be used to ship redo data to the member.
action: Reset any LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameters that are no longer required and reenable the configuration.

description: The redo transport service for member "%s" has an error.
cause: Redo transport services were not able to communicate with the member.
action: Query the LogXptStatus monitorable property for the sending member. Also, check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: Redo transport service for member "%s" is not running.
cause: The redo transport service for the specified member was not running.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file or the Oracle alert log file for more details. If necessary, start the redo transport service for the member.

description: Redo transport service for member "%s" is unexpectedly running.
cause: The redo transport service for the member was expected to be stopped but was found running.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for more details. If necessary, stop the redo transport service for the member.

description: Redo transport service for member "%s" incorrectly set as alternate.
cause: The redo transport service for a member was set as alternate when no other member was set as an alternate for this member.
action: Re-enable the member or the entire configuration to allow the correct configuration property settings to be propagated to the initialization parameters.

description: The LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_N initialization parameter value for member "%s" contains incorrect syntax.
cause: The value of a LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_N initialization parameter that was defined in the server parameter file of the primary database contained incorrect syntax. The Data Guard broker was unable to change its value when the redo transport services were enabled.
action: Fix the syntax error in the primary database server parameter file or remove the entry from the server parameter file. Also, check the values of the redo transport-related properties for the specified member.

description: The member "%s" exceeded its archived log storage quota.
cause: The member exceeded its quota for stored archived redo logs.
action: Remove some archived redo logs from the member or increase its quota.

description: cannot determine status of redo transport service for member "%s"
cause: The status of redo transport to the specified member could not be determined.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: The DG_CONFIG list of LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG parameter is full.
cause: The DG_CONFIG list of the LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG attribute was full and the Oracle Data Guard broker was not able to add a new DB_UNIQUE_NAME to the list.
action: Remove unused entries in the DG_CONFIG list, then re-enable the member.

description: Unable to add DB_UNIQUE_NAME "%s" to the DG_CONFIG list.
cause: The DG_CONFIG list of the LOG_ARCHIVE_CONFIG attribute was full and Oracle Data Guard broker could not add the specified DB_UNIQUE_NAME to the list.
action: Remove some unused entries in the DG_CONFIG list then re-enable the member.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker cannot mount the database.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to mount the database.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: Logical standby database guard could not be turned on.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker could not turn on the logical standby database guard.
action: Check Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker cannot open the primary database
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to open the primary database.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: The member is disabled manually.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker configuration member was disabled manually.
action: Enable the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration member.

description: Failed to activate logical standby database.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to activate a logical standby database during a failover operation.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: failed to enable supplemental logging
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to enable supplemental logging during a switchover to a physical standby database in a configuration that also contained logical standby databases.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: dump system state
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected an internal problem and request a system state dump.
action: None. This is an Oracle internal event code.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker cannot open standby database.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker failed to open the standby database.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: Failed to activate physical standby database.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to activate the physical standby database.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: Failed setting an initialization parameter.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to set an initialization parameter using either the ALTER SYSTEM SET or ALTER SYSTEM RESET command.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: Dump Hang Analysis
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected an internal problem and request a hang analysis dump.
action: N/A, this is an Oracle internal event code.

description: unable to get the value of this property
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to get the value for the specified property because the value for the specified property was not available for the current database role.
action: If the value of the specified property is not available for the current role of the database, specify this property for a database for which the value is available. Otherwise, check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for more details.

description: The specified apply instance is not running.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker could not start apply services on the specified instance because the instance was not running.
action: Start the instance and then retry the command.

description: Cannot start SQL Apply with initial system change number (SCN).
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to start SQL Apply with an initial system change number (SCN).
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: Cannot start SQL Apply.
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker failed to start SQL Apply.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details. If needed, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: cannot stop SQL Apply
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to stop the SQL Apply service.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: invalid database state
cause: Database was not in the intended state.
action: Determine the reason why the database is not running in the intended state and reissue the command.

description: redo transport service for a member is running
cause: The redo transport service for a member was running.
action: For more details, check the status of the primary database using either Oracle Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL CLI SHOW DATABASE command. If necessary, stop the redo transport service to the member.

description: Redo transport service to a member is not running.
cause: The redo transport service to a member was not running.
action: For more details, check the status of the primary database using either Oracle Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL CLI SHOW DATABASE command. If necessary, start the redo transport service to the member.

description: Redo Apply is running.
cause: Redo Apply was running when it should have been stopped.
action: If necessary, stop Redo Apply.

description: Redo Apply is stopped.
cause: Redo Apply was stopped when it should have been running.
action: Check the alert log to see why Redo Apply terminated, correct any problems that may exist, and restart Redo Apply by setting the physical standby database state to APPLY-ON.

description: SQL Apply is running.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker expected SQL Apply to have been stopped but detected that SQL Apply was still running.
action: This normally occurs because SQL Apply was stopped using the Oracle Data Guard broker but restarted again outside of the Oracle Data Guard broker, for example through SQL*Plus. Stop SQL Apply using SQL*Plus and retry the required action using the Oracle Data Guard broker.

description: SQL Apply is stopped.
cause: SQL Apply was stopped when it should have been running.
action: Check the alert log to see why SQL Apply terminated, correct any problems that may exist, and restart SQL Apply by setting the logical standby database state to APPLY-ON.

description: The physical standby database is open in read-only mode.
cause: All instances of the physical standby database were put into a read-only state instead of APPLY-OFF.
action: Use the EDIT DATABASE SET STATE command to set the database to the APPLY-OFF state. Retry the operation.

description: Redo Apply not started because the physical standby database is opening.
cause: Redo Apply services could not be started on the physical standby database because it was being opened. The Oracle Data Guard broker will start Redo Apply services once the physical standby database has been opened.
action: No action required.

description: failover to a physical standby database failed
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker encountered errors when converting a physical standby database to a primary database.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: switchover to a standby database failed
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker encountered errors when switching over to the specified standby database.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: cannot start Redo Apply
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to start Redo Apply.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details. If the database is already open, the broker will not start Redo Apply if the Oracle Active Data Guard option is not enabled.

description: cannot stop Redo Apply
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to stop the Redo Apply service.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: target standby database in broker operation has potential data loss
cause: The target standby database specified for the broker operation did not have all the redo data from the primary database.
action: Confirm that the redo transport service on the primary database is functioning correctly by checking its status using either Oracle Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL CLI SHOW DATABASE command. Reissue the broker command once all redo data are available on the target standby database.

description: Health check of the redo transport service failed.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker could not complete the health check for the redo transport service.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details on why the health check detected errors. These logs should contain other error messages that indicate the cause of the problem.

description: Unable to find the destination entry of a member in V$ARCHIVE_DEST.
cause: Either a destination (LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_N initialization parameter) was manually deleted or no LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_N initialization parameter was available to set up redo transport for the member.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details. If there are sufficient LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_N initialization parameters available, re-enable the configuration using the DGMGRL CLI ENABLE CONFIGURATION command to ensure all members are receiving redo data. If there are an insufficient number of LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_N initialization parameters available, consider using the RedoRoutes property to take advantage of available LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_N initialization parameters on other members so that all members are receiving redo data.

description: Redo transport error occurred for one or more members.
cause: The redo transport service was unable to send redo data to one or more members.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details. These logs should contain other errors messages that indicate the cause of the problem. Also, query the LogXptStatus property to see the errors affecting the redo transport service.

description: The LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter of a member is set incorrectly.
cause: The LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n initialization parameter value in the server parameter file contained incorrect syntax. The Oracle Data Guard broker failed to update the destination when the redo transport service was enabled.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file to see which member has the problem. Fix the syntax error in the server parameter file or remove the entry from the server parameter file. Check if the syntax of the redo transport-related properties is correct.

description: A member exceeded its archived redo log storage quota.
cause: A member exceeded its archived redo log storage quota.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file to see which member has the problem. Remove older archived redo logs or increase the member's archived redo log storage quota.

description: cannot determine status of redo transport service for member
cause: The status of redo transport to the specified member could not be determined.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more details.

description: instance not open for read/write access
cause: The database was mounted on an instance but not opened for read/write access.
action: For more details, check the status of the database using either Oracle Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL CLI SHOW DATABASE command. If possible, open the instance manually.

description: Cannot resolve gap for member %s.
cause: The primary database could not resolve a gap request from the specified members.
action: Copy the missing archived redo log files either from a backup or from another member in the configuration that has the missing files for the members.

description: The member name specified by the Dependency property is incorrect.
cause: The member name that should be the value of the DB_UNIQUE_NAME initialization parameter specified in the Dependency property was incorrect.
action: Reset the Dependency property to the correct name of the member.

description: The database is in NOARCHIVELOG mode.
cause: The database was in NOARCHIVELOG mode when it was either a primary database or when it was a standby database that was being switched over to be a primary database.
action: Set the database to ARCHIVELOG mode by issuing the ALTER DATABASE ARCHIVELOG command.

description: unable to access Oracle Data Guard broker configuration files
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker configuration files did not exist or could not be accessed.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for more details.

description: event for Oracle Data Guard broker worker process testing
cause: This is an Oracle internal event code. This event is used for verifying Oracle Data Guard broker worker process functionality. DO NOT USE.
action: N/A, this is an Oracle internal event code.

description: Unable to set one or more member configurable property values.
cause: The broker failed to execute an ALTER SYSTEM or ALTER DATABASE statement when it attempted to set the ApplyInstances, ApplyParallel, or DelayMins configurable property.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file to see which property could not be set, and retry the statement again using a valid property value.

description: Standby redo logs are configured incorrectly.
cause: Standby redo logs were not configured, or were configured incorrectly for the member.
action: Standby redo logs are required when the redo transport mode is set to SYNC or ASYNC. Check the Oracle Data Guard documentation for more information on the correct configuration of standby redo logs.

description: The value of the configurable property is invalid.
cause: Either an invalid property value was entered, or a reset was attempted for a property that had no broker default value.
action: Set the property to a valid value.

description: Unable to check the existence of the standby redo logs.
cause: The standby redo logs were not found or did not exist.
action: Ensure that the member is mounted and query the V$STANDBY_LOG fixed view to check if the problem is corrected. Retry the command.

description: Configurable property value is inconsistent with member setting.
cause: The value of one or more configurable properties were inconsistent with the in-memory settings or server parameter file settings. This may happen by directly altering initialization parameters instead of editing configurable property values using Oracle Data Guard broker.
action: Query the InconsistentProperties property on the member or check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file to find which properties are set inconsistently. Reset these properties to make them consistent with the database settings. Alternatively, enable the member or the entire configuration to allow the configurable property settings to be propagated to the initialization parameters.

description: Logical standby database guard is off.
cause: The logical standby database was turned off.
action: Issue the ALTER DATABASE GUARD ALL command to turn the guard on and verify that Oracle Data Guard health check error or warning has cleared.

description: database guard is on for primary database
cause: The database guard was turned on for the primary database.
action: Issue the ALTER DATABASE GUARD NONE command to turn off the database guard and verify that the Oracle Data Guard health check error or warning is cleared.

description: The standby database needs to be re-created.
cause: A switchover or failover operation caused this database to require re-creation.
action: Re-create (or flashback) the standby database. Connect to the primary database in the broker configuration and re-enable broker management of that database. Once enabled, connect to the standby database and manage it with the broker. Some client commands cannot be completed on the standby database when in this error state. These commands can be completed successfully on the primary database. Retry the command on the primary database.

description: One or more properties could not be imported from the member.
cause: The broker was unable to import property values for the member being added to the broker configuration. This error indicates: The Oracle Net service name specified in DGMGRL CREATE CONFIGURATION, ADD DATABASE, ADD FAR_SYNC, or ADD RECOVERY_APPLIANCE command was not one that provides access to the member being added. There were no instances running for the member being added.
action: Remove the member from the configuration using the REMOVE CONFIGURATION, REMOVE DATABASE, REMOVE FAR_SYNC, or REMOVE RECOVERY_APPLIANCE command. Ensure that the member to be added has at least one instance running and that the Oracle Net service name provides access to the running instance. Also, check the broker log file for additional information. Then, reissue the CREATE CONFIGURATION, ADD DATABASE, ADD FAR_SYNC, or ADD RECOVERY_APPLIANCE command.

description: Member is not using a server parameter file.
cause: The member was not using a server parameter file or the broker was unable to access the server parameter file.
action: Issue the CREATE SPFILE='..' FROM PFILE='...' command to create a server parameter file and then restart the member to use it.

description: Redo Apply is not running
cause: Either the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration indicated that Redo Apply was turned off, or the MRP0 recovery process was not running. As a result, Redo Apply-related properties could not be set.
action: Turn on Redo Apply through Oracle Data Guard broker and rerun the command to set the Redo Apply-related properties.

description: Redo transport service for a standby database incorrectly set as alternate
cause: The redo transport service for a member was set as an alternate destination when no other member is set as an alternate destination for this member.
action: Re-enable the standby database or the entire configuration to allow the correct configuration property settings to be propagated to the initialization parameters.

description: Redo transport-related property is inconsistent with member setting.
cause: The values of one or more redo transport-related configuration properties were inconsistent with the in-memory settings or server parameter file settings. This may happen by directly altering initialization parameters instead of editing configurable property values using Oracle Data Guard broker.
action: Query the InconsistentLogXptProps property on the primary database or check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file to find which properties are set inconsistently. Reset these properties to make them consistent. Alternatively, enable the member or the entire configuration to allow the configurable property settings to be propagated to the initialization parameters.

description: Database role change operation permitted only by Data Guard broker when fast-start failover is enabled.
cause: Fast-start failover was enabled and a role change was not initiated from a Data Guard broker interface.
action: Use a Data Guard broker interface to perform a role change.

description: Unable to query a database table or fixed view.
cause: Querying a database table or fixed view failed. The database may not be opened or mounted.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for more details.

description: one or more configuration properties have invalid values
cause: Oracle Data Guard broker health check detected that one or more configuration properties in the broker configuration had invalid values. The property values were changed while broker management of the member was disabled.
action: Check Data Guard broker log file for more details on which properties have invalid values and reset them through the Oracle Data Guard broker.

description: Operation waiting for sessions to drain.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker operation is required to wait for sessions to drain.
action: No action necessary.

description: Supplemental logging is not turned on.
cause: Supplemental logging was not turned on while there was a logical standby database in the configuration. This could happen either on the primary database or on the logical standby database that was being switched over to become the primary database.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file for more details. Issue the ALTER DATABASE ADD SUPPLEMENTAL LOG DATA (PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE INDEX) COLUMNS statement to add supplemental logging.

description: unable to change configuration protection mode
cause: An attempt to issue the ALTER DATABASE SET STANDBY TO MAXIMIZE {PROTECTION | AVAILABILITY | PERFORMANCE} failed.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle alert log file for more information.

description: Primary database is not open.
cause: A prior attempt to open the primary database was disallowed because the primary had shut itself down earlier after being isolated from both the fast-start failover observer and the target standby database for more than the number of seconds specified by the FastStartFailoverThreshold configuration property. It was assumed that a fast-start failover was underway. Since that time, the primary database reestablished contact with either the observer or the target standby database indicating that a fast-start failover had not actually occurred.
action: Open the database by issuing the SQL*Plus ALTER DATABASE OPEN command.

description: Multiple warnings detected for the member.
cause: The broker detected multiple warnings for the member.
action: Get a detailed status report by checking the status of the member specified using either Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL CLI SHOW command.

description: Multiple errors or warnings detected for the member.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected multiple errors or warnings for the member.
action: Get a detailed status report by checking the status of the database with either Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL CLI SHOW command.

description: Apply instance not recorded by the Oracle Data Guard broker.
cause: The broker did not register an Apply instance for a standby database.
action: Reenable the standby database to clear the error.

description: Apply services are not running on apply instance recorded by the broker.
cause: Redo or SQL apply services were not running on the instance where Oracle Data Guard broker expected them.
action: Re-enable the standby database to clear the error.

description: apply service not running on apply instance %s recorded by the broker
cause: Redo or SQL Apply services were not running on the instance on which the Data Guard broker expected them to be running.
action: Reenable the standby database to clear the error.

description: Duplicate name specified for observer.
cause: The observer was not started because an observer with that name was already started.
action: Use the DGMGRL CLI SHOW OBSERVER command to check the names of the observers that have already been started. Retry the START OBSERVER command with an unused observer name.

description: member does not need to be reinstated
cause: The member specified was either already reinstated or did not need to be reinstated.
action: No action necessary. Any stale reinstate required status will be cleared after the next health check has completed.

description: incorrect database role
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker detected that the specified database had a different database role from the one that was recorded in the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration. This could be the result of a failed switchover or failover operation, or a switchover or failover operation performed with SQL*Plus.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker documentation to see how to recover from failed role change operations, or from role changes that were performed using SQL*Plus for databases managed by Oracle Data Guard broker.

description: unsynchronized fast-start failover configuration
cause: The fast-start failover target standby database was not synchronized with the primary database. As a result, a fast-start failover could not happen automatically in case of a primary database failure.
action: Ensure that the fast-start failover target standby database is running and that the primary database can ship redo data to it. When the standby database has received all of the redo data from the primary database, the primary and standby databases will then be synchronized. The Oracle Data Guard configuration may then failover automatically to the standby database in the event of loss of the primary database.

description: fast-start failover suspended
cause: The primary database was intentionally shut down. As a result, the fast-start failover could not take place automatically.
action: Start the primary database. This effectively restores the ability to automatically perform a fast-start failover in the event of a failure of the primary database.

description: fast-start failover observer not started
cause: The observer for fast-start failover was not started. As a result, fast-start failover could not happen in the event of a primary database failure.
action: Start the fast-start failover observer by using the DGMGRL START OBSERVER command.

description: fast-start failover observer is no longer observing this database
cause: A previously started observer was no longer actively observing this database. A significant amount of time elapsed since this database last heard from the observer. Possible reasons were: - The host where the observer was running was not available. - The network connection between the observer and this database was not available. - The observer process was terminated unexpectedly.
action: Check the reason why the observer cannot contact this database. If the problem cannot be corrected, stop the current observer by connecting to the Oracle Data Guard configuration and issuing the DGMGRL STOP OBSERVER command, and then start a new observer on another host using the DGMGRL START OBSERVER command.

description: Logical standby database dictionary not loaded.
cause: The logical standby database did not load the dictionary. This status may be returned when attempting to switchover or failover to a logical standby database that did not load its dictionary.
action: Start SQL Apply on the logical standby database if it is not already running. Wait for it to reach the APPLYING state.

description: New primary database not ready for standby database reinstatement.
cause: The new primary database, as a result of a logical standby database failover operation, did not fully complete the failover operation.
action: Wait until the failover operation has completed on the new primary database. Retry the reinstate operation.

description: Real Time Query standby pluggable database is closed.
cause: Redo apply services for this standby pluggable database that was in Real Time Query mode is stopped in response to the users attempt to either close the pluggable database or the database.
action: If the database is in the process of closing, no action is necessary. Data Guard broker will start redo apply services once the database is restarted, or the pluggable database is opened. Alternatively, issue the DGMGRL command: EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE name SET STATE=APPLY-ON to start recovery at the mounted instance in non-Real Time Query mode.

description: Multiple warnings, including fast-start failover-related warnings, detected for the database.
cause: The broker detected multiple warnings for the database. At least one of these warnings may have prevented fast-start failover from occurring.
action: To get a detailed status report, check the status of the database specified using either Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL CLI SHOW DATABASE command.

description: Multiple errors or warnings, including fast-start failover-related errors or warnings, detected for the database.
cause: The broker detected multiple errors or warnings for the database. At least one of these errors or warnings may have prevented a fast-start failover from occurring.
action: To get a detailed status report, check the status of the database specified using either Enterprise Manager or the DGMGRL CLI SHOW DATABASE command.

description: apply service state is inconsistent with the DelayMins property
cause: This warning was caused by one of the following reasons: - The apply service was started without specifying the real-time apply option or without the NODELAY option when the DelayMins property was set to zero. - The apply service was started with the real-time apply option or with the NODELAY option when the DelayMins property was set to a value greater than zero.
action: Reenable the standby database to allow the broker to restart the apply service with the apply options that are consistent with the specified value of the DelayMins property.

description: Flashback Database is disabled.
cause: The broker detected that the Flashback Database feature was disabled. With Flashback Database disabled, the broker could not reinstate a database that required reinstatement. Flashback Database may been disabled manually with the ALTER DATABASE FLASHBACK DATABASE OFF command or automatically by the database in the event of an error.
action: Check the database alert log to determine whether the Flashback Database was disabled due to errors and then correct the problem. If Flashback Database was manually disabled, reenable Flashback Database with the ALTER DATABASE FLASHBACK DATABASE ON command. If, after enabling Flashback Database, the database still cannot be reinstated, then the database must be re-created from a copy of the primary database.

description: invalid value specified for REDO_TRANSPORT_USER initialization parameter
cause: An invalid value was specified for the REDO_TRANSPORT_USER initialization parameter. The length of the user name exceeded the allowed maximum platform-specific length.
action: Check the documentation and specify a new value for the REDO_TRANSPORT_USER initialization parameter.

description: Fast-start failover configuration is lagging.
cause: The fast-start failover target standby database was not within the lag limit specified by the FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property. As a result, a fast-start failover could not happen in the event of a primary database failure.
action: Ensure that the fast-start failover target standby database is running and applying redo data and that the primary database is successfully transmitting redo data. If this condition persists, consider raising the value of the FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property.

description: Primary database isolated from its fast-start failover partners longer than FastStartFailoverThreshold seconds.
cause: The primary database was isolated from both the observer and target standby database for longer than the seconds specified by the FastStartFailoverThreshold property. A fast-start failover probably occurred. If the FastStartFailoverPmyShutdown configuration property was set to TRUE, the broker shut down the primary database.
action: Ensure one instance of this database is running and the database is mounted on that instance so that the broker may reinstate the old primary database.

description: Oracle Data Guard operation not allowed on this member.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker operation was not allowed for the specified member of the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration.
action: Check the documentation for the Oracle Data Guard broker command and then reissue the command with the correct member.

description: User-configurable fast-start failover initiated.
cause: The broker initiated a fast-start failover to the target standby database because a user-configurable condition was detected on the primary database. The broker shut down the primary database.
action: Correct the problem on the primary database that caused the broker to initiate a fast-start failover, then reinstate the primary database.

description: No such pluggable database at this database.
cause: There was no pluggable database with the specified name at the specified container database.
action: Provide the correct pluggable database name or container database name and reissue the command.

description: Specified pluggable database is not a standby pluggable database.
cause: The specified pluggable database name was not a standby pluggable database.
action: Provide the correct pluggable database name or container database name and retry.

description: Source pluggable database was dropped.
cause: The source pluggable database for this standby pluggable database was dropped.
action: Consider immediate failover to make this a native pluggable database, or remove this standby pluggable database.

description: Source pluggable database was unplugged.
cause: The source pluggable database for this standby pluggable database was unplugged.
action: Consider immediate failover to make this a native pluggable database, or remove this standby pluggable database.

description: Standby pluggable database is not applying redo data.
cause: Standby pluggable database was not applying redo data.
action: Ensure recovery was started and is running. Use the EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE SET STATE=APPLY-ON to start Redo Apply services. If this does not resolve the issue, switch logs at the source database.

description: Source pluggable database is not opened in read/write mode.
cause: The source pluggable database was not opened in read/write mode.
action: Open the source pluggable database in read/write mode and reissue the command.

description: Pluggable database must be in mounted mode.
cause: Could not remove the pluggable database that was in open mode.
action: Close the pluggable database and reissue the command.

description: Target pluggable database is not recovering current redo data.
cause: Target pluggable database was not recovering current redo data from the source pluggable database.
action: Start recovery at the target pluggable database using the EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE <pluggable database name> at <CDB> SET STATE=APPLY-ON statement.

description: Target pluggable database has not applied all redo.
cause: The target pluggable database had not completed applying all the redo data.
action: If the target pluggable database is still applying, allow it to apply all the redo and reissue the command. If apply has stopped, check why it has stopped and rectify the situation before proceeding.

description: Multitenant container database name specified does not exist.
cause: A multitenant container database name was incorrectly specified.
action: Specify the correct multitenant container database name.

description: Pluggable database needs to be re-created.
cause: An immediate failover to this pluggable database active target caused this pluggable database to require re-creation.
action: Drop this pluggable database and create it as a standby for its previous target pluggable database that was activated as a new source pluggable database.

description: database does not have a valid fast-start failover target standby database
cause: Fast-start failover was enabled and the current primary database did not have a value set for the FastStartFailoverTarget configurable property or the value specified for this property was not a valid fast-start failover target standby database.
action: Disable fast-start failover or ensure that the primary database has a valid fast-start failover target standby database specified by setting the FastStartFailoverTarget configurable property value to a valid standby database.

description: unsupported attribute specified for the local destination property
cause: The value specified for a local destination property contained unsupported attributes.
action: Ensure that the value specified for the ArchiveLocation, AlternateLocation, StandbyArchiveLocation, or StandbyAlternateLocation property does not contain the SERVICE, ALTERNATE, or VALID_FOR attribute.

description: ArchiveLocation and StandbyArchiveLocation should specify different destinations.
cause: An attempt was made to set the ArchiveLocation and StandbyArchiveLocation configurable properties to the same destination.
action: Ensure that the ArchiveLocation and StandbyArchiveLocation configurable properties specify different destinations.

description: A previous switchover from this database failed with error %s.
cause: A previous switchover operation from this database failed.
action: Fix the underlying problem and reissue the switchover command again.

description: A previous switchover to this database failed with error %s.
cause: A previous switchover operation to this database failed.
action: Fix the underlying problem and reissue the switchover command.

description: A previous switchover from this database was interrupted and aborted.
cause: A previous switchover operation from this database was interrupted. The interruption may have been caused by a stalled switchover.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle log file for more information, fix the underlying problem, and then reissue the switchover command.

description: A previous switchover to this database was interrupted and aborted.
cause: A previous switchover operation to this database was interrupted by the user. The interruption may be caused by a stalled switchover.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle log file for more information, fix the underlying problem, and then reissue the switchover command.

description: A previous failover to this database failed with error %s.
cause: A previous failover operation to this database failed.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle log file for more information, fix the underlying problem and then reissue the failover command.

description: A previous failover to this database was interrupted and aborted.
cause: A previous failover operation to this database was interrupted because the operation may have stalled.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log file and the Oracle log file for more information, fix the underlying problem, and then reissue the failover command.

description: apply lag has exceeded specified threshold
cause: The current apply lag exceeded the value specified by the ApplyLagThreshold configurable property. It may be caused either by a large transport lag or poor performance of apply services on the standby database.
action: Check for gaps (missing archive log files) on the standby database. If no gap is present, tune the apply services following Maximum Availability Architecture best practice guidelines.

description: apply lag could not be determined
cause: Apply lag could not be determined because either apply services were not running or there was no connectivity between the redo source and standby database.
action: Start apply services if they are not running. Also, ensure that there is network connectivity between the redo source and standby databases and that the redo source is sending redo data to the standby database.

description: transport lag has exceeded specified threshold
cause: The current transport lag exceeded the value specified by the TransportLagThreshold configurable property. This error is caused by either poor network performance between the redo source and the member or a network disconnection.
action: Check the network connection between the redo source and the member. If they are connected, check the network performance between the redo source and the member and tune it according to the Maximum Availability Architecture best practice guidelines.

description: transport lag could not be determined
cause: Transport lag could not be determined because there was no connectivity between the redo source and the member.
action: Ensure that there is network connectivity between the redo source and the members and that the redo source is working properly.

description: member disconnected from redo source for longer than specified threshold
cause: The amount of time the member was disconnected from the redo source exceeded the value specified by the TransportDisconnectedThreshold configurable database property caused by a lack of network connectivity between the redo source and the member.
action: Ensure that there is network connectivity between the redo source and the member and that the redo source is working properly.

description: Last communication time from redo source could not be determined.
cause: The member was never contacted by the redo source, so the last time the redo source had contacted this member could not be determined.
action: Ensure that there is network connectivity between the redo source and the member and that the redo source is working properly.

description: request terminated because delete, disable, or failover operation is in progress
cause: The broker terminated a request because it was processing a delete, disable, or failover operation.
action: Wait for the operation to complete and then retry the request.

description: Cannot remove the local configuration when it references a remote configuration.
cause: The local configuration could not be removed because it was associated with one or more remote configurations.
action: First, remove all the remote configurations using the REMOVE CONFIGURATION <config_name> command. Then, retry the remove operation for the local configuration using the REMOVE CONFIGURATION command.

description: ExternalDestination property requires DB_UNIQUE_NAME attribute
cause: The value specified for the ExternalDestination property did not contain the DB_UNIQUE_NAME attribute.
action: Ensure that DB_UNIQUE_NAME is specified as the value for the ExternalDestination property.

description: unsupported attribute specified for the ExternalDestination property
cause: The value specified for the ExternalDestination property contained unsupported attributes.
action: Ensure that the value specified for the ExternalDestination property does not contain any of these attributes: LOCATION, ALTERNATE, MAX_FAILURE, SYNC, TEMPLATE, MANDATORY, DELAY, NET_TIMEOUT, and VALID_FOR.

description: database is closing or is not mounted on the instance
cause: The Data Guard broker health check was unable to complete because the database was closing or was not mounted on the instance.
action: No action is required if the database is closing. Mount the database if it is not yet mounted on the instance.

description: database converted to transient logical standby database for rolling database maintenance
cause: This database was converted to a transient logical standby database because a rolling database maintenance operation was in progress.
action: No action is required. The database will be converted to a primary database when the DBMS_ROLLING.SWITCHOVER procedure is executed or to a physical standby database when the DBMS_ROLLING.FINISH procedure is executed.

description: cannot remove a database that is specified in a FastStartFailoverTarget configuration property
cause: An attempt was made to remove a database that was specified in the FastStartFailoverTarget configuration property of another database.
action: First, remove the database from all other database's FastStartFailoverTarget configuration property values. Then, retry the REMOVE command.

description: Fast-start failover target standby database not viable.
cause: The fast-start failover target standby database was not viable. As a result, a fast-start failover to this database could not happen automatically.
action: After the standby database has been re-created from a copy of the new primary database, disable and then reenable the standby database.

description: fast-start failover target not initialized
cause: The standby database was not ready to be a fast-start failover target standby database. Consequently, fast-start failover could not be initiated to this database in the event of a primary database failure.
action: Ensure that the network connection between the primary and the fast-start failover target standby is functioning properly.

description: rolling database maintenance is in progress
cause: This is an Oracle internal status code. This status is used by the primary database to convey to the standby database during startup, that rolling database maintenance is in progress within the configuration.
action: N/A, this is an Oracle internal status code.

description: fast-start failover target switch is not supported
cause: Automatic switch of the fast-start failover target was not possible because the release of the observer was earlier than 12.2. Consequently, the fast-start failover target switch will not occur even though the primary database has more than one fast-start failover target configured.
action: Upgrade the Oracle client home to release 12.2 and then stop and restart the observer using the DGMGRL CLI in that Oracle home.

description: AlternateLocation and StandbyAlternateLocation should specify different destinations.
cause: An attempt was made to set the AlternateLocation and StandbyAlternateLocation configurable properties to the same destination.
action: Ensure that the AlternateLocation and StandbyAlternateLocation configurable properties specify different destinations.

description: The observer with the specified name is not started.
cause: The operation was not allowed because the observer corresponding to the specified name was not started.
action: Issue the command again after ensuring that the observer corresponding to the specified name is started.

description: The specified observer host is invalid.
cause: The operation was not allowed because there was no registered observer running on the specified host.
action: Issue the command again after ensuring that there is a registered observer running on the specified host.

description: master observer switch is in progress
cause: The operation was not allowed because a master observer switch was already in progress.
action: Wait for a few seconds and retry the operation.

description: observer name not specified
cause: The operation was not allowed because an observer name was not specified and there was more than one observer registered.
action: Retry the command and be sure to specify the observer name or use the term ALL when more than one observer is registered.

description: no registered observers
cause: The operation was not allowed because there were no registered observers.
action: None.

description: master observer cannot be stopped
cause: The master observer cannot be stopped when another observer is registered.
action: Use the SET MASTEROBSERVER command to establish another observer as the master observer. Then use the STOP OBSERVER command to stop the former master observer.

description: Fast-start failover cannot be initiated by a non-master observer.
cause: Fast-start failover was initiated by a non-master observer. This can occur if the Oracle Data Guard broker started a master observer switch at the same time fast-start failover was being initiated.
action: Check the Oracle Data Guard broker log files of the primary database to see why a master observer switch occurred.

description: fast-start failover target switch is in progress
cause: The operation was not allowed because a fast-start failover target switch was already in progress.
action: Wait for a few seconds and retry the operation.

description: standby database is not protecting the current primary database during rolling database maintenance
cause: This standby database was a member of the leading group standby databases protecting the future primary database, or was a member of the trailing group standby databases protecting the original primary database during the rolling database maintenance operation.
action: This issue will be resolved once all the databases have completed the maintenance operation and the DBMS_ROLLING.FINISH procedure is executed.

description: rolling database maintenance processing is managing apply services
cause: Apply services were stopped because a rolling database maintenance operation was in progress.
action: No action is required. Apply services will be restarted by Oracle.

description: unable to translate the DGConnectIdentifier property to a valid connect identifier
cause: One or more members in the Data Guard configuration could not resolve the connect identifier specified by the DGConnectIdentifier property. The connectivity between the members could not be established for this reason. This might be caused by a missing or invalid tnsnames.ora entry, or an invalid connect descriptor, a missing naming method in sqlnet.ora, or another naming issue.
action: Use the command VALIDATE NETWORK CONFIGURATION FOR ALL in DGMGRL and verify which database or instance could not resolve the connect identifier. Fix the problem depending on the naming method used in your environment.

description: The specified observer name is invalid.
cause: A reserved keyword (ALL or NONAME) was specified for the observer name for the START OBSERVER command.
action: Specify a name other than ALL or NONAME and retry the command.

description: A member whose RedoCompression property is set to LZO cannot receive redo data in SYNC or FASTSYNC mode.
cause: A member was specified to receive redo data in SYNC or FASTSYNC mode when the RedoCompression configurable property was set to LZO.
action: Set the RedoCompression property to a value other than LZO and then retry the command.

description: The RedoCompression property cannot be set to LZO for a member that receives redo data in SYNC or FASTSYNC mode.
cause: An attempt was made to set the RedoCompression configurable property to LZO when it receives redo data in SYNC or FASTSYNC mode.
action: Set the RedoCompression configurable property to a value other than LZO and then retry the command.

description: failed to import Oracle Data Guard broker configuration file
cause: A failure was encountered while the broker was importing the configuration file specified by the user.
action: Ensure that the specified file exists, the proper permissions are granted, and the file has valid Oracle Data Guard broker configuration information.

description: Fast-start failover must be disabled before changing between standard and observe-only modes.
cause: Either the ENABLE FAST_START FAILOVER command was issued when fast- start failover was enabled in observe-only mode, or the ENABLE FAST_START FAILOVER OBSERVE ONLY command was issued when fast-start failover was enabled in standard mode.
action: Disable fast-start failover using the DISABLE FAST_START FAILOVER command in DGMGRL, and then reissue the command that failed.

description: Database does not have a valid fast-start failover target standby database in observe-only mode.
cause: Fast-start failover was enabled in observe-only mode and the current primary database did not have a value set for the FastStartFailoverTarget configurable property or the value specified for this property was not a valid fast-start failover target standby database.
action: Disable fast-start failover or ensure that the primary database has a valid fast-start failover target standby database specified by setting the FastStartFailoverTarget configurable property value to a valid standby database.

description: unsynchronized fast-start failover configuration in observe-only mode
cause: The fast-start failover target standby database was not synchronized with the primary database in observe-only mode. However, manual failover is still allowed in observe-only mode.
action: Ensure that the fast-start failover target standby database is running and that the primary database can ship redo data to it. When the standby database has received all of the redo data from the primary database, the primary and standby databases are synchronized.

description: fast-start failover configuration is lagging in observe-only mode
cause: The fast-start failover target standby database was not within the lag limit specified by the FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property in observe-only mode. However, manual failover is still allowed in observe-only mode.
action: Ensure that the fast-start failover target standby database is running and applying redo data and that the primary database is successfully transmitting redo data. If this condition persists, consider increasing the value of the FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property.

description: Oracle Data Guard broker configuration does not exist in the remote database.
cause: A broker operation was requested that required a broker configuration to be available at the remote database.
action: Create an Oracle Data Guard broker configuration at the remote database prior to performing other broker operations for the remote database.

description: invalid Oracle Data Guard broker configuration metadata
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Configuration could not be added because it contains one or more standby databases.
cause: An attempt was made to add a configuration when one or more configurations already contain one or more standby members.
action: Remove all members, except the primary database, from both configurations and retry the command.

description: configuration name mismatch
cause: The expected configuration name value did not match the actual configuration name that the broker contacted using the connect identifier that was associated with that configuration.
action: Verify that the connect identifier correctly connects to the intended configuration. Verify that the name of the configuration the broker expects to find by that connect identifier matches the actual name of the configuration.

description: start database to mount mode
cause: This error was returned by DBMS_DG.SWITCHOVER because the database must be started to the mount mode to complete the switchover operation. Or, the error was returned from DBMS_DG.REINSTATE or DBMS_DG.CONVERT_TO_PHYSICAL when the database must be started to the mount mode to perform the operation.
action: Start the database to the mount mode, wait for the database to start, and wait for the broker to complete initialization using DBMS_DG.WAIT(WAIT_BOOT, <wait time in seconds>). Then, for reinstate and convert operations, retry the operation.

description: start database to open mode
cause: This error was returned by DBMS_DRS.SWITCHOVER because the database was not started in the open mode to complete the switchover operation.
action: Start the database in the open mode to complete the switchover operation.

description: Operation requires a connection to the primary database.
cause: The operation was rejected because it required a connection to the primary database.
action: Connect to the primary database and retry the operation.

description: changing LogXptMode or RedoRoutes property violates overall protection mode
cause: The broker did not allow the attempt to change the LogXptMode or RedoRoutes configurable property for the standby database or far sync instance because, if allowed, the overall protection mode for the configuration would have been violated.
action: If the LogXptMode or RedoRoutes configuration property must be changed for the specified standby database or far sync instance, first downgrade the overall protection mode for the broker configuration. After that operation has completed, the LogXptMode or RedoRoutes configuration property for the standby database can be changed.

description: A rolling database maintenance operation is in progress.
cause: The attempted operation was not allowed because a rolling database maintenance operation was in progress.
action: Wait for the rolling database maintenance operation to complete. Then retry the operation.

description: The specified standby database is not a valid fast-start failover target.
cause: The attempted operation was not allowed because the specified database was not a valid fast-start failover target because of one of the following reasons: - The specified database was not a physical standby database or logical standby database. - The effective redo transport mode for the standby database was not set to SYNC or FASTSYNC if the protection mode was set to maximum availability mode. - The effective redo transport mode for the standby database was not set to SYNC if the protection mode was set to maximum protection mode. - The effective redo transport mode for the standby database was not set to ASYNC if the protection mode was set to maximum performance mode. - The standby database was not configured to receive redo data directly from the primary database when the protection mode was set to maximum performance mode. - The primary database had more than one rule in its RedoRoutes property to the standby database. - The specified standby database was a logical standby database when the protection mode was set to maximum protection mode. - The standby database was disabled. - Redo transport-related properties of the standby database were inconsistent with the database setting. - The specified standby database's FastStartFailoverTarget property did not specify the primary database when the standby is a logical standby database.
action: Check that the specified standby database meets the requirements listed in the Cause section of this error message.

description: change of FastStartFailoverLagLimit property violates configuration protection mode
cause: The attempt to set the FastStartFailoverLagLimit property could not be completed. The new value for the FastStartFailoverLagLimit property did not meet one or more of the following requirements: - The property must be nonzero when the configuration protection mode is set to MaxPerformance mode. - The property must be zero when the configuration protection mode is set to MaxProtection mode.
action: Check the above requirements and retry the operation.

description: Member may be a primary database or is receiving redo data from another primary database.
cause: A role change operation may have resulted in this member either becoming a primary database or was receiving redo data from a standby database that became a primary database.
action: Evaluate all members' roles in the configuration and confirm which database should be the primary database before taking further action.

description: The member was not enabled.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker configuration member was added to the configuration, but not enabled.
action: Enable the Oracle Data Guard broker configuration member.

description: The member was shutdown.
cause: The Oracle Data Guard broker configuration member was shutdown.
action: This status will be changed when the member is restarted.

description: syntax error for the PreferredObserverHosts property
cause: The change to the PreferredObserverHosts property was disallowed because the new value contained syntax errors.
action: Check the syntax of the PreferredObserverHosts property and retry the operation.

description: This observer cannot become the master observer.
cause: The observer specified to become the master observer could not be selected because it was not included in the list of observers specified for the PreferredObserverHosts configurable property of the primary database.
action: Check the value specified for the PreferredObserverHosts configurable property of the primary database. Then, reissue the DGMGRL SET MASTEROBSERVERHOST TO command and select one of the observers specified in the list.

description: Operation not allowed when configuration contains a remote configuration.
cause: An attempt was made to add a remote configuration or a standby database when the configuration already contained a remote configuration.
action: None.

description: Apply state is inconsistent for one or more standby pluggable databases.
cause: One or more standby pluggable databases either have apply running while it is set to APPLY-OFF or apply is not running while it is set to APPLY-ON.
action: Use the SHOW PLUGGABLE DATABASE command to determine the standby pluggable databases that have the inconsistency. Also check the Oracle alert log files to see more details.

description: Redo data from new source database has not been registered.
cause: Redo data from the new source database was not registered for this standby pluggable database.
action: Ensure the previous role change command completed successfully. If there were any errors, address the issues and complete the role change. If this still does not address the issues, try restarting recovery. Use the EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE SET STATE=APPLY-ON to start Redo Apply and switch logs at the source database.

description: Target pluggable database may have been removed or a role change may have occurred.
cause: Either a pluggable database switchover or failover occurred, resulting in this pluggable database not having an active target standby pluggable database; or the target standby pluggable database was removed.
action: If a role change has occurred, after determining which pluggable database is the current source and status of the previous source pluggable database, proceed as follows: - If it is already in the standby role and a switchover has occurred, address the issues that resulted in Redo Apply Services failing to start and then start Redo Apply Services. - If it is already in the standby role and a failover has occurred, verify that the issues that necessitated the failover have been addressed and then start Redo Apply services. - If the previous source pluggable database is still in the primary role, and a failover immediate has occurred, address the issues that necessitated the failover, drop the previous source pluggable database, and add it back as the target standby database using the ADD PLUGGABLE DATABASE command, and then start Redo Apply Services. Note that Redo Apply can be started using the EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE SET STATE=APPLY-ON command.

description: cannot remove a remote configuration that sends or receives redo data
cause: An attempt was made to remove a remote configuration that sent or received redo data.
action: First, clear redo transport using EDIT CONFIGURATION <config name> CLEAR AS SOURCE command. Then, retry REMOVE CONFIGURATION <config name> command.

description: Redo Apply Services were not started at the standby pluggable database.
cause: Redo Apply Services were not started on the standby pluggable database.
action: To start Redo Apply Services for all standby pluggable databases, use the ENABLE DATABASE command. To start Redo Apply Services for a single standby pluggable database, use the EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE SET STATE=APPLY-ON command.

description: fast-start failover incarnation mismatch
cause: This was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: The specified fast-start failover condition is disabled.
cause: The specified fast-start failover condition or Oracle error number was already disabled.
action: This is an informational message. No additional action is required.

description: Fast-start failover lag limit value is greater than fast-start failover threshold value.
cause: The FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property is set to a value that is greater than the value of the FastStartFailoverThreshold configuration property.
action: No corrective action is required. Be aware that the primary database will stall after the value of the FastStartFailoverThreshold configuration has elapsed. It will not continue to commit transactions up to the specified lag limit.

description: Standby pluggable database after previous role change is not ready.
cause: The standby pluggable database after previous switchover or reinstate operation is not recovering redo data from the new source pluggable database.
action: See accompanying messages for more information. If necessary, start Redo Apply services by issuing the DGMGRL command EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE name SET STATE=APPLY-ON.

description: The former target pluggable database executed a failover immediate.
cause: Failover immediate to the former target pluggable database resulted in this pluggable database needing to be re-created.
action: Drop this pluggable database. Then, add a standby pluggable database using the ADD PLUGGABLE DATABASE statement to create a new standby pluggable database.

description: The specified pluggable database already exists.
cause: The command could not be executed because the specified pluggable database already existed in the multitenant container database.
action: Reissue the command with a different pluggable database name.

description: The specified pluggable database already exists as a physical standby role.
cause: The command could not be executed because the specified pluggable database already existed as a physical standby role.
action: Check the pluggable database configuration in the multitenant container database and reissue the command with a correct pluggable database.

description: Configuration not ready for Oracle Data Guard per Pluggable Database.
cause: An Oracle Data Guard per Pluggable Database command was attempted before the configuration was ready for Oracle Data Guard per Pluggable Database. This could be because Golden Gate capture was already running, or the Data Guard per Pluggable Database was not available.
action: If Golden Gate capture is not running, use the DGMGRL command EDIT CONFIGURATION PREPARE DGPDB command before attempting this operation again. If Golden Gate capture is running, the Data Guard per Pluggable Database feature cannot be used.

description: The source and target multitenant container databases cannot be the same.
cause: The command could not proceed because the specified source and target multitenant container database were the same name or same database identifier (DBID).
action: Reissue the command with distinct multitenant container databases.

description: The specified source pluggable database is a standby pluggable database.
cause: The command could not be executed because the specified source pluggable database already existed in the physical standby role.
action: Check the pluggable database configuration in the multitenant container database and reissue the command with a correct source pluggable database.

description: Output document is too long.
cause: The number of pluggable databases protected by Oracle Data Guard for pluggable database exceeds the size that can be represented in the response output buffer returned by the server.
action: Query the names of pluggable databases on the multitenant container database using the SHOW PDBS command. Then, issue the DGMGRL SHOW PLUGGABLE DATABASE command for each pluggable database.

description: Redo apply services of the specified standby pluggable database is waiting for redo data.
cause: Redo apply services of the specified standby pluggable database was waiting for redo data. This could occur if standby redo logs had been added after recovery had been started.
action: Consider switching logs at the source multitenant container database to expedite apply at the standby pluggable database.

description: FastStartFailoverLagGraceTime value must be less than FastStartFailoverLagLimit value.
cause: The value specified for the FastStartFailoverLagGraceTime configuration property is greater than, or equal to the value of the FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property.
action: Specify a value for the FastStartFailoverLagGraceTime configuration property that is less than the value of the FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property.

description: FastStartFailoverLagLimit value must be greater than FastStartFailoverLagGraceTime value.
cause: The value specified for the FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property is less than, or equal to the value of the FastStartFailoverLagGraceTime configuration property.
action: Specify a value for the FastStartFailoverLagLimit configuration property that is greater than the value of the FastStartFailoverLagGraceTime configuration property.

description: Tag is not found
cause: The specified tag does not exist.
action: Retry the command with a valid tag name.

description: Real Time Query will be enabled on an open instance shortly.
cause: Either an open was initiated for this standby pluggable database at one of the instances and was not yet open when redo apply services was starting, or this standby pluggable database was previously open in Real Time Query mode and redo apply services is waiting for this standby pluggable database to be open. Data Guard broker will start redo apply services when an instance of this standby pluggable database is open and available to enable Real Time Query.
action: If the standby pluggable database is in the process of opening, no action is necessary. Data Guard broker will start redo apply services once it is opened. If not, consider opening the standby pluggable database at one of the instances, or issue the DGMGRL command EDIT PLUGGABLE DATABASE name SET STATE=APPLY-ON to start recovery at a mounted instance in non-Real Time Query mode.

description: Tag name is not valid.
cause: The specified tag name is not allowed. - Tag names can contain letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores. - Tag names must start with a letter. - Tag names cannot start with the letters 'xml' or 'ora'.
action: Retry the command with a valid tag name.

description: Cannot connect to partner database.
cause: An attempt was made to connect to the partner database for a per PDB Data Guard operation, but the connection attempt failed.
action: Ensure the partner database is available and accessible. Check the Data Guard broker (DRC) log and alert logs of both databases for further details. Retry the operation once the database is available and accessible.

description: A lost write was detected, no failover will be initiated.
cause: A primary database lost write was reported by a physical standby database.
action: Check the alert and Data Guard broker (DRC) logs of both databases for more information about the lost write.

description: Remote mapped cursors are not supported by this feature.
cause: This cursor is a remote mapped cursor which could not be processed locally.
action: Try to process this statement directly on the remote site.

description: Number of bind variables for this SQL statement exceeded maximum of %s.
cause: Binding this SQL statement failed because too many bind variables were supplied.
action: Pass the correct number of bind variables.

description: Failed to bind this SQL statement.
cause: Binding this SQL statement failed.
action: Check if bind variables for that statement are properly specified.

description: Type of SQL statement not supported.
cause: This type of SQL statement could not be processed.
action: NA

description: SQL parse error.
cause: The specified SQL statement failed to be parsed.
action: Check if syntax is correct and ensure that this statement can be parsed by the specified user name.

description: Unknown error during SQL analyze.
cause: The specified SQL statement failed to be analyzed.
action: This is an internal error, please contact Oracle support.

description: Only SELECT or DML statements are supported for test execute.
cause: The specified SQL statement cannot be tested for execute.
action: NA

description: SQL Analyze time limit interrupt
cause: This is an internal error code used indicate that SQL analyze has reached its time limit.
action: NA

description: DML statements running parallel are not supported for test execute.
cause: The specified DML statement cannot be tested for execute because part of it is running parallel.
action: NA

description: Statement type has been disabled for SQL Analyze
cause: The system attempted to analyze a type of statement that was disabled by the current feature.
action: Try a different feature capable of analyzing this statement type.

description: SQL Analyze could not reproduce the desired plan.
cause: SQL Analyze failed to reproduce a particular plan using an outline.
action: Check the outline data.

description: SQL statement with SQL patch is ignored
cause: SQL statements with SQL patches are not supported by SQL tuning advisor.
action: Check the SQL patch information. Rerun SQL repair advisor on that SQL statement for a potential better SQL patch.

description: SQL statement attempted to begin an autonomous transaction
cause: The SQL statement being analyzed attempted to begin an autonomous transaction, which is not supported.
action: Analyze another statement or remove the autonomous transaction from the current statement.

description: The given user or schema is not supported by this feature.
cause: The SQL statement being analyzed had a parsing user or schema which is not currently supported for SQL Analyze.
action: Analyze another statement.

description: OPC ODM read ahead buffer size
cause: This is an Oracle internal event code. This event is used to control read ahead buffer size in the OPC ODM library. DO NOT USE.
action: The read ahead buffer size is set to the value of this event when appropriate, such as during file open.

description: Invalid ODM object store segment size %s. Valid range: %s-%s.
cause: The specified object store Dynamic Large Object (DLO) segment size was invalid. The DLO size must be within the specified valid range.
action: Specify a valid segment size (_objectstore_odm_segment_size) for use with the Oracle Disk Manager (ODM) object store library.
params: 1) ODM_segment_size: The specified segment size that is outside of the supported range. 2) min_ODM_segment_size: The minimum supported segment size value. 3) max_ODM_segment_size: The maximum supported segment size value.

description: OPC ODM error simulation event
cause: This is an Oracle internal event code. This event is used to simulate specific code errors for testing purposes. DO NOT USE.
action: Various errors can be simulated depending on the level set in this event.

description: Object store file is too large %s %s %s.
cause: The operation encountered a file on the object store that exceeds the maximum size for Swift API Dynamic Large Object (DLO) or Oracle Object Storage Service API file or files.
action: Retry the write operation with a file smaller than the first argument in the error code. Split exports using DBMS_CLOUD or Data Pump into multiple smaller files to avoid the limitation.

description: Object store file %s cannot be closed during a network wait.
cause: An attempt to close a file that is on the object store was made while there was an onoing network wait. A file close cannot occur during a network wait because some resources may be in use by other components and waiting for some external data.
action: Retry the operation that raised this error. Do not attempt to forcibly close any object store files during any database operations which may be using them in some other context, such as a backup or clone of a pluggable database (PDB).

description: User %s in PDB %s network access blocked by %s code %s.
cause: An attempt to access the network is blocked by the specified security check.
