description: error occurred reading %s bytes at block number %s
cause: An error occurred while reading from a file.
action: Other messages should be displayed describing the cause of the error. Correct the error and then retry the copy, backup, or restore operation.
params: 1) read_bytes: The number of bytes attempted to be read. 2) block_number: The corrupt block number.

description: %s RECID %s STAMP %s is no longer valid
cause: The indicated record was marked as deleted. This indicates that the corresponding file has either been overwritten by another copy or restore, or that the copy was consumed by a SWITCHTOCOPY operation.
action: If you know the name of the file that you want to copy, then inspect it and retry the copy specifying the new RECID.
params: 1) object_type: The object type of the record. 2) record_id: The record ID in the control file. 3) set_stamp: The set stamp of the object.

description: %s is not a snapshot or backup control file
cause: The control file that is the source for a backup or copy operation is not a snapshot or backup control file.
action: Specify the name of a snapshot or backup control file.

description: conversation already active
cause: You tried to begin a backup or restore conversation, but another conversation is already active in this session.
action: Either continue the current conversation, or call BACKUPCANCEL or RESTORECANCEL to end the current conversation before starting a new one.

description: backup aborted because job time exceeded duration time
cause: You tried to backup with duration option and the time provided was not sufficient to complete the backup.
action: Adjust the duration time and re-run the command. Or run the backup command without duration option.

description: wrong %s conversation type
cause: You attempted to specify a type of file for a backup or restore operation, but the current conversation cannot process this type of file. For example, you specified an archived log to be included in a data file backup set. The specified file will not be included in the backup or restore operation.
action: No action required: the conversation is still active, and more files can be specified.

description: data file number %s already included as %s
cause: This data file was already specified for inclusion in this backup or restore conversation. A backup or restore conversation can process only a single instance of a data file.
action: No action required. The conversation is still active, and more files can be specified.
params: 1) data_file_number: The data file number of the target data file. 2) data_file_name: The data file name of target data file.

description: control file already included as %s
cause: The control file is already specified for inclusion in this backup or restore conversation. A backup or restore conversation may process only a single instance of the control file.
action: No action required - the conversation is still active, and more files can be specified.

description: archived log %s already included in backup conversation
cause: The indicated archived log had already been specified for inclusion in this backup conversation.
action: No action required. The conversation is still active, and more files can be specified.

description: SPFILE already included
cause: The SPFILE is already specified for inclusion in this backup or restore conversation. A backup or restore conversation may process only a single instance of the SPFILE.
action: No action required. The conversation is still active, and more files can be specified.

description: file %s block size %s does not match backup set block size %s
cause: A file was specified for inclusion in a backup set, but its logical block size is different from the other files in the backup set. All files in a backup set must have the same logical block size.
action: Specify a file that has the same block size as the other files in the backup set. The conversation is still active and more files can be specified.
params: 1) file_name: The name of the file whose size is incorrect. 2) file_size: The offending size of the named file. 3) block_size: The correct block size that the second parameter should match.

description: cannot backup SPFILE because the instance was not started with SPFILE
cause: A backup command requested a backup of the SPFILE, but no SPFILE had been used to startup the instance.
action: Create an SPFILE and re-start the instance using the SPFILE.

description: Block number %s is corrupt in %s %s.
cause: A corrupt block was found in a control file, archived log, or backup piece that is being read to create a backup or copy. Corruption cannot be allowed in control files, archived logs, or backup pieces.
action: No action necessary. The copy or backup operation failed. In the case of a backup set, the conversation is active and the piece may be retried.

description: input file is %s %s (%s)
cause: This message identifies the input file for a failed copy operation. Both the file number and name (if the name has been determined) are shown. For a datafile, the file number refers to the datafile's absolute file number as shown in the DBA_DATA_FILES view. For a datafile copy, the file number refers to the copy's control file record number as shown in the RECID column of the V$DATAFILE_COPY view. For an archived log, the file number refers to the log's control file record number as shown in the RECID column of the V$ARCHIVED_LOG view.
action: See other error message.

description: output file is %s %s (%s)
cause: This message identifies the output file for a failed copy operation. The fields are as described in message 19600. When creating a new datafile copy, its control file record number may not have been determined when the message is printed. In that case, the record number shown is zero.
action: See other error message.

description: cannot backup or copy active file in NOARCHIVELOG mode
cause: An attempt was made to copy or backup a file that was not closed cleanly, and the database was in NOARCHIVELOG mode. This is not allowed because, when restored, the file requires redo application before it is usable, and redo is not currently being saved beyond the contents of the online redo logs.
action: Take the tablespace cleanly offline or close the database and retry the copy or backup.

description: cannot backup or copy an active file with KEEP ... UNRECOVERABLE options
cause: You tried to copy or backup a file, which was not closed cleanly, with KEEP ... UNRECOVERABLE option. This is not allowed because when the file is restored, it will require redo logs before it becomes usable, and redo logs will not have been saved because of KEEP ... UNRECOVERABLE option.
action: Take the tablespace offline cleanly, or close the database and retry the operation.

description: conversation file naming phase is over
cause: A call was made to specify a file for backup or restore operation after the first backup piece was processed.
action: Specifying more files to be processed during a backup or restore conversation is not allowed after the first backup piece has been processed. To more files must be specified, then begin a new conversation.

description: input file name must be specified
cause: The input file name was not specified for a control file copy operation.
action: Specify an input file name and retry the operation.

description: cannot copy or restore to snapshot control file
cause: A control file copy or restore operation specified the name of the snapshot control file as the output file. It overwriting the snapshot control file is not permitted in this manner. Other methods are available to create the snapshot control file.
action: Specify a different file name and retry the operation. If this is a restore, then the restore conversation remains active and more files may be specified.

description: %s is an active control file
cause: A control file copy, restore, or backup specified a control file named in the initialization parameter file as the input or output file.
action: Specify a different file name and retry the operation. If this is a backup or restore conversation, then the conversation remains active and more files may be specified.
params: 1) control_file: The file name of the control file backup.

description: %s is not a backup piece
cause: The specified file is not a backup piece produced by the DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE package. Either the first block of the backup piece is corrupt or this file is not a backup piece.
action: Specify a different file name and retry the operation.

description: %s is from different backup set: stamp %s count %s
cause: The specified file was not from the backup set that is currently being processed. It is part of a different backup set. The identification of the set containing this piece is shown.
action: Specify the correct backup piece and retry the operation.
params: 1) backup_piece: The backup piece being processed. 2) backup_set_actual: The backup set name to which the backup piece belongs. 3) backup_set_count: The backup set count of the backup piece.

description: Backup piece directory block %s is corrupt.
cause: The indicated directory block failed checksum validation. This backup piece is unusable.
action: Supply another copy of the same backup piece, or terminate the restore conversation.

description: backup piece out of order. Expected %s but found %s
cause: This backup piece is out of sequence.
action: Supply the correct backup piece.

description: datafile %s not restored due to %s
cause: The indicated file could not be restored, because all of its data blocks were not found in the backup piece.
action: The restore conversation remains active, and the current piece must be re-processed. If the failure cannot be resolved by re-processing the current piece, then the restore conversation must be cancelled.

description: datafile %s not found in backup set
cause: The indicated file could not be restored, because it is not in this backup set. If the file number is zero, then this refers to the control file.
action: This message is issued when the directory from the first backup piece is read and one or more files named for restoration were not found. The restore conversation is still active, but no data has been read and you must supply the first backup piece of a backup set that contains all of the requested files.

description: archived log thread %s sequence %s not found in backup set
cause: The indicated archived log file was named explicitly for restoration but is not contained in this backup set.
action: This message is issued when the directory from the first backup piece is read and one or more files named for restoration were not found. The restore conversation is still active, but no data has been read and you must supply the first backup piece of a backup set that contains all of the requested files.

description: some files not found in backup set
cause: Some files that were specified for restoration were not found in the backup set directory. Error message 19613 or 19614 is issued for each file that was not found.
action: See the instructions for error message 19613.

description: output file name must be specified if database not mounted
cause: A datafile restore specified no target file name, but the database is not mounted. The database must be mounted when no target file name is specified, so that the target file name can be obtained from the control file.
action: The restore conversation remains active. If you wish to restore datafiles without their target file names, then mount the database before continuing. Otherwise, a target file name must be specified on all datafile restoration calls.

description: File %s contains different RESETLOGS data.
cause: The indicated file contains RESETLOGS data that is different from the archived log files that are already included in the backup set. All archived log files in a backup set must have the same RESETLOGS data.
action: The restore conversation remains active, and you can continue to specify archived log files for inclusion in the backup set.

description: cannot name files after RESTOREVALIDATE has been called
cause: A call was made to specify a file to restore from a backup set, but a previous call to RESTOREVALIDATE had already been made.
action: Cancel and restart the conversation to specify the files to restore.

description: cannot call RESTOREVALIDATE after files have been named
cause: RESTOREVALIDATE was called after some files had already been specified for restoration.
action: You must cancel and restart the conversation if you wish to call RESTOREVALIDATE.

description: %s is not of %s type
cause: When opening the file to be placed in a copy or backup set, to be inspected, or used as the target for an incremental restore, its header was not recognized as a valid file header for a file of the indicated type (datafile, archived log, or control file) belonging to the current database.
action: The indicated file cannot be processed. Ensure that the correct files are being specified for the copy or backup operation.

description: archived log range is already specified
cause: A range of logs was already specified. Only one system change number (SCN) range can be specified for each conversation.
action: The restore conversation remains active and more logs may be specified by thread and sequence number, if desired.

description: archived log thread %s sequence %s not restored due to %s
cause: The indicated file could not be restored, because all of its data blocks were not found in the backup piece.
action: The restore conversation remains active, and the current piece must be re-processed. If the failure cannot be resolved by re-processing the current piece, then the restore conversation must be cancelled.

description: file %s is open
cause: A SWITCHTOCOPY operation specified a datafile copy whose parent datafile is open.
action: Take the owning tablespace offline or close the database, then retry the operation.

description: operation failed, retry possible
cause: A backup, restore, or image copy operation failed with an I/O error. If the source of the I/O error can be corrected, then the operation may be retried.
action: This message is used by the Recovery Manager to decide whether or not to retry the operation.

description: error identifying file %s
cause: A file specified as input to a copy or backup operation, or as the target for an incremental restore, could not be identified as an Oracle file. The file may have been deleted or moved so that it is no longer accessible to RMAN. An operating system-specific error accompanies this error to help pinpoint the problem.
action: Specify a different file and retry the operation. If the problem file has simply been deleted or moved, you can run crosscheck to allow RMAN to update its metadata with the correct file status.

description: backup set type is %s - can not be processed by this conversation
cause: The data in the backup set is not compatible with the current conversation.
action: Either supply the first piece from a backup set that matches the current conversation or start a new restore conversation which can process this backup set.

description: cannot read backup pieces during control file application
cause: This is a control file restore conversation, which is using the offline range information from one or more control files to update datafile checkpoint data. Backup sets are not used during this type of conversation.
action: The conversation is still active and more control files may be applied.

description: invalid SCN range
cause: The starting system change number (SCN) for RESTOREREDOLOGRANGE was greater than the ending SCN.
action: Specify a starting SCN that is less than or equal to the ending SCN.

description: no files in specified archived log SCN range
cause: This backup set contains no files in the specified range.
action: Either supply a backup set that contains files in the correct range or start a new conversation and specify a range which will select some files from this backup set.

description: end of volume encountered while copying backup piece
cause: While copying a backup piece from the OS native file system to an output device, the output device encountered end-of-volume.
action: The copy fails. This could happen if a tape was used which is not large enough to hold the entire backup piece.

description: archived log record does not contain a file name
cause: This archived log record represented a switch into an active log that took place without archiving its prior contents. The prior contents of the log file were lost.
action: Specify the RECID of an archived log record that contains a file name. Fixed view V$ARCHIVED_LOG can be used to examine the archived logs.

description: file name not found in control file
cause: The name passed to GETFNO was not found in the control file.
action: Supply a valid file name.

description: control file record %s is out of sync with recovery catalog
cause: The control file record describing the file to be deleted in a call to DELETEBACKUPPIECE, DELETEDATAFILECOPY, PROXYDELETE or DELETEARCHIVEDLOG does not match the validation data supplied by recovery manager.
action: contact Oracle support

description: file name required for this function
cause: The FNAME or HANDLE parameter was not specified for DELETEPIECE, DELETEDATAFILECOPY, DELETEREDOLOG or PROXYDELETE.
action: Specify the FNAME or HANDLE parameter when calling these functions.

description: input and output file names are identical: %s
cause: Identical input and output file names were specified for a data file copy operation.
action: Specify an output file name that is different from the input file name.
params: 1) file_name: The file name specified for the data file copy operation.

description: archived log thread %s sequence %s already included
cause: The indicated archived log has already been specified for inclusion in this restore conversation. A restore conversation may process only one copy of any archived log.
action: No action required - the conversation is still active, and more files can be specified.

description: Backup piece file name for Oracle Recovery Manager (RMAN) must be specified.
cause: Attempted to create an RMAN backup without specifying the name of the backup piece(s) to be created.
action: Supply a file name using the RMAN FORMAT option and retry.

description: Datafile file# %s is not current enough to apply the incremental backup
cause: The datafile checkpoint is earlier than the incremental backup start SCN. Applying this backup may lead to data loss for changes made in that gap.
action: Provide a backup set that can be applied and retry the operation.

description: Datafile file# %s is more recent than the incremental backup
cause: The target file's checkpoint is greater than or equal to that of the incremental backup. This backup cannot advance the checkpoint and will not be applied.
action: Provide a backup set that can be applied and retry the operation.

description: Datafile checkpoint SCN is %s at time %s
cause: The checkpoint is too old to take an incremental backup of the data file. If you attempted a restore operation, the checkpoint is too old for an incremental backup to be applied on the data file.
action: See accompanying error messages.

description: Backup checkpoint SCN for file# %s is %s at time %s
cause: This message identifies the checkpoint of a datafile in an incremental backup set that could not be applied.
action: See the other error messages accompanying this error message.

description: Backup incremental SCN is %s
cause: This message identifies the starting SCN of an incremental that cannot be applied.
action: See the other error messages accompanying this error message.

description: For data file %s, incremental-start SCN is too recent.
cause: The incremental-start SCN which was specified when starting an incremental backup of a data file is greater (more recent) than the data file's checkpoint SCN, which could cause some blocks to be missed by the backup.
action: Specify a smaller (less recent) incremental-start SCN.

description: datafile %s: incremental-start SCN is prior to RESETLOGS SCN %s
cause: The incremental-start SCN which was specified when starting an incremental datafile backup is less than the RESETLOGS SCN.
action: Specify a larger incremental-start SCN.

description: For data file %s, incremental-start SCN is prior to creation SCN %s.
cause: The incremental-start SCN, which was specified when starting an incremental backup of a data file, is less than the data file's creation SCN.
action: Specify a larger incremental-start SCN.

description: cannot change size of data file %s from %s to %s
cause: Restore required adjustment to the size of the file as indicated, but the file size adjustment failed.
action: Examine the other messages that indicate the cause of the failure.
params: 1) data_file: The target data file to be restored. 2) old_size: The size of the data file before being resized. 3) new_size: The size of the data file after being resized.

description: non-zero LEVEL cannot be specified when INCREMENTAL is FALSE
cause: BACKUPSETDATAFILE was called with a non-zero backup_level and a FALSE incremental indication.
action: Either set incremental to TRUE or change backup_level to zero.

description: datafile %s: incremental-start SCN equals checkpoint SCN
cause: The incremental-start SCN which was specified when starting an incremental datafile backup is equal to the datafile's checkpoint SCN. Since an incremental backup can only be applied to a datafile whose checkpoint SCN is between the backup set incremental-start SCN (inclusive) and the backup set checkpoint SCN (exclusive), there is no datafile that this backup set could ever be applied to.
action: This message might be encountered while taking an incremental backup with Recovery Manager. Recovery Manager should intercept all usual cases of this error and simply ignore the incremental backup of this data file. If you do encounter this error, report it to Oracle Support. Specify a smaller incremental-start SCN and retry your command.

description: offline-range record RECID %s STAMP %s not found in file %s
cause: APPLYOFFLINERANGE was called with a RECID/STAMP which was not found in the indicated control file. This probably means that the specified control file is no longer the same control file that Recovery Manager thinks it is.
action: Specify the RECID/STAMP of a record that exists in the control file copy.

description: Offline-range record RECID %s STAMP %s in file %s has SCN %s
cause: This messages identifies the offline-clean SCN from the indicated offline-range record in the indicated file.
action: See other error message.

description: cannot apply offline-range record to datafile %s: SCN mismatch
cause: APPLYOFFLINERANGE cannot apply an offline-range record to a target datafile unless the datafile's checkpoint SCN exactly matches the offline-clean SCN in the specified offline-range record.
action: Specify an offline-range record whose offline-clean SCN matches the target datafile's checkpoint.

description: cannot apply offline-range record to datafile %s: file is fuzzy
cause: The target datafile for an APPLYOFFLINERANGE call is fuzzy.
action: Specify a target datafile that is closed cleanly.

description: cannot switch to older file incarnation
cause: SWITCHTOCOPY was called with a data file copy for a data file that was dropped prior to the time that this control file was backed up.
action: Restore and mount an earlier control file. It is acceptable to use a control file that was backed up prior to the creation of the specified data file.

description: must use backup control file to switch file incarnations
cause: This SWITCHTOCOPY operation attempted to switch incarnations of a data file, but the currently mounted control file was not a backup control file.
action: Restore and mount a backup control file.

description: cannot switch to incarnation with different RESETLOGS data
cause: This SWITCHTOCOPY operation attempted to switch to a data file that came from a different RESETLOGS version of the database.
action: Either restore a backup control file that was taken from the same database version as the target data file copy, or switch to a different data file copy.

description: cannot backup, copy, or delete online log %s
cause: The indicated log file is an active log. You can only backup, copy, or delete archived logs.
action: The indicated log file cannot be processed - select another file.

description: cannot inspect current datafile %s
cause: The file being inspected is already part of the currently mounted database.
action: None - the file is already part of the database.

description: cannot inspect %s - file is from different RESETLOGS
cause: The RESETLOGS data in the log file being inspected does not match that in the currently mounted control file.
action: The indicated file cannot be processed - inspect another file.

description: incremental restore would advance file %s past RESETLOGS
cause: This incremental backup cannot be applied to the specified datafile, because the datafile is from an earlier incarnation of the database, and its checkpoint would be advanced too far to be recoverable in the current incarnation of the database.
action: This incremental cannot be applied to this datafile. If you wish to recover the file to the RESETLOGS SCN so that the database can be opened with the RESETLOGS option, then you must use redo-log recovery, not incremental restore, to continue recovering this file.

description: some files in the backup set could not be verified
cause: A restore conversation was made to verify all the files in a backup set, and the files which were printed in messages 19661 or 19662 could not be verified because corrupt blocks for those files were found in the backup set.
action: Unless the damage to the backup set can be repaired, the indicated files cannot be restored from this backup set.

description: datafile %s could not be verified due to corrupt blocks
cause: Some data blocks for the indicated datafile were corrupt in the backup set.
action: Unless the damage to the backup set can be repaired, the indicated datafile cannot be restored from this backup set. Examine the alert log and trace files for more information.

description: archived log thread %s sequence %s could not be verified
cause: Some data blocks for the indicated archived log were corrupt in the backup set.
action: Unless the damage to the backup set can be repaired, the indicated archived log cannot be restored from this backup set.

description: cannot apply current offline range to datafile %s
cause: An attempt was made to apply the current offline range to the specified datafile, but the datafile is either not current enough or is not at the correct SCN to apply the offline range.
action: The datafile remains unchanged.

description: file type: %s, file name: %s
cause: This message is issued to identify the file which is the subject of an error.
action: None - this is an informational message. There should be other Oracle messages explaining the cause of the error.

description: size %s in file header does not match actual file size of %s
cause: The size of the file as indicated in the file header does not match the true size of the file. The two differing sizes are shown in units of logical blocks.
action: This file is not usable - it has most likely been truncated.

description: cannot do incremental restore of the control file
cause: The control file was included in an incremental restore conversation
action: If you wish to restore the control file, you must do a full restore of the control file

description: cannot do incremental restore of data file %s
cause: The backup of the data file was a full backup.
action: To restore the data file, do a full restore of the data file.
params: 1) data_file: The target data file being restored.

description: cannot do full restore of data file %s
cause: The data file backup was incremental.
action: To restore the data file, do an incremental restore of the data file.
params: 1) data_file: The data file being restored.

description: proxy copy functions cannot be run on DISK channel
cause: A proxy copy procedure was called, but the device which is allocated to the current session has type DISK.
action: Allocate a non-DISK channel and retry the operation. Note that proxy copy requires a 3rd-party media management software product that supports the this backup/restore feature.

description: file %s already being restored
cause: A proxy restore function has already named this file as a restore destination.
action: Use a different file name. If this message occurs during a Recovery Manager job, then this is an internal error in the Recovery Manager. Contact Oracle Support.
params: 1) data_file: The target data file being restored.

description: media management software returned invalid proxy handle
cause: During a proxy backup or restore, the media management software returned an invalid file handle.
action: This is an internal error in the media management software which is linked with Oracle to provide backup/restore services. Contact the media management software vendor.

description: media management software returned invalid file status
cause: During a proxy backup or restore, the media management software returned an invalid file status.
action: This is an internal error in the media management software which is linked with Oracle to provide backup/restore services. Contact the media management software vendor.

description: error during proxy copy of file %s
cause: During a proxy backup or restore, an error occurred while copying this file, but other files may have been copied successfully.
action: There should be other errors on the error stack that explains why the file could not be successfully copied.
params: 1) data_file: The target data file to proxy copy.

description: File %s is already being backed up with a proxy copy.
cause: The Recovery Manager (RMAN) attempted to back up the specified file with a proxy copy, but the file was already being backed up by another RMAN job.
action: Wait until the other RMAN backup of this file is complete, and then retry the backup.
params: 1) data_file: The specified data file to be backed up.

description: file %s was modified during proxy copy
cause: A proxy backup of the specified file failed because the file was brought on-line or otherwise modified while the proxy backup was in progress. This file was off-line or read-only when the backup began, so the file was not put into hot-backup mode, therefore no modifications are permitted while the backup is in progress.
action: Take another backup of this file.

description: one or more files failed during proxy backup or restore
cause: During a proxy backup or restore, errors were encountered while processing some files. The files for which no error messages are shown were processed successfully.
action: Examine the messages regarding the specific files to determine the cause of the problems.

description: Recovery Manager (RMAN) configuration name exceeds the maximum length of %s.
cause: The configuration name string exceeded the maximum length.
action: Supply a valid configuration name and retry the function.
params: 1) config_max_len: The maximum length of an RMAN configuration parameter.

description: RMAN configuration value exceeds maximum length of %s
cause: The configuration value string exceeds maximum length.
action: Supply a correct configuration value and retry the operation.

description: RMAN configuration number %s is outside valid range of 1 through %s
cause: An invalid RMAN Configuration number was specified.
action: Specify a correct datafile number and retry the operation.

description: some blocks not recovered. See trace file for details
cause: Some blocks are not recovered during block media recovery.
action: See trace files for details of the problem.

description: block media recovery on control file not possible
cause: file number 0 specified in block media recovery
action: check file number

description: file %s not in block media recovery context
cause: Internal error
action: NA

description: real and backup block size of file %s are unequal
cause: block size changed between backup & real file
action: use right backup

description: block media recovery failed because database is suspended
cause: Database is suspended, probably by an ALTER SYSTEM SUSPEND statement
action: Execute ALTER SYSTEM RESUME then retry block media recovery

description: SPFILE could not be verified
cause: Some data blocks for the SPFILE were corrupt in the backup set.
action: Unless the damage to the backup set can be repaired, the SPFILE cannot be restored from this backup set.

description: SPFILE not restored due to %s
cause: The indicated file could not be restored, because some of its data blocks were not found in the backup piece.
action: Unless the damage to the backup set can be repaired, the SPFILE cannot be restored from this backup set.

description: SPFILE not found in backup set
cause: The server parameter file (SPFILE) could not be restored because it was not in this backup set.
action: This message is issued when the directory from the first backup piece is read and one or more files named for restoration are not found in the piece. Supply the first backup piece of a backup set that contains the requested file.

description: control file AUTOBACKUP format(%s) for %s does not have %F
cause: control file AUTOBACKUP format must contain %F for the device.
action: Change control file format using RMAN command CONFIGURE CONTROLFILE BACKUP FORMAT FOR DEVICE TYPE <type> TO <format>.

description: cannot have more than one %F in control file AUTOBACKUP format(%0!s) for %1!s
cause: control file AUTOBACKUP format contains more than one %F for the device.
action: Change control file format using RMAN command CONFIGURE CONTROLFILE BACKUP FORMAT FOR DEVICE TYPE <type> TO <format>.

description: backup piece release %s incompatible with Oracle release %s
cause: The backup piece was created by incompatible software.
action: Either restart with a compatible software release or create another backup using the current release.

description: %s is from different database: id=%s, name=%s
cause: The database name or database ID in the backup piece header did not match the one in the control file.
action: Supply the correct backup piece belonging to this database.
params: 1) backup_piece: The backup piece name being processed. 2) db_id: The database ID of the backup piece. 3) db_name: The database name of the backup piece.

description: missing creation stamp on piece %s
cause: The backup piece doesn't have information about creation stamp.
action: Supply another backup piece which is created by oracle 9i or later version.

description: backup piece %s already included
cause: This backup piece was already specified for inclusion in the restore conversation. A restore conversation may process a single instance only of a backup piece.
action: Remove the specified duplicate backup piece in the restore steps and restart the conversation.

description: Some changed blocks were not found in the change tracking file.
cause: A backup or copy found that some changed blocks were not recorded in the change tracking file. The details of the affected files and blocks are in an Oracle trace file.
action: This indicates that there is a problem with the change tracking feature. Disable change tracking and restart the backup.

description: The fixed table X$KRBMSFT has not been populated.
cause: This is an internal error. The fixed table X$KRBMAFT was not populated using the function DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE.SEARCHFILES.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support.

description: control file not found in backup set
cause: The control file could not be restored because it is not in this backup set.
action: This message is issued when the directory from the first backup piece is read and one or more files named for restoration were not found in the piece. You must supply the first backup piece of a backup set that contains the requested file.

description: standby control file not found in backup set
cause: The standby control file could not be restored because it is not in this backup set.
action: This message is issued when the directory from the first backup piece is read and one or more files named for restoration were not found in the piece. You must supply the first backup piece of a backup set that contains the requested file.

description: %s is from different database: id=%s, db_name=%s
cause: Catalog failed because the database id in file header does not match the one in control file.
action: Supply the correct file belonging to this database.

description: cannot make copies with compression enabled
cause: Image copies cannot be compressed.
action: If the function DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE.BACKUPPIECECREATE is called outside Recovery Manager (RMAN), then incompatible values are being passed for the parameters DOCOMPRESS and IMAGCP. If this message occurs during an RMAN job, then this is an internal error in RMAN, and you should contact Oracle support.

description: device type exceeds maximum length of %s
cause: The device type specified was invalid.
action: Specify the correct device type and retry the allocation.

description: The device name exceeds the maximum length of %s.
cause: The device name specified was invalid.
action: Supply a valid device name and retry the allocation.

description: device parameter exceeds maximum length of %s
cause: The device parameter exceeded the platform-specific length limit.
action: Correct the device parameter and retry the operation.

description: device command string exceeds maximum length of %s
cause: The device command string exceeded the maximum length.
action: Correct the command and retry the operation.

description: file name exceeds maximum length of %s
cause: The specified file name, which was a parameter to a copy, backup, or restore operation, exceeded the maximum file name length for this operating system.
action: Retry the operation with a shorter file name.

description: Tag value exceeds maximum length of %s characters.
cause: During a backup or copy operation, a tag value was used that is too long to fit in the file header.
action: Supply a shorter tag and retry.

description: invalid SCN
cause: The input SCN is either not a positive integer or too large.
action: Check the input SCN and make sure it is a valid SCN.

description: invalid record block number - %s
cause: The specified record block number was either negative or too large.
action: Check the record block number and ensure it is a valid number.

description: Log destination exceeds maximum length of %s characters.
cause: When starting a restore conversation, the user specified a log restore destination longer than the port-specific maximum length.
action: Supply a shorter destination and retry.

description: numeric parameter must be non-negative integer
cause: A numeric parameter to an DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE procedure is negative or contains a fractional portion.
action: Supply a valid numeric parameter.

description: Character set %s is unsupported.
cause: When the target database is not mounted, RMAN sets the character set of the target database to the value specified in the user's environment.
action: Specify a valid character set in the environment. This is usually done via the NLS_LANG environment variable.

description: cannot use RENORMALIZEALLFILENAMES while database is open
cause: An attempt was made to re-normalize all the file names in the control file while the database is open.
action: Close the database before using the RENORMALIZEALLFILENAMES procedure.

description: table name exceeds maximum length of %s
cause: The table name string exceeds maximum length.
action: Retry the operation with a shorter table name.

description: invalid copy number: %s
cause: The copy number is not in a valid range or the maximum limit has been reached.
action: Report the error to Oracle Support.

description: length for generated name longer than %s
cause: The specified format exceeded the maximum length for the piece name.
action: Change the format to create shorter piece names.
params: 1) max_length: The maximum length for a piece name.

description: invalid format %s for generated name
cause: A restricted format or undefined format was used incorrectly.
action: Change the format specified in the additional information by removing the restricted format.

description: error processing format %s to generate name for backup
cause: There were errors while processing the format to generate name for backup.
action: Change the format.

description: for non-OMF search the pattern must be specified
cause: The procedure DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE.SEARCHFILES was called with an empty pattern while the parameter OMF was set to FALSE.
action: Either specify the pattern or set the parameter OMF to TRUE.

description: length for command ID longer than %s
cause: The specified command ID exceeded the maximum length for the command ID.
action: Supply a shorter command ID and retry the operation.

description: length for operation name longer than %s
cause: The specified operation name exceeds the maximum length for operation name.
action: Supply a shorter operation name and retry the operation.

description: Error occurred when converting an OCI number into an SCN
cause: This is most likely caused by an invalid SCN number that came from an external file, such as an export file.
action: See other errors on the error stack to look for the source of the problem.

description: Cannot find data file with absolute file number %s in tablespace %s
cause: One of the data files that should have been in the pluggable set was not found. Alternatively, one of the data files in the pluggable set had already been plugged in from a previous import job and so was excluded from the pluggable set.
action: Ensure that all of the data files are specified using the import command-line option or parameter files. Also, ensure that none of the data files have already been plugged into the database.

description: datafile %s is an incorrect version
cause: The datafile is an incorrect version. It contains either less or more changes then the desired version.
action: Make sure the right datafiles are transported. Make sure the datafile is copied while its tablespace is read only.

description: cannot re-create plugged in data file %s
cause: The data file was plugged in read only or plugged in as part of pluggable database creation or pluggable database plug-in. It cannot be re-created.
action: Use the ALTER DATABASE RENAME FILE statement instead.

description: snapshot too old: snapshot time is before file %s plug-in time
cause: The snapshot SCN is before the SCN at which the referred datafile is plugged into the database.
action: retry the query.

description: can not acquire plug-in enqueue
cause: There maybe another "ALTER DATABASE RESET COMPATIBILITY" command issued concurrently, preventing this process from acquiring the plug-in enqueue.
action: retry the operation.

description: cannot plug data [%s] at level %s into database running at compatibility level %s
cause: Some of the data in the pluggable set requires a compatibility level higher than what is currently allowed by the database. The string in square bracket is the name of the compatibility type associated with the data.
action: Raise the "compatible" init.ora parameter and retry the operation.

description: cannot plug data [%s] at level %s into database running Oracle %s
cause: Some of the data in the pluggable set requires a compatibility level higher than the release level of the Oracle executable. The string in square bracket is the name of the compatibility type associated with the data.
action: Upgrade Oracle and retry the operation.

description: data object number conflict between table %s and partition %s in table %s
cause: The non-partitioned table has the same data object number as one of the partitions in the partitioned table. One can not exchange the table with the partition in this case.
action: Use "alter table move partition" command to move the offending partition, so that the partition will get a new data object number. Retry the operation then.

description: File %s is not the initial version of the plugged in datafile
cause: The file is not the initial version of the plugged in datafile.
action: Use the correct initial version of the plugged in datafile.

description: can not convert offline plugged-in datafile %s
cause: As part of making a tablespace read-write, we need to convert datafiles that are plugged in read-only. The file must be online.
action: Online the datafile and retry the operation.

description: cannot apply change to unverified plugged in data file %s
cause: Recovery was not able to verify the specified data file according to information in the control file. Before encountering the change vector for this file, recovery did not find the file conversion redo required to verify this file. This may happen due to a corrupted or incorrect control file used for media recovery.
action: Use the correct control file and continue recovery.

description: incorrect number of datafiles for tablespace %s
cause: The number of datafiles in the export file for the referred tablespace is not the same as expected. This is most likely caused by a user editing the export file.
action: Use the correct export file and retry the operation.

description: COMPATIBLE parameter needs to be %s or greater
cause: The COMPATIBLE initialization parameter is not high enough to allow the operation. Allowing the command would make the database incompatible with the release specified by the current COMPATIBLE parameter.
action: Shutdown and startup with a higher compatibility setting.

description: wrong creation SCN - control file expects converted plugged-in datafile
cause: When a tablespace is plugged into a database, the tablespace is initially read-only. Oracle converts the header of the plugged-in datafiles (assign them a new creation SCN) when the tablespace is first made read-write. This error occurs when the creation SCN in the file header is different from the creation SCN in the control file, possibly because this is the initial version of plugged-in datafile.
action: Either restore the converted datafile or continue recovering the datafile.

description: wrong creation SCN - control file expects initial plugged-in datafile
cause: When a tablespace is plugged into a database, the tablespace is initially read-only. Oracle converts the header of the plugged-in datafiles (assign them a new creation SCN) when the tablespace is first made read-write. This error occurs when the creation SCN in the file header is different from the creation SCN in the control file, possibly because this is the converted datafile.
action: Either restore the initial version of the plugged-in datafile, or continue database recovery, which will recover the control file.

description: can not plug a tablespace into a database using a different national character set
cause: Oracle does not support plugging a tablespace into a database using a different national character set.
action: Use import/export or unload/load to move data instead.

description: simulate read-only database connection to execute sql query
cause: Set on RMAN foreground connections when archiver was hung.
action: Turn off plsql/sql statistics collection, obtaining the temp segment for sorting and grabbing the sequence number from disk.

description: cannot find language information for character set: '%s'
cause: The compatibility check failed because a character set name that was provided is not valid.
action: Correct the character set name and retry.

description: operation failed, retry is possible and connection is reusable
cause: A backup, restore, or image copy operation is failing with a retrial error. The failed operation can be re-tried on the same connection.
action: This message is used by the Recovery Manager to decide whether or not to retry the operation on the same connection.

description: text is longer than %s
cause: The specified text exceeds the maximum length for text.
action: Supply a shorter text and retry the operation.

description: %s exceeds maximum allowable length of %s for parameter '%s'
cause: The specified string exceeded the maximum allowable length for the parameter.
action: Specify a shorter string for the parameter and retry the operation.

description: The specified control file is not a backup control file.
cause: An attempt was made to mark a control file as unmountable. Only a backup control file can be marked as unmountable during Oracle Recovery Manager (Oracle RMAN) duplicate command processing. This control file is not a backup control file.
action: Do not use this call for a control file that is not a backup control file.

description: could not unmount volume %s:%s
cause: The specified server and volume combination was not found and could not be unmounted.
action: Specify the server and volume name correctly to complete the operation successfully.

description: Volume %s:%s is currently in use and cannot be unmounted.
cause: The specified volume could not be unmounted because it was in use and had open files.
action: Retry the unmount after all open files in the volume have been closed.

description: invalid call to DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE package, reason: %s.
cause: The call to the DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE package was invalid. The DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE API was either called with invalid arguments or called without required parameters set.
action: Use the RMAN utility for backup and restore operations. Do not use DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE package APIs directly.

description: Privileged Procedure call from user without SYSBACKUP role
cause: The call to a privileged DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE procedure was made by an user without SYSBACKUP or SYSDBA privileges.
action: Use the RMAN utility for backup and restore operations. Do not use DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE APIs directly.

description: RMAN remote procedure call from user without SYSBACKUP role
cause: A remote procedure call (RPC) to a Recovery Manager (RMAN) RPC operation was done by a remote user without SYSBACKUP or SYSDBA privilege.
action: Use the RMAN utility for backup and restore operations. Do not use DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE APIs directly.

description: Backup failure due to NULL checkpoint time in data file records.
cause: NULL is populating the data file checkpoint time which is invalid.
action: Validate the data file and ensure that NULL checkpoint time does not get populated.

description: Flashback failed because file# %s metadata is unknown to current control file
cause: The file creation system change number (SCN) is less than the restore point SCN and there is no record of the file on the current control file, causing flashback to the restore point to fail.
action: If flashing back to the restore point is still required, then the database should switch to an incarnation that has the complete information required for flashing back to the restore point.

description: change tracking file: '%s'
cause: This message reports the name of a file involved in other messages.
action: See associated error messages for a description of the problem.

description: could not create the change tracking file
cause: It was not possible to create the change tracking file.
action: Check that there is sufficient disk space and no conflicts in file names and try to enable block change tracking again.

description: block change tracking is already enabled
cause: The ALTER DATABASE ENABLE BLOCK CHANGE TRACKING command was issued, but block change tracking is already turned on for this database.
action: None, this is an informative message only.

description: error writing to change tracking file
cause: An I/O error occurred while writing to the change tracking file.
action: There will be other messages on the error stack that show details of the problem.

description: error reading from change tracking file
cause: An I/O error occurred while reading from the change tracking file.
action: There will be other messages on the error stack that show details of the problem.

description: could not open change tracking file
cause: The change tracking file could not be opened.
action: There will be other messages on the error stack that show details of the problem.

description: corrupt block number %s found in change tracking file
cause: The specified block number was corrupt in the change tracking file.
action: There will be other messages on the error stack that show details of the problem. There will also be a trace file that contains a complete dump of the corrupt block.
params: 1) block_number: The block number of the change tracking file.

description: could not resize change tracking file to %s blocks
cause: An error occurred while trying to change the size of the change tracking file.
action: There will be other messages on the error stack that show details of the problem.

description: failed to enable/disable block change tracking: out of SGA memory
cause: out of SGA memory
action: Increase SGA and restart the instance.

description: block change tracking is not enabled
cause: A command was entered that requires block change tracking to be enabled, but block change tracking is not enabled.
action: None, this is an informative message only.

description: error starting change tracking
cause: Change tracking was enabled, but a problem was encountered while enabling the change tracking subsystem in this instance. The alert log and the trace file from the Change Tracking Writer (CTWR) process contains more information about the error.
action: Examine the trace and alert files. Correct the error if possible, otherwise disable change tracking and contact Oracle Support.

description: block size %s is not valid for change tracking file
cause: While opening the specified change tracking file, it was found that the file header did not contain a valid logical block size. This probably means that the file is corrupt.
action: If the file can be repaired, do so, otherwise disable and re-enable change tracking to re-initialize the file.

description: invalid file type %s
cause: An invalid file type was found in the change tracking file. Some other file was put in place of the change tracking file or the file was corrupt.
action: Disable and then re-enable change tracking.
params: 1) file_type: The file type found while reading the change tracking file.

description: compatibility version %s is higher than maximum allowed: %s
cause: The compatibility version in the change tracking file is greater than what can be used by the current release of Oracle. This can happen when you upgrade, use change tracking with a new release, then downgrade.
action: Disable then re-enable change tracking.

description: database id %s does not match database id %s in control file
cause: The change tracking file is not the correct one for this database. This can happen when the database ID for this database has been changed.
action: Disable then re-enable change tracking.

description: mount ID %s does not match mount ID %s in control file
cause: The change tracking file did not match the one that was present when this instance was opened. In Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC), this error is most likely caused by a change tracking file that cannot be consistently updated by all instances.
action: In Oracle RAC, ensure that the name specified for the change tracking file represents the same disk location for all nodes in the cluster. Disable and then re-enable change tracking.
params: 1) mount_id1: The mount ID found in the change tracking file. 2) mount_id2: The mount ID found in the control file.

description: missing CHANGE keyword
cause: Syntax error.
action: Use the correct syntax: ENABLE/DISABLE BLOCK CHANGE TRACKING

description: missing TRACKING keyword
cause: Syntax error.
action: Use the correct syntax: ENABLE/DISABLE BLOCK CHANGE TRACKING

description: USING clause only valid with ENABLE CHANGE TRACKING
cause: The USING clause was specified with DISABLE CHANGE TRACKING
action: Correct the statement.

description: missing FILE keyword
cause: Syntax error.
action: Use the correct syntax: ENABLE/DISABLE BLOCK CHANGE TRACKING

description: invalid change tracking file name
cause: The USING clause was specified with ALTER DATABASE ENABLE BLOCK CHANGE TRACKING, but no file name was given.
action: Specify the change tracking file name, or omit the USING clause to allow Oracle to create a default name for the change tracking file.

description: cannot rename change tracking file while database is open
cause: The ALTER DATABASE RENAME FILE command was used to rename the change tracking file, and the database is open by one or more instances. The database must be mounted, and not open, to rename the change tracking file.
action: Close the database and reissue the command.

description: change tracking file name exceeds limit of %s characters
cause: The name specified for the change tracking file was too long.
action: Specify a shorter change tracking file name.
params: 1) filename_length: The character limit of the file name of the change tracking file.

description: must specify change tracking file name
cause: No file name was specified with the ALTER DATABASE ENABLE CHANGE TRACKING command, and the DB_CREATE_FILE_DEST parameter was not set.
action: Either specify a file name, or set the DB_CREATE_FILE_DEST parameter.

description: PROXY restore to Oracle ASM disk group or Exascale vault "%s" is not supported.
cause: An attempt is being made to proxy restore a file to Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) disk group or Exascale vault using a Recovery Manager (RMAN) command. This is not supported.
action: Use a different file name and reissue the RMAN command.
params: 1) dg_name: The Oracle ASM disk group or Exascale vault specified in the proxy restore command.

description: Oracle ASM or Exascale file %s cannot be proxy backed up.
cause: An attempt is being made to proxy backup an Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) or Exascale file. This is not supported.
action: Use a different file name and reissue the Recovery Manager (RMAN) command.
params: 1) asm_file: The specified Oracle ASM or Exascale file to backup with RMAN.

description: event to be in hot backup mode for given seconds
cause: N/A
action: Set to test shutdown during proxy backup

description: could not obtain resilvering status for change tracking file
cause: An error occurred while obtaining the mirror resilvering status of the change tracking file.
action: Refer to other error messages shown for additional details of the problem.

description: Active Data Guard option not enabled
cause: Change tracking at a standby database required the Active Data Guard option.
action: Enable the Active Data Guard option.

description: The PROXY option is not supported on sparse file %s.
cause: The PROXY option was used with a sparse file. This is not supported.
action: Do not use the PROXY option with sparse files.
params: 1) sparse_file: The sparse file to backup.

description: event to wait for specified seconds before checkpointing data files in a backup session
cause: N/A
action: Set to test data file deletion during a backup.

description: event to wait for specified seconds before checkpointing data files in a backup session
cause: None, undocumented
action: Set this event to test data file deletion during a backup operation.

description: error enabling change tracking due to ORA-4031
cause: The change tracking writer could not get requested memory for buffer allocation.
action: Try again, if error recurs, increase the large pool size.

description: event to wait for a minute before processing data files in a backup session
cause: None, undocumented
action: Set this event to test pluggable database (PDB) deletion or recreation during a backup.

description: test event to simulate change tracking file corruption during RMAN backup
cause: None, undocumented.
action: Set this event to a data file number to simulate change tracking file corruption during backup.

description: block change tracking is in transition state
cause: The ALTER DATABASE ENABLE BLOCK CHANGE TRACKING statement was issued, but block change tracking was in transition state.
action: Retry the operation after some time. If the error persists, contact Oracle Support.

description: Data file %s cannot be used in this backup conversation anymore: %s
cause: During the backup operation, state of the data file was altered.
action: This is an informational message. No action is required.
params: 1) file_name: The name of the data file being processed. 2) reason: values are 'file is deleted', 'file is recreated', 'file is offlined', 'block 1 read has failed', and 'file is shrinked'

description: Unable to initialize Oracle Managed Destination
cause: The name given for an Oracle managed files destination cannot be initialized.
action: Check previous error messages for the reason Oracle was unable to initialize destination. Take corrective action, if possible, and retry the command or use a different name for destination.

description: initialization parameter DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST is not set
cause: An attempt was made to create a file in DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST when DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST was not set. There are number of possible causes of this error, including: 1) A LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_n parameter was specified using a LOCATION attribute whose value was DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST and an archived log file creation was attempted. 2) STANDBY_ARCHIVE_DEST parameter was specified using a LOCATION attribute whose value was DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST and an archived log file creation was attempted.
action: Specify a valid destination for DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST in initialization parameter file or with the ALTER SYSTEM SET command.

description: cannot use DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST without DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE
cause: There are two possible cause for this error: 1) The DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST parameter was in use when no DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE parameter was encountered while fetching initialization parameter. 2) An attempt was made to set DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST with the ALTER SYSTEM command when no DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE was in use.
action: Correct the dependency parameter definitions and retry the command.

description: Parameter DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE is out of range (1 - %s)
cause: Parameter DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE specified was not valid.
action: Specify a valid number within the range.

description: cannot reclaim %s bytes disk space from %s bytes limit
cause: Disk space of specified bytes from the DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST location for DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE limit could not be reclaimed.
action: Do one or more of the following: 1) Take more frequent RMAN backups of the recovery area. 2) Consider changing the RMAN retention policy. 3) Consider changing the RMAN archived log deletion policy. 4) Add disk space and increase DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE. 5) Delete files from recovery area using RMAN.

description: RECID %s of %s was deleted to reclaim disk space.
cause: The file described by the record in the control file was deleted in order to reclaim disk space from the recovery area for other operations or deleted by another Recovery Manager (RMAN) session.
action: Wait and try again.
params: 1) record_id: The record ID of the deleted object. 2) record_type: The record type of the deleted object.

description: Cannot make a duplex backup to the recovery area.
cause: Duplex backup to the recovery area is not supported.
action: Remove duplex option and retry.

description: duplex number %s is out of range: expected between 0 and %s
cause: The duplex number specified is outside of the expected range.
action: Specify a duplex number that is within the range and try again.

description: recovery destination parameter mismatch
cause: The value of parameters DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST and DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE must be same in all instances. instance. All databases must have same recovery destination parameters.
action: Check DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST and DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE values in all instances.

description: limit exceeded for recovery files
cause: The limit for recovery files specified by the DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE parameter was exceeded.
action: There are five possible solutions: 1. Take frequent backup of recovery area using RMAN. 2. Consider changing RMAN retention policy. 3. Consider changing RMAN archived log deletion policy. 4. Add disk space and increase DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE. 5. Delete files from recovery area using RMAN.
remediation: 1) Same condition as ORA-00257 -- the recovery area has hit db_recovery_file_dest_size. `SELECT * FROM v$recovery_file_dest;` 2) `SELECT file_type, percent_space_used, percent_space_reclaimable FROM v$flash_recovery_area_usage;` -- a high reclaimable percentage means a backup will free it; a low one means the limit is genuinely too small. 3) Back up and delete archivelogs, or raise db_recovery_file_dest_size. See ORA-00257 for the full sequence. 4) Check for orphaned flashback logs and obsolete backups: `RMAN> DELETE OBSOLETE;` and review the retention policy with `RMAN> SHOW RETENTION POLICY;`

description: Cannot create temporary control file %s in DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST
cause: An attempt was made to create a control file for a temporary purpose in DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST.
action: Retry the operation with a new file name.

description: cannot have files in DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST with keep attributes
cause: An attempt was made to 1) Create a backup piece or image copy in the recovery area with KEEP option. 2) Update the KEEP attributes of an existing backup piece or image copy in the recovery area.
action: Reissue RMAN command without KEEP options.

description: cannot use %s without DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST
cause: There are three possible cause for this error: 1) The indicated parameter was in use when no DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST parameter was encountered while fetching the initialization parameter. 2) An attempt was made to set indicated the parameter with the ALTER SYSTEM command when no DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST was in use. 3) An attempt was made to clear DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST with the ALTER SYSTEM command when the indicated parameter was in use.
action: Eliminate any incompatible parameter definitions.

description: cannot have unavailable file %s in DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST
cause: An attempt was made to change a backup piece or image copy in the recovery area to UNAVAILABLE.
action: Correct and resubmit the Recovery Manager (RMAN) command.
params: 1) file_name: The file name to mark unavailable.

description: WARNING: %s of %s bytes is %s%% used, and has %s remaining bytes available
cause: The DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST parameter is running out of disk space.
action: Perform one of the following: - Add disk space and increase the DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE parameter. - Back up the files to a tertiary device using Oracle Recovery Manager (Oracle RMAN). - Consider changing the RMAN retention policy. - Consider changing the RMAN archived log deletion policy. - Delete the files from recovery area using RMAN.
remediation: 1) This is a warning, not yet an outage -- act before it becomes ORA-00257. `SELECT name, space_limit/1024/1024/1024 limit_gb, space_used/1024/1024/1024 used_gb FROM v$recovery_file_dest;` 2) `SELECT file_type, percent_space_used, percent_space_reclaimable FROM v$flash_recovery_area_usage;` 3) Run the archivelog backup ahead of schedule, or raise db_recovery_file_dest_size. 4) If this recurs on a cycle, the FRA is sized below one backup interval's worth of redo -- size it from peak redo rate: `SELECT TRUNC(completion_time) day, SUM(blocks*block_size)/1024/1024/1024 gb FROM v$archived_log GROUP BY TRUNC(completion_time) ORDER BY 1 DESC FETCH FIRST 14 ROWS ONLY;`

description: WARNING: Files may exist in %s that are not known to database.
cause: One of the following events caused this: 1. A database crash happened during file creation. 2. A backup control file was restored. 3. The control file was re-created. 4. DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST has previously been enabled and then disabled.
action: Use RMAN command CATALOG RECOVERY AREA to re-catalog such files. If the file header is corrupt, then delete those files using an operating system utility.

description: database must be in NOARCHIVELOG mode to disable logging
cause: Logging was disabled when ARCHIVELOG mode was used.
action: Execute ALTER DATABASE NOARCHIVELOG in mount state.

description: an intentionally corrupt log file was found
cause: A log file that was intentionally corrupt for testing or benchmarking purposes was found and failed the operation.
action: Remove such log files and retry or use the NOARCHIVELOG option if possible.

description: mmon recovery area usage monitoring interval
cause: Set on all instances to change recovery area usage monitoring interval.
action: level 1 - once every 15 minutes. level 2 - once every 30 minutes. ... level n - once every n * 15 minutes.

description: soft limit recovery area space pressure percentage
cause: Set on all instances to alter recovery area space pressure trigger percentage.
action: level 1 to 100 indicates the percentage when the space pressure has to be triggered.

description: amount of space in MB to be reclaimed on archiver I/O error
cause: none, undocumented
action: Set this event on all instances to alter reclamation of recovery area space on archiver I/O error. The level of this event is the amount in MB.

description: recovery area test event level %s
cause: Event set to test various recovery area error conditions.
action: None.

description: Continue backup in case of dropped pluggable database for test event level %s.
cause: NA
action: This event is set to test backup continuation in case of a dropped pluggable database. The level of this event is the number of seconds to sleep after backup process is in the krbbbdr routine.

description: Restoring preplugin files to a recovery area is not supported.
cause: An attempt to resore a preplugin file in a recovery area failed. This is not supported.
action: Use the SET ARCHVIELOG DESTINATION RMAN command to specify an archivelog destination and retry the RESTORE or RECOVER command.

description: suspend a backup or rekey process for some time
cause: NA
action: This event is set to test backup continuation in case of a moved or rekeyed data file. The level of this event is the number of seconds to sleep.

description: Skip block #1 for all of the files in the backup test event
cause: N/A
action: Test event used to skip block #1 for all of the files in a backup to test the duplicate blocks written at the end

description: error from target database: %s
cause: This error should be followed by other errors indicating the cause of the problem.
action: No action required.

description: incompatible %s.%s.%s.%s DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE package: %s.%s.%s.%s required
cause: This version of database was incompatible with the the indicated DBMS_BACKUP_RESTORE package installed in the database.
action: If the database has been upgraded from an earlier version, ensure that the catxxxx.sql script has been run successfully. Re-install dbmsbkrs.sql and prvtbkrs.plb if necessary.

description: cannot use passphrase encryption for this backup
cause: Passphrase encryption was attempted for a backup that contains encrypted tablespaces and uses compression.
action: Do not use passphrase encryption for this backup. Use Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) instead.

description: invalid blocksize %s in backup piece header
cause: The blocksize of the backup piece obtained from the header was invalid.
action: The backup piece is corrupt. A different backup piece should be used for restore.

description: cannot use this control file to mount or open database
cause: This control file was restored by a DUPLICATE operation used only to restore and recover the data files of the new database. It is not meant to be used for mounting or opening the database, as allowing so might corrupt data files or online redo logs of the target database or both.
action: Re-create the control file manually specifying all of the names of the data files and online redo logs. Do not forget to use NID to change the name or DBID or both of the new database.

description: snapshot datafile checkpoint time is greater than snapshot time
cause: The snapshot time which was specified when starting the recovery less than data file's checkpoint time. The snapshot recovery is only possible with data file's whose checkpoint time is less than snapshot time.
action: Restore the data file's associated for the specified snapshot time or specify the correct snapshot time associated with the data file.

description: SNAPSHOT TIME recovery is not enabled
cause: An attempt was made to use SNAPSHOT TIME recovery. But, the feature was not enabled.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services to enable snapshot time recovery and then retry the command.

description: Cross-platform backups require a COMPATIBLE parameter value %s or greater.
cause: An attempt was made to create a cross-platform backup, but the COMPATIBLE parameter value was not set to a high enough value to allow this creation.
action: Set the COMPATIBLE parameter to the suggested or higher value, and retry the command.
params: 1) the minimum value for COMPATIBLE that is required for a cross-platform backup.

description: The current database incarnation changed during backup.
cause: The backup failed because the current database incarnation was changed during the backup. One of these events caused this incarnation change: - The database was opened using ALTER DATABASE OPEN RESETLOGS statement. - RMAN command RESET DATABASE TO INCARNATION was issued. - If this happened on physical standby database, then redo apply has applied redo data from a new database incarnation.
action: Retry the backup command.

description: Cannot obtain datafile name for datafile %s
cause: While trying to obtain the file enqueue for the datafile the datafile name could not be obtained.
action: Examine the trace and alert files for possible causes. Fix underlying problem before attempting command again.

description: Remote database ID %s is different from local database ID %s.
cause: The database ID on the remote site did not match the ID of the target database. This was caused by an incorrect service name for the remote connection.
action: Supply the correct service name and retry the command.

description: error in %s while communicating with remote database server
cause: An error occurred while initiating backup on a remote database server for network restore. Additional error messages will be issued to describe the failure.
action: Check additional error messages.
params: 1) module_name: The module where error was encountered.

description: cannot read header of the data file %s from remote site
cause: An attempt to read the file header from the remote site failed.
action: Ensure that the data file is accessible on the remote site and retry the command.
params: 1) data_file: The data file read from remote site.

description: cannot read header of control file from remote site
cause: Could not read the control file header from the remote site.
action: Make sure the database is mounted on the remote site and retry the command.

description: cross-platform backup piece requires COMPATIBLE %s or greater
cause: An attempt was made to perform a cross-platform operation from a backup piece created with a higher compatibility than the current COMPATIBLE parameter.
action: Raise the compatibility level or do not attempt a cross-platform restore from this backup piece.
params: 1) min_compat_version: The minimum compatible backup version required.

description: error while reading backup piece from service %s
cause: This error is followed by other errors indicating the cause of the problem.
action: See the other error actions.
params: 1) service_name: Remote instance where backup piece resides.

description: backup piece constructed from service %s is corrupt
cause: This error indicates that the backup piece that was constructed from the service is corrupt.
action: See alert log for details of the corruption. Fix the corruption and retry the command.

description: OS error while managing auxiliary database %s
cause: An operating system (OS) error occurred when managing the automatic auxiliary instance.
action: Check the accompanying errors.

description: error creating services for auxiliary instance %s (error %s)
cause: An error was received while managing the services of the auxiliary instance.
action: Check the accompanying errors.

description: error preparing auxiliary instance %s (error %s)
cause: An error was received while managing the automatic auxiliary instance.
action: Check the accompanying errors.

description: error obtaining connect string from target
cause: Could not obtain the connect string from the target database
action: Check the accompanying errors.

description: cannot use clone mounted control file to drop database
cause: The clone mounted control file could not be used to drop the database because the names of the data files and online logs were not fixed using the RMAN DUPLICATE command. This could cause the original database files to be lost.
action: Manually drop the database.

description: cannot use clone mounted control file to recover database
cause: The clone mounted control file could not be used to recover the database because the names of the data files and online logs were not fixed using the Recovery Manager (RMAN) operation. This could result in the loss of original database files.
action: Manually delete the files restored from the previous Recovery Manager (RMAN) operation by looking at the mounted control file and Recovery Manager (RMAN) output to clean up the partially incomplete operation. When deleting the files, be cautious to not delete production database files because some files in the control file may be pointing to those files.

description: Restore failure test event
cause: For testing only.
action: Set to test restore failure

description: piece validation cannot be performed more than once
cause: The user attempted to validate a list of backup pieces more than once. Validation may only be performed once for a given validation conversation.
action: Do not attempt to validate the pieces more than once.

description: additional backup pieces cannot be validated in this conversation
cause: The user tried to add new pieces to the list of files being validated after the validation had already been performed. In a validation conversation, the list can only be validated once.
action: Add all the backup pieces to the list before validating, or start a new validation conversation for the remaining pieces.

description: backup pieces must be validated before accessing results
cause: The user tried to get validation results for backup pieces before the pieces were actually validated.
action: Validate the pieces before trying to access the results.

description: device block size %s is larger than max allowed: %s
cause: The user specified a device BLKSIZE that is larger than the device BLKSIZE specified during compressed backup.
action: Change the device BLKSIZE to be smaller than the maximum allowed.

description: %s
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Backup piece %s has no data.
cause: No data was returned for the specified backup piece.
