action: Start Cluster Synchronization Services (CSS) and retry the operation.

description: Getting a GPnP attribute has failed with error [%s].
cause: An attempt to get a Grid Plug and Play (GPnP) attribute failed. See the information within the brackets for the cause.
action: Resolve the problem in the included message and retry the request.
params: 1) error: The error causing the failure.

description: Oracle Restart attribute GET failed with error [%s]
cause: An attempt to get the Oracle Restart attribute failed. See the brackets for the reason.
action: Resolve the problem in the included message and retry the request.

description: Oracle Restart attribute SET failed with error [%s]
cause: An attempt to set the Oracle Restart attribute failed. See the brackets for the reason.
action: Resolve the problem in the included message and retry the request.

description: Network interface query failed with error [%s].
cause: An attempt to get the network information failed. See the information in brackets for the cause.
action: Resolve the problem in the included message and retry the request.
params: 1) error: The error causing the network interface query to fail.

description: internal test event
cause: This is an internal test event. Set only under guidance of development.
action: Follow up with the Oracle Support Services using the traces generated by this event.

description: Cannot change user session parameters for a non-user session
cause: An attempt was made to change user session parameters for a non-user session.
action: Execute the operation when connected with a user session

description: Transactions cannot be replayed
cause: The user attempted to replay a transaction.
action: Reconnect and re-execute the transaction.

description: Enable AC performance optimization, only for internal testing
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Dump diagnostics for HA only during internal testing.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: crash for soft assert macros in global enqueue service layer
cause: NA
action: NA

description: invalid identifier %s found while parsing operator name
cause: The specified schema or object identifier for the operator was invalid.
action: Specify a valid identifier for the operator.
params: 1) invalid_identifier: The string that is not a invalid identifier.

description: missing RETURN keyword
cause: The CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement expected the RETURN keyword, but it was missing or a different token was used.
action: Check the syntax for the CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement and specify the RETURN keyword where appropriate.

description: missing CONTEXT keyword
cause: The CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement was expecting the CONTEXT keyword, but it was missing or a different token was used.
action: Check the syntax for the CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement and then specify the CONTEXT keyword where appropriate.

description: missing ANCILLARY keyword
cause: The CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement expected the ANCILLARY keyword, but it was missing or a different token was used.
action: Check the syntax for the CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement and specify the ANCILLARY keyword where appropriate.

description: missing DATA keyword
cause: The CREATE OPERATOR, ALTER OPERATOR, CREATE INDEXTYPE or ALTER INDEXTYPE statement was expecting the DATA keyword, but it was missing or a different token was used.
action: Check the syntax for the statement and specify the DATA keyword where appropriate.

description: COLUMN keyword missing.
cause: The CREATE OPERATOR, ALTER OPERATOR, CREATE INDEXTYPE or ALTER INDEXTYPE statement expects the COLUMN keyword. COLUMN is missing or an incorrect token was used.
action: Check the syntax for the statement and specify the COLUMN keyword.

description: could not find binding #%s for operator %s.%s during indextype export
cause: An attempt was made to export an indextype but one of the operator bindings could not be found.
action: Verify that the indextype and the dependent operators are valid. Retry the operation.
params: 1) operator_bind_number: The binding number identifying the signature of the operator. 2) operator_schema: The schema of the operator. 3) operator_name: The name of the operator.

description: operator does not exist
cause: The current operation could not find the specified operator or it was not in a valid state.
action: Verify that the operator exists, it is in a valid state, and the user has the EXECUTE privilege on this operator.

description: The specified binding for primary operator %s.%s does not exist.
cause: An attempt was made to specify a primary operator for an ancillary operator, but the primary operator binding did not exist.
action: Ensure that the specified binding for the primary operator exists.
params: 1) operator_schema: The schema of the primary operator. 2) operator_name: The name of the primary operator.

description: cannot drop an operator with dependent objects
cause: An attempt was made to drop or replace an operator that has dependent objects.
action: Drop the dependent objects then retry the operation, or specify the FORCE option in the DROP OPERATOR statement.

description: inadequate operator privileges
cause: The user did not have the appropriate privileges to perform the specified operation on the operator.
action: Grant the appropriate privileges to the user and then reissue the statement.

description: missing STATISTICS keyword
cause: This is not a valid option with the ASSOCIATE command.
action: Specify STATISTICS keyword after the ASSOCIATE command.

description: incorrect object name specified
cause: The specified name is not a valid name.
action: Specify the correct name of the object with for which an association needs to be defined.

description: non-supported object type with associate statement
cause: The type of object specified is not supported with the associate statistics statement.
action: Use a valid object type with the associate command.

description: expecting USING or DEFAULT keyword
cause: Expecting the USING or DEFAULT keyword after the names of object(s).
action: Provide the USING or DEFAULT keyword.

description: object being associated is not present
cause: The object for which the association is being defined is not present.
action: Ensure that all the objects for which the association is being defined are present.

description: object being disassociated is not present
cause: Object which is being disassociated is not present.
action: Ensure that the object which needs to be disassociated is present.

description: non-supported option with disassociate statement
cause: The type of object specified is not supported with the disassociate statistics statement.
action: Use a object type which is supported with the disassociate command.

description: column name not properly specified
cause: Name of the column should contain the table and the column name.
action: Specify a valid column name.

description: cannot associate default values with columns
cause: User tried to associate DEFAULT values with columns which is not a valid option .
action: Specify a valid option.

description: the statistics type is not present
cause: The statistics type which is being associated with object(s) is not present.
action: Ensure that the type which contains the statistics functions is present.

description: Primary operator %s.%s does not exist.
cause: Attempted to link a primary operator to an ancillary operator, but the primary operator does not exist, or the user does not have the access privileges needed.
action: Verify that the primary operator exists, and it is accessible to the user.
params: 1) operator_schema: The schema of the primary operator. 2) operator_name: The name of the primary operator.

description: selectivity cannot be specified for the type of object
cause: User tried to associate selectivity with index or indextypes which is not allowed .
action: Specify a valid option.

description: object being analyzed is not a table
cause: The object being analyzed is not a table and is not supported
action: Specify only a supported option.

description: Operator is invalid.
cause: An attempt was made to use an operator in an invalid state.
action: Compile the operator using the ALTER OPERATOR COMPILE statement and retry the operation.

description: invalid indextype identifier: %s
cause: The identifier used during a Data Definition Language (DDL) statement affecting indextype objects had invalid characters.
action: Ensure that the all characters in the identifier are valid and that the name is not a reserved word.
params: 1) identifier_string: The identifier with invalid characters.

description: missing FOR keyword
cause: The CREATE INDEXTYPE statement was expecting the FOR keyword, but it was missing or a different token was used.
action: Check the syntax for the CREATE INDEXTYPE statement and specify the FOR keyword where appropriate.

description: missing USING keyword
cause: The CREATE INDEXTYPE, ALTER INDEXTYPE, CREATE OPERATOR, or ALTER OPERATOR statement was expecting the USING keyword, but it was missing or a different keyword was used.
action: Check the syntax for the current statement and specify the USING keyword where appropriate.

description: invalid name for implementation type
cause: The name or schema of the implementation type was invalid.
action: Verify that all the characters in the name and schema of the implementation type are valid and are not reserved words.

description: implementation type does not exist
cause: The implementation type specified with USING clause could not be found.
action: Check to see if the type exists and the user has EXECUTE privilege on this type.

description: The operator %s.%s does not exist.
cause: The current operation could not find the specified operator or it was not in a valid state.
action: Verify that the operator exists, that it is in a valid state, and that the user has the EXECUTE privilege on this operator.
params: 1) operator_schema: The schema of the operator. 2) operator_name: The name of the operator.

description: failed to find matching bind for operator %s.%s
cause: An attempt was made to add or drop operator bindings to an indextype, but the specified operator binding could not be found.
action: Ensure that the operator bind is an existing bind for the specified operator.
params: 1) operator_schema: The schema of the operator. 2) operator_name: The name of the operator.

description: cannot drop or replace an indextype with dependent indexes
cause: One or more indexes are dependent upon the indextype.
action: Drop all the indexes which are dependent upon the indextype before dropping the indextype itself.

description: The indextype does not exist.
cause: There is no indextype by the specified name.
action: Use public data dictionary views for the indextypes to see if an indextype by the specified name has been created.

description: REF data type is not supported with operators.
cause: An attempt was made to create an operator binding that contained at least one REF data type argument.
action: Create the operator without using a REF data type.

description: ODCIGETINTERFACES routine does not return required interface(s)
cause: The ODCIObjectList returned by the ODCIGetInterfaces routine does not contain the interface(s) required by the current usage.
action: Ensure that the ODCIGetInterfaces routine returns the name(s) of the required interface(s).

description: failed to validate indextype operator %s
cause: One of the operators that was referenced by the indextype could not be validated implicitly.
action: Recompile the operators referenced by the indextype. Use the USER_INDEXTYPE_OPERATORS, ALL_INDEXTYPE_OPERATORS, or DBA_INDEXTYPE_OPERATORS views to identify the dependent operators of the indextype.
params: 1) operator_name: The name of the operator that could not be validated.

description: insufficient privileges to execute implementation type
cause: User does not have privileges to execute the implementation type.
action: The owner of the implementation type must grant appropriate privileges to the user.

description: insufficient privileges on operators referenced by indextype
cause: An attempt was made to create or alter an indextype, but the user does not have the correct privileges to use the dependent operators.
action: The owner of the operators must grant the appropriate privilege on the operators to the user before the operation is retried.

description: failed to validate implementation type %s.%s
cause: An attempt was made to operate on an indextype for which its underlying implementation type could not be implicitly validated.
action: Compile the implementation type and then retry the operation.
params: 1) implementation_type_schema: Schema of the implementation type. 2) implementation_type_name: Name of the implementation type.

description: indextype and implementation type are not in the same schema
cause: An attempt was made to create or alter an indextype whose implementation type was in a different schema.
action: Put the indextype and implementation type in the same schema.

description: invalid option for ALTER INDEXTYPE
cause: The user specified an invalid option with the ALTER INDEXTYPE statement.
action: Review the syntax for the ALTER INDEX TYPE statement and provide valid options.

description: Version %s of the indextype interface does not support option %s.
cause: An option was specified that was not supported by the version of the indextype interface.
action: Either do not request this option or provide an implementation for the correct version of the indextype interface.
params: 1) interface_version_number: The version number of the Oracle Data Cartridge Interface implemented by the indextype. 2) option_name: The unsupported option on the indextype DDL.

description: indextype should support at least one operator
cause: An attempt was made to alter an indextype which would drop all the operators bound to it.
action: Modify the ALTER INDEXTYPE statement to retain at least one operator.

description: duplicate operator binding specified for operator %s.%s
cause: An attempt was made to add an operator name to an indextype that was already supported by the indextype.
action: Remove the duplicate operator and retry the command.
params: 1) operator_schema: The schema of the operator with a duplicate binding. 2) operator_name: The name of the operator with a duplicate binding.

description: indextype does not support local domain index on %s partitioned table
cause: User specified a create local domain index statement using an indextype that does not support local domain indexes on tables partitioned with the given method
action: Use a different indextype or build a global domain index

description: cannot create a local domain index on a %s partitioned table
cause: An attempt was made to create a local domain index on a table that was partitioned by a partitioning method, which was not supported by domain indexes.
action: Build a global domain index on the partitioned table.

description: cannot create a local domain index on a partitioned index-organized table
cause: User specified a create local domain index statement on a partitioned index-organized table
action: Build a global domain index on the partitioned index-organized table

description: Error while processing the ODCIINDEXMERGEPARTITION routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXMERGEPARTITION routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXMERGEPARTITION routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: Error while processing the ODCIINDEXSPLITPARTITION routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXSPLITPARTITION routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXSPLITPARTITION routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: invalid option for creation of domain indexes
cause: The user specified an invalid option like ASC, DESC, SORT or a parallel clause, partitioning clause or physical attributes clause.
action: Choose one of the valid clauses for creation of domain indexes.

description: cannot build a domain index on more than one column
cause: User attempted to build a domain index on more than one column.
action: Build the domain index only on a single column.

description: keyword IS is missing
cause: IS keyword must be specified with Create Index statement for domain indexes.
action: Use IS keyword and then specify the indextype name.

description: keyword UNIQUE may not be used in creating domain indexes
cause: An attempt was made to create a domain index with the UNIQUE attribute.
action: Remove UNIQUE from the CREATE INDEX statement.

description: keyword BITMAP may not be used in creating domain indexes
cause: An attempt was made to create a domain index with the BITMAP attribute.
action: Remove BITMAP from the CREATE INDEX statement.

description: Error while processing the ODCIINDEXCREATE routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXCREATE routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXCREATE routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: Error while processing ODCIINDEXDROP routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: Running the ODCIINDEXDROP routine caused an error. Its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error, and take the appropriate action to resolve it.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXDROP routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: domain indexes and/or secondary objects exist in the tablespace
cause: An attempt was made to drop a tablespace which contains secondary objects and/or domain indexes.
action: Drop the domain indexes in his tablespace. Also, find the domain indexes which created secondary objects in this tablespace and drop them. Then try dropping the tablespace.

description: Error while processing the ODCIINDEXALTER routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXALTER routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXALTER routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: Error while processing ODCIINDEXTRUNCATE routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXTRUNCATE routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXTRUNCATE routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: cannot truncate a table with domain indexes in LOADING status
cause: An attempt was made to truncate a table while there were domain indexes in LOADING status.
action: Retry the operation when the operations that impacted the domain indexes have been completed. If the status of the domain index partition still remains in LOADING state, then contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Domain index %s.%s is marked %s and currently not usable.
cause: An attempt was been made to access a domain index that was being built or was marked failed by an unsuccessful data definition language (DDL) or was marked unusable by a DDL operation.
action: Wait for the index build to finish if the specified index is marked LOADING. Drop or rebuild the specified index if it is marked FAILED. Drop or rebuild the specified index if it is marked UNUSABLE.
params: 1) index_schema: The schema of the domain index. 2) index_name: The name of the domain index. 3) index_status: The status of the domain index (that is, LOADING, FAILED or UNUSABLE).

description: cannot specify FORCE option for dropping non-domain index
cause: A DROP INDEX FORCE was issued for a non-domain index.
action: Reissue the command without the FORCE option.

description: ODCI_WARNING returned by the implementation of the ODCIINDEXCREATE routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXCREATE routine returned the ODCI_WARNING return code.
action: Review the errors associated with this warning and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXCREATE routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_WARNING return code.

description: analyzing domain indexes marked LOADING/FAILED not supported
cause: Tried to analyze a domain index which was marked as LOADING or FAILED.
action: If the index was marked LOADING, wait till it is marked valid before retrying the analyze. If index was marked FAILED, drop it OR rebuild it and retry the analyze.

description: indextype is invalid
cause: The indextype is invalid.
action: Drop and recreate the indextype.

description: cannot create domain index on a column of index-organized table
cause: Tried to create a domain index on a column of an index-organized table.
action: Do not attempt to create a domain index on columns of an index-organized table.

description: cannot create a domain index on a LONG column
cause: The user attempted to create a domain index on a column of LONG datatype.
action: Do not create a domain index on a LONG column.

description: Cannot modify domain index in LOADING status.
cause: Attempted to execute a data definition language (DDL) statement which affected a domain index in LOADING state.
action: Retry after the domain index operation completes. Contact Oracle Support Services if the domain index status remains in LOADING state.

description: Cannot modify domain index in FAILED status.
cause: Attempted to execute a DDL statement which affected a domain index in FAILED state.
action: Rebuild the index or truncate the table to return the index to VALID status.

description: specified options are only valid for altering a domain index
cause: Specified the ONLINE or PARAMETERS clause with a non-domain index.
action: Reissue the statement with the correct syntax for alter.

description: invalid alter option for a domain index
cause: The user specified an invalid option for altering a domain index.
action: Reissue the alter statement with a valid option.

description: parameters clause cannot be combined with the specified options
cause: The user combined PARAMETERS clause with other alter index options.
action: Reissue the statement with the correct syntax for alter.

description: ODCI_WARNING returned during the ODCIIndexDrop routine implementation for index %s.%s. %s
cause: When executing the ODCIIndexDrop routine, the ODCI_WARNING code was returned.
action: Review the errors associated with this Oracle Data Cartridge Interface (ODCI) warning and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIIndexDrop routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_WARNING return code.

description: ODCI_WARNING returned by the implementation of the ODCIINDEXALTER routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXALTER routine returned the ODCI_WARNING return code.
action: Review the errors associated with this warning and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXALTER routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_WARNING return code.

description: Error while processing ODCIINDEXINSERT routine for index %s.%s %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXINSERT routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXINSERT routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: Error while processing ODCIINDEXDELETE routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: Running the ODCIINDEXDELETE routine caused an error. Its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error, and take the appropriate action to resolve it.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXDELETE routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: Error while processing the ODCIINDEXUPDATE routine %s.%s. %s
cause: Processing the ODCIINDEXUPDATE routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXUPDATE routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: ODCI_WARNING returned by the implementation of the ODCIINDEXTRUNCATE routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXTRUNCATE routine returned the ODCI_WARNING return code.
action: Review the errors associated with this warning and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXTRUNCATE routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_WARNING return code.

description: cannot create multiple domain indexes on a column list using same indextype
cause: An attempt was made to define multiple domain indexes on the same column list using identical indextypes.
action: Check to see if a different indextype can be used or if the index can be defined on another column list.

description: such column list already indexed using another domain index and indextype
cause: An attempt was made to create multiple domain indexes on a column list using indextypes which do not have disjoint operators.
action: Check to see if the operator sets for the indextypes can be made disjoint.

description: failed to validate indextype
cause: An attempt to validate the indextype that was referenced by the domain index failed.
action: Verify that the indextype that is referenced by the domain index exists in the database, and then compile the indextype.

description: insufficient privileges to execute indextype
cause: User does not have privileges to execute the indextype.
action: The owner of the indextype must grant appropriate privileges to the user.

description: cannot create a domain index on column expressions
cause: User specified an expression in the column list.
action: Specify only simple columns in the column list for domain index.

description: A domain index is defined on the column to be dropped.
cause: An ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN command was issued on a column on which a domain index exists.
action: Drop the domain index before attempting to drop the column.

description: domain index is defined on the column to be modified
cause: An ALTER TABLE MODIFY COLUMN was issued on a column on which a domain index exists.
action: Drop the domain index before attempting to modify the column.

description: feature not supported for domain indexes
cause: An attempt was made to use a feature that is unsupported by domain indexes.
action: Drop the domain index or avoid using the unsupported feature.

description: cannot support row movement if domain index defined on table
cause: An ALTER TABLE ENABLE ROW MOVEMENT was issued on a table which has a domain index defined on it.
action: Drop the domain index if you want to enable row movement and then reissue the command.

description: cannot create domain index on a table with row movement enabled
cause: A create domain index statement was issued on a table that has row movement enabled.
action: Disable the row movement in the table and then reissue the create domain index statement. NLS_DO_NOT_TRANSLATE[29889,29889]

description: allow a secondary object creation
cause: For internal use only
action: THIS IS NOT A USER ERROR NUMBER/MESSAGE. THIS DOES NOT NEED TO BE TRANSLATED OR DOCUMENTED. IT IS USED ONLY BY IMPORT CODE.

description: primary operator %s.%s does not have an index context
cause: An attempt was made to create an ancillary operator whose primary operator did not have index and scan contexts.
action: Specify a primary operator that uses index and scan contexts, and computes ancillary data when creating an ancillary operator.
params: 1) primary operator schema: The schema of the primary operator. 2) primary operator name: The name of the primary operator.

description: Event to enable debugging in ODCI user-defined routines.
cause: This event level is propagated to ODCIIndex and ODCIStats routines to request debugging or diagnostic actions from the data cartridge.
action: No action required. This is an internal event.

description: Indextypes with array DML do not support the specified data type.
cause: The statement used a REF or a LONG data type which is not supported in a CREATE INDEXTYPE or ALTER INDEXTYPE statement using a WITH ARRAY DML clause.
action: Retry the statement without the REF or LONG data type.

description: INDEXTYPE without column data do not need the specified data type.
cause: The WITH ARRAY DML statement with explicit data types for a CREATE INDEXTYPE or ALTER INDEXTYPE statement was used with a WITHOUT COLUMN DATA clause.
action: Remove the WITHOUT COLUMN DATA clause, or remove the explicit data types on the WITH ARRAY DML clause. Retry the statement.

description: Base or varray data type %s.%s does not exist.
cause: One of the base and varray data types specified in the WITH ARRAY DML clause could not be found.
action: Check to see if the data type exists, is in a valid state, and that the user has EXECUTE privilege on this data type.
params: 1) type_schema: The schema of the missing type. 2) type_name: The name of the missing type.

description: A duplicate base data type was specified.
cause: An attempt was made to add a base data type to an indextype with an ARRAY DML that is already supported by the indextype.
action: Remove the duplicate base data type and retry the command.

description: Length of PARAMETER string longer than %s characters
cause: An attempt was made to specify a parameter value that is longer than the allowed maximum.
action: Reduce the parameter value length.

description: invalid domain index %s.%s found on the same column
cause: An attempt was made to create a domain index on the same column where an invalid domain index exists.
action: Drop the invalid index and then reissue the CREATE INDEX statement.
params: 1) index_schema: The schema of the domain index. 2) index_name: The name of the domain index.

description: The invocation of operator %s does not match operator bindings.
cause: An attempt was made to invoke an operator that had a set of arguments whose data types did not match any operator binding.
action: Change the operator arguments to match any of the existing bindings or add a new binding to the operator.
params: 1) operator_name: The name of the operator.

description: Function underlying operator binding does not exist.
cause: Attempted to invoke an operator binding in a query and the underlying PL/SQL function was invalid or does not exist.
action: Verify that the function corresponding to the operator invocation exists and is in a valid state.

description: Error while processing the ODCIINDEXSTART routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: Processing the ODCIINDEXSTART routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXSTART routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: Error while processing ODCIINDEXFETCH routine for index %s.%s %s
cause: Running the ODCIINDEXFETCH routine caused an error. Its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the other error messages associated with this error, and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXFETCH routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: Error while processing ODCIINDEXCLOSE routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXCLOSE routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXCLOSE routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: method %s does not exist in type %s.%s
cause: A required method with the required signature does not exist in the specified type.
action: Add the required method to the type.

description: indextype %s.%s does not exist
cause: The indextype does not exist.
action: Create the indextype.

description: duplicate labels found in primary operator calls
cause: There were multiple primary calls to operators with the same number in their label argument.
action: Specify unique label arguments to the primary operator calls.

description: missing primary invocation for ancillary operator
cause: An ancillary operator was used and either the label argument to the ancillary operator did not match the label argument of any primary invocation, or the primary invocation could not be found in the same query block as the ancillary operator.
action: Ensure the ancillary operator and the primary invocation have matching labels and are present on the same query block.

description: label for the ancillary operator is not a literal number
cause: The label used for invoking the ancillary operator was not a numeric constant.
action: Use a constant literal number as the label to the ancillary operator.

description: invalid callback operation
cause: Encountered an invalid callback operation.
action: Ensure that all the callbacks executed from callouts are valid in the statement context.

description: null scan context returned by %s routine
cause: The specified routine returned a null scan context.
action: Ensure that the routine returns a non-null scan context.
params: 1) data_cartridge_routine: The name of the Oracle Data Cartridge Interface (ODCI) routine that returned a null scan context.

description: event for turning off direct invocation of CONTAINS and SCORE
cause: This event turns off the direct invocation of CONTAINS or SCORE operators.
action: No action required. This is an internal event.

description: error while processing %s routine
cause: Either processing the specified data cartridge routine caused an error, or the implementation of the data cartridge routine returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the other error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.

description: ODCIGETINTERFACES routine does not return required stream version
cause: The ODCIObjectList returned by the ODCIGetInterfaces routine does not contain the required stream version for external tables.
action: Ensure that the ODCIGetInterfaces routine returns the required stream version.

description: FOR UPDATE clause cannot be used when selecting a collection operand.
cause: Collection operands cannot be updated.
action: Remove FOR UPDATE clause.

description: event for turning on RAW pointer arg to table function
cause: For internal use only
action: Not a user error

description: cannot lock a table which gets its rows from a collection operand
cause: Tables which gets its rows from a collection operand cannot be locked
action: Don't lock the table

description: cannot create domain indexes on temporary tables
cause: An attempt was made to create a domain index on a temporary table
action: Either create another type of index on the temporary table or change the table from temporary to a permanent table

description: Error while processing ODCIINDEXUPDPARTMETADATA routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: Processing of the ODCIINDEXUPDPARTMETADATA routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXUPDPARTMETADATA routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: Partition maintenance operation failed on secondary table %s.%s.
cause: Failed to successfully process the partition maintenance operation of a secondary table in a system managed domain index.
action: Review and solve the errors below this error and retry. If errors cannot be resolved, contact Oracle Support Services.
params: 1) Secondary table schema: The schema of the domain index secondary table. 2) Secondary table name: The name of the domain index secondary table.

description: ancillary operator not supported with set view query block
cause: The ancillary operator matched to a primary operator was outside a UNION ALL view query block while the primary operator was contained in one of the UNION ALL branches.
action: Define the UNION ALL view query block to contain both the primary and ancillary operators, so that the operators are contained by the query block in the UNION ALL branch, rather than in the query block outside of the view.

description: Scan of domain index "%s"."%s" returned an invalid ROWID.
cause: The scan of the specified domain index returned an incorrectly formatted ROWID.
action: Ensure the implementation of the data cartridge index maintenance methods are correct. For external implementations, review the documentation of the data cartridge from the external vendor. Otherwise, contact Oracle Support.
params: 1) index_schema: The schema of the domain index. 2) index_name: The name of the domain index.

description: missing or unexpected signature for %s routine
cause: An attempt was made to invoke a routine for a data cartridge that did not exist or did not have the appropriate signature.
action: Implement the missing routine with the appropriate signature.
params: 1) data_cartridge_routine_name: The name of the Oracle Database Data Cartridge interface whose signature is missing or does not match the expected signature.

description: association already defined for the object
cause: The object for which the association is being defined, already has a statistics type associated with it.
action: Disassociate the object and then associate the object.

description: error in executing the ODCIStatsCollect / ODCIStatsDelete routine
cause: The ODCIStatsCollect / ODCIStatsDelete function is causing an error.
action: Check the ODCIStatsCollect / ODCIStatsDelete function.

description: duplicate default selectivity specified
cause: The keyword DEFAULT SELECTIVITY can only be specified once.
action: Remove the duplicate keyword.

description: missing SCAN keyword
cause: The CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement was expecting the SCAN keyword, but the entry was missing or a different token was used.
action: Check the syntax for the CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement and specify the SCAN keyword where appropriate.

description: COMPUTE ANCILLARY DATA specified without the INDEX CONTEXT clause
cause: The COMPUTE ANCILLARY DATA option was specified without the WITH INDEX CONTEXT clause.
action: Specify the WITH INDEX CONTEXT clause.

description: specified association does not exist
cause: One or more of the object(s) that have been specified to be disassociated, do not have an association defined for them.
action: Verify the objects which have an association defined and issue the disassociate command again.

description: the type being dropped is a statistics type
cause: Some objects have defined their statistics methods in the type being dropped.
action: First drop the relevant associations using the DISASSOCIATE command and then retry the DROP command, or use the FORCE option with DROP TYPE command.

description: object being disassociated has some user defined statistics stored
cause: There are some user defined statistics collected for the object being disassociated.
action: First delete the user defined statistics and then reissue the DISASSOCIATE command or specify the FORCE option with DISASSOCIATE.

description: index specified for association is not a domain index
cause: The user issued an ASSOCIATE STATISTICS command with an index which is not a domain index.
action: Issue an ASSOCIATE STATISTICS WITH INDEXES command on a domain index only

description: missing FROM keyword
cause: The keyword FROM is missing.
action: Specify the FROM keyword or check the SQL statement.

description: NULL association is allowed only with a column or an index
cause: User tried to use the ASSOCIATE command with a schema object other than a column or an index
action: Specify the NULL clause only with a column or an index

description: domain index cannot be system-managed
cause: An ASSOCIATE STATISTICS command was issued with a domain index which is system-managed.
action: Check to see if the domain index has been implemented with system-managed storage tables. To associate statistics with a system-managed domain index, issue ASSOCIATE STATISTICS command with the indextype of this domain index.

description: both indextype and statistics type should be system-managed
cause: Either an ASSOCIATE STATISTICS WITH SYSTEM MANAGED STORAGE TABLES command was issued with an indextype which is not system-managed, or an ASSOCIATE STATISTICS command was issued with an indextype which is system-managed.
action: Check to see if both indextype and statistics type are implemented with system-managed storage tables.

description: failed to implicitly transform user-managed domain index %s.%s to system-managed domain index
cause: An attempt was made to convert a user-managed indextype into a system-managed indextype and the subsequent implicit validation of the domain indexes could not be completed.
action: Issue an ALTER INDEX COMPILE statement on the domain index.
params: 1) index_schema: The schema of the domain index. 2) index_name: The name of the domain index.

description: User-managed domain indexes are not allowed on interval-partitioned tables.
cause: An attempt was made to create a local user-managed domain index on an interval-partitioned table.
action: Convert the underlying index type to system-managed.

description: cannot convert a table with user-managed local domain indexes to an interval-partitioned table
cause: An attempt was made to convert a range-partitioned table with local user-managed domain indexes to an interval-partitioned table.
action: Either convert the underlying indextype to system-managed or drop the local user-managed domain index before converting the table to an interval-partitioned table.

description: ODCI_WARNING returned by the implementation of the ODCIINDEXMERGEPARTITION routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXMERGEPARTITION routine returned the ODCI_WARNING return code.
action: Review the errors associated with this warning and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXMERGEPARTITION routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_WARNING return code.

description: ODCI_WARNING returned by the implementation of the ODCIINDEXSPLITPARTITION routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXSPLITPARTITION routine returned the ODCI_WARNING return code.
action: Review the errors associated with this warning and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXSPLITPARTITION routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_WARNING return code.

description: Cannot modify domain index partition %s which is in LOADING status.
cause: An attempt was made to issue a DDL statement that affected a domain index partition in LOADING status.
action: Retry the operation when the operation affecting the domain index partition has completed. Contact Oracle Support if the status of the domain index partition remains in the LOADING state.

description: Cannot issue a DDL statement on domain index partition %s which is in FAILED status.
cause: Attempted to start a partition maintenance operation on a table with the specified domain index partition in a FAILED state or to modify the parameters of that specified domain index partition in a FAILED state.
action: Rebuild the index partition by using the ALTER INDEX REBUILD PARTITION statement or remove all rows from the partition using the ALTER TABLE TRUNCATE PARTITION statement.

description: Domain index partition %s is marked %s and currently not usable.
cause: An attempt was made to access a domain index partition that was either: * being built, or * marked FAILED, or * marked LOADING, or * marked UNUSABLE by an unsuccessful Data Definition Language (DDL) statement.
action: Wait for the domain index operation on the partition to complete if it is marked LOADING. Rebuild the domain index partition if it is marked FAILED or UNUSABLE.
params: 1) partition_name: The name of the domain index partition. 2) partition_status: The status of the domain index partition. The statuses: LOADING, FAILED, or UNUSABLE.

description: Error while processing ODCIINDEXEXCHANGEPARTITION routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The processing of the ODCIINDEXEXCHANGEPARTITION routine caused an error, or its implementation returned the ODCI_ERROR return code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXEXCHANGEPARTITION routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: ODCI_WARNING returned during the ODCIINDEXEXCHANGEPARTITION routine implementation for index %s.%s. %s
cause: When implementing the ODCIINDEXEXCHANGEPARTITION routine, a nonfatal warning condition occurred.
action: Review the messages associated with this warning, and take the appropriate action to resolve them.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXEXCHANGEPARTITION routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_ERROR return code.

description: cannot create a function-based domain index on a %s table
cause: User specified an unsupported create function-based domain index statement.
action: Issue the create function-based domain index statement only on supported types of tables.

description: ODCI_FATAL returned by the implementation of the ODCIINDEXCREATE routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: Implementation of the ODCIINDEXCREATE routine of a domain index returned the ODCI_FATAL error code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error, take the appropriate action to resolve, and retry.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXCREATE routine; either by being raised from the implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_FATAL return code.

description: Error while executing the %s routine for one or more index partitions of index %s.%s. %s
cause: Execution of specified data cartridge routine returned an ODCI_ERROR_CONTINUE return code while processing one or more index partitions.
action: Review the other error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them. Check the dictionary views to see which partitions are marked FAILED. Rebuild or truncate the FAILED index partitions.
params: 1) routine_name: The name of the Oracle Data Cartridge Interface (ODCI) routine that encountered an error. 2) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 3) index_name: The name of the index. 4) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the routine; either by being raised from the routine's implementation of the routine or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_FATAL return code.

description: line %s, %s
cause: The Oracle Data Cartridge Interface (ODCI) extensible indexing data definition language (DDL) routine had put a warning message into the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table.
action: Review the warning message raised by the ODCI extensible indexing DDL routine.
params: 1) line_number: The line number identifier provided by the Oracle Data Cartridge implementation to identify the external warning. 2) warning_message: The warning message raised by the Oracle Data Cartridge implementation.

description: cannot report all warnings registered from data cartridge DDL routine
cause: A data cartridge implementation of the extensible indexing interface (ODCIINDEX) registered a large number of exceptions to table SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ during the execution of a DDL statement.
action: Review all the reported warning messages by querying table SYS.ODCIWARNINGS$.

description: ODCI_FATAL returned by the implementation of the ODCIINDEXALTER routine for index %s.%s. %s
cause: The implementation of the ODCIINDEXALTER routine of a domain index returned the ODCI_FATAL error code.
action: Review the error messages associated with this error and take the appropriate action to resolve them. Rebuild the domain index or domain index partitions that are marked as FAILED, and retry the operation.
params: 1) index_owner: The schema name of the index. 2) index_name: The name of the index. 3) error_summary: A string describing the underlying errors encountered by the ODCIINDEXALTER routine; either by being raised from the routine's implementation or by being registered in the SYS.ODCI_WARNINGS$ table prior to returning the ODCI_FATAL return code.

description: missing BINDING keyword
cause: The CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement expected the BINDING keyword. Instead, it missed the token or used a different one.
action: Check the syntax for the CREATE OPERATOR or ALTER OPERATOR statement, and specify the BINDING keyword as appropriate.

description: missing ADD or DROP keyword
cause: One of the keywords ADD or DROP is expected.
action: Specify the ADD or DROP keyword or check the SQL statement.

description: specified binding does not match existing bindings
cause: The binding specified in the DROP BINDING clause did not match any of the existing bindings associated with the operator.
action: Specify an existing binding for this operator in the DROP BINDING clause of the ALTER OPERATOR statement.

description: Cannot drop the operator binding. At least one function binding is required.
cause: An attempt was made to drop the only or last binding of an operator.
action: To drop the operator, use the DROP OPERATOR statement instead.

description: cannot drop an operator binding with dependent objects
cause: The operator binding that is being dropped had dependent objects.
action: Either drop the dependent objects first and then issue the ALTER OPERATOR DROP BINDING statement or specify the FORCE option with the ALTER OPERATOR DROP BINDING statement.

description: No primary operator bindings found for ancillary binding #%s of operator %s.%s.
cause: At least one ancillary binding of the specified operator could not be validated because all of its associated primary operator bindings have been dropped.
action: Either drop the ancillary binding whose primary operators are missing, or drop the entire operator if this is the only binding.
params: 1) binding_number: The binding number identifying the argument combination of the operator. 2) operator_schema: The schema of the operator object. 3) operator_name: The name of the operator object.

description: failure in updating parameter, invalid value(s) supplied: %s
cause: One of the values for this multi-valued parameter was invalid.
action: Correct the invalid value and re-run the command.

description: Specified registration id does not exist
cause: An incorrect regid value was passed to dbms_chnf procedure.
action: pass the correct regid value.

description: Specified table name not found or does not have any registrations
cause: The database could not locate the passed in table name
action: CHeck the table name passed in.

description: user does not have privilege to change/ create registration
cause: User passed in an incorrect or someone else's regid/ handle.
action: Check the passed in regid/ reg handle

description: Unsupported query or operation during change notification registration
cause: The user attempted to register an unsupported query type or an unsupported operation like a DML/DDL for change notification.
action: Please check the statement being executed and refer to the documentation.

description: Internal event for PL/SQL debugging
cause: None
action: none

description: Cannot register a query in the middle of an active transaction
cause: User tried to register a query within an uncommitted transaction.
action: Commit the transaction and retry.

description: Unsupported query for registration in guaranteed mode
cause: An operator or expression in the query was incompatible with query registration in the guaranteed granularity mode.
action: Check all expressions, clauses and operators in the query and refer to the documentation for supported query types. The application can reattempt the query registration in best effort mode.

description: Unsupported column type for query registration in guaranteed mode
cause: An attempt was made to register a query with an unsupported column type or too many columns.
action: Examine all column datatypes in the expression and refer to the documentation for supported query types. The application can reattempt the query registration in best effort mode.

description: Internal event for tracing Inband Notifications
cause: None
action: none

description: unsupported row size for query result change notification
cause: An attempt was made to register query result change notification (QRCN) on a table with more than 255 columns.
action: Use object change notification (OCN) instead.

description: Internal event for KTG crash recovery
cause: None
action: none

description: Cannot register query: conflicting DDL in progress
cause: A query registration was attempted while there was a a concurrent DDL in progress.
action: Retry the query registration.

description: Table type not supported for query registration in guaranteed mode
cause: The user attempted to register a query involving an unsupported table type.
action: Examine all tables in the query registration and refer to the documentation for supported table types. The application can reattempt registration in best effort mode.

description: Unsupported query for Continuous Query Notification
cause: The query cannot be registered for Continuous Query Notification.
action: The query has some constructs that make it incompatible with Continuous Query Notification like synonyms or views. Please check the documentation for complete list.

description: Internal event to force CHNF registrations
cause: None
action: none

description: Query Registration is only supported for automatic undo management
cause: User is using manual undo management
action: Switch to using automatic undo management

description: Internal event for CQN to enable slow path ROWID generation
cause: None
action: None

description: Internal event for validating context in KTG Hash Insert Item
cause: None
action: None

description: Event to enable blocking on client cache registrations
cause: None
action: None

description: not enough shared pool memory due to very many CQN registrations
cause: Max allowed shared pool usage for KTCN is 1 percent of shared pool size. The shared pool usage for KTCN depends directly on the number of CQN registrations.
action: Increase shared_pool_size in Init.ora. Check relevant trace files to get more information about the current number of CQN registrations that caused this error message.

description: ROWID threshold greater than 65535 not allowed.
cause: An attempt is being made to set the ROWID threshold to a value greater than 65535.
action: Set the ROWID threshold to a value less than 65535.

description: Specified queue '%s' is of the wrong type.
cause: The specified queue is of the wrong type.
action: Provide a transactional event queue and reissue the Continuous Query Notification (CQN) registration.

description: Server does not support pull model for change notification.
cause: The connected Oracle server does not support the pull model feature of change notification, therefore registrations with pull notifications flag are not allowed.
action: Log on to an Oracle server that supports the change notification pull model.

description: missing either trim specification or char expression in TRIM
cause: Since FROM is specified in TRIM function, either trim specification (TRAILING, HEADING, BOTH) or trim character or both must be specified.
action: Add either trim specification (TRAILING, HEADING, BOTH) or trim character or both.

description: trim set should have only one character
cause: Trim set contains more or less than 1 character. This is not allowed in TRIM function.
action: Change trim set to have only 1 character.

description: SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function is not allowed here
cause: SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function was called at places other than the SELECT list and ORDER BY clause.
action: Remove calls to SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function at places other than the SELECT list and ORDER BY clause.

description: illegal parameter in SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function
cause: NA
action: use a non-empty constant string as the second argument, then retry the operation.

description: when using SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function, cannot have separator as part of column value
cause: A column value contained the string that the SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function was to use to separate column values.
action: Specify another separator for the SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH function to use which does not occur in any column value, then retry.

description: missing or invalid WAIT interval
cause: A non-zero integer must be specified for wait interval (in seconds) after the WAIT keyword.
action: Correct the syntax and retry.

description: resource busy; acquire with WAIT timeout expired or DTP service is unavailable
cause: The requested resource was busy or the Distributed Transaction Processing (DTP) service was being relocated.
action: Retry the operation later.

description: CONNECT BY ROOT operator is not supported in the START WITH or in the CONNECT BY condition
cause: An attempt was made to use CONNECT BY ROOT operator in the START WITH or in the CONNECT BY condition.
action: Remove CONNECT BY ROOT operator from the START WITH or from the CONNECT BY condition.

description: CONNECT BY clause must reference a PRIOR
cause: A CONNECT BY clause did not include a predicate referencing a PRIOR so there was no condition connecting a parent row to its child row.
action: Add a reference to a PRIOR in the CONNECT BY clause.

description: Not enough memory for %s operation
cause: The memory size was not sufficient to process all the levels of the hierarchy specified by the query.
action: In WORKAREA_SIZE_POLICY=AUTO mode, set PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET to a reasonably larger value. Or, in WORKAREA_SIZE_POLICY=MANUAL mode, set SORT_AREA_SIZE to a reasonably larger value.

description: Not enough I/O buffers for the sort operation
cause: The sort was unable to allocate enough I/O buffers.
action: Increase the amount of memory allowed for the sort or increase the maximum number of I/O buffers allowed in the system and retry the query.

description: Error simulated: psite=%s, ptype=%s
cause: error generated for testing purposes.
action: None.

description: undo tablespace '%s' does not exist or of wrong type
cause: the specified undo tablespace does not exist or of the wrong type.
action: Correct the tablespace name and reissue the statement.

description: undo tablespace '%s' is currently in use
cause: the specified undo tablespace is currently used by another instance.
action: Wait for the undo tablespace to become available or change to another name and reissue the statement.

description: operation only supported in Automatic Undo Management mode
cause: the operation is only supported in automatic undo mode.
action: restart instance in Automatic Undo Management mode before retrying operation.

description: previously offlined undo tablespace '%s' is still pending
cause: the current operation is not allowed because an undo tablespace containing active transactions is pending from a previous SWITCH UNDO operation. The operation will be allowed again after all transactions in the previous undo tablespace are committed.
action: Wait for all previous transactions to commit before reissuing the current statement.

description: undo tablespace '%s' is already in use by this instance
cause: the specified undo tablespace is currently used by this instance. The operation failed.
action: If the specified undo tablespace name is wrong, reissue the statement with the correct name.

description: segment '%s' is not supported in %s Undo Management mode
cause: the type of the specified undo segment is incompatible with the current undo management mode of the instance.
action: Check the undo segment name and the undo management mode and reissue statement if necessary.

description: Create Rollback Segment failed, USN %s is out of range
cause: the system runs out of undo segment number. Too many undo segments exist.
action: drop some of the unused undo segments and retry operation.

description: Illegal rollback Segment operation in Automatic Undo mode
cause: This operation only allowed in Manual Undo mode.
action: restart instance in Manual Undo_Management mode and retry operation.

description: Operation not allowed on undo tablespace
cause: This operation is not allowed on undo tablespaces
action: Check the tablespace name and reissue command if necessary

description: Cannot create segments in undo tablespace
cause: Cannot create segments in undo tablespace
action: Check the tablespace name and reissue command

description: Duplicate undo tablespace specification
cause: Cannot create more than one undo tablespace during database creation
action: Modify the command to contain only one undo tablespace

description: Invalid specification for CREATE UNDO TABLESPACE
cause: You have specified an clause that should not used with CREATE UNDO TABLESPACE
action: Drop the clause from the command and reissue it.

description: DROP segment '%s' (in undo tablespace) not allowed
cause: Explicit DROP operation is not allowed on undo tablespace segments
action: Check the undo segment name and reissue statement if necessary.

description: Undo tablespace '%s' has unexpired undo with %s(sec) left, Undo_Retention=%s(sec)
cause: Tried to drop a tablespace that contains unexpired undo information
action: lower setting of UNDO_RETENTION or wait a while before reissue command to drop undo tablespace

description: Undo quota violation - failed to get %s (bytes)
cause: the amount of undo assigned to the consumer group of this session has been exceeded.
action: ask DBA to increase undo quota, or wait until other transactions to commit before proceeding.

description: Automatic Undo Management event for NTP testing
cause: test events for internal use only
action: none.

description: no active undo tablespace assigned to instance
cause: the current instance does not have an active undo tablespace assigned to execute transactions.
action: ask DBA to create an undo tablespace, online the undo tablespace and then retry operation.

description: suppress resumable related error message
cause: none
action: This event is to be used if the errors 30031 and 30032 wish to be suppressed.

description: the suspended (resumable) statement has been aborted
cause: DBA or the user aborted the execution of the suspended statement in the resumable session
action: none

description: the suspended (resumable) statement has timed out
cause: A correctible error was signaled in the resumable session and the error was not cleared within the timeout interval.
action: Fix the correctible error within the timeout. Default is 2 hours. Or increase the (resumable) timeout.
remediation: 1) Find the suspended statement and the error that suspended it: `SELECT session_id, instance_id, status, error_number, error_msg, suspend_time, sql_text FROM dba_resumable;` 2) The error_msg column names the real problem -- almost always a space error (ORA-01653, ORA-30036, ORA-01652). Fix that first. 3) Extend the resumable window if the fix legitimately takes longer: `ALTER SESSION ENABLE RESUMABLE TIMEOUT 7200;` or `ALTER SYSTEM SET resumable_timeout = 7200 SCOPE=BOTH;` 4) Set up notification so the next one is caught before it times out -- an AFTER SUSPEND trigger or an alert on dba_resumable.

description: Undo tablespace cannot be specified as default user tablespace
cause: It is incorrect to specify undo tablespace as default user tablespace

description: unable to extend segment by %s in undo tablespace '%s'
cause: the specified undo tablespace has no more space available.
action: Add more space to the undo tablespace before retrying the operation. An alternative is to wait until active transactions to commit.
remediation: 1) Check free space in the active undo tablespace: `SELECT tablespace_name, ROUND(SUM(bytes)/1024/1024) free_mb FROM dba_free_space WHERE tablespace_name = (SELECT value FROM v$parameter WHERE name = 'undo_tablespace') GROUP BY tablespace_name;` 2) Look for a long-running transaction pinning undo: `SELECT s.sid, s.serial#, s.username, t.used_ublk * 8192/1024/1024 mb, t.start_time FROM v$transaction t JOIN v$session s ON s.saddr = t.ses_addr ORDER BY mb DESC;` 3) Check retention pressure: `SELECT MAX(tuned_undoretention) tuned, MAX(maxquerylen) longest_query FROM v$undostat WHERE begin_time > SYSDATE - 1;` 4) Add space: `ALTER TABLESPACE <undo_ts> ADD DATAFILE '<path>' SIZE 8G AUTOEXTEND ON NEXT 512M MAXSIZE 32G;` 5) If RETENTION GUARANTEE is set, undo cannot be reused even when expired: `SELECT tablespace_name, retention FROM dba_tablespaces WHERE contents = 'UNDO';` Turning it off with `ALTER TABLESPACE <undo_ts> RETENTION NOGUARANTEE;` clears the error but trades it for ORA-01555 risk -- add space first if the guarantee was deliberate.

description: Cannot perform parallel insert on non-partitioned object

description: GLOBAL partitioned index on TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE not allowed
cause: try to GLOBAL partitioned index on TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.
action: Do not GLOBAL partitioned index on TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

description: TIME/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE literal must be specified in CHECK constraint
cause: User is trying to create a constraint on a time or timestamp with or without time zone column without explicitly specifying the time zone.
action: Use time or timestamp with time zone literals only.

description: invalid extract field for extract source
cause: The extract source does not contain the specified extract field.

description: cannot alter database time zone when the database contains TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE columns
cause: An attempt was made to alter the database time zone when there were tables containing TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE columns in the database.
action: Do not alter the database time zone when there are tables containing TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE columns. Alternatively, export the tables containing TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE columns and drop them before altering the database. Finally, re-import the dropped tables.

description: table created/altered with TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE not allowed at current DST upgrade stage
cause: An attempt was made to create or alter a table to have columns of TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE data type or user-defined data types involving TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE data type when DST upgrade is in BEGIN UPGRADE stage.
action: Re-issue create/alter table DDL after DBMS_DST.BEGIN_UPGRADE is complete.

description: imported table "%s"."%s" with TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE data is not ready for access
cause: An attempt was made to read or update an imported table with TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE data, which has not completed the import process through transportable tablespace mode.
action: Re-issue SQL statement after transportable tablespace import is complete.

description: affected TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE data is not allowed at current DST upgrade state

description: delete is not allowed on tables with triggers at current DST upgrade state

action: Reissue DML statement after the DST upgrade is complete with the table.

cause: A level name in a dimension ddl statement did not conform to SQL identifier rules.

description: JOIN KEY clause references a level not in this hierarchy
cause: The level name specified with the REFERENCES portion of a JOIN KEY clause in a dimension DDL statement does not reference a level in the hierarchy that contains the JOIN KEY clause.

cause: The level specified in the REFERENCES portion of a JOIN KEY clause in a dimension DDL statement does not have a child level.

cause: Multiple JOIN KEY clauses were specified for a given parent level in a dimension hierarchy.

action: Check the spelling of the hierarchy name.

description: a table name is required to qualify the column specification
cause: A table name was omitted in a column specification where where the column must be qualified by the table name.
action: Qualify the column with the table name.

description: ADD and DROP cannot both be specified
cause: One or more ADD clauses were found in the same ALTER DIMENSION statement with one or more DROP clauses.
action: Separate your ADD operations into one ALTER DIMENSION statement and your DROP operations into another.

description: specified dimension hierarchy does not exist
cause: A hierarchy name was encountered that is not defined within the dimension.
action: Check the spelling of the hierarchy name.

description: specified dimension attribute does not exist
cause: An attribute name was encountered that is not defined within the dimension.
action: Check the attribute name spelling.

description: query rewrite does not currently support this expression
cause: A complex expression was specified that is is not currently supported by query rewrite.
action: Reduce the complexity of the expression.

description: inconsistent numeric precision or string length
cause: The SELECT expression was of a different numeric precision or string length than the corresponding container column. Therefore, query rewrite cannot guarantee results that are identical to the results obtained with the un-rewritten query.
action: Correct the precision or string length difference, specify the WITH REDUCED PRECISION option, or disable the REWRITE option on the materialized view.

description: expression not supported for query rewrite
cause: The SELECT clause referenced UID, USER, ROWNUM, SYSDATE, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, MAXVALUE, a sequence number, a bind variable, correlation variable, a set result, a trigger return variable, a parallel table queue column, collection iterator, a non-deterministic date format token RR, etc.
action: Remove the offending expression or disable the REWRITE option on the materialized view.

description: Query rewrite not allowed on SYS relations
cause: A SYS relation was referenced in the select clause for a materialized view with query rewrite enabled.
action: Remove the reference to the SYS relation from the select clause or disable the REWRITE option on the materialized view.

description: materialized view container does not exist
cause: A DROP TABLE command was issued directly against the materialized view container table.
action: Use the DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW command to clean up the residual meta data for the materialized view. Then use the CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW statement to recreate the materialized view. Thereafter, use the DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW command rather than the DROP TABLE command to drop a materialized view.

description: the specified refresh method is not supported in this context
cause: The refresh method that was specified is not currently supported.
action: Specify a different refresh method or change the context to enable support of the chosen refresh method.

description: this PL/SQL function cannot be supported for query rewrite
cause: The statement referenced a PL/SQL function that is not marked DETERMINISTIC.
action: Perform one of the following actions: - Remove the use of the PL/SQL function. - Mark the PL/SQL function as DETERMINISTIC. - Disable the REWRITE option on the materialized view. The function should be marked DETERMINISTIC only if it always returns the same result value for any given set of input argument values, regardless of any database state or session state. Do not mark the function as DETERMINISTIC if it has any meaningful side-effects.

description: summary and materialized view are not in same schema
cause: An internal Oracle error occurred.
action: Report the problem through your normal support channels.

description: Query rewrite is not supported on SYS materialized views
cause: An attempt was made to enable the REWRITE option on a materialized view in the SYS schema.
action: Create the materialized view in a different schema or disable the REWRITE option.

description: REF not supported with query rewrite
cause: The statement contained a REF operator. Repeatable behavior cannot be guaranteed with the REF operator. Therefore, query rewrite cannot support the REF operator.
action: Remove the reference to the REF operator or disable the REWRITE option on the materialized view.

description: unrecognized string type
cause: An internal Oracle error occurred.
action: Report the problem through your normal support channels.

description: dimension column cannot be a sequence
cause: The dimension statement referenced a column that is a sequence.
action: Remove the reference to the sequence.

description: columns in a dimension column list must be in the same relation
cause: The dimension statement contained a column list where the columns are not all from the same relation.
action: Specify the list of columns using only columns from a single relation.

description: this level has the same set of columns as another
cause: The level definition contained the same set of columns as another level.
