cause: The argument to STARTOF or ENDOF was not a DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER, or YEAR dimension.
action: Use a DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER, or YEAR dimension argument.

description: (CGTDF01) The argument of the BEGINDATE or ENDDATE function must be dimensioned by exactly one time dimension.
cause: The argument must have exactly one dimension that has a type of DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER, or YEAR.
action: Correct the argument.

description: (CINSERT06) The target position for MAINTAIN ADD or MAINTAIN MOVE cannot fall in the range of session-only values.
cause: The user specified either a BEFORE or AFTER clause specifying a position in the range of SESSION dimension values.
action: Do not use a position clause, or specify a position before the first SESSION value.

description: (CINSERT02) The %j dimension is too large.
cause: The dimension has too many values.
action: Deleted values can still take up space in the dimension and cause this error. Try removing the deleted values by exporting the dimension to an EIF file, and then re-importing it with the REPLACE DELETE option.

description: (CINSERT07) You cannot add session-only values to the %j dimension.
cause: The user tried to add a SESSION dimension value while a spreadsheet cursor was open.
action: Try adding the SESSION value while the cursor is not active.

description: (CINSERT03) %a %j %ld The %1p dimension does not have a value numbered %2p.
cause: The dimension was not long enough to have this logical position.
action: Use OBJ(NUMVALS <dimension_name>) function to find the length of the dimension.

description: (CINSERT20) %a %j Custom member values cannot be added to concat dimension %1p, or to any of its bases, because it is not defined as UNIQUE.
cause: A non-UNIQUE CONCAT dimension was specified for the custom member values.
action: Use the CHGDFN command to change the CONCAT dimension to UNIQUE and retry.

description: (CINSERT04) %a %K %j %d %d %1p is not a valid value for the %2p dimension. Values for this dimension can have at most %3p significant digits after rounding to %4p decimal places.
cause: The user attempted to insert a value that had too many digits for a NUMBER dimension. For example, the user might have tried to insert the value 99999 (5 digits) into a dimension of data type NUMBER(4).
action: Use a smaller number for the dimension value, or define a new dimension with a larger precision and replace the old dimension with the new one.

description: (CINSERT05) %a %K %j %j %j %1p cannot be added to %2p because it is already a value of the dependent UNIQUE CONCAT DIMENSION %3p, from leaf DIMENSION %4p.
cause: The specified value could not be added to a DIMENSION because it conflicted with an existing value in a UNIQUE CONCAT DIMENSION that contained this DIMENSION.
action: The concats causing the conflict could be CHGDFNed to NOT UNIQUE, or either of the duplicate values could be renamed to make them UNIQUE.

description: (CMOVE03) cannot move a session-only dimension value
cause: An attempt was made to move a SESSION dimension value in the MAINTAIN MOVE command.
action: Do not movesession-only dimension values with the MAINTAIN MOVE command.

description: (CMOVE02) %a %j %ld The %1p dimension does not have a value at position %2p.
cause: An attempt was made to move a dimension value before or after a logical position that did not exist.
action: Choose a position between 1 and the number of values in the dimension.

description: (COLDEL01) %a %d %d The starting column must be between 1 and the maximum width of a text value (%1p). You cannot start removing at column %2p.
cause: There was an invalid starting column number.
action: Choose a valid starting column number from the range provided in the error message.

description: (COLDEL02) %a %d %d The columns to be removed must be between 1 and the maximum width of a text value (%1p). You cannot remove column %2p.
cause: The column number is invalid.
action: Choose a valid column number.

description: (COLDEL03) The number of columns to be removed must be greater than zero. %d columns cannot be removed.
cause: The number of columns was not a positive number.
action: Correct the number of columns.

description: (COLEXTR01) %a %d %d The starting column must be between 1 and the maximum width of a text value (%1p). %2p is out of range.
cause: The start argument was an invalid column number.
action: Use a positive integer with a maximum value specified in the error.

description: (COLEXTR02) %a %d %d The columns to be extracted must be between 1 and the maximum width of a text value (%1p). You cannot extract column %2p.
cause: The sum of start column and the number of columns exceeded the maximum width of a text value plus one.
action: Choose arguments that do not access columns greater than the maximum width of a text value.

description: (COLEXTR03) The number of columns to be extracted must be greater than or equal to zero. You cannot extract %d columns.
cause: The optional NUMCOLS argument to the EXTCOLS function was not a positive integer.
action: Either omit the optional argument or use a positive integer.

description: (COLINS01) %a %d %d The starting column must be between 0 and the maximum width of a text value (%1p). You cannot start inserting at column %2p.
cause: The starting argument was an invalid column number.
action: Use a positive integer with a maximum value specified in the error.

description: (COLREP01) %a %d %d The starting column must be between 1 and the maximum width of a text value (%1p). You cannot start replacing at column %2p.
cause: An invalid starting column number was specified.
action: Choose a valid starting column number from the range provided in the error message.

description: (COMPOSITE01) %j is a dimension composite and does not have position numbers that can be used in this context.
cause: This error is shared by commands and functions that require logical position numbers.
action: Do not use the name of a composite with this function or command.

description: (XSDPART51) %j is a PARTITION TEMPLATE and does not have position numbers that can be used in this context.
cause: An attempt was made to discover or supply the position number associated with a member of a PARTITION TEMPLATE.
action: Avoid referring to PARTITION TEMPLATE values by their position numbers.

description: (CRENAME01) %a %j %ld The %1p dimension does not have a value at position %2p.
cause: The logical position did not have a value between 1 and the number of values in the dimension.
action: Choose a valid logical position.

description: (CRENAME02) The %j dimension does not have identifiers that can be renamed.
cause: The values of this dimension could not be renamed.
action: None.

description: (CRENAME03) %a %K %j %j %1p is already a value of the dependent UNIQUE concat dimension %2p, from leaf dimension %3p.
cause: An attempt to rename a value in a dimension failed because the new value conflicted with an existing value in a unique concat dimension containing this dimension.
action: The concats causing the conflict could be CHGDFNed to NOT UNIQUE, or either of the duplicate values could be changed to make them UNIQUE.

description: (CTDDEL04) %a %j %d Deletions from time dimension %1p must occur at either end. %2p values were not deleted.
cause: A request to delete values in the middle of a time dimension was rejected.
action: Delete a range of values ending with the last value or starting with the first value.

description: (CTDINSRT00) You attempted to add a value that was outside the allowable range of dates for time dimension %j.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (CTXENG00) The CONTEXT name cannot be NA.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (CTXENG01) CONTEXT '%v' already exists.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (CTXENG02) CONTEXT '%v' does not exist.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (CTXENG03) %a %n %v %1p has not been saved in CONTEXT '%2p'.
cause: The object was not in the context.
action: Show CONTEXT('context-name') to see what is in the context.

description: (DIMSHOW01) Partition %v does not exist.
cause: The DIMSHOW command specified a nonexistent partition.
action: Specify the name of an existing partition, or remove the PARTITION qualification from the DIMSHOW command.

description: (DIMSHOW02) A partition name may be specified only for a partitioned variable.
cause: A PARTITION qualification was provided for an object other than a partitioned variable.
action: Remove the PARTITION qualification.

description: (DBERR01) Analytic workspace %s does not exist, or you do not have sufficient privileges to access it.
cause: The analytic workspace requested was not in the current database.
action: Check that you are in the correct schema and have access to the requested analytic workspace.

description: Could not create analytic workspace %s
cause: A serious error was encountered while trying to set up the tables for the named analytic workspace. Possible causes for this error include: - A tablespace that cannot be written to. - Corrupt metadata about which analytic workspace exist. - Table names that the code cannot use. - There are remains of a partially removed analytic workspace.
action: There should be another error on the error stack. Consult this error to determine what is causing the problem and remove that table.

description: (DBERR02) %a %s %s Analytic workspace %1p cannot be accessed because it has been damaged or belongs to an incompatible version of %2p.
cause: The attempt to attach the analytic workspace failed because the internal structures could not be interpreted. This could be because the analytic workspace was created by an incompatible version of the online analytical processing (OLAP) option.
action: Re-create the analytic workspace.

description: (DBERRBSZ) %a %s %d %d Analytic workspace %1p cannot be opened. Tablespace blocksize %2p does not match database cache size %3p.
cause: The blocksize of the containing tablespace did not match the database cache size.
action: Change either the size to make them consistent, or set the OLAP_PAGE_POOL_SIZE parameter to 0 to allow automatic OLAP pool management when the compatibility is later than Oracle Database release 10g version 10.2.

description: (DBERR03) %a %s %s Analytic workspace (AW) %1p cannot be accessed because it was last modified by an incompatible version of %2p.
cause: The online analytical processing (OLAP) code was unable to process the internal metadata for the specified AW when attaching the AW.
action: This is most commonly encountered when the AW was previously used on a different platform (for example, Windows 32-bit and Windows 64 bit). The AW must be re-created on the current platform.

description: (DBERRRLS) %a %s Analytic workspace %1p cannot be accessed because it has row-level access control applied to it.
cause: Attempted to access the specified analytic workspace's LOB table. The OLAP option detected the table has row-level security applied, and the option requires full access to this table to operate correctly.
action: Remove the row-level security and use the analytic workspace access control instead.

description: (DBERRTHW) Analytic workspace %s cannot be attached with the THAW option because it was frozen with the NOTHAW option.
cause: An attempt was made to attach the analytic workspace using the THAW // option. The analytic workspace was frozen using the NOTHAW option.
action: Attempt the command again without the THAW option.

description: error while operating on '%s'
cause: Creation of an analytic workspace for the specified object failed.
action: This error is always signaled with another error to provide more context. Resolve the error for the named object in order for the analytic workspace creation to succeed.

description: (DBERR05) Analytic workspace %s already exists.
cause: The AW CREATE command was passed the name of an analytic workspace that already exists
action: Specify a different name.

description: simulated paging error
cause: This is an internal error that should never be seen
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: (DBERR06) Analytic workspace %s cannot be opened. The analytic workspace index could not be found.
cause: An attempt to open the specified analytic workspace failed.
action: This error should not occur. Report this to Oracle Support.
params: 1) analytic_workspace_name: The name of the analytic workspace.

description: (XSCHKRLS01) Analytic workspace %s has open cursors and cannot be detached.
cause: A session attempted to detach an analytic workspace while there are cursors open against it.
action: Close the open cursor before attempting to close the analytic workspace.

description: (DBERR07) %a %s %s Timed out while trying to lock analytic workspace %1p for %2p.
cause: A lock operation that was supposed to happen very quickly was taking too long. It can be due to another session being stopped while holding that lock, another session crashing while holding that lock, or an internal error.
action: If another session is stopped, resume that session to let it release the lock. If another session has crashed, wait for a few minutes while a background process recovers the lock. Contact Support if none of the situations above apply.

description: Autonomous transaction query of an UPDATEd analytic workspace is not supported.
cause: Attempts to reference an analytic workspace that has uncommitted changes within an autonomous query.
action: Either COMMIT or ROLLBACK your changes, or don't use an autonomous transaction.

description: (DBERR08) Another user has analytic workspace %s attached.
cause: Attempted to rename, drop, or truncate an analytic workspace while it is in use by another user.
action: Repeat the command when the analytic workspace is not in use.

description: Analytic Workspace %s.%s could not be upgraded.
cause: A serious error was encountered while trying to alter the tables for the named analytic workspace. Possible causes for this error include: - A tablespace could not be written to. - The metadata for this analytic workspace may be corrupt. * Table names that the code cannot use. * There are remains of a partially removed analytic workspace.
action: There should be another error on the error stack. Consult this error to determine what is causing the problem and remove that table.

description: (DBERR09) Analytic workspace %s cannot be attached in RW or EXCLUSIVE mode until the changes made and updated in MULTI mode are committed or rolled back.
cause: There are changes to this analytic workspace that were updated and not committed when the workspace was attached in MULTI mode.
action: Either try attaching the workspace in RO or MULTI mode, or commit or roll back the transaction before trying to attach the workspace in RW or EXCLUSIVE mode.

description: (DBERRDDP) %a %s Analytic workspace %1p cannot be accessed because the AWLOB column has deduplication enabled.
cause: An attempt was made to access the specific LOB table of the analytic workspace. The OLAP option detected that the LOB column has deduplication enabled. The OLAP option does not support deduplication.
action: Alter the table to disable LOB deduplication.

description: (DBERR10) Analytic workspace %s cannot be attached in MULTI mode until the changes made and updated in RW or EXCLUSIVE mode are committed or rolled back.
cause: There were still changes to this analytic workspace that were updated and not committed when the workspace was attached in RW or EXCLUSIVE mode.
action: Either try attaching the workspace in RO, RW, or EXCLUSIVE mode or commit or roll back the transaction before trying to attach the workspace in MULTI mode.

description: Analytic workspace %s cannot be modified during a Data Guard rolling upgrade.
cause: Attempted to attach the specified analytic workspace for write while the instance was in the middle of a Data Guard rolling upgrade. The is unsupported by the OLAP option.
action: Delay the modifications until after the rolling upgrade completes.

description: (DBERR11) cannot wait for analytic workspace %s to become available since doing so would cause a deadlock.
cause: The attempt to attach the analytic workspace using the WAIT keyword caused a deadlock situation. The WAIT keyword is not allowed. This was an error in the application.
action: Attach the multiple analytic workspaces in the same order that they were locked to avoid deadlock if these analytic workspaces were locked at the same time.

description: (DBERR013) Analytic workspace %s cannot be opened. The temporary analytic workspace flag is set.
cause: An attempt to open the specified analytic workspace failed.
action: This error should not occur. Please report this to Oracle support.

description: (DBERR12) %a %s %s Analytic workspace %1p cannot be opened in MULTI mode before converting it by the latest version of %2p.
cause: The analytic workspace is stored in a format that is not compatible with multi mode.
action: Convert the analytic workspace to a later format using the DBMS_AW.CONVERT procedure.

description: This operation is not permitted on analytic workspaces.
cause: An attempt was made to directly modify the contents of a table containing an analytic workspace.
action: Do not modify the table directly; let the OLAP option modify it.

description: (DBERR14) The specified access mode for analytic workspace %s is invalid.
cause: An attempt was made to change the access status for the specified analytic workspace to an invalid value.
action: The only access modes accepted by the AW PROMOTE command are RW and RO, possibly with a WAIT or NOWAIT added.

description: This DDL operation is not allowed on table "%s"."%s".
cause: A DDL operation was attempted on an analytic workspace table.
action: No action required. Many DDL operations on analytic workspace tables are restricted to Oracle only.

description: (DBERR15) Another user has incompatible access to analytic workspace %s, and the wait timeout has expired.
cause: Attempt to access an analytic workspace conflicted with another user's access, and the timeout specified has elapsed.
action: Wait until the conflicting user is done.

description: The Flashback Table operation is not supported on OLAP analytic workspace tables.
cause: An attempt was made to perform the Flashback Table operation on a table containing an analytic workspace, which is not allowed.
action: Do not perform a Flashback Table operation on analytic workspace tables.

description: (DBERR17) Analytic workspace %s cannot be attached in the mode you requested because another user has it attached in an incompatible mode.
cause: The attempt to access an analytic workspace conflicted with another user's access, and no timeout was specified
action: Wait until the conflicting user is finished.

description: (DBERRSYNC) Analytic workspace %s cannot be attached RW until a RESYNC command has brought it up to the current generation.
cause: Another session has updated the analytic workspace since it was attached in the current session.
action: Use a RESYNC AW command to bring the analytic workspace up to the most recent version.

description: An attached analytic workspace is blocking this command.
cause: An attempt was made to drop a tablespace containing an analytic workspace that is currently attached.
action: Detach the analytic workspace before dropping the tablespace.

description: There are OLAP cubes and dimensions referencing an analytic workspace in the tablespace.
cause: An attempt was made to drop a tablespace containing an analytic workspace that is referenced by OLAP cube and dimension objects.
action: Drop the OLAP cube and dimension objects before dropping the tablespace.

description: (DBERR19) Analytic workspace %s cannot be created, deleted, or renamed while flashback mode is in effect.
cause: The session was operating under a flashback environment.
action: In order to create, rename, or delete an analytic workspace, the session must not be running in flashback.

description: (DBERR20) Analytic workspace %s cannot be opened. The analytic worksace is already open.
cause: An attempt to open the specified analytic workspace failed.
action: This error should not occur. Please report this to Oracle support.

description: (DBERR21) Analytic workspace %s can only be attached read-only (RO) while tablespace %s is READONLY.
cause: The underlying tablespace of the analytic workspace is in READONLY status.
action: Attach the analytic workspace in RO mode or alter the tablespace.

description: (DBERR22) %a %s %s Analytic workspace %1p cannot be opened because it was last modified by an incompatible version of %2p.
cause: The user attempted to attach an old OLAP Services analytic workspace that cannot be converted by this version of OLAP Services.
action: Either create a new analytic workspace or try using a version of OLAP Services compatible with the one that created this analytic workspace.

description: (AWUPG01) Analytic workspace %s is already in the newest format allowed by the current compatibility setting.
cause: You ran the DBMS_AW.CONVERT procedure on an analytic workspace that was created in or previously upgraded to the current compatibility mode.
action: If upgrading the analytic workspace is necessary, upgrade the database instance and then re-run DBMS_AW.CONVERT. If the new features offered by upgrading the analytic workspace are not required, then no action is needed.

description: (DBERR023) Analytic workspace %s cannot be opened. An unexpected error occurred.
cause: An attempt to open the specified analytic workspace failed.
action: This error should not occur. Please report this to Oracle support.

description: (DBERRPLAT) Analytic workspace %s encountered an error that may indicate that it was created on a different platform.
cause: An attempt to transport an analytic workspace from a different platform failed.
action: Transport the analytic workspace using a supported method, either by using export/import or by rebuilding it using an XML template.

description: An unsupported ALTER TABLE operation was attempted on analytic workspace table "%s"."%s".
cause: An attempt was made to modify an analytic workspace table using the ALTER TABLE statement. This statement is not supported.
action: The OLAP option manages the table.

description: (DBVALID01) SEVERE ERROR: Record %.0f multiply used.
cause: The AW VALIDATE command has detected an error in the structure of the analytic workspace. This error will result in the corruption of one or more objects.
action: Export what you can of the analytic workspace.

description: Creation of VPD, OLS, or FGA security policy is disallowed on OLAP analytic workspace table "%s"."%s".
cause: An attempt was made to create a Virtual Private Database (VPD), Oracle Label Security (OLS), or Fine-Grained Auditing (FGA) security policy on an analytic workspace table. These policies are not allowed to be applied to an analytic workspace table.
action: Do not apply a VPD, OLS, or FGA security policy on an analytic workspace table. Review using analytic workspace security features instead.
params: 1) owner_name: The name of the owner of the analytic workspace table. 2) table_name: The name of the analytic workspace table.

description: (DBVALID02) Note: Record %.0f was allocated but not used. This can result in wasted space.
cause: This was a benign message. The analytic workspace VALIDATE command found that an analytic workspace had some inaccessible space.
action: Either nothing, or export and re-create the analytic workspace.

description: (DBVALID06) Note: Record %.0f was allocated but not used. This can result in wasted space. (PS %ld)
cause: This is a benign message. The AW VALIDATE command found an analytic workspace has some inaccessible space.
action: Either nothing, or export and re-create the analytic workspace.

description: (DBVALID03) The AW VALIDATE command cannot be used with read-only analytic workspace %s.
cause: The AW VALIDATE command does not support read-only access.
action: Attach the analytic workspace read/write and try again.

description: Oracle OLAP analytic workspace table was renamed to an invalid name
cause: An attempt was made to rename an Oracle OLAP analytic workspace (AW) table to a name that did not start with \\"AW$\\" or that contained characters that may occur only in quoted identifiers which are not supported by Oracle OLAP DML.
action: Do not rename the Oracle OLAP AW table to an invalid name.

description: (DBVALID04) SEVERE ERROR: Record %.0f was used but not allocated.
cause: The AW VALIDATE command has detected a problem that will result in corruption of the analytic workspace in the future. There is no corruption yet.
action: Export and re-create the analytic workspace.

description: (DBVALID05) SEVERE ERROR: Record %.0f used but not allocated (PS %ld).
cause: The AW VALIDATE command has detected a problem that will result in corruption of the analytic workspace. There is no corruption yet.
action: Export and re-create the analytic workspace.

description: (DECIMAL) %a %d %d %d %d The number of decimal places must be between %2p and %3p, or %4p. It cannot be %1p.
cause: A value was specified for the DECIMALS option that was out of range.
action: Supply a value for DECIMALS that is within the range specified by the error message text.

description: The schema cannot be specified when renaming an analytic workspace.
cause: An attempt was made to rename an analytic workspace that was not in the user's schema. This is not allowed.
action: Connect as the owner of the analytic workspace to rename it or use DBMS_AW.AW_COPY to move it.

description: (DELDENT01) %n cannot be deleted while there are objects dimensioned by it, or formulas, programs, valuesets, or relations that use it.
cause: The dimension could not be deleted because the user did not construct a list of all the objects that depend on the dimension.
action: Delete this list of objects first.

description: (DELDENT05) %n cannot be deleted because it is the target of an external partition of a partitioned variable.
cause: User attempted to delete a variable, but some partitioned variable was defined to use that variable as the target of one of its external partitions.
action: DELETE the partitioned variable or CHGDFN DROP PARTITION the the external partition from the partitioned variable, then delete the target variable.

description: (DELDENT02) %n cannot be deleted while it is running.
cause: The object is either a PROGRAM or a FORMULA and could not be deleted.
action: Find out where the object is getting deleted, and edit the object to ensure that the deletion does not occur.

description: (XSDELDENTANON) %a %n %j You cannot delete %1p while looping over unnamed composite %2p.
cause: While looping over the named anonymous composite, an attempt was made to delete an object which is dimensioned by it.
action: Delete the object outside of a loop over the dimension.

description: (DELDENT03) You cannot delete %n because you do not have PERMIT permission for it or it is READONLY.
cause: READONLY is from Oracle, the PERMIT command may be controlled by someone within your company.
action: You are allowed to delete this object.

description: (DELDENT04) The variable %n cannot be deleted while the NA trigger is executing.
cause: The NA trigger was trying delete the variable.
action: Set the PRGTRACE = YES option to see how this happened.

description: (DNAMELEN00) %a %s %d The object name %1p has more than %2p characters.
cause: For analytic workspaces created prior to version 12.2 the maximum object name length is 64 characters.
action: If possible, update to version 12.2 or later. Object names maximum length, in version 12.2 and later, is 256 bytes.

description: (DOSCMD01) The current directory is %s.
cause: The user entered a CDA command with no arguments.
action: This is an informational message. No user action is required.

description: (DOSCMD02) Current directory alias is not set.
cause: A file name was specified without a directory component, and there was no current directory alias set to supply the missing directory name.
action: Use the CDA command to establish a current directory alias, or provide a file name with an explicit directory component.

description: (DSSEXIST01) Use the AW command to establish a current analytic workspace. Then start your current activity again.
cause: There is no currently active analytic workspace. The command that generated the error requires an active analytic workspace to operate on.
action: Run an AW ATTACH or AW CREATE command to establish an active workspace.

description: (DSSEXIST04) Analytic workspace %s is not attached.
cause: The specified analytic workspace was currently not attached to the session, or the name was misspelled.
action: Attach the analytic workspace with the AW ATTACH command, or correct the spelling of the name.

description: (DSSEXIST04A) Analytic workspace %t is not attached.
cause: The specified analytic workspace is currently not attached to the session, or the name is misspelled.
action: Attach the analytic workspace with the AW ATTACH command, or correct the spelling of the name .

description: (DSSEXIST05) You cannot specify the EXPTEMP analytic workspace.
cause: The command requires a permanent analytic workspace to operate on.
action: Specify an analytic workspace other than EXPTEMP.

description: You cannot detach analytic workspace (AW) %s. It is in use by an API branch.
cause: The OLAP API is in a branch, and you are not allowed to detach the AW while the branch is active.
action: End the branch before detaching the AW.

cause: Space or separation character was missing.

description: (DTINFRMT10) '%v' is not a valid VNF format because at least two of the specifications are of the same type.

description: (DTINFRMT11) '%v' is not a valid VNF format because it does not contain enough fields to match one of the defined VNF templates.

cause: NA

description: (DTTOVC01) Unable to print dates longer than %d characters.
cause: The date value exceeded 128 bytes.
action: Contact Oracle Support to request a larger buffer size in a patch or a future release.

description: (DUPCLCHK01) %j appears more than once in the dimension list.
cause: There was a duplicate entry of a dimension name at the top level of the dimension list.
action: Remove the duplicate entry.

description: (DUPCLCHK02) %a %j %j %1p appears more than once in the dimension list. (It is also a base dimension of %2p.)
cause: The dimension appeared once at the top level of the dimension list and also appeared somewhere further down in a conjoint or a composite.
action: Remove either the dimension itself or the conjoint that contains it from the dimension list.

description: (DUPCLCHK03) %a %j %j %j %1p and %2p cannot both appear in a dimension list because they share at least one base dimension (%3p).
cause: Duplicate base dimensions were specified. This is not allowed.
action: This is a complex problem that can only be resolved by the application developer.

cause: The maximum number of dimensions was exceeded. If the maximum is 32 dimensions, then this is a limit enforced by AGGREGATE. Otherwise, the maximum should be 256 dimensions.

cause: An object with the given name was found in both the EIF file and the current analytic workspace.
action: Rename the object in the analytic workspace that is causing the name conflict. If the object named in the error message belongs to a cube or a cube dimension, rename that cube or cube dimension.

description: (EIFEXPRT08) SCATTER type %q must be a text variable with the same dimension as the name.
cause: NA

description: (EIFEXPRT10) The SCATTER type value must be INTEGER, SHORTINTEGER, SHORT, or DECIMAL, not %v.
cause: An attempt was made to specify a non-numeric SCATTER type value.
action: Ensure that the SCATTER value is of type INTEGER, SHORTINTEGER, SHORT, or DECIMAL.

description: (EIFEXPRT11) The scatter name value %v is not a valid EIF object name.

cause: An attempt was made to specify FULLMAPID or RELATIVEMAPID syntax with the NOAPI option.
action: Either specify the API option instead of NOAPI, or remove the FULLMAPID or RELATIVEMAPID option.

cause: Used in formatting output for the LIST option of EXPORT

description: (EIFMAKEF04) %a %s %d %s Due to insufficient disk space, the extension count of the EIF files(s) could not be recorded. To avoid any potential errors when the file is imported, DO NOT move, delete, or rename any of the EIF extension files. These are files of the form %1p.%3p, where %3p is the extension number. There are %2p such files.
cause: NA

description: (EIFMAKEF05) %a %n %d %1p cannot be exported because EIFVERSION is set to %2p, and objects cannot have more than 6 dimensions in that version.

description: (EIFMAKEF15) CAUTION: Exporting NTEXT objects using %s for the EIF file character set can cause loss of data. To preserve all NTEXT data, export using the UTF8 character set for the EIF file.
cause: The user exported an object with data type NTEXT, but the EIF file that will result from the EXPORT command is not written in Unicode. Because no non-Unicode file can represent all possible Unicode data, it is possible that some data will be lost when converting from the Unicode NTEXT object to the EIF file. The EIF file will be written in the character set indicated by the "nls_charset" argument of the EXPORT command, or, if no such argument is present, in the database character set.
action: If the user is certain that the contents of the NTEXT object can be represented in the specified character set, then no action is necessary. Otherwise, the user can add "nls_charset 'UTF8'" to the EXPORT command string. This will result in the EIF file being written in UTF8 Unicode, which can represent all the data contained in NTEXT objects.

description: (EIFMAKEF06) %a %s %d The expression named %1p cannot be exported because EIFVERSION is set to %2p, and objects cannot have more than 6 dimensions in that version.
cause: NA

description: (EIFMAKEF16) CAUTION: NTEXT object %n will be exported with type TEXT.
cause: User attempted to export an object whose data type is NTEXT, but but the EIFVERSION option indicates a version of Express / Oracle OLAP that does not support the NTEXT data type. The object will be exported as a TEXT object instead.

description: (EIFMAKEF09) %a %s %d %d You cannot use the name %1p, because EIFVERSION is set to %2p. That version does not allow object names longer than %3p bytes.
cause: The object name was too long for the analytic workspace format represented by the current setting of the EIFVERSION option.
action: Change the value of the EIFVERSION option, or remove the object from the list of objects to be exported.

description: (EIFMAKEF09A) %a %s %d %d You cannot use the name %1p, because EIFVERSION is set to %2p. That version does not allow object names longer than %3p characters.
cause: The object name was too long for the analytic workspace format represented by the current setting of the EIFVERSION option.
action: Change the value of the EIFVERSION option, or remove the object from the list of objects to be exported.

cause: NA

cause: NA

description: (EQUPDATE01) The expression for formula %j contains invalid syntax.
cause: The formula had a syntax error.

cause: NA
action: NA

description: (ESDREAD14) %a %j %s Discarding compiled code for %1p because analytic workspace %2p is not attached.
cause: A program used an analytic workspace name in a qualified object name. The named analytic workspace was not attached at program run time.
action: No action is necessary. The program will be automatically recompiled. It is likely that the recompile will fail with an appropriate exception code, in which case the signaled condition should be corrected and the program rerun.

description: (ESDREAD02) %a %j %v Discarding compiled code for %1p because %2p could not be found.
cause: NA

description: (ESDREAD15) %a %j %j %j Discarding compiled code for %1p because %2p and %3p, which were not partition-dependent when the code was compiled, are now partition-dependent.
cause: Two variables are partition-dependent if they share any external partition target variables, or if one is the target of an external partition of the other. If object names referred to non-partition-dependent variables at compile time but refer to partition-dependent variables in the runtime context, the OLAP DML program, formula, or model will be automatically recompiled.
action: None.

description: (ESDREAD03) %a %j %v %s Discarding compiled code for %1p because %2p is now a %3p. It was another kind of object when the code was compiled.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (ESDREAD16) %a %j %j %j Discarding compiled code for %1p because %2p and %3p, which were partition-dependent when the code was compiled, are now not partition-dependent.
cause: Two variables are partition-dependent if they share any external partition target variables, or if one is the target of an external partition of the other. If object names referred to partition-dependent variables at compile time but refer to non-partition-dependent variables in the runtime context, the OLAP DML program, formula, or model will be automatically recompiled.
action: None.

description: (QFGET01) %a %d %s Duplicate files found for extension number %1p of EIF file %2p.
cause: IMPORT searched the directories specified in EIFEXTENSIONPATH and found two EIF extension files with the same name (differing at most by the case used in the final name component).
action: Delete, rename or move any files that are not to be read by IMPORT.

description: (QFGET02) %a %ld %d " %1p bytes read in %2p seconds."
cause: Used in formatting output for the LIST option of IMPORT.
action: None.

description: (QFGET03) %a %d %s Extension number %1p is missing for EIF file %2p.
cause: IMPORT searched the directories specified in the EIFEXTENSIONPATH option and could not find the appropriately numbered extension file.
action: Move the missing file into one of the searched directories.

description: (QFHEAD00) File %s is not in EIF format.
cause: This was not an EIF file. It could not be imported with the EIF specification.
action: Unless this file has been damaged in some way and can be restored from backup, it is likely that this was never an EIF file.

description: (QFHEAD06) %a %s %s %s EIF file %1p cannot be imported because analytic workspace %2p has not been upgraded to version %3p.
cause: An attempt was made to import from an EIF file that was created by a newer version of the product into an analytic workspace that was created by an older version of the product.
action: Ensure that the compatibility mode parameter in the initialization parameter file of the importing instance specifies a version that is at least as high as the parameter was in the exporting instance. Then, convert the analytic workspace to the latest storage format and reexecute the import command. Alternatively, change the EIFVERSION option of the exporting instance to a lower number, re- create the EIF file, and import the new file.

description: (QFHEAD02) %a %s %s EIF file %1p cannot be read by this version of %2p.
cause: The EIF file was created with an internal version number indicating that it may contain objects that are not compatible with the current Oracle Online Analytical Processing (Oracle OLAP) version, or the EIF file was in an obsolete format.
action: If possible, set EIFVERSION in the exporting instance to a lower number, re-create the EIF file, and import the new file.

description: (QFHEAD04) %a %s %s CAUTION: The textual data in EIF file %1p is encoded in a character set that is not recognized by this version of %2p.
cause: IMPORT did not recognize the character set specification in the EIF file.
action: Check the imported text data. If it was not imported correctly, re-create the EIF file with a character set supported by the current Oracle Database version.

description: (QFHEAD05) An EIF extension file header for %s is not in the correct format.
cause: An EIF extension file in a multi-file IMPORT did not contain the correct header information.
action: Ensure that EIFEXTENSIONPATH is set correctly and that all of the extension files for the current IMPORT were created by the same EXPORT command as the main EIF file.

description: (QFOBJECT01) %a %s %s You cannot rename dimensions when you import them. The %1p dimension cannot be imported as %2p.
cause: An attempt was made to rename a dimension during IMPORT. Renaming of dimension during IMPORT is not allowed.
action: Do not attempt to rename the dimension during import.

description: (QFOBJECT02) You cannot import changes to the %n program now, because it is currently running.
cause: An attempt to change a program while it was running failed.
action: Find out where this import is called from and move it somewhere else.

description: (QFOBJECT06) CAUTION: %s is being imported. However, this is a reserved word, so the new object must be renamed before it can used.
cause: An attempt was made to import a reserved word. New reserved words are rarely added to this product but, when they are, this conflict is encountered.
action: Rename the object.

description: (XSMXAGGR07) %a %d %d When using the COUNTVAR clause, the number of variables to be aggregated (%1p) must match the number of COUNTVAR variables (%2p).
cause: The user specified a COUNTVAR clause to the AGGREGATE command, but the number of COUNTVAR variables specified did not match the number of variables to be aggregated

description: (XSAGGCNTPROP) %a %n Variable %1p cannot have both an AGGCOUNT and the $COUNTVAR property.
cause: An attempt was made to add the $COUNTVAR property to a variable which already had an AGGCOUNT, or vice versa.
action: Delete the already existing $COUNTVAR property or AGGCOUNT first.

description: (XSMXAGGR08) %n is not a VARIABLE.
cause: An attempt was made to perform an AGGREGATE or other action on an object which is not a variable.
action: Specify a variable instead.

description: (XSAGGRFORM) %j is not a valid AGGMAP for aggregating a FORMULA.
cause: The user attempted to aggregate a FORMULA using an AGGMAP that is not valid for aggregating FORMULAs. The AGGMAP must specify PRECOMPUTE(NA) for all relation lines and must not specify any caching.
action: Correct the AGGMAP so that it is valid for aggregating a FORMULA.

description: (XSMXAGGR10) %a %n %n COUNTVAR variable %1p must have the same dimensionality as %2p
cause: The user specified a COUNTVAR variable which is missing at least one dimension of the aggregation variable
action: Specify a COUNTVAR variable which has at least as many base dimensions as the aggregation variable

description: (XSMXAGGR12) %a %s %n The data type of the WEIGHT %2p must be numeric or BOOLEAN, not %1p.
cause: The user specified a WEIGHT variable or formula which wasn't numeric or boolean

description: (XSAGGR01) To be used with AGGREGATE, AGGMAP %j must be declared with the AGGMAP command.
cause: The user used the ALLOCMAP command to define the AGGMAP, so the AGGMAP can only be used with the ALLOCATE command, or the AGGMAP has no contents attached to it.
action: Use the AGGMAP command to define the AGGMAP.

description: (XSNOAGM) %a %n No AGGMAP was specified for VARIABLE %1p.
cause: The user used the AGGREGATE command without specifying an AGGMAP on the command line, with a variable which had no $AGGMAP property.
action: Specify an AGGMAP on the AGGREGATE command line, or add the $AGGMAP property to the variable in question.

description: (XSAGGR08) AGGREGATE cannot function because there is a permission clause associated with variable %n.
cause: When using AGGREGATE, only simple permissions and permissions on base dimensions are valid.
action: Remove the permissions clause from the variable causing problems.

description: A VARIABLE cannot have both the $AGGREGATE_FROM and $AGGREGATE_FROMVAR properties applied to it.
cause: The user attempted to add both the $AGGREGATE_FROM and $AGGREGATE_FROMVAR properties to a single variable.

action: Add a position for the variable in the measure dimension.

description: (XSAGGR10) You do not have sufficient permissions for the variable %n.

action: Remove the restricting permissions from the variable or base dimension.

description: (XSAGGR11) %j does not have any AGGCOUNT information.
cause: User attempted an operation (such as the AVERAGE aggregation operator or the AGGCOUNT function) that requires a variable to have AGGCOUNT information on a variable that does not.
action: Define the variable using the WITH AGGCOUNT clause, or use the CHGDFN ADD AGGCOUNT command to enable AGGCOUNT for the variable.

description: (XSAGGR12) You must use a COUNTVAR when aggregating with AVERAGE.

description: (XSAGOP04N) %a %j %s In AGGMAP %1p, the NAOPERATOR %2p must be HFIRST, HLAST or HEVEN.
cause: An invalid NAOPERATOR was specified.

description: (XSAGOP04R) %a %j %s In AGGMAP %1p, REMOPERATOR %2p must be MIN, MAX, FIRST, LAST, HFIRST or HLAST.
cause: An invalid REMOPERATOR was specified.

description: (XSAGOP05N) %a %j %s %s In AGGMAP %1p, you can only specify NAOPERATOR %3p with the PROPORTIONAL or EVEN operators, not %2p.

description: (XSAGOP06) %a %j %s In AGGMAP %1p, you can only specify the MIN, MAX, FLOOR, and CEILING arguments while using the PROPORTIONAL operator, not %2p.

description: (XSOPARM01) A DIMENSION must have a data type (ID, TEXT, or INTEGER), a time period, or a list of bases for a conjoint dimension.

description: (XSLPDSC01) All dimensions in LIST %d are also in the IGNORE clause.
cause: One of the dimension lists in the dimension loop descriptor had no base dimensions except those in the IGNORE list. This leaves no dimensions for looping over.
action: Fix the dimension loop descriptor.

description: (XSLPDSC02) %a %d %d LIST %1p and LIST %2p have different base dimensions.
cause: The base dimensions of the dimension lists given in the loop descriptor do not match.
action: Ensure that each dimension list has the same set of looping base dimensions. If necessary, use IGNORE within a lists to discard base dimensions that should not be looped.

description: (XSLPDSC03) duplicate IGNORE or DENSE information for dimension %j
cause: An IGNORE or DENSE list in a dimension loop descriptor included the dimension twice, included two different valuesets of the dimension, or includes the dimension and a valueset of the dimension.
action: Only use the dimension or a valueset of the dimension once in an IGNORE or DENSE list.

description: (XSLPDSC04) object %q in IGNORE or DENSE list has illegal type
cause: An IGNORE or DENSE list in a dimension loop descriptor included and object that was not a dimension or a valueset, was a conjoint dimension, or was a dimensioned valueset.
action: Only use simple dimensions and undimensioned valuesets in the IGNORE or DENSE list.

description: (XSLPDSC05) %j is not a loop dimension
cause: An IGNORE or DENSE list in a dimension loop descriptor referenced a dimension (or a valueset of a dimension) that was not a base dimension of the loop dimension list.
action: Remove the dimension or valueset from the IGNORE or DENSE list.

description: (XSLPDSC06) A LOOP AGGMAP list must contain an aggmap object, followed by one or more variables and/or dimensions.
cause: An invalid AGGMAP list was specified. Either to few objects were specified, or an incorrect type of object was used.
action: Specify a valid AGGMAP list consisting of an aggmap object, followed by one or more variables and/or dimensions.

description: (XSLPDSC07) The syntax of the $LOOP property on formula %n is incorrect.
cause: Unrecognized contents in the $LOOP property of a formula in the table function measure list.
action: Restrict the contents of the $LOOP property to valid elements (other than OPTIMIZED and MEASURES) of the table function LOOP directive.

description: (XSANALYZ00) object %n cannot be used in the ANALYZE command
cause: An object that cannot be analyzed was used in the ANALYZE command.
action: Analyze VARIABLES, RELATIONS, DIMENSIONS, or SURROGATES.

description: (XSANALYZ01) object %n cannot be used in the INHIERARCHY clause
cause: An invalid INHIERARCHY object was referenced.
action: Use either a VALUESET or boolean VARIABLE.

description: (XSANALYZ02) a level list was specified when a language dimension was present
cause: A level list dimension was specified when a language dimension was present.
action: Remove the USING clause.

description: (XSANALYZ03) the dimensionality of object %n does not match the ANALYZE command
cause: The dimensionality of the object did not match the ANALYZE command syntax used.
action: Match the ANALYZE syntax to the dimensionality of the specified object.

description: (XSANALYZ04) all objects in the current status of the NAME dimension must have the same dimensionality when used with the ANALYZE command
cause: The dimensionality of at least one of the objects listed in the NAME dimension does not match the rest of the objects.
action: Make sure all objects listed in the NAME dimension have the same dimensionality.

description: (XSANALYZ06) the AW format must be 11.0.0.0 or higher to use the ANALYZE command
cause: The AW version is less than 11.0.0.0
action: Make sure the compatible mode is 11.0.0.0 or higher and upgrade the AW

description: (XSANALYZ07) %a %s %s analytic workspace %1p.%2p must be attached RW or EXCLUSIVE mode
cause: The analytic workspace was already attached RO or MULTI mode.
action: Detach the analytic workspace.

description: (XSANALYZ08) %a %s %s object %1p.%2p does not exist
cause: The object name does not exist
action: Check the spelling and case of the object name

description: (XSAGINFO00) When the AGGMAPINFO function is called, %n must be an AGGMAP.
cause: The AGGMAPINFO function was called with an object that is not an AGGMAP.
action: Modify the call to AGGMAPINFO to specify an AGGMAP object.

description: (XSAGHIERPART00) %a %J %J %j Aggregating from partition %1p to partition %2p over hierarchy %3p creates an increase in sparsity.
cause: In the partition creation / aggmap creation a situation developed such that when aggregating over a particular dimension of the aggmap a partition boundary was crossed such that the sparsity of the target partition included dimensions that were not in the sparsity of the source partition. Since the process of aggregation always densifies rather than sparsifying this is an extremely suboptimal design and it is not supported by the aggregate system.
action: Set up your partitioning such that for any partition boundary the source and target partitions of the aggregation will always move towards denser partitions. For any child (c) and any parent (p) where (c) and (p) are in different partitions it must be the case that the parent partition contains no dimension in the composite that the child partition does not contain in its composite.

description: (XSAGPARTDEP00) %a %J %J Can not Aggregate PARTITION TEMPLATE %1p because the path of aggregation would recursively enter partition %2p.
cause: The partitioning scheme was such that while aggregating there exists a cell (m) such that both one of its descendants and one of its ancestors are both in the referenced partition, while (m) is in a different partition.
action: Change the partitioning scheme.

cause: AGGREGATION specified a valueset of a dimension not listed in a DIMENSION statement for the current model.
