description: (SNSYN200) Invalid CLEAR command syntax.
cause: The format of the CLEAR command was incorrect.
action: Correct the syntax and try again. The format of the CLEAR command is: CLEAR [ ALL | STATUS ] [ AGGREGATES | CHANGES | PRECOMPUTES | NONPRECOMPUTES | CACHE ] FROM var1 [var2, var3...] [USING aggmap]. For more information, consult Oracle documentation.

description: (SNSYN272) invalid AGGREGATION function syntax
cause: The format of the AGGREGATION function syntax was invalid.
action: Correct the syntax and try again. The format of the AGGREGATION function syntax is AGGREGATION(dimension-value [dimension-value ...]) [OPERATOR operator-name [WEIGHT | WEIGHTBY weight-var]]. For more information, consult Oracle documentation.

description: (SNSYN338) invalid TRUNC function syntax
cause: The format of the TRUNC function syntax was invalid.
action: Correct the syntax and try again. The format of the TRUNC function syntax is TRUNC(expression1 [, expression2]). For more information, consult Oracle documentation.

description: (SNSYN339) invalid CEIL function syntax
cause: The format of the CEIL function was invalid.
action: Correct the syntax and try again. The format of the CEIL function is: CEIL(number) For more information, consult Oracle documentation.

description: (SNSYN340) invalid FLOOR function syntax
cause: The format of the FLOOR function syntax was invalid.
action: Correct the syntax and try again. The syntax for the FLOOR function is FLOOR(number). For more information, consult Oracle documentation.

description: (SNSYN341) Invalid ADD_MONTHS function syntax.
cause: The format of the ADD_MONTHS function was incorrect.
action: Correct the syntax and try again. The format of the ADD_MONTHS function is ADD_MONTHS (date, number of months). For more information, consult Oracle documentation.

description: (SNSYN342) Invalid LAST_DAY function syntax.
cause: The format of the LAST_DAY function was incorrect.
action: Correct the syntax and try again. The format of the LAST_DAY function is: LAST_DAY(date). For more information, consult Oracle documentation.

description: (SNSYN343) Invalid MONTHS_BETWEEN function syntax.
cause: The format of the MONTHS_BETWEEN function was incorrect.
action: Correct the format and try again. The format of the MONTHS_BETWEEN function is: MONTHS_BETWEEN(date, date). For more information, consult Oracle documentation.

description: (SNSYN344) invalid NEW_TIME function syntax
cause: The format of the NEW_TIME function was invalid.
action: Correct the syntax and try again. The format of the NEW_TIME function is: NEW_TIME(date, zone, new zone). For more information, consult Oracle documentation.

description: (SNSYN345) The format of the NEXT_DAY function is: NEXT_DAY(date, day name)
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XPROPEN01) %a %j %d %d Discarding compiled code for %1p because it was compiled with code version %2p. The current code version is %3p.
cause: Informational message from formula compilation.
action: Set COMPILEWARN off if you do not want to see this message.

description: (XSAGZERO) AGGREGATE attempted to divide by zero. Set DIVIDEBYZERO to YES if you want NA to be returned as the result of a division by zero.
cause: A calculation in the current AGGREGATE command attempted to divide by zero as a result of an AVERAGE, WAVERAGE, HAVERAGE or HWAVERAGE operation.
action: Either fix the data, or set DIVIDEBYZERO to YES to return NA instead of signaling an error.

description: (XSPARTCHECK00) Object %n must be an AGGMAP.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XSPARTCHECK01) Object %n must be a PARTITION TEMPLATE.
cause: The second argument to PARTITIONCHECK was not the name of a partition template.
action: Specify a partition template name.

description: (XSAGPARTDEP01) %a %v %v %J Can not aggregate from PARTITION %1p into PARTITION %2p due to increasing sparsity along DIMENSION %3p.
cause: The user is attempting to use partitions as a means of sparsity control, however they have set up their partitions in a manner that simply makes no sense. It is a simple fact that during aggregation data becomes more dense, not less dense, and yet their partitions indicate the opposite.
action: Modify the partition template add the specified dimension into the source composite, or removing it from the target composite.

description: (XSMXCLEA02) When using CLEAR with the PRECOMPUTES or NONPRECOMPUTES options, you must specify an AGGMAP.
cause: The user did not specify the name of an AGGMAP with the CLEAR command.
action: Specify an aggmap by adding a USING phrase to the CLEAR command, or attach a '$AGGMAP' property to the variable.

description: (XSMXCLEA03) When using the AGGREGATES, CHANGES or CACHE options, specify the ALL keyword.
cause: The ALL keyword was not specified when using the AGGREGATES, CHANGES or CACHE options.
action: Specify the ALL keyword.

description: (XSMXCLEA04) %a %n When using CLEAR on the AGGMAP %1p, CACHE is the only valid directive.
cause: An attempted was made to CLEAR an AGGMAP using a directive other than CACHE.
action: Change the CLEAR command so that only the CACHE keyword is used for AGGMAP.

description: (XSMXCLEA05) To CLEAR ALL AGGREGATES from %n, specify an AGGMAP.
cause: The CLEAR command could not determine how the variable was aggregated because the variable was not dimensioned by a compressed composite.
action: Specify an AGGMAP by adding a USING clause to the CLEAR command, or attach a $AGGMAP property to the variable.

description: (XSSPROPNA) The value of property %s cannot be NA.
cause: The user tried to set a system-reserved property on an OLAP object to NA
action: Set the property to a non-NA value

description: (XSSPROP01) Property name '%v' is invalid because only system-reserved property names can begin with '$'.
cause: The user attempted to add a property which starts with $ but is not a reserved property name
action: Remove the $ from the property name

description: (XSSPROPDTYPE) %a %s %s The data type of property %1p must be %2p.
cause: The user tried to set a system-reserved property on an OLAP object to a value with an illegal datatype
action: Set the property with the proper datatype

description: (XSSPROP02) %q is not a valid variable name.
cause: Not a valid variable name
action: Change to a valid variable name

description: (XSSPROPOTYPE) %a %s %s Property %1p may only be applied to objects of type %2p.
cause: The user applied a reserved property name to an incorrect object type
action: Apply the property to the correct object

description: (XSSPROP03) The property '$%s' requires a leading "$" because it is a system-reserved property name.
cause: The user tried to specify a property name which is reserved, but did not use a leading $
action: Either add a leading $ or choose another property name

description: (XSBADSPROP) %a %s %n %v %3p is an illegal value for system-reserved property %1p on %2p.
cause: The user tried to specify an illegal value for a special property
action: Specify a legal value.

description: (XSSPROP04) %a %s Property %1p cannot be applied to an undimensioned (scalar) TEMPORARY variable.
cause: The user applied a reserved property name to an incorrect object type
action: Apply the property to the correct object

description: (XSSPROP05) Property ignored for object %n:
cause: A property was ignored during import.
action: Refer to the message that follows this one and correct the error it describes.

description: (VCACHE00) '%v' is an invalid value for the VARCACHE option. The only permissible values are 'SESSION', 'VARIABLE', and 'NONE'.
cause: The user tried to assign an invalid value to the VARCACHE option
action: Assign one of the valid values

description: (VCACHE03) '%v' is an invalid value for the $VARCACHE property. The only permissible values are 'DEFAULT', 'SESSION', 'VARIABLE', and 'NONE'.
cause: The user tried to assign an invalid value to the $VARCACHE property on a variable
action: Assign one of the valid values

description: (XSAGHOVERFLOW) The depth of the hierarchies encountered while processing a composite dimension in AGGREGATE caused a counter overflow.
cause: The depth of the hierarchies that are part of a composite exceeded 4 billion levels during the merge.
action: Reduce the number of levels in the hierarchies, reduce the number of dimensions in the composite, or do not aggregate over all dimensions at once.

description: (XSLMS00) Unable to locate a message file for Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) message %k.
cause: An internal OLAP program in the EXPRESS Analytic Workspace failed to retrieve a user message.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: (XSLMS01) invalid OLAP message number: %k
cause: An internal OLAP DML program in the EXPRESS Analytic Workspace attempted to retrieve a nonexistent message.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: (XSAGMODHIER01) %a %j %j There is a cycle formed by MODEL %1p and other embedded or containing models with the same dimension, %2p.
cause: Inclusion of a dynamic model formed a cycle in the named dimension.
action: Edit the models involving this dimension to remove the cycle.

description: (XSAGMODHIER02) %a %j There is a self-cycle equation in MODEL %1p.
cause: The model for relation modification included a self-cycle equation.
action: Remove the self-cycle equation from the model.

description: (XSAGMODDIM00) %j is not a valid dynamic model for AGGMAP.
cause: The model failed one of the following tests: 1) only one dimension (aside from LAG/LEAD dimensions); 2) assignment to dimension values only; 3) a single simple solution block; 4) no time-series functions with variable step values.
action: Edit the model so that it conforms to the above requirements.

description: (XSAGMODDIM01) MODEL %j cannot find the matching embedded model.
cause: AGGMAP ADD model could not find the matching embedded model.
action: Add the matching embedded model to the AGGMAP.

description: (XSAGMODDIM02) %a %j %j You cannot AGGREGATE the individual partition using static model %1p because a partition dimension or its deriver %2p appears in the equation of the step or simultaneous block.
cause: An attempt was made to AGGREGATE the individual partition using the static model with the partition dimension in the equation of the step or simultaneous block.
action: AGGREGATE the variable instead of the individual partition.

description: (XSAGMODLIST00) %a %j %n %2p cannot be added to the AGGMAP %1p because it is not a valid MODEL.
cause: An object specified in AGGMAP ADD was not a model.
action: Specify the name of a model.

description: (XSAGMODLIST02) %a %j %n MODEL %2p was skipped because there is already a MODEL by that name attached to AGGMAP %1p.
cause: An attempt was made to add the same model to the AGGMAP twice.
action: None required.

description: (XSAGMODLIST03) %a %j %n MODEL %2p could not be added to AGGMAP %1p.
cause: The dimension of the model did not match a hierarchy of the aggmap.
action: Add a RELATION statement to the AGGMAP for that dimension.

description: (XSDUNION00) An empty base dimension list was specified in the concat dimension definition.
cause: An empty concat dimension list was specified.
action: Specify a valid list of dimensions when defining a concat dimension.

description: (XSDUNION01) The concat dimension %n is not currently defined as UNIQUE.
cause: An attempt was made to CHGDFN a concat dimension, which was already non-unique, to NOT UNIQUE.
action: Since the concat dimension is already non-unique, this command is unnecessary.

description: (XSDUNION02) INTEGER dimension %j cannot be used as a concat dimension base.
cause: The user cannot specify INTEGER base dimensions when defining a concat dimension.
action: Change the datatype of the INTEGER base dimension, or omit it from the concat.

description: (XSDUNION03) The base dimension %j has an invalid data type for use in a UNIQUE concat definition.
cause: Base dimensions of a unique concat must have TEXT or ID data types.
action: Specify a valid list of dimensions when defining a unique concat dimension.

description: (XSDUNION04) The unique concat dimension %n cannot be changed to NOT UNIQUE, because it is a base of at least one other unique concat dimension.
cause: A non-unique concat dimension could not be used as a base of a dependent unique concat.
action: Run the CHGDFN command to change the definition of any dependent unique concat dimensions to NOT UNIQUE and retry.

description: (XSDUNION05) %a %j The concat dimension cannot be defined as UNIQUE because it has a non-unique concat base dimension %1p.
cause: A non-unique concat dimension could not be used as a base for a dependent unique concat.
action: Using the CHGDFN command, change any non-unique concat base dimensions to be UNIQUE and retry.

description: (XSDUNION17) %a %j %j Concat dimension %1p cannot be changed to UNIQUE because it has a non-unique concat base dimension %2p.
cause: A non-unique concat dimension was used as a base for a dependent unique concat.
action: Change any non-unique concat base dimensions to UNIQUE using the CHGDFN command and retry.

description: (XSDUNION18) %a %j %j %v UNIQUE cannot be applied to this concat dimension because LEAVES %1p and %2p share the value %3p.
cause: The UNIQUE concat base dimensions contained duplicate values.
action: Use MAINTAIN RENAME to change one of the duplicate values and retry.

description: (XSDUNION19) %a %j %j Concat dimension %1p cannot be changed to UNIQUE because base dimension %2p does not have a TEXT or ID data type.
cause: The CHGDFN command could not complete because one or more of the base dimensions of the concat dimension had a data type other than TEXT or ID.
action: Do not attempt to make the concat dimension UNIQUE.

description: (XSDUNION20) %a %j The concat dimension must be defined as UNIQUE because base dimension %1p contains custom member values.
cause: The UNIQUE keyword was not specified in the concat dimension definition and is required if any of the base dimensions contain custom member values.
action: Define the concat dimension as UNIQUE or remove all base custom member values.

description: (XSDUNION06) Concat dimension list contains duplicate leaf dimension %j.
cause: Duplicate concat leaf dimensions were found.
action: Remove the duplicate concat leaf dimensions and retry.

description: (XSDUNION21) %a %j Concat dimension %1p cannot be changed to NOT UNIQUE because it contains custom member values.
cause: Custom members were present in the concat dimension, preventing it from being redefined as NOT UNIQUE.
action: Remove all custom member values from the concat and all of its bases, and retry.

description: (XSDUNION08) Only concat dimensions can be redefined as UNIQUE. %n is not a concat dimension.
cause: The UNIQUE keyword was used with an invalid object.
action: Retry without the UNIQUE keyword.

description: (XSDUNION09) Concat dimension %n is already defined as UNIQUE.
cause: The concat dimension could not be changed to UNIQUE because it was already UNIQUE.
action: No action is necessary.

description: (XSDUNION10) %a %j %j %j %v Concat dimension %1p cannot be changed to UNIQUE. Leaves %2p and %3p share the value %4p.
cause: The concat dimension could not be changed to UNIQUE because of one or more duplicate values among its bases.
action: Use MAINTAIN RENAME to change one of the duplicate values and retry.

description: (XSDUNION11) %a %n %s %1p is not a %2p type dimension.
cause: The CHGDFN BASE ADD command was applied to an object that is not a concat dimensions.
action: Do not use CHGDFN to add bases to this object. Consult the Oracle documentation.

description: (XSDUNION12) %a %j %j %j %1p cannot be added to %2p because it conflicts with the dimensions of object %3p.
cause: The dimension could not be added using CHGDFN because it was already one the bases of the concat dimension.
action: None.

description: (XSDUNION13) %a %j %j %1p is already a member of %2p and cannot be added.
cause: The dimension could not be added via CHGDFN because it was already one of the bases of the concat dimension.
action: No action is necessary.

description: (XSDUENG00) The first argument to the %s function must be an expression yielding a dimension value.
cause: The user supplied an expression to BASEVAL or BASEDIM that did not yield a valid dimension value.
action: Supply a valid dimension value expression to BASEVAL or BASEDIM.

description: (XSDUENG01) %a %s %j You cannot apply the %1p function to %2p because it is not a concat dimension.
cause: You tried to use the BASEVAL or BASEDIM function with an object that is not a concat dimension.
action: Specify the name of a concat dimension when using BASEVAL or BASEDIM.

description: (XSDPART01) specify a dimension list when defining a PARTITION TEMPLATE
cause: The PARTITION TEMPLATE specification did not contain a dimension list.
action: Provide a list between angle brackets (<>) of the dimensions of the variable being partitioned.

description: (XSDPART02) defined a PARTITION TEMPLATE without a PARTITION BY clause
cause: An attempt was made to define a PARTITION TEMPLATE without a PARTITION BY clause.
action: Specify a partitioning method and one or more partition dimensions when defining a PARTITION TEMPLATE. Add a PARTITION BY clause.

description: (XSDPART03) %q is not in the dimension list of the partition template.
cause: While defining a partition template, an attempt was made to specify a partition dimension that was not a dimension of the partition template itself.
action: Choose a partition dimension from among the dimensions of the partition template.

description: (XSDPART04) %q is not a concat dimension.
cause: An attempt was made to define a partition template with PARTITION BY CONCAT(... dim ...) command where dim is not a concat dimension.
action: Only concat dimensions can serve as partition dimensions with CONCAT partitioning. Choose a different partition dimension.

description: (XSDPART05) %t is not a valid CONCAT partition.
cause: An attempt was made to use RANGE or LIST syntax in defining a CONCAT partition template.
action: Use valid CONCAT partition syntax.

description: (XSDPART06) %t is not a valid RANGE partition.
cause: Attempted to use CONCAT or LIST syntax to define a RANGE partition template.
action: Use the correct RANGE partition syntax and retry.

description: (XSDPART07) %t is not a valid LIST partition.
cause: Attempted to use RANGE or CONCAT syntax in defining a LIST partition template.
action: Use the correct LIST partition syntax and retry.

description: (XSDPART08) %q is an INTEGER or NTEXT dimension, or contains an INTEGER or NTEXT dimension. INTEGER and NTEXT dimensions cannot be used as partition dimensions.
cause: User attempted to define a partition template partitioned by an INTEGER or NTEXT dimension or a concat containing an NTEXT leaf.
action: Either pick a different partition dimension, or redefine the dimension to use a different data type.

description: (XSDPART09) Leaves of %q have different data types.
cause: Attempted to define a range partition template with a CONCAT partition dimension, and the CONCAT had two leaf dimensions with different data types. A partition dimension cannot have more than one data type when RANGE partitioning is used.
action: Pick a different partition dimension.

description: (XSDPART10) A RANGE or LIST partition template can only have a single partition dimension.
cause: Attempted to define a RANGE or LIST partition template with more than one partition dimension.
action: Remove all but one of the dimensions from the PARTITION BY RANGE(...) or PARTITION BY LIST(...) clause of the partition template definition.

description: (XSDPART11) Use simple leaf values to identify concat dimension values in a VALUES LESS THAN clause, rather than the <LEAF: VALUE> format.
cause: While defining a RANGE partition template with a concat dimension for the partition dimension, an attempt was made to define a range using the <LEAF: VALUE> format of a concat dimension value.
action: Use the leaf value only. Instead of using VALUES LESS THAN <leaf: value>, specify VALUES LESS THAN value.

description: (XSDPART12) Invalid dimension value starting at %t.
cause: When defining a RANGE or LIST partition template, attempted to specify an invalid value in a VALUES LESS THAN or VALUES clause. An invalid value can be one of two things: 1) A value whose data type does not match the partition dimension's data type 2) A non-constant value.
action: Modify the value of the VALUES LESS THAN or VALUES phrase and retry.

description: (XSDPART13) A RANGE or LIST partition template cannot have a conjoint for its partition dimension.
cause: Attempted to specify a conjoint dimension as the partition dimension of a partition template partitioned by RANGE or LIST.
action: Use the name of a simple non-INTEGER dimension or a CONCAT dimension as the partition dimension and retry.

description: (XSDPART14) Missing dimension list for %t.
cause: User attempted to define a CONCAT partition template, and didn't supply a list of dimensions for one of the partition definitions.
action: Give a dimension list for each partition.

description: (XSDPART15) %a %v %v Duplicate value in value lists of %1p and %2p.
cause: In a LIST PARTITION TEMPLATE definition, a value appeared in more than one value list, or more than once within a single value list.
action: List each value only once.

description: (XSDPART16) %j is missing from one or more partition dimension lists.
cause: In the partition template definition, one of the partitions has a dimension list that does not contain all the dimensions of the partition template.
action: Add the missing dimension to the partition's dimension list, or delete it from the partition template's dimension list. If using CONCAT partitioning and the missing dimension is a partition dimension, add any leaf of the partition dimension or any CONCAT of leaves of the partition dimension to the partition dimension list.

description: (XSDPART17) %a %j %j %j %1p contains a leaf (%2p) that is not part of the partition dimension %3p.
cause: In the definition of a CONCAT partition template, one of the partitions was dimensioned by a dimension that was concat-related to a partition dimension. For example, it shared some leaves with the partition dimension, but it also contained some leaves that were not in the partition dimension.
action: Either modify the dimensionality of the partition template to include a concat dimension that contains all of the desired leaves, or pick a different dimension for the partition.

description: (XSDPART18) %j is not a dimension of the partition template.
cause: In the partition template definition, one of the partitions was attempted to be dimensioned by a dimension that was not specified in the dimension list of the partition template.
action: Remove the unlisted dimension from the partition's dimension list, or add it to the partition template's dimension list.

description: (XSDPART19) %a %s %s Partitions %1p and %2p are out of order.
cause: In the definition of a range partition template, a partition with a lower range boundary was listed after a partition with a higher range boundary.
action: Alter the order of the partition definition list.

description: (XSDPART20) Partition name %t appears more than once.
cause: A list of analytic workspace partitions was specified in which the partition name appeared more than once.
action: Remove all but the first instance of the partition name from the list.

description: (XSDPART21) Partition %t dimensioned by more than one composite.
cause: Attempted to define a partition template where one of the partitions was dimensioned by two or more composites.
action: Check the partition template being defined has at most one composite per partition.

description: (XSDPART22) %a %j %j cannot rename values of DIMENSION %1p because it is the partition dimension of RANGE PARTITION TEMPLATE %2p
cause: An attempt was made to rename the value of a dimension that serves as the partition dimension of some RANGE or LIST partition template.
action: It is not possible to rename values in a dimension that serves as the partition dimension without deleting all RANGE and LIST partition templates that are partitioned by it.

description: (XSDPART23) Only CONCAT partition templates can be subpartitioned.
cause: User attempted to define a RANGE or LIST partition template with one or more partitions dimensioned by another partition template.
action: Use only regular dimensions and composites to dimension each partition of the RANGE or LIST template.

description: (XSDPART24) %a %v %v Value %1p is not in partition %2p.
cause: User attempted to reorganize a list partition template by removing a value from the list associated with one of the partitions, but the value was not in that list.
action: Ensure that the given values match the given partition.

description: (XSDPART25) %a %j %j You cannot use compressed composite %1p to dimension multiple partitions of the partition template, because its dimension list includes the PARTITION BY dimension %2p.
cause: The specified PARTITION BY dimension also occurred in the dimension list of a compressed composite used to dimension multiple partitions.
action: Ensure that no PARTITION BY dimension occurs among the bases of the compressed composite used to dimension multiple partitions.

description: (NTEXTCNV00) Error during conversion from TEXT to NTEXT.
cause: An unknown character set conversion error occurred when converting a TEXT value to an NTEXT value.
action: Unknown.

description: (NTEXTCNV02) invalid escape sequence in argument to UNISTR function: %i
cause: The UNISTR function was called on a string that had an invalid escape sequence. The only valid escape sequences in UNISTR are - An escape-escape sequence. - An escape, followed by exactly four hexadecimal digits.
action: Ensure that all escape sequences in UNISTR arguments are exactly four hexadecimal digits. To represent code points whose value is less than 0x1000, use preceding zeros. For example: - Invalid: 0x10 - Valid: 0x0010

description: (XSRELGID24) A level relation must be specified for the GROUPSET and ROLLUP options of GROUPINGID.
cause: No level relation was specified.
action: Specify a level relation.

description: (XSRELGID25) INHIERARCHY cannot be specified with the GROUPSET and ROLLUP options of GROUPINGID.
cause: The INHIERARCHY option was specified.
action: Remove the INHIERARCHY option.

description: (XSRELTBL01) The value cannot be added to dimension %j.
cause: A value could not be added to a dimension of type INTEGER.
action: Check the context and permission for dimension maintenance.

description: (XSRELGID26) %a %d %d The length of GID dimension status is %1p. The length of LEVEL dimension status is %2p.
cause: The GID dimension status did not match the LEVEL dimension status.
action: Change either the GID dimension status or the LEVEL dimension status.

description: (XSRELTBL02) QDR dimension %j should not be the related dimension of the relation.
cause: An ineligible dimension was specified in the Qualified Data Reference.
action: Do not attempt to qualify this dimension.

description: (XSRELTBL03) QDR dimension %j is not in the dimension list that dimensions the relation.
cause: The specified qualified data reference (QDR) dimension was not in the dimension list of the relation.
action: Select only dimensions that are in the dimension list of the relation.

description: (XSRELTBL04) Dimension %j cannot be qualified more than once.
cause: The same dimension was specified more than once in the qualified data reference.
action: Specify each qualified data reference dimension only once.

description: (XSRELTBL05) The format of the HIERHEIGHT function is: HIERHEIGHT(relation [,] level) level >= 1.
cause: The HIERHEIGHT function was specified incorrectly.
action: Ensure that the format of the HIERHEIGHT function is correct.

description: (XSRELTBL06) %a %n %j %1p should be dimensioned by %2p.
cause: The level relation was not dimensioned by the source relation dimension.
action: Make sure the level relation has the correct definition.

description: (XSRELTBL07) %a %n %j %1p should be dimensioned by %2p and one level dimension.
cause: The destination relation had the wrong definition.
action: Make sure the destination relation has the correct dimensions.

description: (XSMXALLOC00) Variable %n must be dimensioned to be used by the ALLOCATE command.
cause: The user supplied an undimensioned (scalar) variable to the ALLOCATE command.
action: Use a dimensioned variable.

description: (XSMXALLOC01) %a %n %n TARGETLOG variable %2p must be dimensioned identically to TARGET variable %1p.
cause: The user attempted to execute ALLOCATE with mismatched TARGET and TARGETLOG variables
action: Use TARGET and TARGETLOG variables with matching dimensionality.

description: (XSMXALLOC02) Relation %n must be a one-dimensional self-relation to be used as a SOURCE or BASIS with ALLOCATE.
cause: The user specified an invalid source or basis relation on the ALLOCATE command line.
action: Modify the relation to be a one-dimensional self-relation.

description: (XSMXALLOC03) %a %n %n TARGETLOG variable %2p must have the same data type as TARGET variable %1p.
cause: The user specified a TARGETLOG variable that had a different data type from the TARGET variable.
action: Use TARGETLOG and TARGET variables with an identical data type.

description: (XSALLOC00) You do not have the necessary permissions to use AGGMAP %j.
cause: The user did not have sufficient permissions to run the ALLOCATE command
action: Change to a user ID with the appropriate permissions, or use objects that you have permission to use.

description: (XSALLOC01) To be used with ALLOCATE, your AGGMAP %j must be defined with the ALLOCMAP command.
cause: The user used the AGGMAP command to define the AGGMAP, so either the AGGMAP can only be used with the AGGREGATE command, or the AGGMAP has no contents attached to it.
action: Use the ALLOCMAP command to define the AGGMAP.

description: (XSALLOC02) %a %j %n In AGGMAP %1p, you specified an NA or ZERO sourceval but supplied formula %2p as your source for ALLOCATE.
cause: The user requested that source values be modified during the allocation, but that is not possible when using a formula source.
action: Either use a VARIABLE source or remove the SOURCEVAL specification for your ALLOCMAP.

description: (XSALLOC03) %j cannot include more dimensions than the source variable.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XSALERR00) The character '%c' is not a valid format specifier for the ALLOCATE error log.
cause: The user specified an invalid formatter in the ALLOCERRLOGHEADER or ALLOCERRLOGFORMAT options.
action: Correct the option to have a valid format.

description: (XSALERR01) %a %j %d While performing the ALLOCATE command with AGGMAP %1p, the error logging limit of %2p was exceeded.
cause: The user specified an ERRORLOG MAX value in the ALLOCMAP, but more errors were encountered while performing the allocation.
action: Either set ERRORLOG NOSTOP, reduce the allocation errors, or increase the ERRORLOG MAX setting

description: A deadlock occurred allocating data.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: An NA basis parent cell was encountered.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XSLANGDM01) %a %s %J %s Analytic workspace %1p already contains a dimension (%2p) with the %3p property.
cause: An attempt was made to apply this property to more than one dimension in the analytic workspace.
action: Remove the property from the named dimension and try the command again.

description: (XSLANGDM02) %a %s %J %s Cannot modify the %1p property of %2p because analytic workspace %3p is attached in multiwriter mode.
cause: An attempt was made to add or delete a $DEFAULT_LANGUAGE property in an analytic workspace (AW) attached in multiwriter mode.
action: Attach the AW in a different mode.

description: (XSAGGCNTMOVE01) Aggregation variable %n cannot have itself as an AGGCOUNT.
cause: An attempt was made to turn a variable into its own AGGCOUNT.
action: Select a different AGGCOUNT variable.

description: (XSAGGCNTMOVE02) %a %s %n AGGCOUNT variable %2p must be of type INTEGER, not %1p.
cause: An attempt was made to create an AGGCOUNT variable that was not an INTEGER type.
action: Select an INTEGER AGGCOUNT variable.

description: (XSAGGCNTMOVE03) %a %s %s A %1p aggregation variable cannot have a %2p AGGCOUNT.
cause: The specified AGGCOUNT variable did not have the same TEMPORARY or PERMANENT attribute as the aggregation variable.
action: Select an AGGCOUNT variable with the same TEMPORARY or PERMANENT attribute as the aggregation variable.

description: (XSAGGCNTMOVE04) %n cannot be used as an AGGCOUNT because it has an AGGCOUNT.
cause: The specified AGGCOUNT variable had its own AGGCOUNT.
action: Select a different variable, or remove the AGGCOUNT using CHGDFN.

description: (XSAGGCNTMOVE05) %n cannot be used as an AGGCOUNT while there are permissions applied to it.
cause: The specified AGGCOUNT variable permissions were distinct from those on the aggregation variable.
action: Select a different AGGCOUNT variable or remove the permissions. This may require an UPDATE before the command can succeed.

description: (XSAGGCNTMOVE06) An aggregation variable and its AGGCOUNT must have the same base dimensions.
cause: An AGGCOUNT variable was specified with different base dimensions than the aggregation variable.
action: Select an AGGCOUNT variable with exactly the same base dimensions as the aggregation variable.

description: Unable to allocate %s bytes for the OLAP page pool.
cause: Insufficient memory was available to allocate the needed memory for the online analytical processing (OLAP) page pool. One cause is the value of the OLAP_PAGE_POOL_SIZE initialization parameter.
action: Check the value of the OLAP_PAGE_POOL_SIZE initialization parameter. It cannot be larger than 90% of the value of the PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT initialization parameter.

description: (XSPGTRLOW) The amount of available temporary storage is still low. Free some temporary storage immediately. You can do so, for example, by UPDATING or DETACHING an analytic workspace.
cause: Ran out of temporary tablespace storage.
action: Increase the amount of temporary tablespace storage.

description: invalid parameter value specified for OLAP_PAGE_POOL_SIZE
cause: The specified value for the OLAP_PAGE_POOL_SIZE initialization parameter was out of range. The OLAP_PAGE_POOL_SIZE initialization parameter must be between 2,097,152 (2MB) and 2,147,483,647, and it must be less than 90% of the PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT initialization parameter. Furthermore, you cannot set a fixed-size OLAP page pool with multiple tablespace block sizes. The OLAP_PAGE_POOL_SIZE initialization parameter remains unmodified.
action: Specify a value for the OLAP_PAGE_POOL_SIZE initialization parameter that is between 2,097,152 (2MB) and 2,147,483,647, and does not exceed 90% of the PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT initialization parameter. Do not try to set this parameter if you are using tablespaces with multiple block sizes in your database.

description: (IOSEC01) Current Directory Alias is not set. Cannot complete %s.
cause: A file name was specified without a directory component, and there was no Current Directory Alias (CDA) to complete the file name.
action: Use the CDA command to set the current directory alias, or include a directory component in the file name.

description: (IOSEC02) Directory Alias used in %s does not exist, or you do not have sufficient privileges to access it.
cause: The specified directory alias was not recognized.
action: Use CREATE DIRECTORY <name> AS 'path'. Then grant privileges to that // directory alias.

description: Directory alias used in %s does not exist, or there are insufficient access privileges.
cause: The directory alias did not exist, or there were insufficient access privileges.
action: Process the CREATE DIRECTORY <name> AS 'path' statement. Then, grant privileges to that directory alias.

description: (IOSEC03) %s is an invalid directory or file name.
cause: The supplied value could not be interpreted as a directory or a file name.
action: Supply a valid directory or file name.

description: Invalid directory or file name %s.
cause: The supplied value could not be interpreted as a directory or file name.
action: Supply a valid directory or file name.

description: (IOSEC04) File %s does not exist or cannot be accessed.
cause: The specified file could not be found, or the user did not have sufficient privileges to access it.
action: Check the file name for correctness. If the file name is correct, it may be necessary to use RDBMS or file system commands to grant the // user access.

description: (IOSEC07) Error accessing file %s.
cause: A file system error occurred.
action: Make sure that the file exists and is accessible.

description: Error accessing file %s.
cause: A file system error occurred.
action: Make sure that the file exists and is accessible.

description: (XSTBLFUNC01) The OLAP_TABLE function must contain a DATAMAP that executes a FETCH command or a LIMITMAP.
cause: There is no limitmap on the table function and either the datamap does not contain a fetch, or it errored before the fetch was called.
action: Check the datamap for errors, make sure that it executes a fetch statement, if it is not intended to execute the fetch then make sure that the table function has a valid limitmap.

description: (XSTBLFUNC02) The OLAP_TABLE function encountered an error while parsing the LIMITMAP.
cause: Invalid LIMITMAP syntax, or the name resolution failure of an ANALYTIC WORSKPACE OBJECT.
action: Check the syntax of the limit map, check that the OLAP_TABLE function refers to a valid analytic workspace, check that all analytic workspace objects within the limitmap actually exist within the analytic workspace

description: (XSTBLFUNC03) The OLAP_TABLE function refers to an invalid ADT attribute: %s.
cause: The limitmap refers to a matching of ADT attribute to AW object, but the ADT attribute is not an element of the specified ADT table. Most commonly this is a typo.
action: Add the attribute to the ADT, correct the LIMITMAP, or remove the reference from the LIMITMAP.

description: (XSTBLFUNC04) %a %d %d The OLAP_TABLE function LEVELREL clause cannot declare %1p ADT fields from %2p AW fields.
cause: The limitmap has a levelrel clause which has a different number of values in the list to the right of the FROM than it has to the left.
action: Change the limitmap so that there is a 1:1 mapping of adt and aw elements.

description: (XSTBLFUNC05) Analytic workspace object %v does not exist.
cause: The limitmap refers to a non-existent aw object.
action: Change the limitmap or define the object

description: (XSTBLFUNC07) The datatype of the column used in the ROW2CELL clause of a LIMITMAP must be RAW(16).
cause: Datatype of column used in ROW2CELL clause of a LIMITMAP is not RAW(16).
action: Change datatype to RAW(16).

description: (XSTBLFUNC08) The OLAP_TABLE has attempted to use an AW single row function with the aw_attach parameter set to DURATION QUERY.
cause: The OLAP_TABLE aw_attach parameter was set to DURATION QUERY.
action: Change the OLAP_TABLE aw_attach parameter to DURATION SESSION.

description: (XSTBLFUNC09) The %j dimension is of datatype %s which does not support custom member upserts.
cause: Custom members were attempted to be added via an upsert to a dimension that does not support them
action: Disable the AW Hash optimization for this query

description: (XSTBLFUNC10) The LIMITMAP LOOP clause specifies an invalid type of object. %j must be a DIMENSION or COMPOSITE.
cause: An invalid type of object was specified in the LOOP clause.
action: Correct the LOOP clause.

description: (XSTBLFUNC11) A LIMITMAP DIMENSION clause specifies an invalid type of object. %j must be a DIMENSION.
cause: An invalid type of object was specified in the DIMENSION clause.
action: Correct the DIMENSION clause.

description: (XSTBLFUNC12) %j cannot be used in a LIMITMAP %s clause.
cause: An invalid type of object was specified in a LIMITMAP clause.
action: Correct the LIMITMAP clause.

description: (XSLMINFO00) The LIMITMAPINFO function encountered an error while parsing the LIMITMAP.
cause: Invalid LIMITMAP syntax.
action: Correct the syntax of the limit map.

description: (XSTBLFUNC13) An error occurred expanding the cube_name argument in the OLAP table function
cause: Incorrect metadata or invalid cube name
action: Correct the metadata.

description: (XSTBLFUNC14) OLAP C Looper is disabled by event 37395
cause: init.ora event 37395 includes level 8 which disables the OLAP C looper
action: Remove event level 8 and use explicit FETCH function for OLAP_TABLE

description: (XSLMGEN01) View token cannot be NA
cause: A NA was passed as the view token
action: Pass in a valid view token

description: (XSLMGEN02) View token cannot be greater than 4000 bytes
cause: A view token was greater than 4000 bytes
action: Pass in a view token less than 4000 bytes

description: (XSLMGEN03) View token cannot be blank
cause: A blank was passed as the view token
action: Pass in a valid view token

description: (XSLMGEN04) Column tag is greater than 30 bytes
cause: A value greater than 30 bytes was passed as the column tag
action: Pass in a column tag of 30 bytes or less

description: (XSLMGEN05) %a %s %s %s %s Dimension %1p.%2p hierarchy %3p level %4p is missing a COLUMNNAME property value
cause: The COLUMNNAME property has no value
action: Add a value to COLUMNNAME property

description: (XSLMGEN06) %a %s %s The dimensionality of object %1p.%2p is different than the view token
cause: The dimensionality of the cube does not match the view token
action: Check view token for unrelated hierarchies clauses

description: (XSLMGEN07) %a %s %s Object owner %1p is different than %2p
cause: The object owners are different
action: Make the object owners match

description: (XSLMGEN08) %a %s %s %s Dimension %1p.%2p attribute %3p is missing a COLUMNNAME property value
cause: The COLUMNNAME property has no value
action: Add a value to COLUMNNAME property

description: (XSLMGEN09) %a %s %s %s Cube %1p.%2p measure %3p is missing a COLUMNNAME property value
cause: The COLUMNNAME property has no value
action: Add a value to COLUMNNAME property

description: (XSLMGEN10) %a %s %s Cube %1p.%2p has no measures
cause: The cube has no measures
action: Add a measure to the cube

description: (XSLMGEN11) %a %s %s Dimension %1p.%2p was not found
cause: The view token referenced a dimension that does not exist
action: Pass in a dimension that does exist

description: (XSLMGEN12) %a %s %s %s Hierarchy %1p.%2p.%3p was not found
cause: The view token referenced a hierarchy that does not exist
action: Pass in a hierarchy that does exist

description: (XSLMGEN13) %a %s %s %s Dimension %1p.%2p hierarchy %3p is missing a PHYSICALNAME property value
cause: The property PHYSICALNAME has no value
action: Populate the property PHYSICALNAME with a value

description: (XSLMGEN14) %a %s %s %s Dimension %1p.%2p is missing a %3p property value
cause: The dimension is missing a required property
action: Check dimension property values

description: (XSLMGEN15) Owner is greater than 30 bytes
cause: The owner passed is greater than 30 bytes
action: Pass in an owner that is 30 bytes or less

description: (XSLMGEN16) AW name is greater than 30 bytes
cause: The AW name passed is greater than 30 bytes
action: Pass in an AW name that is 30 bytes or less

description: (XSLMGEN17) AW name is blank
cause: The AW name passed is blank
action: Pass in an AW name that has a value

description: (XSLMGEN18) %a %s %s Object name %1p is different than %2p
cause: The object names are different
action: Make the object names match

description: (XSLMGEN19) AW owner does not match View token owner
cause: The AW owner does not match the View token owner
action: Match AW ower to View token object owner

description: (XSLMGEN20) %a %s View token %1p is not correct
cause: The view token is not correct
action: Check view token syntax for errors

description: (XSTFRC01) SQL Cache ID parameter is invalid or missing.
cause: SQL Cache ID parameter is required to identify SQL cache to query
action: Supply a valid SQL Cache ID. Normally, users should not call OLAP Random Access Cursor table function themselves and therefore should not encounter this error.

description: (XSTFRC02) %a %d %d Column number for this SQL Cache must be between 1 and %1p. Specified column number %2p is invalid.
cause: Column Map references a column number that is greater than the maximum column number in SQL Cache
action: Reference a correct column number. Normally, users should not call OLAP Random Access Cursor table function themselves and therefore should not encounter this error.

description: (XSFTDSC01) Object %s cannot be used to define a column in a LIMITMAP.
cause: The object cannot define a column in LIMITMAP most likely because it is of a wrong type such as, for example, a Worksheet.
action: Remove the reference from the LIMITMAP.

description: (XSTFDSC02) Column type specifier cannot be used when the table function data type is specified.
cause: Column type can only be used with implicitly-specified table functions
action: Remove column type from reference from the LIMITMAP or remove the explicit table function data type specification.

description: (XSTFDSC04) Expression %s cannot be used to define a column in a LIMITMAP.
cause: The expression cannot define a column in LIMITMAP most likely because it is of a wrong type such as, for example, a Worksheet.
action: Remove the reference from the LIMITMAP.

description: (XSTFDSC05) LIMITMAP is missing or is not a string literal.
cause: Table functions that have an automatic ADT require LIMITMAP to be a string literal.
action: Either specify ADT for the table function or specify LIMITMAP as a string literal.

description: (XSTFDSC06) The column datatype %s is not supported in OLAP table functions.
cause: The object type layer does not support column datatype.
action: Use a supported column datatype.

description: (XSSRF00) The OLAP DML ROW2CELL function can only be used in a LIMITMAP.
cause: Using the ROW2CELL function outside of the LIMITMAP.
action: Remove use of the ROW2CELL function.

description: (XSSRF01) The second parameter of an AW single row function cannot be NULL.
cause: The second parameter of the AW single row function was NULL
action: Pass a valid OLAP DML expression as the second parameter of the AW single row function

description: (XSSRF02) The first parameter of an AW single row function cannot be NULL.
cause: The first parameter of the AW single row function was NULL
action: Make sure the column specified in the LIMITMAP ROW2CELL clause is the first parameter of the AW single row function.

description: (XSSRF03) The value of the first parameter of the AW single row function is incorrect.
cause: The column specified in the LIMITMAP ROW2CELL clause was not the first parameter of the AW single row function.
action: Make sure the column specified in the LIMITMAP ROW2CELL clause is the first parameter of the AW single row function.

description: (XSSRF04) Error rewriting OLAP DML expression. Column name too big
cause: The column name specified in the OLAP DML expression was larger than 30 bytes.
action: Make sure the column name specified in the OLAP DML expression is less than or equal to 30 bytes.

description: (XSSRF05) %a %ld Error rewritting OLAP DML expression. Rewritten expression is greater than %1p bytes
cause: The rewritten OLAP DML expression was larger than the output buffer.
action: Create a smaller OLAP DML expression.

description: (XSSRF06) Error rewriting OLAP DML expression. Column name %s is not a valid ADT column.
cause: The column name passes does not exist.
action: Only reference columns that exist.

description: (XSAGDNGL43) %a %j %n In AGGMAP %1p, the MODEL %2p is not a model over a base dimension of the AGGMAP.
cause: Model may include equations others than dimension values, or blocks other than simple blocks.
action: Make sure model only includes the simple blocks with dimension values.

description: (XSAGDNGL44) %a %j %n In AGGMAP %1p, RELATION %2p occurs after a dynamic model. The dynamic model must be the last calculation within the AGGMAP.
cause: Before the current relation, dynamic model exists.
action: Make sure the dynamic model is the last statement.

description: (XSAGDNGL47) %a %j %j In AGGMAP %1p, DYNAMIC MODEL %2p can only edit the top level of its matching relation hierarchy.
cause: The model attempted to edit a child node in the relation hierarchy.
action: Remove this attempt from the model definition.

description: (XSAGDNGL48) %a %j %n In AGGMAP %1p, MODEL %2p cannot be simultaneous.
cause: The aggmap contained a simultaneous model.
action: Change the model definition so that it is no longer simultaneous.

description: (XSAGDNGL49) %a %j %j In AGGMAP %1p, LOAD_STATUS object %2p must be an undimensioned VALUESET over the relation dimension.
cause: The object refered to by the LOAD_STATUS clause of the aggmap wasn't an undimensioned valueset over the related dimension
action: Change the aggmap definition so that it doesn't refer to an invalid object

description: (XSAGDNGL50) %a %j %j In AGGMAP %1p, LOAD_STATUS valueset %2p contains both a child and its ancestor.
cause: The LOAD_STATUS valueset is not allowed to contain both a dimension value and an ancestor of that value.
action: Perform a limit remove ancestors on the valueset and confirm that the result matches the intended load.

description: (XSVPMVTOPART01) %n cannot become anonymous because it has properties.
cause: The OLAP DML command would result in a named object becoming an anonymous object, but the object had one or more properties associated with it.
action: Remove the properties using the PROPERTY command. In some cases an UPDATE may be required before the command can proceed.

description: (XSVPMVTOPART02) %a %n %n %1p and %2p are not in the same analytic workspace.
cause: The OLAP DML command requires certain objects to be in the same analytic workspace, and the command string specified objects from two different analytic workspaces.
action: If more than one analytic workspace is attached to the session, make sure that the object names given in the command are unique across all attached analytic workspaces. Use qualified object names (QON's) if necessary.

description: (XSVPMVTOPART03) %n is the target of an external partition of a partitioned variable.
cause: An attempt was made to perform some prohibited operation on a variable which is itself a partition of some other variable.
action: If desired, use the CHGDFN command to DROP the partition from the partitioned variable, and then run the command again.

description: (XSVPMVTOPART04) %j is not a LIST or RANGE PARTITION TEMPLATE.
cause: The user ran a command that only operated on a LIST or RANGE partition template (or a variable dimensioned by a LIST or RANGE partition template) on some other kind of analytic workspace object.
action: Rerun the command on a LIST or RANGE partition template or a variable dimensioned by a LIST or RANGE partition template.

description: (XSVPMVTOPART05) %j is not in a COMPOSITE.
cause: The partitioned variable's composite dimension did not include the // named dimension as one of its bases.
action: Make sure that the variable is dimensioned by a composite containing the specified dimension.

description: (XSVPMVTOPART06) %a %v %j Partition %1p has some values that are not in %2p.
cause: The named composite did not contain all the partition dimension values for the target partition.
action: When the partition dimension occurs in a partition as the sole base of a composite, that composite must contain all the partition dimension values specified for that partition in the partition template. Add the missing values to the composite and try the command again.

description: (XSVPMVTOPART07) More than one variable is dimensioned by %j.
cause: The target of the _MVTOPARTITION command was dimensioned by a composite shared with other objects in the analytic workspace.
action: Apply _MVTOPARTITION only to targets that do not share their composite dimensions.

description: Cannot start a recursive call to Oracle Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) because a ROLLBACK past an UPDATE to an attached analytic workspace was performed.
cause: ROLLBACK past the UPDATE of one of the attached Analytic Workspaces was called. A recursive OLAP call cannot be made until control returns to initial OLAP call and the affected Analytic Workspaces detaches.
action: Change the called SQL procedure to avoid the ROLLBACK.

description: (XSDPENG00) The PARTITION function cannot be applied to %j because it is not a partition template.
cause: An attempt was made to apply the PARTITION function to an object that was not a partition template.
action: Supply the name of a partition template.

description: (XSFCAST22) %a %s %d %d The list of %1p values cannot have more than %2p members. %3p were supplied.
cause: More than the maximum number of OFFSET or PERIODICITY values were specified.
action: Remove some of the OFFSET or PERIODICITY values.

description: (XSFCAST28) The ALLOCLAST parameter cannot be set to YES unless PERIODICITY specifies more than one cycle.
cause: The ALLOCLAST parameter was set to YES when the PERIODICITY parameter specified a single value rather than a list of nested cycles.
action: Set the ALLOCLAST parameter to FALSE (the default), or specify more than one value for the PERIODICITY parameter (in the form of a parenthesized list).

description: (XSFCAST23) cannot specify a cycle number when querying the %s forecasting option
cause: A cycle number was specified in a call to the FCQUERY function to retrieve forecast data not related to a cycle.
action: Remove the cycle specification from the call to the FCQUERY function.

description: (XSFCAST24) %a %d %d The cycle number must be between 1 and %1p. You specified %2p.
cause: A cycle number less than 1 or greater than the maximum value was specified in a call to FCQUERY.
action: Specify a number in the indicated range.

description: (XSFCAST25) There are only %d PERIODICITY values. You cannot specify more OFFSET values.
cause: More OFFSET values were specified than PERIODICITY values.
action: Specify only as many OFFSET values as there are PERIODICITY values.

description: (XSFCAST26) %a %d %d %d The OFFSET value for cycle %1p cannot be greater than the cycle's PERIODICITY, which is %2p. You specified %3p.
cause: The OFFSET for a cycle exceeded the PERIODICITY for that cycle.
action: Supply an OFFSET less than or equal to the PERODICITY for the corresponding cycle.

description: (XSFCAST27) %a %s %d The value of the %1p expression must be an odd number. You specified %2p.
cause: An even number was given for an option that requires an odd number.
action: Supply an odd number or let the option default.

description: Oracle OLAP is not available.
cause: An attempt was made to utilize functionality found only in Oracle OLAP, but Oracle OLAP was not enabled in the executable.
action: Install the Oracle OLAP option.

description: (XSRELTBL08) %a %t %j %1p is not a valid %2p.
cause: The specified value did not exist in the dimension.
action: Specify an existing value of the dimension.

description: (XSRELTBL16) INHIERARCHY object %q should be a valid valueset or boolean variable.
cause: Invalid valueset or variable was specified.
action: Specify a valid valueset or variable.

description: (XSRELTBL09) %j is not a valid level relation.
cause: The specified level relation was not consistent with the parentage hierarchy.
action: Fix one or both of the relations involved so that all parents are at a higher level than their children.

description: (XSRELTBL17) Invalid LEVELORDER valueset %q.
cause: Invalid LEVELORDER valueset was specified.
action: Specify a valid valueset.

description: (XSRELTBL10) %n must be a dimension.
cause: An attempt was made to qualify an object other than a dimension.
action: Remove the named object from the QDR.

description: (XSRELTBL18) invalid INHIERARCHY valueset %q
cause: An invalid valueset was specified for the INHIERARCHY parameter.
action: Specify a valid valueset for the INHIERARCHY parameter.

description: (XSRELTBL11) invalid relation %q
cause: A value other than a RELATION object was specified as the source or destination.
action: Specify RELATION objects as the source or destination.

description: (XSRELTBL19) A merged family relation cannot take the INHIERARCHY option.
cause: INHIERARCHY option was specified for a merged family relation.
action: Remove the INHIERARCHY option.

description: (XSRELTBL12) %n must be a self-relation.
cause: The specified source relation was not a self-relation.
action: Specify a self-relation as the source.

description: (XSRELTBL19) A merged family relation cannot take the LEVELORDER option.
cause: The LEVELORDER option was specified for a merged family relation.
action: Remove the LEVELORDER option.

description: (XSRELTBL13) %a %n %j relation %1p must be dimensioned by %2p
cause: The destination relation was not dimensioned by the source relation dimension.
action: Provide a valid destination relation.

description: (XSRELTBL14) %n is not a BOOLEAN variable dimensioned by all the dimensions of the hierarchy.
cause: The named variable had either the wrong data type or the wrong dimensions.
action: Specify a BOOLEAN variable dimensioned by all the dimensions of the hierarchy.

description: (XSRELTBL15) The USING clause did not name a relation with the same level dimension as LEVELORDER valueset %n.
cause: Either the USING clause was omitted from the HIERHEIGHT command, or specified a relation that contained values of a different dimension other than the LEVELORDER valueset.
action: Specify a USING clause naming a relation containing values from the correct level dimension.

description: (XSRELGID00) invalid GROUPINGID destination relation or variable %q
cause: An invalid relation or variable was specified as the GROUPINGID destination.
action: Specify a valid relation or variable.

description: (XSRELGID17) The GROUPINGID command does not support hierarchies with more than 126 levels.
cause: A hierarchy was specified with more than 126 levels.
action: Decrease the number of levels in the hierarchy.

description: (XSRELGID01) %n must be a self-relation
cause: The source relation specified for GROUPINGID was not a self-relation.
action: Specify a self-relation as the source relation.

description: (XSRELGID18) Property %v can only be set by the GROUPINGID command.
cause: You tried to set the $GID_DEPTH property.
action: Do not try to set $GID_DEPTH property.

description: (XSRELGID02) Variable %n must have a numeric data type.
cause: The destination variable did not have a numeric data type.
action: Ensure the variable is numeric.

description: (XSRELGID19) The format of the GROUPINGID function is: GROUPINGID(gidrel1 [gidrel2]...)
cause: The GROUPINGID function could not be executed because of invalid syntax.
action: Check the error message or refer to Oracle Database documentation for the correct syntax.

description: (XSRELGID03) %a %n %n The destination variable or relation %1p must be dimensioned by all dimensions of the source relation %2p that have more than one value in status.
cause: The destination variable or relation did not have enough dimensions to contain the result from the multi-dimensional source relation.
action: Either limit the status of hierarchy dimensions or redefine the destination object with the correct dimensions.

description: (XSRELGID20) The GROUPLINGID relation %n appears more than once.
cause: The relation appeared more than once in the GROUPINGID argument list.
action: Remove the duplicated relation.

description: (XSRELGID04) A value cannot be inserted into dimension %j.
cause: An error occurred that prevented a value from being added to the named dimension.
action: Check to make sure that you have permission to add values to the dimension.

description: (XSRELGID21) The source relation can be omitted only when using both surrogate GID and level order valueset.
cause: The required source relation was not specified.
action: Specify the source relation or both surrogate Group ID (GID) and level order valueset.

description: (XSRELGID05) %a %n %j Relation %1p must be dimensioned by %2p.
cause: The destination relation was not dimensioned by the dimension of the source relation.
action: Redefine the destination relation or choose another relation with the correct dimensionality.

description: (XSRELGID06) The related dimension of relation %n must be of type NUMBER.
cause: The related dimension of the destination relation had the wrong data type.
action: Redefine the destination relation or choose another relation with related dimension of type NUMBER.

description: (XSRELGID23) GROUPSET and ROLLUP options in GROUPINGID require a destination relation.
cause: Either a variable or a surrogate dimension was specified as the GROUPINGID destination.
action: Specify a relation as the destination.

description: (XSRELGID07) The level relation %n should be dimensioned by a level dimension.
cause: The level relation was not dimensioned by a level dimension.
action: Redefine the level relation or choose another relation with the correct dimensionality.

description: (XSRELGID08) The level relation and level order valueset provide inconsistent level mappings.
cause: There was a conflict between the hierarchy or level relation and the level order valueset.
action: Modify the relation, specify new limits for the valueset, or choose other objects that do not conflict.

description: (XSRELGID09) A level relation is needed to produce a surrogate dimension Group ID (GID).
cause: A level relation was not specified in the GROUPINGID command.
action: Specify a level relation.

description: (XSRELGID10) %a %j %j OBJECT %1p must be a SURROGATE DIMENSION based on the level dimension %2p.
cause: The object specified was not a surrogate dimension based on the level dimension.
action: Select a surrogate of the level dimension.

description: (XSRELGID11) The SURROGATE DIMENSION %j must be numeric.
cause: A non-numeric surrogate dimension was specified.
action: Provide the name of a numeric surrogate dimension.

description: (XSRELGID12) There are duplicate values in the surrogate dimension GID. Use the INHIERARCHY option to resolve the ambiguity.
cause: There were multiple hierarchies in the current computing scope.
action: Modify the level relation to remove the duplication, or supply\\ an INHIERARCHY valueset.

description: (XSRELGID13) %a %n %j Valueset %1p should be defined over dimension %2p.
cause: The specified INHIERARCHY valueset did not contain values of the hierarchy dimension.
action: Supply an INHIERARCHY valueset containing values of the hierarchy dimension.

description: (XSRELGID14) For variable or relation grouping IDs, a level relation is needed when a LEVELORDER valueset is specified.
cause: The GROUPINGID could not derive level information from the arguments provided, and there was no USING clause to provide this information.
action: Specify a level relation.

description: (XSRELGID15) %a %n %n LEVELORDER valueset %1p and level relation %2p do not have the same level dimension.
cause: A mismatch was detected between the level dimension of the LEVELORDER valueset and that of the level relation specified in the USING clause.
action: Specify objects with the same level dimension.

description: (XSRELGID16) OBJECT %n is not a surrogate dimension. A source relation must be specified when creating any non-surrogate grouping id.
cause: A variable or relation groupingid was specified without providing the source relation.
action: Use s surrogate, or provide the source relation.

description: (NOTALIAS00) %a %j %n %2p is not an ALIAS DIMENSION of %1p.
cause: The user specified an object which was not an alias dimension of the first dimension.
action: Specify an alias dimension of the first dimension.

description: You have one or more attached but unupdated analytic workspaces.
cause: The user has attempted to shut down OLAP, but they have active analytic workspaces whose changes have not been saved.
action: Either issue the update command to update the AWs, or pass TRUE as the force parameter to dbms_aw.shutdown()

description: (AWLISTALL01) %d readers
cause: Used in AW(LISTALL) output formatting when %d is 0.
action: No action needed.

description: (AWLISTALL02) %d reader
cause: String used in AW(LISTALL) output formatting when %d is 1.
action: No action is required.

description: (AWLISTALL03) %d readers
cause: Used in AW(LISTALL) output formatting when count is > 1.
action: None.

description: (AWLISTALL04) %d writers
cause: Used in AW(LISTALL) output formatting when %d was 0.
action: None.

description: (AWLISTALL05) %d writer
cause: Used in AW (LISTALL) output formatting when %d was 1.
action: None.

description: (AWLISTALL06) %d writers
cause: used in AW(LISTALL) output formatting when %d is > 1
action: none

description: (XSACQUIRE_DIFFAW) When using the CONSISTENT WITH clause, all objects must come from the same analytic workspace.
cause: The ACQUIRE command cannot keep objects from several workspaces consistent with each other
action: Omit the CONSISTENT WITH clause or make sure all objects being acquired belong to the same analytic workspace.

description: (XSACQUIRE_LOCKED) Object %j is locked by another user.
cause: Could not acquire (or acquire consistent) the object, since it is locked by another user
action: Try to acquire this object later

description: (XSACQUIRE_TIMEOUT) Object %j is locked by another user and the WAIT timed out.
cause: Could not acquire (or acquire consistent) the object for a while, since it is locked by another user
action: Try to acquire this object later

description: (XSACQUIRE_DEADLOCK) Cannot wait to acquire object %j, since doing so would cause a deadlock.
cause: Waiting to acquire the object would cause a deadlock
action: Release some other object that another user is waiting for and try to acquire this object again.

description: (XSACQUIRE_ACQUIRED) Object %j is already acquired.
cause: The object is already acquired
action: Do not try to acquire this object again

description: (XSACQUIRE_YNRESYNC) Object %j is ambiguously listed to be acquired both with and without RESYNC.
cause: The object is listed in with resync list and no resync list. Such usage is ambiguous as to the user's intent on preserving or not preserving private changes.
action: Do not list the object both with and without RESYNC

description: (XSACQUIRE01) You must specify objects to acquire for the ACQUIRE command.
cause: A list of objects to acquire with or without resync is missing
action: Specify the list of objects to acquire

description: (XSACQUIRE03) Multiwriter operations are not supported for object %j.
cause: Multiwriter presently does not work for this object type
action: Attach the AW in RW or EXCLUSIVE modes to modify this object.

description: (XSMULTI01) Analytic workspace %s is not in MULTI mode.
cause: The workspace for an object is not in multiwriter mode. Hence, no multiwriter operations are allowed on the objects in the workspace
action: Attach the workspace in the multiwriter mode or do not use multiwriter commands with it.

description: (XSMULTI02) Object %j is not acquired.
cause: The object must be acquired for this multiwriter operation
action: Do not use this multiwriter operation on an object that is not acquired

description: (XSMLTUPD01) %a %j %j Object %1p cannot be updated without dimension %2p.
cause: One cannot update an object if it is dimensioned by a maintained dimension without updating that dimension or if the object is a relation and the dimension is its target.
action: Include the maintained dimension in the update list

description: (XSMLTRESYNC01) %a %j %j Object %1p cannot be resynchronized without dimension %2p.
cause: An attempt was made to resync an object dimensioned by a maintained dimension without updating that dimension or if the object was a relation and the dimension was the target.
action: Include the maintained dimension in the update list.

description: (XSMLTRESYNC02) %a %j %j Object %1p cannot be resynchronized without modified object %2p because they share a modified composite dimension.
cause: An attempt was made to resynchronize an object dimensioned by a composite dimension causing the composite dimension to be resynced automatically, dropping all new tuples. This cannot be done, however, if the automatic resync of the composite dimension might cause data in an object that shares the composite dimension to become NA.
action: Resync both objects together. Alternatively, you can try to acquire the other object (that will ensure that the composite dimension is locked in the latest generation and will not be resynced when resyncing the first object), resync the first object, and release the other object.

description: (XSMLTRESYNC03) %a %j %j Object %1p cannot be resynced without modified object %2p because they share a modified dimension map.
cause: An attempt was made to resynchronize an object dimensioned by a dimension map causing the dimension map to be resynced automatically, dropping all changes. This cannot be done, however, if the automatic resync of the dimension map might cause data in an object that shares the dimension map to become NA.
action: Resynchronize both objects together. Alternatively, you can try to acquire the other object (that will ensure that the dimension map is locked in the latest generation and will not be resynced when resyncing the first object), resync the first object, and release the other object.

description: (XSMLTMAINT01) cannot maintain %j because it is not acquired
cause: An attempt was made to maintain a dimension in a multiwriter analytic workspace that was not acquired.
action: Acquire the dimension first.

description: (XSMLTMAINT02) cannot DELETE values of dimension %j in MULTI mode
cause: An attempt was made to DELETE values of a dimension in MULTI mode. DELETE is allowed in multiwriter mode only for SESSION dimension members.
action: Attach the analytic workspace in a read/write mode and perform the DELETE operation.

description: (XSMLTMAINT03) cannot MAINTAIN partition template %j in MULTI mode
cause: An attempt was made to add or remove values from LIST partition template lists while the analytic workspace containing the partition template was attached in multiwriter mode.
action: Do the maintenance in read-only or read/write mode.

description: (XSMLTDCL01) can only DEFINE SESSION objects in analytic workspace %s because it is attached in MULTI mode
cause: Persistent object definition in multiwriter mode was not allowed.
action: Specify all persistent object definitions in read/write mode.

description: (XSMLTDCL02) Cannot DELETE objects in analytic workspace %s because it is attached in MULTI mode.
cause: An attempt was made to delete objects in an analytic workspace attached in MULTI mode.
action: Delete objects in read-only or read/write mode.

description: (XSMLTDCL03) cannot RENAME objects in analytic workspace %s because it is attached in MULTI mode
cause: An attempt was made to rename objects in an analytic workspace attached in MULTI mode.
action: Specify all persistent object maintenance in read/write mode.

description: (XSMLTDCL04) cannot change definitions of objects in analytic workspace %s because they are attached in MULTI mode
cause: An attempt was made to use the CHGDFN command on objects in an analytic workspace attached in MULTI mode.
action: Specify all persistent object maintenance in read/write mode.

description: (XSMLTDCL05) cannot maintain triggers in analytic workspace %s because they are attached in MULTI mode
cause: An attempt was made to use the TRIGGER command on objects in an analytic workspace attached in MULTI mode.
action: Specify all persistent object maintenance in read/write mode.

description: (XSACQUIRE_DEP_LOCKED) Composite, concat, dimension map, or internal partition %j is locked by another user.
cause: Some object required locking a composite, concat, dimension map, or internal partition, which is locked by another user
action: Try to acquire this object later

description: (XSACQUIRE_DEP_TIMEOUT) Composite, concat, dimension map, or internal partition %j is locked by another user and the WAIT timed out.
cause: Some object required locking a composite, concat, dimension map, or internal partition, which could not be locked for a while, since it is locked by another user
action: Try to acquire this object later

description: (XSACQUIRE_DEP_DEADLOCK) Cannot wait to acquire composite, concat, dimension map, or internal partition %j, since doing so would cause a deadlock.
cause: Some object required locking a composite, concat, dimension map, or internal partition, which would cause a deadlock
action: Release some other object that another user is waiting for and try to acquire this object again.

description: (XSACQUIRE_DEP_OLDGEN) Composite, concat, dimension map, or internal partition %j cannot be locked, since another user has committed a new one already.
cause: Some object required locking a composite, concat, dimension map, or internal partition in the present generation, which is not possible, since a newer generation already exists.
action: Try to acquire the main object with resync

description: (XSACQUIRE_OLDGEN) Cannot acquire object %j without resync.
cause: Could not acquire the object without resync because another user has committed a newer version of it already.
action: Try to acquire this object with resync parameter

description: (XSMLTDCL06) %a %n %s cannot use the RELATION command with %1p because analytic workspace %2p is attached in MULTI mode
cause: An attempt was made to use the RELATION command on objects in an analytic workspace attached in MULTI mode.
action: Change the default relation when the analytic workspace is attached in read/write or Exclusive mode.

description: (XSAWRESREV01) You cannot RESYNC or REVERT analytic workspace %s because one or more objects have been defined in it during this session.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XSAWRESREV02) You cannot RESYNC or REVERT analytic workspace %s because one or more objects have been deleted from it during this session.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XSAWRESREV03) You cannot RESYNC or REVERT analytic workspace %s because one or more of its objects have had their definitions changed during this session.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XSAWRESREV04) You cannot RESYNC or REVERT analytic workspace %s because it contains one or more unnamed composites renamed during this session.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XSAWRESREV05) You cannot RESYNC analytic workspace %s because another session has changed the definitions of one or more objects it contains.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XSAWRESREV06) %a %j %s You cannot RESYNC or REVERT analytic workspace %2p because one or more SESSION dimensions or composites are based on %1p.
cause: NA
action: NA

description: (XSMCSESS00) Object %n has the wrong type.
cause: The object was not of the object type specified in the APPLY clause.
action: Specify the correct object type.

description: (XSMCSESS01) %a %n %j Applied relation %1p must be dimensioned by dimension %2p.
cause: Applied relation had a different dimension from the dimension currently being maintained.
action: Find or create a new relation.

description: (XSMCSESS02) Variable %n has no default aggmap.
cause: The applied variable has no default aggmap.
action: Use variable with the default aggmap or aggmap directly.

description: (XSMCSESS03) A session-only dimension value cannot be renamed.
cause: An attempt was made to apply MAINTAIN RENAME to a SESSION value.
action: Delete the old value and add a new one with the desired name.

description: (XSMCSESS04) %j is not the type of dimension that can have session-only values. Valid types are TEXT, NTEXT, ID, NUMBER, and CONCAT with the UNIQUE attribute.
cause: An attempt was made to add a SESSION value to a dimension type that did not support SESSION values.
action: Use a dimension of one of the listed types.

description: (XSMCSESS05) Object %n is specified more than once.
cause: The same object name was specified more than once in the apply clause or in the step dimension list.
action: Remove the repetitions.

description: (XSMCSESS06) The dimension being maintained (%n) cannot also be used as a step dimension.
cause: The dimension being maintained was named as a step dimension.
action: Remove this dimension from the list of step dimensions.

description: (XSMCSESS07) The specified aggmap %j cannot be used for AGGREGATE.
cause: Aggmap was specified for AGGREGATE. The current aggmap can be specified only for ALLOCATE.
action: Choose the correct aggmap for AGGREGATE only.

description: Advice requested for hierarchy with too many levels
cause: A request was made for advice on a hierarchy with more levels than are supported.
action: Only request advice for hierarchies with less than 32 levels.

description: invalid percent specified for pre-computation
cause: Advice was requested for an invalid percent value for pre-computation.
action: Request between 0 and 100 percent for pre-computation.

description: advice requested for invalid object %s
cause: Advice was requested for an invalid object name.
action: Specify a valid object name.

description: Output valueset %s must match %s's dimensionality
cause: A request was made for advice for a relation with different dimensionality from the output valueset.
action: Request using objects that have the same dimensionality.

description: %s is not a valueset
cause: An operation was attempted that supports only valuesets as precompute expressions in an aggmap, yet a different kind of precompute expression was used.
action: Replace this limit expression with an equivalent valueset and retry the operation. General precompute expressions are deprecated.

description: (XSOBJORG_BAD_CUBE) %a %s %s %s invalid property "%1p" specified for cube "%2p.%3p"
cause: Either the specified cube did not have an analytic workspace (AW) organization or the specified property did not apply to cubes.
action: Specify a property that applies to cubes or specify a cube with an AW organization.

description: (XSOBJORG_BAD_DIM) %a %s %s %s invalid property "%1p" specified for dimension "%2p.%3p"
cause: Either the specified dimension did not have an analytic workspace (AW) organization, or the specified property did not apply to dimensions.
action: Specify a property that applies to dimensions with an AW organization.

description: (XSOBJORG_BAD_MEAS) %a %s %s %s %s invalid property "%1p" specified for measure "%2p.%3p.%4p"
cause: Either the specified measure did not have an analytic workspace organization, or the specified property did not apply to measures.
action: Specify a property that applies to measures and a measure with an analytic workspace organization.

description: (XSOBJORG_BAD_ATTR) %a %s %s %s %s invalid property "%1p" specified for base attribute "%2p.%3p.%4p"
cause: Either the specified base attribute did not have an analytic workspace (AW) organization, or the specified property did not apply to the base attribute.
action: Specify a property that applies to the base attributes or specify a base attribute with an AW organization.

description: (XSOBJORG_BAD_DIM_LEVEL) %a %s %s %s %s invalid property "%1p" specified for dimension level "%2p.%3p.%4p"
