cause: The discovered database identifier (DBID) for the shard was invalid, but the shard was already converted from a shard seed.
action: Check the DBID for the shard and report this issue to Oracle Support Services.

description: Transparent Sensitive Data Protection (TSDP) feature internal error.
cause: There was an unexpected error during the TSDP operation.
action: Retry the operation. If this error persists, contact Oracle Support.

description: Invalid data has been found and discarded. Valid data has been imported.
cause: The names of invalid or nonexistent database objects were found during import of discovery result in XML format.
action: Check the trace files for the names of the invalid objects found during import of discovery result in XML format.

description: Schema %s does not exist.
cause: The schema specified using the procedure DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE.ADD_SENSITIVE_COLUMN did not exist.
action: Specify a valid schema in the procedure DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE.ADD_SENSITIVE_COLUMN.

description: Table %s.%s does not exist.
cause: The table specified using the DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE.ADD_SENSITIVE_COLUMN procedure did not exist.
action: Specify a valid table in the DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE.ADD_SENSITIVE_COLUMN procedure.

description: Column %s.%s does not exist in schema %s.
cause: The column specified using the DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE.ADD_SENSITIVE_COLUMN PL/SQL procedure did not exist.
action: Specify a valid column in the DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE.ADD_SENSITIVE_COLUMN PL/SQL procedure.

description: An invalid sensitive type %s was provided.
cause: The sensitive type specified did not exist.
action: Ensure that a valid sensitive type is specified.

description: There was no sensitive column matching the given criteria.
cause: There was no sensitive column matching the schema, table or column name provided in the DBMS_TSDP_PROTECT.ENABLE_PROTECTION_COLUMN procedure.
action: Ensure that the schema, table or column name in the DBMS_TSDP_PROTECT.ENABLE_PROTECTION_COLUMN procedure is valid.

description: Column %s.%s in schema %s has already been identified as sensitive.
cause: The column was already identified as sensitive.
action: Drop the sensitive column using the DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE.DROP_SENSITIVE_COLUMN procedure and retry the operation.

description: There are no sensitive columns associated with source %s.
cause: No sensitive columns were associated with the specified source.
action: Specify a valid source.

description: Sensitive type %s already exists.
cause: The sensitive type specified using the DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE.ADD_SENSITIVE_TYPE PL/SQL procedure already existed in the database.
action: Specify a different name for the sensitive type in the DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE.ADD_SENSITIVE_TYPE PL/SQL procedure and retry the operation.

description: Sensitive type %s does not exist.
cause: The specified sensitive type did not exist in the database.
action: Specify a valid sensitive type.

description: cannot drop sensitive type %s
cause: The sensitive type that was associated with one or more columns could not be dropped.
action: Ensure the sensitive type is not associated with any column before dropping it.

description: A Transparent Sensitive Data Protection (TSDP) policy with the name %s already exists.
cause: A TSDP policy with the same name was found in the database.
action: Specify a different name for the TSDP policy.

description: Invalid Transparent Sensitive Data Protection (TSDP) security feature
cause: The security feature specified was not supported by TSDP.
action: Specify a valid TSDP security feature.

description: invalid Transparent Sensitive Data Protection (TSDP) policy %s
cause: The specified TSDP policy did not exist.
action: Specify a valid TSDP policy.

description: One or more sensitive column types already exist in the database.
cause: Importing the list of sensitive columns using DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE succeeded. However, one or more sensitive column types already exists in the database. That column was not imported again.
action: Check the trace files for more details regarding which sensitive column types were not imported. Ignore if the sensitive column types are already present in the DBA_SENSITIVE_COLUMN_TYPES data dictionary view.

description: Column %s.%s in schema %s is not identified as sensitive.
cause: An attempt was made to alter a column that was not identified as sensitive using the DBMS_TSDP.ALTER_SENSITIVE_COLUMN PL/SQL procedure.
action: Specify a valid sensitive column when executing the DBMS_TSDP.ALTER_SENSITIVE_COLUMN procedure to alter the sensitive column type and/or its comment.

description: Policy %s is not associated with sensitive column type %s.
cause: The given policy was not associated with the given sensitive column type while executing the DBMS_TSDP_PROTECT procedures.
action: Specify the valid combination of policy and sensitive column type.

description: Failed to enable a policy on one or more columns.
cause: Failed attempt to enable policy on one or more columns during DBMS_TSDP_PROTECT.ENABLE_PROTECTION procedures.
action: Check the alert log or trace files for more details.

description: Policy %s is not enabled on column %s.
cause: The given policy was not enabled on the column.
action: Specify a valid policy.

description: Policy %s is already associated with sensitive column type %s.
cause: The given policy was associated with the given sensitive column type.
action: Specify the valid combination of policy and sensitive column type.

description: Disabling of a policy on one or more columns failed.
cause: Errors were encountered while disabling policy on one or more columns during the execution of the DBMS_TSDP_PROTECT.DISABLE_PROTECTION procedure.
action: Check the alert log or trace files for more details.

description: Warnings have been generated during the policy enforcement.
cause: The cause of this error could be one or more of the following: - The policy that was associated with the sensitive column type of a sensitive column was not enabled on the column because no sub-policy matched the column properties. - There was no policy associated with the sensitive column type of a sensitive column. - A conflicting redaction policy was enabled on the table.
action: Check the alert log or trace files for more details.

description: Disabling protection failed during import of sensitive columns.
cause: Importing the list of sensitive columns failed because there was a problem in disabling protection on the columns.
action: Check the alert log or trace files for more details.

description: reenabling protection failed before import
cause: Importing the list of sensitive columns failed because there was a problem in disabling protection on the columns. A subsequent attempt to reenable protection on the columns also failed.
action: Check the alert log for more details.

description: reenabling protection failed after import
cause: Importing the list of sensitive columns succeeded. A subsequent attempt to reenable protection on the columns failed.
action: Check the alert log for more details.

description: Dropping of one or more columns from the sensitive column list failed.
cause: Disabling protection on the column failed.
action: Check the trace files for more details.

description: There is no associated sensitive column(s) of sensitive column type %s.
cause: DBMS_TSDP_PROTECT.ENABLE_PROTECTION PL/SQL API executed prior to associating sensitive columns to the sensitive column type.
action: Specify a valid sensitive column for the sensitive column type using DBMS_TSDP_PROTECT.ASSOCIATE_POLICY PL/SQL API.

description: No policy is associated with sensitive column type %s.
cause: There was no policy that was associated with the sensitive column type.
action: Associate policy with a valid sensitive column type using DBMS_TSDP_PROTECT.ASSOCIATE_POLICY procedure.

description: Policy %s is enabled on one or more columns.
cause: A transparent sensitive data protection (TSDP) policy that was enabled on a column could not be altered or dropped.
action: Disable the TSDP policy and retry the operation.

description: Policy %s is associated with one or more sensitive types.
cause: A transparent sensitive data protection policy that was associated with a sensitive column type could not be dropped.
action: Disassociate the policy from the sensitive column type and retry the operation.

description: Policy %s does not have the given condition.
cause: The given condition was not defined for the transparent sensitive data protection (TSDP) policy.
action: Specify the valid condition for the TSDP policy.

description: The default policy %s cannot be altered.
cause: The default policy for Transparent Sensitive Data Protection could not be altered.
action: Specify the valid policy to be altered.

description: The default policy %s cannot be dropped.
cause: The default policy for Transparent Sensitive Data Protection could not be dropped.
action: Specify the valid policy to be dropped.

description: The security feature does not contain parameter %s.
cause: An invalid parameter was found for the given security feature.
action: Enter valid parameters for the security feature.

description: An invalid parameter %s has been found.
cause: An invalid parameter was found for the given security feature.
action: Enter valid parameters for the security feature.
params: 1) parameter_name: An invalid parameter name was supplied during policy creation.

description: Input parameter for '%s' is not valid.
cause: Invalid input was given for the parameter.
action: Enter valid input for the parameter.

description: An invalid condition was given for the policy condition.
cause: The given condition was invalid.
action: Enter a valid value for the condition.

description: Policy %s is enabled on one or more columns of sensitive type %s.
cause: A Transparent Sensitive Data Protection policy that was enabled on one or more columns of a particular sensitive type could not be disassociated from the sensitive type.
action: Ensure the policy is not enabled on a column of the given sensitive type.

description: The discovery result cannot be imported.
cause: One or more columns from the XML input were already identified as sensitive by a different source.
action: Check the trace file for a list of sensitive columns that were already identified as sensitive.

description: Columns on SYS-owned table cannot be marked as sensitive.
cause: A column in a SYS owned table was being marked as sensitive using DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE procedure.
action: Ensure the column being marked as sensitive does not belong to a SYS-owned table.

description: The SEC_RELEVANT_COLS parameter cannot be specified in TSDP policy.
cause: The SEC_RELEVANT_COLS parameter was specified while configuring a Transparent Sensitive Data Protection (TSDP) policy. SEC_RELEVANT_COLS_OPT parameter can be specified to indicate that TSDP should input the sensitive column as input to the SEC_RELEVANT_COLS parameter when enabling protection.
action: Use the SEC_RELEVANT_COLS_OPT parameter to configure the security relevant column.

description: transparent sensitive data protection (TSDP) operation not supported
cause: An attempt was made to perform the TSDP operation from inside the application install or patch begin-end block.
action: Perform the TSDP operation outside the application install or patch begin-end block.

description: The specified column "%s" cannot be marked as sensitive.
cause: An attempt was made to mark the virtual or hidden column as sensitive using the DBMS_TSDP_MANAGE procedure.
action: Remove the virtual or hidden column and then retry the operation.
params: 1) column_name: The column name being marked as sensitive.

description: data file number %s already included as %s
cause: RMAN attempted to use the specified data file number, but this data file number was already in use by a different container database.
action: Resolve the conflict and retry the command.

description: File %s is from different container identifier %s; current %s
cause: This backup piece contained a data file that did not belong to the current container. Cataloging such a backup piece is not allowed.
action: Connect to root or to the correct Pluggable Database and retry the command.

description: cannot rename data file '%s' - file was instantly restored.
cause: During ALTER DATABASE RENAME or RMAN command SWITCH, the rename was specified for an instantly restored file.
action: Rename the file that was not instantly restored or wait until the repopulation work is complete and the retry the command.

description: catalog instantly restored data file copy %s is not supported
cause: This data file copy was instantly restored. Cataloging such a file is not supported.
action: Do not request to catalog an instantly restored data file copy.
params: 1) data_file: The target data file instantly restored.

description: instant restore of data file copy %s is not supported
cause: An attempt was made to restore a data file copy in instant restore mode. This is not supported.
action: Do not restore a data file copy in instant restore mode.
params: 1) data_file: The target data file name.

description: deleting or restoring instantly restored data file %s is not supported
cause: This data file was instantly restored with the full option. A background process was repopulating the data file. An attempt to take the data file out of the process failed. Deleting or restoring such files is not supported.
action: Retry the command later.
params: 1) data_file: The data file restored instantly.

description: moving instantly restored data file %s is not supported
cause: This data file was instantly restored. Moving such file is not supported.
action: Do not request to move instantly restored data file.

description: instant restore of data file %s failed
cause: During an instant restore, it was not possible to initialize the destination data file. A possible cause for this message is that the instant restore feature is disabled in this database.
action: Check the other messages in the error stack, alert log, or trace file to see if there is a specific reason for this failure. If the situation cannot be resolved, then request a regular (not instant) restore.

description: cannot create a control file record for data file number %s
cause: This data file was instantly restored. An attempt was made to create a record in the control file for the data file. Unless the database is mounted, this command cannot be completed.
action: Mount the database and retry the command.

description: Restore, recover or block media recovery may be in progress.
cause: A backup or copy was attempted while restore, recover or block media recovery was in progress. This error should be preceded by another error indicating a file access enqueue problem for a file specified in a backup, copy or restore operation.
action: Restore, recover or block media recovery should not be in progress during backup or copy operation.

description: cannot look up the rewrapped key for tablespace %s
cause: During transport, an encrypted tablespace could not find its rewrapped key as part of a Recovery Manager (RMAN) cross-platform command.
action: Connect to the respective pluggable database and check if the master table is created.

description: cannot restore as encrypted/decrypted on database with compatibility below 12.2
cause: Restore with encryption and decryption is only supported on 12.2 compatible databases and above.
action: Upgrade database or restore without encryption/decryption.

description: cannot restore as encrypted or decrypted from backup piece with pre-12.2 compatiblity
cause: An attempt to restore with encryption or decryption failed because backups must be Oracle Database 12c Release 2 compatible.
action: Create a backup of the Oracle Database 12c Release 2 database or restore without encryption or decryption.

description: cannot backup data file %s because it belongs to a dropped pluggable database
cause: The indicated file was not included in the backup because it belonged to a pluggable database (PDB) that was dropped.
action: Do not backup files in PDBs that are dropped.
params: 1) data_file: The full path name of the data file.

description: cannot backup a mounted control file of type backup
cause: An attempt was made to backup a control file when the mounted control file at that time was a backup control file. This is not allowed.
action: Mount a current control file and retry the operation.

description: physical block size %s does not match logical block size %s
cause: The physical block size and logical block size of the backup piece did not match.
action: Ensure that the physical block size size and logical block size match before copying the backup piece.

description: must use backup control file that has dropped PDB with GUID %s
cause: Some restored files belonged to the dropped pluggable database (PDB) with respect to the current control file.
action: Restore and mount a backup control file that has the dropped PDB.

description: nonexistent backup piece or data file "%s" in the current container
cause: An attempt was made to access a backup piece or data file. This attempt failed because the specified file is not known to the current container.
action: Specify the name of an existing file that can be accessed by the current container. Check the relevant V$ table for a list of possible files.

description: data file %s is offline: incremental start SCN is too recent
cause: The incremental start system change number (SCN) which was specified when starting an incremental data file backup was greater than the data file checkpoint SCN, which could cause some blocks to be missed.
action: Specify a smaller incremental start SCN.

description: no key present in wallet
cause: An attempt was made to restore a backup as encrypted. This attempt failed because the current wallet did not contain an encryption key with which to encrypt the data.
action: Create an encryption key in the wallet and retry the command.

description: multiple keys present in wallet
cause: An attempt was made to restore a backup as encrypted. This attempt failed because the current wallet contained more than one encryption key.
action: Specify with which key to encrypt by using the USING KEY clause of RESTORE AS ENCRYPT.

description: interrupt a backup job
cause: NA
action: Set this event to interrupt a backup job.

description: backup operation interrupted by restoration or recovery of file %s
cause: A restoration, recovery, or block media recovery interrupted a backup or copy in progress. This error indicates that restoration or recovery of file is given preference over the backup operation.
action: Let restoration, recovery, or block media recovery finish before starting a backup or copy operation.

description: Archived log thread %s sequence %s does not exist.
cause: An attempt was made to access the indicated archived log. This attempt failed because the specified file is not known to the backup step.
action: Specify the name of an existing file that can be accessed by the database.

description: Multi-section archived log backup requires COMPATIBLE %s or higher.
cause: An attempt was made to perform a multi-section archived log backup with a database compatibility that was not high enough.
action: Raise the compatibility level and retry the operation.

description: cannot obtain %s enqueue for archived log thread %s sequence %s
cause: The file access enqueue could not be obtained for a file specified in a backup, copy or restore operation.
action: Wait until the conflicting operation is complete, then retry the copy or backup.

description: failed to generate RMAN backup encryption key: %s
cause: RMAN failed to generate a typed key for backup encryption. Error code definitions as follows: 2 : key buffer is too small 5 : invalid owner type 7 : cannot find specified encryption key 9 : master key revoked or disabled
action: Resolve the error or contact Oracle Support Services.

description: PDB %d with GUID %s now has ID %d and GUID %s. RMAN cannot backup file %s due to PDB change.
cause: The indicated pluggable database (PDB) has changed since the start of the backup operation. RMAN can no longer back up the files associated with the PDB.
action: Restart the backup.

description: SBT library callback invalid function value %s
cause: An unrecognized function code is being supplied from the System Backup Tape (SBT) library.
action: The SBT library determines whether this is a fatal error. If this is a fatal error, the SBT reports the error with more detail.

description: SBT library callback invalid function version %s
cause: An unrecognized function version is being supplied from the System Backup Tape (SBT) library.
action: The SBT library determines whether this is a fatal error. If this is a fatal error, the SBT reports the error with more detail.

description: SBT library generic callback invalid function value %s
cause: An unrecognized function code is being supplied from the System Backup Tape (SBT) library.
action: The SBT library determines whether this is a fatal error. If this is a fatal error, the SBT reports the error with more detail.

description: Section size is not aligned to Oracle ASM extent size of 480 MB.
cause: An attempt is being made to restore a multi-section archived log backup with a section size that is not aligned to Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) extent size of 480 MB.
action: Retry the operation with a multi-section backup aligned to 480 MB.

description: multiple foreign datafilecopy records exist for file number %s
cause: Multiple foreign datafilecopy entries are found for the datafile while restoring incremental backups.
action: Uncatalog the foreign datafilecopy records and retry the restore command.

description: unable to convert datafile copy containing encrypted blocks
cause: An attempt is being made to cross-endian convert a data file copy containing encrypted blocks.
action: Follow steps for cross-platform transport of encrypted tablespaces using a passphrase.

description: invalid option to apply XS Data Security
cause: The input value was not a valid option to apply XS Data Security.
action: Use a valid option to apply XS Data Security.

description: The object type for "%s" is not valid for RAS policies.
cause: A Real Application Security (RAS) policy can only be applied to tables and views. The specified object type was not a table or view.
action: Specify an object whose type is either a table or view.
params: 1) subject_name: The name of the subject.

description: An invalid column "%s" was specified as part of RAS policy for "%s" object.
cause: An invalid column was specified as part of the Real Application Security (RAS) policy for this object. The column name must be a valid column name for the object.
action: Review the definition of the object and use the correct column name in the policy.
params: 1) column_name: The name of the invalid column. 2) object_name: The name of the database object for which the invalid column was specified.

description: A RAS policy is not enabled on %s.%s.
cause: An attempt was made to disable the Real Application Security (RAS) policy on an object (table or view) that did not have an enabled RAS policy.
action: Review your requirement to see if a RAS policy must be disabled on a different object instead.
params: 1) schema_name: The name of the schema that owns the object. 2) object_name: The name of the object (table or view) where an XS Data Security policy is enabled.

description: Cannot disable RAS policy since there are multiple policies enabled on %s.%s.
cause: An attempt was made to disable an Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) policy associated with an object while the object had more than one policy enabled. When more than one RAS policy is enabled on an object, the specific policy name must be included when disabling a policy on the object.
action: Specify a policy name associated with the object to disable the policy.
params: 1) schema_name: The name of the schema that owns the object. 2) object_name: The name of the object where the policies are enabled.

description: cannot mix VPD column policy and Oracle RAS column constraint policy
cause: The object was protected by both Virtual Private Database (VPD) column security policy and Oracle Database Real Application Security (Oracle RAS) column constraint policy which is not allowed.
action: Disable or drop either the VPD column security policy or the Oracle RAS column policy.

description: No RAS security policy is associated with database object %s.%s.
cause: The specified table was not associated with any Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) security policy.
action: Review the RAS dictionary view DBA_XS_POLICIES to find existing associations of RAS policies and database objects. Then, rerun the command with a valid database object with a RAS policy.
params: 1) schema_name: The schema name of the table. 2) table_name: The name of the table.

description: There are multiple RAS policies associated with %s.%s.
cause: An attempt was made to drop a Real Application Security (RAS) policy on an object while the object had more than one enabled RAS policy.
action: Ensure that you are dropping the RAS policy on the correct object. If you have the correct object, you need to specify the RAS policy name that you want to drop.
params: 1) schema_name: The name of the schema that owns the object. 2) object_name: The name of the object where security polices are associated.

description: User-built Static ACL Materialized View does not exist
cause: A non-existing user-built Static ACL Materialized View was specified
action: Create a user-built Static ACL Materialized View with the specified name or use system-built Static ACL views

description: User-built Static ACL Materialized View has invalid schema
cause: A user-built Static ACL Materialized View was specified but with an incorrect schema
action: Create a user-built Static ACL Materialized View with at least the required columns with correct names and types

description: Invalid refresh mode specified for Static ACL Materialized View
cause: The refresh mode specified for the Materialized View supporting static ACLs is invalid.
action: Specify either "ON DEMAND" or "ON COMMIT" for parameter refresh_mode

description: An invalid name was specified for the static access control list (ACL) materialized view.
cause: The name specified for the static ACL Materialized View (ACLMV) was reserved for system-provided ACLMVs.
action: Rename the static ACL Materialized View to use a non-reserved name.

description: The RAS security context changed since the cursor was parsed.
cause: The Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) security context was changed after the cursor was parsed due to application roles being enabled or disabled, or the RAS user being dropped.
action: Ensure that RAS security context remains unchanged after the cursor is parsed. Do not drop the application user, and do not enable or disable application roles in the current RAS session after the cursor is parsed.

description: The policy schema differs from the object schema for Static ACL Materialized View based XDS policy.
cause: The specified object schema was different from the policy schema.
action: Make sure the object and the policy have the same schema.

description: no static rule specified in applied policy
cause: The policy applied on the table did not contain any static rules.
action: Ensure the applied policy has at least one static rule.

description: A static RAS ACL materialized view creation failed.
cause: Creation of the Real Application Security (RAS) static access control list (ACL) materialized view failed.
action: Review the RAS documentation for more information about using materialized views. Check the trace file for detailed error information.

description: XS Security - Data Security tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: Oracle Database Real Application Security internal error
cause: There was an Oracle Database Real Application Security internal error.
action: This is an internal error and should not be generally visible to the applications. Contact Oracle Support with the relevant trace files.

description: The RAS application user name was invalid or missing.
cause: The Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) user name was missing or invalid. This indicates that the RAS user name was not in the RAS dictionary.
action: Check for the correct spelling of the RAS user name and call the function or procedure again with the corrected application user name.

description: An invalid RAS session ID was specified.
cause: An invalid Real Application Security (RAS) session ID was specified.
action: Check the RAS session ID and call the function or procedure again with a valid session ID.

description: A valid RAS cookie was not specified.
cause: The function or procedure must use a valid Real Application Security (RAS) cookie name.
action: Call the function or execute the procedure with a valid cookie name.

description: An invalid RAS namespace was specified.
cause: An invalid Real Application Security (RAS) application namespace or predefined namespace was specified. Valid RAS namespaces can be found in the DBA_XS_NS_TEMPLATES database view. User operations are not allowed on the predefined namespace. Predefined namespaces are in the RAS documentation.
action: Check the database view for valid namespaces and call the function or procedure again with a valid namespace. Ensure that the specified namespace is not a predefined namespace.

description: An invalid RAS application role name was specified.
cause: An invalid application role was specified in the Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) function or procedure.
action: Check the role name and call the function or procedure again with a valid application role. Valid application role names can be found in the DBA_XS_ROLES and DBA_XS_DYNAMIC_ROLES views.

description: invalid namespace or attribute specified
cause: An invalid XS Security application namespace or attribute was specified.
action: Check the namespace and attribute, and call the function or procedure again.

description: The RAS namespace already exists.
cause: Real Application Security (RAS) namespaces must be unique. An attempt was made to create a RAS namespace using the same name as an existing RAS namespace.
action: Create the RAS namespace with a unique name.

description: An invalid RAS namespace attribute %s was specified.
cause: An invalid Real Application Security (RAS) namespace attribute was specified. The list of valid namespace attributes can be found in the DBA_XS_NS_TEMPLATE_ATTRIBUTES database view.
action: Check the attribute and call the function or procedure again with a valid RAS namespace attribute.
params: 1) attribute_name: The name of the invalid attribute in the namespace.

description: Invalid ACL identifier specified
cause: The specified ACL identifier is invalid.
action: Check the ACL identifier, and execute the function or procedure again with a valid ACL ID.

description: A valid RAS application user name was not specified.
cause: A valid Real Application Security (RAS) application user was not specified for this operation. Review the DBA_XS_USERS database view for valid RAS application users.
action: Call the function or execute the procedure with a valid RAS application user name.

description: The RAS session ID was not specified in the procedure.
cause: The Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) XS session ID was not specified when the procedure was called.
action: Review the RAS documentation in the topic for session management. Review the procedures to manage sessions and update the procedure with a valid RAS session ID.

description: A valid RAS namespace was not specified in the procedure.
cause: A valid Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) XS application namespace was not specified when the procedure was called.
action: Review the RAS documentation in the topic for session management. Review the procedures to manage namespaces and attributes. Update the procedure with a valid application namespace and call the procedure again.

description: A RAS session was not attached to the database session.
cause: A procedure or function was called when Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) XS session was not attached to the database session.
action: Review the RAS documentation on attaching and detaching a RAS session. Update the code to attach to a RAS session before you call the function or execute the procedure.

description: RAS attribute name was not specified in the procedure.
cause: The Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) XS Security application namespace attribute name was not specified when the procedure was called.
action: Review the RAS documentation in the topic for session management. Review the procedure to get, set, or delete an attribute.

description: attribute value not specified
cause: XS Security application namespace attribute value was not specified.
action: Execute the function or procedure with an attribute value.

description: inactivity timeout not specified
cause: XS Security session inactivity timeout was not specified.
action: Call the function or procedure with an inactivity timeout value.

description: A valid RAS cookie was not specified.
cause: The function or procedure did not use a valid Real Application Security (RAS) cookie name.
action: Call the function or execute the procedure with a valid cookie name.

description: The RAS application role was not specified.
cause: The Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS or XS) application role name was not specified with the middle-tier application or procedure that tried to enable or disable it.
action: Supply a valid application role name with the middle-tier application or procedure to enable or disable it. RAS application roles can be queried from the DBA_XS_ROLES and DBA_XS_DYNAMIC_ROLES data dictionary views.

description: operation disallowed in an application session
cause: Operations were blocked while an application was attached. The following are the common cases: - An attempt was made to enable or disable database roles (through the 'set role' statement) in an application session. - An attempt was made to destroy a direct logon Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) session while the session was active. - An attempt was made to destroy a regular RAS session while the session was attached. - An attempt was made to perform certain session operations (for example, ATTACH_SESSION, DETACH_SESSION, DESTROY_SESSION, ASSIGN_USER, SWITCH_USER, ENABLE_ROLE, DISABLE_ROLE) in the 'parse as user' statement while currently attached to a RAS session. - An attempt was made to change the password for an external RAS user.
action: Do not attempt to execute the SET ROLE statement while attached to an application session. Do not attempt to change the password for an external RAS user. Try using the FORCE option when attempting to destroy an application session. Or, detach the application session first, then try the operation again.

description: insufficient privileges
cause: An attempt was made to execute an XS Security session, function, or procedure without the appropriate privileges.
action: Ask the administrator to perform the operation or to grant the appropriate privileges.

description: An error was returned by the RAS event handler %s.
cause: An error or exception was returned by the Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) error handling function during the current operation.
action: Check the trace files to identify and resolve the error. Since changes made in this session may not have been recorded correctly, detach the session and roll back any changes made in the session using DETACH_SESSION (TRUE). Attempt the operation again after the error has been resolved.
params: 1) event_name: The name of the event handler function.

description: The variable %s size %s is smaller than the required variable size %s.
cause: The size of the output variable of this function or procedure was too small. The variable must meet the minimum variable size.
action: Increase the variable size and retry the operation.
params: 1) variable_name: The name of an output variable. 2) variable_size: The size of the output variable. 3) required_size: The required size of the output variable.

description: cookie already in use by another session
cause: The specified session cookie name was in use by another Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) session.
action: Choose a unique name when creating an application session with a cookie or when setting a cookie for the specified application session.

description: session ID mismatch
cause: The specified session ID does not match the attached session ID.
action: Execute the function or procedure without a session ID or with a matching attached session.

description: already attached to an application user session
cause: The current database session is already attached to an application user session.
action: Detach from the current application user session before attaching to the new application user session.

description: The specified name length is not within the valid range.
cause: The length of the name was shorter or longer than the allowed limits.
action: Try again with a new name that has a length within the allowed limits.

description: argument value too long
cause: The specified argument value was too long.
action: Process the function or procedure with a shorter argument value.

description: An invalid RAS event type was specified.
cause: The event type specified was not valid for Oracle Real Application Security (RAS). The list of valid event types can be found in the description for relevant procedures (for example, DBMS_XS_SESSIONS subprogram ADD_GLOBAL_CALLBACK) in the RAS documentation.
action: Review the RAS documentation for valid values for the event_type parameter and select a valid event_type value. Retry the operation with a valid event_type value.

description: unable to complete the operation with the specified external principal name "%s"
cause: The specified external principal name was either the same as an existing Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) principal, or the principal name was still cached in the database shared pool.
action: To use this external principal name, drop the RAS principal with the same name and try again. If the same error occurs again, you must flush the database shared pool using the ALTER SYSTEM FLUSH SHARED_POOL statement. Another option is to specify another external principal and retry the operation.

description: User status is currently inactive.
cause: The user was marked inactive.
action: Change the status of the user in the enterprise directory to active and retry.

description: User's password has expired
cause: User password was expired.
action: Change the user's password and update status to active.

description: User's account was locked
cause: The user's account is locked.
action: Update user's status to Active in Enterprise Directory and try again.

description: Cannot update the GUID of the principal
cause: The GUID of the principal existed or the external source was not set.
action: NONE.

description: You cannot update or delete Oracle reserved RAS or XS objects.
cause: An attempt was made to update or delete reserved Oracle Real Application Security (RAS or XS) objects.
action: Do not attempt to update or delete reserved Oracle Real Application Security (XS) objects.

description: Cannot add a proxy user when there was no proxy roles.
cause: An attempt was made to add a proxy user to a target user when proxy roles did not exist.
action: Verify the proxy roles and try again.

description: cannot detach from a direct-login XS session
cause: An attempt was made to detach from an XS session created by a direct password login.
action: Log out of the database session to detach and destroy the XS session.

description: switching users not allowed for a proxy session
cause: An attempt was made to switch users within a proxy session.
action: Switch back to the original user and try again.

description: operation disallowed in application session
cause: The specified operation was not allowed in an application session.
action: Do not attempt disallowed operations, such as: - Create a session in trusted mode with a regular Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) user. - Create a regular RAS user session with external roles. - Switch user when the session was created with an external principal. - Enable or disable roles when the session is created with an external principal.

description: unsupported verifier type
cause: An unsupported verifier type was provided.
action: Call the function or procedure again with a different verifier type.

description: The requested RAS event handler is not registered for the event.
cause: An attempt was made to update or delete an Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) event handler that was not registered for the event.
action: Review the associated packages to identify the correct RAS event handler name and retry.

description: requested event handler already registered for the event
cause: An attempt was made to re-register an event handler.
action: Verify the event handler name and retry the operation.

description: The requested RAS event handler does not exist.
cause: An attempt was made to register a nonexistent Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) event handler.
action: Verify the correct spelling of the RAS event handler name or create the event handler first and retry.

description: cannot destroy a direct login XS session
cause: An attempt was made to destroy an XS session that was created by a direct login user.
action: Logout of the database session to destroy the XS session.

description: The RAS user is not within the effective start and end dates.
cause: An attempt was made to create an Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS or XS) session before the effective start date or after the effective end date for the RAS user.
action: Contact the database administrator to check and possibly adjust the effective start or end dates for the RAS user. If the dates are correct and cannot be changed, then the RAS user is not authorized to connect to the database.

description: invalid error code supplied
cause: An error code with an invalid value was supplied.
action: Use an error code from the range of valid values.

description: An attribute in a namespace cannot have both a default value and the first read event set.
cause: Both a default value and the first read event were specified in the namespace template.
action: Specify either a default value or the first read event for the attribute in the namespace, but not both.

description: The %s did not exist in the %s.
cause: An attempt was made to delete an XS artifact which was not in existence within the scope.
action: Check if the XS artifact was created or referenced within the scope.

description: The %s already exists in the %s.
cause: An attempt was made to create or refer to an XS artifact which was already in existence within the scope.
action: Check if the XS artifact name is unique within the scope.

description: feature unsupported or not implemented
cause: This feature was not supported or not implemented.
action: This error is informational only. No action is needed.

description: XS session operations are disallowed during the execution of a definer's rights program unit.
cause: An attempt was made to perform an XS session operation that could modify the current security context inside a definer's rights program unit.
action: Change the program unit to invoker's rights.

description: Circular definition for aggregate privilege %s in security class %s
cause: Definition of an aggregate privilege contained itself.
action: Fix the aggregate privilege definition.

description: privilege %s aggregated in security class %s not found
cause: The definition of an aggregate privilege contained a privilege that was not defined in this or in the parent security classes.
action: Fix the aggregate privilege definition.
params: 1) privilege_name: The expected privilege name. 2) security_class_name: The security class name.

description: Circular definition for security class %s
cause: Security class definition inherited from itself through circular definition.
action: Fix the security class definition.

description: Security class %s cannot inherit from base security classes.
cause: The definition of a security class specified an internal base security class as a parent security class.
action: Remove the internal base security class from the "inherits-from" list.
params: 1) security_class_name: The name of the security class.

description: unable to load security class %s
cause: The specified security class did not exist.
action: Specify an existing security class or create the missing security class.
params: 1) security_class_name: The name of the security class.

description: missing parent security class for security class %s
cause: The specified security class did not have a parent security class.
action: Add a parent security class using the inherits-from tag, and retry the operation.
params: 1) security_class_name: The name of the security class.

description: Privilege %s is not found in the associated security classes.
cause: The specified privilege did not exist in the security classes that were associated with the ACLs.
action: Use a security class that contains the specified privilege.

description: Either the RAS security class name or RAS target namespace was invalid.
cause: The Real Application Security (RAS) security class target namespace attribute was either null or was longer than 4000 characters. Or, the RAS security class name attribute was either null or was longer than 1024 characters.
action: Provide valid values for the security class name and target namespace.

description: Duplicate definition for privilege %s in security class %s.
cause: The privilege name in the security class was previously defined in another security class.
action: Provide a unique name for the privilege.

description: XS Security - ACL tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: Security Class %s specified in the ACL %s does not exist.
cause: An invalid security class was specified in the ACL.
action: Specify a valid security class.

description: A duplicate RAS security class name %s already exists in the target namespace %s.
cause: Real Application Security (RAS) security class names must be unique within the target namespace. An existing security class with the same name already existed in the target namespace.
action: Provide a unique name for the security class.
params: 1) security_class_name: The security class name. 2) namespace_name: The namespace.

description: An invalid identity value used for the RAS operator parameter at position '%s'.
cause: A Real Application Security (RAS) operator was used with an invalid identity value for one of its parameters.
action: Change the value to a valid identity value and try again.
params: 1) position: The position of the invalid parameter.

description: A valid RAS ACL name %s not found.
cause: An invalid Real Application Security (RAS) access control list (ACL) name was used as one of the operator parameters.
action: Review the names of ACLs in DBA_XS_ACLS view and try again using a valid ACL name.
params: 1) acl_name: The name of the invalid ACL provided.

description: An error was raised during the evaluation of a RAS data realm.
cause: The evaluation of a Real Application Security (RAS) data realm failed during SQL execution.
action: Enable tracing to find the cause of the error from the error stack, correct the error, and call the SQL again.

description: The ACL %s is referenced by a namespace template.
cause: An attempt was made to delete an access control list (ACL) which was referenced by a namespace template.
action: Delete the namespace template first if the ACL needs to be deleted.

description: The ACL %s is set on a user or dynamic role.
cause: An attempt was made to delete an access control list (ACL) that was set on a user or dynamic role.
action: Set the ACL on the user or dynamic role to NULL, or delete the user or dynamic role if the ACL needs to be deleted.

description: ACL %s schema must be SYS.
cause: An attempt was made to use an access control list (ACL) whose schema was not SYS.
action: Check and use an ACL whose schema is SYS.

description: ACL must not be NULL.
cause: An attempt was made to specify a NULL value for an access control list (ACL).
action: Remove the NULL parameter, or specify an existing ACL.

description: XS Security - Application Session tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: XS Security - Security Classes tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: XS Security - XS Principal tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support or development.
action: N/A

description: An invalid parameter %s value was specified for the RAS procedure.
cause: An Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS, XS) procedure was used with an invalid value for one of the parameters.
action: Review the RAS documentation for the procedure and re-run the RAS procedure using valid values for the parameters.

description: XS Security - Do not purge existing application sessions when database is restarted.
cause: This is an internal event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support or development.
action: None.

description: The attribute defined the in namespace template cannot be deleted.
cause: An attempt was made to delete an attribute that was seeded from the template from which this namespace was created.
action: Delete only custom attributes.

description: The attribute %s already exists in RAS namespace %s.
cause: An attempt was made to create an attribute that already existed within the given Real Application Security (RAS) namespace.
action: Ensure that the attribute name is unique within the RAS namespace.
params: 1) attribute_name: The name of an attribute. 2) namespace_name: The name of a namespace.

description: handler specified in the namespace template does not exist
cause: An attempt was made to create a namespace template with an invalid handler function.
action: Specify a valid handler function in the template.

description: Handler is not specified in the namespace template.
cause: An attempt was made to create a template or a custom attribute with the events specified. However, a handler function was not specified in the template.
action: Specify a valid handler function in the template.

description: Multiple UID or GUID specified for the resource.
cause: An attempt was made to create a resource with multiple UIDs or GUIDs specified in the document.
action: Provide, at most, one UID or GUID for the resource in the document.

description: User with empty GUID cannot create session.
cause: An attempt was made by an user with an empty GUID to create a session.
action: Update the GUID for the user.

description: Negative inactivity timeout value is not allowed.
cause: An attempt was made to set the inactivity timeout value to be negative.
action: Specify a non-negative inactivity timeout value.

description: Session operation %s is not allowed during global callback execution.
cause: An attempt was made to invoke another session operation while executing an Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) global callback function registered for a session operation event.
action: Remove the session operation from the callback function because it is not allowed.
params: 1) session_operation: The name of XS session operation.

description: circular callback call caused by %s
cause: A circular Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) callback call caused an infinite chain of callback function executions.
action: Check the event handling functions to identify the source of the circular callback call. Attempt the operation again after the error has been resolved.
params: 1) XS_parameter_value: The value of an XS parameter.

description: User switch is disallowed for administrative operation.
cause: An attempt was made to switch user with administrative operation.
action: Attach the application session to a database session first.

description: Source user is not anonymous in user assignment operation.
cause: An attempt was made to assign a user to a named user.
action: Change the source user to the anonymous user, then retry the operation.

description: The RAS entity name length is either too short or too long.
cause: An attempt was made to create an Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) entity with a name length of less than 1 byte (the minimum) or more than 128 bytes (the maximum).
action: Ensure that the name length is in the valid range between 1 and 128 bytes.

description: RAS entity with this name already exists.
cause: An attempt was made to create a Real Application Security (RAS) entity with a name that already belongs to another entity.
action: Use a different name and try again.

description: An unexpected constraint violation occurred during creation of an XS entity.
cause: An attempt was made to create an XS entity resulting in an unexpected constraint violation.
action: Check with the DBA or security administrator for resolution.

description: Deletion of the RAS entity is not allowed while dependencies exist.
cause: An attempt was made to delete an Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) entity with dependent entities in the system. The common cases include: - Attempting to delete a RAS user that had RAS roles granted. - Attempting to delete a RAS role that had been granted to another RAS principal. - Attempting to delete a RAS security class that had effective policies applied to tables or views. - Attempting to delete an ACL that was used in policies applied to tables or views, or was a parent of other ACLs. - Attempting to remove a privilege from a security class while the privilege had been granted to a RAS principal.
action: Remove the dependencies. For example, revoke the roles granted to the RAS user, or use the XS_ADMIN_UTIL.CASCADE_OPTION in the deletion procedure, and then try again.

description: The Real Application Security (RAS or XS) object by the name %s does not exist.
cause: The statement makes a reference to an Oracle Real Application Security (RAS or XA) object that did not exist.
action: Run SELECT * FROM DBA_XS_OBJECTS to get a list of valid RAS objects to use instead.
params: 1) entity_name: The name of the entity.

description: Real Application Security entities are not related.
cause: An attempt was made to remove a relation that did not exist.
action: Review the entity reference and try again.

description: Operation is not allowed.
cause: An unexpected operation was performed.
action: Check with the DBA or security administrator for resolution.

description: unauthorized proxy user
cause: The current user was not an authorized proxy user of the client user during a switching user operation.
action: Add the current user as a proxy user of the client user.

description: Role version numbers mismatch in server and middle-tier.
cause: There was another middle-tier attached to the server session with a different set of roles.
action: Reattach the session supplying the current set of roles.

description: Database is in readable standby mode. Changes are not saved.
cause: An attempt was made to change an application session when the database was in readable standby mode.
action: None.

description: cannot modify an application user that is currently connected
cause: An attempt was made to modify an application user that was currently logged on.
action: Ensure that the application user is logged off, then repeat the command.

description: The RAS principal name %s conflicts with another user or role name.
cause: There was already an Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) user or role with that name.
action: Specify a different user or role name. Review existing RAS users and roles by querying DBA_XS_USERS, DBA_XS_ROLES, and DBA_XS_DYNAMIC_ROLES.
params: 1) principal_name: The name of the user or role.

description: XS administrative operation failed.
cause: An unexpected error occurred during the requested XS administrative operation.
action: None.

description: Granted role is not a regular role.
cause: A nonregular role was granted to a principal.
action: Grant a regular role to a principal.

description: Circular grant for role
cause: The role was granted from itself through circular operation.
action: Fix the role grant operation.

description: Circular definition for ACL %s
cause: The ACL was inherited from itself through circular definition.
action: Fix the ACL definition.

description: Policy parameter %s did not exist.
cause: The policy parameter did not exist.
action: Review the parameter definition and try again.

description: Invalid policy parameter type
cause: Invalid parameter type was specified.
action: Use the correct parameter type.

description: Mid-tier cache synchronization failed
cause: An unexpected error occurred during mid-tier cache synchronization.
action: None.

description: Database user or role '%s' does not exist
cause: An invalid database user or role was specified as the principal name.
action: Make sure the database principal is a valid database user or role.

description: The RAS key manager was not initialized.
cause: A request to sign the Oracle Real Application Security (RAS) message could not be processed because the RAS key manager was not initialized.
action: Refer to the RAS Java documentation on XS sessions, and reinitialize the key manager and resubmit the request.

description: Application proxy user is already configured with a schema.
cause: An attempt was made to add a schema to an application proxy user that already was configured with a schema.
action: Remove the schema configuration of the application proxy user and try again.

description: Application proxy user is not configured with the schema.
cause: An attempt was made to remove a schema from an application proxy user that was not configured.
action: None.

description: Granting a role to XSGUEST is not allowed.
cause: An attempt was made to grant a role to the XSGUEST seeded user.
action: None.

description: The RAS dispatcher session has timed out and does not exist anymore.
cause: The Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS or XS) dispatcher session timed out due to inactivity. The dispatcher session is a connection between the Java application and the database used to attach and detach RAS sessions to the connection pool.
action: Increase the inactivity timeout for the dispatcher session by modifying the timeout on the XSSessionManager class with the setInactivityTimeout method.

description: The request is not signed by the dispatcher.
cause: A request was made without the signature of the dispatcher. The server is configured to only accept requests signed by the dispatcher.
action: Ask the administrator to configure the middle-tier to allow the dispatcher signature. Or, ask the administrator to configure the server to not be in dispatcher-only mode.

description: invalid session or namespace request
cause: The request message was corrupt, possibly due to network attack activities.
action: Check with the DBA or security administrator for a resolution.

description: session operation failed
cause: An attempt was made to either update a Real Application Security (RAS) application session that did not exist, or to create a RAS application session that already existed, or attach a direct-logon RAS application session.
action: Verify the namespace of the application session and try again.

description: XS application session is detached but session changes are not saved
cause: The Real Application Security session detached successfully, but session changes were not saved due to an attempt to update an application session that did not exist.
action: None.

description: This type of database link is not supported.
cause: An attempt was made to use an unsupported database link type in an XS Data Security session.
action: Use a supported database link type.

description: Diffie-Hellman key exchange failed with the supported key size %s.
cause: The Diffie-Hellman key exchange during an Oracle Real Application =Security session initialization failed.
action: Check the Diffie-Hellman public key size from middle tier. The failure is expected if the middle tier public key size does not match the supported key size at server side.

description: invalid value for argument '%s' during %s execution.
cause: An invalid input argument value was mentioned for the procedure.
action: Use a valid argument value.
params: 1) input_argument: The input argument value for the procedure. 2) procedure_name: The procedure being executed.

description: value for argument '%s' out of range
cause: Input value was out of range.
action: Use a value within allowed range.

description: Cannot complete the operation, overlapping job already exists
cause: Cleanup job already existed which spanned the given audit trail type.
action: Drop the existing job.

description: Cannot complete the operation, overlapping property already exists
cause: The property already exists which spans the given audit trail type.
action: Clear the existing property.

description: '%s' already exists
cause: The value being set already existed.
action: Delete the existing entry.

description: Incorrect job name specified
cause: The job did not exist or was not created by DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT package.
action: Create the job using DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT package.

description: Internal error: Audit table is not partitioned.
cause: There was an invalid operation on a non-partitioned table.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Property '%s' cannot be cleared
cause: The property could not be cleared.
action: None. The property can only be set or reset.

description: Cleanup not initialized for the audit trail
cause: DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.INIT_CLEANUP was not called for the erroring audit trail.
action: Invoke the procedure, DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.INIT_CLEANUP.

description: '%s' procedure is not applicable for UNIFIED_AUDIT_TRAIL.
cause: Procedures - INIT_CLEANUP, DEINIT_CLEANUP and IS_CLEANUP_INITIALIZED were not applicable for UNIFIED_AUDIT_TRAIL.
action: There is no need to call INIT_CLEANUP, DEINIT_CLEANUP or IS_CLEANUP_INITIALIZED for UNIFIED_AUDIT_TRAIL.

description: failed to determine the last modified timestamp of the audit spillover file
cause: The audit trail cleanup operation failed because the last modified timestamp of the audit spillover file could not be determined.
action: Check for the underlying operating system error. If there is no error, contact Oracle Support.

description: Internal error occurred during a DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.CLEAN_AUDIT_TRAIL procedure execution.
cause: The audit trail cleanup could not be completed because there was an internal error.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Audit table(s) cannot be moved to '%s' tablespace
cause: The tablespace was either unavailable or did not have enough space to accomodate the audit table being moved.
action: Make sure that the tablespace is online and has enough space for the audit tables being moved.

description: The audit trail is already initialized for cleanup
cause: DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.INIT_CLEANUP was already invoked for the audit trail type.
action: None.

description: Error during DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT operation
cause: Could not complete the DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT operation.
action: Check the PL/SQL error stack and trace files for a possible error. Fix the cause and retry the operation. If the error is internal or if there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Subset of audit trail is already initialized
cause: Audit Trail was initialized which spans the given audit trail type.
action: Use DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.DEINIT_CLEANUP to deinitialize conflicting audit trail types.

description: Missing value for argument '%s' in Oracle RAC enabled database
cause: The DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT API was executed in an Oracle RAC enabled database and AUDIT_TRAIL_TYPE was one of AUDIT_TRAIL_OS or AUDIT_TRAIL_XML. But, Oracle RAC instance number for which DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT API was run, was not supplied.
action: Input a valid Oracle RAC instance number for which the configuration must be done.

description: Insufficient space in '%s' tablespace, cannot complete operation
cause: Could not complete the operation because the DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT API involved movement of one or more audit tables and there was not enough space in the destination tablespace.
action: Turn on tracing using DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.SET_DEBUG_LEVEL to find the amount of space required. Then, allocate that space in the destination tablespace, even if destination tablespace datafile has AUTOEXTEND option turned on. And then, retry the operation.

description: Conflicting operation on audit table(s)
cause: Audit tables were being operated by more than one DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT API from different sessions. The simultaneous execution of the following API with one another and with itself can cause the conflict: INIT_CLEANUP, DEINIT_CLEANUP, SET_AUDIT_TRAIL_LOCATION and MOVE_DBAUDIT_TABLES.
action: Wait until the execution of one of the API's completes and try executing the API again.

description: Conflicting operation on audit files
cause: Audit files were being operated by more than one DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT API from different sessions. The simultaneous execution of the CLEAN_AUDIT_TRAIL API with itself can cause the conflict.
action: Wait until the execution of one of the API's complete and try executing the API again.

description: event to turn off audit commit delay enforcement
cause: This is an internal event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support.
action: Not applicable.

description: Error during DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT operation; database I/O suspended.
cause: An I/O attempt occurred during DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT operation and the database I/O was suspended.
action: Retry the operation after resuming database I/O suspension. If database I/O is not suspended, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Subset of audit trail is already deinitialized
cause: Audit trail was deinitialized which spans the given audit trail type.
action: Use DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.INIT_CLEANUP to initialize conflicting audit trail types.

description: DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT operation failed in one of the pluggable databases (PDBs). Check trace file %s for more information.
cause: The executed DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT operation failed in one of the PDBs.
action: Check the trace file for the PDB information where the operation failed. Fix the cause and retry the operation. If the error is internal or if there is no error, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Error during DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT operation; tablespace '%s' not available
cause: The tablespace associated with Unified Audit Trail is either invalid or is offline.
action: Check if the tablespace is valid and make sure the tablespace is online and writable.

description: DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT operation on unified audit trail failed.
cause: Audit records were not generated in the unified audit trail.
action: Generate audit records in the unified audit trail and retry the operation.

description: Conflicting operation on unified audit trail
cause: Unified audit trail is being operated by more than one DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT API from different sessions. The simultaneous execution of the following API with one another and with itself can cause the conflict: FLUSH_UNIFIED_AUDIT_TRAIL, LOAD_UNIFIED_AUDIT_FILES, CLEAN_AUDIT_TRAIL, and SET_AUDIT_TRAIL_LOCATION.
action: Wait until the execution of one of the API's complete and try executing the API again.

description: Conflicting concurrent operations using DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT procedures.
cause: One of the following DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT procedures was concurrently executed with itself or with another procedure in separate sessions, which caused a conflict. For instance, the following two procedure executions conflict with each other: - SET_LAST_ARCHIVE_TIMESTAMP - CLEAR_LAST_ARCHIVE_TIMESTAMP - CLEAN_AUDIT_TRAIL - SET_AUDIT_TRAIL_PROPERTY - CLEAR_AUDIT_TRAIL_PROPERTY
action: Wait until the execution of one of the DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT procedures completes and retry executing the procedure.

description: Input value for argument '%s' exceeds the maximum length.
cause: The identifier name generated after concatenating with 'AMGT$DP$' exceeded 30 or 128 bytes.
action: Specify a value which does not exceed the maximum length after concatenation.

description: Failure while processing the audit option for %s
cause: An attempt was made to create or alter an audit policy with more than one of the SYS owned objects from the following list: (BOOTSTRAP$, CDEF$, COL$, CON$, FET$, FILE$, FIXED_OBJ$, HISTGRM$, HIST_HEAD$, ICOL$, IND$, IND_STATS$, OBJ$, OBJECT_USAGE$, OBJ_AUTH$, PARTOBJ$, PROXY_ROLE_DATA$, SEG$, TAB$, TAB_STATS$, TS$,UET$, UNDO$, USER$)
action: Ensure the audit policy does not contain more than one object from the above list.
params: 1) object_name: Name of the object causing failure. 46340 - 46500 Use for Auditing

description: Command cannot have both BY <user-list> and IN SESSION <session-information> clauses together
cause: BY <user-list> clause was supplied with IN SESSION <session-information> clause in the command.
action: Use either BY <user-list> or IN SESSION <session-information> clause.

description: ALL STATEMENTS option cannot be supplied with BY SESSION clause
cause: An attempt was made to use ALL STATEMENTS audit option with BY SESSION clause. ALL STATEMENTS audit option can be configured with BY ACCESS only.
action: Specify BY ACCESS instead of BY SESSION.

description: NOAUDIT command cannot be executed with the IN SESSION clause
cause: An attempt was made to use the IN SESSION <session-information> clause in a NOAUDIT command.
action: Do not specify IN SESSION clause for NOAUDIT command.

description: Cannot drop AUDSYS user
cause: An attempt was made to drop the AUDSYS user that hosts the audit trail.
action: None

description: event to turn off OS flush for XML audit file write
cause: This is an internal event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services.
action: None.

description: The unified audit policy %s is already applied with the BY clause.
cause: Attempted to apply the unified audit policy with the EXCEPT clause which was already applied with the BY clause.
action: Remove the unified audit policy using the NOAUDIT statement, before reapplying with the EXCEPT clause.

description: Unified Audit policy %s already applied with the EXCEPT clause.
cause: Attempted to apply an unified audit policy with the BY clause that was already applied with the EXCEPT clause.
action: Remove the unified audit policy by using the NOAUDIT statement.

description: NOAUDIT statement with the EXCEPT clause is not allowed.
cause: An attempt was made to remove audit policy using NOAUDIT statement with the EXCEPT clause.
action: Remove audit policy selectively using NOAUDIT statement with the BY clause.

description: The unified audit policy name is either missing or invalid.
cause: A valid unified audit policy name was expected.
action: Specify a valid unified audit policy name.

description: The audit context or attribute name is either missing or invalid.
cause: A valid context or attribute name was expected.
action: Specify a valid context or attribute name.

description: The system privilege audit option mentioned is invalid.
cause: Creating or altering the unified audit policy was attempted with an invalid system privilege audit option.
action: Use a valid system privilege audit option. For a list of valid system privilege audit options, refer to Oracle Database documentation.

description: missing or invalid action audit option
cause: Creating or altering the unified audit policy was attempted with an invalid action audit option.
action: Use a valid action audit option while creating or altering the unified audit policy.

description: Unified Audit policy %s was not found.
cause: The specified unified audit policy object does not exist in the database.
action: Use the correct unified audit policy name and try again.

description: Audit policy %s already exists.
cause: The name of the audit policy already existed in the database.
action: Use a different audit policy name and try again.

description: invalid auditing option for %s type.
cause: Creating or altering the audit policy was attempted with an invalid audit option for the object type.
action: Use a valid audit option for the object type.
params: 1) type_name: The data type for which an audit option is mentioned.

description: The same auditing option cannot be both added and dropped while altering the unified audit policy.
cause: An attempt to add and drop the same auditing option was made while altering the unified audit policy.
action: Choose either to add or drop the audit option.

description: The unified audit policy cannot be dropped because it is currently enabled.
cause: Attempted to drop the unified audit policy which is currently enabled.
action: Disable the unified audit policy before dropping it.

description: Environment variable ORACLE_BASE is not defined.
cause: An attempt to obtain the value for operating system environment variable ORACLE_BASE failed.
action: Ensure that the environment variable ORACLE_BASE is set.

description: Audit directory '%s' not found.
cause: Could not find the specified audit directory.
action: Make sure the audit directory is created.

description: Audit directory '%s' could not be created.
cause: The specified audit directory could not be created.
action: Ensure that the Oracle process has permissions to create the audit directory.
params: 1) audit_dir_name: The directory where the audit .bin files are stored.

description: Audit file '%s' could not be created.
cause: The specified audit file was not created.
action: Ensure the Oracle process has the necessary permissions to create the audit files in the audit directory.

description: File '%s' is not a recognized Oracle unified audit file.
cause: The file in the Oracle audit directory was not a valid Oracle unified audit file.
action: Remove the file from the audit directory, and retry the operation.

description: Database is not opened for write; cannot complete operation.
cause: An operation requiring the database to be open in read/write mode was attempted.
action: Open the database in read/write mode.

description: The unified audit policy does not have a simple rule condition.
cause: Attempted to create or alter the unified audit policy with a complex rule condition.
action: Use a simple rule expression as an unified audit policy condition.

description: An error occurred while evaluating unified audit policy condition.
cause: Check the error stack for detailed error information.
action: Fix the errors in the error stack and retry the operation.

description: cannot connect as AUDSYS user
cause: An attempt was made to connect to the database as an AUDSYS user.
action: Do not connect to the database as an AUDSYS user.

description: audit file '%s' not found
cause: An operation was attempted on an audit file that was not available in the audit directory.
action: Ensure that the audit file exists in the designated audit directories: - $ORACLE_BASE/audit/$ORACLE_SID in the case of multitenant container database (CDB) root. - $ORACLE_BASE/audit/$ORACLE_SID/<PDB_GUID> in the case of a pluggable database (PDB).
params: 1) audit_file_name: The name of the audit file on which the operation is being attempted.

description: Unified audit policy '%s' must have at least one audit option.
cause: An attempt was made to create, alter, or enable an empty unified audit policy.
action: Use at least one audit option in the unified audit policy.
params: 1) policy_name: The name of the unified audit policy.

description: error during AUDIT or NOAUDIT of audit policy in an Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) enabled database
cause: The operation could not be completed on one or more Oracle RAC instances.
action: Check the trace file for more information. Ensure that every instance in Oracle RAC is operational and then retry the operation.

description: ASM Audit - Event to enable ASM Audit
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: Fine-grained auditing (FGA) policy owner '%s' is not available.
cause: An attempt to import the fine-grained audit (FGA) policy failed because the specified FGA policy owner has not been imported.
action: Import the specified user schema and retry the operation.
params: 1) policy_name: The fine grained audit policy name

description: Unified audit policy cannot be configured on the specified system privilege.
cause: An attempt was made to configure unified auditing on the system privilege which was not supported.
action: For a list of the supported system privilege audit options, refer to Oracle Database documentation.

description: Cannot use bind variable in VERSIONS clause when the object has FGA policy defined on it.
cause: The object being accessed had a fine-grained audit (FGA) policy defined on it and the VERSIONS clause contained a bind variable.
action: Rewrite the query without the use of a bind variable in the VERSIONS clause.

description: Generation of audit session ID failed with %d.
cause: An error was encountered while generating the audit session ID.
action: Retry the operation. If the error persists, contact Oracle Support.

description: invalid usage of EXCEPT clause
cause: Use of the EXCEPT clause and the USERS WITH GRANTED ROLES clause in the same AUDIT and NOAUDIT statements was not a valid combination
action: Do not use the EXCEPT clause here.

description: Audit configuration using global roles is not supported.
cause: A global role was found in the BY USERS WITH GRANTED ROLES list.
action: Remove the global role from the list and retry the operation.

description: cannot alter the role to a global role
cause: The role being altered to IDENTIFIED GLOBALLY had unified audit policy enabled on users to whom it was directly granted. Audit configuration using global role is not supported.
action: Use the NOAUDIT POLICY command to disable the unified audit policy on users to whom this role is directly granted.

description: incorrect order of unified audit policy options
cause: The order in which unified audit policy options were mentioned was incorrect.
action: While defining unified audit policy, specify PRIVILEGES, ACTIONS and ROLES in that order.

description: incorrect order of unified audit policy clause
cause: The order in which the ADD, DROP or CONDITION clauses were mentioned was incorrect.
action: Ensure that sure the ADD clause is followed by the DROP clause which in turn should be followed by the CONDITION clause.

description: DML and DDL operations are not allowed on table "%s"."%s".
cause: A DML or DDL operation was attempted on a unified auditing internal table.
