action: No action required. Only Oracle is allowed to perform such operations on a unified auditing internal table.

description: error during DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.TRANSFER_UNIFIED_AUDIT_RECORDS procedure execution
cause: Either the database was not open in READ WRITE mode, or the transfer of the unified audit records was already in progress.
action: Open the database in READ WRITE mode and rerun the DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.TRANSFER_UNIFIED_AUDIT_RECORDS procedure after the ongoing transfer process finishes.

description: Cannot perform this operation on unified audit internal table
cause: An attempt was made to perform an operation that is not allowed on a non-partitioned unified audit internal table.
action: No action required. This operation can only be performed on partitioned unified audit internal table.

description: unified audit files space usage in container is too high
cause: Space usage by unified audit files in the current container has exceeded the value of MAX_AUDIT_STORAGE for the container.
action: Create some space by deleting the old audit records using DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.CLEAN_AUDIT_TRAIL or open the container in the read/write mode and execute DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.LOAD_UNIFIED_AUDIT_FILES.

description: cannot alter, drop, enable, or disable Oracle predefined policies
cause: An attempt was made either to alter, drop, enable, or disable an Oracle predefined audit policy.
action: Query the AUDIT_UNIFIED_POLICIES dictionary view: - If trying to alter or drop the policies marked ORACLE_SUPPLIED = YES, then retry the operation after the database is opened in migrate mode and after acquiring the necessary privileges. - If trying to enable or disable policies marked PROTECTED = YES in an Oracle Cloud environment, then this operation will fail.

description: invalid tablespace type used
cause: An attempt was made to use a tablespace that was of type TEMPORARY, UNDO or LOST WRITE PROTECTION during execution of the DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.SET_AUDIT_TRAIL_LOCATION procedure.
action: Check the tablespace type and retry.

description: disk group to store audit files is not configured
cause: An attempt was made to move the audit files to a disk group without configuring one for auditing.
action: Execute DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.SET_AUDIT_TRAIL_LOCATION to provide a disk group for storing audit files.

description: unified audit tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services.
action: None.

description: cannot change configurations of a mandatory audit policy
cause: An audit configuration change was attempted on a unified audit policy that was marked as a mandatory audit policy.
action: Retry the operation on a non-mandatory audit policy.

description: column %s does not belong to object %s.%s
cause: An attempt was made to specify a column that does not belong to the object in the unified audit policy.
action: Specify a valid column name.

description: invalid column audit option
cause: An attempt was made to specify an invalid column audit option in the unified audit policy.
action: Specify a valid column audit option.

description: invalid column list specified
cause: An attempt was made to specify an invalid list of columns in the unified audit policy.
action: Specify a comma separated column list.

description: cannot create or alter an audit policy on dictionary tables
cause: An attempt was made to create or alter an audit policy on dictionary tables that hold audit configuration data.
action: Do not create an audit policy with SYS.AUD_OBJECT_OPT$ or SYS.AUD_OBJCOL_OPT$ dictionary tables as objects.

description: Cannot alter or drop the %s policy.
cause: An attempt is being made to either alter or drop the ORA$DICTIONARY_SENS_COL_ACCESS or ORA$DICTIONARY_SNET_RPC_ACCESS policy.
action: Only the ENABLE or DISABLE operation is allowed on this policy.

description: A fine-grained audit (FGA) policy cannot be applied to an object owned by SYS.
cause: An attempt was made to apply an FGA policy to an object owned by SYS. FGA policies cannot be applied to SYS-owned objects.
action: Do not apply an FGA policy to any SYS-owned object. You can apply an FGA policy to an object that is not owned by SYS.

description: Unable to alter the audit policy.
cause: An attempt was made to alter the audit policy which either did not exist or was dropped recently.
action: Recheck the audit policy details in AUDIT_UNIFIED_POLICIES dictionary view.

description: No new traditional AUDIT configuration is allowed. Traditional auditing is desupported, and you should use unified auditing in its place.
cause: An attempt was made to enable traditional auditing option.
action: Create an equivalent unified audit policy and enable the policy. Refer to the Database Security Guide for more information on unified auditing.

description: _ALLOW_TRADITIONAL_AUDIT_CONFIGURATION initialization parameter cannot be set for this database.
cause: An attempt is made to set _ALLOW_TRADITIONAL_AUDIT_CONFIGURATION initialization parameter.
action: Traditional Audit has been desupported. Traditional Audit configuration cannot be enabled for this database.

description: Tablespace for AUDIT_TRAIL_UNIFIED type does not have the same block size as the current tablespace.
cause: UNIFIED AUDIT TRAIL is stored in a partition table and all partitions of that table must be stored in tablespaces with the same block size.
action: Specify a tablespace with the same block size as the current tablespace.

description: Failure while processing the audit option for %s
cause: An attempt is being made to create or alter a common audit policy with one of the SYS owned objects from the following list: (BOOTSTRAP$, CDEF$, COL$, CON$, FET$, FILE$, FIXED_OBJ$, HISTGRM$, HIST_HEAD$, ICOL$, IND$, IND_STATS$, OBJ$, OBJECT_USAGE$, OBJ_AUTH$, PARTOBJ$, PROXY_ROLE_DATA$, SEG$, TAB$, TAB_STATS$, TS$,UET$, UNDO$, USER$)
action: Ensure the common audit policy does not contain object from the above list. Consider creating a local audit policy instead.
params: 1) object_name: Name of the object causing failure.

description: Audit policy condition clause exceeds the maximum allowed limit.
cause: An attempt is being made to create an audit policy with the condition clause length greater than the allowed limit.
action: The audit policy condition can have a maximum of 65535 characters.

description: Error during audit trail cleanup. Number of processes increased.
cause: The number of active processes exceeds the preallocated limit during DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.CLEAN_AUDIT_TRAIL procedure for operating system or XML audit trails (AUDIT_TRAIL_OS or AUDIT_TRAIL_XML type).
action: Retry the audit trail cleanup operation.

description: Number of columns on an object in the audit policy definition exceeds the maximum limit %s.
cause: An attempt is being made to create an audit policy with more columns on an object than the maximum allowed limit.
action: Ensure that the number of columns specified for each object in the audit policy definition is within the maximum allowed limit. The maximum limit can be updated by setting the initialization parameter MAX_COLUMNS.

description: The value of LAST_ARCHIVE_TIME provided (%s) is a future timestamp. The current time is (%s)
cause: The value of LAST_ARCHIVE_TIME provided in the DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.SET_LAST_ARCHIVE_TIMESTAMP procedure is a future timestamp, which is not allowed. Please note that the LAST_ARCHIVE_TIME must be specified in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) when the audit trail types are AUDIT_TRAIL_AUD_STD, AUDIT_TRAIL_FGA_STD, AUDIT_TRAIL_UNIFIED_FILES or AUDIT_TRAIL_UNIFIED_TABLE and the LAST_ARCHIVE_TIME must be specified as the local time zone time when the audit trail types are AUDIT_TRAIL_OS or AUDIT_TRAIL_XML.
action: Provide a value of LAST_ARCHIVE_TIME which is not in the future. Make sure you specify the value in the correct time zone based on the value of audit trail type.
params: 1) last_archive_time: The value of LAST_ARCHIVE_TIME provided. 2) current_timestamp: The current timestamp.

description: User is not a common user. Common unified audit policies can be enforced only on common users.
cause: An attempt was made to apply the common audit configuration to a local user. The common audit configuration can be applied only to common users.
action: Specify a common user.

description: A non-common object was specified in an AUDIT POLICY statement.
cause: Object audit option for the common audit policy was specified on a local object. A common audit policy can have object audit options on common objects only.
action: Specify a common object.

description: Local traditional audit configuration cannot be created in CDB root and application root.
cause: An attempt was made to create a local audit configuration in the CDB$ROOT or the application root. Local audit configuration can be created only when connected to a pluggable database.
action: Connect or switch the session to a pluggable database to create a local audit configuration.

description: AUDIT or NOAUDIT command cannot specify ON <object> and CONTAINER clauses together.
cause: An attempt was made to specify the CONTAINER clause with the AUDIT or NOAUDIT command while configuring object auditing. The CONTAINER clause is not supported for object auditing using the SQL AUDIT or NOAUDIT command.
action: Do not specify the CONTAINER clause while configuring object auditing using the SQL AUDIT or NOAUDIT command.

description: The role is not a common role.
cause: An attempt was made to apply the common audit configuration to a local role. Common audit configuration can be applied to common roles only.
action: Specify a common role.

description: FGA handler schema is not a common user.
cause: An attempt was made to create a fine-grained Audit (FGA) policy on a common object, but the associated handler schema was not a common user.
action: Specify a common user for the FGA handler schema.

description: Fine-grained audit (FGA) object name is not a common object.
cause: An attempt was made to create a common fine-grained audit (FGA) policy on a local object. A common FGA policy can only be configured on common object.
action: Specify a common object for the FGA policy.

description: not connected to root container
cause: An attempt was made to create a fine-grained audit (FGA) policy on an object-linked common object from within a pluggable database.
action: Connect to the root and create the FGA policy on object-linked common objects.

description: invalid combination of values for desupported AUDIT_TRAIL initialization parameter. Traditional auditing is desupported, and you should use unified auditing in its place.
cause: An attempt is being made to set the value of the desupported AUDIT_TRAIL initialization parameter to a wrong combination of the allowed values.
action: Reconsider the need to specify the desupported parameter. Only if needed, specify one among the following valid values: { none | os | db [, extended] | xml [, extended] }

description: invalid ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT command
cause: NA
action: NA

description: missing KEYSTORE, ENCRYPTION, KEY, or TAG keyword
cause: An internal error for debugging was raised.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: missing OPEN or CLOSE keyword
cause: An internal error for debugging was raised.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: invalid ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT CREATE command
cause: An invalid clause was specified with the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT CREATE statement. Valid clauses include KEYSTORE, LOCAL, AUTO_LOGIN, ENCRYPTION, and KEY.
action: Specify a valid clause with the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT CREATE statement.

description: invalid or missing keystore file name
cause: The required keystore file name was invalid or missing.
action: Specify a valid keystore file name.

description: Master key identifier is invalid or missing.
cause: Either a value for Master key identifier was not specified, or the length of the Master key identifier value is invalid.
action: Provide a valid value for the Master key identifier.

description: tag is invalid or missing
cause: Either the value of the tag was not specified or the length of the tag value was invalid.
action: Provide a valid value for the tag.

description: client secret is invalid or missing
cause: None.
action: None.

description: client identifier is invalid or missing
cause: None
action: None

description: export or import secret is invalid or missing
cause: None.
action: None.

description: expecting SELECT query that returns the master key identifiers
cause: An internal error for debugging was raised.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: import file name is invalid or missing
cause: An internal error for debugging was raised.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: Export file name is invalid or missing.
cause: Either a value for export file name was not used, or the length of the export file name is invalid.
action: Provide a valid value for the export file name.

description: missing WITH or CONTAINER keyword
cause: NA
action: NA

description: master key is invalid or missing
cause: NA
action: NA

description: Master key identifier is invalid or missing.
cause: Either a value for the master key identifier was not specified, or the length of the master key identifier value is invalid.
action: Provide a valid value for the master key identifier.

description: Event to enable Key Vault mode for GoldenGate
cause: N/A
action: This event is enabled when the database is used by Oracle Key Vault internally.
note: THIS IS NOT A USER ERROR NUMBER/MESSAGE. THIS DOES NOT NEED TO BE TRANSLATED OR DOCUMENTED.

description: Keystore backup cannot be completed.
cause: Either the backup location was not an Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) path name when the configured keystore location was an Oracle ASM path, or the backup location was an Oracle ASM path name when the configured keystore location was not an Oracle ASM path.
action: Either specify an Oracle ASM path name for the backup location if the keystore location is an Oracle ASM path or specify a non-Oracle ASM path name for the backup location if the keystore location is not an Oracle ASM path.

description: no backup identifier specified
cause: Backup identifier was not specified.
action: Provide a valid backup identifier.

description: Backup keystore location is incorrect.
cause: Keystore location where the backup was to be created was incorrect.
action: Provide a valid location to backup the keystore.

description: cannot create the keystore file name
cause: The keystore name could not be formed. This could be the result of an incorrectly specified keystore location.
action: Specify a valid keystore location

description: cannot find the source keystore
cause: The source keystore for which the backup was requested was not found.
action: Verify that the source keystore exists and try again.

description: backup keystore already exists
cause: A backup of the keystore of the same name already existed in the given location.
action: Change the location of the backup keystore or the backup identifier of the backup keystore and try again.

description: cannot create a backup of the keystore
cause: The backup of the keystore could not be created.
action: Check the trace file for more information and try again.

description: keystore password mismatch
cause: The specified keystore password did not match the password of the keystore that was open.
action: Specify the correct keystore password. If a keystore migration was done and primary and secondary keysotres are used, then provide the password for the primary keystore.

description: Cannot alter the software keystore password.
cause: Attempted to alter the software keystore password.
action: Check the viability of the keystore and replace the keystore from the backup if required. Retry altering the keystore password.

description: Keystore was not open after the ALTER KEYSTORE operation.
cause: The keystore password was changed. However, the keystore was closed during this change, and the change could not be preserved.
action: Reopen the keystore with the new password.

description: Keystore cannot be created at location %s.
cause: The keystore cannot be created at the specified location because a keystore of the same type exists in that location.
action: Specify a different location to create the keystore or rename the keystore file name. If no keystore exists and the operation is failing, check the trace file and retry.

description: The keystore must be backed up.
cause: The keystore was not backed up. For this operation to proceed, the keystore must be backed up.
action: Try again using the WITH BACKUP clause, or first backup the wallet using the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT BACKUP KEYSTORE command and then retry.

description: Password-based keystore does not exist.
cause: Password-based keystore was missing for this operation. An auto login keystore can only be created from a password-based keystore.
action: Specify a location where the password-based keystore exists and retry.

description: creation of a password-based keystore failed
cause: Password-based keystore could not be created at the specified location due to either incorrect file permissions for Oracle on the specified location or due to the nonexistence of the specified location.
action: Check the trace file for more information, create permissions on the specified location, or specify a different location and try again.

description: Cannot create a local auto login keystore at location %s.
cause: The local auto login keystore could not be created at the specified location due to incorrect password specified for the password-based keystore, due to incorrect file permissions for Oracle on the specified location, or the specified location does not exist.
action: Check the trace file for more information, specify the correct password for the password-based keystore, create permissions on the specified location, or specify a different location and retry.

description: Auto login keystore creation failed at location %s.
cause: The auto login keystore could not be created at the specified location due to the incorrect password used for the password-based keystore, incorrect file permissions for Oracle on the specified location, or nonexistence of the specified location.
action: Check the trace file for more information, use the correct password for the password-based keystore, create permissions on the specified location, or specify a different location and retry.

description: cannot add second keystore to the target keystore
cause: The second keystore could not be added to the target keystore.
action: Check trace files for more information. Delete the target keystore and try merging the two keystores again.

description: cannot add first keystore to the target keystore
cause: The first keystore could not be added to the target keystore.
action: Check trace files for more information. Delete the target keystore and try merging the two keystores again.

description: Merging keystores failed.
cause: The keystores could not be merged.
action: Check trace files for more information. If the target keystore is corrupted, replace it from the backup and retry.

description: backup of keystore failed during migration
cause: The keystore location was not correctly configured.
action: Either the keystore location is missing or it is not correct. Specify the correct keystore location using WALLET_ROOT.

description: incorrect file name for exporting keys
cause: The file name of the file to which keys from the keystore will be written was incorrect or invalid.
action: Verify the file name. Ensure that both the full path and the file name are provided.

description: incorrect file name for importing keys
cause: The file name of the file from which the keys will be read and saved in the keystore was incorrect or invalid.
action: Verify the file name. Ensure that both the full path and the file name are provided.

description: The key export destination file already exists.
cause: The file name that was specified as the export destination for the keys being exported from the keystore was already in existence.
action: Specify a different file name that does not exist.

description: The file %s, containing the keys to import into the keystore, does not exist.
cause: The specified file, containing the keys to import into the keystore does not exist.
action: Specify the name of an existing file that contains keys exported from the keystore.

description: The creation or open of file to store the exported keys failed.
cause: The creation or opening of the file specified as the key export destination, where the keys exported from the keystore were to be written, failed.
action: Verify that the file name is valid and that the Oracle process has sufficient privilege to create, open, and write to the file.

description: open of file from which keys are to be imported failed
cause: The file specified as the key import source, from which the keys were to be imported into the keystore, could not be opened.
action: Verify that the file name is valid and that the Oracle process has sufficient privilege to read the file.

description: file from which keys are to be imported is invalid or lacks needed file permission
cause: The file specified as the key import source from which the keys were to be imported was not a valid file or did not have the needed file access permission.
action: Specify a valid file containing keys which were previously exported from the keystore. Also, ensure that the file has the read and write access permission.

description: The specified protection differs from what is specified in the file.
cause: The file specified as the key import source, from which the keys are to be imported, had different protection from what was specified in the SQL command.
action: Provide a valid protection option, ensuring that it is the same protection option that is in the file from which the keys are to be imported.

description: Cannot commit the keys to the keystore.
cause: Writing the keys to the keystore failed.
action: Verify that the keystore is not corrupt. Copy the keystore from the backup if it is corrupt and retry.

description: The master encryption key with the specified identifier does not exist.
cause: The master encryption key with the specified identifier does not exist in the keystore.
action: Specify a valid master encryption key identifier for the SQL command and then retry the command.

description: cannot retrieve information for a master encryption key identifier
cause: The master encryption key or the master encryption key information that is associated with a specified master encryption key identifier did not exist.
action: Check the contents of the trace file to identify the faulty master key identifier. Either fix or drop the faulty master encryption key, and then retry the command.

description: cannot create a master key
cause: Master key creation failed.
action: Check the trace file for errors and retry the command.

description: cannot create tag for the master key
cause: Creation of the tag for the specified master key failed.
action: Check the contents of the trace file for errors and retry the command.

description: cannot retrieve master encryption key information
cause: Retrieval of the master encryption key information for the specified master encryption key identifier failed.
action: Check the contents of the trace file for errors and then retry the command.

description: cannot add the imported keys to the keystore
cause: The operation of writing the imported keys to the keystore failed.
action: Check the contents of the trace file for more information on the cause of the failure and retry the command.

description: no valid keys in the file from which keys are to be imported
cause: The specified keystore, from which keys are to be imported, does not contain any valid keys.
action: Check if the keys to be imported are already present by listing KEY_ID from V$ENCRYPTION_KEYS. Ensure that the keys are correctly exported from pluggable database (PDB) or CDB$ROOT at the source database.

description: operation not valid for container database
cause: The specified operation was not supported for the container database.
action: None.

description: The source keystores are the same.
cause: The source keystores to be merged were the same. There is no need to merge these keystores.
action: Check the locations and types of the specified keystores. Specify the correct path and types for the source keystores, if necessary.

description: keystore not open in the container
cause: The keystore was not open in the container.
action: Open the keystore in the container.

description: master encryption keys for the given PDB not found
cause: The master encryption keys for the specified pluggable database (PDB) could not be retrieved.
action: Check if the master encryption keys were generated for the specified PDB and retry the command.

description: the source and target keystores are the same
cause: The specified source and target keystores to be merged were the same. There is no need to merge these keystores.
action: Check the locations and types of the specified keystores. Specify the correct path and types for the source and target keystores, if necessary.

description: keystore not open in root container
cause: The root container keystore was not open.
action: Open the root container keystore.

description: master keys not created for all PDBs
cause: Creation of the master key failed for one or more pluggable databases (PDBs).
action: Check the trace files for errors. Create the keys in PDBs where the operation failed or retry the command.

description: master encryption keys not created for all PDBs for REKEY
cause: Creation of the master encryption key failed for one or more pluggable databases (PDBs), therefore REKEY failed for these PDBs.
action: Check the trace files for errors. REKEY the keys in PDBs where the master keys could not be created or retry the command.

description: master keys not created for any PDBs during REKEY
cause: Creation of the master key failed for all pluggable databases (PDBs).
action: Check the contents of the trace file for more information on the cause of the failure and retry the command.

description: master keys not activated for all PDBs during REKEY
cause: Activation of the master key failed for one or more pluggable databases (PDBs) and as such REKEY failed for these PDBs.
action: Check the trace files for errors. Activate the keys in PDBs where the master keys were created but not activated or retry the command.

description: master keys not created or activated for all PDBs during REKEY
cause: Creation of the master key failed for one or more pluggable databases (PDBs). Further, activation of one or more created master keys also failed for some PDBs and as such REKEY failed on these PDBs.
action: Check the trace files for errors. REKEY the PDBs where the master keys could not be created. Activate the keys in PDBs where the master keys were created but not activated or retry the command.

description: client not found in the keystore
cause: An entry with the given client name was not found in the keystore.
action: Add the secret for the given client to the keystore, if required.

description: This client already exists in the keystore.
cause: An entry with the given client name was already in existence in the keystore.
action: Delete or update the entry with the client name.

description: the target keystore does not exist
cause: The location specified for the target keystore did not contain a valid keystore, or target keystore did not have valid file permissions.
action: Specify a different location for the target keystore where it exists. Also, check the file permissions of the target keystore.

description: Client secret keystore operation failed.
cause: The client secret keystore add, update or delete operation failed.
action: Open the keystore and retry. If the operation fails, check the trace files for more details.

description: master key not set in root container
cause: Master key was not set in the root container.
action: Set the Master key in the root container.

description: backup keystore file name could not be stored
cause: The file name of the keystore backup could not be recorded in props$.
action: Open the keystore and retry the backup operation.

description: The write operation to the export file failed.
cause: Oracle was unable to write an entry to the export file.
action: Check the trace file for more information and retry the operation. If there is no trace information and trying the operation again fails, contact Oracle Support.

description: The read operation from the export file failed.
cause: Oracle was unable to read an entry from the export file.
action: Check the trace file for more information and retry the operation. If there is no trace information and trying the operation again fails, contact Oracle Support.

description: The write operation of keys for the export failed.
cause: Oracle was unable to write an entry for export.
action: Check the trace file for more information and retry the operation. If there is no trace information and trying the operation again fails, contact Oracle Support.

description: read of keys for import failed
cause: Oracle was unable to read an entry for import.
action: Check the trace file for more information and retry the operation. If there is no trace information and trying the operation again fails, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: specified backup identifier exceeds maximum length
cause: The backup identifier within the Oracle Automatic Storage Management // (Oracle ASM) file name of the keystore exceeded the maximum length of // 12 characters.
action: Specify a backup identifier that does not exceed the limit.

description: cannot encrypt an identity column created with GENERATED BY DEFAULT or GENERATED ALWAYS
cause: An attempt was made to encrypt an identity column created with GENERATED BY DEFAULT or GENERATED ALWAYS keywords.
action: An identity column created with the GENERATED BY DEFAULT or GENERATED ALWAYS keywords cannot be encrypted.

description: Missing or invalid master key encryption algorithm - %s
cause: The specified encryption algorithm for the master key was missing or invalid in the command.
action: Specify a valid algorithm: 'AES256' or 'ARIA256'.
params: 1) algorithm_name: The name of the algorithm.

description: Pluggable database (PDB) master keys must be exported.
cause: The master keys of the PDB were not exported.
action: Export the master keys of the pluggable database before unplugging the database from its container database or use the one-step unplug-plug using 'encrypt using' clause.

description: reverse migration failed for PDB
cause: Reverse migration failed for one or more pluggable databases (PDBs).
action: Check the trace files for errors. Retry the command.

description: Addition of master key string not supported with CONTAINER=ALL.
cause: Attempted to add a master key with the same identifier to more than one container database (CDB). A user specified master key string with a master key identifier can only be used once in a CDB.
action: Remove the CONTAINER=ALL clause and retry.

description: master key identifier exists in the keystore
cause: An attempt was made to add a master key with a master key identifier that was already present in the keystore.
action: Specify a different value for the master key identifier in the master key string.

description: invalid master key identifier or master key value
cause: The master key identifier or master key value was invalid. To be valid, the values supplied for both the master key identifier and the master key value must be hex-encoded and must have the following properties: - For a master key value to be valid, its length must be a valid key length for the specified encryption algorithm. - For a master key identifier to be valid, it must have a length of 16 bytes. - For a master key identifier to be valid, it must have a non-zero value.
action: Specify a correct value for the master key identifier or master key in the master key string.

description: missing or invalid master key string
cause: The master key string was missing or invalid.
action: Specify the correct master key string.

description: operation not supported for HSM
cause: The specified operation is not supported with Hardware Security Module (HSM).
action: Check the trace file for more details.

description: cannot move a master key
cause: The master key could not be moved out of the keystore.
action: Check whether the specified master key identifiers are valid, and if they are in the V$ENCRYPTION_KEYS view. Container keys can be moved from the CDB$ROOT only when the container is unplugged and dropped from the multitenant container database (CDB). Check the trace file for additional errors, if needed. Retry the command. If an attempt is made to move keys of a database that has only one key, the current and the only key cannot be moved.

description: specified master key identifier does not exist in the keystore
cause: An attempt was made to move a master key that did not exist in the keystore.
action: Check if the master key identifier exists in the keystore by querying the V$ENCRYPTION_KEYS view.

description: could not create wallet
cause: The new wallet that was used to store the keys to be moved could not be created. The cause could be the lack of permissions to write to the directory for the Oracle user, or the directory did not exist.
action: Either check the permissions for the Oracle user on the directory or check if the directory exists.

description: The value of the KEYSTORE_CONFIGURATION attribute is invalid.
cause: An attempt was made to set or use an invalid value for the KEYSTORE_CONFIGURATION attribute of the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter.
action: Use a valid value for the KEYSTORE_CONFIGURATION attribute of the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter. When using WALLET_ROOT, set the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter correctly in both the root and in the pluggable database. A value must be provided for the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter if a value is provided for the WALLET_ROOT instance initialization parameter, in order to fully specify the keystore configuration of the CDB$ROOT and of the pluggable database (either both parameters must be present, or both must be absent). For an ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT ISOLATE KEYSTORE operation, the KEYSTORE_CONFIGURATION attribute of the CDB$ROOT must have the value FILE. For an ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT ISOLATE KEYSTORE operation, if a value for the KEYSTORE_CONFIGURATION attribute is set in the pluggable database, it must have the value FILE. If the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter is not set in the pluggable database, the isolation operation automatically sets its KEYSTORE_CONFIGURATION attribute to FILE.

description: Cannot close wallet while in use.
cause: Attempted to close the wallet when it was in use.
action: Close the wallet in every pluggable database (PDB) that is configured with an isolated wallet. Alternatively, use the FORCE KEYSTORE CLOSE clause of the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT command.

description: The WALLET_ROOT location is missing or invalid.
cause: An attempt was made to perform a keystore operation when the instance initialization parameter WALLET_ROOT was missing or invalid. Starting Oracle Database version 23c, the location for Transparent Data Encryption's (TDE) keystore can be configured using the WALLET_ROOT parameter only.
action: Start the database after setting the WALLET_ROOT instance initialization parameter to the directory where all of the wallets are stored.

description: The keys are already in the root keystore.
cause: An attempt was made to unite an isolated keystore with the root keystore, but the keys of the isolated keystore were already present in the root keystore.
action: No action is required. Check the value of the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter of your system and ensure that you are issuing the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT UNITE KEYSTORE command in the correct pluggable database.

description: The value of the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter is invalid.
cause: An attempt was made to set or use an invalid value for the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter.
action: Use a valid value for the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter. The KEYSTORE_CONFIGURATION attribute must be specified and must have a valid value. During recovery, the CONTAINER attribute can also be specified and the value must be a valid container name. The CONTAINER attribute can only be specified when the TDE_CONFIGURATION instance initialization parameter is modified in CDB$ROOT, not when it is modified in a pluggable database.

description: A master key is required by another pluggable database.
cause: An attempt was made to isolate a master key or move a master key out of the keystore when it was still required by another pluggable database. Another pluggable database still required the master key if the pluggable databases were clones of each other.
action: Before attempting to isolate or move the keys of a pluggable database, perform an ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT SET KEY command on each pluggable database that requires the master key, in order to remove any dependency on the master key being isolated or moved. If necessary, include the FORCE clause and issue the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT FORCE ISOLATE KEYSTORE command, which causes the master keys of the pluggable database to be copied to the isolated keystore rather than moved to it, so that the keys remain available to any pluggable database that requires them. The ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT MOVE command has no FORCE option.

description: Keystore password required.
cause: The keystore password clause was not provided for this SQL command.
action: Retry the command with a keystore password clause.

description: CDB$ROOT is not open.
cause: CDB$ROOT was not open.
action: Open the CDB$ROOT and then retry the command.

description: cannot create a keystore
cause: A keystore could not be created. A combination of the following conditions prevented the operation: 1. The pluggable database (PDB) was not open in read/write mode. Note that the PDB must be open in read/write mode for the KEYSTORE_MODE configuration of the PDB to be automatically changed to isolated mode during the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT CREATE KEYSTORE command. 2. The KEYSTORE_MODE configuration of the PDB was in united mode (rather than isolated mode).
action: Open the PDB in read/write mode or configure the PDB to be in isolated mode, and then retry the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT CREATE KEYSTORE command.

description: failed to copy or move wallet
cause: An attempt was made to either copy or move the isolated wallet of the pluggable database (PDB) that was plugged.
action: Ensure that the source wallet location and the file specified in XML exist on disk and are accessible from this database. Also, ensure that WALLET_ROOT is set and the directory specified in WALLET_ROOT exists on the disk.

description: failed to delete source wallet
cause: An attempt was made to delete the source wallet file during the pluggable database (PDB) plug with a MOVE clause.
action: Ensure that the source wallet file and the directory allow deletion of the wallet.

description: failed to switch over the PKCS#11 library
cause: An attempt was made to switch over the PKCS#11 library and there was a problem finding or loading the new library.
action: Ensure that the: - PKCS11_LIBRARY_LOCATION parameter is set when the database is started. - Value of the PKCS11_LIBRARY_LOCATION parameter begins with /opt/oracle/extapi/64/pkcs11/. - Path in the fully qualified library name of the PKCS11_LIBRARY_LOCATION parameter does not contain any component which is a symbolic link. - Each directory component of the path is owned by the root user and is writable by only the root user (for example, drwxr-xr-x root root).

description: Switching over the PKCS#11 library is not supported.
cause: The switchover command was executed on a system with an unsupported configuration of the Oracle Advanced Security Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) keystore.
action: Configure the TDE keystore to use Oracle Key Vault (OKV) and rerun the command.

description: Cannot create keystore for pluggable database (PDB) when the PDB's keystore status is OPEN.
cause: Password-based keystore could not be created for the PDB, because the PDB's current keystore status is 'OPEN'.
action: Close the PDB's keystore and retry.

description: Key is set for the pluggable database (PDB). Cannot create the password-based keystore.
cause: The password-based keystore could not be created for the PDB, because the PDB was using a key from the current keystore of the PDB.
action: Use the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT ISOLATE KEYSTORE statement to create a password-based keystore; so that, the keys for the PDB are automatically moved to the new keystore.

description: PKCS#11 library was loaded from legacy location
cause: When the database instance was started, the Public Key Cryptography Standard (PKCS) #11 library was discovered at the legacy location, which is /opt/oracle/extapi/64/hsm/. The switchover command was not supported because the PKCS#11 library was loaded from the legacy location.
action: Configure the PKCS11_LIBRARY_LOCATION and specify the library in this location /opt/oracle/extapi/64/pkcs11/ and then restart the database.

description: PKCS#11 library location was invalid
cause: The switchover command was executed with an invalid or insecure Public Key Cryptography Standard (PKCS) #11 library location.
action: Ensure that: - The PKCS#11 library is provisioned under the location that was provided in the command. - The fully qualified filename of the library begins with /opt/oracle/extapi/64/pkcs11/. - The fully qualified filename of the library does not exceed 255 characters. - The fully qualified filename of the library does not contain any component which is a symbolic link. - Each directory component of the path is owned by the root user and is writable by only the root user (for example, drwxr-xr-x root root).

description: PKCS#11 library was already loaded with this version
cause: The switchover command was executed on a system that is currently using the library to which the command is trying to switch over.
action: Check if the fully qualified file name of the library to switch over to needs to be corrected and rerun the command.

description: The autologin wallet already exists on disk.
cause: An attempt was made to isolate the keystore but it failed due to an existing autologin (cwallet.sso) wallet under {WALLET_ROOT}/<PDBGUID>/tde/ directory. cwallet.sso was not overwritten because it could contain client secrets that may have been added manually when the keystore was previously isolated.
action: Rename the cwallet.sso file under {WALLET_ROOT}/{PDBGUID}/tde/ directory (to move it out of the way) and then retry the command.

description: keystore is already in isolated mode
cause: An attempt to isolate the keystore failed because the keystore of the pluggable database was already configured in isolated mode.
action: No action required. This operation can only be performed when the keystore of the pluggable database is configured in united mode.

description: keystore is already in united mode
cause: An attempt to unite the keystore failed because the keystore of the pluggable database was already configured in united mode.
action: No action required. This operation can only be performed when the keystore of the pluggable database is configured in isolated mode.

description: The password-based keystore was not open in root container.

action: Open the password-based keystore in the root container.

description: The keystore of the PDB is not in a closed state on all instances.
cause: The TDE_CONFIGURATION for the pluggable database (PDB) cannot be modified because the keystore of the PDB is not in a closed state on all instances.
action: Close the keystore of the PDB on all instances. If the PDB was configured to use an autologin keystore, then before attempting to update the configuration of the PDB, change the configuration of the PDB to use a password-based keystore, and close the keystore of the PDB.

description: Transparent Data Encryption(TDE) keystore configuration cannot be set
cause: An attempt is being made to set a value for the TDE_CONFIGURATION parameter either in PDB$SEED or in ROOT or NON-CDB using container attribute.
action: No action needed. TDE_CONFIGURATION does not need to be set in PDB$SEED as the keystore for PDB$SEED cannot be ISOLATED and it cannot be set for NON-CDB or CDB$ROOT when using container attribute.

action: Re-create the password file and grant the necessary administrative privileges to users.

cause: An attempt was made to apply password file changes made on the primary database to the password file of the standby database, but there was a password file format mismatch which prevented the operation.
action: Re-create the password file on the standby database with the same format as that of the primary database.

description: The password file is not in the 12.2 format.
cause: An attempt was made to perform one of the following operations, but none of these operations are allowed while the password file is in LEGACY or in release 12.1 format. - Attempting to grant an administrative privilege to an external user (a user created as IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY). - Attempting to change the authentication type of an administrative-privileged user from PASSWORD to EXTERNAL. - When a common user has an administrative privilege granted in a pluggable database (PDB) but no longer exists in the CDB$ROOT container, attempting to create this common user again in the root as IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY. - Attempting to grant an administrative privilege to a user with multi-factor authentication enabled. - Attempting to add multi-factor authentication to an administrative-privileged user.
action: Create the password file in 12.2 format or migrate the existing password file to 12.2 format, then retry the operation.
