cause: The rule set being associated to the factor did not exist.
action: Review the definition for accuracy and retry the operation.

description: error occurred from factor %s evaluation expression %s
cause: The factor retrieval method resulted in an error.
action: Review the retrieval method definition for accuracy and correct it as required.

description: Error occurred from factor %s validation expression %s.
cause: The factor retrieval method resulted in an invalid value based on its validation method.
action: Review the factor definition and correct it as required.

description: incorrect identified by value for Factor %s
cause: The factor identified by value is incorrect
action: Please review the factor definition and correct it as required

description: multiple identities defined for Factor %s
cause: The factor has duplicate identities defined
action: Please review the factor definition and correct it as required

description: incorrect labeled by value for Factor %s
cause: The factor labeled by value is incorrect
action: Please review the factor definition and correct it as required

description: command rule violation for %s on %s
cause: The attempted operation failed due to a command rule violation.
action: Ensure that you have sufficient authorization and retry the operation.

description: realm violation for %s on %s.%s
cause: The attempted operation failed due to insufficient realm authorization.
action: Ensure you have sufficient authorization and retry the operation.

description: incorrect evaluation options value for Factor %s
cause: The factor evaluations options value is incorrect
action: Please review the factor definition and correct it as required

description: NULL value returned by factor %s evaluation expression %s
cause: The factor evaluated to a NULL value.
action: Review the factor definition and correct it as required.

description: NULL value for trust level of factor %s
cause: The factor had a NULL trust level.
action: Review the factor definition and correct it as required.

description: negative trust level for factor %s
cause: The factor had a negative trust level.
action: Review the factor definition and correct it as required.

description: ALWAYS AUDIT option set for factor %s
cause: The factor audit option was set to always audit.
action: No action required.

description: ALWAYS AUDIT option set for rule set %s
cause: The rule set audit option was set to always audit.
action: No action required.

description: Realm violation for the EXECUTE command
cause: A realm violation has occurred for a realm-protected stored procedure.
action: In order to invoke the realm-protected procedure, you must have GRANT privileges to execute the procedure, or you must be authorized to operate in the procedure's realm.

description: Command Rule violation for the EXECUTE command
cause: A command rule violation occurred when trying to perform the EXECUTE command for a stored procedure protected by a command rule.
action: Ask the Database Vault administrator to perform the operation or remove the command rule for the protected stored procedure.

description: Insufficient realm privileges to %s on %s.
cause: An operation failed due to insufficient privileges. This is due to an attempt to violate an Oracle Database Vault realm security policy currently enabled and enforced.
action: Check and obtain sufficient privileges for this operation and retry.

description: Cannot use %s due to Oracle Database Vault policy.
cause: The attempted operation failed because Oracle Database Vault policy currently prevents the related feature from being used.
action: Ask the Oracle Database Vault administrator to allow the feature to be used.
params: 1) feature_name: The name of restricted feature.

description: The DVSYS and DVF users are not allowed to switch containers.
cause: An attempt was made to switch containers while connecting as DVSYS or DVF, which is not allowed.
action: Connect as a different user and try again.

description: Cannot connect to database due to Oracle Database Vault configuration.
cause: An attempt to connect to DVSYS or DVF accounts failed because the account is disable on Oracle Database Vault.
action: Ask the Oracle Database Vault administrator to enable the account, or use an account already enabled.

description: Database Vault violation
cause: The attempted operation failed due to a realm or command rule violation.
action: Ensure that you have sufficient authorization and retry the operation.

description: Insufficient Oracle Database Vault authorization for %s.
cause: The attempted operation was denied because it required the specified Oracle Database Vault authorization that you did not have.
action: Ensure that you have sufficient authorization, and retry the operation.
params: 1) authorization_name: The name of the required authorization.

description: Database Vault restricted operation
cause: The attempted operation was denied as Oracle Database Vault was enabled and the operation was not allowed.
action: No action is required.

description: Oracle Database Vault administrative operations require database vault administrative roles.
cause: The current operation was denied because you did not have appropriate Oracle Database Vault administrative roles.
action: Contact the Oracle Database Vault administrators to perform the appropriate action.

description: Oracle Database Vault Operations Control violation.
cause: The operation was denied because when Oracle Database Vault Operations Control is enabled, common users are not allowed access local objects in a pluggable database (PDB).
action: Contact the Oracle Database Vault administrators and inform them your operation was denied.

description: Failed to evaluate Oracle Database Vault rules due to invoker's rights PL/SQL program unit used in the rule.
cause: The Oracle Database Vault rule set evaluation failed because an invoker's rights PL/SQL program unit was used in one of the rules. This is not allowed.
action: Review and update the relevant rules and use only definer's rights PL/SQL program units.

description: Policy %s for Oracle Database Vault exists.
cause: A policy with this name already exists.
action: Choose a unique policy name and retry the operation, or skip the command because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Database Vault policy %s was not found.
cause: The policy being requested does not exist.
action: Choose a policy name that exists and retry the operation.

description: The object already belongs to an Oracle Database Vault policy.
cause: An attempt to add a realm or command rule to more than one Oracle Database Vault policy failed.
action: Make sure the realm or command rule does not belong to any Oracle Database Vault policy and retry the operation, or skip the operation because it is not needed.

description: The object does not belong to Database Vault policy %s.
cause: An attempt to delete a realm or command rule from an Oracle Database Vault policy that did not contain it failed.
action: Choose the Database Vault policy that contains the realm or command rule and retry the operation.

description: User %s owns Database Vault policy %s.
cause: An attempt to add a user as policy owner to a Oracle Database Vault policy already owned by the user.
action: Choose a different user and retry the operation, or skip the operation because it is not needed.

description: User %s does not own Oracle Database Vault policy %s.
cause: An attempt to delete a user as policy owner from an Oracle Database Vault policy that the specified user does not own.
action: Choose a user who owns the policy and retry the operation.

description: The object or its parent object belongs to an Oracle Database Vault policy.
cause: An attempt to modify an object that either belongs to an Oracle Database Vault policy or has a parent object that belongs to an Oracle Database Vault policy failed.
action: Choose a different object or change the related policy state to PARTIAL mode. Retry the statement.

description: The %s scope realm %s cannot be added to policy %s.
cause: The realm scope did not match the policy scope.
action: Add the realm to a policy with the same scope.

description: The %s scope command rule cannot be added to policy %s.
cause: The command rule scope did not match the policy scope.
action: Add the command rule to a policy with the same scope.

description: A common scope command rule cannot be created with local scope objects.
cause: An attempt to create a common scope command rule using a local object failed.
action: Use common scope objects for creating or updating a common scope command rule.

description: Nested tables cannot be added to Oracle Database Vault realms and command rules.
cause: An attempt to add a nested table to a realm or command rule failed.
action: Apply the Oracle Database Vault realm or command rule to the base table. Nested tables are automatically protected when the base table is protected.

description: Cannot rename default policy %s.
cause: An attempt to rename a default policy failed.
action: A default policy cannot be renamed. No action required.

description: Nothing is updated in this procedure.
cause: Nothing is updated in the Oracle Database Vault update procedure because none of the updatable parameters are specified or are specified as NULL.
action: Supply at least one parameter to update.

description: Oracle Database Vault cannot be configured due to missing objects.
cause: The Oracle Database Vault configuration failed because some objects are missing.
action: Run the dvremov.sql script to remove Oracle Database Vault. After successful removal, reinstall Oracle Database Vault.

description: Database Vault has already been configured.
cause: An attempt was made to run this procedure more than once. This procedure can be run successfully only once.
action: If you are attempting to grant the DV_OWNER or DV_ACCTMGR roles, do so manually.

description: Oracle Database Vault is not configured.
cause: Oracle Database Vault could not be enabled unless it was configured with the CONFIGURE_DV procedure.
action: Connect as SYSDBA and run the CONFIGURE_DV procedure to configure Oracle Database Vault before enabling it.

description: Oracle Database Vault is not enabled in CDB$ROOT or application root.
cause: Oracle Database Vault was not enabled in CDB$ROOT or application root for this operation.
action: Enable Oracle Database Vault in CDB$ROOT or application root and retry the operation.

description: Common audit policies for Oracle Database Vault component are not supported.
cause: An attempt was made to use common audit policies for Oracle Database Vault realms, factors, and rule sets.
action: If creating audit policies for Oracle Database Vault objects in CDB$ROOT, then include the clause CONTAINER=CURRENT to create a root local audit policy.

description: Strict mode of Oracle Database Vault cannot be enabled in a pluggable database.
cause: An attempt to enable Oracle Database Vault strict mode in a pluggable database (PDB) failed.
action: Enable Oracle Database Vault strict mode in CDB$ROOT or application root.

description: Oracle Database Vault or Oracle Database Vault application protection is not enabled in CDB$ROOT.
cause: Oracle Database Vault or Oracle Database Vault application protection was not enabled in CDB$ROOT for this operation.
action: Enable Oracle Database Vault or Oracle Database Vault application protection in CDB$ROOT and retry the operation.

description: Oracle Database Vault cannot be enabled inside an application action.
cause: An attempt was made to enable Oracle Database Vault inside an application action.
action: Enable Oracle Database Vault independently of the application action.

description: Oracle Label Security cannot be enabled inside an application action of the application container.
cause: An attempt was made to enable Oracle Label Security (OLS) inside an application action for an application container.
action: Enable Oracle Label Security in each of the application pluggable databases that require OLS enforcement.

description: The SQL firewall is not enabled.
cause: The SQL firewall was not enabled.
action: Enable the SQL firewall and retry the operation.

description: SQL Firewall violation
cause: Operation blocked by the SQL Firewall due to enforcement of the firewall policy.
action: Review the SQL Firewall policy. If it is not intended to block the operation, review and modify the SQL Firewall policy.

description: invalid input value for parameter %s
cause: The value specified for this parameter was invalid.
action: Review and modify the parameter and retry the operation.

description: The SQL Firewall operation is not allowed on user %s.
cause: SQL Firewall cannot be used on certain users such as SYS. For the complete list of the restricted users, refer to Oracle Database documentation.
action: Choose a different user and retry the operation.

description: Flush log propagation timed out in SQL firewall.
cause: The flush log operation across Oracle Real Application Clusters (Oracle RAC) instances timed out.
action: Ensure that all Oracle RAC instances are available and retry the operation.

description: SQL Firewall capture for user %s already exists.
cause: The SQL Firewall capture for this user was already defined.
action: Choose another user and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall capture.

description: SQL Firewall capture for user %s does not exist.
cause: The SQL Firewall capture for this user did not exist. The user cannot generate the allow list, or drop, start, or stop the capture.
action: Choose an existing capture and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall capture.

description: SQL Firewall capture for user %s has been started.
cause: The SQL Firewall capture for this user was already started.
action: Stop the capture and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall capture.

description: SQL Firewall capture for user %s is not started.
cause: The SQL Firewall capture for this user was not started.
action: No action required.
params: 1) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall capture.

description: SQL Firewall allow list for user %s already exists.
cause: The SQL Firewall allow list for this user already existed.
action: Choose another user and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall allow list.

description: SQL Firewall capture log for user %s is not found.
cause: An attempt to generate a SQL Firewall allow list failed because there are no SQL Firewall capture logs found for this user.
action: Choose another user and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall event log.

description: SQL Firewall allow list for user %s does not exist.
cause: The SQL Firewall allow list for this user did not exist.
action: Choose another user and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall allow list.

description: SQL Firewall allow list for user %s is enabled.
cause: When the SQL Firewall allow list for this user was already enabled, it could not start the capture, or enable or drop the allow list for this user.
action: Disable the allow list and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall allow list.

description: SQL Firewall allow list for user %s is not enabled.
cause: The SQL Firewall allow list for this user was not enabled.
action: No action required.
params: 1) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall allow list.

description: SQL Firewall allowed context %s with type %s for user %s already exists.
cause: The specified SQL Firewall allowed context for this user already existed.
action: Choose another context and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) context_value: The value of SQL Firewall allowed context. 2) context_type: The type of SQL Firewall allowed context. 3) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall allowed context.

description: SQL Firewall allowed context %s with type %s for user %s does not exist.
cause: The specified SQL Firewall allowed context for this user did not exist.
action: Choose another context and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) context_value: The value of the SQL Firewall allowed context. 2) context_type: The type of the SQL Firewall allowed context. 3) user_name: The name of the user for SQL Firewall allowed context.

description: SQL Firewall cannot be enabled.
cause: SQL Firewall could not be enabled because the database was in upgrade mode.
action: No action required.

description: Concurrent change on SQL Firewall allow list is not allowed.
cause: The operation failed because there was an ongoing SQL Firewall operation such as generation or dropping of SQL Firewall allow list or SQL Firewall log purging action.
action: Wait until the current change on SQL Firewall allow list is complete and retry the SQL Firewall operation.

description: Truncate operation not allowed on Firewall log tables.
cause: Truncating on Firewall log tables was not allowed because the Firewall was enabled.
action: Retry the operation when the Firewall is disabled, or use the DELETE command.

description: SQL Firewall allowed SQL ID %s for user %s does not exist.
cause: The specified SQL Firewall allowed SQL ID for this user did not exist.
action: Choose another allowed SQL ID and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) allowed_sql_ID: The ID of the SQL Firewall allowed SQL for the specified user. 2) user_name: The specified user name.

description: As SQL Firewall allow list for user %s already exists, the capture must be created with the same top_level_only setting.
cause: The input value for top_level_only was not consistent with the existing allow list for this user.
action: Specify the same top_level_only value as the existing SQL Firewall allow list and retry the SQL Firewall operation.

description: SQL Firewall allow list cannot be imported due to: %s.
cause: The specified SQL Firewall allow list could not be imported because of missing fields or invalid values.
action: Choose an allow list in valid format and retry the SQL Firewall operation.
params: 1) cause: The cause of the failure of the import.

description: The requested operation cannot be done when SQL Firewall is enabled.
cause: SQL Firewall was enabled.
action: Disable SQL Firewall and retry the operation.

description: The SQL Firewall tables cannot be moved to '%s' tablespace.
cause: The tablespace is either unavailable or does not have enough space to accommodate the SQL Firewall tables being moved.
action: Ensure that the tablespace is online and has enough space for the SQL Firewall tables being moved.

description: The corresponding record does not exist in the SQL Firewall %s.
cause: The combination of the input USERNAME, SQL_SIGNATURE, CURRENT_USER, and TOP_LEVEL does not match any record in the SQL Firewall violation log (or capture log).
action: Choose a combination of USERNAME, SQL_SIGNATURE, CURRENT_USER, and TOP_LEVEL that matches at least one record in the violation log (or capture log).
params: 1) log_name: The source log table (violation log or capture log).

description: The SQL record already exists in the SQL Firewall allow list.
cause: The combination of the input USERNAME, SQL_SIGNATURE, CURRENT_USER, and TOP_LEVEL already exists in the SQL Firewall allow list.
action: No action required.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s to perform action %s exists.
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to perform the specified action was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user or action and retry the operation, or skip the authorization because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on schema %s to perform action %s exists.
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault on the specified schema to perform the specified action was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user, schema, action, or any combination of those and retry the operation, or skip the operation because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s to perform action %s not found.
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to perform the specified action was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user or action. Retry the operation.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on schema %s to perform action %s not found.
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault on the specified schema to perform the specified action was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user, schema, action, or any combination of those and retry the operation.

description: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception for user %s exists.
cause: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user and retry the operation, or skip the operation because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception for user %s does not exist.
cause: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception does not exist for the specified user.
action: Choose a different user and retry the operation.

description: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception for %s.%s exists.
cause: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception was already granted to the specified package.
action: Choose a different package and retry the operation, or skip the operation because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception for %s.%s does not exist.
cause: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception does not exist for the specified package.
action: Choose a different package and retry the operation.

description: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception cannot be added to package %s.%s.
cause: Oracle Database Vault application protection exception was not added to the definer rights package.
action: Choose a different package and retry the operation.

description: User %s is not an existing Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) user.
cause: Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) attach session authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified RAS user.
action: Choose an existing RAS user with the authorization and retry the operation, or grant the specified RAS user the required authorization.

description: Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) attach session authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on RAS user %s exists.
cause: Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) attach session authorization for Oracle Database Vault for the specified user on the specified RAS user was already granted.
action: Choose a different grantee or RAS user and retry the operation, or skip the operation because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) attach session authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on RAS user %s was not found.
cause: Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) attach session authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user on the specified RAS user.
action: Choose a different user or RAS user and retry the operation, or grant the user authorization to the specified RAS user.

description: Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) attach session authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s exists.
cause: Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) attach session authorization for Oracle Database Vault was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user or RAS user and retry the operation, or skip the operation because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) attach session authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s not found.
cause: Oracle Database Real Application Security (RAS) attach session authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user with the authorization and retry, or grant the specified user the necessary authorization.

description: Oracle Database Vault application protection cannot be %s.
cause: One or more of the pluggable databases were in read-only mode.
action: Reopen the pluggable databases in read/write mode and retry the operation.

description: Oracle Database Vault application protection cannot be %s for the pluggable database.
cause: The pluggable database is in read-only mode.
action: Choose a pluggable database that is opened in read/write mode, or change the mode of the specified database.

description: SQL Firewall authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s already exists.
cause: SQL Firewall authorization for Oracle Database Vault was already granted to the specified grantee.
action: Choose a different grantee and retry the operation.

description: SQL Firewall authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s is not found.
cause: SQL Firewall authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a user who has SQL Firewall authorization for Oracle Database Vault and retry.

description: AUDIT_ADMIN authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s already exists.
cause: AUDIT_ADMIN authorization for Oracle Database Vault was already granted to the specified grantee.
action: Choose a different grantee and retry the operation.

description: AUDIT_ADMIN authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s is not found.
cause: AUDIT_ADMIN authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a user who has AUDIT_ADMIN authorization for Oracle Database Vault and retry.

description: AUDIT_VIEWER authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s already exists.
cause: AUDIT_VIEWER authorization for Oracle Database Vault was already granted to the specified grantee.
action: Choose a different grantee and retry.

description: AUDIT_VIEWER authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s is not found.
cause: AUDIT_VIEWER authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a user who has AUDIT_VIEWER authorization for Oracle Database Vault or grant the specified user the authorization and retry.

description: OLS policy not specified
cause: An OLS policy name is required for this operation
action: Specify a policy name and retry the operation

description: OLS policy label not specified
cause: An OLS policy label is required for this operation
action: Specify a policy label and retry the operation

description: OLS policy label %s not found for policy %s
cause: The policy label being requested does not exist
action: Choose an object name that exists and retry the operation

description: OLS session label does not exist
cause: The policy label specified does not exist
action: Choose a valid policy label and retry the operation

description: OLS policy label %s is not allowed for policy %s
cause: The policy label specified is not valid for this policy
action: Choose a valid policy label for this policy and retry the operation

description: OLS policy label not specified for identity %s.%s under policy %s
cause: The policy label is required for this operation
action: Choose a valid policy label for this policy and retry the operation

description: Database Vault associated OLS policy %s not fully configured
cause: The Oracle Label Security (OLS) policy was associated with Database Vault. But either the policy was not configured with a factor or the current factor identity was not assigned a label.
action: Based on the cause, either configure a factor with the OLS policy using DVSYS.DBMS_MACADM.ADD_POLICY_FACTOR procedure and assign labels to factor identities using DVSYS.DBMS_MACADM.CREATE_POLICY_LABEL procedure or remove Database Vault association using DVSYS.DBMS_MACADM.DELETE_MAC_POLICY_CASCADE procedure.

description: Failed to add language %s to Oracle Database Vault.
cause: An error occurred while attempting to add a language to Oracle Database Vault.
action: Review the trace file and identify the cause. Contact Oracle Support.

description: Authorization failed for user %s to perform this operation
cause: The operation attempted is not allowed for this user
action: Please ensure you have privileges to perform this operation

description: error adding host %s to domain %s, %s
cause: An error occurred adding the host specified to the domain specified
action: Please review the host and domain definition and correct it as required

description: error removing host %s to domain %s, %s
cause: An error occurred removing the host specified to the domain specified
action: Please review the host and domain definition and correct it as required

description: Privilege capture %s already exists.
cause: A privilege capture with the specified name was already in existence.
action: Choose another capture name or drop the existing privilege capture.

description: Privilege capture %s does not exist.
cause: The given privilege capture did not exist.
action: Choose another privilege capture.

description: Privilege capture %s is still enabled.
cause: The given privilege capture was still enabled.
action: Choose another capture or disable the given privilege capture.

description: Privilege capture %s is already enabled.
cause: The specified privilege capture was already enabled.
action: Disable the current capture or use a different capture.

description: Two privilege captures are already enabled.
cause: A maximum number of two privilege captures can be enabled.
action: Check the ENABLED column of the DBA_PRIV_CAPTURES view, disable one of the enabled privilege captures, and retry.

description: Another privilege capture is enabled.
cause: Another capture of the same type or another nondatabase-wide capture was enabled.
action: Disable the enabled privilege capture.

description: Privilege capture %s is already disabled.
cause: The specified privilege capture was already disabled.
action: Choose another capture.

description: Input %s does not match the given privilege capture type.
cause: The given input did not match the given privilege capture type.
action: Change the input or the privilege capture type.

description: GENERATE_RESULT is already running for privilege capture %s.
cause: DBMS_PRIVILEGE_CAPTURE.GENERATE_RESULT was already running for the given privilege capture.
action: Wait and retry later or choose another privilege capture.

description: Capture context namespace or attribute does not exist or is invalid.
cause: Context namespace or attribute used in the capture condition did not exist or was invalid.
action: Create the namespace or set the attribute or re-create a privilege capture with a valid namespace and attribute.

description: Cannot create a capture condition for SYS user.
cause: Attempted to create a capture with the condition set as SYS user, and this is not allowed.
action: Create the capture condition for non-SYS user.

description: Privilege capture %s has not been enabled with run name %s.
cause: The given privilege capture has not been run with the given run name.
action: Enable the given privilege capture with the given run name.

description: A privilege capture %s with the run name %s already exists.
cause: The specified privilege capture with the specified run name already exists.
action: Enable the specified privilege capture with a new run name.

description: Privilege capture %s is enabled with run name %s.
cause: The specified privilege capture is running with the specified run name.
action: Disable the given privilege capture.

description: Privilege capture %s has not been enabled.
cause: The specified privilege capture has not been enabled.
action: Enable the specified privilege capture.

description: duplicate roles %s in capture condition
cause: An attempt was made to specify duplicate roles in a capture condition.
action: Specify only unique roles and retry the operation.

description: invalid System Privilege - '%s'
cause: An invalid system privilege was passed as a parameter.
action: Specify valid system privilege and retry the operation.

description: required value not defined for parameter %s
cause: A value was not defined for the specified parameter.
action: Specify the missing parameter value and retry the operation.

description: invalid input value or length for parameter %s
cause: The value specified for this parameter was invalid or too large.
action: Specify a valid parameter value and retry the operation.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s exists
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user and retry the operation, or skip the operation because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s on schema %s already exists
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault on the specified schema was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user, schema, or both and retry the operation, or skip the authorization because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on object %s.%s exists.
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault on the specified object was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different grantee, object, or both and retry the operation, or skip the authorization because it is not needed.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s was not found.
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a user who has Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault, or obtain the authorization for your user. Retry after you have the authorization.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on schema %s not found.
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user on the specified schema.
action: Verify the user, schema or table are authorized with DBMS_MACADM.AUTHORIZE_DATAPUMP_USER and retry.

description: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on object %s.%s was not found.
cause: Oracle Data Pump authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user on the specified object.
action: Choose a different user, object, or both and retry the operation.

description: Running EXP with direct path option is not allowed when Oracle Database Vault is enabled.
cause: While Oracle Database Vault was enabled, an attempt was made to run EXP with the 'direct=y' option.
action: Change the option to 'direct=n' or disable Oracle Database Vault and then retry the operation.

description: Oracle transportable tablespace authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s on tablespace %s already exists.
cause: The Oracle transportable tablespace authorisation for Oracle Database Vault on the given tablespace was already granted to the given grantee.
action: Choose a different grantee or tablespace and then retry the operation.

description: Oracle transportable tablespace authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s on tablespace %s is not found.
cause: The Oracle transportable tablespace authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the given user on the given tablespace.

action: Choose a user who has Oracle Scheduler Job authorization for Oracle Database Vault and retry the operation, or grant the authorization to the specified user.

description: DEBUG_CONNECT authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on schema %s exists.
cause: DEBUG_CONNECT authorization for Oracle Database Vault on the specified schema was already granted to the specified user.

description: DEBUG_CONNECT authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on schema %s not found.
cause: DEBUG_CONNECT authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user on the specified schema.

cause: DBCAPTURE authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a user who has DBCAPTURE authorization for Oracle Database Vault and retry the operation, or get the authorization for the specified user.

description: DBREPLAY authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s already exists.
cause: DBREPLAY authorization for Oracle Database Vault was already granted to the specified grantee.
action: Choose a different grantee and retry the operation.

description: DBREPLAY authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s was not found.
cause: DBREPLAY authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user.

description: Oracle proxy authorization for Oracle Database Vault to %s on schema %s already exists.
cause: Oracle proxy authorization for Oracle Database Vault on the given schema was already granted.
action: Choose a different user or schema and retry the operation.

description: Oracle proxy authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on schema %s not found.
cause: Oracle proxy authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user on the specified schema.
action: Choose a different user, schema, or both and retry the operation.

description: Oracle DDL authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on schema %s exists.
cause: Oracle DDL authorization for Oracle Database Vault on the specified schema was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user, schema, or both and retry the operation.

description: Oracle DDL authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on schema %s not found.
cause: Oracle DDL authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user on the specified schema.
action: Choose a different user, schema, or both and retry the operation.

description: PREPROCESSOR authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s exists.
cause: PREPROCESSOR authorization for Oracle Database Vault was already granted to the specified user.
action: Use the DBMS_MACADM.AUTHORIZE_DATAPUMP_USER procedure to authorize the user to perform Oracle Data Pump operations.

description: PREPROCESSOR authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s not found.
cause: PREPROCESSOR authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a user who has PREPROCESSOR authorization for the Oracle Database Vault and retry the operation, or grant the authorization to the specified user.

description: Maintenance authorization %s for Oracle Database Vault to %s%s exists.
cause: Maintenance authorization for Oracle Database Vault was already granted to the specified user on the specified object.
action: Choose a different user, object, or both and retry the operation, or skip the authorization because it is not needed.
params: 1) auth_type: The type of maintenance authorization. 2) grantee_name: The name of the grantee. 3) object_type: The type of object (optional).

description: Maintenance authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on schema %s exists.
cause: Maintenance authorization for Oracle Database Vault on the specified schema was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different user, schema, or both and retry the operation, or skip the authorization because it is not needed.

description: Maintenance authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on object %s.%s exists.
cause: Maintenance authorization for Oracle Database Vault on the specified schema was already granted to the specified user.
action: Use the DBMS_MACADM.AUTHORIZE_MAINTENANCE_USER procedure to grant the user authorization to perform Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) operations.

description: Maintenance authorization %s for Oracle Database Vault to %s%s not found.
cause: Maintenance authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user on the specified object.
action: Choose a different user, object, or both and retry the operation.
params: 1) auth_type: The type of maintenance authorization. 2) grantee_name: The name of the grantee. 3) object_type: The type of object (optional).

description: Maintenance authorization%s for Oracle Database Vault to %s%s on schema %s not found.
cause: Maintenance authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user on the specified schema.
action: Choose a different user, schema, or both and retry the operation.
params: 1) auth_type: The type of maintenance authorization. 2) grantee_name: The name of the grantee. 3) object_type: The type of target object. 4) schema_name: The name of the target schema name.

description: Maintenance authorization%s for Oracle Database Vault to user %s on object %s.%s was not found.
cause: Maintenance authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user on the specified object.
action: Choose a different user or object and retry the operation.
params: 1) auth_type: The type of maintenance authorization. 2) grantee_name: The name of the grantee. 3) object_owner: The name of target object owner. 4) object_name: The name of target object name.

description: Diagnostic authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s exists.
cause: Diagnostic authorization for Oracle Database Vault was already granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a different grantee and retry the operation, or skip the authorization because it is not needed.

description: Diagnostic authorization for Oracle Database Vault to user %s not found.
cause: Diagnostic authorization for Oracle Database Vault was not granted to the specified user.
action: Choose a user who has diagnostic authorization for Oracle Database Vault and retry the operation, or obtain the authorization for the specified user.

description: password same as or similar to user
cause: The password specified similar to the user account name and therefore insecure
action: Please specify the more complex password and retry the operation

description: password length must be 8 characters or more
cause: The password specified is too short and therefore insecure
action: Please specify a password with more characters and retry the operation

description: password is too simple
cause: The password specified can be guessed based on dictionary terms and therefore insecure
action: Please specify a password that is not based on dictionary terms and retry the operation

description: password should contain at least one numeric and one alphabetic character
cause: The password does not contain at least one numeric and one alphabetic character
action: Please specify a password with at least one numeric and one alphabetic character and retry the operation

description: password should differ by at least 3 characters
cause: The password specified does not differ from the previous one by more than 3 characters
action: Please specify a password that differs from the previous one by more than 3 characters and retry the operation

description: Function %s has already been added to Oracle Database Vault index functions list.
cause: The function specified had already been added to Oracle Database Vault index functions list.
action: Choose a different function and retry the operation, or skip the operation because it is not needed.

description: Function %s is not found in Oracle Database Vault index functions list.
cause: The function specified was not found in the Oracle Database Vault index functions list.
action: Choose a different function and retry the operation.

description: Function %s is not an Oracle built-in operator.
cause: The function specified was not provided as a built-in operator.
action: Choose a different function and retry the operation.

description: Cannot run dvremov.sql from CDB root when DV is installed in one or more PDBs.
cause: The Database Vault (DV) removal script was not allowed to be run from the multitenant container database (CDB) root when DV is installed in one or more of the underlying pluggable databases (PDBs).
action: Run dvremov.sql on all PDBs before running it from CDB root.

description: Database Vault removal script must be run as SYS
cause: The Database Vault removal script was not run as SYS.
action: Run the Database Vault removal script as SYS.

description: Database Vault must be linked off and disabled before removal
cause: Database Vault was not linked off and disabled.
action: Link Database Vault off and execute DBMS_MACADM.DISABLE_DV_CHECK as DV_OWNER.

description: The RECYCLEBIN is turned on
cause: The RECYCLEBIN was turned on.
action: Turn off the RECYCLEBIN and then execute Database Vault Removal script.

description: Database Vault protected schema does not exist
cause: The Database Vault DVSYS protected schema did not exist.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services for instructions.

description: Database Vault tracing event
cause: NA
action: NA

description: internal Oracle Database Vault error: %s Error: %s
cause: An internal Oracle Database Vault error occurred.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: Cannot run dvremov.sql from CDB root when one or more PDBs are closed.
cause: The Database Vault (DV) removal script was not allowed to be run from the multitenant container database (CDB) root when one or more pluggable databases (PDBs) are closed.
action: Open all PDBs before running dvremov.sql from CDB root.

description: internal error code, arguments: [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s], [%s]
cause: This is the generic internal error number for program exceptions. This indicated that a process encountered an exceptional condition.
action: Report as a bug - the first argument is the internal error number.

description: thread terminated by fatal error
cause: The thread was in an unrecoverable state.
action: Examine the thread trace file for more information.

description: out of process memory
cause: Operating system memory was exhausted or a per-process limit on private memory usage was reached. The database has an internal limit of 32 GB per Oracle process.
action: Check the use of memory by other Oracle instances and other applications. Exceeding 32 GB in a single process may indicate a memory leak. Consider reducing the size of shared memory to allow more room for private memory.

description: out of shared memory in %s
cause: More shared memory was needed than was available.
action: If using one of the initialization parameters SGA_TARGET, MEMORY_SIZE, or MEMORY_TARGET, increase the value of that parameter. If it is not feasible to increase the parameter, then reduce the value of DB_CACHE_SIZE (if set). If you are not using SGA_TARGET, MEMORY_SIZE, or MEMORY_TARGET, increase the size of the pool that is out of memory. For example, increase SHARED_POOL_SIZE for the shared pool or INMEMORY_SIZE for an IMC heap.

description: illegal argument for function
cause: An illegal argument was passed to dbgc_alloc.
action: Report as a bug.

description: user requested cancel of current operation
cause: NA
action: NA

description: name is already used by an existing product type
cause: An attempt was made to define a product type with the same name as an already defined product type.
action: Use the already existing product type with the specified name, or use a different name for the product type.

description: id is already used by an existing product type
cause: An attempt was made to define a product type with the same id as an already defined product type.
action: Choose a different name for the product type.

description: error encountered when attempting to open a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to open a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check that the specified directory name, file name, and open options are valid.

description: error encountered when attempting to read a file [%s] [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to read a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the specified arguments to the read interface.

description: encountered the end-of-file when reading the file
cause: The ADR file interface encountered the end-of-file when reading the file.
action: Handle the end of file condition.

description: error encountered when attempting to write a file [%s] [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to write a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the specified arguments to the write interface.

description: read mismatch on blocks requested and returned, [%s], [%s]
cause: There was a mismatch between the number of blocks requested for reading and the number of blocks actually returned.
action: Check the file to make sure there are no partial blocks.

description: write mismatch on blocks requested and returned, [%s], [%s]
cause: There was a mismatch between the number of blocks requested for writing and the number of blocks actually written.
action: Check that there is enough space left on the device to write the requested number of blocks.

description: error initializing the ADR %s object
cause: There was an error encountered during the initialization of one of the ADR file objects.
action: Check the validity of the specified directory name and file name.

description: invalid Bfile input, [%s]
cause: An invalid Bfile was passed into the routine to convert the bfile into a file handle.
action: Verify the contents of the specified Bfile.

description: invalid value given for the diagnostic_dest init.ora parameter
cause: The value given for the diagnostic_dest directory is not a valid directory. Either the directory does not exist or the process does not have read/write privileges on the directory.
action: Use a value for diagnostic_dest that is a valid directory with the proper read and write privileges.

description: invalid lock mode for file descriptor, [%s]
cause: The lock mode associated with the file descriptor was invalid in the context of the routine.
action: Verify that a file is not trying to obtain multiple locks and that the file is holding a lock when attempting to release the lock.

description: error encountered while attempting to get a file lock [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered while trying to get a file lock.
action: Check the state of the file and operating system.

description: error encountered while attempting to release a file lock [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered while trying to release a file lock.
action: Check the state of the file and operating system.

description: invalid flags for open file, %s
cause: Invalid flags were passed in to the open file routine.
action: Check to see if the flags are a valid combination.

description: unable to write to stream file because of out of space condition
cause: The system is unable to write the requested number of bytes to a stream file. This is due to an out of space condition. The additional information shows how many bytes were not written.
action: Check that there is enough space left on the device to write the requested number of bytes.

description: error encountered when attempting to close a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to close a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the validity of the file descriptor.

description: error encountered while seeking a file position
cause: There was an error encountered while seeking a position in a file.
action: Check that the requested file position falls within the file boundaries.

description: error encountered when attempting to create a directory [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to create a directory.
action: Check the directory name.

description: error encountered when attempting to remove a directory [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to remove a directory.
action: Check the directory name.

description: error encountered with list directory [%s]
cause: There was an error with listing the elements of a directory.
action: Check the state of the operating system.

description: error encountered when attempting to remove a file [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to remove a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory name and file name.

description: error encountered when attempting to retrieve the file size [%s] [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to retrieve the file size with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory name and file name.

description: error with opening the ADR stream file [%s] [%s]
cause: An error was encountered when attempting to open an ADR stream file.
action: Check the rest of the error stack for details of the actual error that was encountered.

description: error with opening the ADR block file [%s] [%s]
cause: An error was encountered when attempting to open an ADR block file.
action: Check the rest of the error stack for details of the actual error that was encountered.

description: error encountered when attempting to flush a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to flush a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the state of the file.

description: device full encountered during write to a file
cause: The device full error was encountered during the write to a file.
action: Check the amount of free space on the device.

description: illegal identifier length, argn:%s, len:%s, lim:%s
cause: An input identifier was passed in that has a length that is greater than the max length.
action: Make sure the input identifier has a length that is less than the max length.

description: attempting to create a file that already exists
cause: The client attempted to create a file that already exists.
action: Either remove the file or check if it is okay if the file already exists.

description: attempting to open a file that does not exist
cause: An attempt was made to open a file that does not exist.
action: Either create the file or check why the file does not exist.

description: opening of a symbolic link is disallowed
cause: An error was encountered when attempting to open a file that is a symbolic link. Users are not allowed to open symbolic links.
action: Check the specified file name.

description: invalid input for the full path specification
cause: Input was incorrectly specified for the full path specification, or the default extension may have been incorrectly specified. Or an empty string was passed in for the full path.
action: Check that the full path string is non-NULL. If you want to specify a relative path from ADR Home for the full path specification, then use '<ADR_HOME>' instead of the actual path to ADR Home. For ADR Base, use '<ADR_BASE>'.

description: invalid lock parameters for get file lock [%s]
cause: Invalid lock parameters passed in for the get file lock routine. The user must pass in file as the lock type. Or, there is a lock mode mismatch. Exclusive locks are not allowed in read-only mode, and shared locks are not allowed in write-only mode.
action: Check that correct lock type is specified and that the correct lock mode is requested for the file given its open flags.

description: error encountered when attempting to tell the file position
cause: An error was encountered when attempting to tell the file position using the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory and file name of the file along with the open state.

description: requested file lock is busy, [%s] [%s]
cause: The requested file lock is busy because another process is holding the file lock.
action: Try to get the file lock again at a later time.

description: file descriptor has already been opened [%s] [%s]
cause: The specified file descriptor has already been opened.
action: Do not open a file that has previously been opened, or check your code to make sure you are cleaning up a file descriptor that is being reused correctly.

description: invalid file descriptor state for operation, %s, %s, %s
cause: The state of the file descriptor was invalid for the requested operation. An example is that a file was opened for read, but a write operation to the file was requested.
action: Check the state of the file descriptor and make sure it matches the operation.

description: uninitialized file descriptor
cause: The specified file descriptor is uninitialized.
action: Make sure the file descriptor is initialized before passing it into the routine.

description: directory already exists [%s]
cause: Operation failed because the specified directory already exists.
action: Remove the directory or ignore this error.

description: uninitialized file handle
cause: The specified file handle is uninitialized.
action: Make sure the file handle is initialized before passing it into the routine.

description: invalid directory name input for client address
cause: An invalid directory name was specified as part of the address path specification.
action: Check that the directory name is non-NULL and that the directory name length does not exceed the maximum length.

description: invalid input to ADR initialization routine
cause: There was an invalid input to the ADR initialization routine.
action: Check the length of the ADR base, product ID, and instance ID input arguments.

description: the specified ADR Base directory does not exist [%s]
cause: The specified ADR Base Directory does not exist.
action: Check that the specified ADR Base Directory is a valid path name and that the directory exists.

description: error creating directory during ADR initialization [%s]
cause: Error encountered when creating a directory during the initialization of the ADR subsystem.
action: Check the input arguments to the ADR initialization routine and the state of the operating system.

description: invalid permissions input for change permissions
cause: Invalid permissions passed into change permissions routine.
action: Check the value of the permissions input.

description: error changing permissions for a file
cause: Error encountered while changing the permissions for a file
action: Check the specified directory and file and the state of the operating system.

description: error encountered while performing standard file I/O
cause: Error encountered while performing standard file I/O
action: Check the validity of standard in, out, and error.

description: invalid seek location, [%s], [%s]
cause: Invalid seek location specified for routine.
action: Check the validity of specified seek location.

description: missing read, write, or exec permission on directory during ADR initialization [%s] [%s]
cause: Error encountered when checking if the process has read, write, and exec privileges on directories needed by the ADR subsystem. This error occurs during the initialization of the ADR subsystem.
action: Check the input arguments to the ADR initialization routine and the state of the operating system. Ensure that the user has the proper permissions on the ADR directories.

description: invalid home location specification for ADR, [%s], [%s], [%s]
cause: Invalid read or write home location specification for ADR.
action: An invalid home was specified for the ADR Read or Write Home location.

description: error encountered when attempting to move a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to move a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory name and file name.

description: error encountered when attempting to copy a file
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to copy a file with the ADR file interface.
action: Check the directory name and file name.

description: error encountered with set current working directory
cause: There was an error with setting the current working directory.
action: Check the path used, or the state of the operating system.

description: error getting operating system time for a file
cause: Error encountered while getting the operating system time for a file.
action: Check the specified directory and file and the state of the operating system.

description: lock table is full
cause: Lock table is full - too many locks granted
action: Try again later

description: error encountered when getting ADR base directory default
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to get the ADR base directory default value.
action: Check your environment to see if the $ORACLE_BASE and $ORACLE_HOME environment variables are set.

description: reached end of file for alert log
cause: The end of file was reached for reading the Alert Log. There are no more messages to read in the Alert Log.
action: Do not read from the Alert Log

description: error encountered when read alert log [%s]
cause: There was an error encountered when attempting to read a message from the Alert Log.
action: Check the error message and the contents of the alert message.

description: Alert log purge has occurred - retry operation
cause: The purge of the alert log has occurred.
action: Retry the operation.

description: null input to ADR initialization
cause: There was an null input to the ADR initialization routine.
action: Check the ADR base, product ID, and instance ID input arguments.

description: invalid input for ADR base directory
cause: An invalid input was passed in for the ADR base directory name. The ADR base directory name is either NULL or too long of a string.
action: Check the ADR base directory input argument.

description: invalid input for ADR product type
cause: An invalid input was passed in for the ADR product type. The ADR product type is out of bounds.
action: Check the ADR product type input argument.

description: invalid input for ADR product id
cause: An invalid input was passed in for the ADR product id. The ADR product id is either NULL or too long of a string.
action: Check the ADR product id input argument.

description: invalid input for ADR instance id
cause: An invalid input was passed in for the ADR instance id. The ADR instance id is either NULL or too long of a string.
action: Check the ADR instance id input argument.

description: string buffer too small to hold input, [%s], [%s], [%s]
cause: The string buffer is too small to copy an input string into.
action: Check the size of the string buffer and the input string. Look in the argument for the location in the code where the error occurs.

description: error concatenating directory onto path, [%s], [%s], [%s]
cause: Error encountered while concatenating a directory onto a path name.
action: Check the error returned by the OS and the size of the input and output buffers.

description: error concatenating file onto path, [%s], [%s], [%s]
cause: Error encountered while concatenating a directory onto a path name.
action: Check the error returned by the OS and the size of the input and output buffers.

description: user missing read, write, or exec permission on specified ADR Base directory [%s]
cause: The specified ADR Base Directory does not have the correct permissions.
action: Check the read, write, and exec permissions on the specified ADR Base Directory

description: error with opening ADR block file because file does not exist [%s] [%s]
cause: An error was encountered with opening an ADR block file because the file does not exist.
action: Check the existence of the ADR Block File.

description: invalid argument for checking ADR initialization
cause: Invalid arguments were specified for the routine to check ADR initialization.
action: Check the inputs to the ADR initialization routine.

description: the ADR sub-system is not initialized
cause: The ADR subsystem has not been initialized. The requested operation cannot be performed.
action: Check the usage of the call to the ADR services. The ADR sub-system must be initialized for the call to work.

description: incorrect arguments to ADR deferred initialization
cause: There are incorrect arguments to the ADR deferred initialization.
action: Check the input arguments. It could be possible that the product is not set up for deferred initialization.

description: unable to lock file - already in use
cause: the file is locked by another process, indicating that it is currently in use by another process
action: determine which process legitimately owns this file.

description: unable to get share lock - file not readable
cause: share lock request was made on a file not open for read access.
action: file must be open read-only or read-write to get a share lock.

description: unable to find a valid ADR base
cause: Unable to find a valid ADR base. We tried the ORACLE_BASE, ORACLE_HOME, home, and tmp directories, but none of the directories exist for read/write access.
action: Check the validity of the ORACLE_BASE, ORACLE_HOME, home, and tmp directories.

description: error checking directory existence during ADR initialization [%s]
cause: Error encountered when checking directory existence during the initialization of the ADR subsystem. Either the diag or product type directory does not exist underneath the ADR base.
action: The directory in the error message must exist in order for ADR initialization to succeed. Make sure the directories exist.

description: error encountered with get current working directory
cause: There was an error with getting the current working directory.
action: Check the state of the operating system or the size of the path buffer.

description: the path name must not contain the string '..'.
cause: The specified path name contains '..'.
action: Correct the path name and retry the operation.

description: error translating a path name into its full path name
cause: An error was encountered when translating a path name into its full path name.
action: Check the inputted path name to make sure it is a valid relative path.

description: file name with full path information [%s] not allowed
cause: Input was incorrectly specified for the file name. The inputted file name is greater than the maximum length, or the file name has path information. In this case, the file name should not have any path information. The path information should be specified in a separate argument.
action: Check that the string for the file name is not too long and does not have path information.

description: error encountered while reading an ADR block file during ADR initialization [%s]
cause: An error was encountered while reading an ADR block file during the initialization of the ADR subsystem.
action: Check the state of the file system.

description: OS file synchronization failure
cause: OS command to synchronize the changes to a file with the operating system failed.
action: Check the state of the file system and the amount of free space left on your device.

description: OS open system call failure
cause: OS open system call failed. The system failed to open or create a file in the requested mode.
action: Check the OS error code

description: OS write system call failure
cause: OS write system call failed. The system failed to write to a file.
action: Check the OS error code

description: OS read system call failure
cause: OS read system call failed. The system failed to read to a file.
action: Check the OS error code

description: OS close system call failure
cause: OS close system call failed. The system failed to close a file.
action: Check the OS error code

description: OS seek system call failure
cause: OS seek system call failed. The system failed to seek to a position in a file.
action: Check the OS error code

description: OS file size system call failure
cause: OS file size call failed. The system failed to retrieve the file size for a file.
action: Check the OS error code

description: OS check file exists system call failure
cause: OS check file exists system call failed. The system failed to perform the check file exists command for a file.
action: Check the OS error code

description: specified directory does not exist
cause: The specified directory does not exist.
action: Check the directory name.

description: user missing read, write, or exec permission on specified directory
cause: The user does not have valid permissions on the specified directory. The user is missing either the read, write, or execute permission.
action: Check the permissions of the specified directory.

description: OS command to create directory failed
cause: The OS command to create a directory failed.
action: Check the error number associated with the create directory failure.

description: OS unlink system call failure
cause: OS unlink system call failed. The system failed to perform unlink on the specified file.
action: Check the OS error code

description: user missing read or write permission on specified file
