action: Retry the ALTER SYSTEM [ENABLE | DISABLE] RAC TWO_STAGE ROLLING UPDATES statement. If error persists, contact Oracle Support.

description: An instance in the cluster is not ready to enable Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates
cause: A new instance might have joined the cluster while ALTER SYSTEM [ENABLE | DISABLE] RAC TWO_STAGE ROLLING UPDATES statement is in progress. Another reason for this error could be a temporary network outage.
action: Retry the ALTER SYSTEM [ENABLE | DISABLE] RAC TWO_STAGE ROLLING UPDATES statement.

description: Internal Oracle testing event for the Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates module
cause: Set this event only under the supervision of Oracle development.
action: The level controls the Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates testing.

description: Enabling of Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates failed due to %s number of Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling one-offs in environment is higher than maximum %s allowed.
cause: The total number of one-off Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates in environment was higher than the maximum allowed.
action: Apply the release update that contains these one-offs.

description: Enabling of Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates failed due to %s number of Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates in environment is higher than maximum %s allowed.
cause: The total number of Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates in environment was higher than the maximum allowed.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: instance id(s) %s have different set of Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Update than current instance or joined cluster while enable was in progress
cause: The set of Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates were different on instances that were part of this cluster. Another reason for this error could be that instance id mentioned in error joined the cluster while enable was in progress. This could also happen if local SPFILE or PFILE are in use and they are not same across cluster.
action: Ensure that all nodes in the cluster have the same set of Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates. Run the 'ORACLE_HOME/bin/rrputil -l' command on all nodes and confirm that all nodes have the same set of Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates. Optionally, query V$RAC_TWO_STAGE_ROLLING_UPDATES to see what updates are enabled on a node and what updates could be enabled. Updates with ENABLED='Y' are enabled and updates with ENABLED='N' could be enabled in the Oracle binary. All nodes in the cluster should have the same set of rows with the same value for the BUG_NUMBER and the ENABLED column in V$RAC_TWO_STAGE_ROLLING_UPDATES. If error was due to new instance joining the cluster while enable was in progress, retry enable command. If error was due to local SPFILE or PFILE usage, make sure they have same content across cluster. Check alert log for more detail about error.

description: current instance started with pfile and %sOracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Update(s) rolled back in binary
cause: Current instance was started with pfile, and some Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Updates were rolled back in binary before start. This is not allowed with pfile in use.
action: If Oracle RAC Two-Stage updates were rolled back, reapply those in binary. If rollback of Oracle RAC Two-Stage updates is required, start instance using shared spfile.

description: shared spfile not in use
cause: The command was rejected because the Oracle RAC database is not using shared SPFILE.
action: Ensure all instances in cluster use a single shared SPFILE from a shared location.

description: Instance not in exclusive mode
cause: This command can only be run when instance has started in exclusive mode.
action: Set cluster_database parameter to false, shutdown all instances, bring up only one instance using startup exclusive and retry.

description: Oracle RAC two-stage rolling updates could not be restored to last level
cause: Either two stage updates were already restored to the last level in the past, or binary rollback of the two stage updates were done in the past. Another possibility is, two stage updates were never enabled, so we can't go back to last level.
action: We are already as last two stage updates level. No further action is needed.

description: Oracle RAC two-stage rolling updates command is not required in environment where init parameter cluster_database=FALSE or not set
cause: The Oracle RAC two-stage rolling updates command is being run in an environment where the cluster_database init parameter is is set to FALSE or cluster_database parameter is not present.
action: Oracle RAC two-stage updates are always enabled in an environment where cluster_database init parameter is set to FALSE or not present. There is no need to run Oracle RAC two-stage update command in that environment.

description: Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update %s is already present in exceptions.
cause: The Oracle RAC two-stage rolling updates are already present in the exception list.
action: Check V$RAC_TWO_STAGE_ROLLING_EXCEPTIONS and remove the bug which is already present from the ADD command and retry.

description: Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update %s is not present in exceptions.
cause: The Oracle RAC two-stage rolling updates that are being removed are not present in the exception list.
action: Check V$RAC_TWO_STAGE_ROLLING_EXCEPTIONS and ensure that the bug to be removed is present.

description: Enabling Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update %s failed because it is already enabled.
cause: The given Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update is already enabled.
action: Remove the already enabled bug from the list and try again.

description: Enabling Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update %s failed because it is already present in the exceptions.
cause: The given Oracle RAC Two-Stage Rolling Update is present in the exceptions.
action: Check V$RAC_TWO_STAGE_ROLLING_EXCEPTIONS. If this bug no longer needs to be in the exceptions, remove it from the exceptions list using the command ALTER SYSTEM REMOVE RAC TWO_STAGE ROLLING UPDATES <bug> FROM EXCEPTIONS and retry the ENABLE command. Otherwise, remove this bug from the ENABLE command and retry.

description: Enabling Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update %s failed because it is not present in the environment.
cause: The given Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update is not present in the environment.
action: Run 'ORACLE_HOME/bin/rrputil -l' and ensure that the bug that needs to be enabled is present in that list. If not, check the patch inventory and ensure that the patch contains the bug that was applied in the environment.

description: Disabling Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update %s failed because it is not enabled.
cause: The given Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update is not enabled.
action: Check V$RAC_TWO_STAGE_ROLLING_UPDATES and ensure that the two-stage update that is being disabled is enabled.

description: Disabling Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update %s not possible.
cause: The given Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update cannot be disabled.
action: The Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update can be rolled back from the Oracle binary in a non-rolling manner which would disable the update.

description: Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update %s specified more than once.
cause: Each Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update must be specified only once in command line.
action: Specify each Oracle RAC two-stage rolling update only once.

description: %s must be called before %s
cause: The anonymous PL/SQL block did not call the hot block patch procedures in the correct order.
action: Add the required procedure call to the anonymous block.

description: SelectBlock limit [%s] was exceeded.
cause: The number of SelectBlock() calls in the patch exceeded the limit.
action: Reduce the number blocks being patched in a single transaction.

description: PatchStrField allowed only on oratext fields.
cause: PatchStrField was called for a field whose type was not oratext.
action: Use PatchField() to patch non-text fields.

description: Patch field width [%s] exceeds field width [%s] for field %s.
cause: The newValue argument was too wide.
action: Reduce the width of the newValue argument.

description: invalid hexadecimal number [%s]: %s
cause: The hexadecimal number was not a valid hexadecimal number string.
action: The exact cause of the problem is reported in the error message: 0x missing - the string must begin with '0x' too long - the number of digits exceeded 8 even number of digits required - the string must contain 2/4/8 hex digits invalid_number exception - to_number() raised exception

description: PatchField limit [%s] exceeded.
cause: The number of PatchField() calls for a single block in the patch exceeded the limit.
action: Reduce the number fields being patched in the block.

description: Patch field [%s] was not found at offset [%s].
cause: A field with the specified name and specified offset was not found in the block to be patched.
action: Dump the block and verify the field name and offset are correct.

description: missing or invalid site name
cause: The command did not specify a valid site name.
action: Specify a valid site name.

description: incorrect SITE token usage
cause: Site names were provided for some disks in the SQL statement and missing for others.
action: Either specify site names for all of the disks or none in the SQL statement and retry the operation.

description: The attribute %s must be %s or higher.
cause: An attempt was made to set an attribute to a version that was lower than the minimum supported.
action: Set the attribute to at least the minimum supported version. Alternatively lower the minimum supported version and try again.

description: The attribute %s (%s) of the disk group being mounted should be %s or higher.
cause: An attempt was made to mount a disk group whose compatibility was lower than the minimum supported.
action: Advance the disk group compatibility by mounting it in restricted mode or lower the minimum supported compatibility, and then try again.

description: external and global users are not supported for ASM
cause: A user type not supported by ASM was supplied.
action: Check the Oracle ASM documentation that external and global users are not supported for ASM.

description: The disk group being mounted is incompatible with this software version.
cause: An attempt was made to mount a disk group using a software version that is incompatible with the disk group.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: The parameter '%s' is invalid.
cause: The value of the parameter was invalid.
action: Provide a valid value of the parameter.

description: The disk group redundancy is not external.
cause: An attempt was made to rename the disk fail group in a disk group whose redundancy type was not external.
action: Specify a disk group whose redundancy type is external.

description: The disk '%s' cannot be assigned to a site because the disk group '%s' contains Cluster Synchronization Services voting files.
cause: An attempt to assign a site to a disk failed because the disk group contained Cluster Synchronization Services (CSS) voting files.
action: Move the CSS voting files to a different disk group using the command 'crsctl replace votedisk' and retry the operation.

description: Failure group name '%s' is already used by an existing ASM disk.
cause: The specified failure group name was already used in this diskgroup.
action: Specify a different failure group name.

description: Cannot connect to the Oracle ASM instance '%s'.
cause: The instance failed to relocate to the specified Oracle Automatic Storage Management (ASM) instance because it could not connect to it.
action: Check that the specified Oracle ASM instance SID is valid, that the Oracle ASM instance is up and running, and that the network configuration is valid.

description: Disk '%s' cannot be assigned to a site because it is an Oracle Exadata disk.
cause: An attempt to assign an Oracle Exadata disk to a site failed because the operation is not allowed in Oracle Exadata.
action: Run the following command to update the cell site information: cellcli -e alter cell siteName

description: All mirrors of the block are lost, likely due to multiple storage failures.
cause: There were multiple failures in the storage subsystem. All redundant copies of the block were lost and Oracle wrote the hexadecimal value BADFDA7A into the block location of the lost block to signify that the block data could not be recovered from a redundant copy.
action: Check the system logs and storage logs to identify the failure that led to the lost block.

description: file type not supported for the operation
cause: The operation did not support files of the given type.
action: Retry the operation with a file of supported type.

description: Parity is not supported for file '%0!s' with type '%1!s'.
cause: The given file type did not support the creation of parity files.
action: Retry creating the parity files with a supported file type.

description: ASM software is incompatible with disk group %s due to missing patch %s
cause: The ASM software was not compatible with the disk group.
action: Action: Apply the missing patch and retry the operation.

description: client %0!s software is incompatible with disk group %1!s due to missing patch %2!s
cause: The client software was not compatible with the disk group.
action: Apply the missing patch on corresponding client software and retry the operation.

description: ASM software is incompatible with disk group %s COMPATIBLE.ASM %s
cause: The ASM software did not support the attribute value for COMPATIBLE.ASM.
action: Check alert log to identify the missing patches, apply the patches, and retry the operation. Or, advance COMPATIBLE.ASM to a version that is supported by this software.

description: database software is incompatible with disk group %s COMPATIBLE.RDBMS %s
cause: The specified value for COMPATIBLE.RDBMS was not compatible with one or more clients.
action: Check the ASM alert log for information about the clients and missing patches, apply the patches on the corresponding database software, and retry the operation.

description: client %0!s software is incompatible with disk group %1!s patch %2!s
cause: The client software was not compatible with the specified patch.
action: Apply the missing patch on corresponding client software and retry the operation.

description: ASM software is incompatible with disk group %s patch %s
cause: The ASM software did not support enabling the specified patch.
action: Apply the missing patch and retry the operation.

description: database software is incompatible with disk group %s patch %s
cause: The specified patch was not compatible with one or more clients.
action: Check the ASM alert log for information about the clients and missing patches, apply the patches on corresponding database software, and retry the operation.

description: cannot alter exclusive instance mode with more than once instance running
cause: There was at least one other running ASM instance.
action: Ensure that there is only one ASM instance when running the command.

description: cannot alter exclusive instance mode outside of rolling migration or rolling patch
cause: ASM cluster was not in rolling migration or rolling patch.
action: ASM cluster needs to be in rolling migration or rolling patch.

description: cannot start multiple ASM instances under exclusive mode
cause: There was at least one other running ASM instance, and the ASM cluster was in exclusive mode.
action: Ensure that the ASM cluster is not in exclusive mode when trying to bring up another ASM instance.

description: Rolling mode exit prevented by %s.
cause: One or more instances were blocking the rolling mode exit.
action: Terminate the operation or wait until the reported operation is complete before attempting to take the cluster out of rolling mode.

description: Dropping more failure groups is not allowed with the current disk group redundancy.
cause: There was an attempt to drop at least one failure group, resulting in a failure group count below the recommended number.
action: Use the FORCE option when trying to drop failure groups below the minimum required count. Check the trace files of the Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) instance for more information.

description: Taking more failure groups offline is not allowed with disk group redundancy.
cause: An attempt was made to take more failure groups offline than the minimum number required to maintain the quorum consensus.
action: Before taking any failure groups offline, increase the number of online failure groups by switching offline failure groups online or by adding additional (quorum or regular) failure groups.

description: parity requires at least %0!s failure groups; found only %1!s
cause: An attempt to set the redundancy specification of a file group to a parity protection scheme failed because of insufficient failure groups.
action: Add enough failure groups to the disk group and then retry setting the file group redundancy.

description: Disk zones are deprecated for disk groups that use virtually allocated allocation metadata.
cause: Disk zones are no longer supported for disk groups that use virtually allocated allocation metadata.
action: Do not attempt to create or modify a file with file attributes that are related to disk zones.

description: slow or hung relocations during rebalance of group %u
cause: The I/O devices were slow or were not responsive.
action: Rebalance has restarted to address this issue, so no immediate action is needed. If the rebalance process keeps reporting this error, then check the conditions of storage devices.

description: Number of disks that can be added to a disk group is limited to %0!s disks if disk group is nearly full.
cause: Disk group did not have enough space for the metadata needed to accommodate the number of disks being added at once.
action: Reduce the number of disks that is being added with the initial ADD DISK or ADD FAILGROUP command. After the initial ADD DISK or ADD FAILGROUP command successfully executes, more disks may be added once the disk group has the space to do so with the new space it has acquired.

description: EXTENT and BLOCK clauses are mutually exclusive in single files
cause: EXTENT and BLOCK clauses were mixed in the same file to scrub.
action: Ensure that all scrub file clauses are of the same type; either all EXTENT or all BLOCK. EXTENT and BLOCK clauses must not be mixed within the same file in a scrub command.

description: maximum EXTENT or BLOCK ranges exceeded
cause: The number of EXTENT or BLOCK ranges (10) were exceeded.
action: Use 10 or less EXTENT or BLOCK ranges within a scrubbing command. If more than 10 ranges want to be scrubbed, either consider scrubbing the complete file or submit multiple scrubbing commands.

description: the value specified for COUNT must not be zero
cause: A value of zero was specified in COUNT clause.
action: Provide a value for COUNT greater than zero.

description: Cannot update XML file types of Oracle ASM disk group %0!s with current compatibility %1!s, which needs to be equal to or higher than Oracle Database 21c (21.0).
cause: An attempt was made to update Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) file types with a compatible.asm value earlier than Oracle Database 21c (21.0).
action: Upgrade the compatible.asm attribute to a value equal to or later than Oracle Database 21c (21.0) and retry the operation.

description: XML file types of Oracle ASM disk group %0!s are already updated from OSFILE to XMLFILE.
cause: An attempt was made to update Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) XML files from operating system file type to XML file type when the XML files in the Oracle ASM disk group were already updated.
action: None.

description: '%s' is an invalid alias name for the file.
cause: The alias name provided is used as a system alias by ASM instance in the creation of the file.
action: Provide a different alias name to create the file.

description: Disk group is nearly full. Disk resize is limited to %0!s bytes until there is more free space in the disk group.
cause: The disk group does not have enough space for the metadata needed to accommodate the number of allocation units being added at once.
action: First, resize the disk to the specified value. Then, retry the original resize command once the disk group has the space to do so with the new space it has acquired.

description: Internal ASM event: retry due to VAM conversion
cause: A cache transaction must be retried due to VAM becoming active.
action: Internal event.

description: Internal ASM event: for purpose of backport
cause: An attempt was made to replace underscore parameter in transaction which normally cannot be backported.
action: Internal event.

description: Internal Oracle ASM testing event for the Storage Service
cause: Set this event only under the supervision of Oracle development.
action: The level controls the Storage Service testing.

description: Internal ASM testing event for the Metadata Store
cause: Set this event only under the supervision of Oracle development.
action: The level controls the Storage Service testing.

description: unable to create member cluster '%s' in the absence of at least one disk group with the ACCESS_CONTROL.ENABLED attribute set to TRUE
cause: An attempt was made to configure a member cluster when there was no mounted disk group with the ACCESS_CONTROL.ENABLED attribute set to TRUE.
action: Set the ACCESS_CONTROL.ENABLED attribute to TRUE on an existing mounted disk group, mount a disk group that already has the ACCESS_CONTROL.ENABLED attribute set to TRUE, or create a disk group with the ACCESS_CONTROL.ENABLED attribute set to TRUE. Retry the operation.

description: failed to register database with IOServer instance
cause: The database instance failed to register with a valid IOServer instance.
action: Check the alert log to identify the underlying reason for the failure and take the suggested corrective action.

description: RELOCATE CLIENT to %s is already in progress.
cause: Another RELOCATE CLIENT command was already in progress.
action: Retry the command after on-going RELOCATE CLIENT command completes. Check the client alert log for its progress and status.

description: Client '%s' not allowed to reconnect.
cause: The client in Oracle Flex Automatic Storage Management (ASM) mode tried to reconnect to an Oracle ASM instance that did not support the Flex ASM mode.
action: Check that the remote mode configured on the Oracle ASM instance matches the one in the client instance. Oracle Flex ASM must be enabled in the Oracle ASM cluster. Check the Oracle Flex ASM status using the ASMCMD SHOWCLUSTER command.

description: rejecting a request originating from site '%s' to OFFLINE a disk '%s' configured in site '%s'
cause: The request to OFFLINE a disk was rejected by the ASM instance because the request was issued from a site that was different from the site in which the disk was configured.
action: Retry the request from the site in which the disk is configured.

description: instance '%s' shutting down on site '%s' due to rejected OFFLINE request
cause: The instance terminated because the storage was inaccessible from the site that sent the disk OFFLINE request.
action: Run the command 'crsctl query cluster sites <site_name>' to retrieve the status of the indicated site. Address the storage accessibility issues if the indicated site is in a QUARANTINED state. Run the command 'crsctl modify cluster site <site_name> -s rejuvenate' to set the status to ONLINE after the storage access has been restored.

description: database process interrupted due to SQL*Net read timeout
cause: A process on the client instance connected to an Oracle ASM instance was in an SQL*Net read for too long. Possible reasons include failure of the node on which the Oracle ASM instance was running or a communication channel disruption. The interrupt was detected by the Fence Monitor (FENC) process or the ASM Background (ASMB) process, and the call was interrupted.
action: Usually none, as the client instance fails over to another available Oracle ASM instance. If the problem keeps recurring, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: mismatch of parameter '%0!s' between database and ASM instance '%1!s'
cause: The value for the parameter was different in the database instance and in the ASM instance to which it was connected.
action: Set the parameter to the same value in both the instances.

description: invalid GUID '%s' specified
cause: The operation was rejected because the supplied Globally Unique Identifier (GUID) was syntactically invalid.
action: Retry the command specifying the Globally Unique Identifier (GUID) as a text string of 32 hexadecimal digits (0-f) without a hyphen (-) character or the hexadecimal literal prefix (0x). Refer to the command inline help or product documentation for more information.

description: failed to create member cluster '%0!s' because the specified GUID '%1!s' is already configured
cause: An attempt to add the indicated member cluster with the indicated Globally Unique Identifier (GUID) was rejected because a member cluster with that GUID was already defined.
action: Execute the command 'asmcmd lscc' to list the existing member clusters and cluster GUIDs. Retry the original command with a cluster GUID that has not already been configured.

description: unable to modify member cluster '%s'
cause: An attempt to modify the member cluster failed.
action: Check the alert logs and trace files of the Oracle ASM instance for more information about the reason for the failure, as well as check the accompanying error messages.

description: member cluster '%0!s' already configured with disk access mode '%1!s'
cause: An attempt to modify the member cluster failed because it was already configured with the specified disk access mode.
action: No action is required.

description: The specified Oracle IOServer instance '%0!s' does not exist.
cause: The specified Oracle IOServer instance did not exist or was terminated.
action: Issue the 'srvctl status ioserver' command to list the active Oracle IOServer instances. Specify a valid Oracle IOServer instance name and retry the command.

description: Rejected a request to relocate the client to Oracle Automatic Storage Management (ASM) instance %s.
cause: The request to relocate the client was rejected because either the client or the ASM instance with the client connection was not running in Flex Mode.
action: Check the configuration of both instances.

description: The command is not supported on a storage server.
cause: An attempt was made to run a command that was not supported on a storage server.
action: Rerun the command on a member cluster.

description: The service name was missing from the command for relocation.
cause: The command for relocation was specified without the service name which is an invalid format.
action: Specify a valid Oracle service name and instance name and retry the command: ALTER SYSTEM RELOCATE CLIENT TO <service_name/target_id>

description: Could not connect to an IOS instance.
cause: The instance failed to perform the specified operation because it could not locate a required IOS instance.
action: Start the required IOS instance before starting the database instance.

description: The command is not supported on an ACC.
cause: An attempt was made to run a command that was not supported on ACC (ASM Client Cluster).
action: No action is required.

description: Client instance %0!s is already connected to this Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) instance.
cause: A connection already existed from an ASM Background (ASMB) process to this Oracle ASM instance and was still active.
action: No action is needed unless the problem keeps recurring. The connection information may not yet be shared between ASMB processes attempting to connect to this Oracle ASM instance. The connection information is automatically shared. If the issue persists, contact Oracle Support.

description: Deletion of the last set of credentials is not allowed.
cause: An attempt was made to delete the last set of credentials.
action: Add new credentials and then retry the operation.

description: Failover detected during alias scan.
cause: The client reconnected to an ASM instance while there was an ongoing alias scan.
action: The calling process should retry the alias scan sequence or fail the current alias scan.

description: Existing client instance %0!s is connected to this Oracle ASM instance.
cause: A connection already existed from the same client instance to this Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) instance, but with a different version.
action: Ensure that no other client instances with the same instance, database, and cluster name exist in the cluster.

description: cannot open control file %0!s in disk group %1!s
cause: The control file was already opened by another client in the cluster and the CLUSTER_DATABASE parameter was set to FALSE in either instance, or the old client resources were being cleaned.
action: Ensure that the control file is not shared between two instances or, in case of Oracle Real Application Clusters, have all instances set the CLUSTER_DATABASE to TRUE. Once the configuration has been checked, and fixed if appropriate, retry the operation.

description: Instance name '%0!s' is too long.
cause: The specified instance name was more than 30 characters.
action: Ensure that the INSTANCE_NAME parameter has a maximum length of 30 characters.

description: file %0!s has too many mirror copies; %1!s needed, %2!s allowed
cause: The specified file had too many mirror copies when the change was requested.
action: To resolve the issue, try one of the following: - Retry the command by using a lower target number of copies. - If preparing a mirror split, reduce the file's current number of copies and retry the command, - If the sum of the file's current number of copies, plus the additional number of copies requested by the command does not exceed the number of mirror copies allowed, then wait for the BALANCE phase of the rebalance operation to complete. Finally, retry the command. Refer to the error message for the number of mirror copies allowed.

description: A file group redundancy cannot be modified when it is associated with a volume.
cause: An attempt was made to modify the redundancy of a file group that was associated with an Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) volume. The Oracle ASM disk group compatible.advm attribute is lower than 18.0, and the file group contained at least one file.
action: Update the Oracle ASM disk group compatible.advm attribute to a value equal or higher than 18.0 and then retry the operation.

description: moving Oracle ASM internal files to a file group is not allowed
cause: An attempt was made to issue an ALTER DISKGROUP MOVE FILE TO FILEGROUP statement on a metadata file used by Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) to manage the disk group.
action: Do not attempt to move Oracle ASM internal files to a file group because it is not allowed.

description: This operation requires all disks in disk group %s to be online.
cause: An attempt was made to modify the redundancy of a file group when some disks were offline.
action: Drop the offline disks and wait for the rebalance operations to complete, or online the offline disks and wait for the online operation to complete. Then retry the operation.

description: offline disks encountered during rebalance of disk group '%s'
cause: Rebalance was run in the presence of offline disks.
action: Bring the offline disks online.

description: File '%s' not available. File group '%s' has too many disks offline.
cause: A file identify operation failed because the file group specified was no longer available.
action: Consult V$ASM_DISK_STAT to find out which disks are offline, online or drop those which are offline, and then retry the command.

description: Cannot change redundancy of individual file types in file groups associated with a volume.
cause: Attempted to modify the redundancy of one or more file types in a file group associated with an Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) volume.
action: Change the redundancy of the entire file group and not just the redundancy of the individual file types.

description: COMPATIBLE.CLIENT property requires FORCE option for modifications
cause: An attempt was made to modify the COMPATIBLE.CLIENT property of a file group without the FORCE option.
action: Be aware that the COMPATIBLE.CLIENT property cannot be downgraded under any circumstances. Caution should be exercised when manually modifying this property. If the change is still required, use the FORCE option to override this check and then retry the operation.

description: FORCE option cannot be used for file group property '%s'
cause: An attempt was made to use the FORCE option on a property that does not allow it.
action: Remove the FORCE option and try again.

description: cannot move a file that has prepared mirror copies
cause: An attempt was made to move a file that has a prepared mirror copy.
action: Create another database using the existing mirror copy or drop the existing mirror copy and wait for the rebalance operations to complete. Then, retry the operation.

description: The database version %0!s is incompatible with file group '%1!s'.
cause: The COMPATIBLE parameter for the Oracle Database instance was lower than the value of the COMPATIBLE.CLIENT property for the file group.
action: Update the COMPATIBLE parameter for the client instance to a version greater than or equal to the COMPATIBLE.CLIENT version.

description: PARITY requires COMPATIBLE.RDBMS parameter of %0!s or higher for the ASM disk group
cause: An attempt was made to create, open, or modify a file(group) using a redundancy setting of PARITY while the COMPATIBLE.RDBMS parameter of the ASM disk group was set to a version that did not support PARITY protection.
action: Change the COMPATIBLE.RDBMS parameter to match the minimum required version that supports PARITY protection (if the database version is similar or higher), or specify a redundancy setting other than PARITY in the statement.

description: file group '%0!s' is not a template file group
cause: The file group specified in the FROM TEMPLATE clause was not of TEMPLATE client type.
action: Specify a TEMPLATE file group in the FROM TEMPLATE clause so that the newly created file group can inherit its properties from the TEMPLATE file group.

description: file group requires rebalance completion
cause: An attempt was made to modify the redundancy of a file group. ASM could not perform the operation because of the current state of the disk group.
action: Allow the rebalance to run to completion. After the rebalance has completed, retry the operation.

description: Oracle ASM file group of pluggable database '%0!s' was not dropped.
cause: Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) did not drop the file group associated with a pluggable database that was dropped, either because an error was encountered or because the file group contained other files.
action: Check the Oracle ASM alert log for any errors encountered while dropping the file group. Fix the underlying problem and drop the file group using the ALTER DISKGROUP DROP FILEGROUP command from the Oracle ASM instance. Alternatively, query V$ASM_FILEGROUP_FILE to determine which files, if any, remain in the file group. Delete the files or move them to another file group using the ALTER DISKGROUP MOVE FILE command from the Oracle ASM instance.

description: Oracle ADVM volume files of Oracle ASM file group '%0!s' cannot be deleted using the DROP FILEGROUP command with the CASCADE option
cause: An attempt was made to drop cascade an Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) file group that still contains files in it. File groups associated to a volume should not be cascade dropped.
action: Drop the volume files by dropping the volume. If the files are not part of any volume and were moved into this file group, drop the files before dropping the file group.

description: Use the FOR PLUGGABLE DATABASE clause to drop the Oracle ASM file group
cause: The operation requires the name of the database or pluggable database associated with the Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) file group being dropped.
action: Drop the Oracle ASM file group using the FOR DATABASE clause, if it is associated with a database, or the FOR PLUGGABLE DATABASE clause, if it is associated with a pluggable database. Alternatively, delete the files in the Oracle ASM file group or move them to another Oracle ASM file group using the ALTER DISKGROUP MOVE FILE TO FILEGROUP statement. Then, retry the operation. Query the V$ASM_FILEGROUP_FILE view in an Oracle ASM instance or use ASMCMD LSFG to list the files in the Oracle ASM file group.

description: Failgroup %s already belongs to site %s
cause: An attempt was made to add the specified failgroup to more than one site.
action: Retry the operation providing the correct failgroup name and the site name while specifying the disk.

description: Incorrect number of data sites %s specified. Maximum allowed: %s.
cause: An attempt was made to create an extended redundancy disk group with an invalid number of sites.
action: Retry the operation specifying valid number of sites in the disk group.

description: Incorrect number of quorum sites %s specified. Maximum allowed: %s.
cause: An attempt was made to create an extended redundancy disk group with an invalid number of sites.
action: Retry the operation specifying valid number of sites in the disk group.

description: Inconsistent site information in disk '%s'
cause: The site information stored in the disk header did not match disk group information.
action: Drop the disk from the disk group or provide a site name that matches the site stored in the disk header.

description: command requires at least %s data sites and %s quorum sites, discovered %s data sites and %s quorum sites
cause: An insufficient number of sites were specified and discovered when creating an extended redundancy disk group.
action: Check that the command specifies the required number of data sites and quorum sites, and that all of the specified disks are discovered by ASM. A query of the V$ASM_DISK fixed view shows the disks discovered by ASM.

description: Dropping a site is not allowed.
cause: An attempt was made to drop a site.
action: Set the disks of the given site offline with 'ALTER DISKGROUP <dg> OFFLINE DISK <disk>' command.

description: The specified allocation unit size '%s' is less than the minimum required for extended disk groups.
cause: Extended disk groups required the allocation unit size to be at least 4M.
action: Change the allocation unit size to at least 4M and retry.

description: Site "%s" does not exist in disk group "%s".
cause: The specified name did not match the site of any disks in the disk group. This usually indicates that the site name was specified incorrectly.
action: Check the site name.

description: Cluster site operation failed with error %s. %s
cause: This is an internal error.
action: Check the accompanying error messages. Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: No site identified for the disk %s
cause: The disk did not belong to any site.
action: Specify the site information in the SQL command. In the case of an ASM appliance, cellcli command can also be used to record the site information for the disk. For non-appliance, asmcmd can be used.

description: site information mismatch between disk group %s and disk %s
cause: The site information attribute of the specified disk did not match with the existing disks in the disk group.
action: Ensure that new disks have the correct site information specified similar to existing disks. All disks in the disk group should have either no site information or the correct site information specified.

description: The site identified by GUID '%s' does not exist.
cause: An attempt to retrieve a site failed because there wasn't a configured site using the indicated Globally Unique Identifier.
action: Add the indicated site using the command 'crsctl add cluster site <site> -guid <guid>'. Retry the original command. If retrying does not work, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: The site identified by site name '%s' does not exist.
cause: An attempt to retrieve a site failed because there wasn't a configured site using the indicated site name.
action: Add the indicated site using the command 'crsctl add cluster site <site>'. Retry the original command. If retrying does not work, contact Oracle Support Services.

description: The site name '%s' does not exist in the disk group '%s'.
cause: An attempt was made to add a disk with a new site name to a disk group, which is not allowed.
action: Change the site name to an existing one in the disk group and retry.

description: invalid site name '%s' specified.
cause: An invalid site name was supplied.
action: Specify a site name which is at least one character but no more than 15 characters in length. The cluster name must be alphanumeric, it cannot begin with a numeric character, and it may contain hyphen (-) characters. However, it cannot end with a hyphen (-) character.

description: missing site information in disk group '%s'
cause: The site information was not present in all the disks of the disk group.
action: Specify sites for the disks using the 'asmcmd rename' command or using SQLPLUS and retry the operation.

description: dropping all disks of the quorum site is not allowed
cause: Dropping of the specified disks resulted in the loss of the quorum site. If only a subset of disks in the quorum site are specfied, then check the state of other disks in the V$ASM_DISK view.
action: Modify the command to retain at least one disk in the quroum site and retry the operation.

description: rebalance could not complete due to an unavailable site in disk group '%s'
cause: At least one of the sites had each disk in either dropping or forcing state.
action: Undrop the dropping disks or add disks to the site.

description: One or more disks are identified with a foreign site GUID '%s'.
cause: The indicated site GUID was not associated with any of the configured sites.
action: Execute the command 'crsctl query cluster site -all' to list the existing sites. Associate the indicated site GUID with a site using 'crsctl modify cluster site <site> -addguid <guid>' and retry the operation.

description: disk group '%s' mounted but contains foreign site GUIDs
cause: An attempt was made to mount a disk group with foreign site GUIDs.
action: This is a warning. Examine the accompanying error messages for details.

description: data sites in disk group %s have a different number of fail groups.
cause: An attempt was made to create a disk group with a different number of fail groups at each data site.
action: Ensure that the data sites have an equal number of fail groups and try again.

description: active use of disk '%s' precludes its label clear
cause: A LABEL CLEAR command specified a disk that was in use.
action: Dismount the disk group that is using this disk and retry the the LABEL CLEAR command. Query the V$ASM_CLIENT fixed view in an Oracle Automatic Storage Management (Oracle ASM) instance or use ASMCMD LSOF to list active clients.
params: 1) disk_name: Path name of the disk specified for the label clear operation.

description: Oracle ASMFD is not configured in the system.
cause: An Oracle ASM Filter Driver (Oracle ASMFD) command was run without either an Oracle ASMFD library present or kernel driver loaded.
action: Use the command ASMCMD AFD_STATE to find the status of Oracle ASMFD.

description: all disks in disk group '%s' need to be online
cause: One or more disks in the disk group were offline.
action: Online the disks that are offline.

description: SECUREFILE block checking fault injection event
cause: This is an internal debugging event only
action: N/A

description: adding (%s) blocks to save undo segment in tablespace %s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Save undo for the offline tablespace at segment MAXSIZE.
action: Check the storage parameters for the system tablespace. The tablespace needs to be brought back online so the undo can be applied.

description: adding (%s) blocks to temporary segment in tablespace %s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending a temporary segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to table %s.%s partition %s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending a table partition violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to table %s.%s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending a table violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to cluster %s.%s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending a cluster violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to index %s.%s partition %s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending an index partition violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to index %s.%s subpartition %s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending an index subpartition violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to index %s.%s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending an index violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to LOB segment %s.%s partition %s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending a LOB segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to LOB segment %s.%s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending a LOB segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to lob segment %s.%s subpartition %s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending a LOB segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: adding (%s) blocks to table %s.%s subpartition %s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending a table subpartition violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: invalid MAXSIZE storage option value
cause: Invalid value was specified for MAXSIZE storage clause. Invalid value was specified for MAXSIZE storage clause.
action: Correct the value and retry command. Correct the value and retry command.

description: invalid MAXSIZE storage option value
cause: Minimum of 1M should have been specified against the MAXSIZE storage clause.
action: Correct the value and retry command.

description: invalid RETENTION storage option value
cause: Value of MIN retention should have been nonzero.
action: Correct the value and retry command.

description: The ALTER FREELIST/RETENTION operation is not supported on a SECUREFILE segment.
cause: The ALTER FREELIST/RETENTION operation is not supported on a SECUREFILE segment.
action: Check the LOB type and retry.

description: adding %s blocks to rollback segment %s with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending a rollback segment violated MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit and retry command.

description: Creating initial extent of size %s in tablespace of extent size %s
cause: Creation of SECUREFILE segment failed due to small tablespace extent size.
action: Create tablespace with larger extent size and reissue command.

description: Internal event
cause: NA
action: Contact Oracle Support Services

description: Internal event
cause: NA
action: Contact Oracle Support Services

description: Internal event
cause: NA
action: Contact Oracle Support Services

description: Internal event
cause: NA
action: Contact Oracle Support Services

description: Internal event
cause: NA
action: Contact Oracle Support Services

description: Event for temp segment cleanup used for temp lobs
cause: Temp LOB segments used for temporary LOBs are deleted only on session exit which may lead to large amounts of memory being held across multiple sessions.
action: Setting this event will cause temporary LOB segments to be freed when there are no active temporary LOBs in the session. Setting this event will have a significant performance impact as it can cause temporary lob segments to be allocated and deleted many times during a session rather than once per session. Use this event only when temporary LOB segment memory use is an issue.

description: SECUREFILE space double allocation checking event
cause: This is an internal debugging event only
action: N/A

description: Event to ignore missing entry in seg$
cause: Internal errors due to missing entry in data dictionary table seg$
action: Set this event at level 1024 to disable checking seg$. This is to allow dropping the segment that is failing with an internal error because the corresponding entry does not exist in seg$.

description: space preallocation tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event, and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: space preallocation history logging event
cause: This is an internal debugging event, and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: space background task cancellation event
cause: This is an internal event used for space background task cancellation notification.
action: N/A

description: space background framework shutdown event
cause: This is an internal event used for space background framework shutdown notification.
action: N/A

description: Internal debugging event
cause: This is an internal debugging event used for dropping temporary segments in SMON instead of in slave process.
action: N/A

description: Internal debugging event
cause: This is an internal debugging event used for simulating segment creation error.
action: N/A

description: Internal debugging event
cause: This is an internal debugging event used for simulating space background task operation error.
action: N/A

description: Internal debugging event
cause: This is an internal debugging event used for performing SYSAUX file online and offline checks in SMON instead of in slave process.
action: N/A

description: extent allocation alignment event
cause: This is an internal debugging event, and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: temporary space management tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event, and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: fail to repair LOB segment
cause: The segment_repair routine failed to repair the LOB segment. Additional information in the trace file provides details about the error.
action: Check additional information in the trace file.

description: Oracle temporary file creation does not allocate space on file systems.
cause: Oracle temporary file creation did not allocate space on file systems until it was needed. This enables fast creation of temporary files with no system overhead.
action: Enable this event to have Oracle fill empty blocks in temporary files on file creation.

description: ILM activity tracking is disabled
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: SYSAUX is disabled
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: SYSAUX tablespace does not exist
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: Internal event to trigger extension of ILMSTAT segment
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: Unable to allocate memory for ILM activity tracking
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: ILM statistics tracking is disabled
cause: This is an internal event. ILM statistics are not collected either because the tablespace is SYSTEM or because it is bootstrap processing.
action: N/A

description: ILM activity tracking disabled due to multiple errors
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: internal debugging event to disable SecureFile UFS reservation
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: adding (%s) blocks to heat map segment with MAXSIZE (%s)
cause: Extending the heat map segment violated the MAXSIZE limit.
action: Increase the MAXSIZE limit.

description: Heat map segment cannot be created
cause: SYSAUX tablespace has uniform extent allocation and the extent size is not a multiple of megabyte.
action: Re-create SYSAUX tablespace with autoallocate extent management policy or use the uniform extent size which is a multiple of megabyte.

description: Heat map activity tracking is disabled
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: temporary file space management tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: Internal event to trigger extension of heat map segment
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: Unable to allocate memory for heat map activity tracking
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: Heat map statistics tracking is disabled
cause: This is an internal event. Heat map statistics are not collected either because the tablespace is SYSTEM or because it is bootstrap processing.
action: N/A

description: Heat map tracking disabled due to multiple errors
cause: This is an internal event
action: N/A

description: bitmapped tablespace space management tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support or development.
action: N/A

description: extent space management debugging event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: Check the tablespace type.

description: incorrect tablespace specified
cause: Clear free space operation was used on the temporary, undo, or SYSTEM tablespace, which was not supported.
action: Check the tablespace type and reissue the statement.

description: inmemory_xmem_size specified is less than a minimum of (%s) bytes
cause: inmemory_xmem_size was less than the minimum expected by the system.
action: Issue the command after changing the value for the inmemory_xmem_size parameter.

description: invalid combination of parameters passed to the DBMS_SPACE_ADMIN function
cause: Object ID could not be specified for undo or save undo segments.
action: Issue the command after changing the value for the parameters.

description: dropping temporary tablespace with tablespace ID number (tsn) %s is blocked due to active sort segments held by instance %s
cause: The temporary tablespace had sort segments in use.
action: Wait for sort segments to complete or terminate sort session and then retry dropping the temporary tablespace.

description: event used to change retry count before raising ORA-60100
cause: N/A
action: "alter system or session set event 60101 level <retry count>"

description: creating a new sort segment for temporary tablespace (tsn):%s (con_id):%s is blocked due to inactive sort segments for the tablespace not being dropped
cause: The temporary tablespace has inactive sort segments which have not been dropped. This could be caused due to long running sessions that are still consuming temporary space.
action: Execute the following query to check if there are any sessions still consuming temporary space from the inactive sort segments: select USERNAME, SESSION_ADDR, SESSION_NUM, SQLADDR, SQL_ID, BLOCKS from v$sort_usage where ts#=(&tsn); If there are any active sessions, wait for them to complete or terminate the session. If there are no active sessions consuming temporary space from the inactive sort segments, restart the instance to drop the inactive sort segments. The process trace file contains additional diagnostics to investigate the issue.

description: bigfile tablespace space management tracing event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: bigfile tablespace space management debugging event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: N/A

description: tablespace operation debugging event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support or development.
action: None.

description: SecureFiles LOB force FSG creation event
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development. Oracle server does not allocate Free Space Group until needed.
action: Enable this event to force Oracle server allocate FSG at the time of LOB segment creation.

description: invalid value for 'NEXT' property in storage clause
cause: The 'NEXT' property in the storage clause can only assume values 1 M or 8 M or 64 M for locally managed tablespaces.
action: Correct the 'NEXT' property in the storage clause and retry.

description: invalid temporary data block found
cause: An invalid temporary data block was read from the disk. The cause is uncertain. Possible causes are: - The media storage of the temporary tablespace caused corruption. - A latent issue caused by an unsuccessful clean up action for a previously failed operation involving temporary objects. In either cases, there is no permanent data loss.
action: Check the alert log for more information and validate storage media for the temporary tablespace. Retry the operation to see if it succeeds. If the error persists, contact Oracle Support.

description: bigfile tablespace segment creation for space optimization during tablespace RESIZE
cause: This is an internal segment creation scheme whereby space for initial extent is searched starting from smallest file offset. This benefits tablespace RESIZE by allowing for the smallest resize value before encountering ORA-03297.
action: Enable this event when creating table or index.

description: GDR operation could not be performed on all objects in the tablespace.
cause: This is an internal error thrown when we cannot successfully perform GDR operation on an object in the current tablespace.
action: Fix the problem and rerun the Ghost Data Removal(GDR) command.

description: Event for controlling stack gathering for temporal segments.
cause: A stack dump is needed to identify the holders of temporal segments across PDB close. Gathering this information may lead to high CPU cycles.
action: Enable this event when information about temporal segments holders is needed.

description: invalid value %s for parameter %s; must be smaller than %s%% of available SYSTEM temporary space
cause: The value for this parameter was invalid.
action: Choose a value as indicated by the message.

description: specified data file or temporary file size exceeded the maximum allowed size
cause: An attempt was made to resize the data file or temporary file with a value beyond the maximum allowed file size (MAXSIZE).
action: Try with a value smaller than the maximum allowed file size (MAXSIZE).

description: Key-organized is not supported.
cause: The partitioning key of the bottom level partition is not qualified for using key-organized property.
action: The partitioning key must be a single, non-virtual, and Oracle number column.

description: cannot use virtual column as ORDER BY or FILTER BY column of domain index
cause: An attempt was made to create a composite domain index by specifying a virtual column as an ORDER BY or FILTER BY column.
action: Remove the virtual column from the CREATE INDEX statement.

description: cannot create sharded local domain index with indextype %s.%s
cause: An attempt was made to create local domain indexes on sharded tables that were only allowed for a subset of native indextypes.
action: Do not create a local domain index on sharded table with this indextype.

description: Partition maintenance operation cannot affect more than %s partitions in presence of local domain indexes.
cause: An invalid number of partitions were specified for a partition maintenance operation. A partition maintenance operation can only affect a maximum number of partitions when there is a local domain index on the table: - One partition or subpartition for ADD PARTITION or ADD SUBPARTITION. - One partition or subpartition for DROP PARTITION or DROP SUBPARTITION. - One partition or subpartition for TRUNCATE PARTITION or TRUNCATE SUBPARTITION. - Two source partitions or subpartitions for MERGE PARTITION or MERGE SUBPARTITION. - Two target partitions or subpartitions for SPLIT PARTITION or SPLIT SUBPARTITION.
action: Modify the partition maintenance operation to affect only the allowed number of partitions or subpartitions, and then retry the statement.
params: 1) maximum_affected_partitions: The maximum number of affected partitions allowed for a partition maintenance operation on a table having a local domain index.

description: unsupported partitioning scheme for local domain indexes
cause: The creation of local domain index was not supported for the partitioning scheme of the base table. For referenced partitioned base tables, the parent table was using an unsupported partitioning scheme for local domain indexes.
action: Perform one of the following to resolve the error: - Modify the partitioning scheme of the table to a supported partitioning scheme for local domain indexes. - Attempt to create a global non-partitioned domain index on this table. - Do not create a local domain index on this table.

description: Cannot modify partitioning scheme of local domain index %s.%s.
cause: An attempt was made to modify the partitioning scheme of a table with a local domain index to an unsupported configuration.
action: Do not modify the partitioning scheme of the base table.
params: 1) index_schema: The schema of the local domain index. 2) index_name: The name of the local domain index.

description: cannot change partitioned table with local domain index %s.%s into non-partitioned table
cause: An attempt was made to change a partitioned table with local domain indexes into a non-partitioned table.
action: Do not change the partitioned table into a non-partitioned table or drop any domain indexes before attempting the operation.

description: ARRAY DML type %s.%s of indextype must be a VARRAY
cause: An attempt was made to use a type that was not a VARRAY in the ARRAY DML clause of the CREATE INDEXTYPE or ALTER INDEXTYPE statement.
action: Specify a VARRAY type as the collection type in the ARRAY DML clause of the CREATE INDEXTYPE or ALTER INDEXTYPE statement.
params: 1) type_schema: The schema of the type in the ARRAY DML clause. 2) type_name: The name of the type in the ARRAY DML clause.

description: Could not validate return type of generic pipelined table function %s.
cause: The ANYTYPE description of the generic pipelined table function was not found, or it did not describe a collection type.
action: Verify that the ODCITABLEDESCRIBE method of the generic pipelined table function is correct and describes a valid collection type.
params: 1) function_name: The name of the pipelined table function.

description: mismatched data type descriptor from opaque object instance
cause: The data type descriptor returned by the ODCITableFetch interface inside an ANYDATA or ANYDATASET instance did not match the output data type described by the ODCITableDescribe interface.
action: Verify the implementation of the ODCITableFetch and ODCITableDescribe interfaces and ensure the output data type is consistent during the describe phase and the fetch phase.

description: cannot use a BOOLEAN type column as ORDER BY or FILTER BY column of domain index
cause: An attempt was made to create a composite domain index with a FILTER BY or ORDER BY column of BOOLEAN data type.
action: Remove the column from the CREATE INDEX statement.

description: The collection image of type %s.%s is invalid.
cause: An attempt was made to read a degenerate collection image or the collection image was not constructed correctly.
action: Contact Oracle Support.
params: 1) type_schema: The schema of the collection type. 2) type_name: The name of the collection type.

description: The privilege that can be granted or revoked on operator type is EXECUTE
cause: An attempt was made to grant or revoke an invalid privilege on operator. You can only grant or revoke the EXECUTE object privilege on operator.
action: Do not attempt to grant or revoke any privilege besides EXECUTE on operator.

description: The privilege that can be granted or revoked on indextype is EXECUTE.
cause: An attempt was made to grant or revoke an invalid privilege on indextype. You can only grant or revoke the EXECUTE object privilege on indextype.
action: Do not attempt to grant or revoke any privilege besides EXECUTE on indextype.

description: The element type of array DML type %s.%s does not match the specified element type %s.
cause: The element type specified in the ARRAY DML clause for a CREATE INDEXTYPE or ALTER INDEXTYPE statement does not match the element type of the specified collection type.
action: Verify that the element type of the collection in the ARRAY DML clause and the element type in the ARRAY DML are the same.
params: 1) schema: The schema of the collection type. 2) name: The name of the collection type. 3) element: The element type in the ARRAY DML clause.

description: Had error executing RMAN. Error code: %s
cause: Had error either when spawning a process to execute RMAN commands or getting RMAN process exit status.
action: Check the error code and RDBMS logs.

description: RMAN exited with status: %s, more details are available in the RMAN output file: %s
cause: RMAN process exited with non-zero status.
action: Check RMAN output log.

description: Failed to read RMAN output from scheduler backup job. Log file: %s
cause: An error occurred when reading a RMAN output file.
action: Check RDBMS logs.

description: Internal error: database connection should be to the shard PDB when PDB name is not provided
cause: An error occurred when updating a sharded database backup wallet.
action: Check RDBMS logs.

description: Internal error: database connection should be to the CDB when the shard PDB name is provided
cause: An error occurred when updating a sharded database backup wallet.
action: Check RDBMS logs.

description: Internal error: Failed to update backup wallet
cause: An error occurred when updating a sharded database backup wallet.
action: Check RDBMS logs.

description: HOST command is not supported when the RMAN command is submitted from GDSCTL command interface.
cause: RMAN command HOST was submitted from GDSCTL.
action: Remove the HOST command from the RMAN commands to submit.

description: transaction ID specified is not quarantined
cause: The transaction ID (<usn><slot><sqn>) specified in the command is not quarantined.
action: Provide the correct transaction ID. Quarantined transaction details can be found in DBA_QUARANTINED_TRANSACTIONS. This DDL must be run from the container in which the quarantine is present.

description: cannot execute the DML because it encountered a quarantined transaction (%s.%s.%s) holding a row lock (TX) required by this statement
cause: A quarantined transaction holding a conflicting transaction lock failed to recover.
action: Resolve the transaction quarantine by following the recommended steps in the Oracle documentation and drop it using the DDL command ALTER DATABASE DROP TRANSACTION QUARANTINE.

description: (internal) unable to quarantine %s.%s.%s transaction because the system reached maximum number of quarantined transactions %s
cause: (Internal error only) Transaction quarantine maximum limit reached. This will result in escalation. to the PDB: potentially shutting down the PDB and disabling transaction recovery.
action: Try restarting the PDB and if problem persists contact Oracle support.

description: compatible must be set to 23.0.0.0.0 or higher in order to set max_columns=EXTENDED
cause: Setting the parameter max_columns=EXTENDED required the compatible initialization parameter to be set to Oracle Database 23.0.0.0.0 compatibility or higher. The compatible initialization parameter is currently not set to release 23.0.0.0.0 or a later version.
action: Set the compatible parameter in initialization parameter file to release 23.0.0.0.0 or later version.

description: max_columns can not be set to STANDARD as there are one or more objects with more than 1000 columns
cause: Setting the parameter max_columns to STANDARD is not possible because there are existing objects with more than 1000 columns.
action: Remove all objects with more than 1000 columns prior to setting max_columns to STANDARD. To identify all objects with more than 1000 columns, issue the following query: select distinct owner, table_name from dba_tab_columns where column_id > 1000;

description: undo segment file at PDB: %s, TSN: %s, DBA:0x%s cannot be read
cause: An attempt to read a undo segment file failed because the file was dropped or it was never created.
action: Create a valid undo segment file.

description: cannot disconnect an established connection to a remote database when an active transaction exists
cause: An attempt to disconnect an established connection failed because an active transaction exists.
action: Commit or rollback the active transaction before disconnecting the connection.

description: Parameter %s cannot be modified.
cause: An attempt to update the parameter failed because it was allowed only in Oracle Autonomous Database on Shared Infrastructure(ADB-S).
action: Refer Oracle Database documentation for the right parameter to use.

description: Parameter %s conflicts with %s parameter.
cause: An attempt to update the parameter failed because it conflicts with the other parameter.

description: invalid refresh SCN %s specified
cause: An attempt was made to refresh the pluggable database to a system change number (SCN) that was less than or equal to the last refresh SCN.
action: Reissue the statement with a valid SCN number.

description: insufficient disk space
cause: There was insufficient disk space at the specified location.
action: Free some disk space.

description: %s is the wrong type of pluggable database
cause: A list of pluggable databases was given to a command but the named one is not of the same type as the earlier ones in the list. The different types are Data Guard pluggable databases and non Data Guard pluggable databases.
action: Resubmit the command naming only pluggable databases that are of one type or the other.

description: remote site %s not found
cause: An attempt was made to create a standby pluggable database before the remote site had been defined.
action: Check the known remote databases and use Data Guard Broker to add any missing site.

description: Missing credential for remote site %s
cause: The credential required to access the remote site could not be found.
action: Use Data Guard Broker to confirm the validity of the remote site.

description: unable to refresh the pluggable database
cause: An attempt was made to refresh a pluggable database (PDB) using a catalog without specifying the source database link name.
action: Retry the operation with the USING <dblink> clause.

description: operation not allowed for standby pluggable database %s
cause: An attempt was made to perform an operation on a standby pluggable database (PDB) that was not appropriate for such a PDB.
action: Perform the operation against a normal pluggable database or do not perform the operation at all.

description: invalid refresh time %s specified
cause: An attempt was made to refresh the pluggable database to a time that was less than or equal to the last refresh time.
action: Reissue the statement with a valid time.

description: invalid refresh SCN %s specified. Max possible refresh SCN %s
cause: An attempt was made to refresh the pluggable database to a system change number (SCN) that was greater than the source Container Database's (CDB) current SCN or the maximum SCN of the archive logs available in the refresh catalog or in the remote_recovery_file_dest
action: Reissue the statement with a valid SCN number or refresh without the UNTIL SCN clause.

description: invalid refresh time %s specified. Max possible refresh time %s
cause: An attempt was made to refresh the pluggable database to a time that was greater than the source Container Database's (CDB) current time or the maximum time of the archive logs available in the refresh catalog or in the remote_recovery_file_dest
action: Reissue the statement with a valid time or refresh without the UNTIL TIME clause.

description: encountered error %s during Replay Upgrade
cause: An error was encountered during Replay Upgrade of a pluggable database (PDB).
action: Open the PDB in upgrade mode and query the DBA_REPLAY_UPGRADE_ERRORS view to find the statement text and error explanation.

description: missing or invalid application name
cause: A valid application name was not present where required.
action: Reissue the statement with a valid application name.

description: invalid source for a standby pluggable database
cause: An attempt was made to create a standby pluggable database from an inappropriate source pluggable database, such as an existing standby pluggable database.
action: Retry the command using an appropriate pluggable database for the source pluggable database.

description: cannot synchronize an application version or patch that is blocked
cause: An attempt was made to synchronize an application version or patch that was blocked.
action: Unblock the application version or patch. Query DBA_APP_VERSIONS or DBA_APP_PATCHES to find the version or patch that is blocked.

description: implicit application common user cannot own common objects
cause: An attempt was made to set the sharing status to metadata, data, or extended data on an object owned by an implicit user.
action: Do not attempt to set the sharing status to metadata, data, or extended data on an object owned by an implicit user.

description: standby pluggable database %s requires more recovery
cause: An attempt was made to open a standby pluggable database (PDB) before recovery had applied sufficient redo from the primary to make the PDB consistent.
action: Open the primary pluggable database, ensure redo shipping is enabled to the standby, and start managed recovery for the standby PDB. Allow recovery to catch up. Then cancel it and attempt the open operation again.

description: Pluggable database (PDB) %s has a per PDB physical standby
cause: An attempt was made to drop a pluggable database (PDB) that was protected by one or more per PDB physical standbys.
action: If the operation is really required then either drop the per PDB physical standby databases first, or perform a role transition to switch the PDB into a per PDB physical standby and then drop it.

description: Unimplemented operation for pluggable database %s
cause: An attempt was made to perform an operation on the pluggable database (PDB) that had not yet been implemented.
action: If the operation is unplug for a PDB that has one or more per PDB physical standbys then drop the standby PDBs first and then try operation again.

description: cannot enable supplemental logging on PDB without local undo enabled
cause: Local undo mode was disabled.
action: Enable local undo mode before enabling per pluggable database (PDB) supplemental logging.

description: encountered an error during application sync
cause: An error was encountered during application sync.
action: Query the DBA_APP_ERRORS view to find the statement text and error explanation.

description: unable to switchover when a TDE SEPS wallet is not configured
cause: This operation could not be completed because Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) Secure External Password Store (SEPS) wallet was not configured.
action: Configure the TDE SEPS wallet before attempting this operation again.

description: operation not allowed due to lockdown
cause: Lockdown is enforced to disallow the operation, as configured by the administrator.
action: For cloud services please consult the list of allowed operations in the documentation. For non-cloud systems please consult with your database administrator.

description: unable to create pluggable database using XML
cause: An attempt was made to create a pluggable database using XML with a fuzzy data file.
action: Create a refresh clone using XML.

description: invalid pluggable database name specified for root clone
cause: The pluggable database specified for USING ROOT CLONE was either nonexistent or not a root clone.
action: Reissue the statement with a valid pluggable database name.

description: too many database links in use
cause: The pluggable database exceeded the maximum open links.
action: Free up some open links by committing or rolling back the transaction and canceling open cursors that reference remote databases.

description: Internal KPDB error 60525
cause: Internal KPDB error 60525.
action: This is an internal error; contact Oracle Support Services.

description: cannot switch to shared undo mode when perPDB supplemental logging is enabled
cause: Supplemental logging is disabled at CDB$ROOT container but enabled at pluggable databases (PDBs). Switching to shared undo mode would cause PDB-level supplemental logging to be lost.
action: Enable supplemental logging at CDB$ROOT or drop supplemental logging at all pluggable databases (PDBs).

description: cannot externally modify partition containing dblink
cause: An attempt was made to external modify a partition containing a dblink.
action: External Modify is not allowed for a partition containing a dblink.

description: operation not supported for a PET having all dblink partition
cause: An attempt was made to perform an operation on a Partition External Table (PET) having all dblink partition.
action: Do not perform the unsupported operation.

description: more than one database link specified
cause: Only one value of database link is allowed for database link location.
action: Specify single database link.

description: cannot exchange partition containing dblink
cause: An attempt was made to exchange a partition containing a dblink
action: Exchange is not allowed for a partition containing a dblink.

description: operation not supported on a PDB that is not marked ACTIVE
cause: An attempt was made to modify a property for a pluggable database (PDB) that is not ACTIVE.
action: Verify the status of the PDB in DBA_PDBS and retry the operation after transitioning the PDB to ACTIVE.

description: A static lockdown profile cannot be created from dynamic lockdown profile %s.
cause: An attempt to create a static lockdown profile from a dynamic lockdown profile was made.
action: Create a dynamic profile from this profile or create a new profile.

description: Common user or role names must consist of only ASCII characters.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a common user or role with a name that is not valid for common users or roles. In addition to the usual rules for user and role names, common user and role names must consist of only ASCII characters.
