action: None.

description: external partitions not supported with MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE
cause: An attempt was made to use external partition with a MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE table.
action: None.

description: out of memory for MEMOPTIMIZE area
cause: MEMOPTIMIZE memory area was full and did not have any free buffers.
action: Restart the instance with an appropriate value for MEMOPTIMIZE memory area parameter.

description: Bitmap join index not supported with MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE
cause: An attempt is being made to use a bitmap join index with a MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE table.
action: None.

description: Materialized view log cannot be created on a MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE table.
cause: An attempt was made to create a materialized view log on a MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE table.
action: None.

description: online index build or rebuild not supported with MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE
cause: An attempt was made to build an index online with a MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE table.
action: None.

description: timeout occurred while waiting for lock to flush object %s data object %s
cause: While waiting to lock a memoptimize flush object, a timeout occurred .
action: Retry the operation later.

description: Enable MEMOPTIMIZE FOR READ sync insert
cause: Setting this event to level one to enable MEMOPTIMIZE FOR READ sync insert.
action: None.

description: MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE feature cannot be enabled on row archive table.
cause: An attempt is being made to use the MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE attribute on a table with row archive.
action: None.

description: function-based index not supported with MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE
cause: An attempt was made to use a function-based index with a MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE table.
action: None.

description: domain index not supported with MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE
cause: An attempt is being made to use a domain index with a MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE table.
action: None.

description: space error (%s) occurred trying to flush buffered MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE data
cause: During data flush from memory buffers to disk, a space error is being encountered, resutling in failure of flush.
action: Review the space error and take action appropriate for that error.

description: Enforcing a unique constraint using non-unique indexes is not supported with MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE.
cause: An attempt is being made to enforce a unique constraint using a non-unique index with a MEMOPTIMIZE FOR WRITE table.

description: DESC is missing in ORDER BY clause within APPROX_RANK.
cause: The DESC keyword was not specified in the ORDER BY clause within the APPROX_RANK function.
action: Add the DESC keyword.

description: invalid expression in ORDER BY clause within APPROX_RANK function
cause: The expression in the ORDER BY clause within the APPROX_RANK function is invalid.
action: Use the APPROX_COUNT or APPROX_SUM function in the ORDER BY clause.

description: Multiple expressions are used in the ORDER BY clause within the APPROX_RANK function.
cause: Multiple expressions are used in the ORDER BY clause within APPROX_RANK function.
action: Use a single expression in the ORDER BY clause within the APPROX_RANK function.

description: The APPROX_RANK functions used different PARTITION BY keys.
cause: APPROX_RANK functions use different PARTITION BY keys.
action: Use the same PARTITION BY keys across APPROX_RANK functions.

description: PARTITION BY key in APPROX_RANK is not a subset of GROUP BY key.
cause: The PARTITION BY key in the APPROX_RANK function was not a subset of the key in the GROUP BY clause.
action: Use a subset of the key in the GROUP BY clause in the PARTITION BY key within the APPROX_RANK function.

description: Missing GROUP BY clause when approximate top functions are used.
cause: The GROUP BY clause was missing when the approximate top functions were used.
action: Add the GROUP BY clause.

description: Missing HAVING clause when approximate top functions are used.
cause: The HAVING clause was missing when the approximate top functions were used.
action: Add the HAVING clause.

description: Mixed approximate top functions with window functions or non approximate top functions.
cause: An attempt was made to use window functions or aggregates that were not approximate top functions along with approximate top functions.
action: Remove the window functions or non approximate top functions.

description: More than one expression appears in GROUP BY clause but not in PARTITION BY clause.
cause: An attempt was made to involve more than one columns as the top N key.
action: Remove the extra expression(s) from GROUP BY clause, or add extra expression(s) to PARTITION BY part in HAVING clause

description: Missing one or more corresponding APPROX_RANK clause in HAVING list when approximate top functions are used.
cause: One or more corresponding APPROX_RANK clauses were missing when approximate top functions were used.
action: Add the APPROX_RANK clause in HAVING list for each approximate top N function that appears in SELECT or ORDER BY clause

description: HAVING clause can only contain AND predicates when approximate top functions are used.
cause: the HAVING clause contained predicates other than AND when approximate top functions were used.
action: Only use the AND predicate with the HAVING clause.

description: Each predicate in HAVING clause must be in the format of 'APPROX_RANK(PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ... DESC) <(=) n' when approximate top functions are used.
cause: Illegal predicates were used in the HAVING clause when approximate top functions were used.
action: Correct the format to 'APPROX_RANK (PARTITION BY ? ORDER BY ? DESC) <(=) n'.

description: GROUPING SETS, CUBE and ROLLUP cannot be applied to approximate functions.
cause: An attempt was made to use GROUPING SETS, CUBE or ROLLUP over the approximate functions.
action: Remove any GROUPING SETS, CUBE or ROLLUP when using approximate functions.

description: A negative value has been passed to APPROX_SUM function.
cause: An attempt was made to pass a negative value to the APPROX_SUM function.
action: Only pass expressions that have a non-negative value to the APPROX_SUM function.

description: The subqueries that contain approximate top functions must be unnested.
cause: An attempt was made to execute subqueries that contain approximate top functions without unnesting.
action: Remove the hint or the parameters that are preventing subquery unnesting.

description: The Nest handle is invalid.
cause: The Nest handle was not valid.
action: None.

description: The Nest open failed.
cause: The Nest open failed.
action: None.

description: The Nest is already opened.
cause: An attempt was made to open a Nest that was already opened.
action: None.

description: The Nest lookup failed.
cause: The Nest lookup for a given pluggable database (PDB) failed.
action: None.

description: A Child Nest is present.
cause: An attempt to delete a Nest that had a dependent child Nest failed.
action: None.

description: failure to delete a Nest that is not created
cause: An attempt to delete a Nest that was not created failed.
action: None.

description: The Nest is already created.
cause: An attempt was made to create a Nest that was already created.
action: None.

description: The Nest creation failed.
cause: The Nest creation failed with an operating system operation.
action: None.

description: failure to open a Nest that was not created
cause: An attempt to open the Nest before it was created failed.
action: None.

description: The Nest open failed.
cause: The Nest open failed with an operating system operation.
action: None.

description: failure to update a Nest that is not opened
cause: An attempt to update a Nest that was not opened failed.
action: None.

description: The Nest update failed.
cause: The Nest update failed with an operating system operation.
action: None.

description: failure to close a Nest that is not opened
cause: An attempt to close a Nest that was not open failed.
action: None.

description: The Nest close failed.
cause: The Nest close failed with an operating system operation.
action: None.

description: The Nest delete failed.
cause: The Nest delete failed with an operating system operation.
action: None.

description: dedicated broker not enabled
cause: Nest connections require an enabled dedicated broker. The dedicated broker was not enabled in the current instance.
action: Enable the dedicated broker.

description: invalid Nest parameter
cause: An invalid value or length for the Nest parameter was specified.
action: None.

description: The Nest creation failed due to reaching the maximum depth.
cause: The child Nest could not be created due to reaching the maximum depth.
action: None.

description: no PDB nest found for specified PDB
cause: A pluggable database (PDB) nest was not found for the specified PDB.
action: Check the connection broker and listener settings.

description: connection outside PDB nest
cause: The current pluggable database (PDB) connection was outside of the PDB nest.
action: Check the connection broker and listener settings.

description: connection outside CDB or PDB nests
cause: The current connection was outside of the multitenant container database (CDB) or pluggable database (PDB) nests.

description: turn on statistics tracing
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support or development.
action: Contact Oracle Support.

description: invalid statistic group handle
cause: The statistic group handle was invalid.
action: None.

description: invalid statistic group identifier
cause: The statistic group identifier doesn't match the handle.
action: None.

description: statistic group handle mismatch
cause: Specified statistic group handle is wrong.
action: None.

description: statistic group invalid %s
cause: An invalid parameter was passed to statistic group layer.
action: None.

description: PGA Tracing On
cause: This is an internal debugging event and must be enabled only under the supervision of Oracle Support Services or development.
action: None

description: Extent allocation failed.
cause: The unified program global area (PGA) extent allocation in the unified PGA pool failed.
action: None.

description: The requested memory allocation for "%s" (%s bytes) is greater than the allowed number of bytes (%s).
cause: The requested memory size is larger larger than what is allowed by the system.
action: Change the SQL to allocate a smaller size (for example, use a smaller PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET or reduce the amount of data processed by the database operation).

description: invalid extent ownership
cause: The current process did not own the extent.
action: None.

description: MEMORY_SIZE %s is greater than MEMORY_MAX_SIZE %s
cause: The specified value of MEMORY_SIZE was greater than MEMORY_MAX_SIZE.
action: Reduce the specified value to be less than MEMORY_MAX_SIZE

description: cannot dynamically set MEMORY_SIZE if not set at startup
cause: MEMORY_SIZE could not be set. Unified Memory can only be enabled during instance startup by setting MEMORY_SIZE to a non-zero value.
action: Set MEMORY_SIZE at startup.

description: cannot shrink MEMORY_SIZE
cause: The new value of MEMORY_SIZE was less than its current value.
action: Set a new value higher than the current value.

description: cannot set MEMORY_SIZE to zero
cause: The new value of MEMORY_SIZE could not be set to zero while the instance was running.
action: Unified Memory can be disabled by setting the MEMORY_SIZE to zero in a parameter file.

description: MEMORY_SIZE %s is invalid due to insufficent large pages totaling %s bytes
cause: Not enough large pages were available for the new system global area (SGA) size.
action: Increase the number of large pages or decrease MEMORY_SIZE.

description: cannot set %s parameter value since MEMORY_SIZE is set
cause: MEMORY_SIZE when set to a non-zero value enabled Unified Memory and hence did not allow other memory parameters to be set individually at the multitenant container database (CDB) level.
action: Unset or set MEMORY_SIZE to zero.

description: invalid options were specified for FUZZY_MATCH operator
cause: The options specified for FUZZY_MATCH() were invalid. For instance, RELATE_TO_SHORTER and UNSCALED options were mutually exclusive. EDIT_TOLERANCE option could only be applied to WHOLE_WORD_MATCH.
action: Pass in valid options to FUZZY_MATCH.

description: invalid numeric argument was specified for FUZZY_MATCH operator
cause: The numeric argument passed into FUZZY_MATCH() was either not a constant or was outside the acceptable range. EDIT_TOLERANCE percentage should be between 0-99.
action: Pass in a valid numeric argument to FUZZY_MATCH.

description: invalid numeric argument is specified for PHONIC_ENCODE operator
cause: The numeric argument passed into PHONIC_ENCODE() was either not a constant or was outside the acceptable range. Maximum output code length is 12.
action: Pass in an acceptable numeric argument to PHONIC_ENCODE.

description: string argument specified for FUZZY_MATCH operator was too long
cause: The string argument passed into FUZZY_MATCH() was longer than 4000 bytes. Maximum input length is 4000 bytes.
action: Pass in string arguments no longer than 4000 bytes to FUZZY_MATCH.

description: options for FUZZY_MATCH were specified in the wrong order
cause: EDIT_TOLERANCE option passed into FUZZY_MATCH() has to appear before options such as RELATE_TO_SHORTER and UNSCALED.
action: Pass in EDIT_TOLERANCE option to FUZZY_MATCH before other options.

description: DB upgrade terminating due to check "%s" not having been addressed before upgrading
cause: This check has not been addressed prior to upgrading. Hence, database upgrade cannot continue and needs to terminate.
action: Read the comments above the failing check in the upgrade log for instructions on how to address this check. The comments start with the word "DOC". After fixing this check, retry the database upgrade.

description: UUID() generation in the underlying zero trust security library "libnnzsrv" function call to "ztuguid" is failing with the error code %s.
cause: The underlying zero trust security library function call is returning an error. The error code has been printed as part of the error message. The error could be transient, such as an out-of-memory situation, and a retry of the operation may succeed. If the error persists, it indicates an incorrect database installation, such as the required library not having been installed or removed from the system.
action: Retry the operation. If the error persists, then verify the Oracle Database installation. If the error cannot be resolved, contact Oracle Support.

description: %s is not a valid UUID value.
cause: "The specified value is not a valid UUID. It is not a UUID of Version 4 and Variant 1."
action: Specify a valid Version 4 Variant 1 argument.

description: Invalid or unsupported argument to UUID function
cause: "An invalid or unsupported argument to the UUID function is specified."

description: function is not allowed outside of MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause
cause: The function was specified outside of the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause. This function is only allowed in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause.
action: Rewrite the SQL statement.

description: invalid value specified for bounded quantifier in MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause
cause: The specified lower bound or upper bound value was greater than UB4MAXVAL. The lower bound value must be non-negative. The upper bound value must be strictly positive. The upper bound value must be greater than or equal to the lower bound value.
action: Choose an appropriate value and retry the operation.

description: invalid variable name
cause: The specified variable name was invalid. Variable names are not allowed to be "^", "$", or "*".
action: Choose an appropriate variable name and retry the operation.

description: illegal variable definition
cause: The specified variable definition was invalid. Variables defined in the DEFINE clause must be in the PATTERN clause. Variables defined in the SUBSET clause cannot be in the PATTERN clause. Variables cannot be defined twice either in the SUBSET clause or the DEFINE clause.
action: Choose an appropriate variable and retry the operation.

description: illegal variable reference
cause: The referenced variable was invalid. Variables referenced in the SUBSET clause must be in the PATTERN clause. Variables referenced in the DEFINE clause, the MEASURES clause, and the AFTER MATCH SKIP TO must be in the PATTERN clause or defined in the SUBSET clause.
action: Choose an appropriate variable and retry the operation.

description: expression needs to be aliased
cause: The expression was not aliased. MEASURES clause items have to be aliased.
action: Choose an appropriate variable and retry the operation.

description: illegal nesting of operators in MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause
cause: An attempt was made to nest aggregates/FIRST/LAST/PREV/NEXT. Aggregates/FIRST/LAST/PREV/NEXT cannot be nested. The only exception allowed is PREV/NEXT(FIRST/LAST()).
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: illegal use of MATCH_NUMBER or CLASSIFIER in MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause
cause: An attempt was made to use MATCH_NUMBER or CLASSIFIER in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause. CLASSIFIER and MATCH_NUMBER can only be used in the MEASURES clause. CLASSIFIER and MATCH_NUMBER cannot be used inside aggregates/FIRST/LAST/PREV/NEXT.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: illegal use of aggregates or navigation operators in MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause
cause: An attempt was made to define aggregates/FIRST/LAST/PREV/NEXT over multiple variables. Aggregates/FIRST/LAST/PREV/NEXT cannot be defined over multiple variables.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: illegal use of RUNNING or FINAL in MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause
cause: An attempt was made to use RUNNING or FINAL in MATCH_RECOGNIZE. RUNNING or FINAL can only be used on aggregate/FIRST/LAST. FINAL aggregate/FIRST/LAST is not allowed in the DEFINE clause.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: Correlated subqueries are not allowed in MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause.
cause: An attempt was made to use correlated subqueries in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause. Correlated subqueries are currently not allowed in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: Correlation variables are not allowed in MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause.
cause: An attempt was made to use correlation variables in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause. Correlation variables are currently not allowed in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: This aggregate is not yet supported in MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause.
cause: An unsupported aggregate was specified in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause. Only COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX are currently supported in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause. Distinct aggregates are currently not supported in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: Quantified subpatterns that can have empty matches are not yet supported.
cause: There were empty matches for the quantified subpattern in the PATTERN clause. Quantified subpatterns are currently required to match one or more rows.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: AFTER MATCH SKIP TO variable is not bounded in the match found.
cause: AFTER MATCH SKIP TO variable was not bound in the match found due to pattern operators such as |, *, ?, and so on.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: Exclusion syntax cannot be used with WITH UNMATCHED ROWS.
cause: An attempt was made to use exclusion syntax with WITH UNMATCHED ROWS. Exclusion syntax {- -} cannot be used with WITH UNMATCHED ROWS.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: The PARTITION BY, ORDER BY, or MEASURES clause is too large for MATCH_RECOGNIZE.
cause: The number of items in PARTITION BY, ORDER BY, or MEASURES clause exceeded the maximum allowed. There cannot be more than UB2MAXVAL elements in PARTITION BY, ORDER BY, or MEASURES clause.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: Next match starts at the same point last match started.
cause: AFTER MATCH SKIP TO option repositioned the next match at the start of the previous one resulting in an infinite loop.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: MATCH_RECOGNIZE pattern is too large.
cause: MATCH_RECOGNIZE pattern was too large. More than UB2MAXVAL elements in alternation, concatenation, or permute, or more than UB4MAXVAL states in the state machine are currently not supported. Permute with more than 7 elements or bounded quantifier bound greater than 200 are also currently not supported.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: Subquery inside MATCH_RECOGNIZE cannot contain MATCH_RECOGNIZE.
cause: An attempt was made to use a subquery containing a MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause inside a MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause. Subqueries containing MATCH_RECOGNIZE clauses are currently not allowed in the MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: illegal offset for MATCH_RECOGNIZE navigation operators
cause: An attempt was made to use something other than a constant or a bind variable as the offset for MATCH_RECOGNIZE navigation operators FIRST, LAST, PREV, or NEXT. Offset for MATCH_RECOGNIZE navigation operators have to be constants or bind variables.
action: Modify the query and retry the operation.

description: MATCH_RECOGNIZE is not supported on lateral views.
cause: An attempt was made to use MATCH_RECOGNIZE on a lateral view, which was not supported.
action: Remove MATCH_RECOGNIZE from the query or do not use a lateral view. ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

description: Invalid SQL ROW LIMITING expression was specified.
cause: The SQL ROW LIMITING expression contained components other than literals, binds, correlation variables, or subqueries.
action: Modify the SQL ROW LIMITING expression and retry the operation. ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

description: Invalid use of PARTITION BY or ORDER BY clause.
cause: Either the PARTITION BY or ORDER BY was specified on more than one argument of a POLYMORPHIC TABLE FUNCTION.
action: Check the SQL statement and rewrite if necessary.

description: Incorrect use of COLUMNS operator.
cause: COLUMNS function was used outside a POLYMORPHIC TABLE FUNCTION.
action: Check the SQL statement and rewrite if necessary.

description: Invalid use of POLYMORPHIC TABLE FUNCTION.
cause: POLYMORPHIC TABLE FUNCTION was specified inside RECURSIVE WITH clause.
action: Check the SQL statement and rewrite if necessary.

description: Unsupported data types (%s) for polymorphic table function
cause: Non-scalar data types were used in polymorphic table function. Only scalar data types are supported.
action: Use only scalar data types in polymorphic table function.

description: Data types mismatch (%s<<==>>%s) for polymorphic table function
cause: Data types for the source and target did not match for polymorphic table function. In Get_Col and Put_Col APIs, both the type of the collection element and the type of the polymorphic table function column must match.
action: Ensure the collection element type matches the column type of the polymorphic table function

description: Duplicate column name (%s)
cause: The new column name already existed as a passthrough column in the polymorphic table function.
action: Use a different column name that is unambiguous.

description: Invalid column ID (%s) in Get_Col or Put_Col
cause: The column number specified in the Get_Col or Put_Col API for polymorphic table functions was incorrect.
action: Use a column ID that is valid for this polymorphic table function.

description: The API %s can be called only during execution time of a polymorphic table function.
cause: This API was called in a context other than the execution time context of a polymorphic table function. This API is not supported in this context.
action: Use this call only during the execution context of a polymorphic table function.

description: typecode not set for a new column in the polymorphic table function
cause: The type of this new column was not set.
action: Set the typecode and other needed metadata during the describe phase of the polymorphic table function.

description: This new column name (%s) already exists.
cause: This new column name was already created during the describe phase and therefore it is a duplicate column name.
action: Ensure that the new column names are unique for this polymorphic table function.

description: The %s method failed with error(s). %s
cause: This method of polymorphic table function had error(s) during SQL compilation.
action: Look at the errors and resolve them.

description: One of the new column names is a zero-length identifier.
cause: A zero-length identifier was used as a new column name that was created during the describe phase.
action: Specify valid identifiers for new column names.

description: One of the new column names is too long.
cause: An identifier with more than 128 bytes was used for one of the new column names that was created during the describe phase.
action: Specify at most 128 bytes for new column names.

description: invalid use of PARTITION BY or ORDER BY clause
cause: Either the PARTITION BY or the ORDER BY clause was specified on an argument of a non-table semantic POLYMORPHIC TABLE FUNCTION.
action: Remove the PARTITION BY or the ORDER BY clause.

description: nested polymorphic table function is disallowed
cause: A polymorphic table function was specified as an argument of a table function.
action: Modify the query so that there is no nested polymorphic table function.

description: new column name (%s) is invalid
cause: The new column name was invalid. It should be a valid Oracle identifier and should not be an Oracle reserved word.
action: Use a different column name that is a valid Oracle identifier and that is not an Oracle reserved word.

description: new column (%s) has length (%s) that is greater than the maximum allowed length (%s)
cause: The length specified for a new column for the polymorphic table function was greater than the maximum allowed length.
action: Specify a new column length that is less than or equal to the maximum allowed length.

description: object views are not supported with polymorphic table functions
cause: An object view was being created with polymorphic table function in the select query.
action: Do not use object views with polymorphic table function.

description: new column (%s) is not allowed with describe only polymorphic table function
cause: The new column name was created in describe only polymorphic table function.
action: Do not create a new column when no execution methods like OPEN, FETCH_ROWS or CLOSE are specified.

description: row replication flag was not set
cause: A row replication API was called, but the Describe method set ROW_REPLICATION to FALSE (default).
action: Change the value of ROW_REPLICATION to TRUE in the Describe method.

description: The parameter of type TABLE or COLUMN must not be NULL for a polymorphic table function.
cause: An attempt was made to use NULL as argument for the parameter of type TABLE or COLUMN on a polymorphic table function.
action: Use an argument different than NULL for the parameter of type TABLE or COLUMN.

description: target size(%s) is smaller than source size(%s) for column(%s) in %s
cause: When reading a column from database or writing a column to the database, destination buffer should not be smaller than the source.
action: Change the size of destination buffer.

description: character set IDs do no match %s
cause: When reading a column from the database or writing a column to the database, character set did not match.
action: Ensure that the collection and table column character sets are identical.

description: cursor expressions are not allowed with polymorphic table functions
cause: A cursor expression was used as an argument to polymorphic table function.
action: Instead of using the CURSOR expression, use the REF CURSOR bind parameter.

description: The argument of type DBMS_TF.TABLE_T cannot be a TABLE.
cause: A TABLE was used as argument for a formal of type DBMS_TF.TABLE_T.

description: Invalid value is passed to a bitmap operator.
cause: An attempt was made to pass an invalid value to a bitmap operator.
action: Pass only expressions that have integer values to BITMAP_BUCKET_NUMBER and BITMAP_BIT_POSITION and provide only positive integer values for BITMAP_CONSTRUCT_AGG.

description: invalid size value for BITMAP_BUCKET_NUMBER or BITMAP_BIT_POSITION operator
cause: An attempt was made to pass an invalid size value for a BITMAP_BUCKET_NUMBER or BITMAP_BIT_POSITION operator.
action: Pass only positive values that are less than 32 GB for the size argument of BITMAP_BUCKET_NUMBER and BITMAP_BIT_POSITION operators.

description: The bitmap size exceeds maximum size of its SQL data type.
cause: An attempt was made to construct a bitmap larger than its maximum SQL type size.
action: Call BITMAP_CONSTRUCT_AGG with input BITMAP_BIT_POSITION and a smaller or the default bucket size argument.

description: The input is not a valid bitmap produced by BITMAP COUNT DISTINCT operators.
cause: An attempt was made to pass a bitmap that was not produced by one of the BITMAP COUNT DISTINCT operators.
action: Pass only bitmaps constructed by using BITMAP_CONSTRUCT_AGG or BITMAP_OR_AGG to the BITMAP COUNT DISTINCT related operators. ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

description: operation disallowed; cluster cannot be created in Oracle Autonomous Database Cloud
cause: Cluster feature is not supported in Oracle Autonomous Database Cloud.
action: Use heap-organized tables to store data in Oracle Autonomous Database Cloud.

description: operation disallowed; column with ROWID type cannot be created in Oracle Autonomous Database Cloud
cause: An attempt was made to create a table with ROWID column type. By default, Oracle Autonomous Database Cloud runs with ROW MOVEMENT enabled. Hence, ROWIDs stored in ROWID column may not be valid if rows are moved by automated maintenance operations, such as table shrink.
action: Set ATP_ALLOW_ROWID_COLUMN_TYPE=TRUE and disable row movement of the tables that are referenced by the ROWID column. ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

description: A DBMS_KAFKA application does not exist for cluster %0!s and application %1!s.
cause: The procedure call was provided values for a nonexistent cluster and application pair.
action: Pass in names for an existing cluster and application pair.

description: DBMS_KAFKA cluster ID cannot be a NULL value.
cause: A cluster ID was specified as NULL.
action: This is an internal error; contact Oracle Support Services.

description: DBMS_KAFKA generated cluster ID '%0!s' is greater than 40 characters.
cause: The generated cluster ID was too long.
action: This is an internal error; contact Oracle Support Services.

description: DBMS_KAFKA cluster not found. Cluster ID is %0!s.
cause: A DBMS_KAFKA cluster was not found with the specified cluster ID.
action: This is an internal error; contact Oracle Support Services.

description: An attempt to create a connection to Kafka cluster %0!s failed with status %1!s and secondary status %2!s.
cause: An attempt to connect to a Kafka cluster failed.
action: Check the availability of the Kafka cluster and the security credentials required for connecting.

description: Property %0!s is not allowed because it would obscure a 'librdkafka' property with the same name.
cause: An Oracle SQL Access to Kafka (OSAK) property was specified with a property name that was also used by 'librdkafka'.
action: Rename or remove the OSAK property.

description: Property %0!s cannot be NULL.
cause: The property was specified without a value.
action: Update the property and specify a value.

description: OSAK Cluster configuration directory is not specified.
cause: The cluster configuration directory was specified as NULL.
action: Provide a cluster configuration directory name. The directory must be readable to an Oracle SQL Access to Kafka (OSAK) administrator.

description: The OSAK properties file '%0!s' could not be read.
cause: An Oracle SQL Access to Kafka (OSAK) 'osakafka.properties' file could not be read.
action: Check that the OSAK properties file exists in the cluster configuration directory and is readable.

description: OSAK SASL/SSL credential name is NULL.
cause: An attempt to configure an Oracle SQL Access to Kafka (OSAK) cluster failed because the SASL/SSL credential name was NULL.
action: The password for SASL/SSL must be stored as a database credential using the DBMS_CREDENTIAL.CREATE_CREDENTIAL() procedure. Supply the database credential name for the credential_name parameter in the DBMS_KAFKA_ADM.REGISTER_CLUSTER procedure call.

description: The application %0!s is still being used by %1!s and cannot be dropped. Stop all programs that are using this application and retry the drop procedure.
cause: There were one or more programs still using the application with either an uncommitted DBMS_KAFKA.UPDATE_OFFSET call or a global temporary table with pending inserts.
action: Commit or roll back the pending transactions. Alternatively, shut down the programs that are accessing the application.

description: One or more properties required for Kerberos authentication are missing from the 'osakafka.properties' configuration file. The list of required properties are {'sasl.kerberos.principal', 'sasl.kerberos.config', 'sasl.kerberos.ccname', 'sasl.mechanism', 'sasl.kerberos.service.name'}.
cause: One or more required properties were missing from the 'osakafka.properties' file.
action: Set 'sasl.mechanism=GSSAPI' to indicate Kerberos authentication. Add all of the required properties to the 'osakafka.properties' file and retry the operation.

description: The allowed number of columns in a reference table is between 1 and %1!s. The number of columns is %0!s.
cause: The specified number of columns was not within the allowed limit. This number does not include the metadata columns KAFKA_OFFSET, KAFKA_PARTITION, and KAFKA_EPOCH_TIMESTAMP.
action: Specify a reference table that contains fewer columns.

description: The reference table %0!s contains one of the reserved OSAK columns {'KAFKA_PARTITION', 'KAFKA_OFFSET', 'KAFKA_EPOCH_TIMESTAMP'} that either vary in column position or data type.
cause: There were one or more columns in the reference table that did not match data type or position for the Oracle SQL Access to Kafka (OSAK) reserved column names. The first three columns of all OSAK external tables are INTEGER columns named 'KAFKA_PARTITION', 'KAFKA_OFFSET', 'KAFKA_EPOCH_TIMESTAMP' in that order.
action: Specify a different reference table that either does not contain OSAK reserved columns or contains all OSAK reserved columns with the correct data type and in the correct order.

description: There is an unexpected failure for the Oracle SQL Access to Kafka trigger associated with a DROP USER statement for user %0!s while processing type %1!s.
cause: An unexpected failure occurred while processing a DROP USER statement.
action: This is an internal error; contact Oracle Support Services.

description: The reference table %0!s contains at least one invisible or hidden column.
cause: There were one or more columns in the reference table that are invisible or hidden and thus cannot be used as a reference table.
action: Specify a different reference table that does not contain any invisible or hidden columns.

description: The TRACE_LEVELS parameter is a comma-separated list of tracing level values. The supplied value {%0!s} contains characters other than alphabetic characters, underscores, and commas.
cause: The tracing levels list contains characters that are not allowed.
action: Update the tracing levels list to contain a comma-separated list of tracing levels.

description: There is a string element greater than 32,765 characters in the supplied Avro schema.
cause: The supplied Avro schema contains a string longer than the allowed maximum length.
action: Update the schema to shorten the excessively long string element.

description: operation disallowed: data file %s is being moved
cause: The specified data file was being moved.
action: Wait for the move operation to complete and retry the command.

description: File error during move operation on file '%s'
cause: The move operation is encountering an error for the moved data file. The error might be caused by the file going offline or by an I/O error. See the alert or trace files in all instances for further information.
action: Retry the move command.
params: 1) file_name: The name of the file.

description: a data file copy that is not current
cause: An obsolete copy of a data file left from a data file move operation was used for the CREATE CONTROLFILE command or file header read.
action: Pass a valid file or perform a media recovery on the file.

description: a half-done data file copy
cause: A half-done copy of a data file created from a previous data file move operation was used for the CREATE CONTROLFILE command or file header read.
action: Check file headers and pass only valid files.

description: Database names in file headers are inconsistent: %s and %s.
cause: Differing database names were found in database file headers.
action: Check that correct and valid data files are used.

description: Header validation failed for %s File ('%s').
cause: Oracle server failed to read or write to the specified file because the file has an SCN value which is too high for this release.
action: Contact Oracle Support Services.

description: only PDB files can be moved to or from the object store
cause: Either the root CDB or the non-CDB file could not be moved to or from the object store.
action: Check the source and destination of the move operation.

description: only read-only files can be moved to or from the object store
cause: The read/write file could not be moved to or from the object store.
action: Check the source and destination of the move operation.

description: cannot move file to or from the object store on ADG
cause: The data file move operation to or from object store was not supported on Active Data Guard (ADG).
action: Switch ADG to a primary database to perform this operation.

description: cannot make object store files read/write
cause: Tablespaces with object store files could not be read/write.
action: Move the files out of object store to make the tablespace read/write.

description: trace event for recovery data file pre-creation
cause: NA
action: Enable this event to trace recovery datafile pre-creation

description: created file '%s' is located in object store
cause: Files could not be created in the object store.
action: Create the files outside of the object store and then move them to the object store.

description: no DEFAULT_CREDENTIAL in PDB %s available for data file move
cause: When moving a data file to the object store, the DEFAULT_CREDENTIAL was not found.
action: Set a valid DEFAULT_CREDENTIAL in the specified PDB that can authorize access to the object store URI specified for the data file move.

description: no DEFAULT_CREDENTIAL in PDB %s available for data file drop
cause: When dropping a data file in the object store, the DEFAULT_CREDENTIAL was not found.
action: Set a valid DEFAULT_CREDENTIAL in the specified PDB that can authorize access to the object store URI specified for the data file drop.

description: cannot make object store data file read/write during recovery
cause: Object store data files cannot be made read/write during recovery.
action: Move the data file out of the object store to continue recovery.

description: could not cache credential '%s' for object store access : %s
cause: Object store data files require credentials to authorize access. An attempt to cache the credentials failed. Caching credentials is necessary for access in various circumstances.
action: Review the associated error code for more information on other related errors which may have occurred. Check that the specified credential name is valid and is not disabled.

description: could not read DEFAULT_CREDENTIAL in mounted or closed state
cause: The DEFAULT_CREDENTIAL can only be accessed when the PDB is open in this instance. This instance is detected to be closed or mounted.
action: Open the PDB on this instance to access the credential or issue the operation on another instance which has the PDB open.

description: test event for online datafile move operation
cause: NA

description: Primary key column cannot be redacted for JSON Duality View
cause: Attempt was made to have a redacted column be a primary key column in a JSON Duality View.
action: Do not redact the primary key column in a JSON Duality View.

description: JSON Duality View Entity Tag (ETAG) column cannot be redacted
cause: Attempt was made to have a redacted column be part of the ETAG in a JSON Duality View.
action: Do not redact an ETAG column in a JSON Duality View.

description: Cannot create JSON-relational duality view '%s': Operator not permitted for '_id' field
cause: An unsupported operator is used in the '_id' field.
action: Remove the unsupported operator or expression from the '_id' field.
params: 1) view_name: The name of the duality view.

description: Unsupported data type used in column of a JSON Relational Duality View '%s'.
cause: Unsupported data type is used in a Duality View statement.
action: Do not use columns of data types LOB, Abstract Data Type, collections, TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE or XML to compute the ETAG values.

description: Cannot create JSON-relational duality view '%s': foreign key column '%s' of table '%s' should be part of the primary or unique key of the same table
cause: The foreign key column can only be selected if it is also part of a primary or unique key of the same table, which is required to uniquely identify rows in the duality view objects.
action: Add the foreign key columns to the primary or unique key of the same table, or remove it from the SELECT statement.

description: Single-row unnested sub-object returned more than one row.
cause: More than one row is being returned for the specified sub-object, which is not allowed.
action: Change the data to ensure that only one row is returned for the specified sub-object. Alternatively, change the view definition to make this sub-object an array.

description: The data type of input column %s to JSON single-value index is incompatible with the expected data type JSON.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a JSON single-value index on an input column that is not JSON data type.
action: Ensure that the input column is of JSON data type.
params: 1) column_name: The name of the input column.

description: resumable cursor session state mismatch during replay
cause: The session state of the resumable cursor at the replay did not match the state at the capture.
action: Review the current open select cursor to see if it needs repositioning manually and review the request to see if the request is committed, and if not whether it is safe to resubmit.

description: cursor not resumable at failover server
cause: A cursor deemed resumable during capture could not be resumed.
action: Resubmit work to the application.

description: Invalid service attribute value sent by the client driver
cause: At failover, the value of %s sent by the client driver is above the maximum supported value.
action: Upgrade to a driver that supports the relevant feature.

description: Transaction is automatically rolled back since it is blocking a higher priority transaction from another session.
cause: The transaction is holding a row lock and blocking a transaction with a higher priority. The blocked transaction has already been waiting for target wait time and then request to automatically rollback this blocker transaction.
action: Check and rollback the current transaction.

description: ROLLBACK is being used on an automatically rolled back XA branch. Use XA_END and XA_ROLLBACK instead.
cause: User issue ROLLBACK on a automatically rolled back xa branch, they should use XA_END and XA_ROLLBACK instead.
action: Use XA_END and XA_ROLLBACK for the current transaction.

description: Transaction must roll back
cause: User must issue rollback to current transaction to acknowledge that they know that the current transaction has been automatically rolled back.
action: Issue ROLLBACK for the local transaction and issue XA_END and XA_ROLLBACK for the XA transaction.

description: Cannot set the parameter txn_priority inside an Oracle Scheduler job
cause: An attempt is being made to set the parameter txn_priority inside an Oracle Scheduler job, which is not allowed.
action: Set the txn_priority parameter inside an Oracle connection or server process.

description: Cannot alter the parameter txn_priority when there is an active transaction in the session
cause: An attempt is being made to set the parameter txn_priority when there is an active transaction.
action: Either Commit or Rollback the active transaction before attempting to set txn_priority parameter.

description: Dynamic sampling is not allowed on this object.
cause: An attempt is being made to do dynamic sampling on an object that is not a package or a function or an object type.
action: Specify a package, a function or an object type on which to do dynamic sampling.

description: The function (%s) does not exist in the package (%s).
cause: An attempt is being made to do dynamic sampling on a function that does not exist in the specified package.
action: Specify the correct function name to perform dynamic sampling.

description: Object %s does not exist in the given schema.
cause: The specified object does not exist in the given schema.
action: The package, function or type on which to do dynamic sampling must exist.

description: Creating a Timehouse enabled table requires a Timehouse instance.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a Timehouse enabled table on an instance that does not have Timehouse enabled.
action: Create the Timehouse enabled table on a Timehouse instance.

description: Invalid Timehouse command
cause: An invalid Timehouse command is specified.
action: Verify that the SQL statement uses a valid Timehouse command.

description: Cannot combine Timehouse operation with other operations
cause: An attempt is being made to combine the Timehouse operation with other ALTER TABLE operations.
action: Ensure that Timehouse is the sole operation specified in the ALTER TABLE statement.

description: Cannot perform the operation because column name '%s' is a reserved column in a Timehouse enabled table.
cause: An attempt is being made to perform an operation on a reserved column in a Timehouse enabled table. Reserved columns cannot be added, dropped, modified, or renamed. The list of reserved names is: SYS_STARTTIME, SYS_ENDTIME, SYS_STARTSCN, SYS_ENDSCN, SYS_OPERATION, SYS_XID, VERSIONS_STARTTIME, VERSIONS_ENDTIME, VERSIONS_STARTSCN, VERSIONS_ENDSCN, and VERSIONS_XID.
action: Retry the operation on a non-reserved column.

description: Missing RETENTION clause for Timehouse enabled table.
cause: An attempt is being made to create a Timehouse enabled table without specifying the RETENTION clause in the CREATE TABLE statement.
action: Specify the RETENTION clause when creating a Timehouse enabled table.

description: event for internal test of Timehouse
cause: This is an internal event to tests feature of Timehouse and this is for internal use only.
action: None

description: Invalid retention period specified
cause: The specified retention period of the Timehouse enabled table is invalid.
action: Specify a positive integer value for the retention period.

description: Timehouse currently does not support invisible columns.
cause: An attempt is being made to add an invisible column or modify an existing column to be invisible on Timehouse-enabled tables.
action: Do not try to add an invisible column or modify an existing column to be invisible on Timehouse-enabled tables.

description: Cannot enable a table for Timehouse that has invisible columns.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable Timehouse on a table that has invisible columns.
action: Do not try to enable a table for Timehouse that has invisible columns.

description: DROP operation is not permitted on table "%s"."%s".
cause: An attempt is being made to drop a Timehouse history table or a colmap table which are managed automatically as part of a Timehouse enabled table.
action: Drop the Timehouse enabled table to remove its corresponding internal tables.
params: 1) table_schema_name: The schema in which the table resides. 2) table_name: The table name.

description: Timehouse cannot be enabled on a %s.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable Timehouse on an object type that is not supported by Timehouse.
action: Do not use the Timehouse clause on External tables, Nested tables, Private temporary tables, Blockchain tables, or in a CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement.

description: Table has columns with data types that are not supported by Timehouse.
cause: An attempt is being made to add a column with a data type that is not supported by Timehouse, or the table on which Timehouse is being enabled contains columns with unsupported data types.
action: Do not use a nested table column data type in an object on which Timehouse is being enabled. Do not use a single quote in the abstract data type column name.

description: Timehouse enabled table can have at most %s columns.
cause: An attempt is being made either to create a Timehouse enabled table with too many columns, or to add columns to a Timehouse enabled table such that the total number of columns exceeds the maximum limit.
action: Reduce the number of columns and resubmit the command.

description: DDL to %s Timehouse on a database table is not permitted.
cause: An attempt is being made to execute a restricted DDL without the required session-level parameter being set.
action: Contact Oracle Support to set the required session-level parameter before executing the DDL.

description: Cannot exchange partition with a table that is not Timehouse enabled
cause: An attempt is being made to exchange a partition of a Timehouse enabled table with a table that is not Timehouse enabled.
action: Retry with the exchange partition operation with a Timehouse enabled table.

description: Valid time period command is not supported by Timehouse enabled table
cause: An attempt is being made to run a valid time period command that is not supported by a Timehouse enabled table.
action: Do not use a valid time period command for a Timehouse enabled table.

description: Timehouse is already %s on this table.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable or disable Timehouse on a table that is already Timehouse enabled or disabled.
action: Do not enable or disable Timehouse on a table that is already Timehouse enabled or disabled, respectively.

description: Oracle GoldenGate support mode FULL is required to enable Timehouse on the table.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable Timehouse on a table that does not have Oracle GoldenGate support mode set to FULL.
action: Do not enable Timehouse on a table that does not have Oracle GoldenGate support mode set to FULL.

description: Unsupported DDL on a Timehouse enabled table.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable or disable Timehouse on a Timehouse enabled table using the ALTER TABLE ENABLE or DISABLE Timehouse statement.
action: Do not use the ALTER TABLE ENABLE or DISABLE Timehouse statement on a Timehouse enabled table.

description: Cannot enable Flashback Time Travel on a Timehouse enabled table
cause: An attempt is being made to enable Flashback Time Travel (previously known as Flashback Data Archive (FDA)) on a Timehouse enabled table.
action: Do not enable Flashback Time Travel on a Timehouse enabled table.

description: Table includes columns with names that are reserved for a Timehouse enabled table.
cause: The table has columns with names that are reserved for a Timehouse enabled table. The list of reserved names is: SYS_STARTTIME, SYS_ENDTIME, SYS_STARTSCN, SYS_ENDSCN, SYS_OPERATION, SYS_XID, VERSIONS_STARTTIME, VERSIONS_ENDTIME, VERSIONS_STARTSCN, VERSIONS_ENDSCN, and VERSIONS_XID.
action: Rename or drop the columns to avoid using reserved names.

description: Timehouse table is not synchronized until the %s specified in the query.
cause: The Timehouse table is being queried with a system change number (SCN) or TIMESTAMP beyond the queryable SCN or TIMESTAMP.
action: Query the table with a lower SCN or TIMESTAMP or wait for the database to advance the queryable SCN or TIMESTAMP.

description: Cannot drop a Timehouse enabled table
cause: An attempt is being made to drop a Timehouse enabled table.
action: Do not drop a Timehouse enabled table. Disable Timehouse on the table before dropping it.

description: Online redefinition is currently not supported on a Timehouse enabled table.
cause: An attempt is being made to perform an online redefinition on a Timehouse enabled table.
action: Do not perform an online redefinition on a Timehouse enabled table.

description: Timehouse enabled tables cannot currently be added to Oracle Database Vault realms or command rules.
cause: An attempt is being made to add a Timehouse enabled table, or a schema that contains Timehouse enabled tables, to an Oracle Database Vault realm or command rule.
action: Do not add a Timehouse enabled table to a realm or command rule. Do not use the "%" wildcard to add all objects in a schema that contains Timehouse enabled tables to a realm or command rule. Instead, add each object that is not enabled for Timehouse separately to the realm or command rule. Refer to the ALL_TIMEHOUSE_TABLES view for a list of Timehouse enabled tables in each schema.

description: Timehouse cannot currently be enabled on a table that is part of an Oracle Database Vault realm or command rule.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable Timehouse on a table that is part of an Oracle Database Vault realm or command rule.
action: Do not enable Timehouse on a table that is part of an Oracle Database Vault realm or command rule.

description: Enabling a realm or command rule that contains Timehouse enabled tables is currently not supported.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable a realm or command rule that contains Timehouse enabled tables.
action: Do not enable a realm or command rule that contains Timehouse enabled tables. Disable Timehouse on the table and update the realm or command rule.

description: FGA policies are currently not supported on Timehouse enabled tables.
cause: An attempt is being made to add FGA policies on Timehouse enabled tables.
action: Do not add FGA policies on Timehouse enabled tables.

description: Timehouse cannot currently be enabled on a table that has FGA policies added to it.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable Timehouse on a table that has FGA policies added to it.
action: Do not enable Timehouse on a table that has FGA policies added to it.

description: Creating or adding an object-level or column-level audit policy with SELECT action is currently not supported on Timehouse enabled tables.
cause: An attempt is being made to create or add an object-level or column-level audit policy with SELECT action on a Timehouse enabled table, which is not supported.
action: Do not create or add object-level or column-level audit policy with SELECT action on Timehouse enabled tables.

description: Timehouse cannot currently be enabled on a table that has object-level or column-level audit policies with SELECT action on it.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable Timehouse on a table that has object-level or column-level audit policies with SELECT action on it.
action: Do not enable Timehouse on a table that has object-level or column-level audit policies with SELECT action on it.

description: A flashback query on a partition of a Timehouse enabled table is not supported.
cause: A flashback query attempted to access a specific partition of a Timehouse enabled table. Timehouse does not support flashback queries scoped to individual partitions.
action: Rewrite the query to access the full table instead of a specific partition.

description: OLS policies cannot currently be applied on a Timehouse-enabled table "%s"."%s". This functionality will be supported soon.
cause: An attempt is being made to apply OLS policies on a Timehouse-enabled table.
action: Do not try to apply OLS policies on a Timehouse-enabled table.

description: Timehouse cannot currently be enabled on a table that has OLS policies applied to it. This functionality will be supported soon.
cause: An attempt is being made to enable Timehouse on a table that has OLS policies applied to it.
action: Do not try to enable Timehouse on a table that has OLS policies applied to it.

description: Flashback queries with a query %s earlier than when the table was enabled for Timehouse (%s "%s") are not supported.
cause: An attempt is being made to perform a flashback query using a query SCN or TIMESTAMP that is earlier than when the table was enabled for Timehouse.
action: Retry the flashback query using a query SCN or TIMESTAMP that is greater than or equal to the SCN or TIMESTAMP when Timehouse was enabled.
params: 1) flashback_query_type: SCN or TIMESTAMP based flashback query. 2) flashback_query_type: SCN or TIMESTAMP based flashback query. 3) initial_load_value: Initial load SCN or timestamp.

cause: INMEMORY(ALL) and NO INMEMORY(ALL) were used in the same statement.
action: Specify one of either INMEMORY(ALL) or NO INMEMORY(ALL).

description: Failed to detach from a persistent memory region.
cause: Attempt to detach a persistent memory region failed because one or more processes were still attached.
action: Retry the operation.

cause: This is an internal event to tests certain features in PQ and this is for internal use only.

cause: This is an event to ensure that when allocating parallel query servers, we don't get local instance load information from Cluster Global Service.
action: None.

cause: This is an internal event to test slave mapping skew handling and is for internal use only.
action: None

cause: This is an internal event to control keyboard interruption for tracing hint with delay option and this is for internal use only.
action: Set this event only under the supervision of Oracle development.

cause: This is an internal event to control granule distribution to PX servers for in-memory columnar objects and is for internal use only.
action: Set this event only under the supervision of Oracle development.

cause: This is an internal event to test range table queue object sampling for external table and is for internal use only.
action: None

cause: This is an internal event to test clumped and declumped plans for distributed vector index and is for internal use only.
action: None

description: maximum number of elements(%s) in a tuple exceeded for a TVC
cause: An attempt to specify more than the allowed number of elements in a tuple of the table value constructor (TVC) is being made.
action: Do not specify more than allowed number of elements in a tuple of a TVC.

description: each tuple should have same number of elements in a Table Value Constructor
cause: An attempt was made to specify different number of elements in a tuple of Table Value Constructor.
action: Each tuple of a Table Value Constructor should have same number of elements.

description: tuple in a Table Value Constructor cannot be empty
cause: An attempt was made to specify a tuple of Table Value Constructor that had no elements.
action: Each tuple of a Table Value Constructor should have at least one element.

description: columns must be specified with %s
cause: Column names must be specified when Table Value Constructor is used in this context.
action: When a Table Value Constructor is used in contexts like INSERT or WITH, column name must be specified.

description: Number of Columns must be same as number of elements
cause: Number of columns aliases is not same as number of elements of each tuple of Table Value Constructor.
action: Specify the same number of columns in a Table Value Constructor as the number of elements in each tuple.

description: Maximum number of tuples in Table Value Constructor exceeded
cause: Number of tuples in the values clause of Table Value Constructor is more than the allowed limit.
action: Specify less than the allowed number of tuples in the values clause of a Table Value Constructor.

description: Duplicate name in column alias list for Table Value Constructor
cause: Column aliases specified for Table Value Constructor had one or more names spefified more than once.
action: Specify a column alias only once in column alias list of a Table Value Constructor.

description: Table value constructor is not supported in %s.
cause: The Table value constructor was not supported with this feature.
action: Do not use the table value constructor with this feature.

description: list of values in a table value constructor is not well formed
cause: An attempt was made to specify a list of expressions in a Table Value Constructor that were not separated by a comma.
action: Specify each expression in a list of values for Table Value Constructor such that it is followed by a "," or a ")".

description: returning clause is not allowed with INSERT and Table Value Constructor
cause: Returning clause was not allowed when inserting multiple rows by using Table Constructor in this release.
action: Use Insert one row at a time to use returning clause.

description: Sequence as default is not supported with INSERT using table value constructor
cause: Table columns that have default values specified as sequences are not supported when they are referenced as keyword DEFAULT in an INSERT statement inserting multiple rows using table value constructor.
action: Use explicit values of the default when specifying INSERT using table value constructor.

description: INSERT on views with default columns is not supported using table value constructor
cause: Table columns that have default values specified are not supported when INSERT is done on a view defined on that table using table value constructor.
action: Use regular insert statement when inserting rows via views.

description: INSERT on remote tables is not supported when using default values with table value constructor
cause: Table valye constructors can not be used to insert values on remote tables when using default expressions.
action: Use regular insert statement when inserting in remote tables.

description: Incorrect syntax in IN clause using table value constructor
cause: Table value constructors in the IN clause should use comma separated values. For example: select employee_id, first_name, last_name from employees where employee_id in ( values (100), (101), (102) ); Should be specified as select employee_id, first_name, last_name from employees where employee_id in ( values (100, 101, 102) );
action: For a single value IN LIST, use comma separated values without parenthesis.

description: Column names must be specified in the alias for Table Value Constructor.
cause: Column names are not specified in the alias for the Table Value Constructor.
action: Add columns after the alias in the Table Value Constructor. The number of columns should match the number of values in each tuple of the Table Value Constructor.

description: The number of column names must match the number of values in the Table Value Constructor.
cause: The number of columns in the alias list must match the number of values in each tuple of the Table Value Constructor.
action: Change the number of columns in the alias for the Table Value Constructor to match the number of values in each tuple of the Table Value Constructor

description: A column specified in the INSERT INTO SET clause must be in the explicit column list.
cause: An attempt is being made to specify a column outside of the explicit column list.
action: Remove the specified column. Only columns in the explicit column list are allowed.

description: A column in the explicit column list is missing from certain rows in the INSERT INTO SET clause.
cause: A column in the explicit column list is missing from certain rows in the INSERT INTO SET clause. Once the explicit column list is specified in the INSERT INTO SET clause, every row must contain every column in the explicit column list.
action: Check for the row in which this column is missing.

description: Multi-row INSERT INTO SET clause is not allowed in MTI or MERGE.
cause: In MTI(multi-table INSERT) and MERGE, only a single row INSERT INTO SET clause is supported.
action: Check to ensure that the DML only contains a single row INSERT INTO SET clause.

description: RETURNING clause is not allowed with a multi-row INSERT INTO SET clause.
cause: RETURNING clause is not allowed when inserting multiple rows by using an INSERT INTO SET clause in this release.
action: Use single row insert with a RETURNING clause.

description: The global column list among rows exceeds the upper limit.
cause: The global column list in the INSERT INTO SET clause has too many columns.
action: Modify the INSERT INTO SET clause by limiting the number of columns to 1000 or 4000 depending on the database version.

description: A right parenthesis or a comma is excepted here.
cause: A group style INSERT INTO SET clause expects either a right parenthesis or a comma after a column.
action: Modify the INSERT INTO SET clause by adding the expected punctuation.

description: Non-aliased expressions or constants are not allowed in a BY NAME clause.
cause: An attempt is being made to specify non-aliased expressions or constants in the BY NAME clause.
action: Specify an alias for expressions or constants in a BY NAME clause.

description: No duplicated exposed column names are allowed in the BY NAME clause.
cause: An attempt is being made to specify a duplicated exposed column name in the BY NAME clause.
action: Check the exposed column names and remove the duplicate.

description: The explicit column list does not exactly match the exposed column names.
cause: The explicit column list does not exactly match the exposed column names.
action: Check the exposed column names and the explicit column list.

description: BY NAME or POSITION are semantic modifiers of the subquery only and are not compatible with the VALUES clause.
cause: BY NAME or POSITION are not compatible with the VALUES clause.
action: Remove either BY NAME or POSITION clause, or the VALUES clause.

description: BY NAME or POSITION are semantic modifiers of the subquery only and are not compatible with the INSERT INTO SET clause.
cause: BY NAME or POSITION are not compatible with the INSERT INTO SET clause.
action: Remove either BY NAME or POSITION clause, or the INSERT INTO SET clause.

description: Read completion delay detected for database block.
cause: There may be a slow or stuck storage or I/O subsystem.
action: Check storage or I/O subsystem logs.

description: fractured block detected in control file: (block %s, # blocks %s)
cause: A fractured block or checksum error was detected on reading the control file under no-enqueue control file transaction. The reason could be a stalled concurrent block update.
action: Retry the operation later.

description: A local temporary file remote call failed
cause: An operating system error or network error occurred when making a remote call to another instance during a local temporary space DDL operation.
action: Remedy the operating system or network errors mentioned in the error stack and then retry the operation.

description: file size refresh failed
cause: An operating system error or device error occurred when retrieving the file's size.
action: Remedy the operating system or device errors mentioned in the error stack and then perform crash recovery.

description: undo tablespace file suffered media failure
cause: An undo tablespace file was detected as inaccessible due to media failure.
action: Restore accessibility to the file mentioned in the error stack and restart the instance.

description: data file suffered media failure
cause: A data file was detected as inaccessible due to media failure.

description: specified path already exists
cause: The pathname of a new item specified in a DBFS API operation already exists.
action: Specify a valid, new pathname for the operation.

description: invalid parent directory in specified path
cause: The pathname of an item specified in a DBFS API operation has one or more invalid parent components.
action: Specify a valid pathname with valid parent components for the operation.

description: specified path is invalid
cause: The pathname of an item specified in a DBFS API operation is invalid.
action: Specify a valid pathname for the operation.

description: An unsupported operation was invoked.
cause: The current Database File System (DBFS) API operation was unsupported by a provider.
action: Use the provider feature set to invoke only supported operations.

description: an invalid combination of arguments was specified
cause: The current DBFS API operation specifies an invalid combination of arguments for the specified pathname(s) and operation.
action: Specify a valid combination of pathname(s) and arguments.

description: access control checks failed
cause: The current DBFS API operation failed access control checks for the pathname(s) being accessed.
action: Specify valid pathname(s) and principal for the operation, or take store-specific actions to enable access.

description: lock conflict in current operation
cause: A DBFS API locking operation could not be completed due to conflicts in the locking protocol.
action: Follow the proper lock/unlock protocol according to the provider feature set.

description: invalid store specified
cause: The current operation specifies an invalid store name.
action: Specify a valid store name for the operation.

description: invalid mount-point specified
cause: The current operation specifies an invalid mount-point.
action: Specify a valid mount-point for the operation.

description: invalid provider specified
cause: The current operation refers to an invalid or incomplete or non-conformant store provider package.
action: Specify a valid, complete, and conformant (per "dbms_dbfs_content_spi") store provider package.

description: cannot modify store via read-only mount
cause: The current operation attempts to modify a store via a read-only mount (or specifies a read-only store).
action: Specify a valid modifiable store/mount for the operation.

description: cross store operation
cause: The current operation attempts to span 2 or more different stores and cannot be implemented entirely by the DBFS API.
action: Split the operation, at the application-level, into multiple sub-operations to implement the same overall functionality.

description: specified path is a directory
cause: The current operation specifies a path that is a directory element, when a non-directory element is expected.
action: Specify a path of the proper type for the operation.

description: specified path is not a directory
cause: The current operation specifies a path that is not a directory element, when a directory element is expected.
action: Specify a path of the proper type for the operation.

description: directory not empty
cause: The current operation specifies a directory element that is not empty as required.
action: Specify an empty directory element.

description: cannot drop tablespace used by Database File System (DBFS)
cause: An attempt was made to drop a tablespace containing DBFS metadata tables.
action: Use dbfs_drop_filesystem.sql to drop the Database File System and try dropping the tablespace again.

description: %s is not a valid compression option. Use LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH
cause: An invalid value was specified for compression option
action: Specify any of 'LOW', 'MEDIUM' or 'HIGH' as the compression option.

description: %s is not a valid encryption option
cause: An invalid value was specified for encryption option
action: Specify any of '3DES168', 'AES128', 'AES192', 'AES256' as the encryption option

description: Cannot alter both a structured and an unstructured component of an XMLIndex in the same ALTER INDEX statement.
cause: An attempt was made to alter the unstructured component and structured component of an XMLIndex at the same time.
action: Use separate ALTER INDEX statements to change an unstructured component and a structured component of an XMLIndex.

description: Cannot create an XML Index with a structured component on a CLOB column within the object relational storage model.
cause: An attempt was made to create an XML Index with a structured component on a CLOB column within the object relational storage model.
action: Only an unstructured XML Index can be created on a CLOB column within the object relational storage model.

description: Cannot create an XMLIndex on an object-relational XML type table or column.
cause: An attempt was made to create an XMLIndex on an XML type table or column that uses the object-relational storage model.
action: The object-relational storage model does not support an XMLIndex.

description: Column name already used by internal column of the structured component of the XMLIndex.
cause: An attempt was made to use a column name already in use by an internal column of the structured component of the XMLIndex.
action: Chose another column name.

description: Cannot create domain index on XMLIndex internal tables.
cause: An attempt was made to create a domain index on an internal table of an XMLIndex.
action: Create the domain index on the base table.

description: incorrect use of comma(,) punctuation in COLUMN definitions
cause: An attempt was made to define COLUMNS with incorrect use of comma punctuation.
action: Properly separate COLUMN definitions with comma punctuation.

description: The XML Index has been successfully altered but the metadata could not be updated.
cause: An internal error occurred when updating the index metadata. The DBMS_METADATA.GET_DDL function may return improper metadata.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support Services if the error persists.

description: Cannot truncate a table that has an XMLIndex whose internal table has been indexed using Oracle Text.
cause: An attempt was made to truncate a table that had an XMLIndex whose internal table was indexed using Oracle Text.
action: Drop the Oracle Text index on the XMLIndex internal table.

description: A problem was encountered while dropping the statistics of an XML index.
cause: A problem was encountered while dropping the statistics of an XML index.
action: This message is followed by a second message providing more details about the error. Check the second error message for more information.

description: A problem occurred when gathering the statistics of an XML Index.
cause: A problem occurred when gathering the statistics of an XML Index.
action: This message will be followed by a second message giving more details about the error. Check the second error message for more information.

description: XMLIndex: problems encountered during EXPORT
cause: See associated error message.
action: Correct the error and retry command.

description: XMLIndex: problems encountered during IMPORT
cause: See associated error message.
action: Correct the error and retry command.

description: XDB.XDB$XIDX_IMP_T has bad data for "%s"."%s".
cause: This message was followed by a second message giving more details about the error. Check the second error message for the cause.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support to help delete all the rows that belong to the index given in the error message from the system table XDB.XDB$XIDX_IMP_T.
params: 1) owner: The owner of the XML Index. 2) index_name: The name of the XML Index.

description: A problem occurred when export or import XML Index.
cause: A problem occurred when exporting or importing an XML Index.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support.

description: The table used to exchange partition from does not have XML Index.
cause: The table used to exchange partition from did not have an XML Index.
action: Ensure the table used to exchange partition from has an XML Index.

description: incompatible XML index XPATH subsets found when exchanging partitions including XML indexes
cause: The XML index from the table to be exchanged partition with had different XPATH subsets than the XML index from the table used to exchange partition from.
action: Ensure the XML Indexes from both tables have the same XPATH subsets.

description: XMLIndex Exchange Partition: incompatible modes for asynchronous DML
cause: The XMLIndexes on the two tables had different deferred DML modes.
action: Correct the error and retry the command.

description: Incompatible XML index unstructured components were during the exchange of partitions including XML indexes.
cause: One of the XML indexes from the tables participating in exchanging partition did not have unstructured component.
action: Ensure the XML indexes from both tables have unstructured components.

description: incompatible XML Index structured components found when exchanging partitions including XML Indexes
cause: One of the XML Indexes from the tables participating in exchanging partition did not have a structured component.
action: Ensure the XML Indexes from both tables have structured components.

description: incompatible XML index structured components found when exchanging partitions including XML indexes
cause: The XML index from the table exchanging partitions had a structured component different from that of the XML index from the table from which the exchange partition was used.
action: Ensure that the XML indexes from both tables have the same structured components.

description: XMLIndex DDL: failure of the internal "%s"
cause: See associated error message.
action: Correct the error and retry command.

description: failed to run an XML Index recursive DDL "%s"
cause: A problem occurred when running XML Index recursive DDL.
action: This is an internal error. Contact Oracle Support.
params: 1) ddl_statement: The XML Index recursive DDL statement.

description: A recursive DDL failed during the XMLIndex DDL processing.
cause: A recursive DDL (Data Definition Language) command failed during an XMLIndex DDL processing.
action: The error message is followed by a second message with details about the error. Check the second error message for more information and take the appropriate action.

description: A problem occurred when setting an event for an XML Index.
cause: A problem occurred when setting an event for an XML Index.
action: This message will be followed by a second message giving more details about the error. Check the second error message for more information related to this issue.

description: A problem occurred when resetting an event of an XML index.
cause: A problem occurred when you tried to reset an event of an XML index.
action: This message will be followed by a second message giving more details about the error. Check the second error message for more information.

description: A problem occurred at the start of an XML index table function.
